review_text:
Prepare for transport into the days of the Rat Pack at the latest from the owners of Torrisi and Parm. CARBONE -- an overdue exploration of comfort Italian food in a place that delicately balances fur-clad models in stilettos; staff in Zac Posen-designed burgundy suits; art curated by Vito Schnabel; and beef carpaccio so beautifully prepared, you could spread it on the warm, perfect crunch-to-butter-ratio garlic bread.

It's a true testament to what dining looked like in the movies of the 60's and early 70's; when you dressed to dine with friends in a 'Suit & Tie' (sh*t) over a table so full of wine glasses and food, you can't see the stains of red sauce on the tablecloth.

Plan in advance, bring the right crowd, make friends with the right people and you could score the best seat in the house: the back brick room crescent table.

Menu highlights:

-Beef Carpaccio
-Seafood Salad
-Oysters
-Meatballs
-Pasta alla Vodka
-Seafood Pasta
-Lobster Fra Diavolo
-Shrimp Scampi
-Lemon Cheesecake

-Tiramisu

I was not about to spend Friday night moping around the apartment about being past my due date.  

Carbone had opened, early reports were positive... and reservation or not (not) I decided to head down for doors at 5:30 and see about snagging a table before all I could do is read about this place, green with envy.

And green with envy I would have been.  I think we all know by now that Rich and Mario would turn out exceptional versions of the familiar comfort Italian dishes we know and love.  I can confirm this.

What really shines about this place is the service and the vibe that is so tongue-in-cheek-that-its-not-tongue-in-cheek-at-all.  Never has "that's amore" been so perfectly placed in my life - right in between forkfuls of delicious spicy rigatoni a la vodka.

I read an article somewhere over the summer about the "extras" being planned - they came early and often. Clumps of delicious Parmesan, A slice of ham, "Grandma's Bread", House made pickles in olive oil, a bread basket (fans of parm will quickly notice the familiarity of the best garlic bread in town), fried bowtie cookies (cenci alla fiorentina), housemade limoncello, housemade grappa, and the most aw-shucks of them all - Sambuca, which the "wine advisor" (sommelier does not feel right in this instance) left on the table saying - "have as much as you want".  You can only have so much Sambuca, but it was appreciated. 

When asking where is the bathroom, I was not given directions.  I was told "right this way ma'am", and then led there.  

Perhaps the most unanticipated delight of this meal, given they were kind enough to seat us without a reservation (please call ahead on walk ins vs. taking my experience for the norm.) was the comfortable pacing, especially towards the end as we became friendly with the couple next to us - while drinking low margin coffee.  And then at just the absolute perfect time, instead of bringing over the cc billfold, our server came over and asked "can I get you anything else?"

No thanks. Just the check. And that private reservation # please. I know it exists.  

NOTES ON THE FOOD:
Had 2 Starters - the ceasar salad with strips of anchovies & the aged beef carpaccio.
Had 2 Pastas - the spicy rigatoni vodka & ravioli caruso with liver and bacon
Shared a Meat - the veal marsala
Shared Dessert - the blackout cake (OMFG) with two americanos

Perfect amount... if you plan on walking to the east broadway F after.

I'd like to start by pointing out that this is my first Yelp review. However, after seeing the other two reviews on here about Carbone (and I agree with Eater NY that they are a shill), I had to write a review about my experience last night at Carbone. The food was exceptional, I just wish the front of house staff held to the same standards as the kitchen does with the food.

I scored a reservation at Carbone by repeatedly calling the number posted on Carbone's website a couple of days before opening day. With persistence, I finally got through and scored a 7:30pm reservation for two during the second week after opening. We arrived at Carbone right at 7:30pm and were advised that our table "wasn't quite ready yet" and were encouraged to enjoy drinks at the bar. We happily obliged and headed to the bar to enjoy very well crafted Old Fashioned and Manhattan cocktails. At first, there were only a couple of other individuals at the bar so it didn't feel cramped. However, after the wave of 7:30-8pm reservations started rolling in and with no tables ready, the bar scene became a nightmare. We were forced to stand near the dessert station (the bar is kind of tucked into a corner and by the hallway that leads into the kitchen, so it is a heavy traffic area to try and stand) and, ONE HOUR after our reservation time and being incessantly nudged as people tried to claim their space, we were finally seated.

Once we were seated, the head hostess (who was very sweet and apologetic about our wait) offered to comp our cocktails. We happily took her offer, however, it was then obvious that front of house didn't communicate since someone immediately came over and gave us the schpeel on the cocktails, "you've seen these before," blah blah blah. We let her finish since we knew she'd soon find out about our situation. She then brought our cocktails, feeling a little embarrassed, and the "house freebies" started to come. You can tell that Carbone is trying to be like Il Mulino since the "house freebies" mirrored what Il Mulino offers: nugget of parmigiano-reggiano, focaccia (which Carbone refers to as "momma's bread"), and some prosciutto. All delicious, especially the "momma's bread," but, as the "house freebies" were dropped off, no explanation was provided and they were kind of thrown on our table. What happened to the 1950s, Rao's dining experience that the Torrisi boys' envisioned for Carbone? In order to get a sense of what the "house freebies" were, we had to yell to get the servers attention and then ask what was just dropped off at our table. It then took thirty minutes for the menus to be delivered and, before the server ran off, we got our food order in since we already decided what we wanted during our one hour wait for our table. We had to pass the time somehow, right? 

We ordered the aged beef carpaccio and the posillipo pan roast for our antipasti, both delicious and DEFINITELY "must try." For the macaroni, we went with the spicy rigatoni vodka and the tortellini al ragu. The spicy rigatoni was DELICIOUS and it has a kick. The tortellini had a great flavor profile with the ricotta filled center and meat sauce, but it would've been better if it was served hot and not luke warm/cold. Rather than trying to send off the flare gun to ask the kitchen to reheat the tortellini, we pressed onward. We ordered the bass oreganata, considering the note in the NY Times about the "house dried oregano," and the chicken scarpariello. Both were good, nothing to write home to mom about. We then topped our meal off with the carrot cake and black-out cake. I loved both the desserts but my partner, being the HUGE chocolate fan that he is, didn't think the black-out cake was decadent enough. Oh well, to each their own. We loved the house grappa which was a fig and fennel fusion.

Our check came and the comped drinks were not comped, but the sweet and apologetic hostess quickly corrected the situation. We were very surprised at our experience given what the Torrisi boys mentioned in the NY Times and NYMag articles about the vision they had for Carbone, especially with our experience being on a Wednesday night. Don't believe all of the marketing hype about walking in and getting the 1950s, Rao's or Il Mullino experience. Be ready to dine at the current NY hotspot with the usual sense of entitlement and your expectations will be on par with what you'll experience. We hope to check out Carbone in a year or so well after it has gone through its excitement phase. What happened to the days where the Torrisi boys were serving their cheap, GLORIOUSLY done tasting menu and running a sandwich shop in the same spot during the day......sigh

Incredible! My wife and I went there last night and had the best meal we've had in a long time. The T Bone steak is amazing!!!!! 
The Bow Tie pasta with lobster is one of a kind. Great atmosphere and staff!

Do you like to sing Volare & Mambo Italiano with your food? Old school meets new school at the latest Torrisi throwback themed incarnation. The hostess made a reservation for me late the same day- cool. Went when they opened at 5:30. The space has that private feeling and has that retro clubby feel. The proscuitto is cut in house and you see it upon entering.

The food comes and comes and comes starting with -
parmigiano cut from the circle
The proscuitto
Grandma bread
A bread basket

Ordered:
Diver scallops-2
Table prepared Ceasar w/anchovies
Ribs with cherry peppers
Creamed escarole

The diver scallops Sorrentina style were delish- as was everything. This is a gargantuan feast not a meal. They season the imported grissini in house. The standout was the creamed escarole- creamy, cheesey with pancetta- a very nventive dish. Dessert on the cart looked a tad pedestrian and the descriptions of the food did not match the sheer greatness of the dishes, otherwise loved the whole experience.  The service works the "throwback thing." Total bill- $98- no drinks, but the wine & beer lists looked good.

I was looking forward to dinner here so much, I figured there was no way it could live up to my expectations.  Thankfully I was wrong.
What a perfect night.  The ambiance is upscale Italian- you feel transported back to the 1950's with the tuxedoed waiters and the oversize menus.
Drinks are pricey ($17) and are modern takes on old classics.  The Manhattan was incredible. Margarita good but gone in a few sips.  
We started with a truffled beef carpaccio which was amazing.  Followed by a Caesar salad (they mix the dressing right at the table).  For entrees we did the famous veal marsala (yes, it was pricey but in my opinion, worth it).  Just the mushrooms alone that accompanied it were some of the best tasting food I've ever had.  My boyfriend enjoyed the lobster.  I was also obsessed with the spicy vodka rigatoni (mentioned in other yelp reviews).
But whatever you do, do NOT miss dessert.  The carrot cake was phenomenal!!! (and better than the black out cake for sure).
I can't wait to go back.  Perfect for entertaining out of town guests.  Torrisi might win out by just a hair, but in my opinion they both have some of the best food in Manhattan.

Hilarity does not ensue:
I'd like to start by pointing out that I never had any interest in writing reviews about my restaurant experiences, but after this encounter I'd like to share mine at Carbone. After a long wait for my reservation my group and I were very pleased to be there. To begin with I had great expectations for this restaurant, I had heard about this new place in town so naturally I had decided to bring my buddies (Group of 4) here with me, sadly our experience wasn't what we were expecting. The manager seated our group in the very back of the restaurant (near the kitchen). Beware of the service, they are to be treated with extreme caution (be very careful in listening the Captain's in the way they present the menu). We were planning to order three apps, but we were convinced to add our order with a cold antipasti ($45/pp). After this happened the waiter insisted that we also order pastas and told us that he'd "take care of us". We ended up having 4 courses of pastas (each $16 /17 per pasta x 4) , and on top of that he brought us meatballs that were never order! Originally we planned to share 2 entrees and rest assured, but the Captain urged us all that we order our own entrees.  Lobster Fra Diavolo ($87), he never once mentioned the price. My other friends ordered the Veal Parmesan (Make a note that the Veal is enough to feed 3 people), the T-Bone stk, Carabinero Shrimp Special( $64) for 4 grilled shrimp's only, and 3 Contornis ($ 12 each).  
By the secondi (After Pasta course) we were completely bloated, we thought the waiter would actually do his job and take care of us as customers with respect, rather  than bringing us a sea of food and unnecessarily taking advantage of us. I'm serious you can't trust these guys. Before the food had arrived I was looking the room and admiring the floor, pictures. They were all very beautiful, but out of the corner of my eye also noted that this pack was commanded by a tall fat guy who roams the rooms  walking and looking like he had a chip on his shoulders. We called him " Al Capone", later we learn that he was the owner (Jeff Z) who was a very petulant arrogant person and he treated us like a "prey". In the end we felt screwed over by this pack of wolves. 
Over all we were disappointed by all the impositions and suggestions. This is not any Italian restaurant, these guys will leave your wallet for dead. Let's say you order an espresso they will bring a bottle of Sambuca (free), beware this isn't a favor they're doing you. This action act of generosity is all but preparing you to get drunk for the 'Grand Finale'! The check. 
The food is gratifying, but not worth the pay. Marea is a hundred times better than this. The ambiance is weird, the music way to loud,  also did I mentioned that our bill ended up being near to 1 grand! For just 4 people!? Remember I warned you about the 'Grand Finale' (; Though we are young I don't think that would be an excuse for the service provided to use us to their own ends. I don't recommend this place unless you enjoy having your decisions made for you and to come to the realization that you have an excessive amount of food that you won't eat.
FYI - Carbone DOES accept credit cards now. Food was great!! Loved everything - tortellini with ragu, linguine vongole, all delish. Best Parmesan cheese ever!  Will definitely be back.

Wow!!

One of the most disappointing experiences ever.   Almost hilariously bad!

   Service was amateur.. as was the whole place.   Part of what makes a restaurant or bar great is a professional waiter or bartender.    This place is not professional in it's service, atmosphere or food.    The good reviews of this place boggle my mind.   You all must work there...  as it sounds like it from your reviews.

 Are Mauro T and I the only people that actually went there?    Or are we the only two that didn't grow up eating Kraft singles in the midwest?   You all have to be kidding to tell anyone that this is a good restaurant ..at any price....... nevertheless their exorbitant prices.  To say the food was average would be generous.   Noveau cuisine or old school italian???  I don't think they know ... either way it is was AWFUL!!!!    This place should be avoided at all costs.   They will be "doing you a favor" it they even bring your food to the table hot...  as we found out.

Sometimes you get what you pay for....  but surely not here.   

The decor is sad.    They claim they tried to make it  "old school"..  as some people actually mention in their reviews.   Instead they made the place look like a cheap Disney cartoon take off of an old italian place.   Cheesey.  

By the Way....   WHO ARE YOU? ...... your sign says Carbone on top of the old Rocco sign...    Your menu cover highlights Rocco Restaurant sign instead of your name .....

This is a comic book rip off of  good italian food & decor    

I don't wish anyone failure....  but I have to make an exception here. 

The  two "celebrity chef/restaurant owners"   should go back to what ever TV show or radio show they came from.

Known as one of the "hardest" restaurants to get into these days, Carbone really disappointed me with their service.  

As soon as we walked in we were greeted by the hostesses and our jackets were taken.  We arrived about 10 mins early so we waited at the bar.  The bar tender was definitely a character with a full beard and bow tie.  Everyone walking around with bow ties and jackets, it was almost a bit theatrical!  

After waiting, we were walked to our table (#15 - as written on our doggie bag).  When we were sitting all we got for the first 15 mins was water.  I had to ask to see a menu and for some bread as my boyfriend was a bit sick and we were both pretty hungry.  There's a fine line between horrible service and having a "dining experience" but I rarely have to ask for menu's or bread when I go out. 

Finally after another 10-15 mins. a small plate of "mama's bread" and a chunk of Parmesan cheese was given to us.  They were both okay.  The cheese wasn't that sharp and the bread was a bit dry but it was something to eat nonetheless. 

We didn't order any alcohol but got right into the menu.  Our waiter was on the older side and went on explaining the seafood dishes and the entrees.  I was kind of in the mood for seafood so I inquired about the "jumbo shrimp" which he told me was no longer available but that they had scallops instead.  He suggested I try the scampi.  I was excited and asked if I could get that as an entree size.  Now, I only mentioned he was older because I think this is where the misunderstanding happened.  He nodded and said "of course, yes!" and then we ordered our appetizers and the rest of our meal.

Now, the Caesar salad was made fresh but I actually found it to be a bit too garlic heavy.  The portion was not made for sharing but we split it anyway.  

Next came the disappointment of the night.  My shrimp scampi!  It was 3 shrimps sliced in half and served with half a lemon.  Now, I am not one to complain about small portions but $38 for 3 shrimp is a bit cray.  They were good but I wanted a bit more for nearly $40.  

My boyfriend wasn't feeling well so we skipped dessert and our waiter seemed mad at us for not getting dessert but we got the checked and were ready to head out.  I doubled check with our waiter that $38 was the appetizer portion and he replied "there's only one size"....oh?!  

Did I think it was worth $110?  Absolutely not.

Good Food and nice ambiance. The food is good, but beware specials like; $87.00 Lobster Fra D'Avlo and $67 Shrimp Special, along with $45 per person Antipasto. If they start getting real with their prices, they might end up being what they have "Widely Publicized" themselves as being an Old-School Downtown New York Italian Restaurant of The 1950's, instead of a super-expensive "Special Occasion Only" or 1%-ers restaurant. $50 Veal Parmigiano is not in-line with a 1950's NY Italian Restaurant, even filigreeing in Inflation, "It Just Doesn't Compute."

This place is as tasty as it is fun. And despite being arguably the hottest table in NY right now, I found the staff to be understated and friendly. I had such an enjoyable experience that on my way out I made reservations for the following week. 

Much has been written about the style of this new spot such that it need not be repeated. The restaurant, while large by Torrisi's standards, is actually quite small and that becomes an issue if your table is not quite ready (as was the case when we arrived). The bar is a semi circle that can barely fit 5 standing patrons. We were lucky that we arrived early, but I am fearful of how they intend to handle the overflow in the middle of their busiest times. Also, $17 for a Manhattan, albeit a great one, is approaching mid-town hotel prices.***

The freebies are very tasty and I was pleased that they brought extra cheese and garlic bread when asked. I was also glad to see their "wine adviser" was supportive of our choice of the least expensive bottle on the menu ~$40 which really opened up into a great flavor after 30 mins. 

People have begun to complain about the prices and at first blush many are quite high, but I think it is important to think of Carbone as a "family style" Italian restaurant  - even if they don't advertise themselves as such. Two of us split the baked clams (exceptional with a whimsical use of uni), spaghetti de mare, chicken scarpiello, meatballs (pushed on us and the low point of meal which is surprising since they are so good at parm), and chocolate blackout cake. I must note that the chicken was among the juiciest chickens I've had. With the wine and tip it was $220 total. That seems relatively reasonable and we walked out (barely) exceptionally full and very happy.

*** I note that I visited a week later and the same cocktail was now $14 dollars. They explained that they had gotten some flack for the high prices and while they thought it was worth it for a superior product, they wanted to be responsive to customer's complaints.

A terrific meal and experience; I highly recommend it.  In fact, I loved Carbone. After one meal, it s already one of my favorite places to eat in the city--although I doubt I will be back often considering the price tag, it is entirely worth it and excellent. 

The food: simply delicious.

-The freebies--the cheese, prosciutto, pickled veggies, and most importantly the garlic bread and grandma bread were great.  
-We had a half dozen oysters--fresh, spicy, and delicious.  
-The baked clams--interesting (uni on 3 of them) and flavorful.  
-The Caesar salad-- a highlight--the preparation was wonderful and then taste was even better--the best croutons I've had in my life.  
-The pink linguini vongole--perfectly prepared 
-the VEAL MARSALA--holy crap, what a piece of meat.  Perfectly cooked with a crazy-addictive sauce.  The best veal I've ever had. 
-Crispy broccoli rabe--the only disappointment of the meal--who wants tempura broccoli? We did not realize it was fried that way, I guess we should have asked. 
-The desserts looked great but we ran out of room. 

The drinks--I had two manhattans and my partner had a gimlet.  All three drinks were really prepared and delicious.  I don't mind the 15 dollar price tag considering the artistry in the drinks.  

The Service:  I loved the dinner jackets, the attention to detail and professionalism.  Yes, you do not get your menus right away.  I am certain that is on purpose.  You are meant to sit down and enjoy a drink before turning to the food.  Just be patient!   If there were kinks in the service noticed by previous reviewers, it must have been worked out because the service was impeccable.   Our table's captain was charming and knowledgeable and the bussers were quick as well.  The meal was well-paced and did not feel rushed.  

The space:  Really great as well. I love the attention to detail, the lighting (though the front room was a bit too bright), and the ambiance is just perfect.  Special occasion, important date, romance all the way--but also it would be a great spot to go with family.  

Overall: Sure, it is expensive.  But if you want to drop some money on a nice dinner, this is a great place to do it.  We got out for 240 with tip, which is super pricey, but not out-of-control.  We are going to come back for my lady's bday in September!

Left very dissapointed. I was anxious to try Carbone given my love for Torrisi, however, Carbone did not live up to the hype (particularly in the service department). 

Service: 
From all the reviews I've read, Carbone strives to place an emphasis on impeccable service, but this was actually the worst service I've experienced in awhile. We waited some time for our drinks, did not receive half of the "freebies" others have mentioned, and our waiter really pushed adding the meatballs to our order (we had already ordered 5 items which was WAY too much in itself and the meatballs were the low point of the meal). When we received the check, we noticed that a bottle of wine that we did not order was included on the bill. Obviously we asked them to remove this, which they did, but there was a bit of obvious whispering amongst the wait staff that I did not appreciate and only a quick "my apologies" was provided. Furthermore, upon exiting, the waiter came (embarrassingly) running after us saying that we had taken both copies of the receipt. We had not, and when we came back into the restaurant to re-swipe the card, another waiter picked up the signed receipt that our waiter had dropped on the way over to his station. The head waiter then proceeded to scold him in front of all the diners to ensure people have signed their receipts before "letting" them leave. Really?  

Food: Overall was overally-seasoned (VERY salty). Other than the appetizers, I would say the portions are family-size. Perhaps one pasta and one entree to share. 
 
-Carpaccio: Highlight of the meal (likely as it was the most unadulterated thing we ate). 
-Stracciatella w/ Crab Soup: Nothing special, would not advise ordering it
-Black Ties w/ Lobster: The pasta/ sauce was very pedestrian. I will say though, the lobster was incredibly fresh/ sweet and the amount provided here was appropriate to the price tag. 
-Meatballs: Carbone has nothing on Parm's meatballs---would have thought they would be the same?  
-Chicken Scarpiello: Chicken was incredibly tender but the tang/salt in the sauce was overpowering. I could only eat a few bites. 
-Creamed Escarole: Very indulgent dish--could be great if they removed about half of the salt. 

Atmosphere: 
Loved the atmosphere. The art is fantastic and the ambiance was very different here-trendified Little Italy.

What a great restaurant experience!!!  My husband and I went here tonight and I have a feeling this will be the highlight of our one-week babymoon in NYC.  We have access to really good and authentic Italian food in SF but this was an all-around fantastic experience.  Now I know why this is the hottest restaurant in NYC at the moment.

The throwback 1950s ambiance was a fun setting. The freebies (esp. the Grandma's bread, breadsticks, garlic bread, and powdered sugar crispies) were great as well as everything we ordered.  The Spicy Vodka Rigatoni (I don't think, or at least hope, there was much vodka in there!) had the perfect kick and perfect al dente-ness. That was the best Veal Marsala (rather veal period!) we have ever had. The veal literally melted in my mouth...definitely never had a cut of veal like that before.  The mushrooms on top and on the side of the dish set it even further apart. 

Definitely get the Carrot Cake with Ginger Ice Cream!  The Tiramisu was solid but not outstanding (surprising since it was even topped with nutella) unlike everything else we ordered.  I don't normally like nuts with my Carrot Cake (even if the cake is moist and delicious like this one) but this carrot cake did not have nuts in the cake, but toasted bits of nuts were on the outside...was perfect. 

The beer (Southhampton) my husband ordered was really good (snuck in a couple of refreshing sips...mmm) and the service was great!!  We left very, very happy and not overstuffed (since we didn't each order an appetizer, pasta and a meat like everyone else around us who took doggie bags home).  If you can get in, it's definitely worth trying!

Im really surprised that this place hasn't had a flood of reviews on yelp based on the traffic jam at the front door all night while we ate. Even though we had reservations for 7, we still waited a half hour to be seated and had to jam ourselves into the bar area that will hold about 6 people comfortably (standing) and had about 20 people there before we left.I loved Torrisi in its current form and i really liked Parm as well so i was sure that this would be yet another hit. I cant say that it lived up to my expectations. I really enjoyed all the freebies that they brought out to our table and the server who brought us most of our food was very professional,courteous and thoughtful. The head waiter,however, was less so. Although he joked around with the tables to the right and left of us, he seemed baffled by two gay guys out on a date. I think it would have helped if one of us had a vagina, but i digress........Because i had read the yelp reviews, i knew better than to be bullied into getting a shitload of food, and I'm glad because even with the "under-ordering" we still rolled out of there stuffed beyond the limit. And let me say the waiter captain really tried pushing us into ordering more food.The Nonnas bread was pretty amazing, as everyone has noted, and the cheese and other bread were pretty good too. I ordered two Collins from the bar , which were,in my opinion, pretty amazing , and worth the 15 they were charging. Less successful, was the vodka rigatoni. I don't know if was because I'm not a big fan of al dente pasta, the hype of the pasta, or i just didn't care for it but it wasn't very good. At all. The tortellini, on the other hand, was AMAZING. like, i might go back just for that. We also had the potatoes as a side, which came in a giant casserole dish and we couldn't finish them even though they were delicious. They were green,scalloped and came with a ton of olives, which normally wouldn't be my thing, but i really enjoyed them. Also, we ordered the meatballs, which weren't on the menu, and weren't offered by our table captain, but i had seen them on the table next to us and i asked for them.They were very tasty as well. We didn't have room for dessert, so we didn't get the grappa that a lot of people around us got for free, which is fine with me since i don't like grappa at all. For the price that we paid, i don't think i could justify going back. And i really wanted to be able to have that experience where 25 dollars for a plate of pasta would be okay, and i have been to places,like Haven, in Oakland, where i would pay 25 bucks for their pasta, but this place wasn't it. Sorry, Carbone, and good luck.

I've met and talked to Mario a few times, through his path to stardom. He's a good guy, and many don't realize Torrisi almost didn't open. He's a hard worker and created (albeit with some service issues) two stellar spots with Torrisi and Parm.

Now to Carbone. Just tried it, and brought two friends who were in from out of town. With no reservation, we still scored a table walking in. It was what I call the "tourist table", pinned against one side of the bar. As a native NY-er, I would usually object, but the bar was not crowded, so it was fine. And honestly there were no other tables.

My actual rating is 3.5, but that's not an option. The bus boys were great. The hostess was sweet, and the sommelier was "not too snobby"...which makes sense as no bottle is under $60 and we had two. The old school "circa il mulino" waiter was a bit too much. Short and curt, and displeasure written all over his face when we went against his food recommendations. Oh and this old schooler is not thrilled to answer questions either. Just preferring to race to a big tip, but putting very little effort forth.

The food: The "freebies" as other reviewers call them, are not free but rather incorporated into the hefty price tags, and intended to "belly fill you", so your less irritated by the small portions (especially the pastas). Regardless of their obvious tactics, the cheese, grandma bread, thin prosciutto, and garlic bread are excellent. I second and third other mentions of the meatballs...you'd think slam dunk due to parm, but carbones version while flavorful have too much gristle and off putting texture. The carpaccio was great, the simple sounding asparagus was great, and the tortellini (only 7 pieces on a small bread plate @ $25) left you wanting more but was delicious. The wine with the extra mark up for "the show" was still quite good.

FYI- Veal Marsala normal portion is $52...enough said.

This is unfortunately not a great restaurant for $350 for three...and note I think many restaurants are worth $350. It's a fun experience once in awhile that has good food, and will be sustained by special occasion diners and out of towners. With a few tweaks he could grab a lot more regulars, as today's hottest reservation will fizzle in due time.

This place is so over rated.  We had to wait 30 minutes for our table.  There is not a bar area so no place to wait.  I like the hostess suggestion to go to lupa for a drink. It was equally as busy.  So we finally got our table. The grandma bread is very good. We asked for some more. Took like 45 minutes to get some.  The Caesar salad was horrible. Its supposed to be prepared table side. Mine was prepared by the entrance of the restaurant with people walking and talking over it.  The leaves were old and did not like cheese on top.  The meatballs were pretty good.  I got spaghetti which was drenched oil.  Chocolate cake mediocre. The restaurant plays good music.  The service was TERRIBLE. The meal took 3 hours. The wait in between each course took forever. They were hoarding the grandma bread. I won't be going back.  Save your money and time and go somewhere good.

Best. Meal. Ever.

Carbone was insane. As in insanely good. The best Italian meal I've ever had. And I'm 100% Italian, so don't tell my Grandmothers. 

The service was impeccable. We got new plates and silverware for every course. They give you chunks of parm and proscuitto when you sit down. It wasn't family style but we kind of made it that way b/c there was 7 of us. Which reminds me, the tables are small, so big groups, anything larger than 5, are probably hard to fit without a lot of advance warning, like we did. My miracle worker friend got us in there on a Fri night. 

Everything we ordered was amazing. You can't go wrong. They start out the meal by giving you chunks of parmesan cheese, the garlic bread was so good, which sounds odd to write for a 5 star restaurant, but it was. The caesar, the meatballs, the vodka rigatoni, the polenta, oh my!  All better than the next. Go go go!

I have a very ambivalent feeling about my experience at Carbone.  I had read all the negative reviews about it being a simulation or inauthentic recreation of an old school Italian restaurant and I must say I agree with those reviews.  I'm sure our captain's name wasn't really enricco--probably bob or something and his line "here is our beautiful menu" was hard to swallow.  my wife even muttered "that's for me to decide".  I kept comparing everything to il Mulino and the food , service, and overall vibe just fall short of what is in my mind the standard for a real old school Italian restaurant.  If you ignore the simulated Disney-esce vibe and just judge the place on the food which was very good it still falls short of the beauty and creativity of del Posto.   So Carbone to me is between a rock and a hard place not as good as the best old school places it pays homage to and not as exciting or creative as the best modern Italian places in the city.

One of the tastiest and funnest meals of the year; party of 4, Sunday night dinner, back corner table; great decor and music, friendly, albeit slightly pushy staff causing us to over-order just a bit haha

Freebies were great; both the foccacia and bread basket super yummy

Our meal was as follows:
- beef carpaccio: amazing truffle oil and acidity
- seafood salad: refreshing, tasty, sizeable
- scallops: underwhelming
- skate with lemon butter sauce: hearty and delicious
- veal parm: generous portion, honestly a good value, fried basil was great touch
- spicy rigatoni: yum
- lobster pasta: beautifully poached tail with al dente squid ink pasta - could keep on eating this dish
- chocolate cake: so-so
- carrot cake: gorgeous presentation, great contrast with the ginger ice cream

I had a great time, and albeit pricey ($130 pp all-in with 1 cocktail and 1 bottle), thoroughly enjoyed myself, the food, and the atmosphere

I'll begin by saying the food was good, not great. The menu was overambitious, too much over-thinking on complexity of the dishes. Everything from service, to music just does not "click." Music was evidently supposed to set a scene- remind us of an era...but none of the selections were iconic. 

We arrived at 7:10 for a 7:15 reservation and ended up waiting for more than a half hour. The small bar was so crowded that we had to wait outside on the sidewalk. This is ironic because we had a call the day before letting us know that if we did not show up on time our credit card would be charged. So we can't be late without a fee, but Carbone can leave us out on the sidewalk for a half hour with no penalties? Rude.


The pork chop was huge, not possible for one human to eat. This is worthy of the Cheesecake Factory menu, not fine dining.  Everything we ordered was just okay. The noise level was so loud, conversation was a chore. Nothing relaxing, amazing or truly delicious at Carbone.

I have never commented on this site before ,but since I appreciate what Yelp is about,I thought I would chime in.
We were at Carbone on 5/9.I was excited to go,and now I am disapointed I went.It's simply about the food...the veal parm in particular.So greasy,and overloaded with garlic.I think my entire body is still reeking from garlic.How could they do this to  a veal chop?Our server was nice,and I liked his costume.They sat us right next to the front door behind the partition,so we did not really get a chance to see most of  the decor.All this hype...I do not get it.Lupa is right across the street,and that is the side of Thompson I will stay on from now on.So sorry it turned out this way.Too bad.

We had THE MOST amazing meal here for my wife's birthday. I'm pretty picky about this type of old-school Italian place, but Carbone was incredible. By far the best veal parmigiana I've ever tasted. So good. And the service was impeccable. Every single dish was stellar. Not an exaggeration. I hope we go back for MY birthday!

So disappointing. The dinner started off well--delicious bread, cheese, prosciutto. The Caesar salad was great!  Dinner was downhill from there. The pasta with clam sauce was all oil-- no clam flavor. My special of soft shell crabs at $38 was so soggy, oily, and inedible that I left three quarters of my plate uneaten. And what's worse, neither the waiter nor the manager ever came around to ask how was our dinner  I don't want to tell you our favorite places, but you're better off at Otto, Supper or Meatball Shop.  So sorry to have to write this review.

An incredibly hard table to get if you aren't on the Hollywood circuit. But let's cut to the chase. Appetizers are great and the Cesar salad was our favorite. If you didn't catch the Jersey Boys musical, come here. Because all they play is Franki Valli. Gets a bit upsetting and annoying. Pasta isn't fresh. Nor are the fishes or meat. Everyone is raving about how this neighborhood needed a legit Italian place. I call bs. Just a few blocks away is Babbo. And a few more blocks from that is Il Mulino. Babbo and Il Mulino are without a doubt much better than Carbone.

Four stars for the food, plus one for the excellent service and "show-like" atmosphere. 

Our party of four ordered the ceasar salad & seafood salad for apps, the spicy rigatone & linguine vongole for pastas, veal marsala & a side of fried rabe for main, and the carrot cake & grapefruit brulee for dessert, all done family style. This came out to ~80pp all in, including one round of cocktails.  Portions were generous, drinks were finely prepared, the food was fresh and savory, and the atmosphere exuded an old school charm with a twist of modern hipness. Only complaints for the night were that the veal was a tad over salted, and the rabe was pretty greasy (perhaps instead of naming it crispy rabe, fried rabe would allow diners know what they're getting themselves into. 

Having read a handful of reviews from various sources beforehand, I was a bit uncertain going into our dinner. Fifteen minutes into the meal, all the unease lifts. Our captain was warm and attentive, there was no extended wait time at the bar or at our table, no pressure to over order, the service was well paced, and the food delicious. For those more conscious of value, the tab was very reasonable for the amount of food they served. 

All in, Carbone doesn't fall far from it's restaurant roots. Whereas Torrisi's is an excellent date spot, Carbone offers a "rowdier" atmosphere perfect for a group of friends or family. Just remember to bring your appetites!

Hope you don't have to wait, cause there simply isn't any room to be standing inside. The bar is tiny, with room for like 2 people. And you're constantly in the way of the waiters.

The bf really liked their old fashioned with the huge ice cube. Heard good things about the whiskey sour.

We were seated in a corner, next to the speaker, so it was rather loud. The ambiance is pretty nice, has plush chairs - a good date spot. They bring out a few complimentary starters - this really good bread, a slice of proscuitto, a chunk of cheese.

We started off with the tableside preparation of caesar salad. This is definitely a personal portion, or at a stretch, for 2 people. I would pass on the seafood salad, not memorable at all. For pastas, we prefered the spicy rigatoni vodka to the linguini vongole, which was in a red sauce.

The veal marsala was really tender and qutie delicious, but wasn't prepared in the traditional breaded way. More of a grilled chop. I prefer their way! Avoid the broccoli rabe. It's way too oily and you can barely taste any semblence of healthiness.
We ended with a serving of carrot cake and grapefruit brulee. I found the cake pretty dry but really liked the ginger frosting. The grapefruit brulee was so-so.

Portions are sizeable. This definitely isn't a place where everybody orders for themselves. The four of us shared 2 appetizers, 2 pastas, 1 main, and 2 desserts, and we had more than a bit leftover.

And yes, it is a bit pricey.

Good food, but completely overpriced. Reservation accommodation was poor, we waited 40 minutes to be seated, wedged into their miniature bar, dodging the waiting staff as they cruised by. The ambiance was awful; the decor was nice, but the crowd was loud, however, and included multiple tables of thick-necked gumba meatheads singing along to every gangster-era pop song I've heard a hundred times before. NOT a special experience at all, actually slightly annoying.

Food, atmosphere, service - everything here is perfect. This is one of the most enjoyable meals I've had in recent memory.

After reading about this place constantly in every single magazine, food blog, etc., I went to OpenTable when they opened up reservations to sadly see that there were no openings at all for a month. I checked back a few weeks later, and the only weekend table I could find was a 5:30 on a Sunday about 3 weeks away. I jumped at the chance.

And it was well worth the wait and the early-bird special eating time.

I guess they are going for recreating that old school Italian restaurant vibe, and they've got it down perfectly (and this assertion is based on zero actual experience/knowledge, and solely on watching Scorsese-type gangster movies). It's dark in the dining room, and the waiters are all dressed old-school style, and they have great 50's/60's music playing, so you really do feel like you are in Goodfellas.

Already off to a good start from the fun atmosphere, they got off to a great start immediately by serving you with the delicious "Grandma Bread" right after you sit down. This bread is delicious, and goes even better with the complimentary Prosciutto they also give you. I'm already sold before I've even ordered anything.

Next, after they take your order they give you even more bread - a bread basket consisting of some Garlic Bread, a piece of regular bread, and some thin Breadsticks, which are great, and not throwaway like you would expect.

I knew I wouldn't be back any time soon since it's only going to get harder to get a reservation here as the hype is building continuously with all of the rave reviews, so I made it my mission to eat just about everything I would ever want:

- Tortellini Al Ragu ($25):
Excellent. Really delicious, and even though it was about $3 per bite, still very worth it.

- Fettuccine Con Funghi ($28)
This pasta was also a great choice. They split it into two portions, and is actually a decent amount of food for a place like this.

- Meatballs ($18)
These were some amazing meatballs. They give you three huge meatballs, which again was a very good portion. The meat was cooked pretty rare, so the balls were extremely soft and delicious. The sauce was amazing, and I'm enjoying it immensely now with every burp hours after the meal.

- Crispy Rabe ($12)
This was the one things I wasn't too big a fan of. After asking about the Creamy Escarole, our awesome server suggested we instead go for something lighter since it would be heavy with all of the other stuff we were getting, so we got this on his suggestion. This was the one thing he steered us wrong on - this was easily the heaviest thing we ate of all. It was basically just pure fried batter with a thin string of rabe in the middle. If I wasn't so full, or if I was at a carnival, I probably would've enjoyed this a lot more, but definitely not the right choice as a lighter option to go with the heavy meal.

- Veal Parmesan ($50)
Amazing. This is the must order when you come here. Seriously, the best veal parm I've had. The cheese and the sauce and the thinly pounded cutlet were all ridiculously good. Yes, $50 is a lot, but it is a very hearty piece they give you. It's actually probably enough for two people to share if you get some pastas like we did, in which case it's really not too expensive after all.

- Chocolate Cake ($12)
After such a huge meal, a lesser person would probably have busted and/or thrown up with this extremely rich, dense Brooklyn Blackout Cake. I came pretty close. But it was worth it. This was some of the best chocolate cake I've had.

- Carrot Cake with Ginger Ice Cream ($12)
Because, obviously, the two of us didn't already order an insane amount of food, we had to have another dessert. But I'm really glad we did - this was amazing. This is worth ordering just to see the cool presentation too: http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/carbone-new-york?select=a0rHVoNtO8TvfdEEmqcurQ#a0rHVoNtO8TvfdEEmqcurQ. Aside from that, it really was great, and the combination of the cake and the ginger ice cream was perfect.

In addition, they also give you some complimentary Fried Dough for dessert, which, if I ate more than the one piece I did, I really would've lost it. That one piece was tasty, but I was beyond beyond full at that point.

Yes, this is a pricy meal, but it is well worth it. It's not like other fancy expensive places where you blow a ton of money and eat a couple bites of food - they give you some really decent portions here.

This place is a must try. Try to plan ahead for a table a few weeks out, which seem to be the only ones available still since this place is so hot right now (I saw Leslie Mann waiting for a table on my way out, and hear things about people like Jay-Z and Seinfeld stopping b

I couldn't have been more excited for our dinner reservation at Carbone last night, having been to both Parm and Torrisi Italian Reservations I was hyping up Carbone to my work colleagues as we were set for our dinner reservation for 7 people at 6:15pm.  We walked in a few minutes early, and due to the bar being very small part of our party asked to be seated.  As they were brought to the back they sat down and quickly realized the table could barely fit 5 people let alone 7!  When making the reservation (on the morning the first day available) at no point were we warned that the table would be tight.  We were extremely disappointed and when we told the staff, they said there was nothing they could do.  We had no choice but to leave and find another restaurant at 6pm on a Thursday night for 7 with no reservation.  The utter arrogance of this place to charge $50 for veal parm and claim to be striving for "fine dining", while thinking they can have people sitting on each other's laps is unfathomable to me.  Unfortunately, it will a long time (if ever) before I go back to one of their restaurants.

I would give Carbone 3.5 stars. I had a bad feeling when I got there and I was right. We had a 10:30pm reservation but didn't get seated until 11:15pm or so. Luckily there are plenty of bars around so we went somewhere else to wait.

The atmosphere is great and you will feel like you've slipped back in time. 

Besides the wait time the service was great. 

Anthony Bourdain and David Chang were actually eating there that night.

My favorites were the Dungeness crab straciatella and vongole. We were a little full by the time we got to our main course. The crispy broccoli rabe was not that great. We were stuffed but the lemon cheese cake was awesome for dessert! 

I'd go back again to check out their other dishes.
ate there again last night . Could not have been better service was excellent , and the food was FANTASTIC . Cant wait to go back.
Amazing meal! Great food..great staff....would go every time I travel to NYC!!!!

Food was very good but only giving 3 stars because it was ridiculously expensive.   Fun atmosphere, great service....but when that check comes.....it is  just old style Italian food......nothing worth the 40 and 50 dollar price tags....including the portions sizes which aren't family style.  Time and money would be much better spent at their other restaurant Torrisi.

Holy veal shanks. Ok. Dinner here was an Experience that was sublime at the time and left me rolling around in stuffed misery for hours afterwards (in a good way) (I think). 

If you're able to finagle a table in the back room of Carbone, that is 110% the way to go. The back room is relatively quiet, whereas the front room is simply crushed by all the people waiting for their table to open up. The room to the side, where the bathrooms are, is not that great either--all the table are unmoored in the middle of the room, and it's still fairly loud. So back room it is.

The waitstaff here is great about providing guidance when it comes to planning your meal. They're going to suggest how many dishes to order, and they may even go so far as to suggest WHICH dishes to order. Don't get mad. Go with it. The dishes really are meant for sharing, so you'll be strongly discouraged from ordering a starter, pasta, and entree for each person (not to mention your wallet would die). The portions aren't as big as the waiters let on, but they are very dense. What your stomach thinks it can eat at 7pm, it will be yearning to dislodge by 9pm, so be kind to yourself and eat less than you want.

Standout dishes included the seafood salad, the pasta vognole, and carrot cake. Buon appetito!
Love their veal shanks here. Comes right off the bone! So tender and delicious and the flavors were ridiculously good.

I've been here twice and really want to love this place but its just ok. Shockingly for a place this hot in the city right now the host stand is pleasant and professional and doesn't do the usual judging you vibe you get at in restaurants. It's a small space. The bar is smaller than most NY bathrooms which is saying a lot. The first time here I sat in the front room and while the people watching is sublime, its amazing how people who are waiting for tables end up standing over you given the dollhouse sized bar. This last time I sat in the back room and liked the vibe here much more. both times we were made to squeeze into tables that would give flat Stanley an issue in making it to the booth seat. 

Onto the food. Love the hunk of Parmesan cheese that is given to you as soon as you are seated. They then arrive with prosciutto, grandma's bread, garlic bread after you order all of which is a very nice touch. The chopped salad is solid. Fresh and has tomatoes, radicchio, chickpeas. Not memorable. Wish I would have ordered the Cesar -the prep looked great. Tried the crab Stracciatella which had a beautiful presentation and was very good. Split the spicy rigatoni vodka and the veal parm. The veal parm is memorable and definitely what I'd go back for. I like the idea of the rigatoni vodka but there were too many pepper flakes on it making it unnecessarily too spicy taking away from the pasta. Lastly had the tiramisu which has a splash of Nutella. Very good. 

The service. This is what I really struggle with. Your servers are captains  which makes it ominous to start. Not sure if they mean captains sopranos style or captains on all these doomed cruise ships. During my first dining experience my captain was overly pushy. He wasn't really into our ordering the veal parm and kept insisting we get meatballs with out rigatoni which seemed like an odd combination. In the end we were happy with the veal parm and confused why he would dissuade us from the buzzed about dish. We were also never shown the dessert tray which was a bummer. This last time the captain was barely there. He lost interest as there was a large group he was entertaining. We barely saw him. Had to wait 10 minutes to order and we were not told of specials though we heard him reciting them to other tables. We waited 10 more minutes after we stopped eating to get our dishes cleared. Our captain finally appeared conveniently before the check drop (Since someone else took our dessert order) to ask if we enjoyed the tiramisu. 

Overall, food and scene is what everyone is buzzing about. Service not so much.  Really hoping they improve on the service as that's what I left remembering.

The Torrisi/Carbone team continues to impress.  I give Carbone 4 stars, and the -0.5 stars is actually for the "rush-pace" of the overall dinner service; another -0.5 stars for the over-sweetness in some of the dishes.

For those who have been to it's sister restaurant, Torrisi, read below-
Carbone is what I ultimately consider the "grown-up" version of the familiar Torrisi.  (I really enjoyed my experience at Torrisi so I might be a little bias!)  Founded by the same partners (Mario Carbone and Rich Torrisi), the ambience the two restaurants are very alike.  I would describe it as an: Old Charming, Al-Capone Era-style Italian restaurant with a Modern American Edge.  (the place was remodel after the set of The Godfather's)  Its a very comfortable space with tasteful silverwares and staff uniforms designed by Zac Posen!  Occupants consist of a mainly middle-age crowd. The differences is that Torrisi have slightly younger servers and music choices.  And that Torrisi offers a prix-fixe menu; while Carbone offers everything a-la-carte.  Both places defines Italian-American cuisine with despicable classic flavors and modern style of execution.

We started our meal at 6:30pm and finish before 7:45pm; I felt this was very fast for a multiple course meal with cocktails.
Upon sitting, we were immediate brought a continuous amount of complimentary goodies!  1. parmesan nugget  (so good, fresh and mild flavor) 2.prosuitto 3. grandma's bread.  Our cocktail arrived fairly quickly after, I ordered the Whiskey Sour which is made with grapefruit juice and the bf ordered the Old Fashioned which is made with Apple Brandy. And to be honest, both cocktails were unfortunately on the sweeter side compare to the traditional ways.  Not my fave.

Appetizer:
1. Baked Clams: littleneck clams made 3 ways.  1) Traditional Oregana, 2)Casino-Style with roasted red pepper and diced bacon and a layer of thin lardo 3) Fantasia-style with chopped ginger and a layer of sweet uni on top.  #3 was my favorite for its preservation of the seafood flavor of the clam.
2. Octopus Pizzaiola, 20hrs slowed roasted.  Served warm with a sweet glazed,tomato sauce, pepper and fried garlic.  The octopus was soft, eaten with the fried garlic gave a really nice texture. But the sweet glaze with the sweet tomato sauce really bugged me..its just excessively sweet, which i think takes away from the natural umami flavor of the octopus.

In between our appetizer course and pasta course; our server brought us a bread basket with a variation of bread and a small dish of spicy-pickled carrots and cauliflowers in olive oil.  This was a bit inconsistent for me because I think the basket was actually brought to us late.  We already started our appetizer and felt almost interrupted.  Regardless, the spicy-pickled vege was really good and appetizing to snack on; while I didn't care too much for the bread at this point into the meal.

Pasta Course:
Angel hair AOP (aglio, olio e peperocino) - delicious.  And i dont even like angel hair!  the BF picked this one because he have a thing for thin noodle..but wow, the angel hair was perfectly cooked without an additional minute (not mushy at all).  The peperocino gave the noodle a bit of heat; which is always so interesting to me when pasta is spicy! My first experience with Torrisi's tobasco pasta had never found another quiet the same, until now.  The beauty of this dish: fresh pasta, clean flavor, simply classic.

Carni Course:
Veal Marsala, boned-in veal chop chargrilled. - yum! (im eating the leftover as I am writing this review, its even better today!)  this dish was actually ordered by mistake, I really wanted the Veal Parmesan, but its okay because this dish actually quiet good!  I am not a big fan of meat that is braised for a long time; when I first saw the dish I was a bit turned off because it just looks like a chop roasted for a long time with really soft meat. But the veal meat actually has a bite without compromising any tenderness.  The accompanied hen-of-the-wood mushrooms were super yummy, crunchy and airy.

Desert- we passed since we were so full.  I think the other tables around us received complimentary fried pastry and desert liquor.  For some reason we weren't offer this.. maybe because we didn't "order" any desert?  Would have been a nice gesture...

The above menu for 2 people was very filling.  We were stuffed at the end of the meal and had the pack more than half of the veal chop to-go.   I think part of the reason why we got so full so quickly has to do with the timing of the courses. I didn't think we have a single moment to digest our course before the next one arrived. Because of this I felt I wasn't able to savor the meal as much as I wanted, and felt that we were being rushed through the experience.

I love Italian food - and i think Carbone definitely delivers what classic Italian-American is all about.  Classic flavor, happy portion and some modern elements. Will be back!

The food is fantastic! The razor clams were particularly amazing, especially since I am not always a fan.  The sommelier and waiter were incredibly helpful.  The hostess -meh.  She bait and switched us a bit. She said a table would be ready after we told her would come back another time because we didn't want to wait 30 minutes. Well, needless to say-- we waited 35 minutes.  Luckily, the food was really yummy and I don't think it had anything to do with our growling stomachs.

Another gem of a restaurant by the Torrisi team.  Although Torrisi is still my favorite, Carbone made me feel like I stepped into a classic mob movie.  The old school Italian music was a hit.  I took my father here for his father's day gift and he loved it.  Although I must say it was a little overpriced on some items especially on wines by the glass.  I don't think the two bread baskets were necessary so beware don't fill up on the bread.  The food was delicious.  We each had the chopped salad and we split the veal parm and the spicy rigatoni vodka.  The veal was huge so don't hesitate to share it.  Veal Parm was one of the best I have ever had.  Also the Carrot Cake for dessert is a must.   I will be back.  Thanks Torrisi team for continuing to make the Manhattan dinning experience truly genuine.

We went there for our third meal at Carbone over the weekend and sorry to say but had a terrible experience.  Don't get me wrong - the food was fantastic, as always.  However the service was simply shameful, especially our Captain/waiter who served in the front room (when you first walk in).  I get that Carbone's service is meant to be a bit laid back and "old school."  The waiters are meant to have a certain look and demeanor...  However, that doesn't excuse this horrible waiter who was completely negligent the entire evening.  We did not get some of the "freebies" that are supposed to come with the meal like the limoncello and sweet crispy dessert chips at the end.  He couldn't be bothered...  The table next to us had the same experience.  This would never happen at a Danny Meyer place.  Any good restaurant knows that service is a huge part of the dining experience; and no matter how good the food is, it gave me pause to ever return.  What a shame - considering how hard the kitchen works to turn out delicious food.

This was one of the better Italian meals that I have ever had.  For everybody who thinks Carbone is overpriced this is entirely worth the money.

For starters the old school feel of the place with the Godfather floors and then cheesy music is great.  I especially enjoyed the captains in the vintage burgundy tuxedos with the thick Italian accents.  The wine selection was great too and the sommelier was really helpful picking out the right wine.

As far as the food, it was amazing.  The freebies at the beginning of the meal were a nice touch and I really enjoyed the foccacia bread.  We started with the baked clams which were done in 3 different ways and it was definitely a unique dish.  The scampi was phenomenal and the best thing that I had.  The garlic and oil broth the langoustines were prepared in was very tasty.  The next dish was a caesar salad that was really cool how it was made tableside and may have been the best caesar salad I ever had.  The crotuns were so soft and perfect and the cheese added the right spices.  As far as the main dish we had the veal parm with a side of meatballs which also was perfect.  The veal parm may have been $50 but it could feed 3 people it was so big.  The meatballs were really good and had a strong hint of sausage that added to the taste.

Overall Carbone exceeded my expectations from eating at previous places by the same team and I will definitely go back.

A letdown, too much upsell pressure, better places everywhere

After reading some newspaper reviews I had high expectations..but it was a letdown.
Noisy room, waiter really pushed extra food on us that we didn't need.  Especially the non menu items that we never knew the costs until it came.
Pasta portions were too small
Veal Parm, which got a lot of press was way over seasoned and had a weird breading on it that was not really appealling.  The veal itself was good.
At the end we were way too stuffed to order dessert and that was some cue for the waiter to push us out the door.  For 4 people we dropped $700 with tip and they didn't even offer up a cookie or anything...just here is the check...time to go!

The more I think about my experience at Carbone...the more I realize just how subtly good the entire evening was.  I went in looking for this "song and dance" kind of presentation but it turns out...it was everything but that.  The staff was attentive but not intrusive and the food was simple but yet at the same time...full of flavor.  

It was a great evening all around and I am looking forward to going back...I hope you have a chance to visit as well.

Nice setting, good service, underwhelming food and way too steep price summarizes the experience. It certainly does well at being what it's intended to be - an old-school Italian restaurant from the 50s - service is good and proper, music is nice, and the design is appropriate. However, the food is definately lacking, especially given the prices. It's probably average Little Italy fare - which is surprising given the proprietors. And contrary to most information we got, we thought portions were actually rather small if you order to share. Scampi alla scampi were good, but not great. Octopus was too little octopus and too charred. The house chopped salad (for $17) was excellent. For pasta, the linguine vongole were outright bad, the tortellini al ragu were good but not special and the fettucine con funghi were actually pretty good. But overall, not pasta you'd come back for. On mains, we went for the lamb and the veal parmesan - the lamb was one I could have made myself with chewy meat and no special taste. The veal parmesan was good. The wine list is extensive and we were recommended a very good and not too pricey bottle. Overall, I'd say there's no reason to go unless you want to be transported into the 50s for a lot of money and mediocre food.

Carbone is really a magical place. After dining there last night, it has landed a place on my list of favorites in NYC. Everything about the experience was incredible from start to finish. The style and vibe reminds me a lot of Il Mulino in that it's that Old Worl Italian atmosphere with unbelievable food and of course the high prices to go match. The music was an eclectic mix of classics from the 50's, Sinatra, the Rat pack, etc. The waiters are wearing Red tuxedos ala Joe Pesci in My Cousin Vinny. At 5:30, there wasn't an empty table in sight. By 7:30, there was hoards of people with no reservations surrounding the bar gazing at each full table like a pack of hyenas as they waited for their turn to eat.

They serve you complimentary parmigiano cheese nuggets the second your butt hits the chair. Immediate gratification. Next, your incredibly professional and friendly "captain" will hand you gigantic oversized menus, literally. Be careful not to slap the person sitting next to you with it. Following that are tomato focaccia and some wonderful imported prosciutto. The waiter comes back to give you a run down of the whimsical menu, explaining the specials of the day and recommedations for his personal favorites. Then comes the official bread basket containing insanely great garlic bread, crusty Italian bread, and breadsticks with vegetable giardiniera soaked in spicy olive oil. With all the freebies, again very Il Mulino like. There are differences though- the waiters aren't from Italy and there isn't a laundry list of off the menu specials. Also, the music here does blare relatively loud, which I personally love since it adds spirit, liveliness, charm, and nostalgia to the experience. All the diners around me seemed to be singing and humming along as each throwback hit started to play. As I soaked in my surroundings- the sounds, the smells, the free tastes, I was brought back to my Italian childhood. Although I was in a fine dining restaurant, the whole feel was like I was back in my grandparents house. . For that alone, the experience was so priceless.

Carbone is a more refined take on the Old World Italian cuisine, so it's certainly not your classic red sauce joint in Little Italy. Special things are happening with the food here and talented chefs are doing new twists on the classics. You will see familiar things like rigatoni ala vodka and veal parmigiana but of course, they are elevating it to a new level. Both in execution and price.

Speaking of prices, be aware that you will pay dearly for your dinner here. It is a jewelry store as my grandfather used to say. Even from viewing the online menu, prices have risen a few bucks and surely will continue to rise. $25 tuna carpaccio, $38 scampi appetizer, $88 lobster dishes, a fat porterhouse for two, etc. etc. You get the idea. How do they get away with charging such extravagant prices? Because the food is amazing, familiar, yet daring and refreshing. But everyone around me didn't seem to mind the pricetag. Every table was ordering "soup to nuts"- several appetizers, followed by pastas, and huge main courses with ala carte sides, and of course a selection from the old school dessert cart. The moral of the story is to Bring the checkbook. Order as much as possible. Get fat, live life, sit back and enjoy as you're swept back to a prior time when life was much simpler.

Now onto what I actually ate. Everything sounds terrific, and the menu is stacked so narrowing down choices is daunting. My wonderful waiter Jason helped me out and after confiding in him, I got the following:

Tuna carpaccio with diced eggplant ($25)- Yes, incredibly expensive for an appetizer. Still, about the same as you'd pay at Esca but twice the portion. 6 thick slices of the freshest, purest, ruby red tuna are sitting in a garlicy olive oil and topped with diced eggplant that adds some extra texture. Absolutely wonderful light starter, which is needed as you are most certainly eating heavier as the meal progresses.

Lobster mezzaluna- You can't go to an Italian restaurant and not get pasta. All of the 7 choices were tempting, and of course I wanted to try the signature rigatoni ala vodka. But, the pics I've seen of this dish prompted me to order it. 5 large half moon black squid ink ravioli were stuffed chock full of lobster and shrimp, topped with more small chunks of lobster in a buttery yet light seafood laden sauce. It was so awesome. The flavors sang. . It was Italian in every way, yet something I'd never get to eat growing up in my Italian household. It had everything you want and more- perfect al dente, stuffed full of seafood, and that sauce ohhhhh the sauce. By that time I had no more bread to sop up the juices, so I was left trying to scooop up whatever I could with my fork. Not a dish you're going to find in your local trattoria thats for sure. This was a heavy "midcourse" but totally worth ordering. Impressive stuff.

To be continued....

I don't like reviewers who give bad reviews before giving a restaurant a chance, but I think I've earned this rant. My cousin and her family were visiting over the Easter holiday this past year. We had reservations at Carbone and were really looking forward to sampling the menu behind the glowing NY Times review. When we arrived for our 7:30pm reservation (with a 7yr old) we were told there was no reservation to be found. Apparently we had booked at another restaurant called Carbone... odd. Okay, they said they would comp us a car service to their way less formal lunch establishment, Parm. We went, were disappointed and especially ticked off when the driver asked for payment. THEY LIED-- the car was not comped, all they did was CALL the car. I can order an UBER or pay for a taxi myself. This was principal. Okay whatever, we forget about Carbone for a while. My cousin was back in NY this past week, so a month before her solo visit this time, I made reservations at Carbone. We really wanted to try the food! 9:30 was the only available time. Really? A month in advance and that's all we could get? I took it anyway and requested the back room after reading the reviews of other yelpers on how the front gets crowded fast and that the layout is cramped. No problem-- I was told we'd be seated in the back. So, we show up last night at 9:30 and wait... and wait... and then I remember to make sure the hostess knows we want to sit in the back. The front is no place I'd like to experience a meal of this quality-- it's not at all comfortable or welcoming. The woman informs me that "Oh sorry, there's nothing in the back" I explained how I had asked a month in advance for the back and if there was any note of it. Oh there was a note, but she couldn't seat us in the back. I asked if all the diners in the back had requested the room and was told no. UGHHH. Her attitude was rude, unwelcoming, and cold. I called Il Mulino ASAP and walked down Thompson to eat there (the food is beyond). Carbone, it is no secret, has tried to model itself after the wonderful special occasion Italian restaurants that reigned supreme in the mid 20th Century-- they've unfortunately failed to capture the charm and warmth that establishments like Il Mulino and Babbo deliver consistently. I no longer care to try the food, what I saw looked lovely-- but not even close to what you'll get at the other fine dining spots throughout NYC. Carbone, you've disappointed me for the last time.

3.5 stars. 4 stars for food, minus a half star for service. Had a reservation for 9pm. Came early and still didn't get seated until after 930. A couple who came much later than us got seated before us in the back at the table the hostess said was ours. We ended up in the front room, which was fine, but irritating since we knew our true table was in the back in the quieter area. And we had come before the other couple. 

No one came to give us our menus for a good 10-15 minutes despite servers walking back and forth in front of us seeing us twiddling our thumbs. Finally we received our menus about 15 minutes after sitting, and that wasn't until I asked someone myself. Trying to overlook the poor service, we proceeded to order. 

We started with the meatballs and uni special. Both were wonderful. We split the spaghetti de mer which was excellent! I was stuffed by then, but we had the veal Parmesan to go, so I had to buckle down. I could barely eat any because I was so full, but the little I did have was good. Not outstanding, as it lacked a little seasoning, but overall everything was prepared well and portions were generous. We had enough veal left over to bring home, and they included a nice brioche bun which I used to make a veal egg sandwich for breakfast this morning. They didn't rush us like others have written. The initial waiting was a huge downfall for my experience, but the food almost made up for it.

Easily the best time I've ever had at dinner! Went with my boyfriend this past Friday and we're still talking about it. Service was incredible, food was incredible. Atmosphere made everything even better. We'd initially had reservations for the July 4th weekend, but when we got there they told us the a/c was broken and we could either stay, or if we left they'd get us another reservation for the next weekend. We chose to come back when the a/c was back on and I'm so glad we did, because we ended up there for 3+ hours and had the best time. Ordered a ridiculous amount of food, but ate it all bc how could we not, it tasted so good! Especially the caesar salad- I'd heard it was good and couldn't imagine how a caesar could really be anything special but it was. Definitely order it! The spicy rigatoni was also really good, as were the raw bar items. Carrot cake and cheese cake were both delicious, and the cocktails were really well-made.
I could go on and on but really- just go here. You'll have a great time.

Love the old-school Italian feel.  The first thing I saw when I walked in was the dessert cart with a selection of desserts - one of those carts that a waiter pushes around to showcase the goodies.  The carrot cake looked amazing - there were actual carrots placed on top of the cake as decoration.  I ordered the fettuccini with mushroom.  The pasta was fresh and perfectly al dente; however, the mushroom sauce was a little bit too salty for my taste.  My friend ordered the tortellini with fresh riccota in a ragu sauce.  The riccota tasted amazing and I highly recommend that dish.  The prices were a little bit expensive (about $25 for a pasta dish and $50 for the veal parmesean; wine about $15 a glass), but considering how attentive the service was (the waiter came by every 15 minutes or so to check on us but he was pleasant and not intrusive), and that every diner gets a free taste of parmesean, prosciutto and bread, and the fancy decor, the experience was worth the price.  I would definitely come back!

3.5 stars. This place is awesome if you want to spot celebrities. We came on a Monday night at 9:30pm for dinner (it's freaking difficult to get a reservation). At the table next to us sat Nas and Q-Tip. A few tables down, we spotted Russell Westbrook. My suspicion is that celebrities frequent this place often, regardless of the day of the week.

Anyway, onto the food! We ordered the chopped salad to share, veal parmesan, rigatoni w/ spicy vodka sauce, and a side order of mushrooms. The food is incredibly rich -- the mushrooms were drenched in butter. The food is good, but the prices aren't cheap. However, the overall experience was still enjoyable.

-L.

this was the most appalling service that I have ever experienced at a restaurant. 
I turned up at 6.45 for a 7.15 reservation and was made to wait for over an hour and was constantly told 10 minutes. This was frustrating because not only was I being lied to, but they were seating other people before my table, on top of this one of my guests was an elderly man and it would have been nice for us to be a priority especially when we arrived early. 
Once we finally sat down we were still treated badly and served substandard food. As a person that frequents Michelin star restaurants as well as well as the trendy downtown spots I can tell you that Carbone is overrated and the crowd was tacky I will never go back again.

This is a complicated review to write, because Carbone is not really a straightforward restaurant.  It intentionally combines elements of both high and low culture, and fine and casual dining, which I'm sure can take people by surprise, even if they've read the reviews.  For the best chance of enjoying your meal at Carbone, in my opinion, you really have to be in the mood to roll along with the atmosphere and not think about the money.  (It's kind of like Disneyland that way, now that I think about it, but with much, much better food, of course.)

I had a really enjoyable evening there with my family.  We were seated right away (6:30 reservation on a Friday), the service was very attentive, the waiter and the wine lady both happily answered questions, turned down the music a smidge for my Dad, gave us very good wine recommendations, and was not at all pushy or rushy.  

There was way too much food.  Know that if you want to try the different courses, you're going to be bringing a lot home.  Everything tasted so good, though, that you'll want to keep trying different things.  

Everybody at the table had different things, and we all tasted everybody's and it was all really good.  If I had to pick one standout, it would be the tiramisu.  Yes, I know, that's supposed to come with a delicate sprinkle of cocoa on top, but the chocolate ganache that Carbone added lifted the dessert to a whole new level of decadence.

If you're really picky about food and restaurants, there are probably other places where you'd be happier.  But if you want something that's a little louder, a little more fun, a tad on the grotesque side (for the sheer amount of food), and across the board, over the top delicious, then I think you'll enjoy it.

My experience at Carbone was spectacular. I heard of the long wait, but I was seated 15 minutes after my reservation time, which isn't bad at all. 

My friend and I started our dinner with the house salad, which was yummy. I ended up getting the spicy rigatoni, which I loved. The pasta is so fresh and delicious! I highly recommend it! We then had their tiramisu to share. 

As for drinks, we had daiquiris, which were great and strong. We were also offered limoncello as digestifs and then champagne. My experience at Carbone was fantastic- from the food to the service from our server, hosts, and manager, Neil. I will definitely be back.

It was OK. I have had better Italian food at other restaurants.  Not sure what the hype is all about.  

The staff there were excellent though, nice, polite and very professional.  The venue was interesting as well, which is maybe why everyone is giving it such great reviews.

Apologies if anyone disagrees with me but these are just my thoughts.

Beware!!!!
