If you want to spend over $100 a person and get worse service than you would get at McDonald's, then this is the place.  No matter the price point, a restaurant is supposed to make you feel welcome. However, at Carbone they make you feel as though they are doing you a favor by taking your money.

On to the food.  It's good, not great.  It is definitely not worth it (setting aside service, decor, etc.).    

Even after recent forays to Il Mulino (I downgraded them by a star), I would still recommend Il Mulino over Carbone  (hell, I would recommend almost any Italian restaurant over Carbone).  The food is better, the prices more reasonable (I never though I would say that about Il Mulino), and the service nicer.

i am not sure what happened but i am going to give it another shot.
i expected this place to knock me off my feet.  It may have been the high expectations that put it at a three star for me, but all I can say is everything so was salty (outside of having a reservation and still having to wait a half hour) 
i kind of want to give it two stars, but i like parm so much i feel like it must have been a fluke one time bad happening.
i got my reservation over two weeks in advance and was really looking forward to an amazing dinner with my girlfriend.  as it stands now, to me it is incredibly overpriced and just hyped up right now.  
I expected the highest quality of taste.  the only dish i liked, and we ordered a lot, was the pasta and clams.  I sipped water between a bite of everything because it was so spiced or salty that i could not take it 
the experience prompted me to start writing yelp reviews actually

Spectacular and classic NYC ambiance. The energy is great and the way tables are set up you immediately want to start talking to everyone around you. Maybe even sharing! 

The food is brilliant. 

I did order the lamb which was cut behind me by 3 servers. None of them seemed to notice it was ALL fat. Really, ALL fat. For a $48 entree, they should have taken this back. Instead they served it. I sent it back. At that time the waiter admitted he knew it was all fat. They cooked up a simple pasta for us and removed the lamb entree but did not comp the simple pasta. That was a bit odd as I now sat while my table finished their entire meal before mine came out. I believe they did their best, but for such a classy place they could have provided a bit more of a unique way to make me leave wanting to recommend the restaurant. 

I'll go back and try it out again and do recommend. just make sure your meat is cooked and the quality you expect.
"Excellent food and lively atmosphere. Loud and fun 60/70's music. Impeccable service. Beware of the MAFIA-SIZED portions, that can easily serve 2, even 3."

I did have a nice night out here, but I most likely will not be returning. Like many other reviewers have noted, the expectations were pretty high and did not meet the hype. I was expecting spectacular italian food, and I have had some of the best Italian food there is. Honestly, the food was pretty lackluster for such high prices... it wasn't bad, just not great. The bread they serve as a complimentary starter was ok, but to me the sign of a great restaurant is WARM bread. It was surprising to have room tempature bread at such a high end restaurant. I will mention that when we first arrived at the restaurant, we were very skeptical at first as it is located on a more quiet street, and is very deceiving from the outside. It looked dead & kind of gross walking up to the place. But once you walk in the doors, the ambience & vibe is A++. I felt like I was in a contemporary meets classic fabulous restaurant in Italy with the perfect amount of throwback and modern day swank. The music was great, the decor was great, and it was the perfect amount of loud/lively without being chaotic... which I LOVE. It did feel slightly pretentious, which always make me feel uncomfortable. We did not have a reservation, and they were basically fully booked but they told us to grab a drink at the bar and they would try to pull something together. The three of us waited at the bar for about 15 minutes, which was fine but it wasn't really a bar it was more like a little stand with no seating or stools. Very strange but kind of cool. The service was great! Our waiter & bartender were extremely friendly and informed about everything on the menu. We were all jonesing for some good carby pasta so we each ordered a pasta dish and skipped any veggies or protein, being that we were so sick of veggies & protein (cali girl problems). One person ordered the Spicy Rigatoni Vodka ($26), another ordered the Lobster Mezzaluna ($34), and I ordered the Tortellini al Ragu ($29) these are relatively steep prices for pasta dishes, especially for the portions. I was still hungry afterwards, and was not impressed with the flavor. I've had better homemade pasta in the village for $9 dollars that knocked my socks off and actually left me satisfied and full. I also tried the other pastas my party ordered and the Mezzaluna, was too fishy for Lobster, and the lobster definitely did not shine. It was just lacking any popping flavor. The Rigatoni was too spicy, and the pasta was a little overcooked and the sauce was bleh. As for my Tortellini dish, I wasn't a fan of the Sheep's Milk ricotta, the texture didn't do it for me. The Ragu was bland, and to have a stellar Italian Restaurant you have to have EXCEPTIONAL GRAVY, I want vibrant savory red sauce made with real imported San Marzano tomatoes and the perfect infusion of garlic & basil. I mean, I've had better sauce at commercial Italian restaurants. The pasta itself was pretty good, but I really have had better. I mean, it was a fun time... but the food is the most important thing to me and it just wasn't happening. Very overrated and overpriced for what you get. Don't regret the experience, as it fulfilled my curiosity... but just not my hunger.

don't get me wrong, mr fishy loves the idea of this restaurant. it's a throwback to my childhood italian meals at the fancy place in our local town. the atmosphere is great, the waiters are superfriendly, the bartender an all around good guy... but the food was a major disappointment. a small dish of pasta with a simple tomato sauce for $25? burnt broccoli for $15? (ok, shame on me for ordering something called charred broccoli). and pork ribs with as much fat as meat? the nyt gave this 3 stars, but i say the emperor's got no clothes.

Had a ridiculously good veal parmigiana here but the pastas were only "good but not great." All the servers are super old school, often very Italian, and very friendly. Don't be fooled by the cozy, Godfather spaghetti-and-meatballs ambiance: this place is insanely expensive.

Thankfully I have foodie friends that care about me. So when I got the invite to dinner at Carbone I almost did a cartwheel..almost;) Carbone is really hard to get into. The restaurant is tiny, but cozy, which is my preferred way of dining anyway. We went at it the Italian way..family style. There were copious amounts of wine along with copious amounts of food. Then our server came back with the dessert tray & homemade Limoncello! Yes Please... I'll take that wheel barrow now too.. how else am I going to get home. Ciao Gratsi  "Maria's Don't Miss" The Veal Parmigiana

-Maria Taylor "What's New In New York"

First off, what is the deal with the pushy waiter getting us to over-order? We literally didnt touch the octopus or the roasted chicken dishes (ok i took a bite of each for yelp review, and both were meh~). The oyster from montauk tasted like what you smell some days out there (a hint of sewage) and the special santa barbara uni  dish was drowning in bread crumbs and had a bitter after taste, ie NOT fresh.  The linguini vongole had an intense flavor but was overly salty and the pasta limp.  Porterhouse for 2 was aight but for $150, it should be more flavorful (ie Perla or Costata).  It was an underwhelming dining experience -- def not worth a special trip and there are better quality for money italian restaurants within walking distance.

First off, thanks to everyone else who wrote a review -- I studied them before we went to Carbone last night so I knew what to expect (and what not to order). We had a nice evening -- seated on time, delicious dinner, very nice service. Thanks to the reviews we read, we knew we should order something from every course -- but because the serving size is gigantic, we split them. So we had a fresh chopped salad, an order of the vodka rigatoni and the veal parm  before we shared the carrot cake. The bill was still high, but not breathtaking. And while we were the only ones not walking out with a shopping bag of leftovers, we felt full, but not stuffed. I especially liked the veal parm (it was seriously huge, even for the two of us) and the carrot cake. The pasta was very good and the salad was, well, a salad. Loved the extras (any time someone wants to give me some nice parmigiano reggiano I'm a happy girl -- and the prosciutto was also good quality) and the ambiance. Be warned: this place is LOUD and probably the opposite of romantic. Still, we had fun and I'm a fan and I'd love to have another dinner there (probably for a birthday or anniversary because of the price).

The short explanation of my 3 star review: 2 stars for service; 5 stars for food (and since you can't give a 3.5 star rating, I landed on 3).  Snobby hostess, arrogant waiter, excellent food.

We made a reservation for 9:15pm but were in the area shopping around 7:30pm so stopped in to see if we might be seated earlier.  We were promptly instructed by the hostess that while it may seem silly, she must leave the tables open to honor all the reservations before ours.  So we found a wine bar in the area to kill an hour and 45 minutes.

We came back right at our reservation time, and discovered the hostess had clearly forgotten our existence because she informed us before we said a word, that they were completely full and would not be able to accommodate us.  We politely reminded her we had a 9:15 reservation and she said "oh yes, I'm sorry I forgot".  As she scanned her computer, she began to tell us that she would need to seat the 9:30, 9:45, and 10:00 reservation before us.  I reminded her for the third time we had a reservation at 9:15, to which she apologized once again and said there was a table ready for us.

The experience with the waiter was pretty much in line with the hostess (arrogant, not overly friendly, didn't seem genuine); however he did recommend some nice dishes and the food was very tasty.  We shared the caprese salad, spicy vodka pasta, and the chicken tetrazzini.  The pasta was amazing and the chicken was extremely tender and juicy.  We ended the evening with the chocolate cake topped with nutella ice cream, and coffee with a shot of sambuca.

I would recommend dining here once because the food is amazing, but prepare yourself for snobby service and then maybe the food will shine through.

My New Favorite

Until last night, Del Posto was my favorite restaurant; now Carbone is.  This was our overall best NYC dining experience.  My husband & I were warmly greeted by smiling hostesses.  Ricky, our waiter, was terrific.  The ambience is stunning: a cross between The Wolseley in London and the old Bravo Gianni, i.e., old world yet hip & cool.  
We were immediately served yummy parmesan cubes, Grandma's bread, and prosciutto.  We ordered linguini  vongole, meatballs (which are not on the menu,) spaghetti pomodoro, and creamed escarole.  All timeless traditions.  All perfectly done!  We also made friends with the folks at the next table who offered us a taste of their veal parmesan.  What a treat!  We topped it all off with a huge slice of luscious coconut canoli cake.
As perfect as the evening was, I do have one suggestion: add descriptions of the dishes to the menu.  We were surprised that the linguine vongole was fiery/spicy and this was not described on the menu or by the waiter. I was pleasantly surprised that the creamed escarole had prosciutto in it.  This, however, would not have been so pleasant if I was a vegetarian.

This must be the most disappointing meal every.  Not only do you need to make reservations months in advance and with credit card in place, but even with reservations, you still need to wait to be seated.  Perhaps that is how they lure and secure unsuspecting diners to eat their ridiculously overpriced meals.  Portions are miniscule and tasty, but definitely not worth its horrendous price tag.  I'm a big fan of noteworthy restaurants and rarely gasp at prices, but this place blew it out of the ball park when the entrees arrived.  Management could use some adjustment, as can most of the snooty staff who were practically throwing utensils across the table.  We were served undercooked meatballs and advised that it is safe to eat undercook pork (the texture of the meat was mooshy as in RAW grounded pork and beef)...  The only decent person in the restaurant was probably the sommelier, who was probably the most helpful and friendliest of all.  Not only was she knowledgeable, but also offered a spectacular selection of wine for our meal.

Came on a monday night with an 830 reservation for 4 people, wasn't seated until atleast 9. Waited by the bar (not much room to wait though)... but in the end it was worth it-- Caprese salad - amazing! - that cheese!... Veal Parm was incredible..Spicy Rigatoni & Spagetti Pomodoro were the way to go! Other guests had some seafood which they said was delicious.. will definitely go back!

Total Disappointment.

I love Torrisi and Parm, and was so excited about Carbone.  It was totally over-hyped.

The food was mediocre at best (the 'famous' veal parmesan) and inedible at its worst (the charred broccoli).  The service was lovely and the space is cute, but the experience made me wish I spent one third the amount on a dinner at Parm.  

$100 per person for uninspired food is a crime, especially coming from Mario Carbone and Rich Torrisi.

2 stars for warm, attentive service
-1 star for sneaky upselling
0 stars for food

cozy, fun ambiance, front room was abuzz with conversation and good energy, back room was abuzz with bethenny frankel. overall, atmosphere was pleasant.

this is where the warm feelings end. FOOD-wise, NOTHING was special enough to deserve the fanfare, in fact, the other Torrisi/Carbone collaborations FAR surpass Carbone in both value and taste. Do not understand the hype whatsoever, this is a case of the emperor having very bland, overpriced clothes.

VERY disappointed after rave reviews from various (now suspicious) sources, will not be returning unless someone I don't like very much is paying for it and I want to bask in schadenfreude while dreaming about eating a sammie at Parm. 

TOO EXPENSIVE FOR MEDIOCRITY. the end.

If this review had a title, it would be : La Piazza is better than Carbone. 


Carbone. The hottest restaurant in NYC right now. I held out going for a very long time and I can honestly say I was more excited for this dinner than I have been for pretty much any other dinner in new york since I moved here in 2008. I cant remember waiting this long or trying this hard to get a resso. I also really love PARM and so i expected Parm on steroids. 

I am not happy to report my feelings on this extremely sought after reservation. I wanted to love you Carbone. I wanted to feel the way I was told I was going to feel while dining here. I wanted to hop on the Carbone bandwagon and tell all my friends how amazing it was, how it was one of the best meals of my life. But i just did not feel that way, and I cannot lie to my fan base. I honestly don't even think I am being an obnoxious foodie and ridiculously tough critic. Maybe it was an off night but Carbone, I'm just not that into you.

Like a bad relationship, I will blame myself. I probably was too excited and it was way too over hyped. Had I gone in blindly on a Monday, I would feel differently.  

The grandma bread, prosciutto and cheese ball that are served before you order wine or any food are pretty on point. But honestly, they arent anything you cant get at a local italian joint. 

My friends staggered in somewhere between 5:45-6:30. We called about 10x to ask if we could push it back a little and they said there was no chance. They also explained they would need the table back by 8:15 pm. I knew they were going to rush us, but I didnt want to believe it-i wanted the full dining experience. Until about 715 pm, the restaurant was by no means filled. this angered me. 

We decided to order a bottle of red and I will say the wine was delicious. Light, crisp, we were off to a good start. They delivered us a bread basket and I was psyched. I had heard the garlic bread was worth "walking across the desert for". I probably wouldn't walk very far for this garlic bread, or any other part of the bread basket. 

Next came the oysters. Were they the best I ever had? Not even close. Ive had better dollar oysters at the Mermaid Inn. They were good. period. end of statement. 

The Cesar salad and tomato mozz were the next things that arrived. things were coming out fast at this point. The Cesar was made table side and it was the best part of the meal for me. Those croutons.  They created the perfect crouton and as a crouton lover, Id say these were the best I ever had. Perfectly dressed leaves of romaine and amazing croutons-yes Carbone Cesar salad, you rule. 

The tomato mozz was nothing special, the heirlooms are almost out of season, this was disappointing. SKIP. 

For our main course we ordered veal parm, spicy rigatoni ala vodka, ligunine with red clam sauce, burnt broccoli and meatballs. I am not even going to talk about the meatballs because all i could taste was sausage and I dont like sausage, they weren't hot enough, these were a TOTAL let down. 

The rigatoni was delicious. It really was, but our waiter should have recommended we (5 girls) get more because we each got maybe 6 noodles. 

They also did not offer to shred cheese onto our pasta and I saw them offering other tables. like wtf, i love shredded parm. Our waiter was average at best. Rookie move forgetting the shredded cheese bro. 

The veal parm was  MEH. like it was. and im sorry, for 50 dollars, i was expecting a party in my mouth. 

The linguine with red clam sauce was pretty good. I have nothing else to say. I got 7 strands of linguine and a clam, yay? EDIT: this was really good, not pretty good. my best friend brett just called and told me I better change this because it was in her top 5 linguine with clams.

The broccoli was good, I can make better burnt broccoli. it needed more garlic, less vinegar. 

The chocolate cake dessert was good, it was chocolate cake. it was whatever. I was severly underwhelmed at this point. 

Michael Strahan was sitting next to us, that was cool. He was getting the red carpet treatment i was yearning for. 

If i go back, I would only get the Cesar and the Rigatoni from this order. 

Food-6.6
Service-5
Ambiance-6 on a Monday 

Carbone over all let me down. I feel like I went on a first date and both of us just know its not going to work.

Don't believe the hype - Snap
I am a huge fan of Torrisi Italian Specialties. Carbone is riding the HYPE wave. 
It's overpriced for mediocre food at best. The bread that everyone raves about fell short. The oysters were meh. The $30 sea urchin was overpowered by breadcrumbs.(Labeled as "Uni" on our  bill. LOL). Entree we ordered was the $85 "whole" fish of the day which was a branzino. They brought out a 5+ lb branzino for me to inspect and all I got was a butterflied -1 lb fillet. No way was that the same fish for sure! $85 I expected truffles/foie gras with it but all we got was a simple grill fish with a lemon. See picture below. LOL.
Pasta? Nothing special. I had better for half the price.

Service was poor. Drink/wine menu finally arrived 10 minutes later. Table next to us sat down before us and didn't get theirs for 20 minutes. Service just did not stand out throughout the night. Waitstaff needs training to be on this caliber.
For all the hype and the Torrisi name I wanted to LOVE this restaurant. At the end of the day I felt as I am a tourist and gotten ripped off by the mediocre food and service.
I'll stick to torrisi italian specialties for now.

I am a lifelong New Yorker who has no problem paying for a fine meal, but my experience at Carbone left me feeling downright violated. Atmosphere was okay, service was nice....but when you are serving 'house' cabernet for $28/glass, don't you think it would be nice to let your customers know?? Same with the fish 'special' - the highest priced item on the menu is around $50 (already ridiculous), so we expected it to be in the same range, especially since our waiter didn't mention anything. We only discovered when we got the bill that it was $85 - for a piece of mediocre fish!! I had the $30 pasta pomodoro, which was basically a bowl of oil and garlic, very poor. I am sad because this could have been a decent dining experience, but the insanely overpriced and extremely mediocre menu completely ruined it. There are way too many places to eat in this city with much better food for less than half the price. Carbone insulted me.

About 6 months ago I had the best veal parm of my life here.  The Caesar, made table-side was divine.  The waiter was eccentric and delightful.  The place was packed and loud and fun.  Can't wait to go back and have it all once more, Loved it!

It is expensive so be forewarned...

Why are so many people so mad about getting reservations here?  Are we here to talk about food or reservations?  The food here is freaking great.  One of the best Italian meals I've had in NYC all time.  And I've eaten at almost all the best.  The waiter was old school funny sharp Italian.  Works perfectly in the restaurant.  It really is just a more modern version of the red white table cloth Italian you grew up with in your neighborhood except all the food is better. 

The caprese salad with late summer tomatoes, pesto sauce and warm fresh made mozzarella was fantastic.  Get it while you can. 

Baked clam trio appetizer.  Fantastic.  They had 3 different type of preparations.  My two favorite were the one with uni and the saltier version with pancetta.  But all were delicious. 

Scallop crudo was good but nothing worth going out of your way for.  

Meatballs with red sauce.  These baseball sized meatballs were tender.  There were big chunks of fatty meat and coupled with amazing bright fresh gravy.  This was some of the best sauce I've had in a while.  

Spicy rigatoni vodka (chef likes it pink - we like it pink).  Al dente not too spicy but a nice kick.  Perfect combination with the meatballs.

Linguine with clams.  An updated version of the old classic and they nailed it.  Great salinity from the clams with a delicious rich white wine butter type sauce.

Veal parm.  Fantastic.  Would not expect nothing less than the guys with a restaurant named parm.  Same great cheese and same amazing red sauce.  Everybody at the table agreed it was one of the best veal parms we ever ate and wonder why we don't eat veal parm more.

Chicken scapirello on the bone with sausage and peppers.  This was just ok.  The sauce was delicious but I wasn't so impressed with their choice of the sweet sausage.  There were only 3 pieces of chicken - pretty expensive dish. 

It's impossible to get a reservation here but you should keep on trying.  This is real updated classics for the 21st century.

Overrated.  Pastas were 5 star.  Entrees 2-3 star.  Main problem with this combo?  The bill which was incredibly high, especially because we didn't order wine.  Desserts were mixed. Definitely going to become an expense-account only type of place, which will keep out the cool crowd.  In 6 months I predict this place is only filled by business men in suits on corporate amexes.  Everyone else can find better or equally as good italian without the reservation hassle or bill.  If you do go, order the meatballs most definitely.  Highlight of the meal and best I've had (we shared as an app).

The food and service here are excellent.  I went for lunch the other day (I hear it's hard to get a dinner reservation) and had the minestrone soup (overpriced for what you get, but good), the spicy linguini (yum), and the meatballs (the most delicious things ever).  After all of that, I got a cappuccino and the carrot cake (WAY too big).

The servers were excellent.  This ridiculous woman sitting next to me (who was obviously from the UES, rich, and had several rounds of cosmetic surgery) was super rude to the waiters - but they brushed it off and treated her very well regardless.  I would have accidentally dropped a meatball on her wig, but bravo kind servers.  Bravo.

I really don't understand the hype at Carbone. I have been three times. The first time I went was during the first month they opened. I got deathly sick in the middle of the night from their dinner. I do believe it was either the clams or the pasta with the lobster. The second time I ate here I had to try the veal parm that everyone was raving about. I come from a very traditional italian family and i was soooo disappointed in Carbone's sauce. To me it tasted a bit sour. They needed to take the bitterness out of the tomato's.  The third time was this past Saturday evening. We had an 8:30 reso, sat at 9:45. Didn't offer a cocktail, dessert or anything in between. With the bill way over $1k for 4 people I was terribly annoyed. Oh and our  "old school" waiter that went missing for about 45 minutes in between. ...Michelin Star how? One word...Cahoots!!!

DELICIOUS. From the wine list to the maroon suit clad waitors, everything was top notch. I came here with my family for the grand finale of my birthday [week]. We had an antipasto appetizer with tuna tartare, prosciutto and figs, and a few others which were both AMAZING. Oh and I can't forget about the focaccia before the meal. For our entrees we had the branzino special and the lambchops, and it came with a side of the best broccoli I've ever tasted. Dessert was the lemon cheesecake and tiramisu. Everything was amazing, the waitor was knowledgeable and made great recommendations, and it had the perfect ambiance. Would love to come back :)
Old school dining at its best.  The steak entrée with the red wine sauce was the highlight of the night.  The porkchop was so tender, that no knife was required.  Can't wait to go back!
Came here for business - tasty food, and large portions, but not necessarily outstanding enough to justify the price.

Wow. I am so glad that I waited the months it took to get a reservation here. The food and the service added up to be one of the top dining experiences that I have had, not only in NYC - but anywhere. The space screams old New York, with the exposed brick, velvet banquets and the waitstaff uniforms. Our server was amusing and informative and helped customize our dining experience. We started out with the hunk of parmesan cheese and prosciutto waiting for us at the table when we walked in (our host had arrived before us), then ventured on to the bread basket and additional garlic bread! We had a bunch of drinks off the cocktail menu and an amazing bottle of chianti. Everyone was super helpful when helping to choose a wine or cocktail. We then moved on to the baked clams and table-side prepared caesar salad. The caesar salad, was the most amazing caesar salad I have ever tasted in my life - we cleaned the plate! Then came our spicy rigatoni vodka & meatballs. The pasta was out of this world. Everyone at the table raved about this dish and we were all fighting over the last serving. The meatballs were great as well. As a few other Yelpers had mentioned, they are a little on the sausage-y side, but that just made them more delicious! After that came the main courses - we had a veal parm and the lobster fra diavlo. Both were out of this world and the leftovers even tasted great the next day from the microwave! Now on to dessert, we had the lemon cheesecake and the chocolate cake.  I had my eye on the tiramisu, but everyone else wanted the chocolate cake. The lemon cheesecake was delicious! The chocolate cake was good, but I feel like the tiramisu with Nutella would have been better ;) We ordered a bunch of espresso and cappuccino and I was going to add on a limoncello, but our server said, "I was going to bring you some limoncello anyway so don't worry about that!". He then brought out a bottle of limoncello and a bottle of grappa and poured us each our choice. All in all, the space plus the service, the food and all of the on the house items made this a 5 star experience!

Seriously? I mean I loved the decor and the vibe but I came away a lot lighter in the wallet and actually with a very bad tummy ache. There was a point at the end of the meal that I literally felt like hurling. I'm not sure if maybe one of the clams I ate was bad or what but mommy did not feel  so good. I have been wanting to try this place for ever but it's near impossible  to get a reservation. I finally scored one, a month in advance. I showed up with my girlies for  a 9:45 on a Saturday night. Our table was not yet ready so we squeezed into the tiny bar area. Here's a little tip, don't bother. There is a bar in the back that comfortably fits about 2 people and everyone is there waiting for a table, crammed in like sardines,  while all the busboys and waiters rush pass trying not to spill their entire trays on you. I did get a very good Manhattan out of the deal though. We were seated about 15 minutes later. When the bread basket is the best part of a meal where the entree is $54, you're in trouble. The bread basket is really good and they give you a hunk of Parmesan and a few slices of prosciutto to start. For an appetizer we went with the assorted baked clams, these could have been the culprit. There were 3 different types, and they all tasted great. Next up was the spicy rigatoni vodka. They split this for us in the back and again, this was a great dish, if a little rich. I have read so much about the veal Parmesan so we felt like we needed to try it. It's a huge portion but there is no way in hell the price is justified. It wasn't that special and the exact same thing is available in any Italian restaurant  for about 1/4 the cost. Another huge problem I have with this place is the wine list. Come on, you can't find any bottles worthy that are under $100 to add to your list because the few that you do have on there are sub par. Also, there's not a glass of red under $18. We started with the Nusserhof Lagrein Alto Adige Riserva 2007 for $80 and it was perfectly fine bit when we wanted a bit more without spending $18 a glass we decided on the De Forville Langhe Nebbiollo and left 1/2 the bottle as it was so marginal. Now if you have read any of my reviews you know I have no problem dropping coin when it's worth it, heck we dropped A LOT more at Juni and I have no regrets, but when you feel like you're just kinda getting ripped, it leaves a bad taste in your mouth. Like I said, the decor, the vibe, the service all great. The food? I've had much better at any place in little Italy for a fraction of the cost. Don't waste your money.

The food was excellent, HOWEVER our waiter was rude and the service was bad. When we were seated we saw a dish at another table, when we asked to order the same dish, our waiter rudely told us "it was a dish only served to frequent guests", (it was our third time at Carbone). We asked the waiter to please "pace" our dinner, he was tossing our salad (first course) when our pastas arrived to the table. The dinner went from bad to worse. Horrible waiter, the worst I have ever had!

This place is SOOO GOOD!  I recently travelled to NYC and this was at the top of my list.  I love all the extras you get when dining there - chunk of parmesan, proscuitto, focaccia/bread basket, pickled veggies, and more!  Be forewarned - the portions are huge!  I would definitely recommend the veal parmesan and the charred broccoli - both to die for!  Be sure to check this place out, it's worth the wait!
Service was fantastic. Louie made the experience the absolutely wonderful Favorites: Spicy rigatoni, veal parm, pancetta, lemon cheesecake was a dream come true.

Would have given this place 5 stars, but given that we had reservations and still had to wait 30 mins for our table did not keep us very happy. Especially when they kept telling us 5 mins.. Other then that they the manager and our waiter was VERY nice and did end up giving us an order of the meatballs. I don't even care for meatballs very much but these are amazing. They do give complimentary bread which was pretty darn good. After reading reviews, I had to order the spicy rigatoni, and so glad we did (highly recommend). Probably the best pasta I've had, it's fairly simple but it was sooo good and the pasta was cooked perfectly, still a little hard not too soft. Also shared the veal parm and it was delicious. I have to say, this is probably one of the best italian food I've had.

Between this and Torrisi there is not a better meal you can get in New York. Went for my first time this past Saturday it was so good I had to send my parents there today. Had the meatballs to start which even though they were unbelievable my favorite is still cafe martorano. The rigatoni vodka was also really good but would like to try one of their stuffed pastas when I go back. The ribeye Dianne was insane and so was the cherry pepper ribs. Now I pride myself on deep down being a fat kid so for me not to be able to finish my food it says a lot about their portions. People who complain about the prices are morons being that the prices are online.

I travel to New York once a year to see friends, getaway from LA, and to shop... The most important reason? The food. I had the pleasure of eating at Carbone last Friday night and I'm still reeling from the experience. If you want to feel like Vito Corleone could walk in at any moment and order a glass of Chianti, Carbone is the place. The food was excellent, the wine list extensive. We were seated and served promptly. My favorite part? The perfect chunk of parmigiano reggiano I got as soon as I took my seat. Carbone is entirely unique, and I would fly back to NYC for the chance to go again.

OVER RATED!  the look, the smell the vibe.. excellent.. We sat 1 hour late- we made reservation over a month ago, called two weeks ago to make resi 30 min later.. they couldn't and informed us if we didn't show we would be charged 50 bucks a head. so.. after grabbing our first drink at the bar we waited and waited and waited.. then our 2nd drink.. waited and waited and waited.. they bought our drinks at the bar so they did the right thing there, but I noticed this was a standard practice.. everyone was waiting over an hour.. so once we sat-- service was horrible.. we ordered a bottle of wine..we had to serve our self -- do not order the lobster pasta.. lobster something luma- I had food poisoning this am and it def was because of that - veal chop was good. but overall I would never go back until they get there stuff in order.

Chose Carbone for a late (10:00) birthday dinner with my dad, having heard all the hype, instead of choosing a more tried-and-true parent-friendly location. While some of the food was quite good, we had a mixed experience overall. Loved the cheese served when you first sit down, and the caesar salad is phenomenal. The spicy rigatoni vodka was, as everyone says, amazing, but my dad's fettuccine with mushrooms was bland and he barely touched it. 

The restaurant was packed when we walked in at 10:00 on a Tuesday, warm, bustling, and had a great atmosphere, though it is crowded and incredibly loud (it was hard to talk even over the table). My biggest gripe however is that at midnight, they start playing rap music (mainly from the 2000s), which seemed like a real left turn from the atmosphere in the restaurant earlier. It ruined the mood and our conversation and we ended up not even getting a birthday dessert. So, I would NOT recommend this restaurant for a late dinner out with the parents. Probably a fine choice if dinner is earlier and you are out before 12, but be warned about the decibel level which prevents meaningful conversation.

Wine was excellent and was selected by the sommelier Thera who was a ray of light in an otherwise mixed bag of an evening.

Tried the daily oysters (raw), oxtail cavatelli, pork chop, and charred broccoli. First, i loved our server. I thought he was funny, charming, helpful, with just the right amount of attitude/teasing. i loved the old-school decor and the very fancy schmancy waiters. second, the food was flavorful but not too salty. and the broccoli was very interesting with the in-your-face citrusy flavor. all the freebies (parmigiano chunks, bread, prosciutto) were great and a wonderful warm-up/accompaniment to the meal. Wish I'd had room for dessert. for a place that feels very "old boys club," my work friend (female) and i didn't feel out of place and everyone was so nice to us. Wish we'd had bigger stomachs (or a bigger group) so i could've tasted more things.

I feel fortunate to have dined at Carbone twice now. The second meal came about in large part, because my husband finished off the leftover veal parm by himself after the first time. The prices are probably higher than many people think they should be, and some older folks who remember when classy red sauce joints were not a rare novelty may truly balk at what the Major Food Group guys are doing. But I personally think the place has a lot of charm, tasty Italian dishes, decent cocktails and a friendly, capable staff. If you go in a group, it's very easy to share dishes. And trust me that the veal parmesan is enough for three at least, or will reheat nicely the next day for lunch (on the complimentary roll they provide). I loved the baked clams and the oxtail with cavatelli, too. By-the-glass wine pricing being a bit high is really the only thing I'd gripe a little about.

Yes, it's expensive but you will  leave absolutely stuffed!

I ate here yesterday and could not move after the dinner because the portions are huge and there are many extras. 

The service was immediately impeccable. We were treated like royalty any time we turned out heads. Drinks are very pricey. Few beers offered were $11 each. Wine I think started from $18 a glass so in comparison cocktails for $16 were almost a steal. I got margarita and it was excellent.

Once we were seated a guy showed up with a giant bowl filled with inch-sized cubes of parmesan that was offered to us. Then the bread basket showed up with 3 different types of bread in plentiful amount. Then two amuse-bouche. Honestly before we even ordered food I was getting full on all the extras.

We were never rushed through the meal, in fact we were almost expected to take our time through all the various offerings. Did I mention the service was impeccable? 

For our food we ordered appetizer of sizzling pancetta to split and two pasta dishes, one of them, spicy vodka rigatone, was featured in TimeOut New York as one of top 10 dishes of 2013. 

Panchetta appetizer arrived with a lot of noise and steam from the sizzling and turned heads from the other tables. Great presentation and great food. Thickly cut pancetta again in plentiful amount, it was entrée-sized appetizer. I was getting more and more full but couldn't stop eating. Then pasta dishes arrived and mine was very al dente and spicy just enough to be enjoyable. I forced myself to finish every bite and it was worthy being top 10 dish.

Just as I was struggling to take a breath our captain showed up with the tray with 4 desserts and we ordered cheesecake which was also excellent and also huge. Big enough to share with 3-4 people.

I highly recommend the place, you will not leave hungry and it's worth your money.

My husband and I had early reservations Friday night.  We were excited to have some Italian after our Thanksgiving feast.
We were seated promptly and as quickly as we sat down, we were also offered a small piece of cheese.
We place orders for our cocktails.  I had a Mai Tai and my husband had a Manhattan.  My Mai Tai was great.  It was strong but it was properly balanced in taste.  My husband's Manhattan brought back so many memories for me.  I had not had a Manhattan in quite some time and I regret not ordering it as well.  
After reading reviews we settled on a game plan for our meal.  Being a party of two limits us unless we planned on carrying everything back in doggie bags but we figured we would listen to the specials and then alter some of our decisions.  Some staples we had to try were the baked clams and the spicy vodka rigatoni.  The rest we could move around.
We were told of the raw bar specials but honestly, our server could have stopped with uni.  The second we heard that, we knew that was what we were going to try.
Uni it was, the carpaccio, baked clams, spicy rigatoni, lobster fra diavlo and a side of charred broccoli and meatballs as per our server's suggestion.  We were also going to hit up the Cesar salad but he informed us that we probably won't need it.  Who are we to argue?
The uni was, by far, the largest uni I have ever seen.  One huge uni shell about 8" in diameter.  My husband peered inside and he was overjoyed.  Each time we stuck our fork in there, you got a deliciously plump sliver of uni but it was topped with what I think was breadcrumbs and some herbs.  It did not cover the taste of uni but accompanied it in a gentle way.  I wanted to say it made me think that this may be the never ending bowl of uni but alas, the last sliver was devoured.  After we finished the uni, I told my husband that the uni was a tough act to follow and I'm not sure if they could follow what that uni provided for us.  The bar was set high.
I also ordered a glass of the Nebbiolo and it was like wrapping me in cashmere on that chilly night.  Delicious.
We then got the baked clams.  Oregenata, casino style, and uni.  I made a beeline to the casino style as it had a slice of lardo glistening on top of it.  The clams were so meaty and good.  We tasted all of them and I got the last casino clam.
We then had the carpaccio.  We didn't see many reviews on the carpaccio but I took a chance.  Order it.  You won't regret it.  It was lightly drizzled with truffle oil.  It was like butter!  It melted in your mouth.  I tried to keep away so I can taste everything else but I kept on eating it.
Next was the rigatoni.  It was solid.  It had a silky spicy sauce coating the perfectly al dente rigatoni.  It was the first leftover to be consumed when we got home.  We got 3 large meatballs topped with fresh tomato sauce.  It was good but I only had a few bites because I still had the rest of the meal to think about.
We ordered the Roger champagne to drink with our lobster.  The lobster was shown to us and then shelled out.  I think that many places overcook their lobster but this was cooked perfectly.  To be fair, we were stuffed and we barely made a dent in the charred broccoli and the lobster but I HAD to give their desserts a glance.  We shared a blackout cake.  For a person who said they were stuffed, I managed to eat about 3/4 of it.  It was so moist!  We drank a limoncello to cap off our meal.
That day, our server teased us with a box of white truffles.  They had a special with the white truffles - some type of scrambled egg dish that sounded divine but it would have been too much food for us not to mention tack on a lot on our bill so we passed on it. The scent of the truffles was amazing. Next time!
Our server has prompt, no b.s., and had the nostalgic New York persona that you read about in the reviews.  The atmosphere is very cozy and it did make me think about the old school red sauce joints that you don't get to see that much of anymore.
It was clear that everyone was having a good time.  I engaged in a brief conversation about French Bulldogs with a lovely lady at the next table.
I have been to Torrisi and Parm and I haven't had a bad meal/time in any of their establishments.  Great places.
Decent food but for the price not worth it at all.  I love Torrisi and Parm so was disappointed.

What a great restaurant, that is what's like to go out to dinner instead of staying home. Of course not cheap but it really feels like u are out FOR dinner. All the details, from the moment u walk in the door and they take your jacket.
 I love our server Luis from Portugal, he was like being in a movie, always on point! 
He make sure we all have the food on time our drinks ready when we want them, not pushy but funny to everyone @ the table and we were all different people. I read in ny times that someone said he was embarrassed to be there, ny times gave this place 3 stars and only 4 places have 3 stars in nyc.

The Caesar salad and the clams combo are incredible! 
Do not miss this restaurant @ least once!! Bravo

Fabulous atmosphere and service. The veal parm was AMAZING!! The sizzling pancetta was a little too peppery for me but we very much enjoyed the tortellini Ragu and meatballs! Ended with the Nutella cake and it was so yummy! Great place!

Old school ROCKS !!
Great music selection from thurston harris to biggie small when midnight strikes is just pure awesomeness.  Sharp dressed staff & Excellent food & Service makes this gem my TOP 5 restaurant in N.Y !! and make sure to try ZZ Clam bar next door for the most amazing cocktails in N.Y.
RecommendZ:
1.Baked Clams
2.Scottish Langoustine Scampi 
3.Veal ParM.MMmmmmmmmmm

Even in a desolate future-scape where carbs and gluten are so out of fashion as to be nearly extinct, Carbone is so wildly good that it would still eek out a living doling out massive bowls of pasta.

As you have all heard, the Spicy Rigatoni Vodka here is one of the best pasta dishes in the city. Nicely al dente with great tooth covered with a subtle, almost velvety vodka sauce. The baked clams and lobster fra diavolo are also both superb.

While undeniably expensive, at very least the portions here are substantial and the service is impeccable. I prefer this place during lunch time, when it is a little more relaxed (if you can even use that word to describe one of the city's toniest Italian restos). This place isn't good because of the hype or the articles. This place is good because the management obsesses over every aspect of the dining experience. 

Think of me fondly when you order the Rigatoni.

Carbone is in some ways a throw back to the Italian restaurants of my childhood. Its in some ways an absolute, knock your socks off, peel your wig back joyride through the classics... The service we received from our server Marco was absolutely top notch. Hes a real charmer and his experience at other fine dining establishments shines through here. I will definitely be seeking his assistance next time Im at Carbone.
Some people would say "they arent afraid to charge" at Carbone... Nor should they be. The love and creativity that goes into each dish is apparent. My wife and I left after getting fairly well buzzed ad making friends with our neighbors to the left and right. The food really brings out the curious sides of the people that eat here. We watched most of the people ogling other patrons dishes as they were served. Its a lot more of an experience than I thought it would be. I dont know... Maybe Im dorking out too hard. 
Just go if you can. SOON.

Went at 6PM on a Saturday night. Carbone has all the ingredients of a great Italian restaurant, but they do NOT pull it off. I loved the decor, the 50's music and the menu- updated old school Italian. But the service was inconsistent, the drinks were small and the food was mixed. Pastas were great, fish just OK, and the waiter seemed to be pushing the most expensive items. Three times we had to ask for our drinks, after we waited too long for them. There were a number of lulls, when our food did not appear and our waiter disappeared. 
Still, I will give them one more chance...

I had a GREAT TIME here. 
Carbone's design is standout, in part because its been done before so many times. But this time its perfectly curated. The lighting is right. The layout is right. The tables all feel like good tables (with the exception of a few I noticed back by the bathroom....but when are those tables ever good?) Great places are places where you look around and you notice nothing in particular. You just feel like you want to become a regular.
My husband and I were seated it what would be considered the "back" aka not near the entrance. Our waiter was phenomenal. I ask questions quite a bit when out to dinner, but I didn't need to ask him anything. He essentially led us through our meal flawlessly. There was no frantic pace, everything went super smooth. 
The vibe here is uncanny. Dishes come out of the kitchen and everyone turns to see what they smell. Strangers lean towards the patrons next to them and say "Oh I got that I'm so excited it looks amazing." There were a lot of happy faces. People may as well have rubbed their hands together briskly and had their eyes bulge out cartoon style.
And its true, the food was fantastic from start to finish. The bread basket was sinful. The spicy rigatoni vodka dish was perfect, even as a shared plate. While veal isn't my thing I really enjoyed the classic preparation of veal parmigiana; also it was a huge portion....my husband and I shared and and still had some to take home. (which he ate like a half hour after it went into our fridge...thats a good sign, no?)
Weirdly, my least favorite part of the meal was dessert, maybe because it was a little too traditional for me. While I usually eat every visible particle of tiramisu, I left some of it on the plate at this meal. Same with the cheesecake...there was a lot of citrus going on. Anyway, the meal was a solid 8/10 even with the dessert being less than dreamy.
When the bill shows up its a little frightening, but thats New York isn't it? And if you can put a price tag on having x-factor, Carbone can charge whatever they like. I would happily spend hours on end hanging around until they turned out the lights and kicked me out.

Scored a 10:15 pm reservation on a weekday - late, yes - but we've tried getting in next month and they're already booked out.  So, late dinner it was.

A lot of people seem to be bothered by the prices here, but honestly, the whole experience and quality of the dishes is comparable to other restaurants in this price point.

We had:

- Bluefin tuna tartare appetizer
- Pork chop & peppers
- Spicy rigatoni (totally delicious & decadent)
- Veal parmesan
- Nutella tiramisu (ridiculously amazing)

The entree (pork chop & veal) portions were HUGE - we left with a to-go bag which almost never happens.  The pasta was a smaller portion but also not necessarily meant to be served as an entree.  Con: Took a long time to get our second drink.  I had to flag someone down and ask for one.

The ambiance kind of reminds me of Charlie Bird (but way more traditional) - trendy crowd, great/loud music and upbeat vibe.  Music changed from classic Motown to hip-hop after midnight.  Great service, we weren't rushed at all.

Really like this place.  Wish it wasn't so hard to get in now.  Will definitely be back.

Don't believe the hype!! The food is better at Carmines. I went with my husband and 2 sons last night, ages 13 and 17. One had pasta with meat sauce, and the other ordered pasta with vodka sauce. The portions were so small that I asked the waiter if they were 1/2 portions. He said they were full portions, so I had to order them both another portion. I had veal marsala, which was a fatty veal chop with an oily sauce. I ordered a side of broccoli, and the broccoli was sweet? We didn't eat it. My husband ordered the steak Dianne which was okay, but not worth coming back for. The side of mushrooms are just sauted mushrooms and onions like you'd make at home. Our waiter was old school, meaning he mostly ignored us. I ordered 2 slices of chocolate cake to go, and they gave us one. I am giving this place 1 star because the cake was good, otherwise it's not worth it at all. There are many good Italian restaurants in New York. This is not one of them. Dinner cost us $423.00, so I expect really good food for that much money, not mediocre over salted wanna be Italian!

I was at Carbone last night and was pleasantly surprised with the space, atmosphere and crowd. I thought it was hip, trendy, cool and a busy place for a sunday night (assume fri/sat is busier).  Atmosphere and crowd wise I give this place 4 stars.

We skipped appetizers and had first course and second course only. From the pastas we tried oxtail cavatelli and spicy rigatoni vodka. I loved the oxtail cavatelli, it was delicious but I thought it was very heavy and I barely touched my main course afterwards. The spicy rigatoni sauce we ordered to see what the hype was all about since so many people recommended it. I personally thought it was tasty, but I hate vodka sauce so I would not order again. If you like vodka sauce definitely try it. 

For main course, we had the whole branzino for two. They fillet it for you, but the skin stays on, which makes it a tad heavier. It was tasty,  but I was too full from the pasta dish to enjoy it. As a side order we had sautéed broccoli which was great. Food wise I think this place ranks at 3.5 stars.

Overall, I liked dining at this place. I liked the atmosphere and would likely go there again with a group next time. Food wise I thought the prices did not justify the taste.  For example, the branzino for two at $85 was overpriced for the quality. It does not come close to the Branzino for two dish from Esca which is priced at $72. I love splurging on great food but I did not think it was top notch.

The ambiance at Carbone is cute, sexy, chic, and classy. 

The service is top notch, and the sommelier's recommendations were right on the money. 

We ate the shrimp (see photos) and sizzling pancetta to start.  Afterwards we chowed down on the Mezzaluna Lobster and everything was fantastic, fresh, and tasty. 

No complaints, great staff, great service.  A little on the pricey side as 2 appetizers, 1 entree and a bottle of delicious red costs us about $300, but worth the experience and tastings.  

Our palates and stomachs were fully satisfied on all ends. :)

I had no idea what to expect.  I continued my mission to visit all of the NY Times Top 10 Restaurants of 2013, Carbone was next, and I was a bit concerned given some of the reviews.   We arrived for an early supper on a Sunday night and I was pleasantly surprised, if not overwhelmed.

It was like some mockery of an Italian American restaurant that Disney opened in Epcot Center.  If they decided to open "Italian-American Land", this would be its flagship restaurant.    But it really didn't matter since it was so good.   Worthy of a Top 10 spot?  Indeed.

Like the Disney "cast members" at their theme parks, the performance put on by the waiters is well-rehearsed.  Once you get over that, you realize that it's less theatrical and more superb customer service.  They didn't miss a beat any moment we were there and their corniness adds to the fun of the joint.  A joke here and there.  A little wink when you try to order more and they say, "I think that'll be good for you, sir".  Several jovial pats on the shoulder.  It's cheesy but entertaining.

We had mediocre expectations, but were blown away.   I rarely order caesars salad, but we both thought it was the best we've ever had.   The beef carpaccio is so impossibly thin that you scape it off the plate, it's hunk of fresh toppings pushing the limits of what can technically be called "carpaccio", but it was also superb.  Again, "the best I've ever had" came up in conversation.   We sounded like two tourists from Iowa that had never tried any of this before and the fact that we could be so fond of two simple and pedestrian dishes was confusing, surprising and mind-blowing.

We moved on to the tortellini with spicy ragu, which was delicious, accompanied by three awesome meatballs (which the waiters pretty much shame everyone into ordering, btw).  I decided to go "off plan" and avoid the much talked-about giant Veal Parm, opting for the lamb chops instead, which was a great choice.  It was the best lamb I've had in a long time, drizzled with olive oil and heaps of fresh mint leaves.  It came with a trio of delicious sauces, but it was a star on it's own.

The carrot cake was a nobel finish, but not the best we've had.  Bigger doesn't always mean better.   Although the on-the-house limoncello was a welcome treat.

On the wine side, you can mortgage your house if you want to, but there are many decent values by the bottle.   I asked for something under $100 and was recommended a $65 bottle, which was excellent.   With a by-the-glass list that starts at $15/glass, why even bother?

Who cares if you're eating on the Godfather set when the food is this good?

One word sums up this place, "whatever".  I wanted to check it out, the food was just okay and I'll probably never go back.  Had the octopus, linguine/clams, veal parm and carrot cake.  All were solid but nothing had me really wanting more.  No complaints about the service....they brought us the wrong pasta and we had to wait longer for our 2nd course but the waiter was very apologetic.  The prices are the prices so no surprise there but eventually you'll ask yourself, 50+ for veal parm?  I can get it cheaper and just as good at a ton of other places in Manhattan.  Adios Carbone.

Food I ordered was delicious, I mean very good.Colorado Lamb (I think CO, the waiter was unsure) was amazing, if you order it I recommend eating the fat off of the bone, seriously. Calamari salad to start was another star. One of the better seafood salad's I've ever had. One piece of calamari was slightly overcooked and rubbery but when I can single out that one piece it seems like more of an anomaly than anything. 

Dessery: a nutella tiramisu was decent. The soft biscotti like cookies they gave pre-dessert were better than the actual dessert. 

Also, I couldn't help but think of Joe Pesci in My Cousin Vinny everytime I looked at a waiter wearing this hideous red suit. They really have to reconsider that attire.

Overall: Food was good, service was decent but I'd rather Lupa which is literally on the same block.

The drinks were superb, worth every penny. We didn't come with plans to order an appetizer as we almost always order an appetizer and are then way too full for the entree, but the waiter sold us on the shrimp scampi, we caved. We had three pieces of shrimp scampi, super difficult to pull out of the shell, only got thin jagged strips, about 3 bites each (between my husband and I). My husband had the ribeye Diana, he loved it, said it was super juicy, had the potatoes as a side, delicious. I had the lobster mezzaluna, probably the most delicious thing we had all night, crab stuffed ravioli, topped with generously sized pieces of lobster, to die for. We then order the Nutella tiramisu, not really impressed, it was ok. We were completely surprised when we got the bill and found out the shrimp scampi was $51...completely disappointing...for 6 thin slivers of tasteless shrimp...not even my husbands huge steak cost that much, his ribeye was $43. I don't mind dishing out a nice penny for a good quality dish, but $51 for the shrimp scampi was extremely steep, it hurt...I loved the place, loved the drinks and my dish but I don't think I would come here again. I'd rather try out other restaurants in the meantime. Definitely come, experience it for yourself!

Favorite Restaurant in Manhattan. Any negative review you see on here is due to people complaining about the money - but trust me it is worth every penny. 

Purposely didn't eat all day to prepare for the below dinner, so here is a step by step guide to what to order. 

Before You Order Complimentary:
- Prosciutto (5/5)
- Cauliflower (4/5)

Appetizer:
-Octopus Pizzaiolo (5/5): By far the best Octopus I have ever ate. 
-Meatballs (5/5): Better than my grandmother's

Pasta:
-Spicy Rigatoni (5/5): Usually never would order something like penne vodka at a restaurant but the waiter recommended it and it was incredible. 

Sides:
-Squash Agrodolce (5/5): Extremely hard to describe, but it is served with mascarpone and ridiculous.

Main Course:
-Ribeye Diana (5/5): Cooked medium-rare smothered in rosemary out of the charcoal grill. 
-Zuppa di Pesce (5/5): Once again, best I ever ate and unlike any other zuppa di pesce I have ever tasted. If you like clams, muscles, and calamari - you need to order it.

Wine:
Sommelier recommended a great bottle of 'Comptche Vineyard Pinot Noir, Mendocino County CA' went great with the meal and was worth every dollar.

Had dinner here around when it opened.  Was disappointed with the quality of the food - especially given the prices.  The critics seemed to love this place and I was confused, so I have since tried to make a reservation multiple times unsuccessfully.  I wanted to try the food again and a close friend of mine also really wanted to dine here.  

However, the reservation process is truly unpleasant - it is not that it hard to get a reservation - it is the seemingly arbitrary way in which they assign reservations that bothers me.  

To make a reservation, you first have to get through to the Major Food Group.  I would say about 25% of the time that line is busy.  However, once you get through to the Major Food Group it then asks you to press 1 for Carbone and 2 for Torrisi.  About 95% of the time, after you press 1 you are told that the Carbone line is busy and that you should try Opentable or email for reservations.  If you check Opentable, they do not have any reservations available.  If you email, then a few days later you get an email back apologizing and saying that there are no reservations.  Now, for those 1 in 25 times that you actually get through, you are generally told to hold.  This can take up to 10 minutes.  After holding, you are told that the only times available are 530pm or 6pm.  The reservation line opens at 9am and I have gotten through to the reservationist as early as 9:02am and have always been told the same thing with respect to availability.  This simply cannot be the case.  The restaurant must be saving reservations either for American Express or for some restaurant brokers - or just for friends of the house.  

Anway, the reservation process is a joke.  If they wanted the process to be fair, they could open reservations online at 9am.  They could also hire another reservationist or they could establish a hold line where once you get through to Major Food Group, you no longer get disconnected.

As for the dining experience, I would say it is two, maybe three stars.  The veal parmesan is truly fantastic.  A huge piece of tender meat, with delicious sauce and lots of cheese.  It is expensive, but probably the only thing at the restaurant that is worth the price.  The baked clams were a trio - and each one was worse than the basic baked clams you would get a normal red sauce Italian restaurant.  The pastas were okay - they were not crave worthy and there are numerous restaurants in the city that serve better pasta.  I also had a fish dish and a side of vegetables that were unmemorable - in that I remember ordering and trying the dishes - but could not tell you what they were (even if I were looking at the menu).  I think the vegetable side was tempura fried.  

In the end, the dining experience was very similar to going to Il Mulino.  Only that the food at Il Mulino is much better and suprisingly, the food is also less expensive.  I do not understand why I keep trying to make a reservation here.  I think it is because I want to be proved wrong and I really want to enjoy this place.  Unfortunately, they make the process of getting a table here so unpleasant, that I will no longer try.

Once again, I scratch my head at the Yelping consensus. To give this place less than four stars while scores of lesser restaurants enjoy the same inflated rating for shit that isn't even worthy of half that praise is borderline criminal. But unfortunately getting foodie legislation passed is slow going, so I will attempt to right these wrongs one review at a time.

So here it goes... If you've ever eaten at Il Torrisi, than you pretty much know what you're in for, more awesome Italian. 

The highlights are easily the veal parm (best I've ever had) and this special raviolini that was so layered with flavors it took a good 3 minutes of chewing before I felt like I had truly tasted all it had to offer. Definitely one of the best pasta dishes I've ever had.

Also quite good was the wine and the garlic bread with fresh mozzarella.

On the mortal side of things, the stuffed clams and the langoustines.

The only flat out miss was the carrot cake. They should take it off the menu. Along with the napoleon cookies they serve complimentary. Neither are worth the calories. 

As for décor, I really love the vibe of this place, from the sign out front right down to the colorful, unique plates and blue walls.

And service is solid, knowledgeable, friendly and comfortable- with a touch of New York swagger, which I liked. As a result, the place feels like it's been around forever somehow. In a good way.

I ate here for the first time about 3 weeks ago.... I woke up from the fabulous food coma it induced just this morning.
 I would love to go into detail about what was so spectacular and why I was so blown away by my experience there, but the problem with that is that it was all amazing. 
 Our Sommelier, a gentleman named Nathan, was awesome! He quickly sussed out what we would like and didn't assume that I had a billion dollars to spend on wine. (I was grateful for that once the bill came)   
 In essence, they have taken old school "Italian-American" cuisine, including an overall vibe that make you think of The Godfather, and have managed to bring it to us in all it's past glory. 
  To quote the New York Times article that inspired me to try his place: 
 "Carbone is mining the best elements of homegrown American style of service and cuisine that flourished when men in ties and women in heels, woozy from a final shot of sambuca, wobbled to the sidewalk clutching doggy bags.
 We didn't know how good we had it. Carbone is here to remind us."

Love this place. Extremely expensive, and some might think the theatrics of it all are a bit much, but I eat it up. Most importantly though, the food and drink are incredible. Like many people I go with the caesar salad, the spicy rigatoni and the veal parm. Ordering just those three dishes for three people is plenty and actually won't be too horribly $$$. The cocktails are great, and so is the carrot cake. Come across a couple of misses with the chicken dish and one other item, but all in all makes for a great night.

Believe the hype. Carbone is amazing. They start you off with complimentary cheese, ham and bread which is a preview of what's ahead. I had the Veal Parmesan and it was delicious but the star was the Spicy Rigatoni Vodka. OMG. This pasta was amazing. It was perfect. The sauce had a silky smooth texture with a hint of spiciness that hits you in the back of the throat, but in a good way. This is a must order. I wanted to order the meatballs but they were sold out. Fortunately, I was seated next to two women who were kind enough to let me try one of their balls and it was awesome. The sauce was great and the balls were moist and perfect. Just how well made balls are supposed to taste. They're not on the menu but everyone knows to place an order. You will not be disappointed.

The service was great but the music was a tad too loud. I'm actually looking forward to trying the Veal Marsala, the Carpaccio and the Baked Clams. This place is on par with some of my all time favorite Italian restaurants in NYC which includes, Il Mulino, Campagnola, Scalinatella, Maialino, Don Peppe's, Elio's and Babbo. I will definitely recommend this place.

Carbone is awesome. 

I had my birthday dinner there last night and could not have been happier with my decision. The meatballs, spicy rigatoni, veal parm - all  an absolute ten. Besides the food hitting on all cylinders - the ambiance, service, music - you really feel like you're right out of a scene of Goodfellas. 

If you are looking for a spectacular experience (and to not be hungry for a few days after your meal) - look no further.

Having eaten at Parm and Torrisi I was curious about Carbone. It was recommended to me by a Restaurateur.  At 5:45 on a Tuesday it was already half full. They very smartly have a curtain to separate the front door with the dining room. The place is well run and coats we're checked immediately. Reminded me of Blue Hill. They bring you bread, cauliflower, ham and cheese right away. Both cocktails we ordered we're exceptionally good. The Mai Tai is all that it's cracked up to be. The Garlic bread is fantastic. On first inspection it looked oily however because they only use the bottom of the bread and toast it well so it's not. It's just delicious. 

We ordered the Calamari salad which is actually a Fruit de Mer with a little kick to it. Excellent, order it. The baked clams come several ways. We ordered the surprise. One was Oreganata which also has a kick to it (very yummy), another with Uni and the last with lardo. All left you wanting more. For mains we split the Chicken Scarpariello and Pork Chop with peppers. The chicken was perfectly cooked and the sausage they used had a mellower flavor than the classic hot sausage most make it with. Solid dish and well executed. The Pork chops we're tender and their version was well executed. Personally and my friend agreed we would have preferred a spicier version but nothing to complain about. 

Dessert I didn't eat. My friend did the carrott cake and seemed to enjoy it. They give you a couple of rainbow cookies. My friend asked if they could give them some to go for the kids and they we're happy to bring it. Classy touch. 

I like the room. The old school feeling of the place which used to be Rocco for many years works. We sat in the back which I prefer. Service is freindly and precise. The whole place runs like a restaurant should. I'm indifferent to the much talked about Brooklynese approach of the waiters and Tuxedo's. I get what they are doing and it makes sense for the location and feel of the place. Lots of Dean Martin/Sinatra at a sound level where you can hear each other. Tables are on the smallish side for the size of the plates they serve on. Portion size is good but not a traditional family style like Carmine's. Seating is comfortable. 

So the much talked about prices. After food, 4 glasses of wine, 2 cocktails, 1 desert and 2 espresso $325 with tax minus the tip. Be prepared to pay about $150 a head depending on what you drink. Drinks IMO are expensive for the West Village. Babbo right near here is less. Il Mulino is about the same depending on what you order. 

The place is a solid 4 star. Does it deserve a Michelin star? Probably but I'm not the one who decides. They definitely have something different, tasty and memorable. This is not a value place however and for what it is and the quality of the food they're on the expensive side hence the 4 stars instead of 5.  I can't put them in the same category of Le Bernardin, Marea or Daniel and those in my view are all 5 stars. The quality of the food is top notch but what they making with it are standard Italian dishes which I love but the price doesn't justify the cost. 

I'd love to see this place still here in 10 or 20 years I just don't know at the prices they are charging if that can happen.  People thought Il Mulino was nuts 30 years ago charging what they do and they are still around and booked. Time will tell if the guys over at Carbone can do the same. Strangely they don't take Discover card which I can't understand since the fees are less than AMEX. Recommended but bring your wallet and enjoy.

Was invited to Carbone for a friend's birthday. Restaurant is nicely decorated. We were seated with an incomplete party, which was nice and just ordered drinks while the rest of our party arrived.  We opted to order family style. For a party of 5 we ordered the The servers were very attentive throughout dinner and we did not feel rushed. 
We had the pancetta appetizer (could have done without it) , grilled octopus which was really tasty. Meatballs were tasty, completely rare in the middle so beware if you are not into that. We ordered two different pastas, including the penne vodka which was already split for us before it was served. We also had the Oxtail Cavateli which was pretty good. We ordered two entrees since there were 5 of us and we thought that was OK. Veal parmigiana was good and the Halibut but it was a very tiny portion for splitting. Side of Broccoli was good too. Our waiter had said the food was suffice but I think we all felt we needed another.
Desserts were very good, carrot cake and Tiramisu. 
On a side note as far the actual table setting, some of our plates were chipped and our table was annoyingly wobbly and although they tried fixing that, it didn't work.
I think it's worth trying Carbone, but I personally don't get the point of paying that price point for traditional italian that you can get at many restaurants across the city and Brooklyn. 
The Service was Top Notch!

Lets start by talking about the steak. THE STEAK. The Tomahawk Steak. Amazing.
I would't usually order steak, but the waiter (who fit in with the genre and theme of the restaurant perfectly) told us : 'Let me take care of you'. I mean, who doesn't love to hear that. 

Dozens of great things on the menu, what to choose, what to choose. Plus reservations are hard to come by so you try and make the most of it.
He recommended a salad starter, then the spicy rigatoni (helloooooo sooooo creamy), then the STEAK, with these delicious potatoes with garlic (potatoes louie). We ended the night with a Tiramisu cake slice-polished off with an espresso macchiato. We didn't want to leave and think about the amount of steak we had just consumed, but whatever - life goes on.

The food is great here. Yes, on the pricey side, but well worth it.

The vibe is spot on, it's not a huge place, but it lends to the 'authenticity'. Whats even better is that the waitstaff and hosts are friendly, accommodating and capable. HARD TO FIND in restaurants. There are well dressed men and women constantly overseeing tables, checking if you need anything without making you feel rushed.

The waiters do a good job of recommending dishes.

I think I might want to go every week. I still have to try the veal parm, ribeye Diana, and pasta pasta pasta.
My one constructive criticism (if I may): the tiramisu was loaded with a liquor flavor... almost too much. But the rest-LOVE.

Loved this place. Every detail attended to. Service a little brusque but the food was absolutely amazing. Love the decor as well. I do wish they had a bar-- but we had drinks at Lupo across the street which also seems like a great spot to check out. We really cannot wait to return to Carbone.

This is supposedly one of the best restaurants of 2013 and has one Michelin Star, but I don't see what the hype is all about. I got all their signature dishes and while the octopus was good, the rest were just barely good. Good but pricey = 3 stars.
Very noisy. Not good for intimate dates.

Shady rolled into Carbone for a highly anticipated meal. And Shady was not disappointed. Nice familia type place tucked in on Thompson Street opposite Lupa. Place is small and tables are tight, however it works in this setting. Starting with a glass of prosecco at the too- small bar, Shady launched into an epic meal. Starting with a nice tuna tartar, segueing into  the spicy rigatoni vodka-cooked al dente with a nice sprinkling of pepperoncini-it was delicious. Then the piece de resistance-The veal parm. Shady plans his last meal on earth to be a well prepared veal parm, and this here at Carbone might be THE one. It is huge, comes with the bone on the side and was absolutely all that it was said to be. Shadys' lucky dining companion went for the pork chop -huge chop with peppers-again delicious. Dessert was the carrot cake which is another Shady staple and it was, well is there another word  for delicious? A little lemoncello finished off this masterpiece and Shady waddled out with enough food leftover for at least another meal. All in, with a bottle and Shady's typically generous tip for excellent service is 200$ per person. Not cheap at all, but enough for two meals so look at it that way.A word of caution-expensive wine list. Shady cannot wait to go back and try few other things on the menu..and order a veal parm to go!
All the hype is worthy. Place is absolutely legitimate all around. Food, service, atmoshphere all 5 stars.. Loved it

The reservationist is the worst. I felt like Leslie Mann in "Knocked Up" -- you're just a doorman! Doorman! The decor reminds me of Minetta Tavern, as does the attitude of the staff, but the food is great. It's expensive, exclusive, delicious and everything you'd expect from a restaurant group who's never met any criticism from any reputable publication. I wish I could go more often than they allow.

The Torrisi/Zalaznick/Carbone trio have an incomparable knack of recreating tradition with just enough bold choices to push out the fourth wall of their newest spin on Italian home-grown specialties. Entering their heavily shaded bistro in Greenwich village, you will instantly notice that this isn't just another black-and-white tile floored variation on a jillion other Italo-American nightspots, but rather a passionate haven for delivering plate after plate of conversation-stopping variations on traditional dishes that make you want to take ALL your meals from this gem of a nightspot. The intimate wood and brick space is made cozier by the darkest of green walls - yet more approachable by 50's rock-n-roll music. While the Lobster Fra Diavolo and garlic drenched (almost french-toast) croutons in the Caesar salad will seal the deal, the veal parmesan will rewrite cooking history for years to come. The carefully chosen wine list offers large to moderately small producers from the usual producing regions of Italy, but also some strong and surprising representation from Sicily and beyond.

Average,  overpriced Italian food geared for out-of-towners.  The mushroom pasta was bland and oily, veal parmigiana was heavily breaded, salad was uninteresting.   

Service was spotty, I had a difficult time getting a waiter to bring cheese for my tasteless pasta.  The credit card machine wasn't working.  Meanwhile the sound system blasted out music from The Godfather.

There are lots of wonderful restaurants in NYC, don't bother with this one.

I came for a decadent weekday lunch (it's much easier to get reservations here for lunch than dinner). Between my friend and I, we had Montauk oysters, spicy rigatoni vodka, meatballs, veal parm, lemon cheesecake, and ended with espresso (which they offered to add sambuca to).

Everything, from the service to the food, was impeccable. I just wish it were more affordable so that I could dine here more often :(
