Sidenote: the entire time I was dining, I was trying to figure out why the guy at the next table looked so familiar. Turns out it was Mario Carbone. I can't believe I missed my golden opportunity to meet him!

I e-mailed this synopsis of our lunch experience a week ago to a friend who lives in Manhattan and had not yet eaten at Carbone.
"Carbone was wonderful--nice ambience, wonderful music selections,excellent service and extremely good food.  The food is not complicated, at least what we had was not, but it was very fresh, expertly prepared and full of flavor.  The lunch experience was top notch.  We could hear each other talk, a plus.  My kind of place.  Would definitely return."

Spring time in NYC and I finally made it here! It was a wonderful experience from wine choice to dessert. What wasn't good as we had steak clams antipasti & a wine selection that is world class.

Service was silent and anticipated...perfect.

italienska i NY varför inte?

I loved Carbone for what it is but you need to go in with the right expecations. This restaurant is absolutely packed. Reservations a month out are highly recommended. We had dinner very late on a Tuesday night and there wasn't an open table in the place.

The bread that comes out really is magnificent but try not to fill up on it! We shared the scampi alla scampi to start, delicate langoustines with garlic and Olive oil. We also had the pancetta. A huge chunk that is incredibly fragrant. Next we shared a farfalle with peas and greens and the shrimp in the diavolla sauce with a side of zucchini. All the food was very good with the best ingredients.

For dessert the carrot cake looked too good to resist. We devoured it! 

It was a wonderful meal. It's definitely a 'sceney' restaurant but that is part of the fun. A great place to go with friends or a group.

Very good red sauce Italian. Great old school atmosphere, including a waiter who couldn't have been cast better. 
Clams, spicy rigatoni, meatballs, pork chop--all very yummy. Garlic bread is insane. Cocktails where a highlight. My only complaint is that it all feels a little to hyped and inflated--especially the prices. I want a great red sauce Italian place to be more neighborhoody and accessible, not a hot reservation. The food is good enough to stand on its own without all the pretense.

Awesome!!!! The place is great.  The food, the music, people watching and overall dining experience is something you will have to try.  Make sure you have an expense account you will need it here!
We started with the salmon carpaccio and baked clams.  The sea urchin was delicious. We then had the spicy rigatoni  which was perfect, and the meatballs.  (I have had better meatballs but these were good) seemed to be a little sausage meat in them which was an interesting touch.
We then split the veal parm and the branzino both cooked perfectly.  
Save room for their desert and an after dinner drink from the rum cart.  A truly enjoyable experience.

Ask for Marco. Probably order the veal, the clams, and the rigatoni. Duck fat potatoes are optional, but, really, are only skipped by amateurs (and, perhaps, to maintain pristine summer physique). Perhaps you will be fortunate enough to sit the back. Don't f*** this up. Seriously.

Carbone is everything it's raved up to be. I was dubious before I went there but felt nothing but contentment after the end of dinner. 

The starter bread was very plain, literally tasted like pizza crust. You'll be very disappointed if you were to expect better. However,the complementary small starter sides of prosciutto and cauliflower were pretty good. The cauliflower was served in a very vinegary sauce that's good for dipping the bread in.

For our appetizers, we ordered the baked clams and Caesar salad. The Caesar salad was definitely as wonderful as everyone proclaimed it to be. The baked clams came in different favors that I can't recall now but they were good too, but nothing mind blowing. I still prefer the salad to the clams but they make a great appetizer pairing. 

We ordered the veal Parmesan and vodka rigatoni for main entrees. The veal Parmesan was like crack, so cheesy and decadent. Perfectly cooked and tender. It is the best veal Parmesan I've ever had, but then again, it's not like I have it often. The spicy kick to the vodka rigatoni was very addicting, and I loved the al dente texture. The entrees were very big and the server usually suggest to share it family style. We were a group of three and two entrees were plenty for us. 

So I had to recommend the carrot cake for dessert. It is a huge slice served with a side of ginger ice cream. The contrast between the ginger and cinnamon flavors of the cake was wonderful. I wouldn't say the cake is a must get but it is definitely not a weak dessert like many reviewers have stated. It is the best carrot I have had in my dining experience besides baking establishments like Junior's. 

I would definitely come back, and it's a rarity since not many fine dining places make it to my frequenting list because the meal is only good enough for a one time experience. Carbone is like the neighborhood higher end Italian joint that actually provides a personable experience, paired with spectacular food.

Luckily this was a business dinner so I didn't mind the $750 ($110 for the wine) for four tab sans tip. The waiter kept telling us with a smile "I'm going to do for you..." but never mentioned financial sodomy in his repertoire . 

Ordinarily price isn't an issue but the steak for two was obnoxiously priced. Moreover, the waiter showed us what he said was a dry-aged, well marbled, USDA prime grade, Porterhouse steak for two. I couldn't tell whether is was dry aged but the marbling of the steak revealed that is was USDA choice and not prime (or the lowest grade of prime - there are three grades but nobody ever mentions this).The waiter somehow forgot to mention that the steak was $180! This is the most I ever paid for a choice steak for two in Manhattan. Hell this is the most I've ever paid for a 'prime' steak for two! It tasted good but...

The super-hot Venezuelan hostess aside, the food was interesting and surprisingly good. I can't recall what else we ordered but we managed to finish whatever came to our table--whether it was ours to not. 

Very lively old-school atmosphere, great food overall and the well informed wait staff made the visit to Carbone pleasant despite the lingering financial pain in the tuchus.
Amazing italian food and great atmosphere, the waiters are all dressed up like the 60"s, very cool restaurant, a must when you are in nyc

Was the food good? Yes, But the prices were just criminal! It was good authentic Italian food. The Caesar salad although made table side was good but they used shredded Parmiagiano, for $20+ I want to see aged Parmesan Romano not store bought crap. The markup on everything esp drinks is just not worth it. Once I saw the prices it just deflated me from wanting to eat anything because it couldn't possibly live up to the expectation. The overall experience although they try very hard is just a little over the top bordering on cheesy.

I was there yesterday to celebrate my bae's birthday.the decor is old school,sober and I love the design of the plates.the music is too loud for lunch time but I like the playlist,very goodfellas.we ordered 2 pasta dishes,rigatoni in vodka sauce & tortellini bolognese.both delicious and well seasoned.then we decided to try the ribs,too Asian style for my palate!im Italian so I'm really picky when we talk about authentic Italian cuisine and for sure u never get ribs served with sweet sauce in my country.when I made a reservation last week I mentioned that was a birthday celebration so i was very disappointed when they served the tiramisu without a candle.the service was fine but I really don't understand why our waiter tried to sell extra dishes when I already ordered 3 main course for lunch.we will come back cause the pasta is one of the best I ever tried in the city but $16 for a bottle of water,wathahell!!

Some of the best pasta in town. 
The tortellini with bolognese sauce is to die for. We think it's a blend of ricotta and mascarpone for the filling and they top the tortellini with butter! The bolognese is perfect; not acidic or sweet. This is like a last meal before you die good. Do not not order this dish. 

The rigatoni in vodka sauce was pretty damn good too. Al dente and the right amount of heat. The ribs were outrageously big. The fennel on top gave it an Italian taste but they were sweet like Asian style ribs. We were kinda confused with this dish. 

Lastly, the hub was a bit pissed that he made the reservation for my birthday and we didn't get a cake or candle on top of our dessert. Meanwhile, another table got dessert prepared by their table and 2 candles. Go figure. Our waiter took off the glass of wine the hub had, but I think they shoulda still brought out a dessert of something. That was pretty disappointing. Also, who charges $16 for bottled water?

I'll be back for the tortellini but will have no expectations on the service that was very pushy to sell, sell, sell then mess up on a birthday reservation. Boooo

Conflicted after going to Carbone.  Food is solid and I love the idea of upping the ante on Italian American food using great ingredients and excellent techniques.  However, after signing the bill, the wife and I agree we probably won't be going back.

Food -
Free antipasti included prosciutto, tomato bread, garlic bread, bread sticks.   Garlic bread was phenomenal and everything else was perfectly seasoned.  The much talked about veal parm was phenomenal - crisp, juicy, and delicious but not worth the $54 price point my opinion.

Decor - old school NYC Italian joint with songs straight out of good fellas.  I definitely dug it.

Service - not very good especially for the price point.  Tons of managers, wait staff and hostesses, but we waited a good 10-15 minutes to get someone's attention for another glass of wine.  Same with getting the check.  When you're spending 3 bills for two people on dinner.  You expect comparable service from other restaurants in that price point.

Overall a tasty meal but for the same price I'd rather go to Babbo or Marea for a more satisfying Italian experience.

I went here last night and LOVED it. If they had sent us home after the complimentary bread (focaccia, garlic bread, and a sesame sour dough) I would have had a delightful experience, but the dinner that followed just kept amping it up. I got a meatball appetizer (best meatballs I've ever had) and a fettucini with mushroom dish. It was good, but if I were to recommend a dish it would be the spicy vodka rigatoni (one of the best entrees I've had for a long time). I can't wait to go back!

Worth every penny.  I get wary whenever I go to a restaurant that has received a lot of hype but this place definitely didn't let me down.  My fiance and I love Italian food and we frequent Italian restaurants more than any other cuisine.  This also means that we have a higher standard for Italian food.  It took us forever to get a decent reservation at Carbone, and to a normal person a 9:30 reservation is probably still pretty late but we were happy with it.  It also allowed for us to have a few drinks before so our bill didn't end up being as pricey as it could have been.  We usually get a bottle of wine when we go to dinner but this time we opted for a glass of champagne each, and a glass of wine each.  We got the spicy rigatoni as an appetizer...it was so simple and SO delicious.  It would be a sin to go there an not order this dish.  Everything is incredibly fresh and the food is flavored perfectly.  Hands down my favorite Italian restaurant in the city.

Quick Tips: I was lucky to come here on a business trip, but I think we paid less than $300 for two people, with a bottle of wine. I would definitely come back on my own tab. Make reservations on open table as the dining space is fairly small and even then, you may want to make a reservation way in advance. The complimentary parmagiano reggiano at the beginning of our meal was quite a treat. I was tempted to ask for another piece. Great presentation for all courses. 

Food: I dream of the scallops. A light breading on the scallops was a unique preparation, but absolutely delicious and light.  The perfect not too chewy not too hard consistency, with the right amount of flavor. 

The lobster ravioli was also worthy of licking one's plate. Not too creamy, but filling with an al dente pasta. 

Ambiance: Smaller dining area. We were fairly close to the patrons next to us. 

Service: Great service. We did have one hiccup where our waiter was standing over us when we were perusing the wine list. A little bit irritating to feel like you are rushed, when you are about to spend a lot of money for a decadent dining experience (service and food).

Rudest experience I have ever had at a restaurant. We left before eating. The hostess is a disgusting display of a low life given a little power. We had a reservation and 40 minutes later we were still not seated. We asked them why? She gave me a bullshit story about people having reservations before us even though they showed up well after our reservation. The manager is a smug little shit who thinks he has the next cipriani or something. When your restaurant closes soon hopefully I hope that you will remember that being rude and prejudice to your customers doesn't get you far.  I wish I could give no stars but alas this is it.... DO NOT EAT THERE... Walked 10 minutes down the street and actually went to ciprianis... Delicious food and POLITE service, that's why they've been around as long as they have.  FU carbone staff and shove your nasty meatballs where they belong ;)

I just moved to the New York area and had heard so much about Carbone. Naturally I had to eat there and see what it was all about.

From start to finish this meal was amazing. Their complimentary bread is delicious, complete with meats and cheeses to pick on. I got the eggplant appetizer which was very good, but honestly I wanted to try everything. I also had the Caesar salad - excellent and a very large portion. By the time the main course came around I was starting to get full but still managed to eat the famous pasta with spicy vodka sauce dish which had the perfect amount of spice. All in all, amazing food.

It's rare to find awesome food complimented with perfect service, but Carbone managed to wow me. The prices are steep but this meal was entirely worth it and if you can get a reservation, I HIGHLY RECOMMEND dining here.

I'd say this is pretty good for (pricey) comfort food!  Beware - the service is SLOW, even during lunch.  Lunch on a weekday took us a good 2.5 - 3 hours here.  

Personally, I loved the Baked Clams - pretty big portion; about 9 clams per dish. Definitely good for sharing.  The Caesar Salad with anchovies is surprisingly decadent, and very tasty.  The Scallops Francese are a reasonably big portion as well: about 6-7 scallops lightly encrusted in bread crumbs.  My favorite, though, was probably the Spicy Vodka Rigatoni.  Didn't have room for dessert, but the Margarita (with orange and cinnamon) was fantastic!
It doesn't get hipper than this, the food is good to very good but the scene and vibe can't be beat!

Was supper happy to finally go here! Great ambiance and food. Service on the verge of stuffy but right on point.
Will return when I get a promotion!!
Go if you can!

This is the first Italian restaurant that I've been to that's ever given the uber-famous Valter's Osteria in Salt Lake City a run for it's money. Absolutely one of the best dining experiences of my life, hands down.

I'd love to tell you a long story, but there's so many reviews of this place, I just want to quickly tell you what you need to know:

1. It's expensive. Like, really, really expensive.
2. It's worth every penny.
3. Skip the menu. Just let them feed you.
4. The caesar salad made tableside is really something special.
5. The warm mozzarella caprese salad is utterly divine.
6. The Carpaccio Piemontese will make you cry tears of joy.
7. The garlic bread is so good vampires would eat it.
8. The spicy rigatoni vodka is up there with the best food I ever ate, and
9. The veal parm is truly in a class of it's own.

This is just some of the heavenly goodness we gorged ourselves on over the course of several hours, enjoyed over round after round of cocktails and wine. Service, of course, was absolutely impeccable.

As if the night couldn't get any better, we found ourselves the lucky guests of our colleague, who picked up what I can only imagine was an insanely expensive tab. But I can assure you I will be back spending my own hard-earned money here some time soon. A fine dining experience like this, so close to home, is something you just must treat yourself to every now and again. (Unless you don't love yourself, of course.)

LOVED, LOVED, LOVED Carbone!
Excellent! Waiter mad me laugh - guys from Iowa trying to sound like he grew up in Bensonhurst! But the food was great! A must try !
Had dinner here last night. It was very good and the service was great accompanied with a nice Italian atmosphere. I'm a fan.
Very expensive but it is a lot of fun dinning here and the food is very good in an old school kind of way
Carbone is a fantastic restaurant with excellent service from the moment you walk in the door. The food was delicious looking forward to coming back here when I am next in New York.

Food: Carbone's food is excellent. I had a Caeser Salad, Eggplant Appetizer, and the Spicy Vodka Rigatoni. The Caeser had the perfect texture dressing (watch out, there are anchovies in it) with the most perfectly grated cheese on it. The eggplant appetizer was some of the best eggplant I've had in NYC and it cut like butter. But you absolutely have to get the spicy vodka riggatoni - it is the perfect level of spice and the vodka sauce is to die for.

Atmosphere: Tries to emulate the classic Italian-American environment - great music.

Service: Service is top-notch, you have separate waiters for everything, ensuring non-stop service. However, be aware that the waiters are pushy! Every time I have been here they will try and get you to order more food than you want - last time I ate there I only ordered salad, wine, and pasta, and they were trying to force entrees on us. It is understandable however, as the average table here spends a lot of money.

Overall: If you don't mind spending about $65-100 per person for great Italian food and don't mind speaking up to the waiters to tell them what you ordered is enough, this place is a go-to!

Believe the hype. Food was outstanding. You get what you pay for and the portions are huge. 

Had dinner this past Saturday evening for my fiancees Birthday.

I had two glasses of red the $16 one, on the lighter side. Was really good. My fiancee had a white- not sure of the name, but she liked it.

We got the baked clams- really good, caprese salad, veal parm (amazing!), spicy rigatoni vodka, side of meatballs and sea bass- not the oreganata one. Everything was delicious.

The free stuff they give you before the meal- the breads, parmigiana cheese, and pickled veggies all amazing. The bread is really, really good.

We also got the chocolate cherry blackout cake, which was good and they brought it out with a candle.

I'm taking one star away for our server Enrico. He was not very friendly.

I noticed he was more friendly and helpful to the table next to us- he explained the different types of clams in the baked clams, which we never got, never got an explanation what the free stuff was before the meal- just put it on the table, and I noticed he comped the table next to us on a glass of wine because it was their anniversary. Very odd.

If I'm paying big money- $300 with tip for two people then I expect to be pampered, which I didn't feel.

We also took home leftovers and have food for one meal for one person.

The waiter, Marco, padded my bill (total bill $425) which is so unprofessional as I was having a fantastic evening with my two daughter's. Firstly, he kept bringing my daughter's refills on their soft drinks of Coke and Diet Coke.  In fact these were not refills but $5 drinks of which cost $35 in total.  We wouldn't have continued to order more and more Coke's had we known they were going to charge this way.  OK, maybe I can understand this but the most heinous display was when Marco asked me three times if I wanted a glass of wine to which I finally said said I did which I really did.  I asked for a glass of red and and then said, "how about chianti or something like that."  When the bill came, he had charged me for the most expensive glass of wine on the menu, $35 per or $70 for two glass's which I did have.  With the prices of red by the glass on the menu going for: $16, 18,  22, 28, & $35, there was no reason for him to "Upcharge" me in this way.  It was just terrible but he knew my daughter's and I were celebrating.  It's not the money, it's the fact that carbone's has so many "one-time" visitors that they think they can get away with this: and they did.  Too bad as it was a fun place and the food was good: I just didn't need to pay the equivalent of two chicken entree's ($35 for the chicken scarpello which my daughter ordered).   TOO BAD and I hope they enjoy the $70 when things slow down and they loose business to the next-hot-restaurant...

Food: 
More on the traditional American-Italian side, with subtle twists.  The food is perfectly executed, which is what makes it such a good and refreshing concept. 
App: SPECIAL: Langoustine scampi - 5/5
Dinner: Shrimp Su'Modo (Jo Jo Sauce) - 4.75/5
Dinner: Chicken Massimo - 5/5
Dessert: Bananas Foster - 5+/5

I love bananas foster, so I'm partial.  Everything was a throwback to an Italian era that is no defunct or tries to hard and delivers too little.  The staff, the food, the music, and atmosphere, all make you feel like you aren't even in this decade, let alone in the city.  

Bravo.

LOVED: the complimentary bread basket (swoon over the garlic cheesy bread), meats (salami), cheese (pecorino), and pickled cauliflower. A grand appetizer in and of itself!

DEVOURED: the spicy rigatoni vodka (amazingly flavorful - totally worth the hype for me) and the scallops (light, perfectly seasoned, perfect texture, delicious)!

ENJOYED: the side of corn (blissful!), the tiramisu dessert with a tasty madeline to boot (so bad yet so good), and the free rainbow pastry.

APPRECIATED: the cozy festive atmosphere and fine speedy service (maybe it was the end of the night, but our orders came really quickly).

BUT MEH: the veal parmesan. Not sure if it was just the one we got, but I just plain didn't like it. Definitely nothing special or worth the price-tag imo.

Overall, we had a fantastic experience despite the super late dining time (only reservation we could get) and the disappointment of the veal (and the lack of meatballs for order that night).

3.5 stars. Overall, the food was decent to good, but it is definitely not of the caliber of other Michelin star restaurants. Torrisi is way better in terms of food quality and taste. The moscato is delicious here. The bread basket and little snacks before our appetizers and entrees were very enjoyable. The spicy rigatoni pasta was good but a little too heavy for me. The veal parmesan was soggy and a little on the fattier side. We all ate a few bites and had to put it down. Scallops franchese were good but also a bit heavy. Corn was good. Tiramisu was delicious.

Having been to many Italian restaurants in my life I have to admit before we arrived I was wondering if Carbone could live up to the hype.   Thankfully not only did it meet our expectations but in a lot of ways exceeded them.   The food was impeccable and complimented by a great wine list.  Service was great and the atmosphere with the vintage Italian music playing in the background made it a tremendous experience.   Highly recommend the spicy rigatoni vodka,  and the branzino but nothing we had... which was a lot was bad.   Highly recommend if you can get in!!!

Not worth the hype. Not sure why they are so busy to get a reservation. I came here for dinner with a friend and got the lobster ravioli and halibut. Nothing special for the price we paid. There are other great italian restaurants in NYC where I can spend my $.
This was my first visit to the restaurant, and I loved everything about it: great music, charming staff and delicious food. Both the Caesar salad and veal parm were outstanding.
went there for lunch... everything is sooooo yummy~ we ordered baked clam as appetizer, meatball as side, and Spicy Rigatoni Vodka as main. love love love the Rigatoni~
Undoubtedly outrageously expensive.....No menu posted outside is the tipoff.  The windows are curtained completely--no looking in, no looking out.  Pretentious.

Racist！Sommelier looked miserable. Not one smile. Pissy throughout the evening. We asked if we could add to our reservation, they said NO.  Meanwhile two tables behind us were able to add chairs when they had extra people in their party. We only wanted to add ONE. We ordered a porterhouse for 2 and never did they disclose the price or weight. $185 for porterhouse for 2. That was the least of our issues though.  We felt second class in the restaurant compared to everyone else. Rainbow cake was given to EVERY table but ours. In the midst of announcing the desserts, the waitress walked away and never came back. Food was decent but service was subpar. So much good food in ny, no reason to spend it on crappy restaurants.

If you are not Caucasian,  please visit this place to experience what racism means in the US. Being in NYC for 30 years,  I have never felt discrimination until I walked into Carbone. The staff was condescending,  giving us unfriendly looks and service.  Where's Al Sharpton? 
Not one staff smiled or said goodbye to us when we left.  Waitress served us with stern mean look all night like she couldn't wait to throw us out.
Food was very good but service was unbelievably horrifying. I hope this review doesn't get filtered to hidden reviews because it seems like Carbone has paid Yelp to filter all bad reviews, many indicating discrimination. 
We spent over $600 for 4 , it was the most horrifying dining experience ever in my life.  Never never again.

NOT worth the price tag. I kept seeing pictures of the complimentary burrata (fresh mozzarella swimming in olive oil) and prosciutto- of course they changed this practice to include complimentary sliced salami and no mozz. Cutting back already? The ceasar was very good as were the meatballs. However, the center of each meatball was undercooked and NOT WORTH $7  A F#CKING MEATBALL!!! It takes some (meat) balls to charge $21 for 3 meatballs. My girlfriends Veal Marsala was sligfhtly undercooked and had to be sent it back. The meat itself was chewy even before sending it back. If we had paid $25 for that I would have felt ripped off but this was $55. My Veal Parm was awesome as has been stated by basically everyone to ever eat here. The service was good, but they dropped the ball with this:  It was my birthday dinner and they didn't even comp the $15 SLICE OF CAKE!! This was a sliver of cake for $15! Many places may have comp'd dessert for the Veal being undercooked or a birthday alone...but between the two- they should have knocked dessert off the check.  C'mon, that's pretty shitty! Either way, this was a $300 meal and we could have had just as good a meal for less than half the price. The team behind this place and the new hot spot Dirty French (getting bad Yelp reviews) are young and way too cocky. Carbone was good, but not deserving of the hype, a michelin star or our money.
Service impeccable. Nice wine list. Great food. Intimate atmosphere. Don't love the tiramisu. But that's the only thing I didn't love. After espresso and Sambuca.. forgot all about it.

Carbone is clicking on all cylinders! We finally tried it and now are wondering what took us so long. The lively atmosphere is perfect for the style they're trying to evoke, along with a soundtrack that exactly captures the era. Service, from the front of the house to the busboys, is top notch and totally charming. The place is just plain fun! We enjoyed riffing with other diners as much as with the serving team. You're not overly close to neighbors by NY standards, but the place seems to invite friendly interaction. We were at an early seating but never felt rushed.

The meal reminded me of Sunday supper at nonna's where you stuff yourself silly with course after course of delicious homemade food, though with no disrespect to nonna, Carbone kicks it up a notch or three. As for cost, it's not cheap, however we carried home 2 bags of leftovers that we enjoyed for dinner the next day, so on that basis it wasn't all that expensive, and certainly worth the price for the superior quality of the ingredients. We clearly over-ordered, but we wanted to try a lot of dishes.

Shortly after you're seated they bring excellent bread, hunks of fairly good parmigiana reggiano, slices of salami and delicious pickled cauliflower with just a hint of heat. The highly-touted garlic bread also brings some heat and we weren't sure if it was due only to the garlic or some hidden ingredient. There are only two other places in town where we've had focaccia this good (Locanda Verde and Lincoln). 

We started with an upscale take on eggplant parmigiana that featured melt-in-your-mouth eggplant stacked in layers like a millefeuille served with globes of wonderful house-made mozzarella as well as a sublime beef carpaccio, as thin as paper and bursting with flavor. 

For primi, we shared the justifiably renowned spicy (but not too spicy) rigatoni in vodka sauce, perfectly al dente and enhanced by thin strips of onions, and exceptional lobster ravioli comprising of delicate pasta stuffed with chunks of tender lobster that overflowed onto the plate in a creamy herb sauce. We also could not resist having an order of their meatballs. They're fairly large and come 3 to a plate. They are everything a meatball should be. I should mention that our waiter did not push them on us, I asked for them specifically.

Next we shared the tasty monster-sized veal parmigiana accompanied by a side of broccoli rabe. The veal was cooked on the bone, which was detached and served alongside it so you can gnaw on the attached morsels. The veal was tender and flavorful with a bright tomato sauce and that fabulous mozzarella. We couldn't even finish half of it between the two of us.

The tiramisu for dessert was good though not our favorite preparation of this dish.

My husband doesn't drink so I went with wines by the glass, first a delicious Franciacorta followed by a very good Barolo that married perfectly with the meal. The espresso to end our feast was just right. 

We really enjoyed Torrisi Italian Specialties and now we have another favorite.

rudest place ever.  We ask for a different table, there where 5 empty tables.  Told not happening!!!!!! Beyond attitude   We walked right out  so glad   The management needs to seriouly work on improving the attitude

Excellent service however very noisy with loud half drunk people. portions are obscene reflecting an even more obscene price. 

The porterhouse was tasteless, the lasagna was burnt and gross.

Overall very disappointing experience, not going to come again. The only reason there are 3 stars is because of the service.

People who rate this restaurant high have clearly never eaten good italian food.

Decent food, very expensive for what it is.  Staff pretty bad with picking who to fawn over and who to ignore.  The guy in my group who picked up the tab looks like a schlub but is polite and a scandalously good tipper.  He nonetheless got pretty shtty treatment all night.

Ok im throwing out one of my rare five stars.  I have been twice and it is fantastic. 

Its quasi family style and they divide it up nicely for each person.  Each time i have had the rigatoni vodka and the veal parm and the porterhouse.  

The drinks and wines are great. The somm was extra helpful.   But the best part is the waiters and the whole coziness of the place.  Its as if you have been transported to italy for dinner with a 45 year old sinatra. 

Its very expensive and the food is great but the value comes from the total experience.

it was ok-- rigatoni was spicy, and just ok, I don't know why I expected better. Portions were not as large as expected. The garlic bread was very good. The rest of our meal was nondescript. I've had much better meals for 1/5 of the price. The veal was ok, not as good as expected.

Three words...spicy rigatoni vodka! Tastes so delicious and fresh. I loved the atmosphere and nice waiters. My boyfriend  - the birthday boy had the veal parm and loved it! Just be sure to order a side of pasta if you get that dish since it doesn't come with any sides. 

At Carbone they make you feel special and aren't pushy on their specials, etc. like how other restaurants can be which is much appreciated. Lastly, it was pretty cool to run into Kim K's mom, Kris Jenner on the way out.

First, the food....oh man...the spicy rigatoni vodka is ridiculous...the complimentary antipasto (cheese, salami, picked cauliflower) were simple but amazing....we did not have a salad course - between the bread, the antipasto, the macaroni, well, we barely needed a main course but of course we had to....Bass Oreganata and Veal Parm. I insist you do the same. and despite REALLY not needing it, we had the chocolate cake thing with nutella ice cream on it. Because it was there....Great dining experience made superlative by Jason, our captain. The guy is one of the best waitpeople I have ever dealt with.

Not a cheap night out, but worth your hard-earned dough.
The spicy rigatoni is out of this world, but a very small portion:( VERY INCONSISTENT...
Probably has some of the best dishes in the city. Go with the favs, went with the pork chop last time and was pretty disappointed.

UNINSPIRED MENU WITH INSPIRING PRICES!  Our party of 6 ordered a wide variety of items on the menu:  oysters, baked clams, eggplant and octopus antipasti, caesar salad, rib eye, halibut, bass Alison, and the signature "veal parmesan".  All were good and none were WOW! Even our waiter referred to the "veal parmesan" as "veal parm".  We should have known it would be like our local pizza shop's veal parm with the addition a bone. We were served nothing that was special.  A $55 veal parmesan should be outstanding and Carbone's was not.  The  wine list had many more bottles of wine over $1000 than under $100 and the $75 corkage fee for each 750 ml bottle of wine is absurd.  The 4 dessert items were displayed table side on a very large metal tray which had to be rested on our table causing us to adjust our chairs.  Perhaps a more appropriate size tray would make more sense given the crowded space. The service was uneven:  we were rushed at the beginning and dessert was served family style.  We were given forks...no plates.  Very caveman!  Frank Sinatra in the background was banquet hall cliche.  I have no reason to ever return and suggest you find a restaurant that understands hospitality like the late Charlie Trotter-exceed your customer's expectations!

Fell for the hype! But still had a fun experience.  Though this is not at all great Italian food -- walking into this hidden behind velvet curtain doors little place with oldie music blaring and waiters hustling around is an experience in itself.

Garlic bread- overly greasy and far from the best.  Nice cheese served with it.
Had to ask waiter 4 times for a refill on the bread.  How can you eat Italian dishes without dipping your bread in the sauce?
Veal parm - ridiculously priced but not ridiculously good.  Good though and good quality very tender veal. Worth a try once. 4 stars.
My spicy vodka rigatoni- heaviest sauce, way too spicy and rather sickening.   1 star for that dish. 

Service was bad as others have commented. Host/workers seem to think they're hot s--t.

Average Italian cooking but overall a fun/different experience.

Yup, it's crazy expensive, but also crazy good. No one goes here expecting it to be cheap, so this 5 star review is certainly not for value, but for an excellent faux authenic NYC old school Italian meal.  Dinner for the 3 of us on Friday night was 3 hours long and $475 (luckily not on our dime thanks to an overly generous friend in the entertainment industry).

Based on other Yelp reviews we realized that it is hard to go wrong with any of the dishes here so we decided to give it a fair shake so we attempted to try as many dishes as 3 people could eat (luckily I only had a salad for lunch).

First off, they start you off with an amazing basket of breads and cheeses and meats.  While you absolutely must try everything, try to resist eating the whole basket as you will need room for the rest of the meal.
It is smart they bring the basket to tide you over as you will definitely need time to navigate the overwhelming (and comically huge) menu.

Luckily the waitstaff is extremely helpful and attentive (they hit the right balance of making you feel that you are in for an experience at and exclusive place, while having no condescending attitude...this alone made the price of the meal worth it) . While we came prepared with a list of certain dishes we wanted to try, the waiter did an excellent job of navigating us through and following our order that we wanted to feel like we would need to be rolled out of the restaurant in the end.

By the way, the sommelier was excellent.  She gave us no attitude for skipping the wine and helped navigate the proper order to try all their classic cocktails (we made it through the whole list).  My favorite was the rusty nail.

Since it would take me 10 pages to cover all the details of the meal, I will just quickly list some of what we had...tuna tartare (phenomenal), baked clams (good but not as amazing as I thought they would be), spicy rigatoni (phenomenal), tortellini al ragu (phenomenal), meatballs (very good), grilled fish (good but can't remember what fish it was!), veal parm (excellent, but Queen in Brooklyn is better), and 2 other dishes that I am completely blanking on at moment.  We also had the carrot cake which was excellent as well....but I was too stuffed at that point to have more than a bite or two.

One nice touch, was that seeing we were sharing everything, the waiter automatically brought everything out plated on 3 plates so it was family style without having to split things ourselves.  For the fish and veal parm, they brought out as whole dish, presented, then divided in front of us.

Overall it was just a wonderful money is no object evening.  Don't get to do that too often so as long as you go in there knowing and not worrying that your wallet will be a lot lighter on the way out, you will have an phenomenal experience.  We will be back soon.

Ok -- I'm going to go through the cons first because there aren't many for this place. 

The first would be how pricey it is. If you plan on going here and getting a small meal, no drinks, no extras, you'll probably be fine. But if you want to get an appetizer, some drinks, maybe plates to share, etc, you're going to be spending a pretty penny. It's not cheap by any means. 

The second is how hard it is to get a damn reservation here. I called a month in advance for my bf's birthday and the only reservation they had available on a TUESDAY night was at 9:45. No thanks. So, call wayyyy in advance if you want to come here. 

So onto the pros!
The food is absolutely fantastic. I don't eat beef and most pork (and I try not to eat white meat unless necessary) but I was able to split some things with my boyfriend here that were vegetarian friendly. We ordered the eggplant Torrisi, which is basically a grilled piece of eggplant with fresh mozzarella. Very tasty. We also split the Spicy Rigatoni, which ended up being my favorite, and we also ordered the Chicken Massimo to split. We decided to go all out and get the carrot cake for dessert which was so delicious. 

The service was phenomenal. We were sat immediately when we got there, and helped by our server the moment we sat down. He was great at making suggestions and had a cool, old school italian (mafioso almost) charm about him that was a fun touch but I'm pretty sure it was all for show. In any news, everything came out quick and we didn't feel rushed or pressured.

The ambiance was old school italian but in a modern setting. It definitely felt like something straight out of a mafia movie but not as daunting, obviously. I mean that in a good way, if that's even possible. It's fairly small and cozy but doesn't feel that way once you're sitting at the table.

I'd definitely come back here for a special occasion. It's a bit pricey for just an average night out but it's worth it if you don't mind spending a little extra.

Hands down my favorite italian meal i've had in awhile.  Get the spicy rigatoni vodka dish, lamb, oysters and the chocolate cake dessert. Not only do I love the food here but the ambiance is what also stands out. I like the old school new york feel, and it is refreshing to eat in a place where you are not on top of the other table.  The sommelier  was extremely helpful
This small joint is a ripoff over priced full of wannabe people it is totally a joke with so many good real Italian restaurants in the city why bother waiting to get seated and pay high prices!

Overpriced service sucks arrogant environment Had to ask waiter 4 times for a refill on the bread.  Drink before and after you go there otherwise be ready to pay crazy bill for awful drinks .Carbone is a tourist trap ....don't be fooled

I waited for some of the hype to go down on Carbone after being an avid fan of Parm.  Made a reservation a month in advance and came on a Thursday evening. The place was packed and our table was a little too close to the tables next to us but it felt like part of the experience.  Our waiter felt like he was straight out of a movie, in a great Italian best friend sort of way.  My friend and I split the clams, spicy rigatoni, veal parm, crunchy rabe and carrot cake. I have zero complaints about the food, I personally loved the clams and veal and my friend could eat the spicy rigatoni everyday.  We picked these as they are recommended but everything looked good and it was the perfect amount of food.  The people next to us did not share and regretted it. Wine was somewhat pricey. About $100 a head before tip.

I mean, it lives up to your expectations.

The service is so good and fun it's almost tacky, but i love it! Our waiter was knowledgeable and patient with us. He did not rush us whatsoever. I did want to smack him upside the head for bringing by white truffles, casually opening the box for us to smell then shutting the lid and THEN explaining the price. So rude :) and of course how could we say no after getting a whiff? 

We opted for the fresh scallops which he mentioned as an app, delicious. I had a spicy pasta (no clue what the name was) but he said it was popular and basically it was a grown up version of delicious mac n cheese, but spicy. My friends had lobster ravioli and a chicken, both delicious.

Dessert I had the cheesecake and my friends had ice cream and the nutella cake. Nutella FTW! Chianti was good too. YUM

Top ten dining experiences of my life. Simply stunning. Everything done just right. Feels like home without the Italian grandmother asking why you don't have a boyfriend. Jason, our waiter, was 10/10! Get the carrot cake. get the squash. Good lord that squash. The squash!!!

Hard to get a reservation but it is worth the wait!!! It is by far the best Italian restaurant !
I had the tortellini al ragu, the meat is chopped so finely and the taste is amazingly subtle. My friend had the spicy rigatoni vodka, she is not a drinker and hate alcohol and she absolutely loved it!
The service is perfect too.
My new favorite restaurant in town.

A sublime restaurant experience from the service to the food. We felt like nobility from the moment we entered the door.  The waiter treated us as though we were his only  customers.  It is not a big restaurant, so the ambiance was cozy.  I can not add to what has already been said about this wonderful American-Italian restaurant.  But I will gush about the highlight of my night-  the spicy rigatoni in vodka sauce.  It was simple yet so satisfying.  The pasta was tender with the perfect amount of bite.  The sauce was creamy, rich, and flavorful.  The meal progressed at a nice pace, each course was delivered in a timely manner and not once did I feel rushed.  The dishes were presented and described meticulously by each server.  Thank you Carbone for a truly amazing evening.

I dined here recently and had a good time. The food was great and service was excellent. Everyone who worked here was kind and attentive.

So why the one star you ask? This review is mainly about a bill discrepancy and the way the company Major Food (who runs Carbone) handled it.

When I received my bill, I paid with a credit card and left tip in cash. Fast forward a couple days, I see a transaction higher than my original bill. I called Carbone and was then transferred to Major Food, who then told me to email a person named Kate that handles bill discrepancy. When I don't receive a reply two days after emailing her, I called back and was told they will look into it. A week later, still no reply or refund of the difference.

I will not be dining here again.

If you can get in... GO. If you can't try again, and again and again until you can. It's that good.  Is it pricey? Came here on a Monday night at 7:30 with my girlfriend, it wasn't too busy but quickly changed after 8pm.  Yes, it's pricey but It's worth it considering you won't be going too often.  The wine will break the bank but again you're here for the experience, the food, the service which were all wonderful, its the complete package.  Explore the menu, they brought comped pickled cauliflower and prosciutto with fresh cheese with a nice bread basket.  We skipped apps after that, it was the perfect hold over for the real deal (below).  We were never rushed, never felt pressured into spending ridiculous amounts of money on wine (if you are going to get wine go by the bottle).  

Spicy rigatoni vodka A++.
Meatballs A 
Veal Parm A-

Will definitely be back again soon, I hope!

I'm once again confused why so many rave of this place.  Is it simply for the possibility that one may see a celebrity?  Is that a benefit when dining that I don't know about?  The food was mediocre.  I found the same ingredients used in more than one dish.  It's a cute, little place though, hence the two stars.

Got an early reservation a few days before (by calling in as Open Table showed no availability).  We didn't have a huge appetite so between two people, ordered the octopus and caesar  salad to start, linguine vongole and spicy rigatoni vodka for mains and the carrot cake for dessert.  

I was excited for the caeser salad as I read reviews that they make it table side, but it came already prepared and heavily overdressed - I couldn't eat more than a few bites.  Flavors were good, but if they had used half the dressing it would have been more edible.  Octopus was delicious - it was perfectly cooked and had a slightly sweet flavor to the sauce which gave the dish a good salty / sweet balance. 

Linguine vongole was forgettable and nothing special but the spicy rigatoni vodka lived up to its hype.  I would reorder this dish if I ever go back.  Carrot cake good but I would try another dessert next time.  It didn't taste like it was baked that day - had that day old dryness.   

Service was fine - nothing to rave about - though we did appreciate not being rushed despite being there for over two hours.  Tables are small for two people so try to get the bread and charcuterie out of the way before the food starts to come out.

Yum! I loved Carbone, although my experience wasn't exactly perfect. It's a beautiful, dimly lit and cavernous restaurant with Sinatra playing. The waiters too seem like they stepped out of the Godfather- dressed to the nines, intimidatingly stoic and complete with an Italian accent. Gimmicky? Slightly, yes. But it's charming nonetheless. The amuse bouche was good- pickled cauliflower, three types of bread (the plain sesame one was the best) and proscuitto. We got the Carpaccio Piemontese as an appetizer- it was incredible. Extremely rich, however. The vodka rigatoni was delicious, just the right amount of heat and creaminess. Meatballs were delicious, although I've had better at Motorino. However, the linguine vongole was far too salty, to the point where I couldn't even eat it. When we called the waiter over to see if he could get us a less salty portion he flat out refused, saying that was how the dish was supposed to be- "briny". It definitely tasted like the ocean, if you were drowning in it. Cocktails were good, if pricy. I would say stick to the tried and true dishes here: caesar salad, scallops, vodka rigatoni etc etc. Do your research on Yelp and you'll have a great meal.

I was invited by friends to join them and was well aware of the buzz about Carbone.  The decor was great.....very old school a la "The Godfather".   Totally loved our genuine Italian waiter....he was great.   I thought the food would have been "good" at 1/2 the price, but the truth is, it is outrageously expensive for what it is.   I was disappointed with the Gemelli with sausage and broccoli rabe,  which seemed to have some strange thickener used.....the Steak Diane was OK, but not as good as a real steakhouse steak.
And the chicken Scarpariella was probably the worst version of this dish I have ever had.   So, to summarize......a cool place that is very "hot", great service but fair and very overpriced food.

We called a month in advanced to secure a reservation for Christmas Eve.  WOOOOWEEE!  It was everything we expected and more.  The food was incredible!!  Yes, it is expensive but definitely worth it especially on special occasions.  Our server Jason was patient, knowledgeable, friendly, funny, and very attentive.  I will definitely visit again next time I am in NYC.

OpenTable had a spot open on a sunday at 10:30.  We took it.  Arrived 30 minutes earlier and we got a seat.  This place is great.  Can't remember how many drinks i had because everyone was toasting at different tables and the staff gave us drinks oh and free Carrot cake.  Will definitely visit again.  Love this place  

Spicy rigatoni vodka 
Veal Parm
Carrot Cake

I unfortunately was never able to actually try the food here so this review serves only to the way in which Carbone conducts business. My boyfriend & I had a reservation here for New Years Eve. On the day of (around noon) someone called my boyfriend & informed him that they were changing their menu & it would now be $350 per person & urged us to cancel our reservation. There was no apology or explanation as to why they made this change on the day of. Because of this experience, we will never be patrons of this establishment. Awful way to treat new customers.
Not only the best Italian meal I've had in the city... also one of the best meals I've had period. I recommend the spicy rigatoni ala vodka!

Nothing but the best by the infamous Mr. Carbone & Mr. Torrisi. They really outdone themselves. 

Pros: everything! The menu is huge! Literally. Shaved truffles anyone? White or black? The veal is very delicious! As well as the tuna tar tar which was in special! 

Cons: pricey, but sooo worth it!

dont believe the hype! We waited months with great anticipation, only to be greeted by a mixologist who couldn't be bothered to suggest a an inventive bourbon drink and plopped our 35$ per glass champagne on the bar without even a coaster.
The decor got its point across , I did feel like I was in the hole the wall in my neighborhood back in the day , the music was cheery, I'm surprised it wasn't englebert.
Trendy with some traditional notes to ground it ? That's the idea? but surely missed the mark with the food 
Again with great expectations , we were greatly disappointed
Is there deliberately a Chinese flair to the italian dishes? Smokey clams casino , smokey broccoli rabe , pork chop that's tasted soaked in soy sauce , the "best Caesar salad in town" was sweet and sour ? Not a great combination with the 800$ bottle of wine we carefully chose , no help from the wine steward 
Our waiter was great , the real deal in disneyworld
Our surrounding 50 somethings (that's who is spending big bucks on wine) still loving life , out at midnight diners all agreed the chicken parm was what to get there , sorry I missed that

This was my 2nd visit and an average of the 2 times I went.  The first time I thought everything was spectacular (in particular the spicy rigatoni which I was coming back to get again). I actually didn't get the rigatoni on this visit though, I decided to try something new and picked the Fettucine con funghi - so good! I think the pastas seem to be their strong point.  I also tried the baked clams, which is actually 3 kinds of baked clams, 3 pcs each:  clams casino, clams with uni and another I forget.  This dish was very good with the clams casino being my favorite.   For main, we split the rib eye.  Just so you know, this isn't steakhouse rib eye no frills, it came smothered in a rich sauce. Very good actually and the meat cooked perfectly (medium rare!).  Last minute we decided to throw in a side as the main dish came with no sides and just felt bare so we ordered the broccoli rabe. It came out very quickly! But the good news stops there.   I hate to say it, but this was probably the worst dish I've had in a very long time.  The veggies were massive and limp and visually unappetizing and unfortunately tasted the way they looked. We both took a single bite and didn't touch it again.  I was a little disappointed that they servers didn't notice that they were untouched - I feel like most places will ask when a dish hasn't been eaten.  So this is where I take off stars but since overall my experience has been ok, I averaged it out.

It's solid Italian fare in an authentic throwback vibe - loved the old Sinatra playlist.  But its a tad pricey for what it is. Love the pastas though and hoping the broccoli rabe was a fluke. It was almost comical how bad it was.

This place was amazing!! I will make sure to come back every time I am in the city. The food was delicious (especially the tortellini) and the wait staff was very attentive. Very small, rustic Italian restaurant feel. We went for lunch and they had a nice crowd. Just amazing!

hate starting the new year with a bad review but i feel obliged so the others who haven't been won't waste their money.  not. worth. it. i. mean. it.  the service was solid and the free prosciutto was delicious so they collectively garner one star but i definitely had so much better Italian food at other cheaper establishments throughout the city.  complimentary mozzarella was salty and garlic bread was drenched in heavy oil.  spicy vodka rigatoni wasn't bad but not worth 26 bux and their rib eye was tough and super salty.  but the real deal breaker was the blackout hazelnut cake (?) which tasted really...what's the word?.....cheap.  (but 18 bux)  not really worth the hype people.  i am serious.
When you wake up thinking about last nights dinner you know it was great not just good.

I have heard amazing things about this restaurant and seemingly everyone of my friends had experienced Carbone except for me. So it was quite an event when I went the other night for the first time. Walking in there, you feel like you've gone back in time or like you're on the Goodfellas set or something. All the uniforms look like something out of the Sinatra era. Even the wait staff physically look the part. The penne and veal parm were unbelievable and absolutely worth the little food baby I'm sporting today. Nothing a little extra gym time won't take care of. The whole experience was decadent and over indulgent, but fortunately that's kinda what I'm looking for in an amazing Italian spot. They have a really cool rum cart-- I'm not a big rum person but my friends partook in the rum drinking and quite enjoyed it. They had this amazing banana flambé dessert thing that was UNBELIEVABLE. and it's a whole show when they flame it up for you. But don't worry- the fire extinguisher is never too far away. All in all- amazing dining experience and I hope to be returning very soon!

This place came highly recommended from a friend who has great taste, so my wife and I were very excited to go. The service was fun (the waiters all have a schtick that makes you feel like your talking to the Fonz from Happy Days) but still helpful. The guys at the bar made a mean old fashioned, but the sommelier kind of swung and missed with the wine. We asked for a rich, silky red with relatively low tannin. The bottle he brought was low in tannin but not so rich or silky. The creamed escarole had way too much pancetta. All in all it was a fun night out but it wasn't as mind blowing of a dining experience as we had hoped for.

I've been looking forward to trying carbone for a while now. I wish i didn't have the pleasure. Carbone had to pay for the great reviews on yelp, because this food is garbage. A restaurateur, and major foodie myself, this was a real shame. I have no problem paying ridiculous prices for food when i am getting quality stuff.

Lets start...
1.The hostess looked like she was doing you a favor giving you the crappiest seat in restaurant. I would have walked out from here but my girl was starving.
2. $18 dollars for a bottle of pelligrino?
3. baked clams came out raw and ice cold. sauce had no taste.
4. My girlfriend is vegetarian and they did not a thing to accommodate her.
5. ordered spicy rigatoni. size of plate was obserd. We counted 9 pieces of rigatoni. When asked manager he looked at us with a straight face and said that's the order. He did bring us more.... will give Carbone that.
6. They tout there $55 dollar veal chop parm to be the best veal parm in town... It was nothing more than mediocre. on a 1-10 i rate it a 3.5.  The veal was tender but it wasn't very tasty and loaded with salt.

I never do yelp reviews but my experience at Carbone tonight had to be told. I just wish they had lubrication for this hosing.

This place is the worst ever!!! Not to mention it took over a month to get a reservation it's not worth it!!  We arrived early and the hostess was very nice. Upon sitting down as soon as we said we didn't want drinks the waiter gave us a nasty look. We had to ask for a food menu.. That's crazy!!! When we ordered a few things he asked if that's it.. Seriously ?? Had to  pay a sharing fee .. Nuts !!! They showed us a dessert cart 30 minutes later ( mind you we were sitting there with our table cleared) when we asked for the check and said no dessert .. He had us wait another thirty minutes for our check.. Shall I continue??? This place sucks !! The service was terrible and never will I return !!!!!

This is just an average Italian restaurant. I went for dinner, last night , part of a group of 6. While the service was fine, the waiter helpful and cheerful- I didn't think there was anything super outstanding here. I've had better Italian food at the Jersey Shore. While, i wouldn't be adverse to returning,I would prefer trying a new place before going back.

I was thrilled to get a 10:15 reservation here on a recent Saturday night. It seemed too good to be true. It was. Upon our arrival at 10:15 on the dot, my friend and I were told that our table would be ready in a few minutes, and were directed to the already crowded, minuscule bar. We proceeded to wait until10:50 for our table. Now I get that it was Saturday night, but I also get that a well-managed restaurant shouldn't offer reservations that they can't keep. We both thought the food would make up for the wait. It didn't. The bread and cheese offered when we were seated was great and the zucchini appetizer delicious was as well. As for the pastas, we were underwhelmed. After reading all the great reviews of the spicy rigatoni, I guess my expectations were too high. My advice for what it's worth--if you want to feel like you're hanging with the in crowd and are happy to overpay for the experience, go for it. If you want great service and outstanding Italian food, go to Scarpetta.

Carbone is a must when dining out in NYC. As soon as you walk through the door, you know you're in for a special treat. It's upscale, yet casual and comfortable. The atmosphere, decor, music, menu, and drinks are all on point and it's the spectacular service that brings them all together harmoniously. The service alone is enough to make you want to come back. Of course, the chopped salad, spicy rigatoni with meatballs, scallops, spare ribs, branzino, escarole, and tiramisu are all good reasons to return as well. Yes - it may be pricey, but the portions are enormous and meant for sharing. Carbone definitely delivers a memorable experience! I highly recommend!

Classic NY Italian.  The food,  service and the ambiance all allude to the long lost NYC Italian joint.  Not much of a standing bar room.  Is it pricy?  Yes.  Is it worth it?  Depends on who you asks but yes.  Is white truffle worth it?  YES.

Carbone is a gatronomic delight. Each course had me begging for me. We started off with the Octopus Pizzaiolo which was grilled to perfection. The ends were blackened and the interior was unbelievably tender. We also ordered a side of meatballs, which was probably too much. I ordered a soup of the day which served Italian style wontons in a light, refreshing broth.

For the main courses we ordered the Veal Parmagiana, the Spicy Rigatoni Vodka and the Tortellini Al Ragu. Since we were splitting the dishes, the kitchen courteously divided the plates for us. Needless to say, everything was spectacular. I wish they didn't split the Rigatoni because I would have ate the whole thing myself. The Veal Parm was succulent and rich with flavor. The tortellini was delicious, but not a stand out in my opinion. 

The 30 day wait is definitely worth it, I can't wait to come back here again.

TIP: call 30 days before because open table won't have the 7pm reservation you are looking for.

Obnoxiously overpriced comfort food. 

It is exactly what it is.  The veal parm is simply a veal parm. The chopped salad was.. A chopped salad, was a chopped salad, rigatoni was pasta with sauce, etc. Fair pricing for the food would at least be half. And you can definitely find food exactly like this in at least 20 other places around the city (little italy even) that don't get all the hype. 

There is absolutely no element of surprise or creativity to compensate for the excessively high prices for the food. 

The quality of the food was good, but you'd just expect that. 

Reasons to go here:
1. Be in the "know" because its a famous place and you live in NY
2. You're a tourist and want to say you went to the most famous italian place in NY

We went here for a birthday dinner and WOW! We loved it!!

From the Caesar salad to the cheesecake it was amazing!

Excellent veal parm
Excellent langoustines scampi
Puttanesca was inedible - way too salty - and I love salty food
Broccoli rabe tasted burnt and too salty
Excellent cheesecake

Decor is fun.
Service was friendly and fun.

Everything is quite over the top at Carbone, including the prices. I only wish the dishes were more consistently good.

I love these guys' first restaurant, Torrisi Italian Specialties. I found this a bit disappointing in comparison.

Overall, it was a fun dinner, but not at all worth the money.

Honestly, the people at Carbone ruined my birthday. I made the reservation the same day and put my credit card down. I called back to cancel because the reservation ended up being too late and one person was not feeling well and wanted to eat earlier rather than later. I called a couple times and no one answered. Finally- 4 hrs before the res I got to talk to someone. He told me they were so busy that we couldn't come earlier (it was 5pm at this point) and he would charge me $200 if we didn't come. I explained someone wasn't feeling well and that it was my birthday and that I had only made the reservation that morning. There was no reasoning with him, he was going to charge my card if we didn't come. I asked him if he would rather I come and have one drink split between 4 people and then leave and he said yes. Literally this makes no sense- it's not like I was a huge party (4) and if they are THAT BUSY of a restaurant then they could defiantly fill our place. We didn't end up going and I can't wait to dispute the charge on my card. 

I have eaten here before it was just ok-greasy, overly salted, and not worth the money. It was when they first opened so I wanted to give it another try. I will never eat here again- horrible customer service. I am also going to send this review to the NY Times, Zagat, Immaculate Infatuation, Eater, and anyone else I can think of.

i absolutely love carbone. it's so old school NYC italian. the food and the service are just impeccable. my sister and i had such a good time, the waiter was so friendly and funny, he had us laughing every time he came over to our table. also, i must mention, i LOVE that there is no feeling of rush whatsoever at carbone. it's perfectly paced out and supposed to be a long enjoyable dining experience. they bring you a complimentary bread basket, cheese, and a cured meat. there are 3 different kinds of bread in the basket, all so good, my personal favorite is the tomato bread. the octopus appetizer is delicious, perfectly cooked and charred, some of the best octopus i've ever had. the spicy rigatoni vodka is a perfect dish, and so is the veal parm [its HUGE]. my grandparents from italy would even be proud, and they hate knowing i eat italian food anywhere other than their house. oh, don't let me forget the carrot cake & tiramisu - YUM! i can honestly say this was one of the best meals i've had in NYC. it's not cheap, but it's so worth it. my sister and i made a reservation a month in advance.

Had dinner here last night! The restaurant is a throw back to the Sinatra years!! The food was good but not great!! We started with an eggplant appetizer! Poor a tuna tartare, very good!, followed by a ceasar salad! Very good!! Then we had the rigatoni!! Very good! But ridiculously expensive for a tiny portion!!!!! Our entrees my shrimp dish , poor, fish special Dorado, very good , veal parm, good ! A side of broccoli rabe, over cooked and mushy!! Poor !! We had two bottles of wine as for tap water and was given flat!! Costly!! This restaurant is extremely expensive for what it offers !! The waiters were courteous!! Don't think I'll be back !!

I've been here once and I intend to come back again the next time I have plans in the area.  Its a bit pricey and the service is not the best I've seen but the food is delicious and flavorful.  

The last time I came here, I ordered the eggplant as a starter followed by the spicy rigatoni vodka and the meatballs. All were delicious but the spicy rigatoni vodka was my favorite.  Again, the place is a bit pricey so it does get overwhelming looking at the menu and its def a spot you go to for a special occasion . 

I didn't have dessert and just had an espresso which was delicious.

It seems that many of the complaints seem to focus on:

1. The prices. It's an expensive restaurant. Do not go expecting to find a bargain. There are plenty of restaurants in NY to get a great meal at a great price. This is not one of those places and I won't review it as such.

2. The service. My experience was positive the entire evening -- starting with the hostess, our waiter Marco and sommelier. Even the busboys were friendly and courteous. 

The waiter helped us sort through the menu and he split the dishes up for the four of us to share:

* baked clams (good, but the weakest dish of the evening), 
* octopus (delicious, I would have eaten a plate of it by myself).
* meatballs (excellent, perfect texture and amazing sauce)
* rigatoni (yes, it's as good as everyone says, have to try it)
* linguine with clams (I liked it as much as the rigatoni)
* veal parm (also as good as advertised; served with the bone to chew on too, don't be shy).

Two nice touches:

* the wine I wanted was sold out and the sommelier helped me find a delicious alternative in the same Roso di Montalcino group (these seem to be the best values IMO) and at the same price.

* one friend was observing no-meat Lenten Friday so the waiter brought him a half portion of the halibut while we heathens were eating the veal and meatballs.

If you want to splurge, this is a fun night out with really good food in a cool looking space. Probably a once a year visit, if I can even afford that!

Excellent, classic American-Italian food? Yes. Worth the insane prices they charge? Nah, not really. Chances of spotting celebrities you don't care about? 1:5 (Kim and Kanye were there, army of paparazzi outside the door). 

Decor, as has been said, is old school Italian and something out of a mob movie. They'll start you off with a few breads, some cured meats, and a nugget of Parmesan cheese. 

For the edibles, we went with:

Eggplant torrisi - the eggplant was really nice with layers of flavor and texture. The hand cut mozzarella is fine ... Better mozzarella out there. The eggplant is worth getting the dish though. 

Octopus - excellent dish. Perfectly roasted octopus with just a bit of tomatoes and peppers. Big fan. 

Spicy rigatoni - really nice pasta dish and the sauce is balanced with a subtle spice. As good as it was, $27 for pasta with nothing in it? Scarpetta spaghetti is better for less, and Marea has more satisfying and unique dishes for the same money. 

Veal parm - $58 veal parm. $58?!?! It's good, but not mind blowing, and for that price, it better the hell be the best veal I've ever had. It isn't. 

Total for all of the above plus 2 drinks came to $250 before tip. Just way, way too much money for what it was. Is it worth going to once? Yeah sure. Will I go back again? Not unless someone else is paying and going through the effort to make the reservation.

This is an overdue review - went to this restaurant a month ago.  I will say that I absolutely hate waiting weeks for a reservation and so I saw an open 6 pm reservation on Sunday morning for that evening and had an early dinner.  And so glad I did!  The moment you walk into Carbone, you are transported to New York circa 1955.  Everything from the music to the tablecloth makes you feel that you haven't just come to eat, but to be part of an elaborate, immersive dinner theatre.  Frank Sinatra is playing in the background and the waiters are humming and singing along- I literally am thinking to myself "are they required to do that to keep up the vibe?" Not sure but I loved every second.  On to the food- I had the spicy rigatoni vodka- amazing ! Bar non the best pasta dish I have ever had and it was so simple ! My friend had the tortellini al ragu - also very tasty.  But I would go back and order the rigatoni over and over again. I want to go back just for sheer entertainment / time transport value- the yummy food is a bonus.

My family and I came here for NYE dinner and it was honestly probably one of the best meals I've ever had. From hors d'oeuvres to appetizers to entrees to desserts, everything was delicious. 

From the get-go, we were served the freshest, most fragrant focaccia bread. Called Grandma's Bread, it was so good. We then got 5 hors d'oeuvres to split amongst the table. The Black Truffle Arancini, Tuna Toast, and Beggar's Purse were probably my favorites. The arancini was rich and creamy, with the lightest hint of black truffle. It was my first time having it and it was love at first bite. The Siberian Style Winter Point Oysters were also extremely fresh and Jonah's Cotechino was chock full of flavor. No complaints whatsoever.

For my antipasti, I picked the Carpaccio Piemontese because I can never say no to a good carpaccio. Topped with a generous helping of truffle oil and mushrooms, the carpaccio was one of the most delicious I've ever eaten. The beef was sliced so thinly and presented so beautifully--I could definitely eat this all day. 

I ordered the Lobster Ravioli Royale for my pasta. While I didn't love it as much as my carpaccio, I still enjoyed it quite a bit. Coated in a buttery sauce, the ravioli was stuffed with lobster meat. The dish itself also came with huge chunks of lobster accompanying the ravioli, which definitely made me happy, since I love lobster. A tad bit more rich than I like, but still delicious nonetheless. 

After hearing so many good things about the Rigatoni Vodka, I was so excited I was finally able to to try it. And I have to say, I was blown away. I've had my fair share of vodka pasta over the years, but there is no question that this Rigatoni Vodka is my favorite. Served in a creamy, spicy, absolutely decadent vodka sauce, the pasta was orgasmic. I also couldn't get enough of Mario's meatballs, which were not only huge, but also so flavorful. Again, no question that this was the best meatball I've ever eaten.

My choice for carne was quite easy, as I've been dying to try Carbone's Veal Parmesan for ages now. Served alongside the bone itself, the veal was so tender and delicious. As if there wasn't enough meat already, there was also so much on the bone too. I definitely could have gnawed on that thing for days. 

At this point, I was pretty sure I was going to die from a food coma, but I trudged through to dessert and even managed to have quite a few bites. We were given a Carrot Cake with Ginger Ice Cream, a Lemon Cheesecake, a Nutella Tiramisu, Chocolate Blackout Cake, Rainbow Cookies + Almond Turrons. The desserts were all decent, but I wasn't as blown away with them as I was with the rest of the meal. I probably enjoyed the tiramisu the most. 

I still cringe a bit when I think that that meal was $350 a person, but I have to say that it was definitely worth every single penny. I will definitely be back once my wallet recovers.

Excellent food - we ordered a steak for two and the waiter was nice enough to cart it over (we went one size down and didn't even manage to finish that). The service was great (understated, but I don't remember ever having an empty glass or dirty plate). 

Definitely closer to $$$$ than $$, but it also stands out as among the best steaks I've had - including Peter Lugar's in NYC and Ringside in PDX. Carbone's traditional Italian plates were excellent as well, and we enjoyed the old school atmosphere.

Prices are inflated, but the food is fantastic and certainly worth it for special occasions. Loved that as the night progressed the music went from oldies to hip hop. We got baked clams  (the ones with uni were great), caesar salad, sizzling panchetta, spicy rigatoni, linguini, chicken scarp, and the veal. Truly a spectacular meal but very pricey. When a place is able to take an experience to the next level, I'm ok with paying inflated prices, and Carbone was able to take it to the next level for me.

Overall: Would recommend to go, if you're willing to spend a lot for your dinner.

Ambiance: nice, layed back, not too noisy or too stuffy...

Appetizer
ctopus izzaiolo: very good quality, good flavor, tender...maybe not work $25 but still recommend to order

Mains
orteini al agu: This was amazing amazing...did half portion so $14 for 4 pieces...bit pricy for the quantity, but the quality was definitely there, from texture and flavor...it just melted in your mouth

ork hop  eppers: I normally don't order pork chop, but the waiter recommended it...the meat was very tender and good flavor...little bit on the salty side, but good for the price of $37...

Veal Parm...everyone raved about it, but when I saw the size you get for the price, not sure that it could be worth over $50!

Dessert
Carrot cake: I'm a big carrot cake fan...presentation was great...if you like ginger you will like this carrot cake. cake was moist, but the ginger flavor was a bit too strong for me, so for that reason I wouldn't order it again.

Overall, I quite enjoyed my experience at carbone. I like the ambiance, it is very easy, lay back, but with good energy. The food is very good, but not amazing. I really loved my appetizer octopus, that was the best dish among all dishes I had that night. Sizzling pancetta smelt so good but taste was a little bland, zuppa di pesce was good but nothing special. I skipped my desert because they just didn't look appealing, they looked cheap and not fresh.

Yes a bit expensive yes small yes tough to get a reservation but all the rest of complaints just don't get that New York vibe. Scallops delicious (raw) Carpaccio after a touch of lemon great rigatoni alla vodka great ribs great may not be on the menu. My only complaint was the Tiramisu  worst I've ever had. Wines pricey but delicious . Hope you have an expense account.

Over hyped in every way. The food is good, not great. The music is played so loud that conversation is difficult (we asked three times if they could turn it down). It's not a restaurant for conversation or catching up. It's a restaurant where you pay high prices for average food. The only special bite the clam with uni. Otherwise, I'd say go to little Italy. Really.

Great ambiance, service. Young guys who talk with Bronx accents, but the service is totally professional, and couldn't be more helpful. Host was awesome, made us feel like members of a club. You can't blame the staff, but the chef is another matter.

We had all their signature dishes. Where do I begin? The apps? Nothing stood out, but the baked clams were excellent... give them a 9 out of 10. Sizzling pancetta - grease and pork fat central, a strange starter, tired of it after two bites, give it a 6. Gratis house mozzarella - great. Give it a 9.  The spicy rigatoni? OK, absolutely nothing special. So mediocre I can barely remember it. 5 out of 10 The Capellini Aloilo? Any actual taste masked by the overabundance of pepper heat. The veal parm? A high-quality chop, flattened and doused with an unrefined tomato sauce and a dollop of cheese. Mat dry, flavor absent, a gigantic 3 from 1-10. The bone, included, had some juicy meat but was frankly greasy.The Scallops were good, plump, well cooked in a tasty creamy sauce - a lot more French/modern American than Italian. Give them an 8.5. But, the most amazing was the chicken scarpariello. This was an absolutely disgusting rendition, sickly sweet, with absolutely NOTHING to do with how a scarpariello should be made - balancing the acid of lemon with the fruit of white wine and depth of chicken broth in a tangy, elegant reduced sauce redolent with rosemary and garlic, the chicken crisped on the skin. At Carbone, you get a gloppy, red (peppers? tomatoes?) mess, the greasy skin sliding off the meat, repulsively sweet with no suggestion of vinegar or lemon to cut the cloying mess. This was like a bad cacciatore, not a scarpariello.
