I am still stunned by it, Scarpariello is my favorite dish in the world, and I've had it everywhere - from the departed Gino's and Elaine's, to every great Italian place in the City where, if it's not on the menu, I ask for it, and even in Italy, where it is not really known, but they understand the idea ("in the style of the shoemaker" - It takes time, but I'm willing to wait.) I cook it. My wife cooks it. I swear, my dog could probably cook it. It's really a simple dish at heart. But I'm telling you I have never had anything as awful as the "version" Carbone put on the table. 

I really wanted to like this place - it does so much right,, and has such a big rep. But, I'm sorry. In the end, this is a tourist trap, or maybe we just got unlucky with our choices or the night. I am stunned by the great reviews. Do you people actually know anything about Italian food, or go to the great Italian restaurants in this City?? Honestly, there is no justification for that scarpariello. Even if everything else had been totally awesome (which it was not) that big a fail means Kim, Kanye and the other celebs who go to a joint for the name can keep Carbone. And, by the way, I did not consider their prices outrageous, though the portions were a bit small, especially considering the great tradition of Little Italy "joints" where you used to take your shirt off before you ate, and the bowls and plates overflowed.
Like the 50s, 60s vibe in there with music and decor. Good was great. Meatballs. Pastas. All very good. Be prepared to pay 15-20% above what you would typically expect.

Four of us came here for dinner. Had a 9:15pm seating in the back room near kitchen. Couple of us were running late as usual so didn't get seated until later. The ambiance is traditional chic, average noisy for NYC and as down to earth as a "dressy" place can be. If you end up waiting, the bar quality is comparable to ZZ's (same group). Otherwise, straight into the extensive wine list. We had a full Barolo which worked really well with the rich dishes we ordered.

Overall: Excellent food and enthusiastic staff. Sommelier is knowledgeable as expected. Great to do family style. Not perfect but I will recommend, with no hesitation, to anyone looking for a great grandma's kitchen style Italian-American meal, if budget is not an issue.

Pro: The variety BREAD BASKET! Yes, the bread... and it's charcuterie/olive/spread accompaniments. Often overlooked because it's a spoiler if not properly managed but surprisingly a great appetite starter kit. I would go back just for the bread if it were the only thing left. SPICY RIGATONI VODKA! I can live on this. Hit all the right notes. It was slightly salty for my buds but it didn't take away from it's simple yet flavorful sauce. The pasta was cooked to the right al dente firmness. Chef Mario's MEATBALLS were excellent, just the right amount of juice. The TORTELLINI AL RAGU was most memorable for me and perhaps my favorite. It was full flavored, chewy and most importantly not fluid.

Con: Only feedback from the table was that the pasta and mains were slightly salty. The CHERRY PEPPER RIBS were not stellar but this criticism is coming from eating a lot of good ribs at rib specific joints, so take it with a grain of salt. Speaking of salt, yeah it was salty but the flavor was good. I would rather reserve the room for more pasta or other more traditional mains. If you're really keen on chowing a rib, the VEAL PARMESAN comes with one but not everyone can stomach the $60 price tag. Advance reservation but if you email them they usually will help to accommodate as best as they can. Call ahead to see if they have lasagna. Unfortunately it was not available on our night. 

With that said, you will enjoy dining here.

We went here tonight for dinner and truly enjoyed the food, service and ambiance. It is pricey but it's worth the experience. 
The complimentary breads were excellent- grandmas bread was doughy and the garlic bread was buttery and delicious. I ordered the octopus appetizer and was really impressed. It was cooked perfectly with the outside charred and the inside soft and moist. I had the linguine vongole as my main dish and it was out of this world. It was full of clams- those in shells and then a big spoonful of clam meat on top. My husband enjoyed the baked clams appetizer and was pleasantly surprised to learn they give 9 clams, cooked 3 different ways. Our favorite were the ones topped with uni. 
We enjoyed a delicious 2009 bottle of red wine from Veneto- can't recall the name but it was "Terra forte" maybe ? At $85 a bottle it was one of the least expensive wine options, and while I know you're supposed to have white wine with seafood, we very happy with this selection. The sommelier even said it was one of the hidden gems on the menu. We highly recommend this bottle. 
Our waiter reminded me of Christopher from the Sopranos, he was quite a character. The old school Italian ambiance transports you back in time to the 50s or a scene out of 'Goodfellas'- everything from the all male staff to the music, to the decor. The staff was very professional and very attentive. They sang and hummed along to the Music throughout service. It was a truly wonderful experience all around and we will return.

Amazing, worth the hype in every way.  Starting from the awesome garlic bread in the bread basket, its super greasy but so good.  
Get the caeser salad - I'm not even a fan of caeser salads but still thought it was delicious.  And like almost everyone else on yelp recommends, get the spicy rigatoni, make sure you get the side of meatballs, and then ofc the veal parm.  And ofc end the meal with the carrot cake!
I actually thought the service was great, wait staff was gracious and attentive, we went on a saturday night and had no complaints and was seated on time.

Carbone was a fantastic dining experience. The ambience, food and staff were amazing. We ordered the oysters, spicy rigatoni, meatballs, and the veal parm.  All the dishes were delicious. Wine recommendations were on-point.  When we left, our waiter was kind enough to wrap the left over veal parm and added a roll in order to make a sandwich for the lunch the next day. Great service, great food. We will return in the near future.

Wonderful experience! Great service, great food, great atmosphere. Can get a little noisy.

It's very small, and from the outside you won't be able to tell how good it is. But my frd recom me and told me that it's also recom to reserve a table a month in advance. She's right, it was a Monday night 5:30 and it's already packed.

They have free small tastings(cheese ham bread and picked cauliflower). And we had mussel and crab cake for appetizers. Amazing! The white wine that the server recommended me to pair the spaghetti with is also an excellent choice. They splitter the spaghetti into two plates for me and my mom so we didn't hv to struggle.

Love it and will suggest anyone who has a little spare money to swag to eat here! The average is about $100 per person.

So, i have been two times to Carbone and both were disastrous. This restaurant group is capable of much better things such as Santina but that spot gets the Michelin star which i do not understand.

The atmosphere is weird. It is that pseudo-italian that strives so much to be old school but it can not pull it off, rather it comes of as gaudy.

Menu is ok, but nothing authentic. Has the nuts and bolts of italian cuisine such as a huge veal parm and some pastas and meatballs and burrata and some desserts -such as a nice tiramisu, a good carrot cake, a non-impressive chocolate cake all served with ice cream- but they do not have a dessert menu which is weird.

I would recommend trying a pasta and a dessert or an appetizer, since the portions of pasta are rather small. The main dishes are to the contrary quite large and the taste does not impress -although you can have a veal parm and do it 3-way it depends on what you are in for.

They bring you some nice focaccia and olive oil to start with your meal, which is good but again nothing too impressive for a michelin starred place. 

Drink menu should be better. Carbone is supposed to be italian do not forget and the choices are extremely limited, even more so than torrisi -which used to be everything but flexible, but i will give them a pass since it used to feel authentic at least.

The service is not very good and attentive. They usually make you wait too much and there is a good chance you can be ignored or worse. Which makes me question why this place exists again.

Try Parm, definitely try Santina but beware of Carbone at all costs!

I'm torn, for me, this place is really 3.5 stars. I had a great time, but a few things short it from being a 4.

The wins...
The bread basket - so good.
The carrot cake was INSANE. I was skeptical of ordering carrot cake in an Italian restaurant, and even more skeptical when it came to the table looking all architectural (I am rarely impressed with desserts that look like sculpture), but HOLY COW...it was incredible. We had also ordered the tiramisu, and STILL ordered a second piece of the carrot cake. We were all in agreement that it was that good.
Spicy rigatoni vodka - I enjoyed it, but it wasn't mind-blowing

The meh
The scampi appetizer, my brother loved it, I was less into it. There was a lot of critter on the plate, not my jam. I was willing to overlook that for flavor, but it wasn't memorable.
We ordered a few salads, I don't even remember what - so that tells me everything.

No outright fails, but the service was tricky...it was a win and a fail. 
We had an old-school waiter, who clearly brings personality to the table (pun intended)...but for all the pomp and circumstance, the service wasn't actually that great. 

My brother had waited for me at the bar, and got a cocktail...when I arrived we were sat at a table. We waited probably about 10 minutes before being given menus, and when he came to give us our menus, he swiped my brother's unfinished cocktail off the table. It wasn't empty. My brother didn't notice right away, and I said "were you done with that?" He said he wasn't, and kinda shrugged. It's not tragic, but at about $18 a pop...ASK before removing. 

When we didn't order wine right away he took away the wine list, even though we were just trying to decide what we wanted food-wise before picking a wine. The service was style before substance.

We had fun, they've nailed the vibe they are going for, the food was good, but not memorable. Loved the music...the crooner hits you'd expect to be playing in a nice Italian chophouse in the 1950s.

Sidenote - seated at the next table was Vito Schnabel - the art dealer/collector, who curated the art in the restaurant.

It's a fun night out.

Hands down, this is one of the top five fine dining Italian experiences I won't soon forget. Each table is served pickled cauliflower, cubed Parmesan, peppered Salami and a bread basket with tomato focaccia, and the worlds best buttery garlic bread. All that and we hadn't even ordered the first course. The chopped salad served our whole group along with a grilled shrimp app which was cooked to perfection and definitely a wild caught flavor.  The entrees were each perfection from the homemade tortellini, delicate little pillows with light whipped filling over ragu alla Bolognese; linguine and clams with the perfect balance of garlic, parsley and sauce to the Veal Parmesan. Our table also shared a side of charred green beans and while more Asian than Italian with crushed peanuts were delicious. The lemon ricotta cheesecake is seriously making me consider flying back to the city next month, accompanied by coffee brewed authentically in a Moka pot, nothing was flawed in this meal. Be prepared to spend worth every penny.

Also we loved the transition from classic Italian music to Drake at 11:30pm perfect vibe

My eyes bulged out of their sockets when I saw the prices at this joint. I couldn't believe some of their appetizers -- $45 for a sliver of sautéed foie gras (rich, slightly over-salted, a little small), $51 for scampi alla scampi (a few measly langoustines), or $19 for a salad ("normal food," as my friend put it). 

Carbone attempts to recreate classic New York Italian red sauce joint, and they do with some of their entrees, but I didn't feel my heart pounding out of my chest when I left*. The zuppa di pesce was a little spicy and rich with flavor, but for $49 I would expect more than a single scallop, a lonely shrimp, and one dissected squid. They aptly supplemented my entree with four pieces of toast, knowing that the food they gave me was about enough to feed a large cat. We also ordered a pasta dish for ~$30 (again, "normal food") and the cherry ribs ($36) which proved to be the exception: surprisingly jumbo-sized and very fatty.

But for the price (the bill for three was ~$500 -- we ordered a single bottle of wine and some cocktails), the quality of the food certainly doesn't match up. I'd rather spend that money on a trip to Paris.

*Well maybe after I saw the check.
Good food, good service, but overpriced. Hard to spend less then $ 100 to $150 a person.

Really enjoyed the atmosphere, our waiter Ricky and overall experience. Food was very good. Veal was way above average. Actually a class all to itself. Would go back in an instant to try other dishes.

We dined last night at Carbone.  We had to make the reservation a few weeks in advance but wanted to get in on this date to celebrate my daughter's birthday. The place is very busy, noisy and a little cramped - especially if more than a couple of people are trying to check in at the same time. Once we were seated it was fine.  Loved the Sinatra music being played.  A charming man (don't recall his name - I think he said he goes by AA?) came over to welcome us and take a drink order. The prices are over the top but I had checked the menu before arriving so it did not shock me.  They brought over delicious bread, pickled cauliflower, some sort of prosciutto and cheese for the table.

He then reviewed the menu with us and explained it's meant for sharing. He told us what some his favorites were including some seafood dishes and the meatballs...he offered to get the meatballs started for us and put those in first.  We placed our order for 3 people - Caesar salad, Tortellini al Ragu, Spicy Rigatoni Vodka, Chicken Massimo, Mario's Meatballs.  We asked if he thought that was enough and he said if you order a side that would be perfect...we selected the Charred String Beans. (Note about the string beans - there is no description on how these are prepared and they came out covered in crushed peanuts which was ok but would not be for someone with a peanut allergy.)

He actually said "I am excited about your order"!  The salad came first, then the 2 pastas and then the chicken and string beans.  With each course new plates and silverware are laid down.  Overall portions are very small but high quality.  As we were eating the chicken and string beans we inquired with Mr. Charming about our meatballs. Within a couple of minutes another gentleman came over to inform us they had run out of meatballs. He apologized profusely and offered us complimentary dessert.  We were really disappointed and said ok...but honestly were still hungry.  

Then we saw an order of meatballs delivered to the table across from us!!  We called Mr. Charming over to see why the other table were served meatballs when we were seated and ordered before them and were told they had run out.   He suddenly tried to make it seem like we didn't order them in the first place!  The other gentleman that had offered the dessert came back over - apologized profusely and said he should not have made it seem like we didn't order them.
Mr. Charming never put our order in and it would have been better if he would have just admitted he made a mistake.  They should have offered us another meat entrée - not dessert - we were hungry.  We declined dessert.  They ended up removing the string bean charge. 

Meatball-gate as I am now calling it really ruined our night and the joyous feeling we had when we got there.

Carbon from the outside is unassuming.  The sign that hangs outside makes it appear as if it's been there for 50 years.  It's no different inside either, from the waiters in maroon tuxedo jackets and the classic tunes that are played throughout.  There is no doubt you are transported back in time and the menu follows suit. 

We went on a Saturday night and nabbed an early reservation.  The restaurant was busy with the early seating.  It's small and cozy although your tables are very close to one another.  I'm never a fan of this, but in NYC it's a serious trend.  The waiters were prompt with our menus and it only took us a few minutes to decide.  He was helpful with suggestions and gave us a few guidelines.  

Now the food, it's very good Italian American food.  I'm Italian American and like to think my opinion matters.  We settled on baked clams, which come 3 different ways, oreganata, casino and ginger with scallion and sea urchin.  I wanted to love these so much, but there was sand in most of the clams. I didn't tell the waiter although maybe with such a high price tag I should have.  We shared the spicy rigatoni vodka.  I almost never order this out but Carbone does it justice and makes it right.  The pasta had a great texture.  I'm going to assume they were freshly made because I never had dried rigatoni with such a great texture.  It was a bit salty, but the flavors were definitely on point.  Lastly we shared the Veal Parmigiana which is for two.  It was really good.  The veal was super tender and was worth every penny.  As a side the creamed escarole was awesome and something I had never tried before.  I was pretty stuffed but being my birthday and all I had to get a piece of cake.  Carrot cake is the way to go.  It was superb.  

All in all I really liked Carbone and would return.  Call for reservations 1 month in advance.

The food is delicious and I'm glad I tried it once, but as other reviews have noted, it's a poor value. At $64 for a veal parmesan, my expectations were very high. The result was pretty good, but probably not worth the price tag. Spicy rigatoni was excellent, as was the octopus antipasti. Carrot cake was great as well. In terms of the service, it seems hit-or-miss. Our server was polite, but not all that attentive and each dish took forever to come out. Credit is due for excellent food, but at this price point, I've definitely had better dining experiences.

Sometimes when you hear to much about a restaurant your let down.... Not the case at Carbone. First, I was greeted by a handsome refined looking Ben Affleck looking guy, He must have gone to some university for refinement and a gangster if you will coolness, with his personality plus. He made us feel welcome. Service is insane... They're  on there game. We started with fresh buffalo mozzarella and grilled bread and Salumi .... Delicious, our Cesar salad arrived freshly tossed at the table bursting with wonderful flavor...  While Waiting for our second course nostalgic music is playing in the background further completing this amazing atmosphere .. Our food arrives ... Service continues to be impeccable Meatballs to die for ... 
Pasta arrives al dente flavorful penne spicy vodka sauce I'm in heaven now... Carbone lives up my expectations and then some.... I'm in love!!!!
Tortellini al Ragu was absolutely amazing. The Ragu sauce and the ricotta filling was very good. Octopus plate was great. Overall an great experience and I would return.

If you haven't be to il Mulino, you may believe that Carbone is the best Italian that NYC has to offer. While it definitely ranks high, but il Mulino still holds #1 in my heart (& stomach!) 

Portions are smaller than il Mulino but priced higher. If that doesn't bother you, let's move on. 

- The waiter was incredibly polite and pleasant! 5 stars here. 

- Garlic bread: delish & also had a pizza-esque bread...also very good. 4 stars here only because the garlic bread at il Mulino is a touch better. 

- they bring out some complimentary cheese & salami -- nice touch, but again, il Mulino does so with much more generosity than seen at Carbone. 3.5 stars. 

Appetizers:
We shared ceasar salad (it was ok-Wolfgang's is better!) and meatballs. The meatballs were the BEST part of this meal. Absolutely PERFECT with just a sprinkle of cheese and delicious, rich, red sauce. EXCELLENT. 5 stars. 

On to the meal... we shared: 
- Veal parm: delicious even as a left over!! 
- Veal milanese: same as the parm without the cheese. 
- Swordfish: this was a special, very good. lightly cooked and served atop vegetables. 
- Spicy Rigatoni Vodka: also delicious, if you can't handle spice, probably not for you. (They charged us $81 for about a fist full of pasta per person -- 6 people total) 

Overall meal: 4 stars. 

Had a good time and enjoyed the meal. Would be willing to come back, but would likely make reservations at il Mulino first :)

Nice atmosphere, cool vibe, attentive service, good food.  But $64 for veal parm?  Really???  There are a number of places in NYC serving equally good or better Italian/American food for 1/4 to 1/3 the price.   If you're a hedge fund manager or a rich tourist who doesn't know any better, you'll probably love it. Otherwise, look elsewhere.  I can't complain about the food or the experience, but I'm just not into paying $275 per person for baked clams, penne a la vodka, veal parm, a low end bottle of Barolo and some carrot cake.  I'm not going to say where I go to get the same meal for $80, because I don't want to compete with Carbone's clientele to get on a wait list to eat there.  But I assure you, these places still exist in NYC, and have been putting out similar food for decades with no hype, publicists, or Michelin stars.

There's a reason Carbone is on every top ten list. Quintessential old school Italian menu done to the most sophisticated culinary standards. Ambiance from old time NY. Everything was best in class- even the traditional chopped salad was amazing. Pastas, perfect veal Marsala, incredible perfectly prepared branzino and Dover sole (ok- we ordered everything). Service so attentive but not hovering . . . And did we mention President Obama at the next table? (Maybe they knew we were Yelp reviewers ;-) )

Food was decent but definitely not the quality and flavored I expected after reading the reviews and talking with friends. The highlight of the meal was honestly the bread and cheese they serve you to start. Cocktails were only eh.

Rarely does a restaurant live up to it's hype, Carbone does. I love the food here. My third visit was on Friday night. The street was closed off. Secret Service frisked me. Why? Obama was sitting two tables away from me. Normally, I don't like my politicians to eat south of 57th street but I'll make an exception. 

The Food:

Baked clams 3 types, Original, Sea Urchin, Casino. The Clams casino was probably the only dish i've didn't  like there, ever.

Octopus - Very good

Spicy Rigatoni - Amazing

Veal Parm - Amazing

Porterhouse - Very good BUT it was m/p and if I knew that meant $200, I wouldn't have ordered it.

Dessert - pretty good.

Heitz Cellar Cabernet is my new favorite wine ($135)

All in all, 4 people, $1000. Not cheap, BUT, I spoke to a US president and had amazing food. 

Looking forward to going back for a 4th time.
Thoroughly disappointed with this overhyped restaurant. Everything was just ok - not memorable.

Had a very enjoyable meal here. Prices are over the top but regardless if you can get pass this you will really enjoy this place. Started with tomatoes and a burrata/mozz that was incredible. Followed with meatballs that were very good. After that had a very light tortellini stuffed with cheese that was very good. Followed with the highly recommended veal parm that was just ok and cherry pepper ribs that were outstanding but ridiculously fatty.

All in all great place but you will have to slide with their over the top pricing. Highly recommend this place.
Awesome experience. Took a few clients out for an amazing dinner. Everything was fantastic. A little tight at the bar area, but nothing that hindered the experience.

I was initially dreading such an early dinner reservation after a humid day and a late lunch, but everything changed as soon as I walked in the door. Carbone exudes a classy authentic charm that totally swept me off my feet. The service here runs like a well oiled machine. The staff excels at what they do with a cheeky sense of humor in true New York style. The ambiance, service, and complimentary starters (specifically that chunk of Grana Pradano cheese and garlic toast) blew me away.  

Definitely get the caprese (if available) and the spicy rigatoni pasta and the meatballs. Those three dishes are on another level. Seriously who knew a simple caprese could look and taste so fine? The spicy rigatoni in vodka sauce surpassed the hype. Meatballs were also superbly tender. 

Unfortunately I was too full to truly enjoy the veal parm since I was not hungry to begin with, and the caesar salad and the carrot cake did not impress, but the rest of my night at Carbone was so fabulous, that two days later and from over 2500 miles away, I can still taste how comforting and delicious it was. I totes get why the First Lady loved it so much, she came back with her man within a week. I would so return for another inconveniently early or late dinner here. Expect $100 per person give or take with a drink.

Have been here many times and it's currently my favorite restaurant in NYC.  Was there 2 days ago for lunch and had the ribs (amazing) and the Dover Sole, which was disappointing.

That being said, I LOVE this place!

Over hyped. The food is no where near the prices they charge. Claims to be old school authentic but its anything but. I don't understand the reviews but if you look at the clientele it will explain. 

The waiter ordered for me and claimed the caprese salad is the best in the city. More oil than tomatoes. My wifes caesar salad wasnt horrible but over dressed and incredibly peppered croutons that were inedible. We ordered the ravioli but they ran out. The side corn dish was great but so random for an italian restaurant. Lastly the $64 veal parmasian. Punded breaded fried with no seasoning and some cheese. Olive Garden could do better. $64?

The restaurant is loud and the wait staff and hostess are very average. I didn't get this on a bad night. Don't believe the hype. There are plenty of restaurants to choose from and better prices.

The best Caprese salad I've ever had -- fresh, warm mozzarella on delicious heirloom tomatoes OMG it was awesome!  The bread was lovely, the amuse bouche too, and the truffled corn was out of this world.  A giant and delicious veal parmigiana had to be enjoyed over time, as I was too stuffed to eat all that, but it even came with a bone.  I can see why it was hard to get a reservation, but we will be back.  Also, in contrast to another restaurant lately, I was dining alone and got exceptional service and kindness (the caprese was a recommendation) that made me feel very welcome and pampered:)

Food was quite good.  No complaints there at all.  But patrons need to be aware of the behavior of the servers (at least our server) that appears to be tolerated by the owners of Carbone.  We were actually advised to look closely at our bill before it came.  At the time, we were not sure what exactly that meant.  At the end of the evening, when we received our bill, the reason for the warning was very clear.  We ordered 2 bottles of very nice wine and were charged for 3.  We ordered one octopus appetizer and were charged for 2.  We had 2 bottles of water and were charged for 3.  And when we brought this to the attention of our server he was not at all apologetic, didn't seem surprised and didn't hesitate to correct it.  It appeared he took a chance.  He was caught.  It didn't seem to faze him at all.  He had the "you win some, you lose some" attitude.  It was clear to us, based on the fact that we were warned before hand, and based on his reaction when we brought it to his attention, that this is a routine of his, that I suspect he gets away with quite often. It is egregious, it is stealing and IT IS NOT OK.  Patrons deserve much better.  Please be warned.  If you chose to go, look very closely at your bill before you pay.

Don't believe the hype. This Restaraunt is terrible.
Pros
*BreadBasket with spicy garlic bread.
*Beautiful crowd.

Cons
*Unfriendly hostess 
*Unfriendly Bartender who kept slamming the shaker on the bar. Very small bar that has NO stools and can only fit 6 people standing up. We felt strange standing there as it is blocking the hallway from the dining room to the kitchen. 
*Very small space with tables on top of each other. We could hear everybody's conversation next to us which was that all the food was too salty.
*Waiter unfriendly and bossy.
*Chipped plates.(waiter said that is how their supposed to be.)
*Never served us the complimentary Cheese that he said was coming out.
*They were out of Shrimp at 9:00pm on Friday night.
*$64 Veal Chop Parm was terrible. Almost no sauce or cheese on it and dry. Campagnola or Il Mulino is 100% better for this type food.
*My wife sent her Bass back to be made more well done and it didn't come back for 20 minutes. I was done with my dinner by then. Ruined our Anniversary dinner.
*Ordered chocolate cake for dessert and was served Black Forest Cake which we didn't like.
*Overcharged for an extra glass of wine we never ordered. Apparently they do this as standard procedure as many other reviewers have stated. The place should be investigated for criminal activity.

We were so disappointed and don't understand why this place is so highly rated. People who know high quality NYC Italian food would never come here twice. Off my bucket list.

Everything I had here was ABSOLUTELY DELICIOUS!!! I came here by myself for lunch and the food was EXCELLENT. The wait staff was incredibly friendly and hospitable. The garlic bread was the best I've ever eaten in my life!!! It's tough to get normal reservations during dinner time! Good news they're open late but book early to find desired times

Food like this is a staple of New York City's restaurant business. My entire day was a blur, but time stopped when I came to this venue. My friends and I completely stopped talking, except to smile and say how amazing the food was. Until you've tasted the amazing taste of Carbone you haven't had food.

I've dined many times at modern restaurants, however fancy it could be and I'm already kind of tired of fanciness and needed some sort of old-fashion style. Yep that is exactly Carbone could bring you the second you stepped in.

King crab was their specialty for the day as appetizer, meat was so soft, chewy and juicy! We skipped the meatball, as we were too concerned about its huge size, however it seemed like we were making a wrong decision...essentially skipping any of the course would be a big miss! Garlic bread was exceeding my expectation by a large margin. The linguini vongole was probably the best I have ever tried, with a strong flavor of spice however not overwhelming at all. Last but not least, if you are still hungry yet don't want to be bombed by the large size of meat ball, go for the shrimp (with basil sauce)! Can not be more satisfied! Friendly reminder, the cocktail named Manhattan is like the real Manhattan...dessert was always the best part, as there was an old saying - girls born to have two stomachs, one for food and one for dessert. So true!

Very nice experience, would recommend this Michelin one-starred restaurant!

Wouldn't come back. For $120 per head I would rather take my money elsewhere. Ordered shrimp scampi and totally not fresh. And service is terrible!! Totally echo the other posts about arrogant and bossy waiters. If you are going to pretend to be an upscale restaurant, at least train your waiters to be respectful, not singing while your customer is tasting wine and spilling water over your customer because you are distracted and trying to act cool. There are lots of other upscale restaurants I would rather spend my $120.
This is my new favorite restaurant in NYC. We had an incredible meal. Everything we ate was outstanding. Great recommendations from the waiter. We have been raving about it every since.

I came here Sunday night to celebrate a friends engagement. This was our third time visiting Carbone. I must start by saying that the food was excellent. Everything we ate was delicious. However, the service was terrible and therefore I didn't give it 5 stars. When you dine in such an establishment you expect top service, especially since we all know it is nearly impossible to get a reservation. Our waiter was rude and tried to up sell us like crazy. We asked him to help us figure out how much food we would need to order (two couples) and he kept on getting annoyed when we wouldn't take his suggestion. He wrote things down that we didn't even ask for and when I told him to cancel it he got angry. At the end he ended up suggesting 3 appetizers, 2 pastas and 2 entrees. We agreed and ordered. It was way too much food and we couldn't finish it all. When the bill came I noticed that they charged us for 4 pastas (2 of each) when we only ordered 1 because we wanted to share everything. I pointed this out to him and he said "THIS IS HOW WE DO IT HERE". Even though the food is great I will have to think if I want to visit again. There are plenty of high end Italian restaurants in NYC that treat you way better. Ex: Il Mulino.

I finally was able to make a reservation for a Saturday night at 7:30. First when entering the restaurant we were seated in the first room where the tables are on top of each other we asked to be moved and were re-seated in the "back" room which was much nicer and more comfortable. We ordered the Caprese salad, zuppa de mussels,spicy rigatoni all a vodka ,and the veal parmesan for the 2 of us to share, The caprese salad was the best we ever had the most delicious tomatoes (it is the perfect time of the year for tomatoes) and an excellent homemade burratta still warm. When did you ever have zuppa de mussels and not want to dip a loaf of bread in the sauce, well this was our first time, The mussels are made with ground sausage and very little sauce. The mussels were fine but the dish was very disappointing. The rigatoni was good with a little kick. The veal came out, its big but not as big as some people make it out to be. Its about the size of the plate, but pounded very thin.
The waiter cut it into 4 or so sections and gave us each 1 to start. We could barely finish the first piece he gave us since it was so salty it was inedible. When they came to clear the table and saw how much we left over they asked if there was a problem, we told them about how salty it was, they said had we told them they would have made another one, but they did take it off our bill, which for $64 i would hope so, for $64 it should never have come out the way it did in the first place. We were willing to pay their prices, but quite honestly based on my experience there are much better restaurants for the money and much much better Italian food.

Every dish we ordered was phenomenal! We started with the octopus, moved onto the spicy rigatoni, and ordered the halibut and ribs for entrees. Bananas foster prepared table side was delicious also also a fun experience. Noise level was a little high for my liking and drinks were extremely expensive, but overall Carbone provided us with a lovely anniversary dinner!

Wow wow WOW. hands down best pasta i've ever had. got the spicy rigatoni and the meatballs, both were melt-in-your-mouth insane. getting a reservation can be difficult, i walked in and ate at 10pm but well worth the wait.  service was amazing, our server sal was the best, gave us some great wine recommendations and had us smiling the entire time.  also i assumed prices would be exorbitant but they are absolutely not, all reasonably priced similar to any nice nyc restaurant, but the food is so much better. i dream of their pasta every night now. definitely recommend!

Lives up to the hype...especially for a celebration.

Carbone is not cheap but despite all the hype somehow still manages to live up to expectations.  It is a lively space with lots of staff eager to help you have a good experience. The loud festive music was a little unexpected, but definitely contributed to the upbeat atmosphere.  They brings lots of complimentary bites to begin the meal. The menu is relatively traditional with a few twists.

The Ceasar salad is prepared in the dining room which is nice but I wouldn't get it again. It was overpriced for what it was and I didn't love the anchovy-heavy flavor of the dressing.

The spicy rigatoni was really remarkable and pleasantly spicy but nothing too hot.  I would definitely get this again and I see why it is a specialty of theirs.

The shrimp entree was not at all what I expected based on the description by the waiter and sadly was also not good.  The shrimp were cooked well but the flavor was really weird and sour and not pleasant at all.  Not to mention $44 for 6 normal sized shrimp seems over priced.

The corn side was pretty amazing.  I imagine they rotate sides with the season but this definitely gives me confidence in their ability to cook some great vegetables.

We also split the lemon cheesecake which was tangy and delicious with a great crust.

Overall a wonderful meal and a great place for a special occasion as they clearly focus on quality service.

I came here with my husband for our anniversary after hearing some good reviews from our friends. It is definitely a pretty ambiance and great for people watching. The food was solid but I don't think we made the right choices in everything we ordered.

The staff was polite although we never received a wine menu which was odd. We ordered a tuna tartar to start with the octopus. I have to say that both were just ok. I wish we would have ordered the carpaccio and caprese (the people around us ordered these dishes and they looked delish!). For pasta we ordered the spicy rigatoni vodka which was amazing and one of their most popular (if not the most popular) dish on their menu. We also ordered the franco bolli royale which we did not like AT ALL. The way the dish was described did not truly reflect the execution. My husband and I do not love scallops and this dish was basically a thin ravioli stuffed with scallops, way too heavy for our taste. I wish the waiter would have told us the dish was mainly scallops (it felt like the dish was being pushed on us too much). For the last course we ordered the veal parm and potatoes, both were great. 

Overall the experience was good and we will go back but will not get talked into ordering expensive dishes without asking more questions about it. A total miss on our part that served as a lesson for future restaurant visits.

What a waste.

Service: My husband and I had a 9:45 reservation. We arrived at 9:40ish and was told that it would be a 5-10 minute wait. Excellent, we thought. 10pm rolls around and nothing. At about 10:10, someone comes up to my husband with wine and says that someone told him that it was his birthday. It wasn't his birthday, so that was confusing. Finally, at 10:15, we are taken to a table. No one apologized for the wait.

During the dinner, my water glass was frequently empty and it took forever for them to refill it. Additionally, the entrees were basically flung onto the table and the server disappeared. No one came to check on us until we had mostly finished.


Food: We ordered the octopus and caprese salad to start. The octopus was fine, but nothing special. The caprese salad was wonderful, however. Our mains were the spicy rigatoni vodka and steak Diana. The steak was fantastic. Best steak I've had in a long time. I really didn't enjoy the rigatoni, as the spiciness overwhelmed any sort of flavor. For dessert, we split the carrot cake. Very good.

TL:DR - Terrible service (long wait, not attended to). Food was hit or miss.

This place is incredibly overpriced and overhyped. My husband and I ordered the porterhouse for 2 which was $200. It was burnt on the outside and undercooked on the inside. No sure how that's possible given the price tag. We also ordered the potatoes which were good and different, but nothing super impressive. I will say that the glass of wine I had was perfection (it's no longer on the menu). The tiramisu was quite underwhelming. Service was okay and the atmosphere was enjoyable. But overall don't bother spending the cash because there are too many great restaurants in NYC for A LOT less.

Waited over an hr to be seated for our on time reservation.Ok I get that its a hot spot sure Ill suck that one up...BUT
 Horrible by the glass Champagne/Wine selection.
 Very mediocre food and DEFINITELY NOT  worth the prices. Over Hyped and under delivered my opinion. Im Italian myself and can say without a doubt BICE on 54th kicks its butt in every way!
 Staff was satisfactory  Bartender was the most cordial of all.
If you like very simple, bland southern Italian food at high prices this is the spot!
Each dish had its own unique taste and was amazing with every bite the service was outstanding! Enriqo was the BEST!

The best mussels zuppe out there !!!! big dish , so good !!!
Excellent rigatoni in spicy vodka sauce 
And to finish ,a clean not that sugary and sweet cheese cake.
Very recommended Italian .
Fantastic service as you can expect from those "old style" Italian places .
Not that cheap , but worth every cent .

We have been huge fans of Carbone for many years.  Perhaps they have allowed their Michelin rating to go to their heads.  Although the food was as delicious as ever, it was as though they had hired the cast of Jersey Shore to run the restaurant for the evening.  Only the bus boys seemed the least bit interested in serving the patrons shelling out $500 for their meals.  The "head" wait staff were too busy checking instagram on their cell phones, or running out for smokes, or counting their tip money, to even bother bringing the wine menu, making dinner suggestions, or presenting the bill in a timely fashion.  Even the overhead music was pathetic.  We will never be going back, and we hope for the sake of the food being served that the management find a way to restore some class to the establishment.

It felt like a theme restaurant - but fun. "I'll take care of you guys - it's a beautiful thing" said our smiling waiter as he told us to get the Scampi Alla Scampi which was market price. When our 4 pieces of mediocre shrimp arrived we shrugged and ate them. The shrimp was 74.00, WHAT!? Grossly overpriced for what it was. We liked the rigatoni with vodka. Overall, a $400.00 semi-authentic meal for two - with waiters who seemed like actors. The tourists will eat this one up - but native New Yorkers know good Italian and for that price it better be amazing!

I would give this place six stars if I could. I have heard about this place for years and I finally made it. The staff is awesome and I love the servers in their burgundy tuxedos. There is a small bar in in the back as you walk in and the decor is awesome. 

We were a party of eight and the server suggested we do family style and we ordered a lot. The cheese to start, the rigatoni, lobster ravioli and the meatballs had me right away. the food was so good. I plan on adding photos soon. 

I highly suggest coming here and having the awesome meal that I enjoyed. I will 100% be back.

I came here with my husband to celebrate our anniversary and it was a fantastic choice.  From the old school Italian vibe to the incredibly attentive service, we enjoyed every second. 

First off, the menu is HUGE.  Not the options inside, but the physical menu is just SO BIG! I'm not really sure why, but was just funny trying to come up with a reason for why they would want to make the menu so incredibly large!  Definitely appreciated the art featured on the menu and on the to-go bag which seemed like it was made for Carbone exclusively.  

Before we even placed our order, so much food came out! 
- Bread basket - tomato bread (FANTASTIC, left me wanting more), regular bread, and garlic bread (way too hard, not my favorite)
- Fresh cheese cut straight from a parmesan wheel 
- Pickled cauliflower, delicious 
- Salami 

Then came our order: 
- Baked Clams - must get! This was delicious.  3 different flavors came out with this: herbs, bacon & cheese, uni.  All were so good but uni and herbs were the standout personally. 

- Funghi Fettucine - Pretty clear that the pasta is made in house.  However I couldn't tell if it was the nature of the pasta or if it was just over cooked; but the texture of the pasta was too soft for my liking.  Flavor was good, but softness of the pasta threw me off. 

- Truffle Corn - AMAZING.  This is an absolute must-get.  I could have eaten a whole bowl of this and been happy. 

- Veal Parmesan - Sauce to cheese ratio was excellent.  Sauce was also not overly acidic or too sweet, it was just right. 

- Carrot cake for dessert - came with ginger ice cream.  Presentation was excellent but actual cake was too dry.  Probably wouldn't order this again. 

We had enough leftovers for 1 lunch the next day.  When we opened up the boxes we were pleasantly surprised that they had given us a loaf of sesame bread which very, very good.  

Great spot for intimate dinner with friends our spouse.

It only gets one star because the food was absolutely delicious.  However, the service was so incredibly terrible it was embarrassing. Our party really wanted to like it here and went in looking forward to having a great meal. However, the service was so abysmal that our whole experience was ruined.

The hostess was unhelpful and almost rude when making us wait for our table after our scheduled reservation time. This would have been fine but waiting at the bar was impossible because it was already too cramped. We ended up in an awkward space where all of the waiters were walking through with food.

When we were finally seated, it literally took half an hour for someone to come over and ask us if we wanted to order drinks. Someone in our party had to literally ask the waiter if we could order drinks.  Ordering dinner was much the same. When the waiter finally came to take our dinner order, we asked for a recommendation and he pushed the caprese salad. We told him that someone in our party did not eat tomato, and asked for another suggestion. He responded that he'd just bring a big ball of mozzarella. We told him to forget it.

Our pasta course came in an appropriate amount of time and we all had the spicy rigatoni which was delicious. Then, we waited, what felt like an eternity for the entrees.

My entree was finally placed on the table and none of the others were served.  We asked if the other entrees were being served and we were pretty much blown off.  After about three minutes, we asked again, and again we were promptly blown off.  Finally, approximately 10 minutes after my entree was put on the table, the other entrees were served.  Mine was cold by then.  No one apologized or seemed to care that this had happened.

The food was good, but we all walked away from the experience feeling like we had been treated terribly because we were not some celebrity or high-roller.  The food is decent, but for the price point, there are many many better options in New York City.  Don't waste your money here.

The T Bone steak for 2 was $200 and the chewiest pice of meat I have had at any restaurant, price aside it was almost inedible. Also had veal Marsala which was a chewy veal chop sliced off the bone with mushrooms.  That was also tough. Pasta was delicious and I should have just stayed with that. Lots of fanfare, crowded and noisy.  Hardly space to even walk to the restroom through all the tables and people standing at the tiny bar.

I LOVE the Carbone/ Torrisi/ Zalaznick restaurants. This was a great anniversary pick. The decor is Goodfellas chic: close, cozy white tableclothed tables, dark panel (great artwork, though), Frank Sinatra on the stereo, large waiters and a lot of old school dishes.  We were advised to get appetizers AND pasta AND entrees but honestly, the portion sizes are really big. Appetizers and pasta would have been fine--we had a big doggie bag at the end. Food was delicious.

Quite possibly the best Italian food in NYC. There's a real old New York vibe inside, which is nice. The staff are super friendly and helpful, not hoity toity at all. We started with the octopus pizzaiolo which was really good. The spicy rigatoni vodka was actually a little spicy, and the angel hair AOP was super thin and tasty. The scallops were cooked just right and the cherry pepper ribs were delicious. Perhaps the stunner of the night was the corn tartufato, which the waiter recommended we get, and we're glad we listened. They're strongly flavored with truffle oil, and who doesn't love that? I'd love to come back again and again, if only my wallet would allow.

Simply delicious! I dined here on a Friday night at 7pm and I lucked out in getting that reservation time because I haven't been able to get a decent one since. Thanks a lot, Clooney! This place was pricy so my boyfriend and I each decided to order a dish and split them. Of course, we got the veal parmesan and spicy vodka rigatoni. 

The decor is old-school and classic. Don't expect a trendy restaurant if it's your first time coming here. Also, the tables are spaced VERY closely together, so much so that you pray that you don't bump the table next to you when squeezing out from the booth side.

The only major complaint I have it that I enjoy drinking red wine with my Italian food but the server was not very helpful in helping me choose one. I told him I usually drink malbec and he said they had nothing like it. I would have appreciated a few recommendations but oh well, I just didn't get a drink. I would love to come back if I can score a normal time reservation.
Everything we tried was absolutely amazing. The only thing we did not like was the tuna tartare ( I guess my fault for ordering seafood when they're clearly known for their meats).

After hearing quite a bit about Carbone like any other restaurant the concern becomes is it more hype than anything else.  Do people like it because of the excitement   Went on a Friday night for early dinner and arrived 20 minutes   We were seated immediately.  As others have said it is a little cramped in there and you are very close to anyone seated near you.  Kinda charming but no this in advance if you wouldn't like that.  The service was very good and with a busy place you are not rushed which is nice.  
Clams three ways.  Pretty good 
Spicy rigatoni  very very good.  Not overly sauced and the pasta cooked just right.  
Lobster ravioli excellent. Pillowy raviolis with extra lobster and a light cream sauce.  Best lobster ravioli I have ever had 
Scallop dish was not bad
Veal parm also excellent.  Lightly friend and crispy around the edges   Tender veal again not overly sauced. 

The desserts looked tasty but at that point there was no room left. 

Pretty good meal overall along with a cute dining room, good service and music.  Definitely worth getting a reservation and heading there at least once.

Worth the wait (and struggle to get a reservation).

Great food, service and atmosphere.  They ran out of the special lobster appetizer so we got a house chopped salad with a great simple dressing.  Spicy rigatoni vodka was one of the best dishes I have ever eaten.  Veal marsala came with a 2-inch thick chop - something I have never seen.  This meal did not disappoint.  

For two people we had one appetizer, one pasta and one main dish and one desert and we had food left over.

Outstanding! Their grandma's bread is just out of this world. I'm still having a major separation anxiety thinking about how good it is! Their homemade Mozzarella cheese is also a must. Spicy rigatoni vodka and the veal also lived up to its hype. Although the lemon cheesecake (which our waiter recommended to us as number one dessert at Carbone) was pretty average.

My polish american grandmother makes better Italian food.  Allow me to explain.  The spicy rigatoni was too soft (al mushe) and the cream sauce was no better than the one served by my college cafeteria Vietnamese fast food trained cook.  The pork chop was nearly raw, very fatty and chewy.  The "famous" chicken parmigiana was good but not great (but for the price, it should have been heavenly).  The seafood tower was tasteless and filled with barely edible shellfish (most oysters were left in place and they never inquired why).  Even the scampi (a true delight elsewhere) was simply ok.  Oh, and they charged a post-Lehman regulatory questionable $85 for a microscopic dish of king crab with mayonnaise (I hope it was Helman's and not the Costco volume special Miracle Whip).  The desserts were fine but deemed medically necessary to wash away the awful residual taste of the often abysmal and generally mediocre meal.  Service was good (although they never asked about our food) and the scene was loud but festive (note: cramped quarters and no elbow room).  So now the kicker, the price was $350 per person.  Granted, we ate and drank plenty, but $200 per person would have been acceptable (considering the bar tab) but at $350, the place is a complete ripoff.  Of course, I will never go back and I caution any Italian food lover (or any consumer of food in general) to avoid this establishment and find one of the 1000+ NYC Italian restaurants that serve much better food.  I can only assume that the "good" or "great" reviews are from (1) friends of the owners of, or investors in, Carbone, (2) rare types infatuated with "scenes" and anatomically devoid of taste buds or (3) culinary sophists who have to believe that the meal was worth the second mortgage.  Sarcasm aside, this joint is 100% style over subsistence (and yes, I meant subsistence).  Big thanks to our patron of the evening for picking up the tab.  Even gratis, Carbone merits a pass, unless the world food supply expires everywhere but 181 Thompson Street, and then, but only then, necessity trumps starvation.

Managed to sneak in a 10pm reservation here on a Monday night. Food and service did not disappoint. We ordered the clams three ways, the veal Marsala and the lobster fra diavolo that was a special. Huge portions and yet we wanted to try the meatballs so we got them to-go. However, the meatballs were not given to us in our takeout bag. *sad face*. Will go back for the veal Marsala for sure.

SOOO delish. Food fantastic; amazing service. The soundtrack made everything fun. Clams delish...rigatoni delish...squash agrodolce outstanding; veal parm delish: carrot cake and tiramisu delish-especially the ladyfinger with the tiramisu which was a highlight. I am not a pushover and I promise this is a totally wonderful old timey but really not, Italian restaurant.  PERFECTLY cooked pasta...absolutely al dente with the right amount of sauce. ENJOY!

Came here on Saturday with a party of six. We had a 9:30pm reservation and were seated almost 45 minutes after our reservation time. We waited by the bar, which is awkwardly positioned in an angle of a narrow hallway where servers are carrying food out. It was an annoying start to the evening but we looked past it.  

We ordered a bunch of everything to share and I do recommend sharing as the portions are huge. For appetizers, the baked clams were the highlight. They were the best clams I've ever had!

We then shared the linguini vongole, spicy rigatoni vodka, and the pappardelle. All were delicious and cooked to perfection. We then had the veal parm, cherry pepper ribs, and chicken massimo. I would not order the chicken again, but everything else was great.

Going with a group proves to be difficult as they couldn't accommodate our party on time, we were crammed into a corner table that was suited for a party of 4, and overall the timing of the meal was not great. With all of that said, it's a really fun atmosphere with good food and I would return.

Having come to Carbone several times, the food and service, again, did not disappoint.  Word to the wise: MUST order the clams appetizer, the spicy vodka rigatoni.  We also had the tortellini in ragu (great).  Previously had the lobster ravioli (also great). Seems the pastas are the way to go. The ribs were okay.  We've had the veal and that is delish.
My only qualm was the wait. I expected to wait 30 minutes at this packed place but we were standing for over an hour.  The staff was extremely apologetic and gave us a few free items which was very nice, as it was obviously not their fault.  However, I think perhaps a suggestion to the manager/owner is to take fewer reservations to avoid this going forward.  We've had to wait successively longer each time.  While I understand this is par for the course at a crowded place, other popular places with reservations do not have this problem.
Either way, we'll be back for more pasta!!

Went for lunch and loved everything! The food was amazing! The meals starts off with bread, charcuterie and fresh mozzarella cheese. The portion sizes are big and perfect for sharing. The chopped house salad was great! Vongole pasta was perfect! Can't wait to go back!

After all the hype and sparse availability, I would have expected a finer dining experience. The food was mediocre at best and the service was actually bad. Our waiter (Ryan) was downright rude and also not very knowledgable at all. I'm not sure if he had some personal issue with us based on appearance or if he was just always negligent in his responsibilities, but for example, the specials weren't shared with us, he didn't know if the cheeses were pasteurized or not (like a pregnant woman has never eaten there before? Hard to believe!), and the staff had helped others pull out their tables when getting in/out from their seats (tables are placed very close to one another) but I was left to help myself.  The spicy vodka pasta was really delicious, but the apps, bread basket, fish (bass, tasted very fishy and not flavorful), and dessert (the ice cream cake at parm is 5x better than the chocolate cake here) were just OK. I have no interest in returning and I wouldn't recommend it, especially with all the other delicious and non pretentious Italian joints in the city - probably all of which have better service than Carbone!

Solid spot in The Village with a cool ratpack ambiance.

Not cheap but not outrageous either. They spoil you with complimentary aged reggiano cheese, salami and great bread--especially the garlic bread. Splitting the bone in veal parmigiana and a pasta dish is the way to go. The veal was excellent quality yet not too filling as they do not smother it with cheese and sauce as other Restos serving inferior quality veal often do. Baked clams for an app were not bad.

Washed the meal down with a glass of French Pinot each and the damage, including tip, per person was $105--not bad for the caliber of food.

I thought I would give a 5-star rating given this place has been talk of the town for awhile. I think in general the food is more salty than usual so I cannot bring myself to give a perfect rating. We had a party of 6 and had a 6pm reservation. We got seated right away when everybody arrived. We tried all the pasta dishes and the Caesar salad. I would say some my favorite were
- the bread they gave us in the beginning! 
- The Parmesan chunk they gave to everybody
- Spicy Rigatoni Vodka
- Fettuccine con funghi
- Spaghetti Laurita

I also like the waiter services. Attentive and not pushy. However, I wonder why they don't have a higher turner of table reservation. Almost an hour there were 3 empty tables by us. I am sure given the hard time we hard making the reservation, those tables weren't available for reservation. Also there was a long wait between different courses. It will be great if lovers come and want to savor their time at the restaurant. But a 2.5 hour dinner was a long stretch for me personally.

I wish Torissi Italian Specialties was still open because it was a zillion times better than Carbone. Overall the food at Carbone is solid. You get great Italian food for fancy French prices. For what I paid I would have rather gone to a NoMad or gotten really good Omakase somewhere else. It also doesn't help that when they first sat us down in a fairly empty restaurant it was right near the bar and halfway thru our meal my husband's chair got bumped every 30 seconds from waiters trying to get by patrons near the tiny bar. Luckily they were nice enough to move us to a different table only for some other poor soul to have to sit there next. My husband ordered their special tuna tartar which was more like grade A tuna that was put thru a meat grinder. My shrimp scampi was great though with nice lobster looking shrimp (I have no idea what they were called). We shared a pasta and then I had the scallops and my husband had the veal chop which were also both solid. At the end of the night I ordered a bananas foster which took about 30 mins to make. When I asked if it was going to be done soon (since we had been sitting there for so long) the waiter rolled his eyes, gave me a dirty look, and said they had to look for a gas can to light the flame. Overall I don't think I would return. It was overpriced for service that was rude and food that was just "good". I need a little more than free cheese and a good bread basket to pay $$$$ for a meal. And I mean $$$$$. I would rather buy an awesome purse or some David Yurman jewlery for what we paid.

I'm giving this place three stars because of the service. The food was very good, a little salty for my taste but good. The service is what really threw me a curve ball. The trendy rave of Carbone set my expectations high so I was fairly appalled by the demeanor of staff. Our flamboyant server was an older gentleman with a white goatee and red framed glasses. He walked around with his nose in the air ignoring us for the majority of our stay. Nobody in our party wA able to understand a word he said about the menu or specials because the tiny room we were seated inside the left was obnoxiously loud. We had to ask the bus boy several times for basics like water, olive oil, and pepper. The staff also treated these condiments as if they were gold. Within seconds of pouring a little olive oil on a plate someone rudely snatched the container back off of our table in the midst of us dipping the quite wonderful focaccia bread in it. Two minutes later, another staff removed the plate of olive oil entirely while we were still using it. My next qualm was that the reservation request was specifically for the rear room near the kitchen and I later confirmed the accommodation by phone. Instead we were placed by a wait station and the restrooms. I finally had to request to be moved due to a restroom line that ended with our table and people leaning their rear ends on our table next to our food. The manager Patrick was friendly, apologetic, and accommodating. After moving to the original table reservation we encountered Ricky as our new wait staff. He was outgoing but just as into himself as all other staff. Almost all staff had the demeanor of them being better than everyone else just because they work at the renown Carbone. Since it was a birthday event, I asked Ricky to serve us the best deserts even if it included the whole menu. He said he had just the thing and brought out a large piece of carrot cake that was relatively tasty. As if it were another slap in the face he brought out a desert tray to the table next to us 5 minutes later. This tray had every available option which is what I had requested. All in all, the food was great and service should be better for their prices and the fact that they apparently have Michelin stars. I wasn't very impressed with this place overall. I probably wouldn't come back because of the service. 
I ordered the linguine and chicken for my entree. The lobster fra diavolo was ok but I expected more spice for the $95. Both dishes were good, but nothing to go out of my way for again. Reservations are a must, you can't get in without a reservation so book ahead of time if you decide to try this place. They also play old school music like Frank Sinatra, that was enjoyable.

Carbone! Very Good but honestly not as amazing as everyone makes it out to be. The decor which is made to look very American Italian is a bit lacking and too casual for my taste. The tables extremely close together even for nyc standards. Service was very good however!
To start, they bring out some meats along with Parmesan and assorted breads including focaccia! 
We Started out by sharing the mushroom pasta which was the highlight of the meal!
For our main dish we shared the bass oregano which was very flavorful as well as the shrimp sumodo. 
All in all a great meal!
Great food, great atmosphere and delicious wine. Ask for the pasta special with vodka sauce! Beyond amazing.

I cannot say enough wonderful things about this restaurant. From the moment we walked in the door to the moment we left (the last table an hour after closing) my friends and I were treated like royalty. Having had a horrible dining experience at a popular Italian restaurant the night before, we were especially hopeful when Carbone was recommended and disclosed this to the person who sat us. Needless to say they did not disappoint! We started our meal with complimentary champagne, then ordered a round of perfect hot toddies. After a few complimentary snacks it was on to the appetizers: baked clams (delish!), meatballs (by far the best I've ever had) and tuna tar tar (the last one was on the house). All were amazing and the staff was so friendly and kind as they brought each new dish out! For our mains we ordered the veal parm (a touch salty), pappardelle (melt in your mouth divine), and spicy rigatoni (my personal favorite) and beamed with every bite. At the end of the meal we were able to speak to the chef and readily sang him out praises as he sat with us at our table then brought out complimentary moscato, NY cheesecake and the most incredible poached grapefruit and cucumber sorbet. It was truly the most memorable dining experience I have ever had. Cannot wait to go back!

I am obsessed with this place. These are my favorite dishes and the ones you must try...baked clams, Spicy rigatoni vodka, meatballs, garlic bread with mozzarella, veal Parmesan and the ribeye Diana. Good luck getting reservations but once you do it is well worth the wait.

Had dinner there last night with a group of seven people and it was off the charts delicious!! Great vibe, very attentive and nice staff. Everything was perfect!! We ordered family style which was definitely the way to go. Highlights were baked clams, meatballs, spicy pasta,  veal parmesan which was probably the best veal parm I've ever had in my life, and the cheesecake which was tremendous. You know it's good when you're so stuffed but can't stop eating. Love this place and can't wait to go back!!

So disappointed in this restaurant. Only one kind of beer, which was pretty sad. The server did not care about us at all! Paid absolutely no attention. Waited ten minutes just for the menu alone. Me and my husband both ordered the bass Alison which was completely bland and small portion. $38 per entree and we had to eat something else after leaving. Was not asked by our server how our meal was, lacking on refills, and waited almost 20 min once we were done eating to be acknowledged. A manager came over and asked how our meal was (by this time I was completely pissed off) and I told her. She asked what she could do I answered we just want the check. Did not even get comped or offered dessert until after we paid! Came to $96 for two entrees and one beer plus tax and tip on top of the $96. Worst of all, we came here on our honeymoon and I even wrote that down with the reservation. Again, not acknowledged. In fact, this was the only restaurant not to. Save your money. There are way better places around NYC!

Two stars for food 4 stars for service 3 overall
This is the most hyped up mediocre food I've ever had in my life. Perhaps the chef wasn't in today or something went wrong so I will try again in a few months unless more poor reviews come along. 
The cocktails were decent the wine was overpriced. 

The bread plate and pickled vegetable olive oil is excellent

Caesar salad is a standard no-frills Caesar salad for $20 not exciting at all

The spicy rigatoni has decent flavor however the pasta wasn't cooked to perfection and it had no appeal whatsoever, just bland Chef Boyardee looking pasta on the plate

As for the veal parm,  this might be the reason I never come back. For the prized possession of the restaurant to be so flavorless and dry is just a disgrace

Desserts were all very nice looking but only tried the tiramasu and it was decent

Nothing stood out. Nothing was special. Sorry guys

Omg. Amazing amazing amazing! Ricki was our server, he was incredible. The food, omg the food! 
The Beef carpaccio literally takes your breath away and the spicy vodka macaroni is so yum! Don't think we didn't get the veal parm! Overall, the Ambiance literally takes you back to the 50's and you feel like Sinatra is eating at the next table. Have to come back here! Resi's are hard to get so book in advance

Very good food.  It is not "all that", as they hype would have everyone think.  It's sort of an upscale version of traditional classic Italian.  The service was excellent - our server's name was Ricky. Big thumbs up there.  

I think I'd prefer to hit up Arthur Avenue and pay half the price.  Nothing to complain about here, but nothing over the top or special to justify the high prices.

Wow, amazing food, great service, decent cocktails. I mean really good Italian food! But yikes, in a city with SO MUCH amazing Italian food, I find it hard to justify the extremely high prices. I think you should definitely try this place out, and enjoy it for the experience it is, but once is enough, move onto the affordable amazing meals you can pay for on a regular basis.

Let me start by saying this is easily one of the best Italian spots in the five boroughs. I would love to give a perfect 5 stars after the delicious meal I had here. However I am deducting a star because of the sniveling, condescending, weasel-like human with red framed glasses that we were so unfortunate to have as a waiter. Someone in management needs to remind him that he works in the service industry (keyword being service). He behaved as if our innocuous inquiries were beneath him. I don't spend money on dining out to have a waiter dismissively talk down to a group that was nothing but polite. But aside from his snide comments the meal was nothing short of amazing.

I would probably rate it as a 3.5 realistically, but may be generous with rounding up to 4 as I wasn't paying. The food is tasty, but there are some favorites I would suggest and some areas for improvement. To start, before you even order, they bring out the following complimentary items:

1.) A delicious bread basket including the famous tomato focaccia bread. It looks large, but you will have no trouble finishing it. The bread is so light and fluffy that I could have eaten a basket of it

2.) A small plate of tasty salume and a nibble of fresh grand padano

3.) A Pickled cauliflower giardinera.

**Full disclaimer:  I did not pay for my meal as I went as a guest so we ordered pretty heavily for 2. 

For our antipasti, we ordered the Octopus Pizzaiola. If you get one dish, get this. The octopus is cooked to perfection. We also ordered the Scallop Carpaccio which had great flavor with the herbs and the scallops were quite tasty. Presentation was great too.

For our macaroni, we split the famous Spicy Rigatoni Vodka. They already separated the plates and the vodka sauce was on point. We probably could have just ordered a salad and been fine with this. However, gluttony ruled and we got:

1.) Zuppa di Pesci for me. I wish I had taken a photo as the portion was much more generous than the one of another reviewer. There were 3-4 large shrimp, several mussels and clams, plenty of calamari and at least 2 scallops for the $49 dish. That said, it may have been my least favorite. The tomato-based broth was quite greasy and while they gave my 5-6 tasty warm slices of bread to accompany it, I think it was to absorb the grease and I was already beyond full so was trying to skip the additional carbs.

2.) My dining partner ordered the Veal Parmesan and the portion could have easily fed both of us. In fact,  our waiter asked if we were sharing the Veal after we ordered everything else before and before taking my order and we said no as we were fine with leftovers. She said the Veal was delicious.

For drinks, I ordered the Barolo by the glass which  paired very well with all of the food and had some great acidity. She had 1 or 2 manhattans and liked them a lot. 

We skipped dessert as we were beyond full by the end of the meal. Our tab came out to $311 pre-tip so not a place you'd go to often. I'd probably subtract 1/2 a star for the value of the food ($65 for Veal Parm and $49 for a Zuppa di Pesce is a bit much, even for the village) and that's me not paying. The other improvement area would be  restaurant flow. The bar is in the middle of the restaurant and being seated in the back and having to use the restroom was difficult. They also have 2 unisex restrooms that were quite crowded and the "waiting area" is by the rack of wines and another heavy traffic area. 

Overall, I'd say you could probably save some money ordering the delicious antipasti and have a macaroni. The entrees for me weren't a wow factor enough for the sticker price.

Love! From the food to the service and ambiance, everything was spot on.

The complimentary bread basket to start was delish - I appreciate restaurants that put some extra effort into their bread.  We ordered the baked clams, prosciutto and mozzarella, and caesar salad as appetizers.  The clams were good, but pretty standard.  The mozz, as you'd know if you've been to Torrisi, was so so good.  Caesar salad was good, but again nothing special - although I loved the whole anchovies on top and the crispy croutons.

For our mains, we knew we had to order the veal parm and the spicy rigatoni vodka.  We asked our waiter for a recommendation for a third dish, and he suggested the Tortellini al Ragu.  All 3 mains were outstanding, but the tortellini was actually my favorite!  Melt in your mouth pasta and a hearty ragu.  The rigatoni was so creamy and decadent - although I was glad we were sharing, because I think it'd be a little too rich to eat alone as a main.  The veal parm was also delicious.

We were so full, but our waiter kept pushing their cheesecake (the best in the city!) so we had to try it.  It was excellent- rich and creamy, but also light from the lime.

Carbone is certainly not cheap and not easy to get a reasonable reservation time, but lived up to the hype, and I definitely look forward to coming here again!  The only thing I'd detract for is that we shared all the dishes, and they added additional charges for each dish for this - which is fine, but it would have been good to have been told in advance.

I liked this place, very old school vibe. We had dinner reservations at 10:30pm ( I would recommend coming earlier, only because most of their items on the menu were sold out)!!!!!

It was cute and staff was friendly! We got two sorts of pasta which were very good! And also omg the mozzarella was amazing!

Carbone is truly an Italian experience right here in NYC! The ambiance is great and as soon as you walk in, you'll see a warm inviting row of tables and hear Motown playing in the background. The staff is very friendly and will help make suggestions on the favorites on the menu. Their homemade meatballs are amazing and I highly suggest trying them. All the pastas are delicious. In all honesty, you can't go wrong with any of the items on the menu. Expect a large check, but it's worth every penny.

The food here is really good and the service was spot on. We came for an early lunch. When we first arrived it was empty but quickly picked up.

The lobster ravioli was excellent with big meaty pieces of lobster. The ceased salad was a well done classic and the mozzarella that accompanied the meal was also top notch. I think something that stood out to me was the quality of the bread that was used in all dishes. 

I would definitely come here again for dinner.

An Italian classic.... high end experience with a down to earth staff and decor. Nothing bad in this hard to get into downtown restaurant. Try it all.... nothing disappoints. Cocktails delish and red sauce... just yummmmm.

Carbone continues to shine as a top New York Italian dining venue.

Seated at a table for seven the Maitre'd suggested we let him handle things - from appetizers to desserts including wine - white and red.

And off we went...

We shared Baked Clams (Littlenecks / Baby and Razor Clams), and the wonderful Octopus Pizzaiolo - garlic, onion, pimentos, oregano in a terrific unique sauce. The pastas here are on another level. The Spicy Rigatoni Vodka and Cheese Ravioli are dishes you will remember for quite some time. The sweet tasteful tomato sauce rules here.

And the hits keep on coming - The Branzino here is one of the best I've experienced. Subtle flavors mix resulting in a extremely tasteful offering - no lingering oil. The Veal Parmesan (an extra thick cutlet)  coated in breadcrumbs, smothered with their wonderful tomato sauce, and mozzarella. Nothing better...

Of Note: We also received The Rib-Eye selection which was returned as too rare. Once again received a few at our table felt the steak was too fatty. Desserts were winners with the Carrot Cake and Tiramisu being highlights.

Service continues to shine here as Sinatra continue to sing.

A must visit...

Our server Ricky was extremely attentive, service was excellent. The veal parm was perfectly cooked with a crispy thin bread crust on the outside. Lobster fra Diavolo, a bit pricey at market price of $95 but I'd have to say it was cooked just right, not overly done or tough. The tomato sauce on the meatballs was delicious, however the meatballs were a bit too heavy on the sausage and pancetta, for my taste. Loved the little treats they included which they tastefully inserted between the courses you ordered such as the rainbow cookies, different pieces of cheeses, fruits and even dried raisins on the stem. The portions are extremely generous, it is a good idea to come with more people as it can get pretty filling. I did not get to try one of the popular choices on the menu which was the spicy rigatoni but this definitely gives me a reason to return. The staff also sang "Happy birthday" wonderfully and with an Italian flair!! Octopus pizzaiolo was a great recommendation for the antipasti. Overall, it's an once in a blue moon splurge.. Be mentally prepared for a hefty bill.

While the food was wonderful, we had thoughtless service and an unfortunate impression that was left with us about different treatment for us, three women dining, versus the tables of men and women around us that were treated with significantly more attentiveness.
