Specifically, we had to ask two or three times after our appetizers came about getting bread (having seen all the tables that had come after us receiving a bread basket and accompaniments, which alerted us to the existence of a bread basket).  We had to flag another person over to bring us glasses of wine after our main course was served.  (We noticed a sommelier at other tables;  no one asked us if we wanted any wine, a wine list, etc...)  Finally, we had questions about ordering, and the waiter was unresponsive (essentially having almost nothing to say, mumbling that everything was good), but we saw him chatting at length with other patrons in response to their questions at other tables.  Again, the food was great, but the service marred the experience.

Finally scored a ressie here and came last night with a party of 4. Can def see why it's tough to get a table here! 

Loved everything about the place. Old school Nyc dining vibe, first class service and great food. Loved our waiter.. He was funny, attentive and def made you feel at home. Prices steep but worth it. 

We ordered a lot and everything was very good but the stand outs to me were the baked clams with 3 variety; the spicy rigatoni vodka, steak Diane and meatballs. Dessert tray they brought over was a nice touch.. Mostly cakes and ordered one of each. Carrot cake with ginger ice cream was my personal favorite! 

Great place! If you love seafood, their sister restaurant is down the block; zz clam bar. Same amazing attentive service and great food.

Carbone is a restaurant with tons of personality and is like walking back a few decades to a local New York Italian restaurant. Their menu is very diverse and offers the traditional Italian menu items while bringing in some creative new options. One guest required a vegetarian menu and they were more than accommodating to his dietary restrictions. We were told, "no problem. We will make it happen." The veal and cocktails were great, the personalities were even better. If you can get a reservation, go!
This is my go to spot for pasta/Italian. Carbone never disappoints and their pasta is always cooked to perfection. I also enjoy its casual chic intimate atmosphere.

Arrived early for 9:30 reservation on a Saturday night. The host told us they only had us down for 2 people meanwhile we made the reservation a month ago for 4 and had an email confirmation to prove it. Regardless, We waited at the cramped bar for 45 minutes until our table was finally ready.  We ordered three varieties of baked clams to start which were ok but a friend  couldn't eat one (peanut allergy). Meanwhile we warned the waiter of this allergy in advance of our order. We double checked with a bus boy who told him don't eat it. I don't remember what other appetizers we ordered. Next course was three pastas- manicotti, spicy rigatoni, and linguine in clam sauce. Spicy rigatoni was ok and the clam sauce we sent back cause it was too fishy. After the pasta course we ate veal parm and chicken scarp and the abundance of salt was the only memorable aspect. the meal was a $650 disgrace.

1) We were seated 40 mins late after arriving early for our reservation. Not to mention took forever to get our order in. 2) Our table was next to the bar and people kept bumping my pregnant wife. 3) $85 corkage. No one bothered to tell us at the start and it's just over the top. 4) I've been several times and the food used to be spectacular. Now it's mediocre. Parm their sister restaurant does many of the same for a fraction of the cost with greater consistency. 6) they double charged us for one of the pasta dishes. We didn't realize this until we got home. 7) they did send out some meatballs and artichokes to make up for the wait and waived half the corkage. Still a bad experience all around. Staff lack empathy.

Carbone continues to be a place that I recommend over and over again to out of towers and Manhattanites alike. It's a quintessential New York restaurant you just can't find elsewhere. As I see it, every dollar an out-of-towner spends at Carbone is a dollar not thrown away on a tourist trap in Little Italy, at a crappy midtown steakhouse, or at Il Mulino. Carbone's cooking represents something most Americans are familiar with; the huge, saucy, melty portions of Italian-American cooking, but at level of refinement, creativity, and technique that's more common for high-end French fare. This level of service and pampering is becoming relatively uncommon for an a la carte venue, though admittedly you still end up paying as much at Carbone as you would at a tasting menu restaurant: Dinner for three can easily exceed $500. I don't buy the argument that Italian-American cuisine has to be cheap because it was born out of poverty. To be quite honest, most cuisines were born out of poverty. And I like to think a victory for Carbone is also a victory for Alex Stupak's ambitious Mexican establishments, and every other so called "ethnic food" restaurant pigeonholed into the culinary bargain bin. But here's the thing: If a restaurant charges top dollar it has to render the best versions of these dishes. Is the $55 veal parm the best I've ever had? Eh, it's pretty darn close. Is their spicy vodka rigatoni the best rigatoni dish I've ever had? I'll go one step further... And say it is the best pasta dish in all of NYC. Bold statement I know, but for me everything else from the best fettuccine carbonara to the greatest version of spaghetti & meatball pales in comparison. Also during multiple separate visits to Carbone, I've encountered the best veal Marsala than anywhere else I've ever been; and I've consumed my fair share of Marsala growing up on Long Island. The service is always on point, but isn't the reason I come to this adored Italian ristorante with its innovative cuisine that offers a contemporary touch. It's plain and simple really, there are things on this menu that you'll never have taste better anywhere else in the world. Mario Carbone once again gets it right.

This place is nuts.  Had a 9:45pm reservation and sat down at 10:30pm.  That was pretty painful.  The place is absolutely mobbed and no place to stand while waiting for a table.  I thought the food was really delicious although the prices are just absurd.  Good thing I wasn't paying the bill.  The cheesecake is amazing!  Service great throughout the meal.
My favorite spot in NYC.  I've never had anything bad and it's a great spot for small groups.

So a few people have recently posted with the same thoughts - we're not sure what the heck happened...

Food is still good, but the vibe has changed. This time around it felt cramped vs intimate, music was louder and the crowd a little more rambunctious, the staff seemed slightly less professional and immature. I'm thinking there might be a pretty substantial difference in experience between a weeknight and weekend night - a older crowd on a weeknight gives the place the softer and traditional feel perhaps. 

I hope this isn't a turning point for a restaurant that many people usually would seek out for an intimate and old-world traditional Italian meal/dining experience.

Over priced under served

This place is outrageously expensive for what it is.

I have never been served lamb chops that were only cooked on one side.

The only thing good was the rigatoni and the cherry ribs.

The fish was fishy.

Save your money,  100 yards north you will find Portobello.  You can eat wonderfully there 5 times for the cost of Carbone,

I enjoyed my 2nd visit to Carbone. The starters, the meatballs, veal parm, and the pasta with vodka sauce--all fantastic. The artichoke dish and red snapper just ok.  Great service, amazing red wine @ $150 a pop, cool music, and a great seat next to a state senator. I'll be back at some point but dont think ill become a regular. Rather, I'll try Santina in the Meatpacking (same owners and great ambiance). Overall bill for four @ Carbone=$550.00

Worth the hype!   I ordered family style: Cooked Pancetta is a must!   They cooked the octopus better than the Greeks!  Ordered a salad for the girls.  Spicy Sauce Rigatoni is perfect .... Veal Parm and the Bronzino really sent me home feeling good!    The espresso is short and strong, the way it should be!  I grew up after dinner eating fruits and nuts ... They bring you fruits and nuts, Grazie style, on the arm.   Music is fresh!  Staff knows how to get you lit and spend that flash cash!   This place is not for the weak and I will be back!

Looking forward to dining here, having enjoyed other restaurants owned by the same group.  Our party of four arrived early for a 7:15pm reservation.  Appetizers and a bottle of wine were consumed by 8:15....then we waited...and waited...and waited.  At 8:45, we asked where our entrees were.  The Maitre' D said "very soon," yet 20 minutes later, we still had no food, nor had anyone bothered to tell us why there was a delay.  Tables arriving after us were finishing their entrees.   At this point, at 9:05 we asked for the check.  Suddenly we got their attention and were told that there was a mix-up in the kitchen, that part of our order wasn't cooked properly (we ordered shrimp and three pasta dishes...how hard is that? More likely, our order was ignored).  The captain patronizingly insisted it had NOT been 20 minutes since we'd first inquired.  As we stood to leave, having been there for nearly two hours, suddenly two dishes of pasta arrived, but it was too little/too late.  We were charged only for the wine but will not return.

I've been to Carbone twice for work dinners. Both times the food was excellent, however I can't say the same for the service. From being seated nearly 45 minutes after our reservation time to just generally being slow on service, the management could really do a better job of running this small restaurant. I've even had friends that received a call from Carbone an hour before their reservation time saying that, because of a partial buyout, their reservation would not be honored. That's really not acceptable. It's too bad since the food is really delicious.

Easily one of my faaaavorite places to eat.

I love everything about Carbone - the food, the vibe, the service. I could go on. It's one of the most sought-after reservations in the city, with good reason. But I guess it's all in line with all of Major Food Group restaurants.

Food: Overall, seasoned to perfection. I've had quite a bit of dishes here, but am calling out favorites- don't remember exact names so sorry about that. Obviously spicy rigatoni, you can't really come here without having some. I also like to pair their meatballs with it. Their pancetta appetizer, solid. Fresh mozz appetizer, don't think this is on the menu, but emphasis on fresh. And am obsessed with their tiramisu- the lady fingers, A1! And shout out to the waiter who gave me extras from the pastry chef! Oh, and the croutons in the salad! How could I forget, best I ever had.

Ambience: Love the vibe, love the music. It can get pretty noisy here, but personally never truly annoying. Gives off the old world feel, but again I've noticed some differences between weekday/weeknight. I love that it's an upscale restaurant with a casual vibe. As much as I love a fancy meal, i cannnnot stand overtly fancy experiences. 

Service: It's amazing. Staff is so helpful and attentive.

Price: Expect to pay a decent amount here. Without alcohol and getting a nice sampling of dishes with two people will run your tab to about an average of $200ish, depending on your orders.

Go here, eat everything, don't ever feel bad about it.
Loved everything about this place: the decor, the ambiance, the service, the wine, the FOOD! Worth the wait and the calories!!! Can't wait to go back :-)

The restaurant looked interesting from the outside because it seems as if it a hole in the wall great find. After high expectations it did as all the other major food group restaurant have done. Disappoint as usual with their awful service and bland food. Do yourself a favor and do not pay for overpriced microwaveable food you can get for a dollar in your local supermarket. An overpriced menu may fool some people to think they are eating quality but that won't work on me and hopefully others will read this and be warned before they make the same mistake I made.

Food: Great basics. Most dishes were bursting with flavor and tasted freshly made. Rigatoni vodka hit the spot. Linguini con vongole sadly was drowned in salt at the end. Prosciutto can't go wrong - very light and fresh. Meatballs delicious. Ribs were good. The special of Dover sole with truffle oil - way overpriced at $130 and not worth it. Bread was fantastic: especially the buttery tomato very airy but filling

Service: old-school and knowledgeable waiters. Fair pace to their check-ins. Found the kitchen to be rather slow in bringing food out.

Ambience: extremely loud in here. Alcohol helps to fuel the raucous conversations at each table, and you're practically party to every conversation around you.

Delicious!! Far the best pasta I have ever tried and Im comparing this to pasta I had in Italy! Their appetizers are incredible too! You must order the beef carpaccio, bread with mozzarella, lobster ravioli, and spicy rigatoni

So, I've been trying to get into carbones for about a year or so...and finally was able to make a reservation. Heard how amazing the food was ect...well, unless your a movie star let me just say the Veal Parmigiana is 65.00. So after reading such stellar reviews here on this item, I decided I had to try it. The taste was fine, but nothing really out of the ordinary. Certainly not worth 65.00. I've had better veal for less than half this amount. That said, the drinks themselves range about 17.00 for a glass of wine?  We had the spicy rigatoni in vodka sauce, again, it tasted fine. It wasn't amazing. So after 2 pasta dishes,1 beer and one glass of wine and a veal parmigiana bill came to 200.00. I personally would never go back. This was on my bucket list of restaurants to try. Save your money and spend the 200.00 on a better place.

It just didn't live up to the hype for me.  I enjoyed my time at carbone, but found the food and overall experience to be average.  The staff was very nice and friendly.  There were a few mistakes, but they took care of them immediately.  The fresh mozzarella was over salted to the point where we didn't even eat much of it.  The meatballs were tasty, but also a little heavy handed on the salt.  The veal parm was tasty, but not worth the $65 price tag...  I would put the chicken parm at Sauce and Quality Italian up against it any day.  Yes I realize I just compared chicken to veal but at the end of the day when you bread it, fry it, and douse it in sauce and cheese - is it that much different?  The spicy rigatoni was definitely tasty.  They were out of the lasagna verde which I am told is a show stopper.  They also did not have shrimp.  The Dessert was also good not great.  Nutella tiramisu was good but by no means memorable.  The cookie served on top was my favorite part!  Everyone describes this as "authentic old school Italian basics at their best".  While the staff was good - none were Italian.  Authentic basic Italian at those prices seems almost like an oxymoron.  I knew that going in though so I am in no place to complain about that.   

The price wasn't the issue.  Take price out of the equation and the experience was still very average.  I really wanted to love this place...

Carbone's for us sets the bar!
Have snuck in here a half dozen times never able to get a reservation (even on a Monday/Tuesday) but able to charm the very accommodating maître d'. 
 I can start by saying Amazing!
Very friendly staff, beautiful decor and some of the best Italian American dishes we ever eaten. 
Every visit we have to start with the table side caesar don't know how they do it, A+. Want to order a side of croutons with our main course if we could. If we get the porter house we get the filet tartar as an app, amazing. 
The most amazing mozzarella ever! Served in oil they cut it with a pair of scissors at the table. I've never had another mozzarella that I can compare it to. 
Then one of the best pastas I've eaten the spicy rigatoni Period. 
Porter house excellent perfect melt in your mouth. Not the best ever but better than most of the old guard steakhouses in Manhattan. 
Chicken massimo, ribeye Diana or veal chop all worth trying if you can get a table. 

Seasonal favorites acorn squash with marscapone. 
Five stars all day long!

There's not much more to say about this place other than it's amazing! The service was fast and attentive, and our waiter was awesome! He was funny and witty, yet was able to recommend everything to our liking. 

The baked clams were good, not great. The spicy rigatoni without a doubt lives up to all of its hype. It was so good it made me think about ordering one to go! The ribs came out way bigger than expected so be aware of that. The veal parm was delicious and a perfect size to split for two. For dessert I tried some type of chocolate cake with a scoop of Nutella ice cream on top, it was ok! The desserts need to be changed up a little in my opinion. 

Overall, we had an awesome experience here and are definitely look forward to coming back!

I knew it was you Carbone, and you broke my heart!

Not only have I dined at Carbone before, but I consider it one of the best dining experiences I've ever had. Upon sitting, you're overwhelmed with a barrage of bites: Parmesan cheese off the wheel, amazing bread basket and pickled vegetables. Next up, we ordered our drinks. One of the best old fashioned I've ever had. Unfortunately, I can't say the same for my wife. She ordered a spicy margarita, which turned out to be excessively spicy. Each of the 8 of us at the table tried it and could not tolerate it. When we asked the waiter to fix it, his response was "you said you wanted spicy!". In any case, he stood by the table, trying to figure out how to fix the heat on it. Add juice? Add syrup?  Dude, it's not that hard- take it back and remake the drink!! He did not do that, instead adding juice, which had no effect on the spice. We ended up sending it back, to his chagrin. He later came by and said that he tasted it and it in fact was undrinkeable. 

Next up, we ordered our food. We got the classics such as spicy rigatoni (2 orders) angel hair pasta, and other items such as beets, clams, minestrone and chopped salad. The lamb chops, veal parm and branzino. Despite such a large and varietal order, the waiter was visibly upset, claiming we ordered too little. His dramatics were funny at first, but concerning later- shaking his head and muttering no to us, in clear and obvious disapproval. 

The food was simply amazing, but the service was significantly under par for such an amazing restaurant and it was much worse than what we experienced on previous visits. The two orders of rigatoni were brought on one plate and we were noticeably short-changed. We know this because we ordered one more rigatoni later and received the same amount as our "double" order. Far worse was the fact that we were charged for two orders of veal parm when we only ordered one. 

We ordered three desserts. All great. However, no cookies. No mandarin oranges. No walnuts to finish the meal. Complimentary little additions that make you feel welcome and truly define the experience. Our waiter all but abandoned us, despite us ringing up a check for over $1500. Although the food is great, the service and experience is what sets this restaurant well above others. On this occasion, they were significantly below their high standards.

I don't understand what the hype is about. I'm from LA and supposedly this is one of the best restaurants to dine at in nyc but my mom makes better pasta. It has an old New York vibe but the food was not what I expected it to be.

What an absolutely fabulous restaurant!! The food is to die! You really do feel as though Sinatra is about to come through the door. The service is top notch (Hi Ryan!) eat everything, but make sure you have your uber right outside waiting after dinner because you will feel like a total stuffed animal. I'll def be back!

First off, you must get a reservation in advance, but totally worth the wait. Carbone is one of the best restaurants I have ever been to, period. I came with a friend for dinner for a 5:45 res on a week day. The decor was very Godfather like and the lighting really set the mood. We had the Caesar salad to start, I had the spicy rigatoni vodka, my friend had the bass, and we closed with a slice of tiramisu. Everything was amazing. I strongly believe that you can't go wrong with anything on the menu. The service was great and by the end our tummies were on cloud 9. We can't wait to go back.

Was all the hype worth it ? Definitely not. We were pleasantly greeted and luckily sat down by the time our RSVP was. ( even though I heard there are very long wait times ). I'll get straight to the pros and cons. The only pro I would say is that the food is decent , especially the meat balls. Everyone raves about the spicy rigatoni, they were tasty but not mind blowing like others have made it seem. Now about the cons - first it was my mothers birthday and we had told our host who booked it for us and we were completely forgotten. No special attention no nothing. There was very little attention paid to us. The second and most annoying problem was the music. There were saxophones and trumpets blasting into our ears from the speaker the whole time !! We could not hear each other or communicate at all. We had to yell every time  we wanted to say something to each other . I left the restaurant with a mild headache thanks to the roaring sounds of the trumpets and saxophones. One of the dishes we ordered were the pork chops but being a pork affectioniado , one of our guests was certain they brought him the beef instead. Aside from that there were other little issues here and there such as wrong knives being brought, etc. there are many better choices especially for Italian in nyc that aren't as pretentious and hyped. I liked il mulino much more than carbone. All in all , if you love blasting saxophones and trumpets all night with decent food check this place out, but there are many other more elegant , tasty and attentive restaurants in nyc.

The staff at Carbone are very friendly. We enjoyed the food even though it took a while to get our orders but the waiter gave excellent recommendations. Really glad we went here and will definitely come again.

very different place compared to when I visited 2+ years ago (and thought it was in my top 10)

-Ambience: still nice but crowd very douchey/extremely loud, music overly loud/clubby--especially for a Monday evening - (used to be a more refined crowd with elegant atmosphere) 

-Food: still top quality ingredients but pricey 

complimentary bread, reggiano, salumi :  9/10
ceasar salad                                          : 9/10
spicy rigatoni vodka                               : 8/10
veal parm                                               :7/10  (used to be better)
sweet pepper ribs                                   :6/10  (used to be better)


I used to rave about this place. Given the new douchey atmosphere, decline in food quality, high prices and difficulty in geting a rez,  I probably won't be back soon.

Wow, Carbone blew away my expectations!  It was incredible.  We were lucky enough to snag a dinner reservation here for last Friday and I am now officially obsessed.  The atmosphere was so great with black and white old school style tile floors and then fun oldies playing in the background.  The food was delicious also - especially the vodka pasta.  It was even amazing gluten free! Hopefully I can get another reservation so I can go back again ASAP!

What makes an excellent meal vs a great meal? Well you can find out first hand by visiting Carbone. My husband and I have eaten countless plates of pasta from top Italian places from NY to LA,  from rustic Tuscany to hidden gems in Burano. Even after all that, we were still floored by how delicious Carbone's Spicy vodka rigatoni was. The chewy al dente pasta and perfectly spiced sauce...it was a match made it heaven. Every course served had balance...starting with the complimentary bread, sopressata and pick lend veggies...warm soft bread, rich earthy cured meat, and a bright lemony pickled cauliflower...a perfect way to prepare your palette. The meatballs were hearty and moist served with a bright tomato sauce to offset some of the richness of the fat. Our last course was the grilled pork chop with red peppers and it was nothing less than exceptional. But...a meal is only as good as its services and theirs is TOP NOTCH. Never did my water glass go below the middle of the glass and never did our hands have to reach to pour our wine. Courses all came out in a steady stream of a food concert, never missing a beat. If you are visiting NY, please plan ahead and make your reservations here soon! I plan to make every effort to go there every time I am in NY from this day forward.
Get the Veal Marsala and Spicy Rigatoni Vodka. Fish soup is also good, and service is impeccable. Drinks bar also amazing. I love this place.

Oh man.

Carbone is quite a little gem. I was blown away by all the flavors that I encountered while dining here with my friend late one evening. I already had an inclination that the food would be great but my expectations were beyond exceeded. I was probably served the best pasta dish ever. No lie. WARNING: This place is pretty pricey. Take note of the four $$$$. However, every bite is worth it. Also, all the hosts/servers were beyond pleasant and accommodating. I'd highly recommend snagging a reservation because the space is very intimate and gets booked up weeks in advance. 

Back to the food. 

We started off with a loaded bread basket and sliced salami. Their focaccia bread was out of this world. I had to tell our server to bring back double the amount the second round. It was THAT good. Once it was time to order, I kept it simple with the Spicy Rigatoni Pasta and my friend got the Lobster Ravioli. I can't even put in to words how good my food was. I savored every single bite. By the time it was over, I almost told them to bring me out another plate. Seriously! Sauce was packed with flavors, pasta was cooked perfectly, and the portion was larger than expected. Lobster ravioli was just as spectacular. For dessert, we opted for the lemon sorbet. SO CUTE. and very tasty. Ugh. I can't wait to go back. 

Definitely worth the $$$$ and the wait. Book your table now!

Great atmosphere, brings your back to the old Italian mafia movies.
Excellent food, highly recommend on the sizzling pancetta and the octopus!!
Overall a great place which I would highly recommend for high quality Italian food.

woo i dined again at carbone. this is still my favorite reasturant in NYC . I would give again a 2 michelin star . food quality is outstanding as well as service which is quite unique as they waiters make you feel special.
From the waiter to each sauce on the food was amazing. The clams were amazing. Best garlic bread I've had In a while.

This was one of the best meals I've ever had. The ambiance was incredible. Great music (rat pack style) and the staff is so charismatic and attentive. Went there for lunch so I can't speak to the dinner vibe but it was amazing. My husband and I split the baked clams, beef carpaccio, and spicy vodka rigatoni. I recommend all three. Splurge!

Also the salami, mozzarella and garlic bread they bring out first is just a taste of what's to come. If you can make it here on a trip to NYC, please please visit. 

This is so worth it.

Best Italian restaurant in NYC!!! Everything is perfection. We started with the beef carpaccio and gorgonzola salad which was soooooo GOOD. For mains, we had veal parm (incredible), clam pasta (also so good). Do not leave without having their tiramisu. Best tiramisu in NY. I promise!
Absolutely amazing!  Our server "A" provided the best service I've ever experienced. The spicy rigatoni was impeccable. Chicken scarp was second to none. Cannot wait to go back.

I do not get what all the hype is about. We were excited to dine here but honestly the serve was so uppity. What an attitude. And the entree prices were absolutely ridiculous. Spicy vodka pasta very good but not exceptional. Gorgonzola y aceto salad was very average. Passed on entrees after first two very average courses. For these prices this should have been the best meal of our lives!!

I heard so much rave about this place, I decided to have lunch there with a group. 
The service was not as attentive as everyone spoke of. One must wait for the Captain to take your order, for everything. That's where the waiting came in. 

My guests were stuck in a taxi, so they arrived late. While waiting I wanted to order 2 appetizers, I was told the full party needed to be there and that we needed to order the selection. ( apps/entree). So we waited and sipped water. I finally was able to order a glass of wine. It felt like I was volleying for the servers attention.  

Okay?

The complimentary fresh mozzarella, sopressata and garlic bread was delicious! 
The menu appetizers were limited. Each one of us had a different app. All equally delicious. 
The entrees chosen were Veal Parmesan, Chicken Scarpiello, Scallops. Food was very tasty and seasoned to perfection. 

The prices are extremely high; Veal cutlet = $56.  Total bill pushing $600.  I think I expected so much more from all the hype. It's a veal chop pounded and made into veal parmesan.  Yes, it was tasty but not the best meal as many Yelpers posted. 

I think atmosphere does lend itself to the meal and this for me was lacking in hospitality. Staff smiles were definitely not the feel of the day.  Not sure I would return.
This spot is on fire. Had the ribs, meatballs, and everything else. Unsuspecting exterior is my style--don't miss the spicy rigatoni

Yes to the spicy rigatoni. Yes to the bread and mozzarella that comes to the table first. Yes to the croutons in the Cesar salad. The veal parm was good. It's a family friendly restaurant but it is still classy. The portions are good. I was able to take a small portion home. Excellent service! I would definitely return and since I saw children, I'm bringing my son next time!!!

It is a hush hush cul de sac location. make your reservations well in advance unless you know somebody. If you want authentic Italian food this my new love. Next to Del Posto, it had the best homemade tasting Bolonaise ever. Antipasto traditional with out weird fusion. I loved every morsel. I love it here expensive but guilty pleasure.

Fun place with a lively atmosphere.  Food is very good although other places do these "old school" Italian dishes better for significantly lower prices i.e. $28 for veal parm as opposed to Carbone's $65. Recommended if you're not paying.

This place is good if you're looking for authentic Italian American cuisine. Warning, it is very pricy but overall worth it. When you're seated, you get an assortment of bread (grandma bread, garlic bread, etc.) & pickled cauliflower & a meat plate. The pickled cauliflower were surprisingly very good & well seasoned. 

For dinner I got the infamous spicy vodka rigatoni & it definitely lead up to its expectations. Amazing!!! No wonder why everyone gets it. 

I'll definitely be back.
Authentic Italian food and atmosphere. Service was great and the food was even better. A must try.

One of the best if not THE best Italian food in NYC. The complimentary bread and pickled vegetables to start kicks off a great meal. 

Got the Baked Clams 3 ways, tableside Caesar, Spicy Rigatoni Vodka, Meatballs and Veal Parm. Can't complain at all about any of them but the rigatoni and meatballs in particular stood out.  

It's definitely going to set you back a few $ but I'm a city that's loaded with average Italian, I'd recommend splurging here at least once.

Pretentious and overrated. The spicy rigatoni was good, but that was it- everything else was just ok. Worst of all was the service- our head waiter ruined the entire evening. For some reason, he decided to order for us and brought out whatever he thought we should eat, rather than what we wanted to order. He was way too pushy and actually argued with us when he disagreed with what we were ordering. I will NOT be going back mostly because of the rude and arrogant head waiter, but also because the food is overrated and just not that great.

The best Italian food in the city, hands down. Way better than their sister restaurant, Parm. 

The ambiance is great and the service is exceptional. Servers are so attentive and genuine. Our server brought out dessert on the house bc I was full and he insisted I try just one bite of the tiramisu, can't beat that!

The complimentary assortment of breads in itself is worth the visit! I recommend the assortment of clams to start, they're each so different and packed with flavor. Believe the hype about the spicy vodka rigatoni, you're doing yourself a disservice if you don't order it. We ordered the lobster ravioli which was also good but nowhere near the rigatoni. Everything about the rigatoni is truly perfect!

Carbone is a must and also a good place for celeb spotting, a true gem!

Really great place. Awesome vibe. The service was slightly above average.  The waiter messed up out order but l threw in 2 glasses of wine on the house. Definitely a great feel when you walk in. Packed !  Food was delicious

carbone is priceless!!!!!
had dinner last night at carbone with my son-the best
the service is amazing and nice
we started with the cesar saled (table side) a must
then the meatballs (better than grandma)
then we had 2 different pasta's the spicy rigatoni and the tortellini al ragu (too dye for) and of course the veal parm
dessert was lemon cheesecake and ice cappuccino
can not wait to go back again and again

Excellent food and great atmosphere accompanied by rude and obnoxious staff. 
I was looking forward to a special treat for my 50th birthday dinner.  Waiter wanted to control our dinner order and when we chose to order ourselves he seemed totally agitated and messed up our order. We had to send two meals back.  If you want amazing food and a wait staff that makes you feel like they are doing you a favor, this is the place for you.

This place is the total package for an NYC dinner experience.  As soon as you walk in you feel like you've been transported back to the 1950's based on the decor of the place and Elvis playing on the speakers.

Waiters and sommelier all introduced themselves and did not forget our names the rest of the night.  The fresh made garlic bread was fantastic for table bread.  And that was just the start. 

Somellier was very helpful and helped us pick out a great Barolo in our price range.

Food was fantastic.  3 dishes I would recommend in order

1) Spicy Rigatoni (just look at the other reviews. its a no brainer)
2) Tortelli Al Ragu (this one came out of nowhere of how delicious it was)
3) Veal Parmesan (duh! and they leave you the bone)

The best part of this place is the vibe.  It just seems like everyone is having a good time and the staff is in no rush to get you out the door like some other infamous NYC Italian spots that I won't name here.   Our reservation was at 10pm so we were there pretty late and around midnight the Elvis turned into Drake and Rihanna so that was a nice touch to keep the party going.  

If you want a great Italian spot in NYC.  This should be your first choice.  But be warned.  You need to make reservations at least a month out.  It books up fast.  But its oh so worth it.

After coming home from an Italian getaway in October, I thought I'd never be able to taste of authentic Italian food....

Carbone proved me wrong. The garlic bread and mozzarella cheese to start was absolutely amazing. We ordered the mussels, veal, meatballs, and spicy rigatoni (as recommended by other helpers). The veal was my absolute favorite! But all dishes were just as tasty. 

Definitely worth five stars.

Arrogant and rude. They screwed up a reservation and refused any accommodation for the error. Didnt make the slightest effort to seat us. That kind of disdain for customers should be disquslifying for any restaurant.

Started with the meatballs which were fantastic. Moist and flavorful with a good consistency on the sauce. Also had the beef carpaccio which was very fresh but soaked in oil. Dinner ordered the Veal Parmesan  which was as good as advertised. Big portion can probably split between two so don't get scared by the price point. Lastly shared the spicy rigatoni with vodka sauce. Way too spicy for a pasta dish. Overpowers the entire dish. For dessert get the Nutella tiramisu. Overall great service and experience.

Outrageously expensive even for NYC
Veal parm 65.00
Meatballs, the house specialty,  were raw 
The hot place in town will cool down soon if my experience is commonplace

Yes, and more yes. The spicy rigatoni here could be a whole food group for me.

However, the space is intimate, a little dark, and great art. The service is great as well. The only thing I was a little worried about is how I feel that my allergy wasn't taken as serious. When food is put in front of you and they come back a minute or two later to say that what I am allergic to could be in it... Thankfully I didn't just take a bite of it and end up in the ER. 

Besides that, the food is delicious. The seafood towers, octopus, baked clams, burrata and caviar to start were all delicious. However the showstopper for me is always the pasta. The spicy rigatoni is phenomenal. So good in fact, I almost didn't try the spaghettini and pesto. I was already full by then so when all of the proteins came out I just had a couple of bites of steak and a bite of one of the largest prawns I may have ever seen in my life. Large bowls of what seemed like lightly macerated strawberries and plates of nectarines, with tiramisu, chestnuts, and many many other desserts. I didn't try them all obviously or I might still be in a coma. But everyone enjoyed them. 

Thanks for a lovely night Carbone.

The food at Carbone deserves 5 stars but the service is not the greatest. It might have been just our waiter who was having a bad day. The place is nice and cozy, and the food is delicious! My favorite was the Bronzino... It was out of this world amazing!!!!! Carbone is by far my favorite Italian place, and I would definitely go back again despite the fact that it is pretty pricey.
The baked clams was good. But the scallop was way too salty. The overall experience was great.

great decor, great food, (although a little too salty for the capaccio).
only thing they could change: the art on the walls. everything else is perfect: the walls themselves, the retro curtains, the lamps, the tiles on the floor (totally beautiful), just, why not better pièces of art on top of all this otherwise perfect decor? something that fits more with the decor...

The food here is definitely fantastic. Most of the Italian people that have been to Carbone, and say they can get the same stuff at home are probably full of it; quite frankly because they don't know any better. The food is here simple, but focused, with clear refined flavors thanks to perfect execution in the kitchen. The veal parm is worth every penny, and the chicken massimo is sublime. My only problem was the meal was definitely rushed, and the service was not genuine. It in no way came close to the familial hospitality they are going for. Also, I said I was celebrating a special occasion when I made the reservation, and not one acknowledgement from the restaurant or our captain.

The best restaurant and service ever had! Honestly have never been to a place that has it all together so well! Amazing food and unreal service! Thank you carbone for a great night :) definitely recommend it here!

Let me start by saying my husband and I enjoyed our experience at Carbone. The drinks were great. The best Manhattan I ever had. Wine by the glass was excellent. The service was exceptional, a constant stream of attention without being intrusive. I could of sat all night just watching the action and listening to the music.  However only three stars because the food was not that special. Started with a wonderful bread basket  , some Soppressata, and pickled vegetables all delicious. There is not much I can say about the rest of the meal because it was not that memorable. I can say the pasta and the veal Parm were good but way too salty.  It's too bad it is so $$$$$$$ we would love to go back for the vibe , but not the food.

I don't eat much Italian these days, but was I in for a treat at Carbone! It's in the same neighborhood as Minetta Tavern, and the old-school lighted sign outside ushers you into a dining room that is very similar to Minetta in having a vintage feel. It's not terribly large, and it's not done up to be as fancy and cosmopolitan as a lot of upscale restaurants in NYC, but that retro vibe belies the absolutely delicious meal you have coming. Our waiter and the sommelier were absolute champs - great sense of humor and, from our sommelier, absolutely fantastic selections on wine. I'm not a big wine person, but the Etna Rosso red wine we had had phenomenal flavors and was complex without being too heavy on the tannins. I also had a couple of White Ladies, which was a bit sweet but still incredibly delicious cocktail that packed a lot of punch (in the form of gin) to boot. The only downside (and this is the case for the entire restaurant) - it ain't cheap.

For the food, we ended up sharing the food, and it's arguably some of the best Italian that I have had (price considerations aside). It was definitely setting up to be a good night when we were served a bread plate and, in lieu of butter, was given a decent-sized square of aged Parmesan cheese and a plate of mild sopressata...paired atop of a slice of sourdough, and you have a delicious charcuterie bite right off. Everything was delicious, and it's hard to really pick a favorite. If I had to, it'd probably be the spicy rigatoni, which is just as good as everyone who raves about it says it is. It has the taste of your typical vodka sauce, but then that divine heat starts to creep up on your tongue, and before you know it you have a warm glow in your mouth and in your belly. The mussels were also excellent, possibly because it was served in a sauce that looked and tasted quite similar as well. The seafood here overall is great; the sole was de-boned on the side after being presented and served piccata - with the small slices of jalapeno adding a little bit of heat to each bite as well and adding even more acidity on top of the lemon-butter base. We had some langoustine to start, and it's presented in a very unique fashion - the meat is served in-shell, with the crustacean cracked open along the back. I just got back from Maine, but the meat here rivaled the quality of any of the lobster that I've had - juicy and succulent. The meats here ain't that shabby either; we shared an order of meatballs that were as hearty and tasty as one could imagine. They are basically better, bigger versions of your classic meatballs served in tomato sauce. We also had the veal parmesan - excellent in its own right (especially the cheese), even though it was probably the dish that I was probably the least blown away by. The night ended with a proper sampling of dessert. Surprisingly, my favorite was actually the carrot cake, which had a very strong presence of the orange veggie but plenty of sugar to give it a taste akin to a candied cake (if there is such a thing). The chocolate-frosted cake with crushed nuts on the outer edge was also good, if not as memorable. We finished off with some small slices of mint-infused poundcake, where the bread was decorated in the tricolor of Italy.

This was an absolutely fantastic and memorable meal, and it's definitely worth the visit for several of the dishes. It seems hard to go wrong here, as virtually everything was so tasty. A definite must-visit for me in the future again. Carbone is a modern take on vintage Italian that comes out in stellar fashion.

This place.  So we lucked into a last-minute 5:30PM reservation, which turned out to be perfect -- we sat in the back room (highly recommended) and got a great deal of personalized attention before the crowd descended.  We were also able to enjoy the old school Rat Pack tunes before it got loud -- music that in every way completed the 50s vibe of the joint.  I would rarely return to a restaurant (a pricey one at that) solely for the service but like I said.  This place.  Jason took tremendous care of us -- he was smooth, verging on slick, and at the end of our first interaction with him we had ordered way more food than intended (to say nothing of wine and cocktails).  I loved every minute of it.  He was our guide into a live action version of Goodfellas and I couldn't get enough.  (At one point he informed us that he was but the fifth "captain" at the restaurant and thus we were having merely the fifth best experience possible.  I can hardly believe there are four people better suited to his position than our man Jason.)  Carbone leans in hard to the nostalgia curve and does so perfectly.  Which wouldn't work if the food weren't so damn delicious.  Like really guys, it's pretty fricking good.  Two dishes were "I will go back immediately for" worthy -- the prosciutto melone (a surprise standout) and the spicy vodka rigatoni (the raves are all true).  Everything else was merely totally excellent.  In short, a great restaurant, a great night -- most highly recommended.

I gave in to the hype. At first I scoffed, laughed it off with a dismissive wave. But it lingered, and started to eat away at me like a cancer. So much praise for one dish that is essentially penne a la vodka with a little extra kick, and at close to $30?!

That particular pasta dish is worth the money folks, it is that damn good. If I remember correctly, they put unicorn blood and Mila Kunis' breast milk in the sauce- so that's why it's so expensive.

There are no words to describe how wonderful our dinning experience was. Thank you to Jason and Ryan , your attention to details along with food and wine selection deserves 5 stars. Thank you for making this Birthday Celebration one we will remember for a very long time.

We came to the famous eatery on a Thursday evening and the place was the usual busy! I was so excited to try Carbone, as my husband has been multiple times, and says the spicy rigatoni vodka is one of the best pasta dishes he has ever had. There was six of us so we decided to order just about everything on the menu! Before ordering a large bread basket comes out with focaccia, garlic bread and semolina all delicious in their own right. You also get salami, Parmesan cheese and cauliflower gardenia. For apps we did Baked clams, which came orreginata and casino style, zucchini flowers, and the freshest mozzarella caprese salad I've ever had. The tomatoes were so tender and ripe, they were delicious covered in the salty cheese. For the pasta course we did the tortellini ragu, and of course, the famous spicy rigatoni. The tortellini was  delicious, but I could have eaten at least two orders of the spicy rigatoni myself. It was that damn good!! The veal parm is a must have there and the rib eye Diana,  tender and delicious. We definitely saved room for dessert and ordered the tiramisu, carrot cake, and bananas flambé with ice cream. Each dessert was better than the next. You could not go wrong with either. This place is legit. Truly an NYC legend.

Does Carbone really need another great review to convince you to go there? No. I can't help it. The food is really amazing. My boyfriend took me here as a surprise for my birthday and it lived up to every dream I ever had about this food and more. Being a vegetarian, is it more often than not, hard to find really great meals at Italian restaurants. We told our waiter I was a vegetarian and he was happy to tell me about what I could have. I started out with the beet salad, which I basically have every time I have Italian, but the one here was so good it really stands out in my mind. The dressing was so light and the tangerine (okay, not positive what citrus fruit it was) brought this baby up even one more notch. Obviously I had the spicy rigatoni and it was really everything I thought it would be and more. I'm sure you all know that by now from the other reviews........ But really....  THAT GOOD. My OH got the veal parmigiana and he really enjoyed it but said my pasta might have been the best thing on the table. A win for vegetarians everywhere! We had to cheesecake for dessert and it was so good! I really don't usually eat cheesecake but this one was light and not too sweet which is nice after a huge meal! The service was great, the sommelier was wonderful and the food was a dream. You have to go here!

the spicy rigatoni, just like everyone else said! This isn't even a dish I would typically order at any italian restaurant but there is something about it here! It really is out of this world!

And the pasta is cooked perfectly al dente. Love it.

Intimate setting and great wine selection.

So after touring  NYU with my daughter we decided to have lunch at this snobbish establishment.  Although there seem to be an ample amount of empty tables the host asked if we had reservations and was turned away immediately. I guess they are so sucessful that they can turn away customers. This was on a week day afternoon. Do yourself a favor and eat at Lupa across the street for great food and excellent service.

KenScale: 8.5/10

The super chef duo of Mario Carbone and Rich Torrisi never play it safe. Within their vastly growing empire, Carbone certainly is at the forefront when it comes to exuberance of dining experience. It's been a while since I visited this Italian American palace, so I figured a revisit is in order. I didn't have quite the same magic as I had on my previous visits, but the meal at Carbone can still be a very satisfying affair.

As with all my other visits, I had to start the meal with Caesar salad, which was still an impeccable salad dish with richness of flavor and fresh vegetables working wonders in my taste bud. Scampi all scampi was also a nice shrimp appetizer dish, but didn't leave a ton of impression. I tried the spicy rigatoni vodka on my first visit to Carbone, and on this visit the buttery sensation of the pasta was displayed prominently to spectacular effect. I just didn't remember if I had enjoyed this pasta dish that much. On the other hand, linguini vongole felt a little flat even though I had no complaint about the fine texture of the noodle. For seafood entrée, we went for red snapper oreganata which was very nicely cooked and had a balance of flavor that would be hard to replicate elsewhere. Double lamb chops were also cooked perfect medium rare, although the seasoning was somewhat uneven throughout various parts of the meat. I felt the magical experience I've had at Carbone on my previous visits wasn't quite there even though the meal was generally very good. Is it just a matter of not choosing the best dishes of the restaurant or is the kitchen showing some signs of slowing down? I couldn't tell, but then the desserts happened. My dining party, which included two girls and two guys including myself, was just going after the tiramisu and chocolate cherry cake like we had just started eating. Tiramisu still had the perfect moistness that I had thoroughly enjoyed on my last visit, and chocolate cherry cake was another delightful dish that had all the decadence of a big-time dessert without being overly sweet. 

Getting a reservation at Carbone can still be a Herculean affair, although to my great surprise the restaurant reservation app Reserve was able to secure tables for a party of four on almost a last minute notice. In addition to all the classic cocktails, there is a very large, Italian-centric wine selection (a bottle of Piedmont Barbaresco that I ordered was absolutely spot on in the course of our meal). Carbone still offers that memorable dining experience with a retro Italian American décor and setting. Perhaps I should compile a list of my favorites from my previous visits and cherry pick those dishes on my next visit for a truly remarkable meal.

Came here for a lunch during the summer had an amazing experience. When you are first seated, the waiter brings out garlic bread, salami, and mozzarella. The mozzarella is made fresh at the restaurant and it definitely shows. Our group decided to let the waiter order for us, and he did an incredible job. He started us off with the spicy meatball rigatoni, which is one their well-known dishes, and the lobster ravioli. Both were delicious, but the rigatoni really stood out in my mind. For entrees, we went with the branzino and the veal. In my opinion the veal was the better of the two, but I am partial to meat. The service was also spectacular throughout the meal. The ambience is also great. It is a small, intimate setting that makes it great for lunch and dinner. The decor, waiters, and size of the restaurant make it feel as if you are in a movie. You also wouldn't feel out of place if you strolled in from off the street in jeans and a t-shirt. I was so full at the end of the meal that I could barely stand up, but it was well worth it. Hopefully I'll be able to make it back soon.

Americanized Italian food executed perfectly. 

People generally think of the amazing food when they come to Carbone, but the very first thing you notice when you walk in is the 1920s inspired Italian ambiance. The garlic toasts and parmigiano reggiano that they serve once you're seated are a delicious start to the meal. We ordered the octopus and it was impeccable, I could only critic the potatoes that had very little flavor. The well known spicy rigatoni is a must, so long as its accompanied by the mind blowing veal parm. Pricey, but definitely an experience worth having.

The place is rather small and it took a great deal of effort to get a reservation. Customer service was good-no complaints there. The complimentary bread and cheese were delicious! Now, the entrees were not so great. I think the dishes were a bit over priced for what you got---very small portions! It was totally not worth the money. I've had better Italian food elsewhere in NYC.

I am not sure what the hype is all about.  You are greeted by a hulking doorman who welcomes you into a dark brick face venue that is divided into three "sections".  We were seated by the kitchen and had a very loud woman/table next to us.  Okay, so maybe the loudness colored my review.  Food - Appetizers: Polpette was not dry so also good.  Fried zucchini flowers (stuffed w crab meat) was too mushy or buttery.  Chopped salad had too much dressing.  Entrees: spicy rigatoni very good. spaghetti w pomodoro good. Branzino (whole fish) was very good and moist.  Angel hair in olive oil -meh.  Verdict: Good food.   Complaint/Heads up: We were a party of 4 and said appetizers came in 3.  Waiter never asked us if we wanted extra so just added an extra zucchini flower ($8 extra) and polpette ($7 extra) and opened up 4 large bottles of San Pellegrino sparkling water (for my wife and our two tweenies) again without asking everytime we were done with a bottle and quite a sloppy pourer.  Branzino is market price so our fish must have been $26-30 per pound or $95.  They were polite but just presumptuous in not explaining/adding costs although I can see if they decided not to bother us with small details.  Carone would have received 3.5-4 stars IF it had just asked about water and adding extras. NYC is an expensive place to eat well and for the price, the food was good but not great.  On to the next "you gotta go eat there" restaurant.

Service was a little rushed but they brought the sexy back in big way. Food was superb. Wine was outstanding. Decor was that downtown cool that's long been absent from downtown. My friend, a CEO, who I had not seen in many years, loved it  -- and he's been everywhere and been to every great restaurant around the world. Yeah, Carbone kicked a lot of ass that night.

There was nothing wrong with Carbone, but I didn't love it.  It felt like a little Italian restaurant in the Village. . . until you looked at the menu and the prices.  It wanted to be Babbo but its offerings were more like a standard neighborhood Italian joint--not that there's anything inherently wrong with that.  Its menu read much like a menu at The Olive Garden would read, except the prices were three to four times higher.  Now, I'm not saying that Carbone was the same quality as The Olive Garden.  I'm definitely not saying that.  I'm saying the dishes were not particularly creative in any way.  They were classic Italian American dishes.  We started with a complimentary bread basket with some garlic bread in it.  (Sound familiar?)  We were also given some pickled cauliflower (admittedly, Olive Garden probably doesn't offer that) and some uninspired salamis.  It was all good but certainly nothing made us say "wow".  We once again got the zucchini flowers.  (Hey, when they're in season, what are you going to do?  You can't pass 'em up!)  Their batter was not sufficiently sturdy and their filling was forgettable.  (The filling had peekytoe crab in it but I literally can't remember it, just two days later.)  They were still good but they were not among my favorite zucchini blossoms, to be sure.  We ordered two pastas.  (In retrospect, I wish we had come hungrier and tried a secondi, but our stomachs wouldn't allow it.)  My wife got one of her favorites:  penne with vodka sauce, although their "creative twist" on this dish was to substitute rigatoni for penne.  (There was not culinary envelope pushing going on at Carbone.)  The dish was good.  It was solid.  But it certainly wasn't spectacular.  I got the "Granchio e Pepe".  I had to ask what this dish was.  Granchio is apparently Italian for crab.  It was a crab pasta dish.  It was okay.  It felt like tuna noodle casserole with crab substituted for tuna.  (Did I mention that no one was pushing any culinary envelopes at Carbone?)  I think we got dessert, but I can't remember that, either.  Now, admittedly I'm getting old but I think my inability to recall details of this meal has more to do with the vanilla nature of the food and less to do with my forgetfulness.  My general impression was that Carbone was okay.  But who wants to pay big bucks for okay?  Who wants to settle for "okay" in NYC?  I probably wouldn't go back to Carbone and in a few months I probably won't even remember why.

I went in thinking this restaurant might be over hyped. Au contraire! Food, service, everything was perfect. The house prosecco is dry, cold and delicious. The wine list is filled with very expensive options, but we found a very good French at reasonable cost. The thinly sliced soppressata and the marinated cauliflower served with the bread basket were just right. The caprese served with deliciously ripe tomatoes, as well as delicately sun dried cherry tomatoes and the house made mozzarella was a dream. Clams baked three different ways were delicious and the zucchini flowers topped with thin slices of poached zucchini really hit the spot. The spicy rigatoni was outstanding, and the side of fresh corn covered with shaved truffle is something I want to eat every day of my life. 
One thing I will change when I go back - I will stick to appetizers and pastas. The veal parmigiana was good, but among dishes that delivered such delicate and complex flavors, it was just ok. Same with the sea bass entree. Can't wait to go back, when I can get a reservation!

We celebrated my birthday here last week - we had trying to come here for a long time and were so glad that we finally made it and for a great celebration! First of all, the food is outstanding - everything was superb! the tasting that they bring to the table includes italian sausage, parma cheese, delicious bread, and vegetables. The appetizers were also delicious - we had the melon and the clams - then of course, we had the vodka pasta and the veal parmesan - all of which are superb and the portions enormous. But what I loved most was that every aspect of the place, from the tables, to the chairs, to the decor, to the waiters - everything was a table in brooklyn - the old real brooklyn. It was fantastic -

Spicy rigatoni. Lobster ravioli. Veal parm. Don't even think twice just order those and you'll have the best meal of your life. Seriously best food I've ever eaten in NYC the service was phenomenal I can't wait to come back.

Reviews are helpful if they tell you what to order or advice to skip the destination. I think this is a "skip-it". Everyone talks about the spicy rigatoni, right? And of course you were going to order it, because you almost have to. Well...its not that special. a cream and tomato sauce that reminds me of buffalo wing sauce. For the price and simply the meal, I think you should keep looking. I gave it 4 stars for ambiance and really, it equates to 80%, but I certainly think the food isn't quite worth the stop.

Incredible. Incredible food, people, ambiance, menu and wine. Great for special occasion meals or an expensive night on the town. Have to try the meatballs and the spicy pasta, along with almost everything else on the menu. The specials are always amazing and imported directly from Italy. We order a variety of dishes for two people and they were all amazing. The portions were a good size which is odd for a spot like this. Great for a date too. Carbone earned Michelin star for a reason; this is a must ad to your NY restaurant list.

Been putting off my 100th review for quite a long time, but I knew I wanted Carbone to take the spot. Came here with the wifey to celebrate myself entering Graduate school and had zero expectations even though I had seen numerous reviews. (mostly on the $75 veal parmesan)

The atmosphere here is excellent. It was incredible how small the place was without the seating being cramped, and I truly enjoyed the old school Italian mob restaurant vibe from the black and white tile floors to the waiter's burgundy tuxedos. 

Having had a reservation made on the OpenTable website, we were seated promptly in a nice cozy corner table for two. Before even meeting our waiter we were served some focaccia and a pretty plate of prosciutto which was more than perfect because I was already starving. 

For drinks we had a mai tai and a sarsaparilla which were both very tasty but a lil heavy on the ice. For dinner I ordered the spicy rigatoni vodka, an order of meatballs for the table, and my lady ordered the fettuccine con funghi. Midway into waiting for our meal I noticed another couple at the table next to us get a veal parm to split between the two of them and it looked incredible. I asked them how it was and the girl informed me that this was the only place she would ever order veal. (I'm getting that next time!)

When our meals came out I was ecstatic because it looked like everything I had hoped for. Presentation on point. The spicy rigatoni was cooked perfectly, the vodka sauce was not overly thick and had a little kick, but not overpowering whatsoever. Each bite was like a journey for my tastebuds. The fettuccine was cooked al dente and was incredibly savory. One complaint the wifey had was that it was a tad bit on the salty side, and while I agreed, we both would order it again. The meatballs were HUGE and way more than enough to add to our pasta. They were not too tough or too soft and had excellent flavor. Reminded me of my nonna's meatballs which is of course, a great thing. 

After we finished our meal we were more than stuffed but had to get a dessert as the waiter was walking around with a big dessert cart that smelled wonderful. We got the carrot cake and ginger ice-cream. THIS IS A MUST! the cake is cut into a crescent moon shape with a little dollop of ginger ice-cream in the middle and the two together are just heaven man really, you have to try it. We also had complimentary espresso and the waiter left an entire full bottle of sambuca on the table with us, so I totally took advantage and had at it. 

Overall I would come back again without a doubt. Loved everything about it, and while a little on the pricey side, one can't deny the enormous amount of food you get for the money.

Came here because of all the great reviews and it was hard to get reservations. So i had HIGH expectations. This is not your typical fancy place ie Per SE or Daniel. It is very old school italian joint. Our waiter was not the best. This is why i'm giving Carbone a 3 star. Time after time he keeps messing up our order. Not sure if it was language barrier since he didn't speak fluent English. We ordered the famous spicy rigatoni, but instead we got the tortelini. After we finished our pasta and appetizers, he came and gave us the dessert menu and we told him that we haven't gotten our main courses yet . And our main course took over 45 mins  to cook. I seriously think he forgot about us. We were so annoyed that we told him that if they didn't make it we were going to cancel the dish. And miraculously the pork chops showed up 5 mins later. Also, we asked for a bottle of wine and he sends the wine sommelier to give my friend a glass instead. Sigh..So i'm not sure what happened, but for a place that has high standards for service, I expected exceptional service.
As for the food, the pizza bread was good. The caprese salad and prosciutto/melon app were fresh and delicious. The spicy rigatoni was ok. Crespelle Verde was different. It's like a crepe pasta. The pork chops were typical. Overall, i think it's a good joint but not the BEST i have. 
I personally like the dishes at Felidia and the service was better there too.

For what it's worth, this is bothering me still so I'm writing a review nearly two months later. came here on a work lunch, and food was excellent. But, were five girls, and while we did get a lunch budget from our firms it's not unlimited - and we like sharing. So we first asked if we could get the meatballs as an appetizer, and our pushy waiter said that was really better as a side with pasta (which while I do get, the rigatoni and the meatballs are in two different sauces, and meatballs are appetizers at plenty of Italian restaurants,, but whatever). Then we ask how big the meatballs are and how many - he said 3, and made them sound pretty small and nearly forced us into getting an extra. And while we could have said no, he really convinced us they weren't capable of being split. First lie - the meatballs were huge and we ended up taking our entire extra meatballs we paid $7 for home. 

 Then, two of us just wanted rigatoni, but the remaining three wanted to just have a taste of the pasta. So they decided decided to split the spicy rigatoni dish and two entrees. When it arrived, the pasta was split into three dishes. And while the portions looked large for a three way split, the waiter had said nothing about half orders (which aren't on the menu) so we thought they were just being generous - BOY we're we wrong. In the end, the waiter charged us for 3 half orders - and once again, one of those orders went nearly untouched.  What kind of restaurant - especially one SO EXPENSIVE - there is no lunch menu so we were paying full price for lunch - charges you for half orders without asking?! Because we were rushing back to work, i just paid the bill and left. Three of us ended up having to split anything over budget, which was probably nearly $30 more than we should have spent because of the meatball and pasta we didn't need but were convinced we had to get and/or not informed we were getting. 

The food is good, but like all major food group restaurants is not that special for the price, and the ambience is great, but I don't need to be pushed into ordering things when I don't want or need them and I do NOT want to be charged for food I didn't know I was ordering without being told. Appalled that such a "classy" place such as Carbone would have waiters akin to used car salesman (dramatic, yes, but how we felt).  I've now told like everyone I've met this story so I hope it doesn't happen to them - and if I ever am forced to go back, you better believe I'm ordering what I want when I want how I want, and taking the time to complain when I am unfairly charged for something I didn't want or need. Rude.

My children made a reservation the obligatory 3 months in advance for our anniversary reservation. We experienced unexpected 3 hour traffic on our trip to the restaurant which normally would take 30 minutes. We attempted to call many times to inform of this but the recording prompted us to email which we were unable to do en route. When we arrived 45 minutes late we were curtly told we could no longer be accommodated even though there were many empty tables visible. When I explained our travel issues as well as the fact that our children had generously gifted us this dinner for our 39th anniversary they were unfazed and unimpressed. Our disappointment was unimaginable. I have survived cancer - I can survive the rest of my life never going to Carbone.

Everyone was incredibly funny, helpful, and cordial. I don't care what anyone else says, but I came for the tableside Caesar and the spicy rigatoni vodka, and I was not let down at all. AT ALL. I loved the texture of the gigantic crouton and the peppery bite was a bit of a surprise. The salad was well worth the room in my tummy.  The pasta is amazing - sauce was perfectly creamy and tomato-y, nice balance of acid and sweetness and the rigatoni were perfectly al dente. Also the meatballs were really good.

We could have lived without the Ribeye Diana, which was great, but we were just incredibly full by the time it arrived at our table.  Date has a nut allergy, which we alerted the captain before ordering, but the carpaccio had the garnish of walnuts on it. Date didn't die, crisis averted, but that would have been disastrous. 

If anything, just order a nice bottle of wine, the Caesar, the spicy rigatoni vodka with meatballs and you're golden. or you know, just eat everything, and I think you'd still be golden.

My boyfriend and I came here for our 4 year anniversary, and it was definitely memorable. We had reservations for 9:45 and was seated shortly after arrival. It was pretty loud, due to the Italian music they were blasting so it was hard to hear the specials of the night from our waiter. We ended up ordering the meatballs as an appetizer, spicy rigatoni vodka for me, ribeye diana for him, and the corn tartufato along with the potatoes louie as sides for us to share. 

Before our appetizer was served, they brought us over four complimentary samples of bread, cauliflower, cheese, and prosciutto. Everything was amazing besides the cauliflower. i honestly do not even recommend trying it. Followed by this, we were given our appetizer, and lets just say the meatballs were the size of a baseball and full of flavor. My tastebuds couldn't get enough. Our entrees were over the top, incredible. The spicy rigatoni vodka was AMAZING. The ribeye diana, was very juicy and just melts in your mouth. We couldn't have asked for a better meal. The bill came out to around $200, which I think was great given the amount of food we ate the how flavorful everything was. We will definitely be back again!

 NOTE: we didn't order any drinks, so if you are planning to drink the cost will definitely be higher...

Old-school, throwback menu, service that caters to your every whim, and retro Rat Pack glam, this is one of the best dinners I've ever had. 

I went last winter with my travel companion and one of his friends who is the CEO of a large company, and his daughter.  He pulled some serious strings to get a reservation for four on a weeknight, and I enjoyed every last bite that entered my mouth.  

It was a rainy night and we were lucky enough to find a cab outside our hotel, a chariot to a magical land of fine Italian cuisine, fit for royalty.  

We each tried something different, but the most impressive dish by far was the Veal Parmesan, Carbone's signature dish, of sorts.  I was the lucky recipient of all the left-overs.  We toted that unmistakable Carbone bag all over NYC with us the next day, on the train, through the airport, and back home.  I devoured every last bite the next evening, after having made it home.  

I can only dream of having the opportunity to dine here once again.  I would call myself a lucky girl to have dined at five of the toughest reservations in NYC:  Carbone, Rao's, 11 Madison Park, Per Se, and Gramercy Tavern.
The food and atmosphere are amazing. A bit salty but delicious. Love the cocktails made fully by hand. Sal was a great waiter. Tiramisu is fantastic. Try the vodka pasta and the amazing corn.

I'm catching up on a visit here at the end of July.  This place is expensive, by anyone's standards.  You pay more than the experience is really worth...dinner for 2 with tax and tip just over $500.  There is a little too much shtick to the place...the fake hit man outside the front door, the waiters who act all chummy and use the exact same phraseology on every guest at every table (like I saw the matinee and evening show of the same show).

Some of the food is great, such as the veal parmigiana which is the best I've ever had, and I grew up in Brooklyn and have it at many excellent places over nearly 60 years. Theirs is simply the best I've had...a delicate chop that is pounded, breaded. fried and then just the perfect amount of sauce and cheese (actually lightly done, but perfect), that you really didn't even need a knife as the meat was so tender.  The bone from the chop was roasted and presented alongside the veal, and again was the most tender veal rib bone I've ever chewed into...it was veal "two ways!"  The dish was intoxicatingly good.  My wife had the linguine vongole which was way too garlicky and way too salty and used what looked like basic supermarket pasta...quite a contrast to the noticeably delicate, first class, preparation of the veal parm.  I love linguine with clam sauce and it was causing burning pain on our palates.  I should mention that the Caesar Salad prepared tableside was also about as good as I have ever had.

The wine list is stupid expensive with obscene price markups...shame on you, seriously shame on you.  You are going to drink very mediocre wines unless you spend close to $200/bottle.  Corkage is $85/bottle (which I didn't do, but should have).  This alone would be reason for me to write the place off...except for the fact that they have this veal parm that I daydream about.

Dessert was a hazelnut tiramisu that was also really excellent.

In short, I'd go back for the veal parmigiana, maybe try the spicy rigatoni I've read about, possibly have the Caesar Salad, and bring my own wine.

Food is just ok, service is abhorrent, overall this place was a pretty big disappointment... We came for my husbands birthday and our waiter was impatient, pompous, rude, and eager to get us ordered, fed and out. (He serviced the table next to us in exactly the same fashion, so I'm certain it was him, and not anything particular about us)... It was in a nutshell not the experience we had hoped for given the establishment's price point. Food is ok - we weren't expecting to be blown away by the food (and we weren't), but thought the premium paid here would go towards a nice atmosphere and experience,  but we received neither of these things. And our reservations was at 5:30 on a weeknight, so it was not particularly busy.  Will never be back and wouldn't recommend - meatballs are better at Frankie's and pasta is better at Scarpetta.

This is one of the best meals I have had in NYC and I have lived there for 15 years.  They really do things well.  When you walk in, you will feel like you walked back in time.  From the old school dude working the door to the even older-school (not a word), dude working the desk  You will also be waited on by a guy wearing a shirt and tie, most likely having been there for years.  

Menu: there is not a single thing on the menu that doesnt sound awesome and not a single thing that we ordered didnt cover what we thought it would.  You must order the Caesar salad, its delicious.

 As several people have mentioned, the spicey rigatoni was so great.  I didnt share it  With anyone.  

The bread that they bring to the table at the beginning is amazing too.  Used most of it to sop up the left overs of the mussels (you must order them too).

Service: The service here is fantastic.  They will take care of you and you wont want for a single thing before they grab you and bring you what you need. 

Worth every single dollar you spend here and you will spend a bunch.  Steep!!

Food was excellent, especially the rigatoni and veal parmesan! The wine selection was varied, which allowed for plenty of tasty drinks with dinner. The atmosphere is old school Italian - reminded me of a scene out of The Godfather. You half expected the mob to be wheeling and dealing at the tables. The noise level was a little too loud, it could just be the large parties sitting next to us. We're told celebrity sightings were not uncommon, as evidenced by an unassuming A-Rod at the table next to us.

Went tonight for dinner with my son and husband.  We always plan one special night out when we visit NYC.  A little disappointed in our choice tonight.  Our reservation was at 5:00.  We were seated in the corner of the back room.  The music was so loud we couldn't hear half of the features our server was telling us.  

We let our server recommend most of what we ordered.  We started off with a glass of wine for myself and an old fashioned for our son.  He didn't rave about the cocktail, so I assume it was fine.  Table bread was delicious as was the salami and pickled cauliflower.  All were complimentary.

The clams were good.  There were supposed to be 3 of 3 differently prepared clams.  Instead, there were 4 of each, since  they were on the smaller side.  We ordered the rigatoni, which my son loved.  I guess I'm a bit harder to please because I wasn't overly impressed.  We also had the tortellini and fish filet.  As a side we ordered the corn.  It was pretty good.   We opted to pass on dessert.  

For me, the food was good, but not the best I've ever had.  We waited for over 20 minutes after we finished before our server had time to check back with us about dessert.  By that time, we were out of the mood.  The server simply had too many covers (17).  Entirely too many for a restaurant in this price range. 

I suppose the lack of attention may have skewed my opinion, but service is a huge part of fine dining.  I like to have dinner and experience.  Unfortunately, that didn't happen tonight!

While this was not my first time at Carbone, I do think it will unfortunately be my last. We had a phenomenal waiter and the sommelier was absolutely brilliant and lovely, the food was sub par- at best. We ordered things we had there before- the baked clams and the spicy rigatoni. The rigatoni remained delicious, but the clams were truly overcooked- something I've never experienced in my life- and the sea urchin on three was SO overly fishy (and as someone who eats fish 4 nights a week- I don't ever have this issue).
