The special of the night was Marios meatballs-  but meatballs for $30? I'm not cheap (I mean, obviously, we eat at Carbone) but that is ridiculous. We tried them, and they were fine, but my aunt in New Jersey could make better. 

The veal parm was delicious, as usual, but not better than any other parm (chicken, eggplant, or otherwise) at any other Italian spot (looking @ you Parm). The real kicker in this meal though-  I wanted something simple- we had so much red sauce already, and I had heard mixed reviews of the other macaroni, but figured I'd give it a whirl. I ordered the Angel Hair, which didn't get the greatest response from the waiter- but I explained my reasoning and while he understood he suggested adding the Madagascar Shrimp "Shrimp Su'Modo" to it to make it more interesting- alright, I'll bite. He asked how many pieces I wanted (mind you he had the menu in his hand)- and I said, oh I don't know, 3? 

Now having actually eaten shrimp in Mauritius (next to Madagascar) a few years ago, and the shrimp being large, but no larger than a prawn, I thought nothing of this order- right? Well- out comes HUGE shrimp.  How exciting! One bite- and I wasn't sure if it was shrimp, or a tire. I was shocked. And the pasta- my goodness! Didn't taste homemade at all and was DRENCHED in oil that it could have lubed up the tire shrimp in an auto shop. 

To top it off- each shrimp was $22. The worst pasta dish of my life cost me $90. That is Carbone.

my 33rd birthday tonight for weeks I wondered where to go and finally decided on here since I am a lover of alla vodka. if you are a lover of alla vodka like myself you need to come here! seriously the best I ever had. I will dream about it tonight. the mozzarella here is also the coolest and most delicious thing ever. the service here is beyond amazing and was perfect for my birthday. no other restaurants can compare after our captain/waiter here. he was awesome. I only wish we had gotten the meatballs to share but with just a bunch of girls and only my husband we couldn't lol. us girls eat like birds. 

this place was just perfect and probably one of the best dining experiences I've ever had. and I go out a lot and eat at very nice places.

This is a gem in the village! My team from work made a reservation for 8, which I think is the maximum number of people you can bring to the restaurant without making a private event. We were able to try so many different dishes, and everything was phenomenal! The old school ambiance was awesome and the service was exceptional. I'd recommend going as a group so you can try

Classy Carbone! Well, there aren't many places in NY with quite this feel.
The food is great but it's all about the atmosphere in my opinion. It's lively, it's old school NY, wonderful service, great crowd (a mix of Euros and show biz types). While it sounds pretentious, it's actually not at all. Great place to relax & have a great meal in a fun neighborhood.

Omg!!!! Sexy, romantic, cool, family friendly ambiancey. Hospitable hostess, attentive waitstaff, quick service, AMAZING FOOD. I repeat AMAZING FOOD!!!!!!!!!!!! The best minestrone soup (I hate minestrone soup, or atleast I thought I did) I ever ate!! The golf ball sized meatballs are to die for. Waiiiiitttt.... the complimentary fresh homemade mozzarella and salami served with a crusty piece of bread soaked in sauce was the kick off to this magical palate ride. The portions are shareable so you know I ate the left over balls as a sandwich  for lunch the ver y next day. yummm!! Please go try!y

One of the best Italian restaurants I have ever been to. I even saw Chris Rock dining here when I went! He seemed to be a regular. The veal Parmesan was out of this universe! I've never tasted anything like it. Also the spicy pasta was very good. If you order the Cesar salad you will be very happy, they come to your table and make it nice and fresh for you. Great food! Friendly staff!

My children gave me a special birthday dinner at this lovely restaurant on September 18.  The food was excellent as well as the service.  This restaurant was especially important to my daughter who made sure to have reservations 30 days in advance.  All went well until two men were seated in the corner less than two feet from our table.  Dressed inappropriately they then proceeded to have loud video chats with others not once but twice.  They also began taking flash photographs of their meal a number of times. Considering how small this restaurant is I don't see how the waiter couldn't have noticed.  My son wanted to speak with these men but I didn't want to ruin our meal.  But it pretty much was anyway and when pointed out to the waiter he said he'd tell management which meant he'd do nothing.  Such a lousy way to end a special day.
Where do I begin! One of the best italian restaurants I have ever been to! Must get the spicy rigatoni and the carrot cake- both amazing! Will definitely be back

I came here for dinner in 2013 with a group and we had a great time.  It was pretty difficult to get a reservation, and ours was pretty late - around 9:30.

We ordered family style and shared:
- caesar salad, which was great - they make it at the table for me
- carpaccio was one of best I've had
- octopus had great flavor and was grilled perfectly
- oysters were fresh and tasty
- tuna tartare was pretty good 
- the lobster fra diavolo was solid but could've been a bit spicier - it came in the lobster shell to the table
-  the lobster mezzaluna actually wasn't that great, and it's supposed to be a signature disk
- the porterhouse for 2 was good - the filet side was better than the other in my opinion, and it was cooked to a perfect medium rare
- veal parmigiana was a huge portion (it's $50), and if I had ordered that alone I could've eaten it for 3 days - I thought it was also one of the best veal that I've had.

We were too full for desert and we ordered way too much for 6 people. It was overall a solid meal and I will be back eventually.

Amazing restaurant! Food was great! Service was great ! Expensive but worth it m. HOWEVER they withdraw to much money out my account. I signed for $190 and they took $261 instead. I'm very upset with that !

From the minute you step foot into this unbelievable dining establishment your fine dining experience begins. 

The ambiance at Carbone takes you back to an old-world Italian joint. Everything here is perfection, from the decore to the service to the food. 

As a self-proclaimed penne ala vodka aficionado, I will confidently say that the spicy rigatoni lives up to its reputation. The portion is not huge, but man is every bite good. The pasta is not drowning in sauce, and the pasta is perfectly cooked. A must try. 

The caprese salad is another stand out dish on Carbone's menu, and is a true testament to the quality of the restaurant. The homemade mozzarella cheese is so fresh, as are the heirloom tomatoes that accompany it. Your server comes to the table with cooking scissors and cuts the fresh ball of cheese right in front of your eyes. 

As someone who is happy to sit on my couch in a sweatshirt and order in delivery any night of the week, do trust me in saying that this place is worth making a reservation 1 month out and worth the hefty price tag your meal is sure to come with... Remember, you're paying for an experience, not just a meal!

Great place...can't wait to come back. Classy atmosphere and the chef made the best lobster ravioli I've ever had. Waiters knew their stuff and were attentive. Kudos to the manager for running a tight ship.
I had the cesear salad, spicy vodka pasta, and meatballs. Loved it. Fairly simple dishes but very well done and delicious. Note to self: try the lobster ravioli next time.
Very tough to get a reservation but if you do it is well worth it. Spicy rigatoni is amazing. Great atmosphere and wait staff is incredible. Great restaurant for special occasions/celebrations.
This restaurant is small but the ambience is happening.  I really enjoyed the minestrone soup. The pasta is delicious, and my favorite was the fresh home made mozzarella. I truly recommend Carbone!

Went with a group of six. First they lost our reservation, then we waited 45 mins for our table. At these prices they should have a better host system. Food was good but nothing to splurge on. Oh and check your bill, the waiters like to "decide" you need more than one order of things...without asking. Del Posto, dell'anima, da umberto blow this out of the water.

Spicy rigatoni vodka is famous for a reason. Absolutely incredible. And the MEATBALLS. Oh my god. The meatballs. Like absolutely nothing you have ever had before. Really hard to get a reservation so we opted for 5:30 rather than 10:30. Turned out well because we basically had the restaurant to ourselves the first half of our meal. Lovely restaurant and waiters. Will definitely be returning.

Overall great meal and great experience. The service was truly top notch. Food highlights include the veal parm, rigatoni, prosciutto mozzarella, and carrot cake.

One critical note, we ordered a special: the tortellini. They didn't tell us the price before and we had expected it to be more or less in line with the prices on the regular menu. Big mistake, huge! $130 for eight pieces of cheese stuffed pasta. One star docked for the robbery.

Wonderful customer service. We were late for our reservation so they reheated my soup when I arrived (our friends had ordered in advance) and replaced my appetizer. 

I got a salad but my friends raved about the pasta and the mozzarella cutting table side is a sight to be seen.

This is probably one of the best dining experiences, in terms of food, service, and ambience, I've had in a very very long time. Maybe one of the best ever. The second you walk into the door, you enter another world. You feel like you have been brought back in time to the 30s, 40s, with the music, the staff dressed in suits and the decor. This is the first time ever at a restaurant I forgot about where I actually was. It did not register to me it was 2016 and I was in Greenwich Village in New York City at 6 pm on a Friday and I LOVED that. Everything we ordered was delicious. The bread and cheese were amazing. The veal parmesan and the spicy rigatoni were sooooo good. I was so sad when the plate was cleared. The cheesecake was one of the best cheesecakes I've had as well. Also the service was outstanding. Never in my life have I had a waitstaff, when I got up to go to the bathroom, refold my napkin to make sure it was properly presented when I got back. Also, they would hold my chair open for me and helped me put on my coat. They were very attentive. That is a rarity in NYC. Incredible dining experience.

My wife and I visited NYC for our 10 year anniversary this week as well as the NYC marathon.  I made a reservation at Carbone one month in advance to the day, which is pretty much the only way to get a table during normal dining hours.

The food here was excellent - the best Italian I've ever had!  We split the prosciutto and mozzarella appetizer, spicy vodka rigatoni, lobster ravioli, and meatballs.  We also had a piece of coconut pie that was the best I've ever had.  They do a nice old fashioned as well.  The rigatoni was our favorite although everything was excellent.

The service however was subpar.  Our waiter was pretentious, and rarely checked on us except to take our order and deliver our food.  We waited nearly 20 minutes after we were done to get our check.  When paying $100 a person or so for dinner, I expect better service.

All in all, the quality of the food made up for the poor service.

Awesome. Came here for an early reservation on a Saturday night. You go to your table like something out of Goodfellas with well dressed waiters greeting you, Sinatra playing and a classy atmosphere. The waiters (at least ours) have an Italian schtick - presenting the menu with "everything is beautiful" "I got friends in the back" and other catch phrases. It plays well. Off the bat you get a hunk of pecorino , an amazing breadbasket, some salami and some pickled cauliflower. All delicious. The sommelier is super helpful and friendly and the cocktails are well made and simple. We ordered the baked clams (amazing) the spicy rigotoni (amazing) the meatballs ( amazing) the veal Parmesan (very good) the carrot cake (good) and the Nutella tiramisu (solid). The service is fantastic and makes the experience. The only reason for the four is the deserts were too big and the bathroom was ok...but other than that - this is a 5. Can't wait to come back!

This place is worth all of the hype, all of the praise, and all of the price. 

Without a doubt the best Italian meal I've ever had, and may have dethroned ABC Kitchen as the best meal I've actually ever eaten. 

Oysters, Caesar Salad, Spicy Rigatoni, Tortellini Ragu, Veal Parmesan, Coconut Cream pie. Everyone one of those things I just listed were the best versions of those I've ever eaten. 

We asked for a moderately priced, full-bodied and dry Italian wine that that was perfect. 

And last but not least, Ryan, our server, was probably the best and most "with it" server we've ever gotten. He immediately picked up on the vibe of our table, was honest about the menu and never really led us astray. He especially took care of us knowing I was celebrating a birthday, which made everything all the better.

Simply amazing!  I made a reservation for dinner with a friend last night while we were in town on business.  Love the old school vibe of this place along with the professional service.  They started us off with bread, pickled cauliflower, cheese and salami to start (nice touch) - it paired nicely with my Italian rose...so tasty!  We ended up sharing the spicy rigatoni vodka (one of the best things I have ever tasted and am seriously craving it while writing this review) with meatballs, the veal marsala and artichoke hearts...quality ingredients served simply.  A definite must visit in NYC!
Worth every penny! Don't skip out on the perfect oysters, pasta, veal, salads and dessert, it was an unbelievable meal. The service was also fantastic!

I love this place so much, it's so cute and romantic. Impossible to get a reservation but so happy we booked a month in advance for my birthday. I ordered the Rigatoni with vodka sauce - it was incredible! The bread was also amazing, so soft with red tomatoes. My boyfriend got the clams spaghetti, he liked it but I hate clams so didn't try it. I will definitely be coming back here again. Highly recommended!

Okay so, I spent this past summer in NYC working and found myself at Carbone way more often than should be acceptable. That being said, allow me to give you the run through...

First and foremost, this is the home of the best meal that I have ever had, so there.

Expensive? Yes. 
Worth it? Yes. 
Hard reservation? Yes. 
Special occasion? Yes. 
Date night? Yes. 
Whenever? Yes.

So, while the bill will total up to not exactly what you may be used to be paying for, you absolutely get what you pay for here. I have extensively tried the menu and have yet to be displeased with a single item. 

The bread basket and antipasto given upon arrival is divine; I could live off of the focaccia and tomato bread. 

The wine list is thorough and the staff is wildly helpful with pairings and recommendations.

I haven't tried their cocktails, but friends who have did not complain. 

As for the main dishes and sides, my number one, do not miss choices are he creamed truffle corn and the spicy rigatoni. After all, those dishes are what Carbone is known for. 

The tortellini with ragu is also magnificent. The lobster ravioli literally has me salivating just thinking about it. The meatballs will forever taint your experience with every other meatball that you will ever eat. The truffle mushrooms were definitely delicious, but not something that I find myself craving. As for desserts, I never have room myself, but have had nibbles of the carrot cake (amaze) and their coconut cream pie (best ever).

Everyone from the hosts to the wait staff to the bartender is pleasant every single time. 

Plan ahead, make that weeks-prior reservation, don't eat beforehand, and enjoy every bite. I guarantee it won't compare to anywhere else.

My husband and I had a 2pm lunch reservation and we're running a few minutes late. By 2:15pm we were told the kitchen is closed with no further explanation or help. We had tried calling in advance to see if they could push us to a later reservation but they only answer to an email service. We were not able to get through. We were incredibly frustrated with the lack of customer service and attitude we received at the door. I don't care how good the food is, when the staff is that rude and unaccommodating, it ruins the experience and isn't worth the money. We will never try to go here again.

5 all around. The pastas are fantastic!

Bake clams 
Penne alla vodka (the best)
Linguini with clams 
Tortellini with meat ragu (very close second) 
Veal parm

Great pastas, perfectly al dente. The place is small and cozy, so be prepared to sit close to your friends and the table next to you.  We were a table of 4 and ordered 2 appys, 2 pastas, 2 entrees, 1 side, unfortunately no room for dessert.  Beef carpaccio and mussels to start were amazing.  I could fill myself up with their delicious bread and the mussel broth.  Spicy rigatoni is a must-order and the tortellini was super cheesy/rich. Best to share your plates otherwise you may fill yourself up after 2 pieces of tortellini!  Scallops were a nice counter to the heavier pasta dishes, nicely cooked and yummy.  The chicken massimo was a bit disappointing since it was so salty.  Artichoke hearts were a good dish to help balance the meal, it has a kick to it so don't order if you don't like spicy.  We had leftover pasta to take home (tortellini) but we weren't super hungry that night, so the amount could be perfect for 4 people if you go in hungry.

Minus 1 star just due to the awkwardness of sitting next to the bar and at a small table, since the place is small, small tables come with the territory.  But patrons at the bar were literally hovering over J due to how crammed the quarters are, so we had to talk a little bit louder since he felt like he was more a part of their conversation than ours.  Our table could barely hold all the plates of food and glasses so it was a game of Tetris each time new plates arrived.

I cannot have more nice things to say about this establishment.  The staff was so welcoming, funny, generous - top notch all around.

The restaurant is very traditional in its flavors and they execute their menu splendidly.

This may be one of my favorite NYC restaurants!  At first, I was really debating on giving this place only four stars because the first time I tried coming here, the reservation process got all confusing and basically we got bumped for Derek Jeter.  I do feel like they try and keep this place uber exclusive.  We finally got to attend this place a month later, and boy was it worth it!

Food: the bread basket was delicious!  I ate two pieces!  we started off with the baked clams and they were great!  So full of flavor!  My only gripe is they ran out of the uni one :(. Then we shared the spicy rigatoni...the whole point of coming, and I'm not even a pasta person.  Wow! This was an orgasm with every bite...yes, believe the hype!  You also must order the side of meatballs!  The combination of pork, beef, and veal were to die for!  Lastly, I hate veal and haven't had it in over 10 years, but was told it was one of their signature dishes.   We were thinking, $65?!?  TOTALLY WORTH IT and phenomenal!!!  Something about their sauce being so simple yet packed with flavor.  The veal was so tender!  Everything was so flavorful without any ingredient being over powering!  We were so stuffed by the end of dinner, and regret not getting a dessert..

Ambiance:  very dark with an old school Italian restaurant vibe.  Waiters in maroon tuxedos.  Artwork is very interesting, it doesn't really match, yet it works.  The music consists of all my favorite oldies.  Service is impeccable!

I would highly recommend this place!!

Landing a reservation at Carbone at a normal time for dinner is nearly impossible.  I decided to finally give in to a 6:30 PM reservation for the boyfriend's birthday.  Mind you, we were still eating dinner at 8:30 and some tables were empty (hmmmmm!!)

The ambiance and service are awesome - real Godfather / old school Italian style.  Simple, good Italian food should never cost as much as they charge, but I'll let it pass since the overall experience on this special occasion was great.  

They start you off with lots of complimentary bites - fresh chunks of Parmigiano-Reggiano (cut straight out of a huge wheel), pepperoni, pickled giardiniera, and a bread basket with delicious tomato pasted focaccia that I needed more of.  We started with cocktails - I got my go-to Manhattan and he got the Whiskey Sour (which he wasn't really fond of).  The rest of the evening consisted of glasses of vino - I highly recommend the Barolo!  

To start, we shared the baked clams (would skip this) and the Caesar alla ZZ (awesome freshly-baked large croutons).  For our main, we shared an order of the spicy rigatoni and the veal Parmesan.  Both dishes tasted good, but again.. not worth the price point.

For dessert, we had a slice of their very tall carrot cake (quite yummy).  They provided us with complimentary rainbow cookies (I've had better) and an Italian digestif.

Like I said, the food is good but nothing extraordinary.  The overall ambiance and complimentary treats are what makes the experience great.   You must go once!

Fantastic. Period. Make it a point to dive into the pastas. The meats are great but you can get meat anywhere. You cannot get pasta that tastes this good from many places. Just gonna say the spicy rigatoni and tortellini are fire. Order them. For dessert get whichever dessert had the Nutella ice cream. That is all.

It's a very nice ambiance and I would say it could be chosen for a romantic place to. The food and service was great, staff were so attentive but one of the reason I give the 4 star is, our waiter during the menu introduction his body language wasn't very professional . I felt his entire body was over our table and the way he was resting his hands on our table and leaning forward made me uncomfortable. And another reason for giving them 4 star is the lady next to our table while leaving she knocked the all the sauce on our table and was a big mess and in such an expensive place I was expecting the waiter to change the table cloth and not covering the mess by napkin which was a total off situation for us and not impressing otherwise food was great

Waiters are nice but the food is over rated it's a typical New York tourist place where people not from here go to try "authentic Italian" it's one step above an Olive Garden and the waiters although nice have fake accents, one of my waiters when I asked what part of the city he's from (because of his accent) said he is actually from Minnesota. Ravioli truffle is 150 bucks and its ravioli with line little shaved truffle. Order meatballs and it was suppose to come with three but the waiter "because he liked me" said he would take care of us, and ended up only bringing us two meatballs. Stupid don't waste your time unless you're into fake cheese tourist crap. Go to little Italy and walk into any restaurant. And it will be ten times better and not even a quarter of the price.

Crowded & loud, populated by a very young group overly impressed with their ability to have gotten reservations (I know this because we were seated elbow-to-elbow with 2 couples who kept sharing their "how we got in" stories across our table). 

The wine steward knew nothing about wine, the service was spotty and the rigatoni was overcooked.

The only bright spot:  it's not terribly expensive (except the truly horrendous wine I was talked into instead of the delightful Amaroni I actually requested).  

The highlight:  no-one either noticed or cared that we drank none of the wine and left quickly.  They are trendy & busy and they know it.  One customer's opinion matters little to them.

If you are planning a nice Italian dining experience in the city stick to Il Molino - they'll actually notice you are there . . .

We went to Carbone last night for my husband's bday and it 100% lived up to the hype. We looked at Yelp reviews and asked friends for their recommendations and the general consensus was to go with the spicy rigatoni and the veal parm. Both were fantastic. I am not typically a veal lover but this was absolutely delicious. The rigatoni was not spicy (to me) but still definitely worth ordering. We also had the Caesar salad, which they make table side, and the escarole. I was so stuffed after but we really had a fantastic meal and would highly recommend to anyone. The staff was also very professional and accommodating. Aside it being very hard to get a reservation, the entire experience was top notch.
The food was extremely good. The vibe and ambiance is perfect.  The issue is the arrogant waiter.  With the price for dinner for 2 service was terrible

Small spot - packs a big punch when it comes to food. Order the ceasar salad and chopped salad (Get both, ceasar preferred), Tuna crudo appetizer special (expensive at $40, so make sure you ask about prices, but absolutely worth it), oyster special (still appetizer - this was superb). Next was Entree - Obviously everyone gets the spicy rigatoni (a bit heavy on the sauce but very good) and the Veal Parm (another classic here) was a bit salty but the meat was well cooked. Dessert - carrot cake (don't ask, just get it), tiramisu was good too. Lastly on the wine - its expensive but you already knew that :) Get a bottle of the Polvento 2010 (Set you back about $130 but worth it). Bottom line, great food, excellent service - you get what you pay for!

This place tries to recreate the whole old school Italian movie vibe. It does a good job in terms of the ambiance, however, food wise it fell short for me. First, if you don't order a bottle of wine (or several) expect them not to go much the distance for you service wise . I had a glass of wine and cocktail. I get it, you're a business, but it starts the experience off on the wrong footing for a customer. I had a salad, it was alright but nothing worth remembering. I moved onto the linguine vongole. It was like eating a salt lick and barely edible (and I like my salt). My friend had the tortellini al ragu. She liked it and I had a bite. It was alright but again nothing that made me want to come back again. Portions are small for a pasta dish in an Italian restaurant btw. We had a cheesecake which was the best part of the meal for me and was just rich enough. To sum up, if you want to check out this place to say you did and take in a bit of nostalgic old school vibe, go for it . But there are better authentic Italian places in NYC area for a second meal. Sometimes ambiance is just not enough.

Honestly, thinking about our dinner at Carbone conjures up so many feelings I'm getting emotional writing this. It's hard to know where to begin, but I'll first say it lives up to all the hype, and it's everything you hope it will be. 

You walk into a cozy little restaurant with exposed brick, white table cloths, red leather wood chairs and Frank Sinatra playing overhead, and as soon as you sit down you're presented with a bread basket that would make a delicious light meal in itself, by a friendly server who greets you like a long lost friend. It's New York Italian at its very best, a joint the mob would frequent, which is really what everyone's thinking when they go to a fancy Italian place. 

But that's enough of my gushing, here's what's important: 

Email them first thing, 9 am 30 days before you want to eat there. The most difficult part of dining at Carbone is getting in the door, it books lightning fast. I can't emphasize this enough. 

Now to the fun part, we were told by our server that we ordered perfectly, and I don't know if I'd try anything else because I couldn't bear not eating one thing that we ordered. Everything we had was unbelievable. I can't stress that enough. It's one of those meals that makes you happy to be alive, and when you're dieting you daydream about. It's one of the best meals we've ever had. 

Appetizers: 

prosciutto & mozz 

Salad: 

Caesar Salad (sounds run of the mill but it is not, believe me) 

Pasta: 

Spicy Rigatoni 

An order of meatballs

Entrees: 

Shrimp Su'modo 
Ribeye Diana 

Vegetable: 

Squash Agrodolce 

Dessert: 

Cheesecake

TRUE ITALIAN!! If you are looking for something authentic, this is the place for you. Walked in and it immediately had an atmosphere that was hard to resist. Sat down and was served with various breads, cheeses, and veggies. The food is simply amazing! The spicy vodka sauce was so smooth and perfect. Meatballs were amazing and the ragu melted in your mouth. Hands down my favorite Italian restaurant.

Carbone is sooo delicious and so much fun!!! All the food is excellent except for the Dover sole, for the price you'd expect it to be a little fresher. But, the spicy rigatoni vodka is just to die for, it must be 50% butter and I'm okay with that. I love the atmosphere here, it's really special and fun.

It's not every day that a restaurant regarded as "the best Italian spot in the city" lives up to its hype; however, in the case of Carbone, the hype was real. In a city with an Italian joint on every block, Carbone sets itself a apart. From the ambiance to food, it knocks it all out of the park. With waiters in tuxedos and a buzz in the air, you're immediately sent back in time. A giant menu with high prices should not deter you from this experience. We split the octopus appetizer and the osso bucco and spicy vodka rigatoni for dinner, and one was better than the next. Capped off with a curved slice of carrot cake and a couple limoncellos, and this was quite simply the perfect NYC Italian meal. Is it a little loud and over the top? Sure. But it's all part of the "scene" and worth the price of admission to experience this "event" at Carbone. Everyone should have a Saturday night dinner here in the village.

Delicious, but expensive, Italian food. Feels very authentic

Pros:
+Spicy rigatoni was some of the best pasta I've had. Perfect firmness. Rich, creamy sauce that didn't get heavy when cool
+Delicious veal parm. Well seasoned and tender
+Yummy baked clama
+Great bread and starters

Cons:
-Meatballs and veal parm were a bit on the salty side
-Service staff talks really fast

Amazing! If it were not so difficult to get into this restaurant I would be here way more often! The old school feel is grwat. I love the servers in burgundy tuxedos and the constant streaming of Sinatra! The eggplant stack was delicious and the vodka sauce left me wishing I could lick the plate. YUM!

An accidental 24 hours in New York (looking at you United, reliable purveyors of misery and delays) would have been an entirely freezing and frustrating affair en route to a wedding in Mumbai were it not for the opportunity it afforded me to attend a birthday lunch for a Gotham based girlfriend at Carbone. 

Utterly magic from start to finish - the chunks of Parmesan to start were just the right level of crystalline. The meat balls were so good (and it was so cold) that we shared another serving instead of birthday dessert. It's Italian American as supposed to full blown Italian - but it's seriously well executed. And served in a faultlessly in a cosy but crisp ambience. An absolutely first class lunch. It's not cheap. But in my book it's still great value. Tables can be difficult to book at normal times of day if you don't call reasonably in advance - plan well and arrive hungry!
Very cool & hip . Food is good and staff was nice . Hard to get reservation so plan ahead .

This place is the worst Italian I have ever eaten. They have one dish worthwhile which is the spicy rigatoni everything else including the awful super dare I call it borderline rac$st reservation system (heard from within they did a bit of research on you prior to emailing you back a yes or no) is miserable. I ate there and in vegas and both times were terrible. Go to the best place in town which is mullino nearby

Overall: Carbone is and has been one of my favorite restaurants in NYC since its opening.  It's exactly what you're looking for in an Italian restaurant: tucked away into a quiet corner of the village, it's mysterious from the outside and comes alive the minute you walk through the door.  Carbone is great for special occasions, but even better for no occasion whatsoever.

Atmosphere: The atmosphere is one of the most enjoyable aspects of Carbone.  Eating here is truly an experience and you will feel as though you've been transported back in time.  The music is FANTASTIC, the vibe is very relaxed, and each table feels private yet still apart of a larger production.

Food: People come to Carbone for the experience, but rave on and on afterwards because of the food.  I have never had a disappointing meal here.  Of course the bread basket is amazing (yes, pizza bread), the meatballs are heavenly, and the pasta divine...but we've also enjoyed the veal parmesan, the rib eye, and several fish options.  On this night, we shared the cesar salad (a must), the spicy rigatoni (lives up to the hype), the dover sole (as beautiful to eat as it is to look at), the ribeye Diana, potatoes louie (maybe our favorite part!!), and last but certainly not least, the carrot cake.  I wouldn't change a single thing about our menu, although I did miss the meatballs and will never go there again and forego them.  The portions are generous but you won't leave feeling overly stuffed.  

Service: Overall, service is great.  If I have any complaints about Carbone, they would most likely be due to service.  The service is excellent, the staff is very friendly and personable...but, they do tend to rush you.  Sitting down at a place like Carbone is not meant to last 45 minutes.  Each time I've been I have felt like we were rushed to make our orders, only to wait for up to an hour for some things to arrive.  It's not a deal breaker, but it can be a pain point in the overall experience.

Carbone is a NYC must. I went here about a week ago and still can't stop thinking about the whole experience. From the time you arrive to the meal itself, the whole thing is somewhat theatrical yet also partially classic New York. The food at Carbone is great - although I'd suggest skipping the Veal Parmesan and getting another main - but what really sets this place apart is the service and amazing staff. They really make you feel special and will go out of their way to put those extra touches on each part of your experience. Highly recommend at least coming to Carbone once if you are in NYC but make sure to get a reservation in advance.

The spicy rigatoni vodka is, as expected, the best part of every Carbone meal - the best pasta I have ever eaten. The complimentary breads are tasty. Other than those the appetizers and entrees have never quite impressed.pretty good but not amazing.

At first we were upset because we had to wait an hour after our reservation was made...but it was because the Obama's were sitting at the table we reserved! So, I think that about sums it up. The food is amazing. I couldn't stop eating the bread and I can confirm that the Spicy Rigatoni Vodka is to die for.

My boyfriend and I were very excited to go to Carbone. The pictures and reviews looked amazing. Of course we had to have the spicy rigatoni but we weren't sure if we should try two different pasta dishes or get our own rigatoni. After our waiter assured us that the portions were "family style" we decided to get the spicy rigatoni and the lobster ravioli to share thinking that the portions would be big considering we were told it was family style and that the prices were steep. Both pasta dishes were very small even for an individual portion, let alone family style. 

We were heavily persuaded by our waiter to get another dish and he recommended the meatballs. We got the meatballs and they were clearly RAW. Our waiter tried to convince us that this was normal and that was just the color of the veal. He came back again and I voiced my concern for a second time but again was trying to act like it was fine and that's just how it looks when it's cooked. Finally, we got the managers attention and he explained that they serve them "pink" here. Out of the hundreds of meatballs I've tried I've never seen or heard of a meatball being cooked underdone (I also have a lot of experience with cooking-this is not a thing). He took it off the bill but the whole experience was weird and felt very uncomfortable that our waiter was trying to act like a raw meatball was fine. 

Everything was good (except for the meatball) but our whole dining experience was ruined by this meatball incident. Our waiter was also very pushy with ordering more and was acting alarmed that we didn't want dessert or drinks. Again-the portions were not family style despite what the waiters might s
Good restaurant, great vibes. The food is good and their dessert (carrot cake) was excellent. The truffle corn is so delicious
Had a bad server who had a smug attitude then it went downhill from there. This place is overrated.

I have never before given a five star review. The fact is Carbone does everything right. Food is fantastic (highlights include the Caesar salad and the spicy rigatoni, though we left confident everything on the menu is superb and eager to go back to find out). The service is first class (from the hostess finding us seating even though we arrived early, to the bartender making this poor pregnant patron a delicious mocktail, to waitstaff, bussing staff, and supervisors circling the floor treating every move with respect, the point is the customer is going to be taken care of). The ambience is perfection; a nondescript neon sign on the street leads into a room full of energy, great music and just enough noise so you don't have to worry about your neighbors eavesdropping but you can hear your table. The meal will be expensive, but it's worth it. One of my best dining experiences ever. Go if you can, whenever you can.

While the food was adequate, management was less than appropriate about some lost valuables.  When we checked in, they asked to check our goods.  We asked for our goods when leaving.  While they checked for our goods, we waited and waited and ..... after a 20 minute wait  I asked for the manager and told him the situation.  They were indifferent about our lost (actually thrown out goods)  and refused to reimburse us for the cost.
They are much better at marketing than cooking and customer service.  I would caution diners.  Very expensive for adequate food!

Got lucky grabbing a spot here- a friend had a reservation but was unable to go, so ended up giving me the spot. Really enjoyed the atmosphere, very cool, old timey NYC decor.  The service was fantastic, had a very friendly and attentive waiter. 
Food is made to share, which is something I enjoy and adds to the experience. 
Nice wine list as well. Would definitely return

Because Torrisi's was one of my favorite NYC restaurants (and not to mention the hype surrounding Carbone), I couldn't wait to come here.  But one word kept droning on in my head during and after my meal: "brainwashed."  Sure, the food and the service were perfectly delightful (though I could've done without the da-doo-run-run-run, da-doo-run-run music). Loved the table-side Caesar, but it certainly wasn't the best I've ever had (lacked that "bite").  Nor was the rigatoni anywhere near the best I've ever had (certainly no comparison to the pastas I've had Scarpetta).  And the famed veal parmigiana?  The $60 price tag made me feel like I was taking part in some sort of social experiment to see just how big of suckers (or pretentiously self indulgent) New Yorkers can be.  I felt SO incredibly stupid and guilty for paying that kind of money -- for what I got -- I ran home and donated to my local food bank.  Shame on me for being such a fool and buying into that.

We took a close friend here for his birthday tonight and I could not believe how wonderful this place is!

The warm ambience of this place was the first thing I noticed. They seated us in a lovely booth for the four of us. The seats are a lovely blue velvet with shiny gold buttons. 

The menus are as big as the new york times and very clear. Our waiter was fantastic. He guided us with our order and he did not disappoint. The music is nostalgic and not too loud. 

The food. Oh my god. We were served a lovely assortment of foccacia, garlic bread and normal bread accompanied with pickled cauliflower, table cut parmesan and some cuts of salami. 

We ordered the meatballs, spicy rigatoni, cheese tortellini, veal parmesan and pork. All super tasty and fresh.

I was so full from dinner that I only had a few bites of the carrot cake and tiramisu. They were good, but not as incredible as their dinner menu.

The service was really superb. My water glass was never less than half full (I drink a lot of water).

Cant wait to come back! Carbone- i love you!

I had been trying to come here for A YEAR and finally was able to make a reservation for my birthday. The spice rigatoni is definitely delicious but we were told this was family style and those dishes are NOT family style. If you're not getting a meat or fish dish, the pasta can be eaten for 1. 

Service was also SO slow and the waiter felt so bad so he brought us 2 desserts so he redeemed himself :)

Meal was delicious and I'm very glad I tried it after all the hype. I went early on a weekend ~6:30. Servers were very nice. The rigatoni is a must and I was able to split an order with my friend as an appetizer (but it left me wanting more!). The prices for everything else, however, are just absurd. $60+ for veal--even splitting being able to split it with another person is insane. Come on?! Will probably never go back unless my rich fairy godmother is paying.

10 STARS. THIS PLACE. HANDS DOWN BEST ITALIAN IN NYC. JUST GO.

Okay, let me reel myself in a bit. You walk in and you're transported back in time in Italy. The place itself is small but cozy and intimate. The décor is very old style, classic New York. There's fab music playing in the back and the waiters are a delight. Now onto the food. This is the best Italian food I have ever eaten and the best I think you will. I know that's a loaded statement but I am confident enough in the food that you will agree with me once you try it.

My boyfriend took me here as a surprise on a special occasion and I could not be more excited as I have had this place bookmarked FOREVER but 1. its impossible to get a reservation and 2. it is preeeetty pricey BUT TRUST ME, its so so so worth it. You start off with some complimentary bread which I'm telling you you'll have to cut yourself off because its so damn good. Its a mix of foccacia, garlic bread and regular bread that is just so warm and toasted to perfection. They also provide some cheese and prosciutto to eat with your bread. We then ordered the baked clams, the meatballs, veal parmesan and the FAMOUS SPICY RIGATONI. The baked clams come three different ways- all of which are so flavorful and juicy. The meatballs were equally as good but the star dish was the veal parmesan and the gold medal goes to that damn spicy rigatoni. I could eat that one dish the rest of my LIFE. It is SO beyond simple but packed with so much flavor and oomph. Pasta is cooked to perfection, sauce is phenomenal and the combination is pure magic. If you can only get one dish, this is the one. 

I honestly don't remember if we got dessert because I think I blacked out after the pasta dish but I'm sure the dessert here is nothing short of amazing as well. I can honestly go on and on about this restaurant but nothing will beat getting yourself a reservation and experiencing yourself. 

I WILL BE BACK.

We came here tonight for our 10 year anniversary on a friends recommendation. 
Wow what a recommendation it was. Everything was amazing. We started with octopus and prosciutto and it was amazing. Mozzarella was just perfect.  We also had the rigatoni was great.  For entrees I had the Dover piccata and it was beyond amazing and my husband had the veal. With every bite we commented on how good it was.  Lastly for dessert, we had the chocolate bomb I think which had Nutella ice cream. It was delicious.
The service was great and the staff were very attentive. It was definitely on the pricier side and I wish I had asked how much my Dover piccata was first! $100.  Overall a great night and for a special occasion, I would highly recommend.
By far the best of the best Italian restaurants in NYC! Phenomenal manager, wait staff with incredible Sal and Tera the finest sommelier of all! Heaven on earth!

The Chicken Massimo was juicy, cooked very well, seasoned and gently glazed with herbs to enhance the flavor. The Scallop Piselli (basically with peas and sauce) was amazing. Seared to the expectations I was seeking. Definitely enjoyed everything from the Antipasti to the Dessert.

There was a lot of hype around this place so wanted to check it out. When we arrived we were given really yummy bread and some antipasto. Came for the spicy vodka sauce and got it. It was decent. SUCH A SMALL PORTION, way to small for the $29 price tag.

Despite booking our reservation a month in advance, we were made to wait an hour for our table. We were finally sat at the worst table in the place, right by the tiny but super loud bar area. The waiter was obnoxious, the octopus was rubbery, the meatballs were somehow both fatty AND filled with bread, the veal parm was on par with any New Jersey pizzeria, the sides were either way over or way under seasoned, and the tiramusi tasted like it was from a grocery store freezer aisle. The only dishes worth the hype were the spicy rigatoni and the clams, but they weren't worth the terrible service and high price tag. Hard pass on going back.

Great service Great food Great experience.... Do it Do it!!!!

Spicy Rigatoni, Mario's Meatballs and Lobster ravioli was cooked perfectly ... Starter bread, spicy pepperoni and fresh mozzarella was soooo delicious

Felt like we were in a different decade with great music and old school ambience

4.5 stars! My family was visiting this week, so I browsed through my yelp bookmarks a lot to find the perfect restaurants to take them to. Carbone has been on my list for a while but I just haven't been able to make it yet. Plus, reservations are incredibly difficult to snag. I looked on their online reservation system via Reserve, and miraculously, they had an opening for 6:15pm for 6 people!!! I immediately signed up for an account on Reserve and booked it. Remember to cancel ahead of time if you can no longer make it as they charge $50/pp! Our party was a teeny bit late to our reservation time, but they still accommodated us and even allowed some of us that arrived a little earlier to get seated first.

Once you walk in, you really are transported to a different place with great ambiance. Tables are a bit cramp but I guess that's part of the experience :). 

Service is a little pushy (they "suggest" doubling on portions, and when we said we would just order later if we were still hungry, we were told the kitchen doesn't operate that way and we couldn't do that) and I didn't love the attitude, but whatever, wasn't super terrible. Also, ridiculous pricing (really hurts the piggy bank!), but I guess if you're willing to go to carbone, you shouldn't care about the prices anyways...!

To start, they serve you up some complimentary bread, this pickled cauliflower dish, and some salami. THAT BREAD BASKET is to die for! There's a glistening pizza bread that sits on top, and then below that, there's some crispy garlic bread I believe, and some sour dough. Every piece was amazing.

Burrata $30
Don't believe this is on the menu, but the burrata was extremely well made and creamy! They cut the knot for you on the table, and stuff it with an eggplant mix / sea salt. $30 is extremely steep for such a small and simple dish though...

Spicy Rigatoni Vodka $29
Their most famous dish apparently. At first, I looked at it and thought, wow this is literally plain pasta with regular vodka sauce and NO toppings/other ingredients, how lame/how can they charge so much!? Once you bite into it, you kinda understand. The texture is like no other pasta I've ever tasted. For all my mandarin speakers out there, I would describe the texture as being super Q! Not al dente, but chewy in a good way :). Kinda like if you mixed pasta dough with mochi. FYI - The server recommended that we get 2 servings of this, so we did...if you look at the picture, the serving is pretty teeny, definitely NOT worth $58 bucks!!!

Fettuccine con Funghi $30
Meh, didn't really think anything of this dish. The fettuccine did not have the same chewiness :(

Bass Oreganata $39
Fish was cooked well, wish the skin was a little crispier! Nothing too special though.

Veal Marsala $64
This was really good!!! I was expecting a flattened piece of veal steak, but instead, it was perfectly sliced pieces that were pink in the middle and looked exactly like regular steak. This was delicious...!!!

Steamed Asparagus $16
Worst scam ever. Literally maybe 8 sticks of steamed asparagus. RIDICULOUS PRICING.

Tiramisu $15
This was just OK. Wish the tiramisu cake was more moist. The madeleine-like cookie on top was pretty good though!

I think this place is great to come once in a blue moon, but definitely too pricey to make this a regular. If I had friends coming in from out of town, I would definitely put this as a spot to take them to!

As a Manhattan resident of nearly 8 yrs, I understand the normal process for getting a reservation at a place such as Carbone. Besides the above normal hoops they make you jump through to request a reservation, I had two failed attempts as 1. They confirmed our reservation and then called back to revoke it and 2. Refused another request as they "filled up in the first 30 seconds of opening the lines that day." 

I don't care how good the food is, it's NYC and there are at least a dozen Italian restaurants of equal or greater quality that haven't made me feel like it is my privilege to spend money at their restaurant. I'll never eat here.

5/17/17 - Yes, reservations are hard to come by, but it's worth it to have the experience.  Carbone came highly recommended from a few close friends, so my wife took me here for my birthday lunch.  They did not disappoint.  The service was exquisite, and left absolutely nothing to be desired.  We picked on the fresh mozzarella, garlic bread, and chorizo while deciding what to have.  We ended up sharing: Caesar Salad, "Spicy" Rigatoni Vodka, Ribs and Peppers, the veal park, and for dessert the carrot cake with ginger ice cream.   The food was excellent but if it was as equally as great as the service was this would be hands down my favorite restaurant of all time.  This is not a knock on the food, I enjoyed everything - it's a compliment to the excellent serve staff

Getting a reservation here is slightly impossible but one hundred percent worth it. A group of friends and myself got a spot a little last minute (booked a week in advance) for lunch on a Friday and it was so delicious. 

We went family style with our meal and it was absolutely delicious. They start you off with warm bread with mozzarella/oil/prosciutto that I honestly still dream about. We opted for the spicy rigatoni for our meal and it lived up to all the hype. It was cooked perfectly and the sauce was so delicious with the perfect blend of spice/flavors/onions - it all came together so beautifully. We got carrot cake for dessert and again no regrets, so good. Service was also great, 10/10 would recommend.

This restaurant came highly recommended by many celebrities. So it took 2 weeks to get a reservation through their own online reservation service. Upon arrival, we were promptly seated in the front entrance not an ideal location but it was ok bc the restaurant was booked. Our waiter was polite  and didn't make any suggestions and recommendations to us as it pertains to specials. It would have been useful because their menu  only had 20 items which essence was limited. The service was slow and our waiter probably check on us 2 times.  I ordered the chicken and part of it was undercooked. When i complained to the waiter about not liking the sides, he said: " its not bout the sides but more about the chicken." Finally towards the end they  gave us the wrong bill and thank god i looked bc it increased our bill by $100. He apologized but it was not the best experience. The food is pretty average so i have no interest on dining there again.

From start to finish this place is amazing. 

Ambiance: Great mix of old school NYC flare with modern touches. Amazing decor, perfect for date night or an intimate dinner with close friends. 

Service: Exactly what you'd expect while fine dining A+ service from the moment you walk in. 

Food: TO DIE FOR. They start you off with an assorted bread basket (you must have their garlic bread) and delicious pickled veggies. My group split their Italian chopped salad which was divine and I had the vodka pasta.....sooooo delicious. 

I can't wait to go back the next time I'm in NYC.

Top of the line food... Come correct or don't come at all! Came here for my birthday and literally had the whole entire menu. No complaints! Can't go wrong! Check out my instagram for places to visit and eat @expensive_appetite

This place is incredible. Meatballs, pasta, veal parm, the works!

Going to come back here next time in the city!

This was the best meal of my entire trip to New York. Everyone must go here. The spicy rigatoni vodka is absolutely amazing. So rich and creamy. The experience is wondering. The service is outstanding and the food is delicious.

Some of the best Italian food I've ever had. Carbone is more than a restaurant- it's truly a food experience. From the second you walk in, you can feel that it's a special place. You are first greeted by the waitstaff who all are beautifully dressed- some wearing maroon suits. The interior is gorgeous and upscale. The menus are huge and awesome and make you feel tiny- but in a fun way. I have so much to say about the food that I'm salivating while writing this reminiscing on my recent birthday dinner. 

They first brought out this amazing bread with just a bit of tomato sauce on top and it was the perfect way to start the meal. Then they came out with Parmesan bites and spicy Salami. The combination was fantastic. We ordered the Prosciutto and Mozzarella for our appetizer and since I'm a huge fresh Mozzarella lover- I fell in love fast. Next came our entrees. I ordered the spicy vodka rigatoni which I've literally seen so many photos of on Instagram, I really felt like I was missing out on it for years. It did not disappoint. Perfectly cooked and fresh, incredible sauce. My boyfriend got the squid ink lobster ravioli which was rich and absolutely delicious. We also had their chocolate mousse cake with blackberries for dessert which was soooo amazing but we were beyond stuffed and couldn't even finish it, which for us, doesn't happen often. Overall an amazing place to celebrate a birthday or any special event. They had seamless service and we loved the evening.

9 stars. I come here when I want some good food at a good price! I've taken a few dates here and the price points really let you ball out of control and get just enough food and drink. I usually avoid desserts at places but I can order all kinds of food and still fit dessert inside a reasonable check.

Clearly over rated! $65 for a breaded veal dish that is nothing spectacular. The pasta dishes are appetizer portions but entree prices. Salad is entree prices. It's way over priced in a cramped space. Nothing special. All the glowing reviews are highly suspect. Try it and you will be disappointed, unless you don't care spending $100 per person for a simple Italian meal.

Dinner was AMAZE. I'm so full, we really over-ordered, but the whole experience was perfect for my family. We're big foodies, and value the quality, as well as the experience of eating. Carbone is really traditional, upscale Italian. Everything from the music to the service was perfect. 

The must-try items of the night: spicy rigatoni (obviously), the veal Parmesan, pancetta, mozzarella with prosciutto, and Caesar salad. All phenomenal. You really can't go wrong. Each person at the table had different favorites, but if you order any of the above, you'll die in heaven. I can't wait to fully digest, then return every day. So perfect.

This is my favorite restaurant. I fell in love with every detail of Carbone. From the food, to the staff and even the red water carafes that go so well with the dark blue walls. When you leave make sure you take a to go bag, even if you don't have any leftovers..they're beautiful!

We do not eat meat or shellfish but the waiter worked with us on the pasta dishes. We ordered the famous spicy rigatoni and the tortellini (in red sauce as a substitute). Both were absolutely delicious. Do not underestimate the tortellini, it melts in your mouth! 

The caesar salad is a must -- they make the dressing right in front of you!

Such an amazing experience. I already have a second reservation booked.

In a nutshell, this restaurant is full of non-native New York "foodies" who don't know good Italian food and are more focused on the "scene" rather than the food that is in front of them.  If you want to Instagram your 18 dollar glass of wine with your spicy rigatoni and let all your friends know you were able to score a reservation at Carbone, then this is the place for you.  If you want a truly memorable experience food wise, don't waste your time.

I had really high expectations for this restaurant based on reviews, word of mouth, and a wonderful experience at Major Food Group's Santina.  Let's just say my girlfriend and I were left extremely underwhelmed.  After trying on and off for nearly a year, we were finally "blessed" with a reservation from these guys.  Given that this place is next to impossible to get a reservation, that added to the expectations that this would be a great meal.  

The meal started off well, we were seated at a nice table in the corner, and we were given an assortment of breads, meats, olives, and cheeses (complimentary).  They had a good old school playlist going and we were off to a nice start.  

We started with the Caesar Salad which everyone raves about.  The salad was drenched in dressing and it was not prepared table side as described.  We also asked for it without anchovies and the waiter agreed that it would not be an issue.  When we received the salad, it was topped with whole-filets of anchovies.  We notified the waiter and he begrudgingly took it back and then we were handed our (average at best) Caesar salad for double the price of a normal restaurant.  We ordered the infamous Spicy Rigatoni which was good, but nothing special.  If you grew up in the New York area, it's vodka sauce with red pepper flakes over  pasta which does not require all that much skill to prepare, and it is certainly not hard to find in the New York metro area.  It wasn't bad, but it was nothing special at all.  The Lobster Ravioli (which was nearly 40 dollars) tasted pretty fishy and seemingly not made with fresh meat.  I've eaten a lot of Lobster Ravioli and needless to say this did not live up to expectations that come with a nearly 40 dollar pasta entree.  Given that we were underwhelmed with the food, we decided to forego dessert and just have the rainbow cookies which everyone says are given with the check.  Needless to say the check came without rainbow cookies. 

Essentially, if you do not order an expensive bottle of wine, you can kiss your hopes of good service goodbye.  Given the quality of the food, Carbone is not in a position to have this pretentious attitude.  There are countless Italian restaurants in New York City and I have been to many.  I have attended some in the same price range of Carbone (some even more upscale) and walked out and said "that was pricey but wow that was worth it."  If you are a native New Yorker, know anything about good food or the preparation behind it, you will leave here underwhelmed and you should not even bother with the effort to get a reservation here.  If you are a self-proclaimed "foodie" who likes a "scene" or if you want to entertain clients who will leave knowing you made an effort to get a reservation and that you spent a pretty penny on expensive wine, you'll probably find your efforts more worthwhile.

Atrocious experience for father's day dinner.  Food was inconsistent and definitely not worth the price.  Great antipasti, terrible pastas, and good entrees.  Angel hair with clams was so salty it was inedible.  Restaurant was incredibly noisy throughout the meal especially the table next to us.  At the end of the meal when we made a comment amongst ourselves about the noise, a woman at the other table cursed us out, calling us "a--holes" and she told us to "shut the f--k up."  When we responded her father threatened to "knock us the f--k out" because we were getting into it with his daughter.  Restaurant did absolutely nothing to respond and although they cannot choose their customers, they could have kept us from leaving visibly upset.  This meal quickly became a salty and atrocious experience.

Carbone has been on my bookmarks list for a long time and seeing it featured on Master of None sealed the deal for making a reservation here. We were lucky to find one easily online, albeit for 5:45 PM on a weekday. It was well-worth the visit and early dinner time, and I can definitely see why people rave about it - though, I will admit that I haven't personally ranked it amongst my all-time favorite meals. 

The hostesses and wait staff here are all extremely attentive and friendly. Our waiters were joking with us throughout the night which really made for a fun dinner experience. The atmosphere is perfect and really does make you feel like you're having an authentic home-cooked meal in the heart of an Italian village. 

We received very good recommendations for wine and were quickly presented with a complimentary bread basket. To my surprise, we also got complimentary sides of pickled cauliflower and spicy pepperoni (both yum!). The bread was so good and I was scared I was going to fill myself up just on that before the meal had even started. 

Because Carbone won't be a frequent visit for us (based on price alone), my fiancé and I ordered the dishes that we had heard the most about. We got the baked clams to start, followed by the Veal Parmesan, Meatballs, and Spicy Rigatoni to share. The clams were very fresh and came in three preparations, all of which were really flavorful and unique. The star of the dinner was definitely the Spicy Rigatoni... I can see why this is a "must order" here as I've never had such simple but tasty pasta before. The side of meatballs was HUMONGOUS but really delicious. They were very tender and paired with an amazing tomato sauce. The veal parmesan was the epitome of Italian comfort food... meat was cooked perfectly, my fiancé ate it to the last morsel on the bone, and it was a big enough portion to share between two people (also priced as such at almost $60). 

We forced ourselves to make room for dessert and ordered the carrot cake - thank goodness, because it was THE best carrot cake I've ever had. I really enjoyed the ginger ice cream which wasn't overwhelming at all and actually served as a good palate cleanser for the end of the meal. 

This is definitely one of the priciest meals we've had in NYC but we were stuffed and in food comas for the rest of the night. It was a really enjoyable dinner including both the food and service, so the hype is certainly deserved. Highly recommend and great for both dates and large family gatherings/celebrations with friends!
By far first class service and unbelievable Italian food. A must stop for anyone visiting ny

Went here for a celebratory dinner. We had a reservation and were seated on time with no trouble. The good- everything we ordered was delicious (meatballs, spicy rigatoni, veal parm, tuna appetizer and clams appetizer). Enormous portions, friendly staff. The not so good- our waiter definitely tried to up sell us. You're not going to this restaurant and not spending money though so ok, fine, fair game. My biggest issue was the sommelier brought us a bottle of wine which didn't taste right to us and we were told to let it rest so we did for 10-15 minutes and it took another 10-15 minutes to get us another bottle. At the prices they charge if the wine is bad it should be taken right away and replaced immediately no questions asked. All in all, if you get the chance to go to carbone, go.

My friend and I were sat around 5:45PM on a weekday. Sure we were dining like early bird's but when it comes to Carbone, you take what they can give you. Once sat, the waiter greeted us with menus and a bunch of enthusiasm. I wonder how many times our waiter has gleefully said, "Here's a nice small menu for you," as he hands over something that resembles one of those jumbo gag cards that you get when retire from a job or an over-the-hill birthday. If his smile were a sound, it would be, "Ba-dum-tush."

Anyway, he was attentive, albeit slightly cheesy but answered all of our questions which was mainly how to pronounce 'scungille.' 

The bread basket was a great way to ease into the meal. In order to prepare for my 5:45PM dining experience, I moved up my lunch about 2 hours earlier than usual. At 5:45PM the effects of waiting this long were showing and my stomach was singing the sounds hunger. I polished off the focaccia, and garlic bread, and a few slices of cured meats. They also had pickled veggies which broke up the richness of all the carbs I had just consumed. 

We placed our order and may have been a bit overzealous:

To start, we had the Octopus Pizzaiolo which was described as a 5 hour slow braising technique followed by some charred grilling. Unfortunately, the effects of cooking for 5 hours shown through and the octopus, while flavorful, was not as tender as I would have liked. Sorry Italy, the Greeks may still have the best octopus for me. 

Next, we split the Caesar salad which was a strong recommendation by my fellow yelpers. Thanks for the tip, it was delicious. Those croutons were buttery, crispy perfection

For the pastas, we split the tortellini al ragu and the spicy rigatoni vodka. They kindly divided the tortellini into two plates, each with 4 pillowy pockets of cheesy goodness nestled on delicate bed of ragu. This was bangin! I cut into each tortellini like it was a ritual and every bite had to be savored. The spicy rigatoni vodka was placed in the middle of the table to share. I started with a small scoop of three rigatoni's but was quickly back for more. This is where all the hype is; these pastas were awesome and this is why you come to Carbone.

My friend and I looked at each other painfully as we were both delightfully bursting at the seams after the pasta dishes. We had ordered too much food again, story of our lives. But we kept on eating, the sequel to the story of our lives. 

We had more food coming and it was the veal parmesan. We said things like, "we'll probably just have a bite and get it wrapped up to go," for the most part, this was true but not before we polishing off a quarter of the dish and even the crispy bone. Definitely eat the meat off the bone, this was the best part of the dish for me. 

I'm sad to say, we did not have room for dessert. I wish we did since I brought my friend here to celebrate her birthday. Our waiter didn't skip a beat though, he stuck a candle in the complimentary Italian cookies which was a lovely and sweet way to finish the meal. 

Carbone is your answer to finding that quintessential New York dining experience. You feel special, somewhat elite while here. Once you step out of Carbone, it's back to reality and you're broke again.

What an honor to have dined here. It literally took me FOREVER to get a reservation. Finally, one fateful night a month in advance, I got my reservation for 7:15pm on a Sunday. 

Let me say that I just ADORE how much bread they give you before the meal starts. Three different types and some soppressata - love it! 

We started with the ceaser. It was definitely impressive how they make it in front of you, but not as cool as these other yelpers make it out to be. I mean, it's just a guy mixing some lettuce and dressing together in a bowl. Have you people never seen a salad been made? It was covered in cheese, so much to the point it felt like I was no longer eating a salad. But I could have told the guy to go lighter, I'll take responsibility for that one.

For entrees we had the spicy rigatoni, tortellini, and a side of meatballs. I was really confused by the meatballs. They were firm, yet pink in the middle as if they were raw. It was pretty baffling. I would have thought raw would make them softer but IDK man something was off. The rigatoni was creamy and good, but not a life changer. Definitely over hyped for sure. It's photogenic but it's just pasta with sauce people! The tortellini was light and tasty but nothing to write home about.

The rainbow cookies they gave at the end were good...like really good. Some of the best I've had. Wish I could have asked for more of those!

Overall, this is a good Italian restaurant. It most definitely is overrated and overpriced but if you can get a reservation and have the money, YOLO!

Our family dined here last evening to celebrate my daughter's 20th Birthday.  We will echo the other reviews and say +1 on excellent food and service.  Rigatoni, burrata and the meatballs did not disappoint and our captain delivered smooth and attentive service to our table. 

We did have an issue early on that was handled very poorly by a woman who was either a hostess or some sort of assistant that manages the seating.  You should know before you go that the restaurant does have background music that can be quite loud.  We were seated directly under a speaker and it really was problematic. We could not hear each other or our captain.   We asked if the captain could lower it and he did try to accommodate us, however it really did not solve the problem. Oddly enough it was my two children that suggested perhaps they could move us.  We asked the captain and he said he would see what he could do.

A highly annoyed woman then appeared at our table and proceeded to give us a lecture about   the music they normally play and the level it is normally played at. But if we insisted she would move us to the back room. Although taken aback by her demeanor we took her up on her offer.  She then proceeded to move us to another table for 4 under another speaker in the back room-- and 2 of us now also had a view of the kitchen door. When we politely pointed out to her that this table was also under a speaker, she angrily told us that every table for 4 was tucked into a corner  and all corners had the speakers.  So why not tell us that before moving us and why the bitter attitude??? Very passive aggressive and unpleasant individual.

We thought the food and service were excellent but a party of 4 is easily going to spend $500+ for dinner and a glass  of wine. On that level one would expect a little more professionalism from staff.

From the start we had amazing service by Sal. And the food. Yum. I ordered the spicy vodka rigatoni from seeing it on Yelp and I ate it all, literally licking the plate.  but the focaccia was the best tasting focaccia I have ever eaten. The meatballs to start really got the meal going for me. All in all. Excellent.

I really enjoyed my night out at Carbone, the food was great and the service was impeccable. 

This isn't high brow Italian like del potato, this is a traditional Italian steakhouse reborn in what used to be Rocco's. It's got a old New York Italian vibe with a twist on otherwise traditional dishes.  The vibe and atmosphere was relaxed but the service was attentive of every detail. 

Our meal was great - we enjoyed the crispy pancetta, and Caesar salad to start. Along with the spicy rigatoni to split. We tried the ribeye and also the veal Marsala.  Everything was great and cooked perfectly.  The bread basket was as good as the rest of the meal.  We had cocktails but their wine selection was great.  

We ordered their tiramisu to go and it was great as well.

If you sent your Italian-American Nana to cooking school and had her only learn to make the same dishes she has been cooking her entire life better, then maybe you'd have something like this. It's not revolutionary; it's Italian staples done perfectly. 

Our waiter was awesome. Ordered our entire meal. The sommelier was a mind reading genius. This place is worth the wait. The money and the whole thing. Thanks Carbone.

New York doesn't lack amazing Italian restaurants. We've waited so long before coming to Carbone, mostly because it's really hard to get a reservation, and in the same neighborhood there's abundance of great Italian restaurants (Babbo, Lupa, L'Artusi, to name a few). So during 4th of July weekend when everyone is out of town, we scored a reservation and decided to give Carbone a try.  

Decor felt very old school. Tables were a bit too tight to my liking (when you could hear the girl next to you complain to her date she's the only woman without a ring on her finger, it's too tight). We were welcomed by bread basket, cured meat, and pickled cauliflower, all of them were delicious. Then we were handed those humongous menus, I get that they want it to look classy and cool, but when the menu couldn't fit on the table and I had to put it down on the bench, it was a problem. 

We got the spicy rigatoni, spaghetti puttanesca, meatballs, and double lamp chops. I don't recall exactly how much each of the dishes cost, but the lamp chops were a whooping $90. It was the best dish of the night. But let's go back to the pastas first. Rigatoni was very creamy and very well cooked. Spaghetti puttanesca was perfectly seasoned and cooked as well. Both pasta dishes were solid, but I didn't find them that much better than other places. Meatballs was a big turnoff. I mean if you didn't ask me "how would you like your meatballs cooked, medium or medium rare", then don't bring me meatballs that were completely pink in the middle. I've never had undercooked meatballs anywhere in my life and I don't intend to start here. Now comes the double lamb chops - perfectly seasoned, perfectly charred on the outside, and perfected cooked medium rare. I usually don't eat lamb because they could be very gamey. Here the gameiness was minimum. All I could taste was the juicy and flavorful meat. It's the best piece of lamb I've ever had. 

We ended dinner with a carrot cake. It looked pretty, but the cake was really not moist and border-lining hard and dry. It was another let down. Our total check before tip came to about $250 (including two glasses of wine). It's definitely not cheap. 

I'm torn between a 3 and a 4. Very solid pasta dishes plus amazing lamb chop, offset by undercooked meatballs and below average dessert. Consider my rating a 3.5 even though it's a 3. Until next time.

Excelent service. Very good food.The Caesar salad is a most! Made with real anchovies. Wine list is very extensive but also very expensive. There's no way to order a bottle of wine from there menu. The lobster ravioli was also really good. Chocolate cake amazing.

Made reservations via email  the day before and got in at 8 pm for a table of 4. The waiter was pushy and had lots of opinions. We got the following: 

1. The complimentary appetizers...came out of no where but they were delicious. Meats, variety of bread, and pickled veggies. Don't over eat! 
2. Prosciutto and mozzarella- decent but nothing exciting
3. Caesar salad- they say it's made table side but it really isn't. They made it elsewhere (definitely not table side) and delivered it. It was a really good Caesar salad. I found myself going back to it the entire meal. Weird because a Caesar salad is pretty basic but this one is awesome. 
4. Two orders of the spicy rigatoni vodka -AMAZING. Also I'm a big fan of vodka pasta in general and this one tops the chart. The hype is real. Yes- we had to get two orders for a party of 4. 
5. Lobster ravioli special - stuffed with tons of crab; solid 
6. Veal Parmesan - Good but nothing out of the ordinary here. 
6. Side of meatballs - decent meatballs; definitely was not pink in the center like other reviews 

Overall it was a really good dinner and the spicy rigatoni is really pushing this yelp review to a 5 star.

**pricey** go with your parents or for a business dinner

Beautiful interior & they play fun oldies (at least when I was there for lunch). Warning...VERY expensive for Italian food. Probably why some people give lower ratings. However, they do do a couple things REALLY well that I'd come back for. 

MUST GET: (seems everyone was getting the same 2 things!) Spicy Rigatoni Vodka -- pasta was al dente & the sauce was perfect, I'd have this everyday! Veal Parmesan - the veal was super tender & I loved that it came with the bone so the meat by the bone was the best part. However, if I had to get ONE thing it would definitely be the rigatoni vodka pasta.

DON'T GET: linguini vongole -- way too salty & too much parsley. Tiramisu was just okay...and not your traditional tiramisu, more like a tiramisu cake.

I don't know why this hidden gem does not have 5 stars!!!
I was recommended by multiple friends and finally went in today after a brief weekend trip. We were luck to get a 2pm reservation on a Monday. Be sure to make your reservation ahead of time on line. 

Where do I begin? The wine recomendación was great! 

We had the Cesar salad, the most amazing cartapacio (it had crushed walnuts in top) meatballs, rigatoni pasta cooked al dente and spiced to perfection and the branzino was de boned for us at the table. 

It was truly a great way to end our weekend trip ! 

Thank you to the wonderful staff who were so attention to detail and so great with your recommendations. 
We will be back !!!!

I've read so many things about Carbone online, that I knew we had to go try it for ourselves. Now, I am a purebred Italian, so it takes ALOT to impress my with Italian food. We arrived at Carbone at 5:30pm and were seated. We were greeted by our waiter, and after taking some time to look at the menu we decided to do 1 appetizer course and as our main entrée that we would both get the spicy rigatoni vodka with meatballs. As we were ordering, the waiter interrupted us and said "usually most people order an appetizer, a pasta course, and a main meat entrée" and proceeded to say that "we must not be that hungry to only order an appetizer and 2 pastas". He recommended we get the almost $70 veal parm in addition to our appetizer, pasta, and meatballs. I looked at my husband baffled, because I knew we would not be able to eat all that food.
