But in the end we decided to add the veal parm on just to see if it was worth the hype. (Meanwhile, the table next to us ordered the exact same food and he told them the same about the veal parm. When they refused to add it on to their meal, the waiter said "don't blame me if you leave here hungry tonight then"). 
We felt very rushed throughout the entire meal, and by 6:15 we were already having our pasta plates cleared from the table. I had to keep leaving food in my plate so they would stop taking the plates from out in front of us!
I did enjoy the bread and complementary salami and chunk of parmesan. The garlic bread was very good!
Our appetizer of prosciutto and fresh mozzarella was also very good (the mozzarella was still warm!). The rigatoni and meatballs were also very good, but nothing astonishing. The meatballs were pink in the center, which my husband did not care for. 
The veal parm was very good and great quality, but the portion size for $70 was fairly small for what I am used to at a typical Italian joint. It was very nice that when they packaged up our leftovers, they gave us a roll so we could make a parm sandwich for lunch the next day! The rainbow cookies were extremely good!
Overall, the service and portion sizes did not justify the $225 bill. I have had Italian food at the same quality and a larger portion for half the price. Again, I have grown up in the restaurant business and am 100% Italian, so my views may be a bit skewed. Overall, it was a good experience but not good enough for us to visit again.

The food here was amazing, my favorite being the famous Penne all vodka. To start we had the focaccia bread which was so good.  We also had the shrimp which I loved.  The only bad thing I could say was that the service was not good and it took them awhile to even acknowledge our table once we sat down.  But hopefully I can give it another try and the service will be better next time
Well worth the wait. Might take awhile to get a reservation & the prices might be steep but it is worth it! Old school Italian vibes mixed with impeccable customer service & mouth watering food.
So delicious. Old time Italian food. Go hungry!  The food is delicious and so filling!  The cheeses and bread are to die for. Love the wine choices!  The staff is very nice and helpful.

After more than a month of chasing a reservation, we finally got early bird dinner 5.30 pm on a Sunday. It was lunch+dinner combined 

Reading the reviews took out a bit of the surprise element, as I was already expecting the complimentary snacks before dinner and the jokes from the guy handing us the menus...

The environment is nice, classy, cozy, romantic, with a bit of a homey feeling. We were seated in the back room, near where Master of None's episode was filmed. One drawback is that the tables were quite near each other and I could listen to the couple next to us talking. AC was also not high enough for Italian fare. I would also recommend coming here on winter months as the food lends itself to cold weather. Not many "light" options, which is fine as Italian food is never light. I guess the roots of Italian cuisine are from the countryside, where people needed as much energy as possible to work the land.

We tried the pickled cauliflower (loved it), spicy salami, and parmigiano that the break from the wheel in your table. Very nice touch. Grandmas' bread was outstanding, particularly the garlic bread and the one with tomato sauce. As appetizers we shared the Baked Clams ($24) that come in three styles. The green ones were my favorites. Followed by Caesar Salad ($23) that is mixed next to you. This was one of the most authentic Caesars I had in my life (I feel everywhere else they are fooling you). It had tiny bits of anchovies (which they ask you if you want before mixing). We also shared the Spicy Rigatoni Vodka ($29) as it was highly recommended and I agree. It is a must. I cleaned the plate with my bread. I know it might not be very classy to do this in a Michelin Star restaurant, but the chef would have been happy to see me enjoy his master creation (and deep in me I'm a grandma who doesn't care what other people think). Then we had Chicken Massimo ($37) which is a half chicken cooked with a reduction of balsamic vinegar and a thin layer of melted parmigian cheese, on top of some greens and onions. We were so full we had half of that to go. No room for dessert unfortunately. I had my eye on the Carrot Cake, so I hope they have it next time I visit. The couple next to us ordered very similar and had dessert (so jealous!), so it all depends how big your stomach is. I had a feeling all the tables around us over lots of food. Makes sense after a month of waiting for your table - you better get everything you want from the menu!

The wine selection was excellent too. We had a 2007 La Querciola 'Cornole' Dogliani ($65), a true gem. The somm mentioned they are lucky they have their wines on consignment, so it allows them to have a greater and varied selection.

All in all great experience. I'm knocking one star off because we had to wait a lot to get our wine (which was better after 20 min of opening up) and tables were way too close. May come back again when I have family visiting, as the food lends itself nicely for sharing with loved ones.

CARBAGE !!

Well that might be a much better name for major foods Carbone.  We had been planning dinner there for the last month.  My excitement was palpable my palate was prepared.
The ambiance was perfect a nice summer evening a cool breeze wisp the back of my neck as I entered. I was fastidiously hurried toward the back as our table was not prepared.  We didn't mind waiting 20 min for our table we enjoyed a nice drink by the surreptitiously planted bar, dug into the corner of the Room and inline of kitchen traffic.  We didn't complain when the bar keep had no expertise in mixology, know we settled for old fashions and manhattan's a little dry and a little sweet.  
So when we finally hit the table around 10 we started with a wonderful mussels with a bolognese sauce, never imagined that to be good, but it was.  They prepared  a wonderful trio of baked clams.  
I ordered two pastas for the table and we were splitting two whole bronzino's.   Well I think what happened is that they caught the pasta at the same time they caught the fish. Can you say salty !! 
My three year old makes better pasta that's a fact. 
Our waiter, straight out of Donny Brasco, was all talk and more like Freddo, I know it was you! 
He promised new pasta, removal from the check and better enters to come. 
Well when it rains it pores that's what the Morton's girl has taught me and that means salt!! 
One dish after the next and this is after bringing it up multiple times.  I mean it was so bad I couldn't even taste the wonderful 1997 Barbaresco we splurged on.  In any event my suggestion is stay away!! 

Ciao

Possible the best Italian meal I have ever had.  Every dish was next level the mozzarella with heirloom tomatoes was unreal. Our waiter was awesome bought my friend and I glasses of wine, we're going back tonight it's unbelievable how good the whole experience is.
There's no point in leaving a review. You see the 5 stars. Order the caprese, the rigatoni with vodka sauce, and pork chop. You'll understand.

A bit over rated as far as I am concerned. Bread basket and cauliflower was very good, along with parmigiana cheese, seconds were not offered. 

Spice vodka rigatoni good. 

Veal park - eh
Dover sole - eh

Wine list - extensive but over priced 

Service - inattentive
Hospitality!! The food speaks for itself but the hospitality is the soul of the restaurant.
Veal dishes were delicious! Cozy atmosphere. Bartender stirred up a proper boulevardier.

After seeing Carbone on many lists for "best" in the West Village area, I decided to take a chance and try it with my niece last Saturday.  We arrived in the early evening without a reservation and were fortunate to get a table, or so they were very happy to tell me several times.

The atmosphere in the restaurant is lovely.  It's cozy and comfortable, if maybe a bit tight. Not knowing what I was getting myself into, I was a bit taken aback when handed the comically over-sized menu. The menu was nearly the size of our table.  Anyway, it wasn't the size that made me look twice.  It was the prices. The cheapest glass of wine on the menu was $16, but almost all were well over $20, nearing $30, and there weren't any really special bottles on the menu.

Now for the food.  Again, it is well over-priced.  Almost all appetizers are over $20, including soup. I was in the mood for pasta, thank God.  Veal parm is $55 and chicken scarpariello is $36.  I know what you're thinking: Portion sizes must be huge.  Well, you will be hugely disappointed, because they are actually small.  My niece ordered the $29 tortellini ragu.  When it arrived, I think there were approximately 8 tortellini.  Now we knew why the waiter told us to order an appetizer and two entrees for EACH of us. I ordered the $25 spaghetti pomodoro.  The portion was small, entirely too salty and had approximately 3 cloves of garlic in it. Even for a garlic lover, that is a bit over the top.  I spent 10 minutes picking out the ridiculous amount of garlic slivers.  We also ordered the meatballs, which were the highlight of the meal, which isn't saying much.  The sauce was decent, if a bit too salty, and the meatballs were good.  The only complaint about them is that they were made with fennel and I'm not a fennel fan, but that comes down to personal taste. My niece finished with the chocolate cake for dessert, which she enjoyed.
 
I am happy to pay a high price for an entree if I am getting my money's worth in taste, portion size and experience. Carbone failed to live up to the hype and doesn't warrant the prices they are charging. Take my advice and go around the corner to Monte's for delicious real old school Italian at reasonable prices.

3 stars for the food. Negative 2 stars for extremely poor value and ambiance. 

There is nothing original here. Major Foods stole the concept of offering free snacks upon arrival coupled with extremely high prices and an emphasis on even more expensive "specials" from Il Mulino, which is just two blocks away. Then they dumbed it down by adding a cheesy Italian American vibe. The waiters sound like Joe Pesci in My Cousin Vinny. The sound system is playing Italian American hits like Volare. The menu is so incredibly oversized that it's like holding a piece of poster board. Tables are too close together, especially for high end dining. It sort of feels like a bad joke, but when you check out the prices, the joke is over. Appetizer salads and pastas are around $25 to $35. Chicken and fish entrees are around $40, veal is $65 and some of the specials are $75 to $90. The wines by the glass are $16 to $30. Few bottles on the wine list are less than $100 and the mark-ups appeared to be 3x to 4x retail prices. It's certainly no surprise that the menu on the restaurant website does not include prices.

As for the food, it's slightly better than what you'd find in most Italian American red sauce joints in the NY area. Unfortunately it costs 2x as much and it's fairly inconsistent. The mozzarella was strong, but it was $25 for about 6 ounces and a sliced tomato. The tortellini were embarrassingly soggy to the point of having a baby food consistency. The famed veal chop parm was quite tasty, but for $65 the portion was paltry. Like others have noted, the meatballs (at $7 each) were boring and were not cooked through. Other dishes were generally unmemorable. 

If you are looking for a high end Italian experience I would recommend Del Posto, Scalini Fedeli, Marea, Ai Fiori or Babbo. All offer superior cuisine with professional service for a comparable price. But if you enjoy throwing money in the street and are more interested in geotagged Instagram photos than pasta, maybe Carbone is for you.

When I come back to visit NYC, Carbone is a non-negotiable stop. 

This restaurant is the perfect special occasion spot. It is pricey - but I believe it's worth it. The old-school Italian meets downtown modern vibes make diners young and old feel at home. Once you're seated, they serve a number of table snacks (different breads, fermented cauliflower, cheese, meat, etc.) and it's all fantastic. This is something that sets Carbone apart. I always order the veal parm and spicy rigatoni to share and highly recommend both.

Carbone is an authentic Italian gem well worth the cost. We started with wine and were served three choices of delicious breads, cauliflower and spicy pepperoni. Then the server came around with a block of delicious aged Parmesano Romano cheese. We ordered the prosciutto and melon which was a perfect combo and they didn't skimp on the Serving! Then, our attentive waiter brought our meals. The lobster fra diavolo was incredible. They made it fresh, table-side and the portion of lobster was impressive! I got the spicy rigatoni vodka and the pasta was cooked to perfection. Desserts were on display and told to us so we got the chocolate blackout cherry cake with Nutella ice cream. YUM. So rich and sweet. We would highly recommend this restaurant for a divine date night.
My favorite spot for any occasion!! Food is super tasty, and I love the people who work there!!

5 stars.
Service impeccable, old school, personable. 
Out of all the torrisi crews places, carbone is the standout. 
Simple, Italian American fare, done properly. They don't advertise anything else. 
Everything is in the details here..the old school decor, the perfect, warm, and heavily seasoned house baked bread that they bring to your table, and the tableside service. 
The best veal parmesan in the city, by far. Yes it's pricey, but one of the few places that you get what you pay for. The portions are massive. 
One of the best meals I've had in the city. Can't wait to go back.

Best Italian restaurant I have ever been too.... Quiet and exclusive feeling, inside is totally authentic with Frank Sinatra music playing.

Great wine section. Amazing service. Delectable food.

Must email for reservations in advance. I recommend making a reservation far in advance as they are not so quick to answer their emails.

Must order the spicy rigatoni vodka.

Excels in excellence. While it was a bit of a hassle to get a birthday reservation (for a Tuesday, might I add) it was definitely worth it. The vibe that you get while seated is one of class, comfort, and fun. The black and white floors, the blue walls, the delightful bar cornered in the front room, and the waiters dressed to impress in a, seemingly rarely pulled off, burgundy. It only took a few minutes to get our cocktails ordered, be given a large chunk of freshly severed parmesan (right from the wheel in the front room), a gorgeous bread basket, salumi, and picked cauliflower and onion... wait, and I just sat down?! perfection.  Baked clams were very good. Beef carpaccio was also great, even though I would have preferred a more classic take vs hazelnut. My husband and I split spicy rigatoni and lamb chops - both beautifully prepared. Tiramisu for dessert was a HUGE piece (I think 4 people could have shared that things). Also, cheers to complimentary anisette withy coffee. Overall Carbone is everything people say and more.

Where do I start... I suppose the beginning would make sense. It's seldom that an online reservation pops up but I'm happy it did for tonight. My two friends and I were supposed to go but one of two cancelled on us. Luckily the restaurant was flexible and seated the two of us at a four top, even 15+ minutes late - thank you! Would have invited another two had I know we'd be at a four top but I digress. We ordered the baked clams, spicy rigatoni, pork and peppers, and accompanied the food with a few glasses of chianti. 
The complimentary bites of three types of bread, charcuterie, a huge chunk of Parmesan, and a dish of pickled cauliflower filled me up quickly. Unfortunately for my digestive tract, I proceeded to polish off the next three courses. 

The baked clams were deliciously filling but also incredibly rich. I felt like I was drinking butter in the best possible way. The spicy rig is a must get and honestly only Satan wouldn't like this dish. If anything, however, the pork surprised me the most. They serve Berkshire pork, a heritage breed which I appreciate. Also it is cooked to a medium rare as meat should be, but nearly everyone commonly overcooks pork. 

The rainbow cookies at the end were excessive, but not to be overtopped, I also got a tiramisu to share with my friend. Mmm

Do not come here if you are on any sort of budget. That being said, GET TO CARBONE. It is the best Italian restaurant in New York City. Wine selection is huge, amazing service, and I really can't think of the word to describe how great the food was. The baked clams are some of the best I've ever had. The spicy rigatoni is my favorite pasta dish in New York City. This is the only place I'd ever consider ordering veal parm from, and it was worth it, easily the best I've ever tried (though at $60, I probably would never get it again.) The carrot cake is a must if you even remotely like carrot cake. The old school Italian setting and service just adds to this place. Get here whenever you can (and have money to spare).

Carbone is possibly my favorite non-sushi restaurant in NYC. The atmosphere, service, and most importantly food, is phenomenal. My wife and I have now visited twice and we're blown away each time. 

The bread bowl is amazing, as is the house chopped salad. We've always seen what appears to be a fantastic Caesar salad, but have been unable to try it (wife is pregnant). The spicy rigatoni is better than any pasta either of us have ever eaten. This is a must order. 

We had the veal Parmesan during our first visit and it was excellent. Neither of us are huge veal fans but we still enjoyed it. 

I highly recommend Carbone for anyone interested in a world class red sauce joint in NYC.

Amazing experience! The beef carpaccio and the corn tartufo are a must have! I don't love veal, but their Veal Parmesan it's so worth it. Especially if you're a fan of veal. The spicy rigatoni was good, but I wasn't super impressed with it. Our server John was phenomenal. Excellent and friendly service. Loved him!!!!

Perfect place for a special occasion - obviously amazing food and incredible service. The spicy rigatoni, meatballs and veal parm are next level, and let's not forget about the bread and cheese that they give you in the beginning. Come hungry, because this place will have you leaving stuffed to the brim. I'd avoid the Caesar salad - it's bland and there are definitely way better options on the menu.

Yesterday was my first time at Carbone, and I highly recommend! The ambiance is romantic, upscale, and the music is phenomenal. The servers are SO attentive and professional. I recommend the chicken parm, which you have to order ahead by a day or two. Their corn side was delicious too. Definitely worth the splurge for a date or special occasion. Just be careful, plain black coffee is 7 dollars!

Carbone...is it worth all the hype? Yes! 

The food is obviously incredible but that isn't the whole story you also come here for the vibes and the service. It feels luxurious and old timey. Like when people dressed up to go out to dinner. Definitely special occasion appropriate. 

As for the food: expect lots of freebies and take that into account for how much to order. Also feel free to take a lot home to go! I have MEALS FOR DAYS. 

-freebies when you sit down: 
      -bread basket with unreal garlic bread, tomato bread, and plain bread all amazing 
       -salami
       -pickled cauliflower delicious
       -fresh from the wheel piece of Parmesan 
-Caesar salad with the best croutons I've ever had. If you're a fan of Caesar salads get this
-spicy rigatoni vodka. You're coming to Carbone for this so get it
-veal parm. You're also coming here for this so get it and you'll have leftovers because it's massive so enjoy it multiple times
-corn truffle side. Not amazing...you can skip
-carrot cake with ginger frosting and ice cream. I'm not a carrot cake person this turned me and I will never say that again
-Nutella tiramisu. I AM a tiramisu person and this was bad. Way to cakey and dry and zero flavor of Nutella. Skip it. 
-another freebie: almond rainbow cookie. A classic that's good if you like that almond flavor 
-great wines by the glass ask your server for recs. I loved the chianti Classico.

Wow ... just wow. Brought my girlfriend here for her birthday , the place is rather tight but it's beautifully decorated. Everyone is dressed elegantly , and the service is heartwarming. Very interactive waiter , but the food. The food was absolutely delicious , we got the rigatoni vodka and the ribeye diana with side of the corn. Ended it with the carrot cake with side of ginger ice cream. I will be coming back here. Thank you for everything!

This is the place I wanted to go for my 30th bday and so glad we came here.  Beautiful restaurant with an old school feel.  I have always been a huge fan of penne vodka so I knew I just had to try this one. 

You get a lot of complimentary items when you sit down: amazing focaccia bread, garlic bread, pickled cauliflower, spicy salami. All delicious. 

My husband and I got the burrata with eggplant caponata and it was DEVINE-- this was a special but they have it often I believe. 

Up next we got the meatballs - again insane. Get this. 

Guys next up was the rigatoni spicy vodka and truly this was spectacular.  I ate each noodle so damn slow to really enjoy it. 

Then we had the veal parm --- at this point of the meal I was full so I don't think I enjoyed it as much as I should (especially for 65 smackas).  If I came back here which I will I won't order this dish...

Insane in the membrane this place.

An upscale restaurant tucked away by NYU in a small narrow street. We had a reservation and were seated immediately with a quirky waiter. Awesome Italian/early Sinatra-esque music playing with waiters singing along. You are started with complementary garlic bread, pickled cauliflower, and a chunk of Parmesan cheese. The caprese was excellent and I will not describe the unique way they bring it out. I ordered an old fashioned that came out with a block of clear ice a beautiful presentation. As for the entrees I had pasta and the way it works is you order a meat dish such as meatballs and then pasta to accompany it. I had the spicy rigatoni which was excellent and the right portion size. I didn't have dessert because the quantity of food was crazy. The waiter brought over a couple Italian flag colored almond cookies which were tasty. As you leave make sure to grab some mints and a carbone matchbox as a souvenir. Definitely check it out if you have 100-200 to spend with a couple people. Unfortunately I didn't see former president Obama or Kelly Ripa.

i do understand why people return for the rigatoni - haven't had it quite like how they make it. definitely give the spicy rigatoni vodka a 4 star for sure! especially since i asked them to make it extra spicy and it actually had a kick! everything else about the restaurant was just mediocre. we started with the house made (from scratch) ceaser salad, as well as the clams. the clams were definitely great, made with 3 different sauces, very delicious. i loved that they served complimentary appetizers, which included their housemadw bread, cheese and meats. my boyfriend ordered the fettucine con funghi, wasn't impressed, said it was nothing special and actually kind of bland. the service was good, but wasn't exceptional. i definitely expected more considering how much i'm paying for my meal and being on the Michelin guide. i give it 4 stars because i would come back for the rigatoni but probably without my boyfriend, unfortunately he was not very impressed. he actually prefers Lilia over Carbone, for the price and quality/portions. but if you haven't been, you must go at least once! reservations are a must!

Octopus pizzaiolo
Caprese (the freshest mozzarella ever!)
Lobster ravioli
Spicy ragatoni vodka
Scallops piselli
Tiramisu & Chocolate cake 


Totally worth the hype. Please go if you can get a reso!

Worst Customer Service Ever; we will NEVER again seek to dine here, nor should you.  The management, staff and owner never got the memo that even purportedly "hot" restaurants are in the service business.

This restaurant has a byzantine and ludicrous email system for making reservations that is truly insulting and callous towards would-be guests.  Only email is acceptable; there are no provisions for phone calls. While this has become more often the case with some desirable restaurants, at least their procedures are transparent and specified online, which is not the case with Carbone.  

Our saga began when I (stupidly, as it turns out) identified Carbone as my first-choice destination restaurant for my milestone birthday dinner.  My sweet (and extremely busy, professional) husband contacted the restaurant, by email, for reservations for the two of us on my birthdate, and he received an officious "form" email (demanding our credit card) that only 6 PM was available, which is an unacceptable time for a celebratory dinner.   Never one to give up, he entered into a lengthy email correspondence, over the course of one week, with a Carbone reservationist, who instructed him to request another date.   We were extremely disappointed not to obtain reservations on my birthday, but, after a discussion, we selected a different date.   In an email, the reservationist explained that Carbone accepts email requests starting at 9 AM weekdays and 10 AM on weekends.   She specifically instructed my husband NOT to send his email request prior to those designated times, as those emails are sent to the rear of the queue and reviewed only after the "timely" email requests were processed.  He was appalled.

Nevertheless, my intrepid husband followed these instructions precisely, sending his email at 9:01 AM for a time between 7:30 and 8:30 PM.   To his shock, rather than receiving reservations for the requested time frame, he was sent yet another officious "form" email, this time from a different reservationist, informing him, again, that only 6:00 PM was available for our newly-requested date.   He requested by email the opportunity to discuss our reservation by phone, referencing the lengthy email correspondence with the first reservationist.  He received no reply whatsoever.  This is a restaurant that clearly plays "favorites" when filling reservations requests, and its staff, and owner/management, does not have the decency to care much about other prospective diners, much less deign to speak to them by telephone when warranted.  Their silence speaks volumes.

Based on mixed reviews alone, this restaurant is clearly NOT in the same hemisphere as The French Laundry, where we had the pleasure of dining earlier this year, and its reservation system and procedures are clearly explained online.  While this narrative may make certain readers more eager to obtain reservations here because of the perception of exclusivity, I shudder to think about the treatment diners receive upon arrival, having been forced to follow certain "rules" to make reservations.  This is not a restaurant for humans, but for trained animals that have been made to jump through hoops and then ignored.  And I'm quite sure most dogs receive better treatment than our "reservations experience" with Carbone.  As a longtime Manhattanite, who "dines around" regularly,  I can assure you that there are many fine and exclusive restaurants in New York City.  Seek to be parted with your money at one of those establishments, and not this one.

Overall: great food, poor service

For starters, myself and my husband arrived promptly at 8:55 pm for our 9:00 pm dinner. This promptness was not reciprocated. We proceeded to stand by the door for greater than 25 minutes until 9:22 when our table was finally ready...finally.

The waiter seemed busy and uninterested from the very beginning.

Next the food. We ordered the caprese (amazing) , beef carpaccio (could of skipped) spicy rigatoni (a must get), veal parm, meat balls, and carrot cake. The caprese and the rigatoni are both a must try. We barley saw our waiter our entire meal. This was a disappointment as part of the draw to this place was the fun atmosphere provided by the servers. This was not so with our experience

When finished we waited for over 20 minutes again for our waiter to even come to our table. To top it off when our bill came it was wrong with more than one item we did not order and we where left with the uncomfortable task of correcting our waiter. When dropping over $250 for a meal for two I expect top notch service. Unfortunately this was not the case.

Yerrrrr ...alright so boom check it. Date number five. I haven't had carbs on a regular basis in some time, especially pasta so I was excited. M'lady arrived before me and when I got there, I saw some cauliflower, obviously bread, some cheese and what tasted like salami but better. The place is dope. The music, surprisingly awesome. I don't know why I said surprisingly but it wasn't what I expected. On to the food. So the server suggested we get the branzino and split it...he might have been right. She got the sea bass, I had the spaghetti pomodoro. Here's where I could split hairs. The Spaghetti was great on its own. The server sold me on the meatballs. I didn't need the meatballs. The meatballs were huge. Massive. I couldn't finish them. I took them home and they were dope. Also...a little pricier than I'd have liked. Anyway, the place is dope. If you like good Italian food and a nice ambiance, check this place out.

My boyfriend and I came here for an early Sunday dinner and we were not disappointed! I'm not usually a huge fan of traditional 'red sauce' Italian restaurants but I had heard so many good things about Carbone - it seemed like it was worth a try.  I thoroughly enjoyed two very different but delicious Italian wines and a tuna crudo dish, plus all the freebies you get when you sit down - cured meats, an assortment of breads, house made giardiniera and a nice hunk of aged parmesan. Boyfriend was thrilled with his tender veal parmesan and spaghetti pomodoro, which was sauced perfectly. We shared a Caesar salad, with the dressing made fresh tableside, and tiramisu (not traditional, but very tasty!) 
I see some complaints about saltiness (I found the dishes perfectly balanced) and service (in our experience, perfectly attentive without being in your face) - I think sometimes people just feel the need to nitpick. The only thing that struck us as odd was that the waiter kept referring to the dishes as 'family style,' but the portions weren't big (compared to some other Italian restaurants, at least). All in all, this meal was fantastic and I'd love to go back.

This place is great. Went with a group of friends on. Saturday night, had to make reservations a month in advance, but was easily able to change the guest number just a few days before the reservation. Spicy rigatoni was delicious, caprese salad was good, octopus was good but a small portion. The mussels were the best appetizer. Service was great. Carrot cake is the best dessert, the cheesecake was the second best. The Nutella tiramisu was just ok. Wine selection is huge, but they have someone to help you narrow down the choices. The old fashions were good. Price is on the higher end, but overall a decent value.

The food made up for the 20 minute wait! We had 5 of the 8 pastas they have, all of them were fantastic. We had the very best waiter Sal, I highly recommend asking for him when making a reservation. The veal was official, and the steak was tender and very juicy. The lemon Cheesecake was phenomenal and so was the Nutella tiramisu. They lost 2 stars for 2 reasons:
1. The reservation process is ridiculous. Emailing them to get a reservation is pointless. I emailed them to get a reservation a few weeks ago and they responded an hour and a half later. Very unprofessional and frankly a waste of time. No other restaurants do this, even busier then them, and if they are trying to start a trend it's not happening. 

2.The hostesses are a waste of space. They run around and act like they are busy when in reality they are just singing along to the music and twiddling their thumbs. One is sufficient and it was obvious because one guy was the only one moving around. Having 2 hostesses is useful if it's packed but 3 or 4 is just excessive. 

Overall, for my 2nd experience there, it's still a great spot and frankly my favorite MFG restaurant. Atmosphere is typical "wannabe nouveau riche" Americans. The waiters and the food are the best parts of this place.

I have been wanting to try this place for the spicy vodka rigatoni ($29) for years, and it did not disappoint (5/5). For such a simple pasta, this was truly outstanding and one of the best pastas I have had. I also had the meatballs (3/5) and I think they were around $18 and not very good at all. My mom and grandma do meatballs better. These were basic with nothing to justify the price point or the calories. I also had a glass of the aglianico ($18, $21 with tip) which was outstanding, but then you realize that the price of the bottle is between $22-24. The nerve of restaurants these days charging the price of the bottle for one glass. On a brighter note, they did provide a lot of free stuff including a block of parmesan cheese, delicious spread of breads, pickled cauliflower in olive oil, and cured meat. 

The ambiance is old world Italian. There is no denying that it is stuffy in there. And, very difficult to get in. Overall, the spicy rigatoni is worth the price, the hassle, and the stuffiness.

Zucchini leaves stuffed with crabmeat, and big eyed tuna seafood cocktail to start. Rigatoni vodka and meatballs were the main course. And we had tiramisu for dessert.  Two glasses of wine. Cappuccino/anise to finish the meal. Every dish was near perfect.  It was a great lunch . One warning though, It is quite pricey. $200 for lunch is over the top for us but  we both felt it was a great way to end our vacation.

We are Italian food obsessed, so we felt it necessary to rate this restaurant. After hearing many good things, we decided to take the trip. The bread was okay. We just didn't even feel like we were in an Italian restaurant and it was really over priced for the quality of the food. We got the sizzling pancetta (literal garbage), the tortellini ragu (the only meat sauce on the menu) which was actually pretty good, and the veal Parmesan was the last thing we ordered. The entrees were good but honestly the service was awful and so was the wine. Honestly, it was just okay and definitely not worth the money.

Way over priced and not close to the best Italian food I have ever had or even 3rd best.  Veal parm was very salty. The actual veal was great quality but the breading and cheese were just ehh. Expected it to be way better for $64.  The service was excellent.  The food was just okay and any mom/pop Italian restaurant is better.  The vodka sauce was very good but again nothing special!!!

I embraced the idea of Carbone.  After Torrisi Italian specialities did so well in all categories.  But Carbone?  Carbone is an expensive mildly theatrical experience of what one might have experienced had they been in NYC 30 years ago in an old italian neighborhood.  My experience with Carbone was not bad, per se.  The food was good, no better than the old-school italian red sauce joints that have been around for years.  The problem?  You order a lobster fra diavalo at an old school italian restaurant and you get (or I should say "got") a run-of-the mill salad, a side dish (pasta or roasted vegetable) -- INCLUDED in the price.  At Carbone?  No such luck .Carbone is akin to the "country expositions" in Epcot Center in Disney World in that it seeks to mimic the draws of its predecessors (think dessert cart pushed around the restaurant) but without the quality per unit of price that the true traditional italian restaurants offer(ed).  If you are swimming in disposable income and can let go of what you once knew (or maybe never knew) about a real italian red sauce joint, then Carbone won't bother you.  But I was sorely disappointed and saddened as many of the old-school red sauce joints who served equal, if not better food, close and this place gets praised as if its some kind of novel idea.  Because, guess what?  It's not.

After finally trying Carbone, I have to say I was a little disappointed. For all the hype this place gets, I excepted it to be amazing. It was okay. The meatballs were okay, the spicy rigatoni was pretty good but not amazing, the lasagna was horrible. Our waiter was knowledgeable about the menu but tried to push too much food on us (we ended up ordering about 6 dishes for two people...we could have stopped at 4 max). I don't like a pushy waiter!  Overall, I'm glad I tried it but there are way too many other great Italian restaurants in NYC to go to ones that are just okay.

I made this reservation for two a month in advance. I got a 5pm reservation on a Sunday.  Other than that, I couldn't get anything during the week that wasn't 11pm. The ambiance was really nice.  They are on their game, there was no wait in serving us the bread and taking our orders and getting our food to us. 

They gave complimentary great bread, salami, a chunk of parmesan, and cauliflower to start. All delish. 
We ordered the octopus, Cesar salad, spicy rigatoni vodka, the veal Parm, and the carrot cake. 

You MUST order the rigatoni, it melts like butter and was amazing. The veal Parm was good but not worth $67. A little crazy. The carrot cake was good, but also $16. 

Overall it was a great dinner but won't be returning anytime soon as it was a very expensive meal.

Decided to give this place a go after friends had made a reservation and extended an invite to my fiancée and I. I wasn't completely blown away. The food was overtly expensive and good, not amazingly good, just good perhaps slightly great but overextended due to the price of each plate. I loved the wine that was recommended but came to find that we had overpaid upon googling it to further my knowledge on exactly what we had drank that night. We spent $120 on this bottle that has an msrp of $54.99 to maybe $60.00. This furthers my opinion on Carbone - the food is good, the spicy rigatoni was delicious which I can agree with all the reviews below. Upon being seated, we were served a bread basket, a small plate of pickled cabbage and individual chunks of Parmesan. I love cheese, bread and anything pickled - great start. 

Appetizers that I tasted: the mussels, octopus and fresh mozzarella made in house. All were very tasty, especially the mussels. The octopus was fantastic as well.

Dinner: a shared plate of spicy rigatoni and cherry pepper ribs. The ribs were okay, however the bed of greens that accompanied them were prepared amazingly with a lot of great flavor notes. It was probably by far the simplest dish we ate but I enjoyed it the most.

Dessert: carrot cake, tiramisu and cheesecake topped with grappa and espressos (our waiter also presented us with a bottle of house Sambuca; and no not Romana Sambuca just some cheap version which baffles my mind because how expensive everything is on the menu) nothing special in my opinion.

Our bill was extraneous - however, we had a table of seven and each had a cocktail or two so it made sense.  

As a first generation Italian, there's better Italian out there for less money. Our waiter also slightly irked me when he kept putting on a "show" and acting like he was an extra on The Sopranos. It really kills the mood and gives Italians this gimmicky rep. Next time, I'm going to refrain from eating Italian food out and stick to my mother's cooking - more authentic representation and Italian food. There wasn't any passion or real thought behind each dish to honest.

Carbone is truly a dining experience that lives up to the hype. I had to ask myself after stalking the reservation site religiously and finally getting a 10:00pm reservation on a Wednesday 30 days ahead of time, "is it worth it?" Yes, it absolutely is. The drinks, service and of course, the food are all incredible. I don't know how I'm going to ever eat another Italian meal after this one (sorry mom). 

To start, we ordered two martinis - one dirty and one with a twist. They were perfect. We were also served bread, salami and cauliflower as a nice little starter. For the meal, we ordered the Caesar alla ZZ, Caprese, Spicy Rigatoni Vodka, Veal Parmesan and Meatballs. I was obsessed with everything. You really cannot go wrong with that selection. We obviously over-ordered for two people but having leftover veal parm and meatballs was the next best thing to repeating the experience all over again. The only mistake we made was ordering another round of drinks and feeling a bit hungover the next day.

Overall, you need to come here at least once for a special occasion. I cannot say enough about how great the food is. 

A few things to note: Unless you know someone, it will take a while (30 days) to get a reservation here so plan ahead! Attire ranged from very dressy to nice-casual so you can make that decision. Meatballs (and possibly the Caprese - but I saw it on the menu online) are not on the menu but simply ask, and you will receive. The vodka rigatoni is a small portion but it is perfect for splitting if you are ordering multiple other dishes. And last, if you have to choose between the veal and the meatballs, go for the veal.

What hasn't been said already about Carbone. I've fortunately been a patron since the spring opening in 2013 and always enjoyed my meals. 

On a recent visit I was very pleased to try the beets siciliana, [raw] tuna over eggplant puree, spicy rigatoni vodka (as always), fettuccine with mushrooms, the meatballs (lunch only) and the squash .. I'm as amazed with each bite each visit like it's my first time. For dessert, I'm always a sucker for carrot cake. I like the chocolate cake too but I think the presentation of the carrot cake is fun. And as one would expect it's quite tasty. The complimentary garlic bread and salami and fresh mozzarella is a great way to start the meal and whet the appetite. I am not sure how comfortable they are to wear but I do get a kick out of the uniforms too. 

I don't think you can go wrong with any item on the menu. Previously I've had (the one and only) veal parm, the veal marsala, the rib-eye and the ribs - and I keep coming back for more.

Planning some travel soon and look forward to trying the newer restaurants in Hong Kong and Las Vegas

This Italian restaurant has to be on the top of my list. I usually don't go for Italian food because I don't find it having much flavor but let me tell you... THIS place has flavor that explodes in your mouth.  A must try are the meatballs and the lobster ravioli. To die for! I even had a dream about these two things the same night.  I also had the rigatoni (it was good but it had nothing special).  They make the cesar salad right in front of you and place a block of pecorino cheese on your plate. It was quite nice! The oysters were super fresh and the sauce it came with was delicious! I recommend you try these dishes if you decide to head to Carbone.

Carbone definitely lives up to the hype - a must-do for any New Yorker or visitor. I luckily found 10pm reservations for two on a Saturday night, although any open time you can find is absolutely worth it. This place is booked a month or two in advance.

It boasts a charming, old-school Italian atmosphere with Frank Sinatra and the likes playing in the background. The captains (not waiters) are dressed up in tuxes and are extremely friendly, knowledgeable, and accommodating. Service can be a little slow at times, but it didn't bother us.

As soon as we sat, we were given complimentary salami, picked cauliflower, and a bread basket with Italian, garlic, and grandma's bread. The grandma's bread was my personal favorite. Our waiter never came to take our drink order until we flagged him down, but as soon as we did, he apologized and rushed back to the table with our wine.

Per his recommendation, we ordered the carpaccio and baked clams to start. The clams come in three variations, one of which was clams casino. The carpaccio is topped with olive oil, black pepper, and walnuts - it was delicious. Definitely order this.

For dinner, we shared the spicy rigatoni which was possibly the best pasta dish I've ever had. It's perfectly cooked and the sauce is rich, creamy, and cheesy, not really spicy. The split portion is the perfect amount. We also shared the veal parm, another dish worth the rave reviews. Though expensive ($67), there is a lot of veal and they include the bone, which has been fried and sprinkled with parmesan. Unfortunately, we forgot to order the meatballs, but we were so full we decided we were better off.

Dessert fell a little flat. We ordered the carrot cake, which ended up being compliments of the restaurant because we waited so long for our wine. I'm a huge carrot cake fan and theirs was just okay. The ginger cream cheese frosting is unique - it's the saving grace of the dish as the cake itself is pretty dry. It also comes with a scoop of ginger ice cream. I would skip this and try the tiramisu.

The best Italian place in New York! The veal parm and spicy rigatoni are a must. Along with reservations lol. There's also a possibility you could be dining among celebrities! The ambience is old world Italian. It's defiantly worth trying! You won't regret it.

After hearing about how amazing this restaurant was, I knew I wanted to celebrate my 40th Birthday there.  A girls weekend to NYC was concluded with my birthday dinner celebration at Carbone.  Reservations were secured well over a month in advance, taking whatever time we could get, 10:00pm. Needless to say, we were quite committed to this experience.

At first, the waitstaff and service was impeccable. The antipasti that was provided was amazing.  The wine was wonderful and we were enjoying this culminating dining event, with great ambiance and company.  And then we ordered. 

I am not certain if the items we ordered were not 
expensive enough....sausage with rabe, spicy rigatoni (4 half orders), meatballs, and Caesar salad or the fact that we were not locals played into the sudden decline in attention to our table but we were only seen one more time the entire evening- when a second bottle of wine was ordered and never brought to the table.  In fact, after sitting for over  20 minutes without any attention to our empty plates and wine glasses, we asked to speak to a manager.  

The manager arrived and asked "so, what's wrong? What is it you need? All I can offer you is food or drink. So will a half glass of wine make it all better for you?"  An apology was all that was needed and then a fresh experience with the same level of attention that was given at the initiation of the dinner. 

The birthday celebration that was noted to the hostess at the onset by my friends, was haphazardly acknowledged, by not giving the same dessert that was clearly afforded to every other table celebrating- of which I will never know what it was because the dessert tray, which is proudly paraded through the restaurant at the end of each meal to other patrons, was never offered to our table.

I want to be fair here. I would return, because the atmosphere of Carbone is simply fabulous. The music, the lighting, and interior make for a wonderful experience. 

We were not blessed with a great waiter. He was a "know it all" and would walk away literally mid-sentence to deal with another table and acted like it was par for the course. It was odd. Then, we placed an order for a great 2012 white wine and when it arrived, it was very good, but the color was almost orange. My travel companion is a wine distributer and was disturbed by the color and the fact that the year listed in the wine list was 2012 and we received a 2013. There was no offer to replace the bottle and for a restaurant of this caliber, that is an expectation. Our waiter tried to explain that there are many orange wines and insisted there was nothing to worry about! He had no idea that my friend is a wine expert.

Food: The bread, cauliflower, and salami were outstanding and great way to begin a dinner. We ordered the rapini and sausage, and prosciutto and mozzarella as appetizers. The rapini was flavorless and sausage was very salty. The prosciutto was excellent, but the mozzarella was salty. We then tried their house chopped salad. Honestly, it was my favorite dish on the menu. Really unexpected flavors. The salad is a must try dish. After appetizers, we tried the Linguine Alla Vongole and Spicy Rigatoni Alla Vodka. The rigatoni was excellent and is a must try dish. The linguine was salty and nothing stood out.  Next, we tried the Dover Piccata. It was well done and a great dish to try. Market price for this dish was $100.00 - a little steep even  for NYC. 

Overall, I had higher expectations for a $400.00 dinner for two. I expect the service to be better and the food to be a little less salty. However, I would give it a second chance.

Such a great restaurant!  The fried calamari is delicious--much better than what you would expect. Loved sharing the dishes--and they custom sized them perfectly for our table of four. We had two great pasta dishes and salads. Fabulous bread basket. Could have done without the side order of meatballs.  Good but a bit salty for my taste. Great service and wine recommendation too.

SO WORTH IT. Had been dying to try Carbone for so long but couldn't secure a reservation (probably one of the only negatives I'll mention in this review) after many failed attempts. A friend and her bf had a res on a Sunday at 515pm and unfortunately couldn't make it so they let us use it (yay for us)!! 

Immediately lahhhved the basement/mafia/OG Italian vibe when we entered - small/cosy, waiters in tuxedos, checkered floor. We sat a table away from the hostess against the right wall as you enter, which was fine at first but got a little tight when there were parties on both side of us. So tight the table had to be pulled out for me to use the bathroom and I'm pretty small.

We started out with 2 glasses of chianti. AWESOME complimentary fixins at the start - 3 types of bread (garlic/asiago, grandmas, normal italian), pickled cauliflower, salami, and a chunk of parmaggiano each. We opted to order the burrata eggplant caponata special served with yet more delicious crostini. Buratta was legit out of this world. Haven't had a fresher one since being in Italy. Next up we decided to split the 2 signature dishes - spicy rigatoni vodka and veal parm. Let me start by saying I don't love veal, I actually hadn't had veal in YEARS, but I quickly became obsessed with that veal. Perfectly crisped breading on the outside, not dry on the inside. Served aside the bone (P bit into that ish). The spicy rigatoni was also delicious yet didn't find it spicy at all! Right on par with creamy and rich sauce yet not overwhelming in the slightest. Almost felt like a cross between a vodka and tomato base. To end, 2 complimentary rainbow cookies were served. I don't have a huge sweet tooth so P ate both.

Will definitely be back and cannot wait to try a few different pastas and the meatballs. Fantastic service too...our waiter wasn't pushy and honestly answered when we questioned how many dishes to order.

Food: mediocre
Presentation of food: nice 
Atmosphere: stuffy
Too many work- staff members makes it feel overcrowded and uncomfortable.

So the easiest way to begin this review is by saying you will appreciate Carbone if you value service/quality over portions. The restaurant is positioned in Greenich Village which is just off of Houston. My experience is as followed.

Arrive a few minutes before my 6:15pm reservation to be welcomed by a doorman who welcomed me with a smile. Walk up to the hostess stand who informs me that my guest has arrived and walks me to the table. My buddy and I order around of drinks to begin. In addition to our drinks, we are brought out a bread basket, a few slices of pepperoni and cauliflower in olive oil and garlic.

We put in our orders and the food came out in good time. Wine was flowing, conversation was going and the food was stellar. What else can you ask for?

Plan to return and enjoy more nights at Carbone.

We dined here Sunday, October 29th for my sons 25th birthday.  His choice he had heard such wonderful reviews.  The online reservation request worked great even though it displayed NO AVAILABILITY after emailing they accommodated the four of us.  I have to be honest it was a HUGE DISAPPOINTMENT.  Our waiter dressed in a plum suit was great.  We ordered thinking portions are family style but once plates arrived it was clear this was not FAMILY STYLE PORTIONS.  I have eaten at Carmine's which does serve family style portions but the portion size at Carbones could be shared by TWO but in my opinion it's best suited for ONE.  We ordered the house chopped and the Caesar salad to start, the spicy rigatoni vodka which was NOT spicy and arrived COLD to the table.  Nothing worst than cold pasta especially at a price tag of over $30 for such a small serving. The Rib Eye Diana and the Potatoes Louie and the chicken scapariello.  For desert we had the Lemon Cheesecake which was the only thing that appeared oversized. The food in my opinion was mediocre.  I ordered coffee and requested amaretto in my coffee.  I got a cold cup of coffee with something that was not amaretto.  It was undrinkable.  Not worth the bill of over $300 for a family of four.   Also be mindful of how you get your water.  Initially when we arrived we were asked if we wanted sparkling, flat, distilled..... we chose FLAT thinking it was FREE... it wasn't our water came out to $36.  Everyone around us seemed to be enjoying the free water out of a red jug which is what you should choose.  Also when I got my coffee I kindly asked one of the guys in a suit for splenda sugar and he looked at me as if he was insulted that I asked.  Evidently he was a host not a waiter and he never brought me the Splenda for my COLD cup of coffee.  I WOULD NOT RECOMMEND Carbones I feel it's greatly overrated and overpriced for average tasting small servings. I believe that for Italian food their are much tastier economical choices out their like Carmine's who truly sell family style portions.  Would not dine here again.

Truly worth every speck of the hype. Reservations are impossible to get so we finally ended up just taking one on a weekday at 10pm about a month out, and it was such a good decision. We split the caesar salad, which is mixed table side, and is huge (easily can be split between between 2 people). I had the spicy rigatoni bc of course and it was probably the best food I've ever eaten. The servers were excellent - so attentive and friendly, and you get a ton of bread / cheese / meats included with your meal. The vibes are prohibition-y and super cool, and while it is pricey it is reasonable based on what you're getting. One of my favorite dinners I've ever had.

Service was wonderful from the moment you approach the door, you're greeted with a smile by the doorman. The atmosphere was everything I wanted it to be - from the plates to the music to the chairs. It added to my joy. 
The bread, pepperoni, and cauliflower were delicious - and I don't like cauliflower. The fresh piece of parm cheese was perfect with all of it. 
We ordered the tuna crudo special and burrata special. Tuna was good - but wasn't blowing me away. Burrata was excellent. It had eggplant and pine nuts on top which I usually don't mess with perfect cheese and prefer it plain - this was a nice sweet balance to it however and didn't take away from the creamy flavors. They take some of the inside out and put it separate from the larger ball of mozz and they add a pinch of salt to it. I loved it like that bc it brought the flavors out more. But I have read other reviewers saying it was too salty. The larger ball of mozz was not salted so just stick to that if you don't enjoy salt. 
Next we ordered the spicy vodka rigatoni and the tortellini ragu. 
The spicy rigatoni -- I know everyone is raving about this dish. It's all over social media. Other reviewers can't get enough of it. I had high expectations for it - however - it was just ok. It wasn't spicy. It wasn't your typical creamy vodka sauce either. It came no where near blowing me away and when I return to Carbone, I likely won't order it again. My personal opinion?  It's overrated. People I think enjoy it so much bc of the hype and excitement but flavor wise it was probably one of my least favorites of the night. 
Now the tortellini??  Our waiter convinced us to get that instead of the meatballs and I am so glad he did. Holy delicious Batman!   This dish was probably the best we had all night. The pockets of fresh cheese and the little taste of meat and red sauce with each bite melt in your mouth. I could have licked that plate if it was acceptable. 
We then had the ribeye and the squash side. By this time we were almost going to explode we were getting so full but the meat was perfectly medium rare and the mushrooms on top were divine. The meat had the perfect salty char on the outside that complimented the flavor so well. 
The squash. Let's talk about the squash. This was on another level of deliciousness that I didn't think existed. The cheese. The pumpkin seeds. That butter sauce they pour on top. Unreal. Truly a genius combination. Get the squash side. You'll thank me later. 
We left zero room for dessert unfortunately. They bring you almond rainbow cookies at the end which I forced myself to enjoy. I don't like rainbow cookies or almond flavored desserts but they were good. 
I will definitely return one day. I think I'd like to come with a larger group of people rather than just 2 people so as to try a lot more as there is just too much to choose from!

This was a hard reservation to get, and I'm sorry to say it was not worth the wait. I was a big fan of Rocco, the decades-long resident of this Thompson Street red sauce hot spot. The ghost of restaurant past is still present there, although the red curtains obscuring the street view and the new decor do all they can to gussy it up. 

From beginning to end, this experience was culinary theater. It's a Hollywood version of a high end Italian eatery, and nothing quite comes back around to make sauce. We started with Caesar salad, which was assembled table side. Or, sort of table side. The elements were shown to us before they whisked away. What returned was basically just romaine, cheese, and croutons with a goopy pre-made dressing. Think Marzettis.

The wild boar sausage was so greasy it was barely edible. Skip it for sure.

We did order three Yelp favorites--the spicy rigatoni, meatballs, and veal parm. All were delicious and would be totally acceptable at a checkered table cloth establishment in Little Italy, alongside a chianti bottle in a straw basket.  Unfortunately, it was served at one of the hottest tables in town...with a price tag that rivals Per Se.

Pass.
Such a snobby place. Will not serve me because I'm wearing jeans and a hat. Food is good but will not go back!

Beautiful restaurant great music but food is subpar. Sent pasta and meat back. Too salty. Not impressed at all. So many better Italian restaurants in city. Il Mulino far superior as well as most neighborhood Italian eateries.

Okay....so here is an honest review of this very exclusive...sought after restaurant.

Overall...this place is an experience...certainly worth going to...once...our dinner was literally 3-4 hours...so it's a whole night!

Let me preface by saying that I've eaten a LOT of amazing Italian food....a LOT...both in Italy and NY...I'm from Brooklyn...no shortage of great options.

Anyway...I immediately have to take off a star for the BS. I eat out a lot and entertain a lot for my job so I've been to my fair share of upscale, snooty NY spots. I've tried maybe for a few years to take clients here, but since we always have too many people, I could never get a res at a reasonable time.  On this occasion, my friends were in town and I literally marked my calendar to make a res here a month in advance...let's just say it still wasn't easy but I did it. I can't stand that they don't have a phone...we ran late and I couldn't call them like I would a normal place. I legit thought they would give our table away based on the difficulty of getting the res. Of course we get there and our table wasn't ready, we waited an hour at the bar. They did comp drinks so overall it was fine but still, the stress of rushing there was put a damper on the night. 

Anyway, on to the service and food. I must say once we were seated, I was very impressed. The waited was so attentive, great recommendations and explanation of everything. The bread, cheese and antipasti that came out to start was yummy and the perfect way to start the meal.

Now...the rigatoni...that everyone raved about..."you must get that and the veal parm everyone said..."meh...it was just okay. Solid at best, I've had better from a friends Italian grandma. The veal parm was also just solid...nothing to rave about.

What I LOVED was the spaghetti gricia, this was phenomenal...I'm a huge fan of cacio e Pepe so this was similar and delish. Al dente...peppery, bacony...yum! 

We got meatballs on the side...they were okay...a little underdone even.

We also had some gigantic shrimp from Madagascar that was epic, we were lucky enough to get the last two, highly recommend. Definitely get the home made mozz as a starter as well.

We over-ordered for sure, wish the waiter told us we had too much, none of us could finish the ribs we also got so sent most of it back.

The carrot cake for dessert was also delish...super moist and great presentation.

I think I would only go back though if they made the reservations a bit more reasonable...not worth the hassle, many great restaurants in ny...like OTTO and Lupa for example, few blocks away and none of the fuss. Also...get a F'ing phone! Seriously it's pretentious as F not to have a phone.

We got to sit in the legendary back room. The wait staff were very attentive, friendly and fun. Service was excellent, no complaints. The atmosphere is fun, Sumatra music playing in the background at a comfortable volume. But the room is small and it is loud. Say hi to Ricky, and ask about his Maroon suit. The spicy rigatoni is the signature dish. The meatballs were delicious but my only complaint is they seemed a bit undercooked (pink). 
For appetizer we had the beef carpaccio and the sausage. Both outstanding. 
They make only 2 trays of lasagna a day so we decided to try it. While it was delicious- made with a crispy cheese top, and green pasta with some broccoli rabe, and lots of sauce on the side, note that it is different for traditional. 
For dessert we had the Nutella tiramisu (must have this) and the cassata. 
The place is an experience. If you are looking for traditional authentic Italian food, this is not the place. This is more Americanized Italian - very good with a Godfather atmosphere (again, not authentic Italian but Americanized). It was a lot of fun with very friendly staff. It is worth a trip but don't stress if you can't get a reservation right away.
Love this place! It's never let me down! Great decor, quality authentic food and great service!

Huge disappointment.  The hostess was rude and the waitstaff was flat at best. The incredibly overpriced food is mediocre. I can't believe this is a place where people wait months for reservations. I felt like I was on Candid Camera, waiting for someone to pop out around the corner and scream, "Surprise- here's your real food!". Sadly, that never happened. I wish I paid attention to the reviews and looked elsewhere. NYC has so many amazing places to eat and Carbone is NOT one of them.

Wow! What a place! Have been a number of times..Food is always amazing! A must go to place! The wait staff is fantastic and super on it! The Spicy Rigatoni is off the charts delicious! Cant go wrong with it! Chicken Parm...a real 10! Killer wine list! Great Vibe! Julian at the front is insanely awesome, a true gentleman! Do yourself a favor and go have dinner here!

I felt like I stepped into a time warp of Italian magnificence when I stepped into Carbone. The decor was beautiful and the waitstaff was dressed in pink tuxedos that mimicked an era of the past. The food though..... holy Mama Cucina. Deliciousness. Every single thing I put in my mouth was amazing. Go here people...... make a reservation in advance and enjoyyyyyyyy

Can I give it 6 stars!?  I didn't know service u til I came here.  Our waiter is Jason.. I actually had to do this here because I did not want to forget.  You HAVE TO COME HERE. They greet you upfront and walk you back to a cute rustic Italian intimate setting... i love the atmosphere and Sinatra type music with incredible service!! Our waiter Jason couldn't be more friendly or engaging..and everything on the menu looks great. They gave us a taste of amazing Parmesan cheese, bread, and picked vegetables before ordering... then the tossed Salad. It's not just a salad. Just get it!!!  My main course is the linguine fungi and the pasta is perfect!!!!! My boyfriend got lobster ravioli and said it's the best!!!
The lemon cheesecake!! Omg. I can't!  So good!  He even brought a candle in it. Said we looked like we are celebrating:)

Just come here. Make a reservation a few days before and make it happen. Love it!!!!

Absolutely worth the wait and hassle to get a table. There is not a single thing on the menu that I would not recommend. Try and go for this indulgence every few weeks... Especially when friends and family are in town. One of my favorite restaurants in New York City.

My sister and I went to Carbone for lunch. We ordered the clams appetizer, which was fantastic. It's prepared three ways and we enjoyed each one. Then we split the famous spicy rigatoni and the lobster ravioli. The rigatoni was good, although definitely not worth the $30+ price for the small portion, I expected it to be amazing but it wasn't. The most disappointing was the lobster ravioli, it tasted like Chinese dumpling to me, but not a good one. Couldn't eat more than one piece of it, again a hefty $36! I can cross this off my list and won't go back, much better Italian food elsewhere.

We made it! We made it! Carbone - you were totally worth the wait and struggle to get into your restaurant. The most amazing italian place I have been to in a while with the 10 star service you only dream of.

Hypes:
- This is a dining experience that lives up to its reputation. By experience I mean the service, the food, the atmosphere, even the breads in the beginning...damn
- Definitely get the meatballs - amazing dish...saucy, soft, awesome.
- the caesar salad is fantastic
- the rigatoni vodka is amazing -  they know its so popular they will split it in a plate for you so both of you don't have to kill each other for tastes and bites of one dish - its that good. I would kill for it.

We can't wait to come here again - if we ever try to make it out - it will be totally worth it.

Authentic Italian! The place is small but intimate setting. Inside reminds me of an old mobster joint. I was not able to have everything on the menu however, we sampled the must haves! Calamari was outstanding. Oyster were fresh and really great. The Veal Parm did not disappoint, spicy vodka rigatoni was superb. Meatball is a must try. Portions are larger than usual and advised to share which is always a great for a large group. Overall the food, the crowd, the staff is a solid five!

I chose to eat at Carbone for lunch due to a very high recommendation from a friend. 

Despite the hype, it was very easy to make a lunch reservation with only three days in advance (but I believe it's more difficult to make dinner reservations with that short of a notice). I went to their site to make the reservation, which will direct you to use Reserve.

Upon arrival, my friend and I get seated almost immediately. The waiter provided us with huge menus with few to select from, but I can imagine that each of these items on the menu are made to perfection. We order and are shortly served soft bread with complimentary prosciutto and fresh mozzarella - delicious!

Then comes my entrée - the famous Veal Parmesan ($65)! It was a big portion but the proportion of veal to cheese to sauce with the fresh basil leaves were perfect! And as an added bonus, this meal comes with a rib with a little meat to enjoy. The entrée was highly enjoyable and the portion was pretty big for lunch, so I was able to take some home to enjoy later. So I made two meals out of one, which helped me to justify the amount spent. haha.

I also did not finish my veal parmesan because I had to have dessert while dining here! We ordered the Carrot Cake with Ginger Ice Cream ($12). It was a good balance to have the cake with the ice cream.

I definitely have to come back and I want to try the other well known dish here - the Tortellini Al Ragu!
The food here was amazing! The service was incredible our waiter Jarrod was very attentive. Can not say enough about this place...the food was very authentic.

Cozy, it gives you the feel of an authentic Italian restaurant. The decoration adds a dash of nostalgia wish I love. Every plate is made to perfection. Portions are pretty reasonable. Service is incredible. My favorite dish was the rigatoni ala vodka, outstanding! I was crazy about the meat balls as well and I'm not even a fan of meatballs. Best meatballs ever! The scallops were delicious as well as the the "Prime Porterhouse" and this steak is huge and cooked to perfection. I tried hard eating it all, but failed! Anyways, everything else is absolutely delicious.I have to admit I was not crazy about the veil parmigiana to be honest also the Sea bass was slightly overcooked (asked rare)  but honestly, they are still very good. I went with a large group with gave me the chance to taste pretty much everything in the menu. The wine selection is outstanding and amazing cocktails. The staff gets a "five stars" everyone so attentive including the hostess and bussers.
 Is a most visit restaurant in NYC! Just really hard to get a table. So good luck with that!

It is worth it!
Excellent ambiance and service. Went for the birthdays of my friend and me - it was excellent food and experience. Veal parm was amazing - can not wait to go again!

Simply put , this place is a rip-off. The manager is rude, the music is loud, the chicken came out raw, and the prices are unconscionablle.  The chef is clearly a prima donna. The waiter tried to make the best of a bad situation, but even then he offered 3 people 2 desserts. We declined and I suggest anyone who plans on going there do the same !
If, I had any doubts about how cool this place was, those were erased when I saw Keith Richards walking in Monday evening to celebrate his birthday.
Carbone. I love thee. Old world Italian charm. Every single course is spectacular. From the bread to dessert and everything in between. Very pricey. But well worth it.

Hands down my favorite meal in NYC. 

Authenticity you can taste. The vodka rigatoni and caesar salad were excellent and definite stand outs. I crave these two at least 4 times a week! 

Too bad I live in LA. :(

Ambience was intimate and cozy. Service was great, our server was friendly and very informative. 

Can't wait to go back!

I have lived in NYC for my entire life and regularly  frequent many many restaurants throughout the city . I can honestly tell you that Carbone is an overrated and extremely expensive restaurant. The food is average/good  but the value is terrible. The Caesar salad, tuna crudo, meatballs and veal parm were good. The baked clams were cold and the chicken scarpariello was very fair. There are so many much better Italian restaurants in NYC for much less money. And the joke is that Carbone basically makes you beg to get a reservation. Carbone will  cost you $150 per person if you have 2 drinks. This place is a tourist trap and I would bet that many of their good reviews come from out of towers who are not used to the quality of food (and the values) that are available in NYC. Of course any good restaurant in NYC is not cheap but at least many of them leave you feeling like you had a good meal. Sorry to be so frank but this place is a ripoff.
Carbone is a super hot spot. The food is excellent. It's expensive and you'll know that before going in. The veal parm and spicy rigatoni and incredible. It's certainly an experience and scene.

I liked the atmosphere. It was a special evening for my wife's birthday and we celebrated with our daughter and her boyfriend. Service was good and our waiter was very attentive. Did not like that we were seated next to the kitchen. Can't say anything bad about the food, but when I go out I want something that I don't get at home. So in the area of "special" dishes they failed. Prices are very high, so much so that I found them insulting. Bottle of wine I normally pay $44 at retail was $185, and they do not buy at retail. I understand they need to make a profit, but again I found it insulting. Enjoyed the evening, but would not go back. It's the City and they can get away with ridiculous pricing because there is an endless pool of special occasions and people, like me, that will pay for one night. My New Years resolution is to avoid the temptation - just go to places that are really good and without the hype. And there are more than one can count.

Love the food, but don't love the service. Not sure what it is, but I just can't get into the fake red-sauce join vibe. The staff is great, but I think some of the schtick is very forced, and is really not warranted at a place with these kind of prices. We had the veal, rigatoni, lobster ravioli. All were amazing. I definitely recommend dessert.

Carbone is surely a must-try New York staple. The atmosphere is top notch, the food is good and the allure of not being able to get a reservation is enticing. The only downside - the extremely high price tag that comes with it.

When you're ready to go, add 3 weeks onto that and book your reservation. Before you've even ordered, you'll be treated to an amazing bread basket and a piece of parmigiana cheese. The mozzarella is a good addition to the starters as well. Obviously, as I am sure you are aware, the vodka rigatoni is definitely a must order. I'd suggest splitting this up, as it is quite heavy. Additionally, I went with the veal chop as my main which was good, but not outstanding. The side of truffled corn is also a delicious addition to any meal. 

Great spot for visiting out of towners who want a real New York experience.

TLDR: italian food that lives up to the hype; one michelin star; reservations are a must; would recommend the tortellini al ragu

Made a reservation for two about a week in advance for my sister's 25th birthday. The only time they had available was 10:15pm on a Tuesday. Upon arriving, we were greeted warmly and had our coats checked. Once seated at the table, we were promptly poured water and given ample time (would say a bit too much time) to look at the menu. The waiter informed us that a few of the appetizers were no longer available (calamari marco, scampi alla scampi, and wild boar sausage). He then recommended the tortellini al ragu, spicy rigatoni vodka, and veal marsala and then left to give us more time to decide.

We decided to order two glasses of chianti, the octopus pizzaiolo, tortellini al ragu, and spicy rigatoni vodka. We were first served a complementary bread basket, plate of salami, and pickled cauliflower. The bread basket came with three types of bread--a traditional white bread with sesame seed crust, garlic bread, and grandma bread covered in tomato sauce. I was a little hesitant to try the pickled cauliflower, but actually enjoyed it and thought the sour taste complemented the bread well.

The octopus pizzaiolo came next and was great--served hot, cooked well, and very flavorful, served with caramelized onions and peppers. Next, the pastas arrived. Although everyone usually raves about the spicy rigatoni vodka, my favorite was actually the tortellini al ragu. These were like little ricotta cheese pillows on a bed of hearty ragu. The spicy rigatoni was good as well and had a unique, spicy aftertaste.

Make a reservation in advance and try out this place for a special occasion!

WOW!!!  I've had an apt above Carbone for the past two years and have said hello to Carbone's Doorman since I moved in. Finally went inside and could not believe the incredible meal that we had!!

Bread - awesome
Albert Pinot Noir- awesome
Wild Boar Sausage - awesome
Italian Wedding Soup - awesome
Spicy Rigatoni - OUT OF THE PARK
Gnocchi -  awesome
Cherry Pepper Ribs - OUT OF THE PARK
Veal Parm - OUT OF THE PARK
Lemon Cheese cake - awesome
Triple Chocolate Layer Cake - awesome 
Coffee - awesome

Can't wait to come back!!

The best part about Carbone is that not everyone can just walk in and that right there makes it already worth going because now you have to find a way to get in if you don't book a month in advance! The restaurant is beautiful, floors from one of my favorite movies "The GodFather" when Michael has to kill the police commissioner, very dope! Food is a 10 of 10. Spicy rigatoni, the veal, the ribeye, everything's pretty much amazing! Love Carbone!

I have to say that I am really surprised at how good the other reviews are. I had been dying to try this place so we went for my birthday. We had a lovely table and I really liked the atmosphere but the prices are over the top expensive. Unpretentious Italian-American fare does not warrant the prices nor does it warrant a wine list where the least expensive bottle is $100. I will say that I did enjoy my food (I got the chicken scarp). We shared some appetizers that were delicious (seafood salad and a couple of other things). We found the spaghetti alla gricia and the fettuccine con funghi to be just mediocre. All in all, I'm glad I went since I was dying to go but I don't see any reason to go back. I much prefer Lupa or Maialino to satisfy my Italian restaurant fix.

Spicy Rigatoni deserves all the heart eye emojis out there. Went for my birthday dinner and definitely enjoyed the amazing service and decadent food. As I am vegetarian I stuck with pasta dishes and got plenty of dessert. I would go back just for a plate full of the spicy rigatoni and skip everything else.

A bit of an 'Italian' let  down. The song 'La Amore' was a hit in its day I guess, however the crappy music didn't  make up for the mediocre menu or pseudo Italian fare.  No lobster pasta available, just one choice of meat pasta (ragu) and waiters in velvet suits. The tiramisu seemed manufactured. Nothing special to see here, well, in my opinion.

After reading all the wonderful reviews about this place and making a reservation about a month in advance i didnt know if it would live up to the hype
