I thought i would be going into a very pretencious stuffy restaurant,i was dead wrong,from the second you walk in till the moment you leave they make you feel like family,from the service to the atmosphere to the tile floors which were inspired by the godfather this place gets it
As far as the food goes the portions arent huge but theyre just right,we shared everything,we started with the caesar salad and baked clams,we then had the rigatoni ala vodka and the meatballs[which were delicious]we then had the veal parm and the chicken scarpiello
The things that stood out was the meatballs,the veal parm,the caesar salad for $24 couldve been bigger and the baked clams were very good but i think are better at don pepe in ozone park
What makes this place so good is the total package,the service is the best ive ever had,the table was so comfortable[not on top of anyone]and the atmosphere
I will definitely to be back in about a month [when i can get another reservation] to try some other things on the menu

Excellent Italian American cuisine. Only buy reservation and it's kinda of a wait but well worth it. The decor is beautiful and dimly lit the staff is great and ambiance was wonderful. The go to dish is the meatballs and spicy rigatoni the baked clams are also a must try!!! Pricing can be a little better but not to bad. Other than that it's a really good place to try if you have some extra bucks to spare. Enjoy

Came here for anniversary dinner. Stellar service from start to finish. I love the burgundy suits all the waiters were dressed in. Great ambiance as well with all the old mob movie songs playing. Veal parmigiana was everything and was cooked perfectly. Lovely touch that they serve it to you from a platter! Spicy vodka sauce was incredible as well. If you can grab a reservation take it. Well worth it.
I've been twice now. First time was fantastic...chicken parm, mussels, wine, everything just great. Second time was a disappointment as the chicken parm was undercooked. Unsure if I'll be back

Still love this place! Second visit was even better because I got to try their Nutella tiramisu and it was as good as the rigatoni! Their service is as phenomenal as ever and the complimentary wine refill was much appreciated and noticed. They pay attention to every detail including beautiful monogrammed paper towels in the bathroom and a sleek bag for leftovers as well.

WOW! I had been trying to go to Carbone for years now and finally snagged a reservation for my boyfriends birthday. It was just what I was hoping it'd be from start to finish. Our table wasn't quite ready so we grabbed a drink at the bar, a dirty martini for me and scotch on the rocks for him, both were perfect. Once we sat down, we were given some amazing bread, salami, and cauliflower complimentary. I had obviously done my research inside and out so already knew what I was going to order, but before I could the amazing waiter Ricky read my mind and recited everything I wanted. 

To start, we got a Caesar salad, made table side and prosciutto and mozzarella. Both were so delicious and fresh! 

Next, we got a spicy rigatoni to share and an order of the meatballs. I cannot say enough good things about these dishes, they were the highlight of the meal, and that's saying a lot since I come from an Italian family who knows how to make a perfect meatball. These were moist and flavorful, honestly the best I had ever tasted.

Then, we got a veal parm to split and could only eat a few bites since we were full by the time this came. It was great, not not necessary.

Lastly, since it was my boyfriends birthday we couldn't not order dessert and got the carrot cake. This was good but not great, the cake was a bit dry and the cream cheese frosting is kind of on the side. 

Overall, we went overboard with the ordering and the bill reflected it ($300 for 2 people) but I wouldn't have done it differently. We both had a great meal and night thanks to Carbone!

Place is far from terrible but the hassle of reservations and wild menu prices are a turn off. I guess if you have never had Italian food before you would think its the greatest, but its not. Did I mention the ridiculous pricing? There are many great options all over the NYC. If you want to get an authentic "old school" NYC Italian restaurant experience visit Arthur Ave in the Bronx. Which Carbone seems to have drew inspiration from.

I've been dying to get a reservation here but it's nearly impossible cause it's so popular. Checked on the reservation site multiple times and finally landed one. LFG.

First off, I'm just a huge fan of Major Food Group's restaurants and Carbone is at the top of that list. The restaurant has the same vibe that the group's restaurants all share: awesome traditional feel with a bold but subtle modern twist that makes it unqiuely (Parm, Dirty French, ZZs Clam Bar - all awesome restaurants individually). The restaurant is nice and intimate that at first glance looks like a nice old school trattoria but look closer and the modern paintings and red lighting in the back makes the place cool af.

The food here was incredible. No frills Italian food. Best part is that after you order your meal, they immediately bring out picked cauliflowers, smoked meat (I think it was speck), and a variety of the most excellent bread (my favorite was the one with tomato sauce over it - clearly the sauce was made in house and super fresh).

-Tuna Crudo (Special): Good, light thick sliced raw tuna with some light asian-like dressing on a bowl of ice for nice presentation. 

-Gnocchi Toscana: Gnocchi covered in a butter and mushroom sauce. Though pretty good, this was my least favorite dish we ordered. The gnocchi itself was as soft as pillows and unlike some gnocchis I've had that are a little chewy. The stickler for me was that the sauce was not flavorful and a little bland. I would recommend going for another pasta dish. 

-Veal Parmaginana: Beautiful slab of veal fried to perfection with fresh tomato sauce and mozzarella melted on top. Tender (meat), crispy (breading), fresh (tomatoes and basil), and cheesy (cheese). All the key elements of a Parmaginana done with perfection. Don't forget to eat the meat off the bone (which they gratuitously salt)!

Our server had a dope red blazer on and he was also very attentive and checked up on us regularly asking how our meal was. There was a slight wait of ~20 min between our pasta and veal but the restaurant was packed and not his fault. He continued to check on us while we waited so he clearly knew.

Come try this place. It's A Must Do (AMD).

We waited months to go to Carbonne.  A reservation is not easy to get!  And WOW were we disappointed.  This place is like comic book Italian food.  Where to begin....the menu is basic Italian and quite impressive--especially the prices.  OK but it's New York so we all pay top dollar for amazing dining.  If only the food weren't so lousy.  The openers begin as soon as you order.  The waiters put down bread, a hunk of peccorino cheese, some salami slices and a raw cauliflower salad.  This is the chef's offering to start.  No stand outs here.  The cauliflower salad is pickled in hot red pepper flakes and vinegar and I would say inedible.  The cheese is not special and the salami is so stringy and fatty it's unchewable. 
Our first course were 2 large shrimp made scampi style.  The waiter was sure to ask how many shrimp we wanted to order as they are $24 per shrimp.  The plate was cold, the shrimp were not hot, were clearly made earlier in the day, and were over cooked and dry.  Next we had the Caesar salad made at table side.  This was delicious!  The lettuce was wonderful--crisp and perfect Romaine-- the dressing delicious and the croutons were superb.  Our main course was the famed Veal Parmigiana and the Spaghetti Ala Gricia.  One worse then the next.  Again both came out on cold plates and both were room temperature.  The veal nothing special.  The cheese wasn't melted, the veal was not seasoned well, and given it was not hot it was very unappetizing.  The spaghetti was also room temperature served on a cold plate, the pasta itself was over cooked and it was a tiny portion for the price, that was drenched in a gluey unrecognizable sauce.  Not good.
We passed on deserts to cut our losses.   We had ordered a bottle of Pellgrino water and what I really really hate is when the wait staff decides to open a second bottle of water to pour even before the first bottle is finished to pad the bill.  For the prices here the nerve of them to gouge us with a second bottle of $10 water when we didn't drink the first.
This was so thoroughly disappointing and even offensive with the extra water bottle.  What a missed opportunity for them.  It should be a wonderful, generous place serving piping hot plates of delicious Italian food in excess portions with melted cheese flowing off the plate.

Absolutely excellent and fun and yummy and great atmosphere. 

And absolutely the most overpriced meal of my life. I've had more expensive many, many times. But I never have had more overpriced. There are about 200 places in Brooklyn and on Staten Island that are as good for 20% is the price. 

Enjoy. Once. Then move on.

Food was amazing! The bread they start you off with started the night off right. The spicy rigatoni was extremely tasty. But the best part of the night was the veal Parmesan.  The portion of the Veal was good, def enough for two people. And  It was probably the best I've ever had. Service there was very good. I can not wait to go back!

AMAZING restaurant! Loved the ambiance and LOVED the wait staff! Waiter was incredible but honestly everyone who worked there had a wonderful personality. Immediately felt like family. The food was spectacular. The complimentary bread basket and salami were incredible. The restaurant is a PRO at splitting things and letting you take food home 
Me and my friend shared 
- table side made Cesar salad
- meatballs 
- spicy vodka rigatoni 
- veal parm 
- carrot cake 

Yes, it's pricey. But it was worth every penny. I CANNOT WAIT to go again!

Skip it...I've been there a few times and overall the food is good but not worth the attitude. Making a reservation is extremely trying and time consuming. I had to follow up three times to get an initial reply and then when I did so the reservation time was terrible, even 30 days out. While I originally was going to take the reservation time, I found another restaurant. I've attempted to cancel the reservation several times now - bc they have my credit card number - but I can't get a clear reply indicating it's been cancelled. Perhaps someone will read this review and adjust the way they reply to and treat customers.

I so did not want to write this review but I have to be honest. 
Like most of these reviews will say, everyone who comes here loves the food and ambiance. You are treated like a VIP from the moment you walk in. I have to say, the customer service here is like no other. 
On Saturday night, prime time, the night before the Grammys The four of us sat in the back at a round both that was way too large for us but definitely made us feel extra important. My friend knew someone who knew someone so it is how we managed to get such a coveted  reservation only a week in advance. I will say that the flower arrangements in that section had a really strong odor and reminded me of being in a funeral parlor (not good)!
Our waiter Ricky was nice but not as helpful as we would have liked. When we asked for suggestions (as one person in our party did not eat meat), he would mumble something like I got it don't worry but wouldn't really do anything other than get what we ordered without any sort of help with the menu. He would however chime in when we asked about meat dishes and the popular items. He was super nice just not overly friendly I guess. BIG shout out to Jared, I am assuming he was the busboy (not a waiter because he wasn't wearing the same jacket as everyone else) who would come over and while filling our water and helping bring food to our table, answered a lot of our questions, made awesome suggestions and made us feel like we were part of the family there. Even Eddie, another waiter who would also help our table, was extremely funny and chatty (in a good way). 
Now on to the food:
While most restaurants bring bread and butter to the table, Carbone brings out a basket of bread with the most delicious sauce on top, a plate of salami, a huge chunk of cheese which everyone at the table gets a piece of and pickled cauliflower which was a lot better than I thought it would be. 
For appetizers we shared the Scampi Shrimp and Calamari. Both were delicous but the Calamari was the best as it was cooked just like I like it with a little crunch and spice.  
For the pasta we shared the famous Spicy Rigatoni Vodka and the
Gnochhi Tuscana. The rigatoni blew my mind. It was so tasty and with just the right amount of heat. The Gnocchi had the most delicious truffles on top. 
For our entree we shared the Dover Piccata, Double Lamb Chops
and Veal Parmesan. They will fillet the fish right at your table and the technique is impressive (I certainly can't do that!).The fish was so soft and buttery and literally melted in your mouth. The lamb chops were also very good but at this point I was so full I couldn't finish them. I didnt eat the veal but my b/f said it had way too much breading. 
For dessert the waiter brought out a tray of Rainbow cookies for us to share and we also ordered the Nutella Tiramisu and Carrot Cake. The tiramisu was not impressive and nothing special to it. The carrot cake on the other hand was the winner. The ginger ice cream it was served with was to die for!
All of this food plus about 3 cocktails each made our bill a little over $785 (not including gratuity). I think its a bit on the expensive side but it's the price you pay when a restaurant is so popular I guess. 
Now the part I have been dreading to write:
As we were waiting to pay the bill, a MOUSE ran behind me. I was able to see the movement out of the corner of my eye and I saw the mouse run behind the walls. Since we were at the booth in the back, the mouse ran over the top of the booth and into the back wall. I wanted to freak out but kept my composure. I did not say anything to anyone at the restaurant because one of the people I was with would have made a huge scene and since we were guests of a friend of a friend I did not want to embarrass anyone or make anyone feel bad. I don't think I have ever experienced this before especially at such a popular place and it was a shame that my great food experience was ruined by this moment.

I loved everything about this restaurant.

The service was incredible - so personable. My aunt arrived earlier than I did, and I came into the restaurant with a stranger (who would soon become our amazing server) sitting down in my seat and chatting with her. 

Even the little bites you get at the beginning were amazing, from the fresh mozzarella to the salami and the garlic bread.

Between the two of us, we shared the Clams (there are three varieties, and two of each variety - They were good, but not amazing), the Meatballs (a little undercooked for my taste), the Veal Parm (AHHHmazing. I appreciated that they bring out the bone for you to enjoy) and the Ragu pasta (good, but not amazing).

They also bring out rainbow cookies for you at the end, but we were the fatties who ordered the Tiramisu (a bit too rich for my taste). 

The price tag is steep, but it's been a while since I've walked out of a restaurant so happy. Definitely go - and you can even go for lunch if it's been hard to peg a dinner reservation. We walked in for lunch and every other table was empty.

I was raised Italian American with all of the traditional southern Italian food.  Carbone was amazing, the food and the staff.  I felt like I was in my Grandma's house.  Our waiter took so much time with us and cared about what we liked and did not like.  He helped us decide what we should order and how much.  Our waiter was spot on.  I cannot wait to go back. I could not believe the negative review below by Mady A.  Wow she was fortunate enough to get a reservation as a favor!  I was very confused by her review as it sounds like she had an amazing experience but decided to nit pick.  She seemed to contradict herself.  Also, the fresh flowers made her think she was in a funeral parlor????????  I could not believe how stunning the fresh arrangements were.  How many restaurants go through that trouble and expense.

Everyone should try Carbone at least once.  Carbone, keep doing what your doing.  See you soon.

From the start the music was phenomenal. Anytime I walk into a place and Frank Sinatra is blasting it's a good sign. The waiting area is very tiny so either come right on time or post up to the cozy little bar. The service was great. As for the food, we started with the burrata and meatballs then we got the rigatoni and for the entrée the veal Parm of course! Everything was very good, but I was waiting for one of the dishes to blow me away and that didn't happen. Overall, the ambiance and service was a 5 and the food was a four.

i love everything about this place except for the fact you have to email them to make a reservation and takes forever for them to get back to you. I ordered everything here and everything is delicious service was great the drinks were done to perfection but because of the whole reservation process 4 stars it is again the food is great. I highly recommend trying as much as you can because next time it be a while. The pasta is hands-down one of my favorites in New York City

As most reviews we were treated as vips upon arrival.
We were 4 people celebrating a friends birthday. The service was very friendly and helpful.
Much to my amazement the food was unsatisfactory.
We ordered the clams 4 ways, the fettuccine with truffles and the veal parmigiana 
The clams were bland and tasteless, the truffle fettuccine was just ok and the veal was too salty to eat.
At these prices I expect much better.
Does not compare with I'll Mulino
JE

Five stars for the food , six stars for the service and atmosphere. What a fun spot!!!! Spicy rigatoni totally lived up to my expectations, which were sky high after drooling over it on Instagram for months. The veal parmrsean was also superb, maybe even better when I had the leftovers for lunch today. The experience was definitely worth the price in my opinion.

Unreal food and worth the wait. Yes, it's expensive and packed, but our whole group left happy and will definitely be back again. 

Spicy rigatoni is a must, and I wish we could visit our family in NYC more frequently if only just to eat this dish.

Carbone, you'll always have a special place in my heart. It's tough to book a table here but if you can snag a reservation, it'll be worth your while despite the damage.

I love the interior here, it makes me feel like a dining experience from the early 1900s. Super retro and cool. The servers here are absolutely fabulous. Knowledgeable, accommodating and they make you feel very comfortable.

The complimentary garlic bread and fresh mozzarella are just bananas. The garlic bread is perfectly crispy with this soft layer of cheese on top. The mozzarella is in a small bowl of olive oil and it will feel like you're chewing on heavenly clouds of mozz.

On my most recent visit, started off with the Carpaccio Piemontese. Oh man, white mushrooms, arugula, truffle oil, nuts and the beef. Jesus this was incredible. Savor every bite because this is legendary carpaccio.

For the Macaroni, you can't go wrong with the Spicy Rigatoni Vodka. It's such a classic dish you've had so many times before but with a twist. Al dente done right, just enough heat from the spice. If you're being mindful to not overeat - the portion will not trigger the food coma.

For a Secondi, Veal Parmesan. I've never been to another place that serves it with the bone.. perfectly breaded with a single leaf of crispy basil. I just think the way they do this here is fabulous. It's a slight crispy layer followed by deliciously tender veal. 

If you're still hungry, you can get a side of the meatballs. Mario's Meatballs are so soft as you slice through it, drag it through the olive oil in the pan and then eat it.

If you got all of the above, chances are you'll be quite full. Here's my tip to you. Skip the meatballs and order the carrot cake. It is the best damn carrot cake I've ever had in my life. I've had dreams about it since. And.. I don't even really like carrot cake.

Carbone, until we meet again. Because we absolutely will.

Ok so I guess you don't really come here for anything but "the experience" unless you don't mind spending $67 on veal parmigiana..either way don't come here expecting to dine like you would at Carmines or Tony's DiNapoli. Should everyone come here at least once? Maybe. I don't know. The food was really good and the staff was very pleasant and warm...surprisingly! It's so hard to get a reservation here and A-Listers and socialites are known to frequent this place so I was expecting the staff to be rude, but as soon as we walked in we were treated very nicely and it was totally the opposite of that meatpacking district vibe. 

The restaurant was dark and intimate, with tile floor and an old school appeal. They played 60's music and all of the waiters were in burgundy tuxedo jackets. The waiters graciously offered suggestions on how or what to order and were not pushy and did not use any cunning sales tactics on wine. They were very open and honest. They also included the prices after they mentioned the specials of the evening which we appreciate. 

They start you off with some antipasto. The spicy rigatoni although was delicious it was probably the smallest portion I've ever seen to date at any restaurant. They split it for us on two plates without asking which was nice so we both could try but if there were 10 small rigatoni shells on the plate that was a lot. I think they definitely can make the pasta course a little larger for the price. The veal parm was really good but also probably the most expensive I have seen to date in the city. The meatballs were ok - a little undercooked for me. Really mushy. We also had calamari al marco which was really tasty. 

I would go back but not anytime soon ..and if it's a little over budget for you or you can't get a reservation, trying Sauce in the LES or Parm on the UWS is a similar concept and much cheaper and much easier to get into.

What a disappointment! We had reservations for over one month, and were seated directly next to the kitchen. When we asked for another table, we were told none were available even though two were unoccupied. Even after 2 hours, the tables were not being used.
Our waiter was obnoxious and annoyingly loud. He convinced us to order the fresh mozzarella to share, but the seasoning had no flavor & was bland. The sommelier wasn't any better, and was rude and a know it all. 
 The food was just o.k., nothing great, but very expensive. Our bill was $640 for 4, which we would not have minded if the food and service were excellent- which it was NOT. This is like eating at Olive Garden or a chain restaurant.
Do not waste your time or money dining here. I don't know how the restaurant has stayed open.
Absolutely horrible restaurant. Only a complete fraud would like this place. Waiters were terrible and food was some of the worst Italian I've ever had. Save yourself the money and agony.

A completely different experience the second time around. The service was excellent and all of the food was great. The tortellini al ragu and spicy rigatoni vodka were excellent. The mussels were out of this world and ended up as our favorite dish of the night. Although the high prices are a common complaint, you know that coming in and if the price point is too high, then you may want to pass. I'm glad we gave Carbone a second chance.

Mario Carbone should be ashamed of this restaurant he attaches his name to. He accuses David Chang of bastardizing Italian cuisine. Well, Mario...Before you accuse someone of that, YOU should learn how authentic Italian dishes should be prepared, and if you want to deviate from that tradition, the menu should indicate that, or your staff should make the customer aware of your spin on that tradition. 

Anything prepared "marsala" should be dredged in flour, then sauteed with wine, mushrooms, and onions.  Not at this restaurant. At least the Veal, anyway. This was roast veal. Who decided that roast veal is the same as Veal Marsala? Apparently Mario Carbone does. I guess he missed class that day.

Now, let's backtrack for a moment. When you order a bottle of wine, regardless of the price, (this bottle was $100+) it should be opened in front of you, not shown to you, and then 15 min later the bottle arrives already opened. When I questioned the server I was told, "this is how we do it". Well, Carbone still has quite a bit to learn about serving wine.

If you question the practices of this establishment, odds are you will be asked to leave. Apparently, they don't like patrons that actually know how authentic Italian dishes should be prepared, or what the protocol for opening a bottle of wine is. The sniveling little snarky yet insecure host will summon the bouncer to rudely ask you to leave.  This was my awful experience. DONT EAT HERE!

Incredible scenery, and one of the best old fashions to date.

I went on a Tuesday and the veal parm was dry and the pasta pretty good.

Over priced although a fun experience. 

I most likely wouldn't go back anytime soon.

What an experience! For a few hours we were transported.... this was absolutely the best meal I've ever had. The service was comfortable and polite, the restaurant itself is stunning, my Mai Tai was perfectly dry and strong, but the real star and unsung hero is the FOOD. 
There is a complexity to this seemingly simple food. The cauliflower giardiniera is bracingly vinegary, cleansing your palate but at the same time teasing you with an underlying sweetness and chili pepper burn that is just addictive. The Caesar salad has soft, garlic croutons that have a chew and a heft that just makes the umami bomb of the salad even more scrumptious. The real revelations of the meal for me were the pasta dishes. I'm not one to order pasta at restaurants, but we tried the rigatoni everyone raves about, as well as the angel hair. Stunning. Both were stunning. The rigatoni has a depth of flavor that takes you from a light, soft tomato at the beginning to a warm burn from the combined heat of the chili and temperature, to a lingering salty umami as you get ready for the next bite. The angel hair sang with fresh fresh herbs and toasted garlic with the thinnest whispers of chilis. Two pasta dishes with absolutely different flavors, both outstanding. We finished with the ribeye Diana, which was pleasantly dark and robust with its mushroom sauce. We asked the waiter to choose a wine by the glass for us, having no idea where it would fall between the $18-$35 range and were pleasantly surprised that our fabulous reds were on the lower end at $23. 
It was a truly wonderful experience, and I am so thankful that the executive chef and other partners in this business have had such vision for their art and allow us all to enjoy it. I can't wait to go back!

I've been meaning to get to Carbone for almost 3 years now after seeing the amazing reviews (and photos) of the spicy rigatoni vodka. The reservation process is incredibly difficult so make sure to plan a month in advance.

Upon walking in, the ambiance was delightful. Old school jazz music playing in the background, red curtains everywhere, flowers - even the plates were decorated beautifully. Everything in there just made you feel happy and classy. They bring out pickled cauliflower, some cheese and the doughiest garlic bread with a great red sauce on it to start. We also went with the Octopus Pizzaiolo to start, which had great spices and peppers with it. We also had ordered a bottle of Italian red wine which was great and they never let your glass go empty.

Now for the real deal - the spicy rigatoni vodka. I have very few words to say other than it was the most incredible pasta and alla vodka I've ever eaten in my life. It was spicy. It was cheesy. It was flavorful. It was pure perfection. I ate so slowly because I never wanted to run out. The rest of my party also tried the tortellini ragu and the lobster ravioli and said it was absolutely fantastic. We also tried the infamous carrot cake and blackout cake for dessert, both of which were so delicious. They also had put candles in the desserts for my parents anniversary which was very thoughtful. The servers were very attentive and friendly which was great.

Honestly, the best meal of my life. Prices are steep but it's worth going to at least once.

My friend took me to this place last night for my birthday.  It was INCREDIBLE.  The servers shook our hands and went out of their way to make the whole experience unforgettable.  The food was absolutely stunning.  We had the spicy rigatoni, scallops, mussels, chopped salad and shrimp.  It's not a place I could ever go to often due to the prices but for a once a year endeavor I would highly recommend this place.  The only criticism I have is that I didn't see and female staff members other than the hostesses.  It could have been a fluke, or there might have been women working that night and we just couldn't see them based on where we were sitting.

In my personal opinion, places like this often get a bad rep, because people come here expecting miracles. 

Places like Carbone are meant for you to sit down and leisurely enjoy multiple courses. If you come here, expecting to just spend $30 on a pasta dish, you will leave unsatisfied and perhaps angry at Carbone, but I would say that people who do this have shot themselves in the foot. 

I am definitely not the kind of person to come here and drop hundreds of dollars on a single meal regularly, but I appreciate the existence of a restaurant of this caliber for those who do. 

We ordered the baked clams to start, which comes with three clams and three different flavors (9 clams total). All were delicious and I will leave it up to you to decide which is your favorite when you order, because I highly recommend this dish. 

Next up, we ordered the Spicy Rigatoni Vodka and the Spaghetti alla Gricia, as we just wanted a light lunch. Both pastas were delicious as expected, but not life changing. The Spicy Rigatoni Vodka had a very unique texture, very chewy, but al dente at the same time. This was the best pasta I have ever had. The Spaghetti alla Gricia was nice and simple, with quality ingredients you can taste. 

Although this review isn't raving, we had a very pleasant meal ant Carbone and would return for another light lunch or for an all out dinner on a special occasion.

As if you stepped into a time warp to the days of mobsters. The food is great and the service was perfect! Once you walk in you feel the nostalgia! No walk ins, so make a reservation. As if your in a members only club!

Sorry, but I did not drink the Kool-Aid.

Dined at Carbone last evening with my husband.  Found the ambiance to be more kitschy than classic.....felt like I was in a restaurant in a Disney park....the music, the tuxedoed waiters....meh.   Food was very good, but not outstanding.  Very overpriced for what it is.....$67 for veal parm?  Over-hyped and doesn't live up to the over-the-top glowing reviews.

Loved everything about this place! The vibe, the service and the food. 

Liked: Baked Clams, Spicy Rigatoni Vodka, Whiskey Sour (cocktail), Carrot Cake (dessert) and the starter complimentary bread 
Okay: Homemade Pepperoni, Upside Down Pineapple Cake (dessert)
Disliked: Jumbo Shrimp

We've lived in the Hartford area for years and have never gone to any Carbone's, and it was my 59th birthday so we decided to finally 'get around to it'. Went to the Franklin Ave location. First impression: Exterior was run down stucco. Okay... "Doesn't matter if the food is good"... Went in, had a drink at the bar. Bartender was chatty with the regulars, not a bad thing, but he was a bit foul mouthed... surprising. Hostess came to the bar area and was reading a recent negative restaurant review out loud to the bartender and the regulars. Kinda weird. We moved to the restaurant area, had another drink and ordered dinner. Very disappointed in the quality of the food, especially given the prices. I ordered the gorgonzola salad, which came with way too much dressing... then the Carbone's carbonara... it was average... dry chewy peas, sticky, not flavorful at all. My husband ordered the gnocchi, also average. in the end, the check was $150.00. Wow. Really? 
We had had a comparably priced but incredible Italian meal in DC the week before (Floriana's) for the same price! The food there was so good we didn't even speak while we were eating, because we were so absorbed in the flavors.
Don't know what's going on with Carbone's... maybe we were there on an off night.... but again, a big disappointment.

Definitely worth the hassle of getting a table. 

I had been trying for months and finally managed to get a 6pm slot on Friday.

I'm the waiters we're great, your glass was never empty, always there at the right moment.

The complementary appetiser they bring out is a great start - some meat, Parmesan, breads and picked cauliflower - all really delicious.

Between two of us we shared the meatballs (they're not in the menu but they do make them), the spicy rigatoni and the mushrooms. The rigatoni is a must try, to be fair the meatballs and mushrooms were also amazing. 

For dessert we shared the carrot cake, it looked impressive, it was a little bit dry, not the best carrot cake I've had.

We spent $230 between two, we did have 4 mojitos and a glass of wine between us too. 

So I would definitely say it's on the pricey side but not insanely expensive by slant stretch.

Definitely worth a visit if just for the starter and spicy rigatoni!

The food was amazing. Expensive, but worth it. My only complaint was the size of the cocktails. The martinis were in the medium size glasses vs most quality restaurants that have them in the traditional full size glass.

While I don't think this place quite lives up to it's infamous hype, I still had quite a fine time and decent meal. 

The hits:
-The starter breads were top notch. We were served three kinds: a sliver of bread with 'grandma's' sauce on top, a crisped buttery piece (my favorite) and a third piece with no bells and whistles (still quite good). They were served with cauliflower florets in a tangy vinegar sauce which I also gobbled up. 
-THE SPICY RIGATONI. I kid you not, probably the best pasta I've ever had. It was creamy and delicious, with just the right kick at the end of each bite. The pasta is also homemade which you can definitely taste. I even asked for the recipe, but was unsuccessful. 

The misses:
-We started with the prosciutto and mozzarella platter which was lackluster at best. The lukewarm temperature of the pieces were bizzare and overall I found the prosciutto pretty tasteless and the mozzarella kind of dry. You can probably buy better in the supermarket. 
-The menu had just been updated for spring so we decided to try the seasonal asparagus as a side. Again, while not bad - I found it pretty bland and unremarkable. 

Other things to note:
-For our carne we decided on the Ribeye Diana. I quite enjoyed the meat served with pancetta, rosemary and tomato paste but am not sure it warranted the high price tag compared to other steaks I've had.
-A piece of complementary parmesan was served straight from the wheel after our appetizers. While kind of gimmicky, I am a cheese hound so I loved nibbling on it while waiting for the next course.

All in all, I'm glad I went to see what all the fuss is about but I'm not sure if this is where I will return when I'm expecting to spend $300 + on a dinner for two.

This restaurant is exclusive and incredibly popular. I was delighted to have gotten a reservation at what Harper's Bazaar claims to rival the best Italian in the city. The service was wonderful but the wine list is incredibly overpriced. I was disappointed with my meal.  I ordered the linguini vongole, which was too salty for me.  I did enjoy the Caesar salad, and rigatoni.  Next time I visit New York I might skip this one.

We went to Carbone tonight for an 8:30 reservation. It turned out that we were mistaken; our reservation was for the following Monday, April 2. The male host at the check in told us that the rez was for next Monday. We asked him if there was any way he could take us in tonight. His answer was a firm "no". He did not offer to "see what I can do", did not invite us to have a drink at the bar, simply did not show any manner of hospitality to make guests welcomed. 
We walked over to Lupo and had a sumptuous meal. We were seated immediately, without a reservation, a very nice table I might add, and had a wonderful meal and a delightful service experience.
After our memorable meal at Lupo's, we walked over to Carbone and canceled our reservation for Monday, April 2. We will not be dining at Carbone any time soon, We are regular diners at various Major Food Group restaurants on both coast. It is unfortunate that a check in host can create a negative experience and turn off loyal customers. We are hopeful the Management will take notice and remedy the situation ... believing in second chances ....

Well worth the 1 month wait. I came here with a friend on Monday night at 10 pm and there was not an empty table in the entire place. Food was great service was better. I will definitely be coming back and while this restaurant is not "cheap" it's money well spent on a delicious meal and great dining experience. 

Must get the veal parm and spicy rigatoni!

Probably the best Italian restaurant in NYC food service amazing the Captains especially Sal take great care of you , def get the spicy rigatoni but everything is awesome Major Food Group does it right.

Amazing, highly recommend!  I've been trying for awhile to get a res. for dinner, so was excited when invited here to a girls lunch!  Everything was so fresh and absolutely delicious, including the bread and cheese to start, yumm!  We got the caesar salad & spicy rigatoni both amazing...The meatballs were a bit under-cooked for my liking, but the quality was suburb.  Well worth the experience of dining here!

the food here is delicious and lives up to the hype - i had no trouble getting reservations but i think it's because it was during thanksgiving week and no one was in the city
(my roomie spent nearly a month email/calling to get reservations, and said it wasn't worth her time once she actually ate here)
so i guess if you can get an easy res, it's def worth the visit! 

my friend and i only ordered two dishes as we weren't too hungry

the bread basket and salami that comes out as the free starter are also really filling, the tomato sauce on the bread is yummy but wish it were served warmer

we got the calamari which was supposedly a new item on the app menu - crispy and well seasoned, this dish had a little kick to it in terms of spiciness

we got the famous spicy rigatoni in vodka sauce with noooo regrets. so creamy and the noodles were perfectly cooked
would come back just for the rigatoni, it's not too heavy and hits the spot

cute free dessert bites at the end that came with the check
forgot what they were called

server was very friendly but not too attentive throughout, didn't mind it much 
the ambiance is kind of stuffy in my opinion but for an intimate dinner it was a cute space!

A meal at Carbone isn't just a meal, it's dinner theater. I recently went with my fiancé to celebrate my birthday. The minute we walked in the door we knew we were in for something special.

First off, the restaurant feel like it's right out of Goodfellas. The music, bow tie and jacket-clad waiters, and decor evoked a true old-school Italian joint and made the place feel like it's been around a lot longer than it has been. 

The restaurant was packed and buzzing. We were seated and not long after, brought some cheese, charcuterie and pickled cauliflower...delicious! The service was amazing and our waiter did a great job of leading us through the wine menu and providing recommendations. We ordered a bottle of red, then baked clams, the octopus, spicy rigatoni and the tortellini al ragu. Our favorites was the tortellini...the ricotta was so silky and the sauce was unmatched! We finished it off with banana foster 

All things considered the damage wasn't too bad. They also bring complimentary rainbow cookies at the end. 


Carbone is absolutely worth the visit. It's a great place for a celebratory meal or if you want to impress someone. It's more than just the food, it's an experience....but the food is pretty damn good too.

People complaining that they've "had better Italian in New York" are just not getting it. Carbone is about the experience -- from the kitschy old Italian American decor and servers clad in bow-tied uniforms, to the tableside shows when serving your food -- you come here for the scene as much as the raved about spicy vodka rigatoni. There's even a big red neon sign outside for irony's sake!

Yes, it's expensive and reservations are difficult to come by. Luckily, my party of 3 were able to snag a table on a Friday evening for a birthday celebration without too much hassle (email nicely and say please). The only downside to a packed house from open to close is that they're trying to turn tables quickly, so we felt a bit rushed at the end of our dessert.

That's not to say we didn't enjoy our meal. Dinner started with complimentary antipasti of soppressata, giardiniera, a variety bread basket with the most delicious garlic bread and grandma bread, and wheel of parmigiano reggiano cut tableside. The knowledgeable sommelier delivered us a bottle of 2009 Cupano Brunello (go big or go home?). The crudo specials of the day, sea urchin and scallop, came in small portions but were tasty. The mozzerella served with prosciutto was made fresh to order, warm, creamy, and delicious! Spicy rigatoni seems to be the star here (although I quite honestly wonder if I can easily recreate it at home). We also had the lobster ravioli. The filling tasted like oden (Japanese fishcake) to me, but there surely was no shortage of lobster in the dish. For dessert, we had the tiramisu (lackluster, but the giant ladyfinger sitting on top is homemade!) and the pineapple upside-down cake (whipped vanilla bean mascarpone accompanying it was divine). They serve complimentary rainbow cookies to end your meal, and they'll bring you a bottle of Sambuca to go with your espresso!

TLDR; if frills and "upscale red sauce joint" are not your thing, skip Carbone. For a celebratory dinner where you don't mind throwing down the Benjamins to feel like a mob boss, try your best for a reservation. 

P.S. I love their Richard Ginori dinnerware.

This spot lives up to the hype. The decor is old-school supper club glam all the way, but there's substance behind that style. 

First, try not to fill up on the complimentary bread, salami, fresh-cut chunk of Parmesan or pickled cauliflower (all super tasty) because the Caesar salad--not exactly prepared "tableside"....but prepared nearby, at least--was perfection, the famous spicy vodka rigatoni was exquisite, and the bone-in veal parm ($55) was delish. Their wine list soars into the thousands but we requested a bottle in the $100 range and the guy didn't bat an eyelash of condescension. On the contrary, he recommended a fabulous red. And to cap off the meal, they served complimentary rainbow cookies and a shot of limoncello. Mwah!

Despite the cool, moneyed atmosphere, the service was exceedingly friendly. Our waiter was affable as hell. The only misstep of the evening was when one of the other waiters dropped a megafart while we were paying our bill. Ah well, still a 5/5! 

Tip: to score a res, email them a month in advance.

If you call Carbone anything other than the apotheosis of a perfect dining experience, your soul will promptly exit your body.

I read about forty seven reviews before I dared enter Carbone. The Yelp reviews for Carbone are in the same vein as the infamous Amazon reviews for Haribo sugar-free gummy bears or the Three Wolf Moon T-shirt; while scrolling, you lose yourself in the lore of what people write and begin constructing an alternate universe out of the facts and fiction, neither of which are distinguishable from one another.

The first fact-or-fiction moment begins on the corner of Bleecker Street, where Carbone's effervescent letters cast neon on passersby, the sign acting as either a beacon or a hooded figure leaning from under a shadow to warn that your life will fundamentally shift after you pass through.

The Carbone experience is an experience that happens to you. I purposefully chose "to" as the preposition to follow "experience" because Carbone unfolds and draws you close; the staff flutters about, dishes are served as if delivered by a stork, food likely to be the best food you'll eat in your entire life is waxed lyrical before, during, and after consumption, and an ineffable feeling of ease among all guests settles in as gently as a penumbra.

The staff at Carbone is comprised of human talismans who eddy through the restaurant on panache and conviviality. Ask for the location of the restroom and you'll be escorted to it via Moses separating the sea, or dine on distilled colloquialness from the waiter and you'll feel like old pals.

James Joyce once wrote, "The artist, like the God of creation, remains within or behind or beyond or above his handiwork, invisible, refined out of existence, indifferent, paring his fingernails."

Joyce's quote is the foundation on which I imagine the owners of Carbone: three masters cloaked in velvet burgundy suits hidden behind a Julian Schnabel painting poked with peepholes, observing their patrons marveling at the spicy rigatoni vodka and how they'll never again enjoy vodka sauce because Carbone's is so perfect it could be consumed as soup, tearing up at the sight of a cast iron skillet of meatballs borne by divinity, and gasping at how all future life experiences involving veal parmesan are forever ruined by Carbone's lionized and utterly unmatchable dish.

"'What is life if not the shadow of a fleeting dream?'" says one of the owners, quoting Umberto Eco.

Another owner, swirling the last drops of an orange and cinnamon margarita over ice in a glass that catches the glint in his eye, says, "What is Carbone but the fleeting dream itself?"
Hard to get in...and frustrating too...but the food is supposed to be so amazing and I can say the folks working to help with their reservations are lovely.

At 10:15pm (normally my bed time), the small restaurant was packed and in full swing, with a classly, but personable old school vibe. It was the only time I could get for dinner, and I had made the reservation several weeks in advance. I came with a friend who really wanted to relive  a scene in Master of None, but unfortunately had to bring me along for the scene. 

[Dinner]
I really loved the complimentary parmesan and tomato breads served to us, as well as the pickled cauliflower and salami. Carbone has an extensive wine list, but my friend and I picked a conservative $28/glass Tuscan red. However, the wine made me so excited that by the end of the delicious beef carpaccio appetizer, we had our server bring out a full bottle (he was concerned). 

There was a nice gap between the appetizer where we were able to enjoy more of our wine before our entrees came out. Following the popular lead, we ordered the spicy vodka rigatoni as well as the veal parm. This, along with the appetizers, was more than enough food for two people. I was stuffed by the end and couldn't even order dessert. The meal was nicely finished off with a complimentary Italian colored mini slice of cake at the end. 

[Service]
Servers are dressed to the nines and the mood is vibrant. I really liked that they give you a sip of wine to try if you're indecisive. Everyone is having a good time and you really feel like someone important as you look at the old school bar and other patrons in the restaurant enjoying a good meal at 10:15pm. 

Definitely recommend Carbone for the atmosphere and high-end Italian! Although the 4/5 rating here reflects my own opinion that the menu was not revolutionary (but with staple and very tasty dishes), I can see why this restaurant was full at 10:15pm on a Wednesday!

The other reviews are right about the service, which is impeccable.  However, my husband and I were pretty underwhelmed by the food.  The bread basket was delicious, and the spicy rigatoni vodka was very good, but you don't go out to a place like this for bread and pasta with vodka sauce.  We ordered the lamb chops, which were very good, but they were $105 with hardly any meat attached to them.  Their tortellini al ragu and lobster ravioli were very underwhelming.  I wouldn't recommend ordering either.

The place is really cute and old school, the service was great. I was not impressed by the food, just about every dish was SO SALTY i felt gross the entire night and next morning after this meal. We had the spicy vodka rigatoni, the veal parm and octopus appetizer. My favorite was the octopus but the other 2 dishes were good for a few bites but I couldn't stand how fucking salty this food was, it should be illegal. I feel like I poisoned myself by eating here. Its frustrating bc the food would have been so outstanding if it wasn't so salty. Others in my party had this same feeling about the food being too salty.

Pro tip: unless you are a VIP, your tortellini will be cold, all your food will come out at once, and they will forget to serve you half of the bottle of wine you've already paid for. 

At this price point, I leave this experience feeling bamboozled. At a restaurant of this supposed caliber, I expect to be picking apart particularities of the food at the end of the night. Instead, I find myself wondering if we did something wrong to be treated differently from the VIP tables near us in this small space. 

All of the food was good, some of it great, some of it OK, none of it mind blowing. But they recommended we order way too much food (thankfully we did not need the advice of our waiter on how much to order). I will say that the vodka sauce pasta and the tiramisu were divine! Otherwise, there's better or equally as good versions of these dishes (especially for the price tag) elsewhere in the city. 

But I honestly don't know how to put into words how insulted I feel leaving this dinner ... I was feeling uncomfortable almost all night. And then my blood absolutely boiled when we noticed that half of a $100 bottle of wine we ordered was sitting behind us neglected - and only noticed after we paid our bill. The wait staff apologized but did nothing to assuage the bad taste in our mouths. 

Everyone at my party left disappointed. 

Thank you Carbone, for showing me what it's like to feel unwelcome in your own city. I feel tourist whose been swindled.

Great quality food, ambiance and serving staff. Was here for lunch last week. Veal parm was stellar, (one portion shared by two diners), as was the mackerel crudo, raw oysters, (from Montauk), and chopped salad.
Linguini and clams was respectable and decently sized to share between two people. Aperol spritzers was the drink of choice, and were satisfying and generously portioned. Dessert included carrot cake and cheesecake. Both were delicious. My choice in not giving this place five stars is the price point. It was just not worth $400 we spent on the small amount of food we ordered.

Came here with my girlfriend around 5 pm without reservations on a Sunday night. The host said usually they don't seat people without reservations but we were fortunate enough to get a seat. The server was great and the food was outstanding. We ordered the vodka rigatoni, baked clams, grilled asparagus and the spaghetti. The complimentary starter bread basket is also outstanding. Would definitely come here again and recommend to others.

Elevated Italian....yes, please!!!  My friend organized this dining experience for our party of eight. She emailed the restaurant a month before our desired dining date. I'm assuming most reservations are done this way unless you are a VIP. 

We ordered:
Cesar salad with house made humongous croutons....AMAZING!!
Octopus - grilled to perfection, melts in your mouth, not chewy at all
Lasagna with broccoli rabe-light and does not lay in your tummy like a lead balloon
Meatballs-disappointing, not exactly sure what the chef's recipe is but there appeared to have a good amount of pork which made the texture seem off
Dover sole - did not eat, but everyone at the table raved about it. 
Bread basket - amazing focaccia- soft and delicious 

There was one unfortunate event at dinner. I had a drink spilled on me by one of the waiters. Thank god I ordered a gin cocktail and it didn't stain. Everyone was apologetic and the manager told me they would take care of my dry cleaning bill. Such excellent service was displayed by the entire restaurant team. Bravo!!  I never freak out by any mistake, we are all human. I was very impressed with the entire experience.

As soon as you walk in, you feel like you're in a quintessential New York Italian restaurant. The small crowd is bustling and the the low ceilings, dim lighting, and white table clothes give an intimate and authentic vibe.

The food definitely lived up to my expectations. Honestly, any place that gives complementary bread and butter is already solid in my book. We ordered the truffle ravioli and baked clams which were both heavenly, my mouth waters just reminiscing about the food. The service was also top notch. A must try if you're in NYC!

Definitely in the top ten restaurant experiences of my life. I'm very proud to cross Carbone off my bucket list and throw it into my list of "must returns". 

Everything was perfect about this experience from the Old Fashions during our wait, to the Denzel Washington sighting and obviously, the food. We ate everything: Garlic bread, assorted baked clams, caesar salad, lobster ravioli, spicy rigatoni vodka, full veal parmesan and ended things with a carrot cake.

Cannot wait to return.

Carbone is the answer to a question that you might not have asked - if you craft Italian-American food with the finest ingredients at an almost uncanny level of execution, can you create a true fine dining experience? 

Our meal began inauspiciously - we were led to a table situated almost directly in the entrance to the kitchen. The house haughtily refused our relocation request at first, and we actually endured a bit of snark from one of the captains. Things got testy, but we held our ground and eventually we were moved to a slightly smaller table in the front by the windows. The feinschmecker can be formidable when dinner is on the line.

Once re-seated, we were treated like kings. Most downtown restaurants have bailed on the bread basket, the focaccia with tomato (almost a sfincione) in Carbone''s, is almost worth the price of admission on its own. Along with it, peasant bread and garlic toast which you can use with the bit of salumi, grana and pickled cauliflower.

My wife's glass of a white Friuli was quite good, the rest of us shared a bottle of Ca' Monti Valpolicella ($130). There are many fine vintages if you have some stacks burning a hole in your pocket.

First up was the Posillipo Pan roast - in that pan you will find clams, plump mussels, a couple oysters, and a good bit of sausage. You also get toast to soak up that unctuous sauce (save any leftover peasant bread for that). It's not only delicious, it's a good value. Fried calamari arrived soon after, in a less generous portion. It will stretch your definition of the dish - the sort of beurre blanc with it, is also great and the ratio of tentacles to rings is on point. We then received scallop crudo - instead of the seafood salad we had ordered. Unruffled, the captain left us the crudo on the house, and went off to get the seafood salad. This error resulted in one of the highlights of our meal. Two large scallops had been pounded within an inch of their lives. They did not seem to be entirely raw, but how they had been transformed into such buttery goodness was a mystery. The seafood salad ($45) was also very good, but was one of those dishes you might reproduce on this level yourself.

You'll probably demand the rigatoni in vodka sauce which nearly everyone swoons over. It's now running $32. Yes the pasta has been precisely cooked a few seconds past al dente to a perfect texture. The sauce is creamy, savory with a spicy finish. Yes, it's a very good pasta dish, but it is something you can make at home - or get something similar elsewhere in greater quantity, for  less coin. If you only choose one pasta, have those ethereal tortellini (more like tortelloni) sitting on a smear of delicious ragu. They are perfection and you will not make something this good yourself. Until now the best tortelloni I had in Manhattan were pumpkin, enjoyed many years ago at Grifone. These have replaced Grifone's in memory.

This was not one of those meals where the main courses fail to live up to the starters. Lamb chops are large and prepared to perfection, as were the salsa verde and red pepper jelly that accompanied them. However, you can have their equal at Sparks for less. As recherche as the rigatoni, the veal parmigiana is worth the price. It's a fine rib chop and the bone is worthy of a gnaw. If you've ever wondered what the fuss is about branzino, have it here. Perfectly cooked and just a tad crisp, it's the winner in a strong field.

At this point we were nicely full, just about stuffed. When the desert tray appeared. there was no question of multiple desserts.. Not to worry, a few rainbow cookies appear with the espressos, and the slice of tiramisu we ordered was enormous, and balanced out some of the smaller portions served earlier, In fact, the large homemade ladyfinger on top was not finished.

I might also mention that although they wanted us in early (5:30) they were in no hurry to see us leave, and we pushed them a bit to get out the door at about 8:10, as we had tickets for a concert at 8:30.

Go, it's an experience not simply a meal. The answer to the question is yes.
The bread with cheese and ham is great and also the ribeye diana and lemon cheesecake! The spaghetti does not live up to the reputation I think.

I came here for my birthday recently and we had an overall great meal. This place was pretty hyped up so we were afraid we might get let down, but we left pretty happy. 

The restaurant itself has a super cool old school vibe. We were seated in the front area of the restaurant and started with two glasses of champagne. Our waiter was great and asked us the types of things we liked / wanted and helped us put together a menu for the night (we shared everything as he suggested). We got the tuna crudo to start, followed by two pastas and a side of the meatballs that were on special. The pastas were absolutely amazing as were the meatballs. We weren't super impressed by the tuna crudo though and wouldn't recommend it. It was also very expensive and we didn't feel worth it. Everything else made up for it!

They had a super detailed wine list and helped a lot with picking out what to get.  We were happy with our choices.

Overall this is a nice meal. The place is a bit of a scene and nearly impossible to get a reservation, but if you can get one you will have a solid Italian meal.
Very cool old school Italian flare, family style...the spicy rigatoni is on point. Can't go wrong with any item really, we tried a bunch!

We got the restaurant's go-to: spicy rigatoni vodka and the veal parmesan. 

I really liked the rigatoni but it was definitely not spicy. There wasn't even a hint of spice/heat. The veal was well prepared. 

The mozzarella was amazing. Glad that we got them for free with the bread (that was close to perfect) and also with the moz and prosciutto appetizer. 

You will get two types of servers: one who gives you the menu, answers questions, takes your order, dresses in a nice suit; and the others who will actually serve/wait on you. It was interesting.

Mmmm...YUMMMMM...MMMM 
This is all I can think about when I am thinking about Carbine. From start to finish they just set the tone of excellence. 
Once you are seated you get a bread basket that puts all other bread baskets to shame. They have three types of bread but the only one I really always want is the one topped with red sauce and cheese. Also a plate of pickled cauliflower (which you should not pass on) and some sliced salami! That's just how they start the meal, you haven't even ordered yet! 

If you are into cocktails then you need to make sure you order them here. My favorite cocktail is the Old Fashioned, maybe one of the best I've had in the city. My husband usually ordered the Manhattan, also delicious but my fave is still the O.F. Oh and their wine selection, I mean Italian and red wine right. 

Things you should start off with: Carpaccio Piemontese, Prosciutto & Mozz, and Assorted Baked Clams. The carpaccio is on another level, the Mozz is fresh and they serve it in a cute fashion where they cut it with little scissors in front of you and the baked clams are a must. 

Now if you're read other reviews you'll see that the Spicy Rigatoni Vodka I probably one of the greatest items available on the menu. It just so delicious and wonderful and I wish I could get it by the bucket. And to round out the meal get the Veal Parmesan. I'm not a huge fan of veal (it always seems dry and flavorless), well I was pleasantly and delightfully wrong in my vote no to ordering it. It is/was/is delicious. 

Dessert: Tiramisu, tiramisu, tir...a...misu...Order it. Promise you you'll love every bite. 

Buen Provecho!

All in all, the service, food and ambiance were top tier. That said, it's probably not the best value for your hard-earned cash (we spent $388 for four people including tip). That combined with the fact that it takes 2-4 weeks for a reservation shaved off a star for me. 

I can honestly say that everything we ate was perfect. 

Starters - garlic bread was crispy, chewy and cheesy all at the same time. Pickled cauliflower was so good that we ordered doubles of both of these. They gave everyone a little wedge of Parmesan cheese, picked off a roll. I was honestly savoring it the entire meal, as the plates switched. 

Appetizers - Artichokes were absolutely worth getting. Plump and gorgeous artichokes, slightly boiled, mixed with tasty olive oil, parsley, red pepper flake and anchovy paste. Probably the best artichokes I've ever had. 

Rigatoni with vodka sauce is a must. Noodles are homemade, and it's spicy and delicious. I'd also highly recommend the Branzino. It's $95 but basically about four portions. De-boned in a lemon butter sauce, crispy skin and beautiful texture. It also came with a few different sauces, pepper, Balsamic and a cream sauce on the side.

I get the hype but the portion sizes here were so small! I was barely full from the spicy rigatoni alla vodka. Also, I gotta say that aside from the rigatoni, all the other dishes were pretty forgettable.

Im extremely torn about this restaurant..certain things were good and certain things weren't at all! 


The bread=amazing!
Pasta = absolutely delicious.. i wanted more 
Chicken = i did not like at all! I couldn't even eat my food bc i didnt like the flavor 
Steak = my husband ordered steak and it wasnt cooked looked practically raw. And he didnt enjoy it either wasnt fond of it. 

Unfortunately overpriced for not so great meals..

Located in Greenwich Village and just south of Washington Square Park. Once entering the front doors, I felt like I was taken back in time as of Ol'Blue Eyes - Frank Sinatra was seated there. The staff are dedicated to providing you their undivided attention. Dressed in maroon blazers, crisp white shirts and bow ties they tend to your dining needs. 

You start with salami, bread basket, and pickled cauliflower - not to mention huge chunks of Parmiggiano Reggiano. We then move to appetizers of Caesar salad where all the ingredients are shown to you and then made just to the side before it's returned to your table. Minestrone soup that is again made at your table. 

The entrees were lobster ravioli (which is the best thing I have ever eaten to date), spicy rigatoni, and the softness most flavourful meatballs that Sinatra wouldn't disapprove of. 

The chef is featured on the Netflix show Ugly Delicious. Nothing about this place is ugly but it's 100% delicious. 

Everything is about detail and detail is surely everything your five senses will notice.
I had dinner in a bad Italian restaurant in Pa. the other night that made me home sick for Carbone's. I'm heading there as soon as I get back in town. THE BEST!

After dropping more than $300pp, we won't be coming back. The food was just mediocre and it took forever to even snag a reservation! I don't get the hype. Definitely don't get the porterhouse- dry dry dry. 

The meal started off strong and the it just went downhill. We ordered 3 different pasta dishes and it wasn't that great. I can get better from Parm take out/delivery!!
Amazing!!!!!!! I loved the cheese , the vodka pasta , and the veal parm the best !!!!

I've been dying to get a reservation here and apparently it's tough to get one at a decent time. My boyfriend surprised me last minute with a 6pm reservation on a Monday which he saw was available the night before. I'm assuming someone cancelled. They charge $50 per person if you don't show up. 

Does Carbone live up to the hype? Yes. Absolutely. Just sitting there alone feels cool considering so many notable artists, actors, etc have been there, and have even mentioned it in their work (Drake)

We started with the Calamari and a Caesar salad. I thought the calamari was a little salty but the sauce they put on it is great. It's a little spicy which I love. We got the Caesar salad for like $25 and I thought ..how could you really mess up Caesar salad? But they went the extra mile. They have someone come to your table and prepare the salad with fresh romaine leaves, anchovies (which we asked them not to include), parmesan, dressing, and some olive oil. I might never eat a Caesar salad again because it probably won't ever compare to this one. This is a must. 

For our entree, we ordered the spicy rigatoni and the chicken massimo. The spicy rigatoni lived up to the hype. My boyfriend and I shared one portion but both wished we had ordered our own. The sauce is rich and creamy and the pasta was fresh. The chicken massimo was cooked in balsamic aged 10 years and it was delicious. It comes on bone, which I'm not a huge fan of usually. But I would get this chicken again. The glaze is great. 

Finally we finished with the ginger carrot cake, which also lived up to the hype. The ice cream it comes with is rich and thick; I almost asked for another scoop. The cake was delicious too. I usually hate raisins but the way they were cooked in this cake, it was great. 

Overall, I'm so thankful my boyfriend got this reservation last minute because I'm not sure when I would've gone. If I knew an Italian grandmother, I'd be proud to bring her here.
Carbone is an exceptional dining experience. The decor is great, service is on point and the food is delicious. The wine list is fantastic. Reservations are difficult, but definitely worth the wait.

Went to this restaurant again and was blown away again. 
This time around they served us this amazing bread with the best tasting mozzarela ive ever had and great salami.
Then for main we had the usual suspects (spicy rigatoni vodka, branzino and artichokes) but this time around we also tried the baked clams (1 of the 3 kinds was amazing, the other 2 were just ok), the meat carpaccio lacked a little bit of taste (maybe a lil salt, lemon and olive oil), the spaghetti alla vongole (delicious) the prime rib Diana (to die for)
As for dessert, the tiramisu was ok (im usually not big on tiramisu, so not the best judge), the chocolate cake (with nutella ice cream) was sooo goood, the carrot cake and ginger also really good and even the chocolate ice cream was delicious. 
Service is top notch here and the sommeliers there are the best (that Saint Emilion was perfection). I would go to this restaurant time and time again. I just love it

Great vibe...excellent service and cool decor.  Food is mediocre (at best) with the exception of the Spicy Rigatoni which was great.  Veal Parm (purported to be their specialty) was pretty fair...no better than that at our local pizzeria. The prices are outrageous.  The real interesting thing is "how do they keep the exclusivity" in a city with amazing restaurants while serving food that is mediocre and certainly not even close to worth the prices charged?  Sorry...I realize its "hip" but you might want to "hop" across the street or to another Italian!

We came in a little early, as I didn't want to be late for our reservations and at the same time it was raining. They let us in before they opened and let us sit on the take out chairs by the store before the restaurant opened. As soon as 11:30 hit, there were people there for their reservations. It was nice that we got seated first, however we did have reservations even though it was at 11:45. 

The service is top notch, as expected especially with a one Michelin star, when you get that you're pretty much expected to have a higher level of service. However, there's some places that don't have service and was purely for food, but for this place got it right.

So what did we order? We got an order of the Prosciutto with Mozzarella, an assortment of clams (cooked three ways), the spicy rigatone, and definitely the veal. 

The prosciutto was amazing especially with the mozzarella. I have to say that was a definite top notch and you can definitely taste the difference in comparison to packaged mozzarella. There was no match. Carbone does give a free sample of this, but we couldn't get enough!  The assorted baked clams were great, definitely have favorites, but that's personal preference.

For entrees, the spicy rigatone was alright. I felt like it lacked a little bit of flavor. There wasn't as much spiciness as you would think, and I tasted a bland for me. I don't think it would've been bad for having more of a spiciness to the dish, but hey, that's just personal. The veal was freaking awesome though. I think this is a dish that you have to get if you're here. It was different, and the portion of the dish was pretty big. I think you could feed two on this one dish, but I would definitely recommend at least two dishes and and there could be some leftovers, but for us it was great as far as portion wise. 

Overall, this place has some hype, even though Italian food isn't my forte, the quality here was different than what I could get at home. Expect the service to be stellar, good food, and a great overall experience. I would definitely come back and would recommend this place if you can't get good Italian food from where you're from.

I thought Carbone would be "basic" and overrated. Boy, was I proven wrong. Best Italian food in New York and up there with some of the best Italian food in the world- including everywhere I've dined in Italy. 

The highlights: the "grandma" bread served  at the onset of the meal.

The meatballs that cut like butter and had impeccable texture. The normal portion is $21, but we got 7 for the table and were charged $7 for each additional meatball.

The spicy rigatoni, carrot cake and veal Parmesan completely lived up to the hype. Each of the five people at our table got a half portion of the rigatoni (15pp) and split the veal amongst the five of us. When I come back I am definitely ordering the veal Parmesan just for myself it was that good. 

The broccoli rabe deserves a notable mention as well. 

Some of my friends were unimpressed by the carrot cake but I [have a massive sweet tooth] and tried to restrain myself but couldn't stop reaching for another bite. The tortellini I was unimpressed with and could have done without. 

Carbone is slightly better than lartusi because it's old school Italian and it's old world charm. Out of all the Italian restaurants in Manhattan I'd give Carbone and LArtusi both 9.5/10. LArtusi is just more new school.

The meal was exquisite from start to finish. Our waiter Jared was extremely knowledgeable and charming. However, I did think he was a bit of a sly salesman. His unbeatable knowledge of the menu and his suggestions wooed everyone at the table to want to order things I don't think we would have ordered otherwise. He definitely knew how to "stretch our budget" and "sold the dream" so to speak. I think if we had a different waiter we wouldn't have driven up our bill to over $110 pp.

AMAZING!!!!!

This restaurant lives up to the hype. The food was absolutely delicious! You should get the Cesar salad, the veal parmigiana, the pasta with vodka sauce, the lemon cheesecake, and the prosciutto/mozzarella. We also had the meatballs, which were good. The cheesecake was the only thing I didn't love.

The ambiance was lovely and we couldn't have asked for a better dinner.

Definitely did not live up to the hype.  I dined solo and had read the previous reviews re: recommendations.  I enjoy good food.  I have no problems paying for an amazing experience.  However, that being said, if I ask a waiter for recs re:the quantity I order, I would hope (and expect) that an employee at a reputable restaurant would be honest when asked about portion sizes and recommendations in regards to being a solo diner.  I had already decided to splurge and order the branzino, knowing full well that I'd be over ordering for one person.  However, upon speaking to my waiter, and asking him point blank re:recs for quantity of plates ordered for 1 person,he insisted that ordering an appetizer, pasta dish and the branzino would not be ordering excessively for 1 person. I ordered the carpaccio to start and when the plate came out, it was a large quantity for 1 person.  The couple sitting next to me expressed disbelief that my waiter insisted that the carpaccio, rigatoni and branzino would not be too much for a solo diner.  They were 100% correct.  The waiter clearly had me order way too much to pump up my bill.  It's really unfortunate that a reputable restaurant would allow for subpar wait staff to work there to basically work for their own gain.  It's one thing for a person to order an excessive amount without reserve, but I specifically asked my waiter recommendation re:portions and quantity of items ordered as a solo diner.  At one point in the evening,he asked if I was visiting New York or lived here bc he mentioned that the excess food would not last in a hotel.  I am not a tourist.  This was just more evidence that he tried to inflate my bill bc he thought I was visiting from out of town.  All in all, the branzino was dry/overcooked.  I mentioned this to my waiter, and he recommended that I supplement my dining experience by using one of the 3 sauces they provided to complement the branzino.  If I'm going to pay $95 for a branzino, it should be prepared well enough to stand alone by itself with or without supplemental sauces. As for the carpaccio, it was decent, but def nothing to write home about.  The best part of my meal was the rigatoni.  Take that with a grain of salt since I literally had 1 bite bc I didn't have any other room for more w/the other things ordered.  Although my waiter realized my displeasure re:his dishonesty and false counseling in re:to portions and #of items ordered, it was too little too late. He comped the rigatoni after he saw that I literally had 1 small bite and complained re:quantity ordered.  The diners at the table on my other side commented that they couldn't believe that I ordered the same quantity as they did for their table of 2. We laughed bc they thought that we should've just ordered their meal for the 3 of us rather than me ordering the same quantity as a solo diner as for their table of 2 people.  I went to Carbone to treat myself on my birthday last minute and am dissatisfied by the whole experience. The rigatoni and my old fashioned were the best parts of my meal...and I only had 1 bite of the rigatoni.  I don't believe that I will be going back there.  The one saving grace was the bartender that made my old fashioned.

incredible. This definitely lived up to the hype that it gets. I emailed them exactly one month before to get a table for 5 on a Saturday night. we got stable at 5:45. 

Everything we ate was more and more delicious. It was a classic Italian meal, nothing fancy or new world, but abolsutely incredible. Our waiter Jared was incredible, he did not seem to look down upon us as we all were under 23 at the table, unlike the people next to us who shushed us. He proposed we order for the table: a half order of the spicy rigatoni each, all split the veal part, 5 meatballs, tortellini for the table, and a side of broccoli rabe and potatoes. 

The spicy rigatoni ($15 per half portion) was incredible. the al dente pasta was cooked to perfection and lived up to the hype. The veal parm was also amazing and was enough to feed 5 of us (I hoped it would be at $69). I did not like the tortellini, as there was too much ricotta cheese it was too rich and overwhelming. The meatballs also fell right apart and were DELICIOUS. He gave us 5 meatballs that cost $7 dollars each. I think he oversold us on the sides, he proposed getting some vegetables as we did not have any involved in the meal over doing the ceasar salad. Little did we know each small plate of vegetables would by $18. We also ordered the carrot cake that was good. 

To start they gave us grandma bread with sauce that was AMAZING, some sort of Italian meat also very good, parmesan cheese, and a pickled cauliflower that we ordered 2 more of all on the house. At the end they also gave us rainbow cookies on the house.

We also each ordered 2 drinks at $18. We had martinis, margaritas, and the gin and vanilla drink which were all good. 

Overall, the food was all incredible and I could not stop eating, each thing was better than the other. the only disappointment was the tortellini. The services was also impeccable and Jared attended to everything we needed. The prices are steep, but I think are worth it for the quality of the food and service. The only thing I thought was a little ridiculous was the $18 dollar vegetable sides that were kind of forced on us. The total was $110 each (with tip and tax) for 5. If you are looking for old school Italian and are ok with paying these prices this was an incredible experience.

I really wanted to like this place based on all the great reviews, but I had such a bad experience I will not come back here again...the food is mediocre and the service was HORRIBLE!  I've never wanted a meal to finish as quickly as the one I had at Carbone.  Here it goes...

We were shown to our table at the time of our reservation and everything started going down hill from there.  Our waiter handed us the menus and mumbled what the specials were for the night.
