When it came time to order, he strongly suggested us to order 2 appetizers, 1 pasta, and 1 entree each.  We decided on 1 appetizer (the octopus), the spicy rigatoni, and a fish dish (there are no description on how anything is cooked on the menu, and we asked if there was any cheese on the octopus, and our waiter very SMUGLY answered 'cheese? on octopus? if we had cheese on octopus we wouldn't be in business.....' okay ASSHOLE...how am i suppose to know how the octopus is prepared?) I felt extremely belittled by his response and didn't think it was funny at all, I feel like he needs a lesson on customer service.  The spicy rigatoni was mediocre, nothing too special.  I don't know what the hype is all about, I felt that I could probably get a better pasta dish elsewhere.  The sea bass was dry, nothing too special either.  We ended up getting a dessert because we felt kind of pressured.  The chocolate cake with nutella ice cream was probably the best part of the meal.  After we paid, we asked our waiter what he would suggest us to order if we came back again....and his response was "Like I said, I would order 2 appetizers, 1 pasta, and 1 entrees each"....what a dismissive answer.

My brother convinced my sister and I that Carbone was THE place to go to when it came to celebrating my parents' 40th wedding anniversary a couple of weeks ago. Apparently this restaurant is one of the hardest to get into in NYC, so since my brother secured us a reservation, we just had to see what the hype was all about. 

As soon as my family and I were seated, our Captain (Carbone's sophisticated way of saying waiter) barked at my sister and insisted that she remove her Poland Spring water bottle from the table. Seriously?! Heaven forbid a non-Carbone item touch their oh-so-delicate cotton tablecloth! I didn't hear the Captain when it happened, but my brother filled me in later on after dinner. My sister is the sweetest human being on the planet and seldom gets confrontational, so she moved the bottle to the floor to avoid an argument. 

In terms of the food, yes, it was delicious. Was it as incredible and life-changing as most claim it to be? No. The bread (it tasted like pizza), penne vodka, meatballs, and veal parmesan were solid. The calamari, house and Caesar salads, clams, steak, other pasta dishes, potatoes, etc., were pretty good. We actually had asked the Captain if we could order chicken parm instead of the veal and he said no. We would've had to put that request in 24 hours in advance. If the restaurant has other chicken items on the menu, was it really that difficult to add some breadcrumbs, tomato sauce, and cheese to it? We also noticed a nearby party eating chicken parm, so one would think there'd be leftover ingredients from that preparation..?

When we were wrapping up the entree course, I handed the Captain an empty plate and asked if he would mind taking it from me. He made a face and it took him a few seconds to oblige. I guess he thought he was above that task and wanted a busboy to do it. That exchange irked me. I've dined at plenty of (high-end) restaurants where the owners, managers, and even servers who weren't waiting on my table were more than happy to assist. If they see empty dishes or glasses on tables, they simply act on it. It's instinctual/not a big deal. That's what (fine) dining is all about. There's no room for ego in the restaurant business -- your reputation is on the line. 

Anyway, we received some "free" rainbow cookies as a pre-dessert (not really since we were paying good money to be there) before the chocolate cake with Nutella ice cream and carrot cake came out. I'm not a fan of carrot cake, so I didn't bother trying it, but my family members enjoyed it. I can tell you, though, that chocolate cake was excellent!

On the plus side, I can cross this experience off my bucket list. Regrettably, I'm in no rush to return to this restaurant. I'd much rather go to local places where I can eat tasty food, pay a fraction of the cost of Carbone, and have a better rapport with my waiter/waitress.

Just finished my first dinner at Carbone and the food was a 10/10, the service was 15/10. Our waiter, Jared, was incredible. Jared made the meal that much better, I highly suggest requesting him when making a reservation. He was knowledgeable, passionate, and all around great company. He exemplifies why Carbone is Carbone and why I will be back as soon as I can. Jared recommended a few items that are absolute musts. The meal started with the beets siciliana, the octopus piazzaiolo, and an off menu mozzarella dish that I'm sure Jared will be glad to let you know about if you're good people. Next time around I will definitely be adding the Caesar salad to the mix. For pasta, Jared recommended the spicy rigatoni vodka calling it the "DNA of Carbone" and he was far from wrong, FANTASTIC dish. The highlight of the meal was the veal parmesan which was one of the best dishes I've ever had the opportunity try. Jared will help you with portions based on party size, but this lineup of dishes made for a great night. I'd highly recommend Carbone and can't wait for my next meal there.

We went here for our Anniversary lunch. Jared was also our waiter, and after reading a few negative reviews about service, we were glad we had him. Nice guy, didn't push anything on you. Very friendly and professional. The entire wait staff was also. We did not order drinks. Just couldn't see spending $18.00 on a drink. Ordered the clams, which were delicious, especially the ones with uni on them. He advised a half portion of the spicy rigatoni pasta. I thought it wouldn't be enough but in the end , it was the right decision. There is so much hype about this pasta and while it was very good, it wouldn't be my top choice of pasta. The pasta itself was very good and cooked perfectly. The sauce, more spicy, than I anticipated, was very good and clung nicely to the pasta. We shared the veal parmesan and it was large. Very good and tender. I know it's a red sauce place with emphasis on quality of ingredients. As good as it was, I can't say it's the best meal I ever had. Would I go back...yes if I had the money or if someone paid. But I can get my fix on these dishes at other places, or even when I cook. Albeit, it won't be as good, but maybe I prefer dishes that are more unique that I can't create myself. Kudos to the lemon cheese cake. Although everyone says the carrot cake is the way to go, it was hot out and the lemon cream cheese cake appealed to us. It was delicious and light with a slight tartness of lemon on the top layer. I passed on the rainbow cookies. First off, never my favorite cookie and I just didn't want to loose that delicious taste of lemon that lingered on my tongue. On a side note, they don't give you the focaccia or parmesan cheese during lunch. It's reserved for dinner. Overall, very happy with our meal. We left stuffed, and for my husband, that's a good thing. For the two of us $175.00 no drinks. Pricey, but somehow worth it for special occasions.

After all of the hype around this place, I decided to give it a try for myself. 

It definitely has a old school Italian restaurant feel. Very simple, white table cloths. 

The waiters are so funny, and they seem to sneak up on you when you aren't expecting it (which was also funny)!

We started with the Caesar salad, which they make right in front of you. Wowza! It was sooo good! I had three helpings! We ordered meatballs to share, but they never came out (we mentioned it towards the end of the meal and our waiter played it off like he was saving them, but he definitely forgot). He ended up bringing them as "dessert" but they were completely raw (I guess because he was rushing to make them?) so we didn't eat them.

I ordered the spicy rigatoni (how could you not after all of the reviews) and it definitely lived up to the hype! It was perfectly cooked and had a nice, light heat (from the calabrian chili oil). I would come back just for this dish! You definitely have to get this!!

been here a million times but wanted to write this for all my gluten free sisters and misters out there...Carbone is out of this world amazing. Incredible Italian food, and they are SO accommodating to my Celiac allergy. They always bring me the spicy rigatoni gluten free, tastes and looks exactly the same as everyone else's...someone else was ordering apps and the server brought out a gluten free version of all the apps without even asking! It was so nice. The service is impeccable, food is delicious, what more can I say? This is my favorite Italian spot in New York.

Wow  this place really lives up to the hype. Spicy rigatoni was the bomb wish i had the the whole pot that's how good it was. Place was jumping on a Friday night even up until 11pm ppl was still coming in

We went back when we were in town again and it was as good as I'd remembered! The food is top notch and the service is even better! If you can get reservations, go!! You will be so glad you did! We had langostines, rigatoni, and veal Marsala with fresh corn & truffles. We ended our meal with tiramusi and espresso. Delightful!

I've been here twice and each time I opted to have the same meal: spicy rigatoni and carrot cake. It never disappoints! 

The meal begins with complimentary tomato bread and sopressata. I'd recommend saving room for the pasta and not overdoing it with the bread (I know it's hard). 

Almost everyone I ate with ordered the spicy rigatoni. It really lives up to the hype. The pasta is cooked perfectly and has a nice kick to it. Regardless of how full I feel by the end of the dinner, I make sure I have room for the carrot cake. It's big enough to share with a few friends and is a nice way to top off the meal.

Yeah livin the raw deal, THREE COURSE MEALS
SPAGHETTI, FETTUCINI, AND VEAL.
But still, everything's real in the field
And what you can't have now, leave in your will
But don't knock me for tryin to bury
THE SPICY RIGATONI over in rio dijanery. 

Had the octopus pizzaiolo and stone crab. The lobster ravioli / The spicy rigatoni / And veal Parmesan. All decent (stone crab) to great (spicy rigatoni). 

Service and vibes are on point. 

Dinner for two will cost you a couple hundred bucks.....but is it really all about the benjamins? 

Approved.

Ugh Carbone is everything. Though this restaurant is a 2010s vintage, its retro style is reminiscent of 1930s Little Italy. White table cloths and waiters in suits belie an atmosphere that is vibrant and unique. Sinatra played as we got our bread basket (with some fire tomato bread and garlic bread) and Parmesan cut straight out of the wheel. 

The waiter tried to up-sell us on everything. When we'd ask for a review of two items, he'd just recommend both. And his favorite pasta, meat and fish happened to be the most expensive of each. Once the smoke had cleared, our table was covered with calamari, Caesar a la ZZ, tortellini al ragu, spicy rigatoni vodka (x2 of course), meatballs, and veal parm. We also got a special pasta with squash that tasted like airplane food, but not even LeBron hits a home run every at-bat. Everything else was incredible. Incredible. The spicy rigatoni is obviously the face of the restaurant, but the veal parm is the knees - the bee's knees, that is. Carrot cake for dessert is a must-have, but you're bound to be too full. Would be better as an app.

Waited 4 weeks for reservations and totally worth it! They ask what kind of water you want, we just went for tap but it's warm you have to ask for ice. Bread that comes on the table delicious. 
1st course:Started with artichoke hearts- spicy but delicious and calamari the sauce on top is so tasteful and they were crispy. 
2nd course: split the famous rigatoni vodka and meatballs- both out of this world yummy! 
3rd course- my husband ordered lamp chops (market pricing) lamb chops $110- pricey but lots of meat on it. Only downfall is we couldn't finish because they were sooooo rare! We asked for medium. And we don't like to send food back, so finished 2 out 4. I ordered linguine white clam sauce, delicious but small portion. 
Dessert- complimentary rainbow cookies, the menu wasn't anything special- my husband got pistachio gelato  one scoop $5 
Our server Ricky was great! Great recommendations for wine and food. 
Definitely a place to splurge for special occasions- if you can get a reservation a must try!

It's been a long wait to finally eat at Carbone.  As it turns out, it was well worth the wait.

Just a skim through some of the Yelp reviews will tell you this is a restaurant to be reckoned with, many saying it's the best Italian food they've ever eaten (some say including Italy).  I'm going to hop on board with that.  Carbone has some of the best Italian food you'll find anywhere. My Italian Aunty Connie, who I think is one of the best Italian cooks in the world, would LOVE and approve of this food.

Ricky, our waiter, was such a treat.  When he took our order, he pulled up a chair and sat down, crossed his leg, and started to chat with us about the menu.  That right there, made my day!  I have the picture below to prove it. And that accent - it was quintessential NY mafia accent with all the frills of the NY culture and personality.  100 percent accommodating, no bull, very dramatic. If and when you go, I hope Ricky is there for you.

Appetizer "Grandma" Bread (5/5)  Truly special, this crusty, garlic and butter-laced pillow bread will arrive to your table first.  It's everything garlic bread should be.  You won't be able to talk or concentrate on anything as you eat it, you'll be speechless.  

Fresh Mozzeralla (5/5)  Are you kidding me?  We were told that the mozzarella is made to order?  How can that be?  I should have asked.  But I think what that means is that they do that last step of cheese-making as the order comes in.  It was delicious spread over the bread.

Rigatoni Vodka (5/5)  This is their signature dish.  I can't tell you how much my daughter obsessed over this dish.  "I've waited years for this moment."  Apparently Justin Bieber loves this place and only orders the Rigatoni Vodka.  After tasting it, I can see why. It is one of the best pastas and sauces (possibly THE best) I've ever tasted.  This dish is life-changing and worth the trip to the restaurant all by itself.

Lobster Ravioli (3/5)  This was my dish.  It was way over-salted, and a couple bites in, I realized I had to say something.  So I called Ricky over and he took care of it without batting an eye-lid and without making me feel bad about it.  He apologized and said "let me bring you something you're going to love".  If the dish wasn't over-salted, it would have been a spectacular dish.

Ricotta-filled Tortellini (5/5)  This is what Ricky brought out to replace my salty ravioli.  The ricotta inside the tortellini was plentiful (compared to the usual speck you find in most tortellini).  It was the freshest, creamiest, decadent ricotta - made from sheep's milk.  I could only roll my eyes and shake my head.

Steamed Lobster (5/5)  We were stupid enough to order the lobster in addition to everything else you see here.  We were only two people but we figured we would take some home for my wife who wasn't feeling well.  We ended up taking the lobster to-go.  It never came to the table.  For dinner, we split it up  at the hotel as an appetizer before we went out to dinner.  It was, not surprisingly, cooked perfectly, sweet and delicious.

Carbone is a special restaurant.  You will talk about this restaurant for years after you dine here.  You will put it on your list of best restaurants ever.  I'm in shock to read some of the 3 star reviews here - one in particular that calls into question the portion sizes of the pasta. She wrote that she left hungry after the Rigatoni. I found the  portions very regular and more than enough.  I could have left stuffed with just the bread and the Rigatoni but we chose to indulge big-time as you can see.  Trust the five star reviews.  No hype here.  100% real deal.

I can't say enough good things about Carbone. Anytime I have ever eaten here it has been nothing less than a five-star experience.  Not only is it good amazing, but the service and staff are excellent. Simply put, they do it right.

My boyfriend surprised me here for my birthday dinner and I couldn't have been more ecstatic. I'd been dying to come here forever and FINALLY got to try all the dishes I'd read so much about. The complimentary bread, salami, and pickled cauliflower were a nice way to start the meal. The tomato bread is to die for and my boyfriend loved the vinegary spice of the pickled cauliflower. The restaurant is dark and definitely has that old-school Italian charm.  

For our appetizers, we got the baked clams done three ways (loved the Oreganata and Casino, but I don't remember having sea urchin on the Fantasia ones) and the mozzarella with roasted peppers. They cut the mozzarella in front of you and it was warm, freshly made, and delicious; but maybe needed a little more salt. We split the lobster ravioli (very meaty with a lot of lobster and a mild, buttery cream sauce) and the spicy rigatoni which was out of this WORLD orgasmic and definitely lived up to the hype. Wish both wished we'd had more of that! We also got an order of meatballs which were sausage-y and delicious. Lastly we got the veal Parmesan, which in my opinion was over-hyped and not worth the price. We finished our meal with the carrot cake with ginger ice cream, which was excellent, even though they forgot to light my birthday candle lol. The icing on the cake was Frank Ocean eating across from us #lifecomplete. I will DEFINITELY be back, but when I do, I'm probably just sticking to appetizers, pastas, and carrot cake. Overall an amazing restaurant for any type of celebration or special occasion!

I've been waiting to get into Carbone for quite some time, and am so glad I've finally tried it. It can be challenging to get a reservation that works with your availability, so book in well advance, and know that it's worth the wait! 

Tucked away in Greenwich Village, this mid-century Italian-American joint makes the perfect venue for a special occasion or celebratory meal. The retro ambiance is will take you back to the era of Frank Cinatra with servers dressed in maroon blazers and bow ties. Carbone offers quite possible New York's best Italian-American cuisine and is definitely up there with the quality and service of that in Italy.

Carbone provides guests with a bread basket, salami, cauliflower antipasto and hunk of parmesan cheese to start - all of which are delicious. Grandma's focaccia and the sourdough garlic bread especially stood out to me. 

For appetizers we ordered the Caesar salad and calamari. I'm a Caesar connoisseur and there's is definitely the best I've ever had. They use baby gem lettuce, fresh anchovies, oversize cemolina breadcrumbs, and douse it in their buttery, garlicky dressing. It's a generous serving, suited to share. I wanted to save room for my entree so ended up taking at least half home. As far as the calamari goes, it's crisp without being greasy - think light and tender served with a spicy marinara sauce on the side. 

For our entree, we ordered the spicy rigatoni. The spicy rigatoni vodka lives up to the hype - and that's coming from someone who doesn't typically like vodka sauce. I hate creamy sauces and usually stay away from those of the vodka variety but had to give this one a try due to its famed reputation. Carbone's signature dish is unlike any other vodka sauce I've ever tried - it's not very creamy, the pasta is cooked perfectly al dente and has a slight chili bite to it without being overkill.

If you're like me, and rarely indulge in desert, Carbone is a place worth splurging on. We ordered the coconut cream pie, which is a new dessert addition. It's so full of coconut flavor, it exudes the essence of the warm tropics. It's creamy and sweet enough without being heavy or sugary. We also enjoyed a slice of tiramisu which was rich in a espresso, liquor flavor without being too sweet. The complimentary rainbow cookies served after dinner score extra bonus points in my book as they were my favorite as a little girl.

I love Carbone for what it is - an upscale take on classic, Italian-American cuisine with impeccable service, attention to detail and quality ingredients. Dining here is truly an experience that I recommend saving Carbone for special occasion. It's slightly formal, and almost theatrical - like stepping into the set of a Frank Coppola or Martin Scorsese film. What makes Carbone so memorable is that it's definitely reminiscent of old school, red sauce joints on Arthur Ave or in Dyker Heights - but elevates the whole Italian-American fine dining theme in the most sophisticated, and cultured way present-day New York's ever seen.

Food was really good, some great (like the worth-the-hype spicy rigatoni), but the service really needs an improvement here. I got the vibe that the servers' main goal was to turn tables as quickly as possible. We, a couple dining at 6pm on a Sunday, ordering 2x glasses of wine, 2x appetizers, and 2x pasta dishes, should be given the same respect as any other party. I sensed our waiter's annoyance at the fact that we didn't order any proteins, and that attitude immediately cast a negative cloud over the meal. Luckily the food was very enjoyable, but a true fine dining experience should treat every diner as though they are valued and appreciated. The waitstaff here need to take a clue from the experts at Gramercy Tavern and 4 Charles Prime Rib.

Went here for lunch for my stay at New York. Decided to check this restaurant out because its considered a Michelin star restaurant. A lot of people have been raving about this place. This restaurant has more of a vintage feeling, its not so upscale and luxurious. Upon entering, everything was really fancy such as the table setting and the waiters. I asked our waiter what the most popular dishes were and he replied saying " everything." What a helpful answer seriously. I just wanted to know what dishes people ordered and liked the most. Anyway, we started off with the baked oysters, which were pretty good. I ordered the Ribeye, it was really bland. Didnt come with any sides so all i had was the meat alone. The bread, cheese and ham they brought out was pretty good. My companions all ordered pasta. Out of all the dishes we had, the best was the spicy regatoni. We also tried the truffle corn which is more suitable for people that enjoy eating "
Truffle".

Good restaurant in the village lots of celebrities go there when I was there paul McCartney was sitting by me and Woody Allen would I try this place again? yes I will! Food is the best I tasted in nyc
Bring back Rocco's!! You ruined a quaint neighborhood restaurant, which was very special to us. It was "our" place. Thanks for nothing!!

took me forever to get a reservation here (because i didn't want to eat at 11:15 pm, but thanks), but great when we came. food was delicious and our server was awesome. i actually think he may have been drunk, but he was high-functioning.

Maybe I set my expectations too high. This place didn't amaze me at all considering how long it took me to make a reservation. 

We ordered baked clams, spicy rigatoni, lobster ravioli, and ribeye Diana. 
The only thing we truly enjoyed was the baked clams. Rigatoni and ravioli were too Amarican-- too saucy and salty. They did not taste like Italian food..And ribeye was just really disappointing. My fault to order a steak at an Italian restaurant, but they had it on the menu! 

Overall, I think this place is overrated, but service was excellent though! I recommend other Michelin-starred restaurants such as Marea or Ai Fiori over this.

Good food but not equivalent to cost and POOR service
I have been living in New York since 2004 and my experience at Carbone yesterday made me think it may be time to leave NYC. My reservation was at 5:45 and at 8:35 the floor manager said "I'm sorry to be rude but I need you to leave we have people waiting for this table, I can buy you a drink at the bar if you like". Few facts: If you have been to Carbone you know there is no actual bar and given that we had already shared a $175 bottle of wine and where drinking tea we did not need drinks just 5 more minutes to finish our tea which took 15min to arrive (and contributed to the delay if the floor manager would have checked with the water we also decided after our main course arrived to order more food). Carbone is expensive and we went to eat and splurge so our bill was a bit over $600. I expect that when you are spending that type of money (I consider this an expensive meal) you can be at a restaurant for 2  1/2 hours without being thrown out. I want to add that the other times I went to Carbone this did not happen in fact the same floor manager brought out Zelta glasses and gave me his card but I was there with clients and spending $200o just on wine. Service should be the same regardless of party size and amount being spent. Lastly, the food is good but has never been equivalent to the prices

This is some of the best Italian food I've had in the US. The ambiance is cozy and the staff is great. It's perfect for a small group who wants to share several dishes. 

Recommendations: scallops, spaghetti pomodoro, Caesar salad, calamari, ragu, carrot cake

I ate at the Carbone in Vegas 1 week ago. Amazing, so amazing I've been obsessing over the Caesar salad the entire week. I was so excited that on this mom/Daughter trip my mom would would be able to try it. Tonight I went to a Carbone in NYC pretty late around 10pm, all I wanted was a take out salad for my elderly mom and I to share because how amazing the it was. I was told by the bouncer, mate r' d' and the hostess there was no way  I could get a salad To Go unless I had to have a reservation. I cannot believe how demoralized I felt (Though they were polite). I never leave yelp reviews because most fair/bad service is excusable in some way because hey, everyone has bad days. If I was Beyonce or assistant that just wanted a salad to pick up in a plastic bag I'm sure they would have been more than happy about it.  If any manger reads this, just ask the hostess stand how it went down. I've worked in f&b this is incredibly sad

Simply amazing. I loved the decor, the service, and the food. 

The setting gives me a vague sense of Murtle's apartment in Luhrmann's "The Great Gatsby". It was small yet dramatic in a pleasant way.

We ordered the prosciutto & mozz, vodka sauce rigatoni and lobster ravioli. The melons that accompanied the prosciutto were soft and sweet, almost melted in my mouth. It was a simple and delightful dish that reminded me of summer. 

Vodka sauce is a lot more popular in New York than in LA. This was my first time to try it. I wouldn't imagine it to be this delicious, but it just was. The fact that there was nothing accompanying the rigatoni apart from the sauce made it more outstanding. Now I can't wait to try John & Vinny's vodka fusilli in LA. 

The lobster ravioli was even better. The skin was cooked al dente and went well with the almost springy lobster filling. 

I just wish I was here a little longer so I could try the veal parmesan too. Carbone has become a must-go spot in NYC for me.

Food value to price was great! The interior is a bit old, but the food tasted like a great home cooked Italian meal. I would definitely revisit this place, but its just a bit hard to get a reservation...

Amazing, left wanting more. The service was excellent, upon arriving and confirming our reservation we were seated right away. The food was spectacular, only disappointment was when we had our baked clams they had run out of one of the toppings so we were given two of the sane as oppose to three different kinds of baked clams. 

The entrees were amazing from the spicy rigatoni, to the pork chops with peppers and finally the dessert. Will most definitely be coming back in the future with my parents.

YOU GUYS! WHAT is going ON? This place is good, but YES, it is over rated! AND over priced. C'mon Yelp community...

Tell me why a Caesar salad should EVER be $25?? Do you know the ingredients that go in a Caesar salad? I don't care if the croutons are giant and the lettuce is unusually cut...give me a break. All the appetizers were ridiculously expensive so we did not partake.

Let me start from the beginning: I got duped from all the Yelp reviews and people instagramming the rigatoni and thought this was going to be some other-worldly pasta. So I booked a lunch time rez for me and my friend. (Tip: they have lots of lunch time/off hour slots available, just book a "doctors appointment" during work and go eat there, seriously. Problem solved.)

Ok so I arrive and yes the interior design is kinda funky, kinda vintage, super charming. The hostess is super cute and very sweet and friendly, she seats you and introduces you to your "captain" (AKA waiter. I was honestly confused about this, it's not a nautically themed restaurant, why is my waiter called a captain? Is this an ode to something old-school that's going over my head? If yes, someone LMK.) The waiters are super friendly, there's really great music playing, I was bouncing around to it a little in the booth cuz I was anticipating some taste bud bliss... waiter was nice, came over immediately with their ENORMOUS menu. Note: it's not a robust menu, there aren't that many items on it, it's just size wise and enormously large printed paper menu. The wines were horrendously overpriced. What is WITH New York wines?? The scene here is not impressive. I got the $18 red, and it was too dry upon tasting so he recommended the pinot (which was $21 FOR A GLASS) and it was so weak sauce but I just couldn't be f*cked to send it back again and ask for another one. That glass of wine should've been like 13  at best. I'm FROM California, I go to Napa and Sonoma constantly, ok? I know my wines. I'm not a vintner or sommelier, but I can talk about wine and identify a bad one.

My friend was running late and I knew we both wanted to try the rigatoni, but I was also eyeing the lobster ravioli so I ordered that too. 

They came out quickly after with 2 pieces of really good cheesy bread, 4 pieces of freshly cut mozzarella (they cut it for you at the table with scissors) and it's swimming in olive oily goodness and 4 pieces of salami.

Friend arrived, she balked at the drinks menu (oh forgot to mention that their cocktails were $18 for absolutely no seemingly logical reason other than this place thinks it's way better than it actually is and it just upcharges for everything. Like, this is somewhere that I just saw Kylie Jenner dining in back in July, and we know she's the youngest billionaire, people like that just don't know what normal things normally cost, so they just go to places and think it's fine to pay $18 for a Manhattan. Then, the rest of the world thinks that because Kylie Jenner ate there, that it means it MUST be really good, so then we all go there and leave these inflated Yelp reviews thinking that it tasted good but did it taste good or did you just feel cool that you were eating somewhere Kylie Jenner did and you felt fancy, and you wanted to feel like because you dropped $18 on a Manhattan it was the best Manhattan in Manhattan?

The food arrived very quickly, and you guys, the rigatoni was FINE. Super middle of the road, averagely good, nothing to write home about, not even spicy...didn't think twice about it. Like I didn't even blink. All this "al dente to perfection best thing I ever tasted in the history of my life on this planet" just no. I HONESTLY enjoyed my al arrabiata from Serafina more than the rigatoni here. 

Moving on though, credit given where due: the lobster ravioli was pure heaven. I like that the chef doesn't shy away from the punch-you-in-the-face sourness of the lemon in the sauce for this one, me and my friend seriously wanted to lick the plate clean. I almost asked for more bread to soak up the rest of the sauce.

At the end they offered us dessert and we didn't even bother. THEN they brought us out these two adorable little marzipan Italian flag colored chocolate covered slices of goodness which we both loved. Then we went to La Newyorkina.

In conclusion...you're probably still going to get the rigatoni, cuz fomo and peer pressure, also instagram. I say skip the drinks, just go somewhere before and get normal priced good drinks. Or, I wonder if they let you bring your own bottle and just do a corkage fee if you're dying to drink wine with your meal at this joint. If you're not allergic to shellfish and like lemon white wine creamy sauces for the love of god get the lobster ravioli, appreciate the largeness of the menus, enjoy the music, definitely check out the bathrooms because they're cute and then please write an honest review on Yelp. 
Bon Appetite, Y'all!

I chose to come here for my birthday and I was so glad I did! Its true that it's hard to make reservations here but ny friend used her Amex concierge service to help us do so. The four of us shared the Caesar salad, spicy rigatoni vodka, tortellini al ragu, veal parmigiana, steak with a side of garlic potatoes, carrot cake, and tiramisu. Everything was delicious and we ordered perfectly for the four of us. We didn't have any leftovers but very full yet wanting more of everything we had. I'm not sure what my favorite was between the salad, pasta, potatoes, and complimentary garlic bread, which was so good. The service was great - I think they went out to buy A Sprite when he ordered it because that took a while. I preferred the carrot cake to the tiramisu, which was very strong. We will definitely come back again to try more things.

Delicious food in a cozy, old school setting.

We split several dishes as a party of three, and we enjoyed every dish we had. The whole branzino was extremely well prepared and very flavorful, and every pasta we had was also delicious. It's a bit darkly lit, but it's an intimate setting for a small group, and the service was very attentive. It's a great place for an old-school Italian meal.

I love the complimentary starters - the bread basket was delicious and the cut of cheese and salami were superb. But, I have to warn others that overindulging in these freebies would cost you your appetite for the main courses.

My favorite two dishes were the meatballs (not on the menu, but ask them and they'll have it) and the linguini vongole (seafood pasta). They definitely have one of the best meatballs I've tasted in NYC. A lot of people talk about their spicy vodka rigatoni, but I have to say I'm not a big fan (perhaps, I'm not that into creamy/vodka pasta sauce).

The service was pretty good and they help you split the dishes if you plan to share. With the meatballs and 2 pasta, we were super full and definitely can't consume any of the dessert.

Is this place cool.. yes.  Like a little speak easy back in the day. The waiters are professional and polite but they hype around this place... I just don't get it ... WAY WAY overpriced and i only returned because had some friends from out of town who wanted to try it. They won't go back..after1100.00 check and entrees came out 15 minutes apart and the food was only ok. We grabbed pizza around the corner after we left because the salmon was raw and the rigatoni was cold. This place was all the rage when it first hit the seen but now it's just living off of the Frank Sinatra era ambiance with waiters in custom suit jackets..

There are few places that really make your dining experience magical, and Carbone is without a doubt one of them.  From beginning to end, you'll have a fantastic meal, inimitable service, and a wonderful experience from the time you step into the restaurant to the time you leave.  Notwithstanding the notoriety Carbone has gotten from Drake, from Billions, and from other wildly popular cultural icons, Carbone is truly a legendary institution that can stand on its own. 

This was my second visit to the restaurant, for lunch rather than for dinner, and it was just as impeccable as the first.  The dining space is small and intimate, as you'd expect in the neighborhood, and elicits the classical Italian restaurant aesthetic.  Dark wood, dark red curtains, red brick and tile, and waiters / Captain in tuxedos, you feel transported to a time and place where eating was centered around the pleasure and the experience, not just the exigency of subsistence. As you walk in, you're greeted and brought to your seat by the friendly host/hostess and quickly introduced to your captain, who will serve as your almost encyclopedic knowledge base for the menu.  After rattling off the specials, somewhat of a forgotten art in food service, your choice of water is brought out.  (I have to give a nod to the small, but thoughtful, comment made by our captain that Carbone charges once for a bottle of sparkling water, and you get unlimited bottles throughout your stay; some other, more greedy restaurants, will charge you $9 per bottle, rather than $9 per person). 

The meal starts with an unbelievable appetizer (that didn't survive long enough for a photograph) consisting of salami, burrata (I think), and garlic bread.  The waiter snips the burrata, which is mixed with a dash of olive oil, into fourths, and leaves you to it to build your combination of the ingredients.  It's a delicious start that properly prepares you for the uncomfortable meal that comes next.  

We next moved into the scallop special appetizer, consisting of raw scallops served carpaccio style with fennel and peppers.  The presentation was beautiful, served on an open scallop shell on ice, with a side of lemon to spritz.  Fresh, bright, and light, the scallops had a touch of spice with the citrus backdrop that was perfect for a starter.  The seafood flavor was not too powerful and the dish was a great prelude to the pasta.  We also had the ceasar salad, which is prepared in a bowl visible from your table, which was truly fantastic.  Rarely to you have REAL caesar dressing, which Carbone of course prepared expertly, but the real showstoppers are the croutons.  Thick, toasted, and sliceable garlic bread croutons accompany the salad, and they're truly a delicious wonder to behold.

Of course I had, for the second time, the spicy rigatoni, the dish that truly catapulted Carbone to the forefront of New York fine dining.  Creamy, rich, spicy, and served with the perfect al dente rigatoni, it is imperative for a first time visitor to try a bite.  It truly defines what spicy rigatoni alla vodka is supposed to taste like.  Until you've tried this, you have no baseline understanding of the proper flavor from any restaurant. 

To pair with the pasta, we opted for meatballs at the suggestion of our captain, and a side of the broccoli rabe.  The meatballs were moist and tender, falling apart from the pressure of a fork.  Covered and cheese and topped with a fried(?) basil leaf, the meatballs add a perfect sweet/savory mix to the rigatoni that can be enjoyed with the pasta or on their own.  The broccoli rabe was expertly prepared, but a bit too bitter for my taste, which speaks more to my affinity for broccoli rabe than Carbone's skill at preparing it. 

Lastly, we asked the Captain for wine recommendations to accompany our dishes, and left such a decision up to his judgment.  His choices were on point (or seemingly so for a wine novice like me) and reasonably priced (under $20 each for the glass).  I'd recommend deferring to the wine choices of your captain for wine pairings. 

Carbone is the definition of classical fine dining.  Attention to detail, delicious food, and relatable and attentive service all combine to give you an unforgettable experience.  If you're lucky enough to snag a reservation, be confident it will be the best choice you've made in a long time.

Despite the appearances in pop culture (ie. Suits), Carbone's does deserve its standing as a NYC icon.  The service is always fantastic, the food sublime, and the ambiance cozy and intimate.  It's a classic Italian restaurant with a flawless execution.

Some of my go-to's:
1.  Octopus pizzaiola: Tender octopus in a savory and light tomato, white wine, and garlic pizzailoa sauce.  The octopus was cooked perfectly - incredibly tender and flavorful.
2.  Lobster ravioli:  This was one of my favs.  Al dente pasta with a delicate and savory lobster filling in a cream-based garlic sauce topped with more lobster.  It's decadent yet still feels light.
3.  Veal parmesan: Tender veal with a crispy and light batter covered in burrata and a robust marinara.  This also comes with a huge rib!  
4.  Spicy rigatoni: Delicate and tender rigatoni in a creamy arrabiata sauce.  Very solid
5.  Cherry pepper ribs: 4 gigantic and meaty ribs marinated and roasted so that meat is fall-off-the-bones tender.  Flavorful and juicy.
6.  Grandma bread: Fluffy and dense topped with mozzarella and asiago.  Perfect for getting any drops of the pasta sauces!

There is a reason why this is a legend and the food and service justify it.  Simple and classic are how I would describe the food - BUT with sublime execution.  Worth a visit if you can get a reservation!

Carbone is fire. F with it.. I should have got two spicy Rigatoni instead of the lobster ravioli but that's just how I was feeling that night.. i also would of chose something different for dessert rather than the carrot cake. But that's just me. My friend liked the cake. Veal was top notch. Only thing bad bout Carbone is trying to get a reservation..

WOW. Just wow is all I can say. Me and my friends went to Carbone on September 9th. We ordered carpaccio, spicy rigatoni and corn. Everything was excellent. The service was impeccable & the food was even better. At the end they even give you complimentary rainbow cookies which are so good I haven't stopped thinking about them.

AMAZING AMAZING AMAZING! I have NOTHING negative to say about this restaurant because it was nothing short of AMAZING! The beef carpaccio was unbelievable and the spicy rigatoni pasta will melt in your mouth. You MUST try this pasta because it will exceed your expectations if you are a pasta lover !

We celebrated my wife´s birthday there. It was very hard to get a reservation but we finally did it!! 

I was not disappointed at all. The quality of the food was superb and everything we had was cool to absolute perfection! 

For starters we shared the meatballs and baked clams. Meatballs were big and a little bit undercooked (which for us it was great since overcooked meat is usually very dry). Optimum amount of sauce (basically scuba diving in a red delicious perfectly balanced ocean)
Baked clams were juicy and very tasteful. I´m almost getting horny while I type this. Sometimes these come overcooked and rubbery but these were plain amazing. Even the one that was breaded had a nice crunchy touch but kept all its flavor. 

Then my wife had the Spicy Rigatoni. Yes, I wrote it with capital letters because I heard is one of the most acclaimed pasta dishes in NY. Well. The pasta had the perfect texture. I wonder how the hell they do it. I would like to go there every day and ask for the same dish to see if they can achieve the same texture every damn time!! 

I had the Veal Parmigiana one of their signature dishes. It was delicious and again, well balanced. It was a generous portion even for a beast like me. Note: if you come here and order this plate, YOU MUST EAT THE MEAT OFF THE BONE!!! They deep fry it and makes the leftover meat in the bone a real treat. Most people don´t do that because they would be embarrassed to chew off a bone at a restaurant like this. People, don´t get it wrong. Not doing it would be nothing less than an insult to the chef. If you choose not to do it. Please, save them and send them to ME! 

For dessert (yes, we also had dessert) I had the Nutella Tiramisú and my wife the carrot cake. They were good but not sure if it was that we were already full, but we did not enjoy them that much. Coffee was great! 

All that being said we paid a lot of money. I feel it´s a bit excessive for a restaurant that serves traditional Italian food but I can't argue with the quality of everything we ate. 

The service was good but I feel like it´s not at the level required for a restaurant that charges $69 for a piece of a breaded fried steak with cheese on top. 

I would come back and maybe I will try to choose a wine out of the wine list that is not $190 (if I can find it).

The food was good. A bit pricey. Service could use some work. They brought the wrong drink, and seemed to be a bit rude. The meat balls were under cooked, and cold in the middle. We were given new ones. This is the second time I have been there. The first time was a much better experience.

I had an absolutely wonderful experience here a couple weeks ago! I did dinner, reservations are essentially mandatory. I was seated immediately. They brought out an amazing bread basket, as well as salami and a delicious cauliflower snack. My water glass was never empty and my server was very pleasant. I had the famous rigatoni and it did not disappoint. My meal closed out with a rainbow cookie. I highly recommend!

loved the dinner here! When you first come they give you salami and Parmesan cheese with the most amazing garlic bread and bread with tomato sauce on top. The salami and cheese were so fresh. We started with the burrata/eggplant caponata and baked clams. The burrata was amazing and the eggplant was the perfect combination. However, we didn't enjoy the baked clams. They tasted a little fishy and probably wouldn't get this again. We then got the spicy rigatoni. The pasta was cooked perfectly and the vodka sauce was amazing (not too spicy). We also got the tortellini ragu. The pasta was so thin, which made the tortellini light and fluffy. One of our favorites of the meal was the corn side dish with butter, pecorino cheese and truffles. It was amazing !! The waiters were very nice too. I would definitely come back

Overhyped.  It was clear from the onset that they are just trying to flip a table asap rather than genuinely caring about your experience.  Such a bummer.  Heard very good things about this spot.  However, if you're not a celebrity or some other vip you get treated second class.  Everything was rushed.  It felt like we were a nuisance to them rather than a patron.  Just felt like go go go.  Also, the space isn't big but its not super small either.  The waiters and other staff probably slammed into me 8-10 times either brushing my back or bumping their butts into my shoulder.  It was obnoxious.  
The food itself was very good however I just won't be back due to the service. I don't mind spending money on a good meal but if I'm treated like s*&t then see ya plenty of other Italian joints in the city that will value me as a patron.

I always enjoy my meal at Carbone. After waiting a month for a reservation, it better be worth it - and it always is.

The Veal Parmesan is fried to perfection, tender veal, topped with marinara sauce, mozzarella cheese and fresh basil. Pro tip: eat the remaining meat off the bone - it tastes like bacon! 

The Tortellini Ragu was out of this world. Of course I had their famous Spicy Rigatoni too. Both were amazing, but if I had to pick a favorite, I'd go with the tortellini.

Everything is amazing. Including the service!
If I could give Carbone six stars I would. I highly recommend the baked clams appetizer, and the spicy rigatoni entree. Hard to get a reservation, but so worth it!

I had the pleasure of eating at Carbone for my birthday dinner this year with two of my best friends. Patiently waiting a month before to catch a reservation slot on Reserve, I luckily got tipped off to email them directly and within 15 minutes I was granted an 11pm table by the person on the email chain (thanks so much Jaime!). It was later than I wanted, but I knew I had to take my chances with getting something or I'd loose out entirely.

Upon arrival (15 minutes late on our end.. sorry!) we were seated at our table (it was by the kitchen but not too bad of an area). Our captain Eddie was so kind and our sommelier (who's name was escaping me now, my apologies) helped us pick a $75 Riesling (I know, overpriced, but it was so good).

Then the famous pre meal nibbles came:
-Prosciutto 7/10
-Pickled Cauliflower 8/10
-Grandma Bread I believe it's called? 100/10 It was a rectangle bread stick with this amazing tomato sauce baked on top--Bury me with this stuff it was so damn good and will echo the rest of the food we ordered that evening.

We then ordered:
-Grilled octopus: honestly some of the best that I've ever had, do this instead of the overpriced Cesar salad 
-Spicy Vodka Rigatoni: Just do it. Get two servings and don't share. It's that good. 
-The Infamous $70 Veal Parm: incredible. Did it hurt my wallet and morals paying that much. Yes. Was it worth every penny and certainly filled us up. Absolutely.
-Chicken Marsala: had one bite because we were so full, but this was also a rockstar dish.

Because we were full, we weren't able to get the famous carrot cake or table side banana foster, but Eddie gave us complimentary rainbow cookies with candles and "lemon drops" which was stronggggg haha.

I'm honestly very fortunate that I was able to eat here on my birthday considering I know how difficult it is to get a table here. The food was certainly very good and I'd want to come back but I'm not sure if I'll find such luck again! As a native New Yorker that has eaten at hole in wall Italian restaurants or Sunday dinners with my friend's Italian grandparents with arguably more "authentic" flavors, this was a nice array of food, pricey, but very nice.

After having dined at the Las Vegas location of Carbone twice, we were excited to get reservations at the New York location.  The occasion was a celebration of a good friend's 50th birthday.  Her husband was able to get an 11:15 PM reservation on Saturday, 10/6.  We spent the day chatting with various people who told us that they were so jealous that we had reservations and had us pumped up for the dinner.  Sadly, we were rather disappointed with the experience and wholly prefer the Vegas location.

The good - All of the selections that we were able to get were delicious.  The Caesar salad was as we remembered and croutons were fabulous.  The meatballs were large and delicious in and the marinara was bright and flavorful.  The spicy rigatoni vodka was the star of the show and the veal parmesan was cooked perfectly and very tasty.  Our friends enjoyed watching me gnaw on the bone which was deep friend in parmesan cheese.  Our captain bought the first (and only) round of drinks for the ladies, as well.

The bad - After arriving promptly for our reservation, it took another 30 minutes before we were seated.  We waited at the bar and the ladies ordered drinks but 30 minutes is a long time to wait to be seated in such a small venue.  To his credit, our captain did cover the drinks.  The bread basket, which we had raved about, was missing the infamous tomato foccacia bread, which we had talked up the entire drive from Baltimore to NYC.  Upon greeting us, our captain informed us that the restaurant was also out of the lamp chop and pork chop options on the menu.  Not really a problem, since we had planned to order other mains anyhow.  We ordered the shrimp appetizer along with our Caesar salad.  Perhaps it is because the NYC location is so small but we didn't see the Caesar made tableside as they do in Vegas.  When the salad was served, we were told that the shrimp appetizer was no longer available and the captain brought an order of langoustines as a replacement.  OK, I guess that's nice but we didn't really want them.  We were also charged $80 for these prawns that nobody wanted.  We also received our extra order of croutons for the Caesar as everyone was just finishing their salads.  The meatballs came out next and were delicious and we got a 4th meatball in the order so everyone could have one.  The captain told us he would add the 4th as a complementary item but we were charged for it also.  When the veal parmesan main arrived, we were informed that the potato side that we ordered was unavailable as the chef didn't like the way that the potatoes looked and was not comfortable serving it.  All four of us just assumed that this was an excuse to not tell us that they were out of yet another menu item that we ordered.  I also did not receive the side order of marinara that I ordered to go with the veal.  We did receive complementary sides of mushrooms and squash that sat on the table untouched.  We declined dessert as we were somewhat full and had a long drive back home.  As we finished the meal and paid the check, we also did not get the red, white, and green cookies or the house made limoncello.  We felt rushed to leave the restaurant by the staff.  If we hadn't so enjoyed the company of our good friends at this dinner, this review could easily have been a one star review.  I'm sure that we'll return to Carbone in spite of the missteps in service and lack of menu items available but it will be at the Las Vegas location.

This is actually a hard review to write for me. I have had this place bookmarked since forever and I do not remember why it has been so long. Coming here for lunch it was weird being somewhat of a casual peg trying to find a home in a seemingly over the top place. When the menu boards came out (and I do mean boards as these things would give the sign tossers on the street corners practice for the slightly larger going out of business signs they normally flip around)...where was I, okay... slightly lost on what to get to experience great Italian food for lunch.

I ended up getting a house chopped salad (go figure that one) as my lunch. I loved the endive in it (if I am remembering correctly -- it is not like they tell you what is in it on a menu when staff can provide that answer in real time) and I thought it was generally great. The person sitting next to me, however, had the opposite experience with the same salad. Yes, personal taste is going to run longer here to the finish line than perhaps is the usual.

Yes, I would come back. I would come back for dinner and I would come back at a time when I can sink into the experience further with more time on my hands. I know there is something here and unfortunately I just only saw a glimpse of it for lunch.
What a gem! It takes you to another dimension: intimate, hip, great food and amazing service! Ricky is one of a kind...

We went two Sunday's ago had a reservation at 7 at night. The bread they give you to start is amazing, there is a pizza bread, garlic bread, incredible. Manhattan and tequila soda, both great. Octopus pizzaiolo for an app was tasty. I had the Spicy rigatoni vodka and have been craving it everyday since, so much so my wife tried to recreate it this week for dinner. My wife had the lobster raviolis and loved them. Left feeling full and will be back. Pricey place but good experience.

Ok , I'm first generation Italian AMERICAN and proud. Family members where successful restaurant owners.
Carbone's , Loooooong wait list to get seated Is definitely worth it ? Like anything else in life, good things don't come easy. 
The tortellini  is to Die for!!!!  DIE!!! 
Fresh homemade and filled with a burst of fresh ricotta cheese.  Unbelievable!!!
Veal was so damn good !  Spices texture was perfect! Nothing not to like.
Holy shit, The Tiramisu is without a must!!!
Let's not forget the staff and ambience. Perfecto
Bon appetite

This restaurent is to die for!! I love everything about it. The food is amazing. We had multiple dishes to share and they were all exquisite. The service was impeccable! Our waiter, Eddy, took great care of us making sure we were having a great time. My favorites were: 
Lobster ravioli - amazing!
Spicy rigatoni vodka - I've never had anything like it before. Delicious! 
Whole branzino - so well done, the fish felt like melting in the mouth.

This was the best vodka rigatoni I have ever had. The grandma bread, was unbelievable. The croutons in the salad were unlike any other crouton I have ever had. One of my top 2 favorite places I have been to in NYC. Recommend for a special occasion. Super hard to get a res.
Great from beginning to end.  Excellent complimentary snacks. Great service and energy in the room. Recommend lobster raviolis, rigatoni vodka, meatballs and veal parm. Cheesecake for dessert.

It takes some maneuvering to get a reservation here, but it is worth the effort.  We had the prosciutto with mozz (wayyyy more exciting than it sounds from the description - the mozz is hot and served atop the prosciutto, tableside), Caesar salad, tortellini al ragu, spicy rigatoni vodka, orecchiette al la gricia, Dover piccata, artichoke hearts, and finished with one slice each of the chocolate and the carrot cakes.  Somm made excellent pairing suggestions based on our preferences, the wait staff was flawless in their service - I would definitely return, for the fish alone.  It was better than Robuchon, which was my previous high water mark for Dover sole.

Finally figured out what everyone was raving about. Great food paired with impeccable service = a great night out. Came here for a friend's birthday and was not disappointed. Full disclosure : someone else was picking up the check, so we really got to enjoy. 

First off, your waiter is your best asset. Yes the cute tuxes are adorbs, but the knowledge and reccs off these guys is amazing. Cocktails were nice and strong, impressive wine list and wonderful pairings.

We ate like it was going out of style. Highlights: clams 3 ways (4 of each, perfect for our party of 4) followed by scallops (once again, four of each) perfectly seared and buttery. We also had two pasta dishes, because when in Rome. The surprising winner had to be the EVOO and pepper angel hair pasta. So simple one could overlook it easily. So happy we took our waiter's advice. It. Was. Delish. 

Mains were equally impressive. Dover sole, deboned at the table was Devine. Double
Lamb chop was impressive, some sort of steak, also tasty and to round it off veal. While the meat was wonderful, the fish was the standout for me.

Dessert of espresso, assorted sorbets and what I am sure was some sort of tiramisu were all wonderful, but I was in such a good coma I could not walk. 
Overall, grown up atmosphere, nice and dark inside. Food was excellent, but the knowledgeable staff made it perfect!

Woahhhh dude. This place blew me away.

Sometimes I wonder whether fancy food is actually worth it for me. I ask myself, "do I really like this more than a good burger?" And sometimes I'm not sure.

Well, this place reaffirmed my faith that it's worth dropping big bucks on top-notch food. From start to finish, Carbone nailed it. They serve unpretentious and classic Italian-American food, perfectly executed.

They started us off with an absolutely killer complimentary bread basket. The garlic bread and focaccia in here are to kill for. Please, though, don't eat too much and fill up on this. You will be hungry in the beginning, and it will be hard, but you must resist.

We then had a few apps. I've never had better meatballs, and I've had a ton. Keep some of the garlic bread around for these if you can... it's an unbelievable pairing.

Next it was time for the veal parm, spicy rigatoni, and tortellini. All amazing, spicy rigatoni was probably my favorite. You can tell the pasta is handmade. One of the most perfect "al dente" textures I've experienced.

Finally, we capped it off with carrot cake. How exciting can carrot cake be? Pretty damn exciting. You'll be fighting your dining mates over it.

The crazy good food would have been enough, but we got fantastic service to go along with it. I want to give a special shout out to Jerry, who was a class act from start to finish. Most notably, he was incredibly nice to my Grandma, and boy did she notice. As we walked out, she couldn't stop talking about how Jerry made the experience.

Dare I dish out the superlatives? I think it was the best Italian food experience I've ever had.

I can't even say enough nice things about our dinner at Carbone. It was amazing!!! The ambiance is great, when you enter you feel like you are stepping into an old NYC institution (but it opened in 2013). We arrived about 20 minutes prior to our reservation for dinner, were told it be a few minutes and the hostess directed us to the bar. It's a small bar, no seats, but enough room for a few people to wait at without being in the way of the servers getting drinks for their tables. My husband and I ordered our drinks, and before they were made the hostess said our table was ready, the bartender said he would bring our drinks over. Our server was great! We had a few famous people at the table next to us, so people were stopping over to say hi, and it seemed like our server had met them a few times so they had a nice rapport. But I did not feel forgotten about our server was great, and so was the rest of the wait staff! Anyways onto our meal, we were super hungry and our reservation was hard to get so figured we would do it up for dinner. We got the Lobster Ravioli, Spicy Rigatoni, and the Veal Parm. Our server said he would serve the Lobster Ravioli as a first course and send out the other two together. After we placed our order then came over with our bread service, salami, pickled cauliflower , and chunks of Parmesan Reggiano taken off the wheel. That Grandma bread was so so so good, I almost had to tell them to take it was so I would eat my meal. I liked taking a bite of it with a little chunk of the parm :)Our first course arrived and Wow the Ravioli was melt in your mouth delicious, the tender buttery pieces of lobster were so yummy! The spicy rigatoni and veal parm came next. The veal is one of the best things I have ate in my life, it was perfect! We found the spicy rigatoni to be a little underwhelming, was it cooked to perfection, yes... but it was our least favorite. Maybe I had read too many reviews where people said it was amazing so I was looking for this life changing pasta, haha! It was very good though. We were so full but wanted something sweet at the end of our meal, didn't have room for a piece of cake so our server said the had gelato. So we finished our meal with the coconut gelato, so tasty! We loved our meal so much and felt it was worth the price!! If you can get a reservation definitely take it! So yummy, until we meet again you will be in my food dreams Carbone!

Definitely a classic NY restaurant to try. Very hard to get reservations but we were lucky to get a 9pm reservation during the week and was seated right away when we arrived. Wonderful service and food was great. A bit overpriced for Italian food but nice for special occasion.  We ordered the Caesar salad which was prepared at our table. The baked clams are a must. And we thoroughly enjoyed the spicy rigatoni and veal parm. Will definitely visit again!  :)

After quite some time trying to get a reservation here that wasn't at 2pm on weekday or 11pm on any given evening, I FINALLY managed to snag a table for 2 on a Saturday afternoon for lunch! 

We were seating promptly upon arriving, clearly they have their reservation system down and there is no messing with it. (Learned my lesson the hard way, thinking I could walk in right when they opened one day - HA!) The restaurant really is quite small inside, which explains why there are so few reservations available. 

After perusing the comically large menus, pretending I didn't already know exactly what I wanted to have, we ordered 2 glasses of Nero D'avola (Yum!) and enjoyed complimentary the freshest mozz (which is cut with a scissor right in front of you!), salami and buttery melt-in-your mouth garlic bread.

After our amuse-bouche, we started with an order or Mario's meatballs. Wow, they were big balls and they were really tasty and flavorful. They're cooked on the medium rare side which you definitely don't see often for meatballs! 

For entrée we shared the Chicken Scarpariello and the reason I came first and foremost, the spicy rigatoni vodka. Everything was as good as I built it up in my head to be, and the chicken was the most buttery, smooth chicken I think I've ever had. I wish I knew how to cook chicken like that! The spicy rigatoni vodka was creamy, cheesy, deliciousness with a kick of spice over the perfect al dente cooked rigatoni. 

After watching the table next to us devour the Nutella tiramisu, I really considered it but really just wanted a bite of theirs - not the huge piece that it was! Lucky for me, I still got my sweet tooth fix with my rainbow cookie they give to everyone with the bill. 

I definitely want to return, would love to get a reservation for a table for 4 during normal dinner hours! I was told the Cesar salad is a must, just hard to stomach the price of leaves and croutons at that price! 

Also - service was impeccable. Everyone was on their a-game, very helpful wait staff all around.

You're somewhere else the moment you step through the door. It's an impressive restaurant, but it's an equally impressive show. Quaint tunes, old-fashioned post-war decor. Waiters are outfitted with maroon tuxedos and polished words. The menus are three feet wide. It's almost gleefully excessive; it's just right. 

Service is friendly, helpful, accommodating. Happy - yes that's right, with a smile, too. 
Food is amazing. Classic red sauce Italian. 

Buffalo mozzarella and prosciutto. Definitely to share. Mozzarella is fresh and milky, paired with complex yet delicate slices of prosciutto. 

Wedding soup. Intensely flavorful. Finished the soup and just wanted a second bowl, and a third, and a fourth.. and I'll just take it all, thank you. 

Lobster ravioli. Every ingredient has its role. Nothing was unnecessary. Infinite depth, rich soul. 

Just indulge.

A small but nice decorated restaurant.  I was looking forward to trying it and nothing let me down!! The ambiance and service are both great, but what I care about the most is food.  The food here totally worth the money! The spicy rigatoni is phenomenal!

Truly truly dreadful food.
This is as American as Italian food gets. Overpriced for very poor food. If you like authentic food, and not just atmosphere then please do not come here.

The waiter rolled his eyes when I told him about my nut allergy and my grandfather found a hair in his appetizer...
Best,
Schwarzy

I've been wanting to eat here since my last trip to NYC 3 years ago when I couldn't get a reservation. I finally got a reservation this trip, and I now see why it's so hard to get in here. 
I'm not even exaggerating when I say the spicy vodka rigatoni is the best pasta I've ever had. The lobster ravioli was also delicious & loaded with lobster. Even the Caesar salad was amazing. 
Service was outstanding,, our waiter was super friendly and gave great suggestions. I loved the whole atmosphere and the Frank Sinatra music in the background. Wonderful dining experience, I wish I lived closer.

Was very excited to finally get to Carbone after a month of waiting. Had high expectations after reading many good reviews.
The restaurant had a good atmosphere, was decorated with fresh flowers and had an old world feel. We ordered mozzarella prosciutto, baked clams as appetizer, the famous spicy regatoni , lobster ravioli and veal parmigiana. Everything was delicious especially the lobster ravioli. The carrot cake was average at best. 
The acoustics of the room was disappointing. One table of 4 guests was exceedingly loud and noticeable. Management did not make any attempt to suggest that they consider those around them- very disappointing and infuriating!
What could have been a memorable dining experience was minimized by the noise pollution.
Our waiter was robotic, not providing warm and attentive service. You would expect that after tolerating the stressful and ridiculous reservation process, that once your dining date arrived, you would be treated warmly.

The bread basket is delicious. I really like the complimentary appetizers. Everything was delicious but nothing was the best I ever had. Very nice service, Meatballs above average. Veal Parm above average. Spicy Rigatoni, you want the best go to John and Vinny's in Los Angeles. I was expecting to be blown away. I was not. Very good wine service.
What a place. Excellent food, beautiful fun atmosphere, and great service. The price is the cherry on top. Well done!!

This is probably my favorite restaurant in Las Vegas.  The food is outstanding and the waitstaff is attentive and very knowledgeable.   We let our waiter pick out our dinner and wine, and he did an amazing job.   Don't miss the beet appetizer and the spicy rigatoni.  Delish!

Getting a reservation can be quite difficult. Would suggest booking at least a month in advance because otherwise you will be stuck with a reservation at an odd time. 

I had the lobster ravioli and my friend had the spicy rigatoni vodka dish. We liked the each others' dish so we kinda switched meals halfway through! I liked the chewiness of the rigatoni; it was cooked perfectly. My friend liked the lobster bits of the ravioli. 

Overall, it was a great experience but was very pricey.

Carbone has exceptional food and ambiance! Wide variety of free appetizers that included two types of bread and pickled cauliflower. We ordered the meatballs as a starter and were very surprised by its deep flavors and soft texture. My boyfriend ordered spicy rigatoni and I ordered the lobster ravioli. Both were outstanding. By this point we were stuffed but wanted to try a dessert so we ordered the Nutella tiramisu, which was delicious, particularly the lady fingers. 

The décor had an old world vibe which was accompanied by the waiters' attire and the midcentury jazz music. Great option for date night.

We were able to get 11pm reservations but put ourselves on a waitlist for earlier seating and voila, they called and could take us much earlier. Much appreciated.

A pretty perfect meal. Delicious breads, pickled cauliflower and cheese for starters. We shared the lobster ravioli, spicy rigatoni, and veal parmigiana, which were all fabulous. But my star of the evening was the tiramisu. It was without a doubt the most delicious tiramisu I have ever had in my life, and different from any I've ever tasted. I don't think I could order tiramisu anywhere else for the rest of my life because it couldn't possibly measure up to Carbone's.

Carbone is one of those mystical restaurants that always seems to be booked - but fear not, for persistence will get you a table, though a month down the line.

I took my girlfriend here for her birthday. The meal started off with a delicious bread and fresh mozzarella. Then we ordered the famed spicy rigatoni pasta dish and the meatballs. After, we shared the veal, and finished off with carrot cake. 

I would say each of those dishes resulted in extreme fullness, but luckily, the restaurant is very accommodating about taking food home. Given the journey it took to snag the reservation, we had to make sure to try all of the greatest hits.

I want to come back...

Amazing Italian food. Even better service and staff. Thanks to Ricky!

Just wish we can land another dinner reservation to order the other antipasti, macaroni, and carni we didn't get to try.

I love Italian food and think this is decent restaurant, food-wise. Honestly the food tastes like most other Italian restaurants I have been to in NY and NJ. 

It is a small restaurant and on the night I went, they had put in an extra table of 8 so it was tight. One of my dinner guests had to sit in a quite tight corner. 

Prices are high for what you get-- for example one single large shrimp costs $24. Most appetizers ranged from $25-35, most entrees were $40-70. Linguine Vongole has overcooked rubbery clams. I'm not sure why but eating the Linguine Vongole and the Shrimp made me feel very very sick to my stomach for hours after. (Not sure if they were old because it was a Sunday night?)

I think there are better Italian restaurants but here you pay for the atmosphere of old school Italian and New York (Frank Sinatra etc) music, and male waiters with burgundy suits and big bow ties.

Carbone is a true throwback to the classic red sauce joint, whose ranks seem to keep thinning in the city, particularly beyond the tourist trap variety. The scene is cozy, and stays true to form with few frills. It makes for an intimate and relaxing time free of pretension. In keeping with the theme, the menu is chock full of those old school classics. Enjoyment of the place really comes down to your willingness to drop serious dollars for the classics generally obtainable at a fraction of the price. Don't expect a modern scene, cocktail mixologists, tweezered garnish, or 'a different take' on Veal Parmesan, despite the lofty prices (conspicuously missing online). The cuisine is executed perfectly and certainly does befit Carbone's one Michelin star. No doubt it's a fun time.

Atmosphere
-Old school, no frills red sauce joint sort of feeling.
-Tighter space with most tables in relatively close proximity, bar area has ~ 5 seats but again, rather tight.
-Dress was very flexible, patrons ranged from casual in jeans to dressed up - anything goes.

Food
In throwback fashion, an oversized menu presents each dish with little fanfare or description. Not that this presents any issue, as most dishes need no introduction. For two, our waiter suggested getting an antipasti, two pastas and a meat option. Would echo his recommendation. We enjoyed:

- Eggplant Stuffed Burrata ($32 - special): Very tasty, eggplant is not something we see paired with burrata everyday.
- Tortellini al Ragu ($34): Decadent and creamy, the pasta and ragu just melts in the mouth. Recommend.
- Spicy Rigatoni Vodka ($32): Seemingly a very popular item. Tasty, with lingering finish to the heat; pasta was al dente.
- Veal Parmesan ($69): Presented and portioned tableside, bone-in. Best veal parm ever! Breading was present but not overdone. Succulent, tender and moist veal. Highly recommend!
- Broccoli Rabe ($18): Overly bitter, even for rabe, which the added heat just amplified. Could use some further balance, wouldn't reorder and certainly not worth cost.
- Carrot Cake ($15): Like your mom would make, though presented with more flair. In other words, tasty and comforting. Liked that it wasn't doused in icing.

Overall, everything (except the broccoli rabe) was very flavorful, retaining the comfiness of the original, but elevating it with precision in execution.

Beverage
Cocktail menu straight out of Mad Men, replete with the 'Unforgettables' (Gibson, Manhattan, Mai Tai, etc.). We began with the very enjoyable Whiskey Sour (Scotch, Grapefruit, Honey - $18). 

Carbone's wine list is a treasure trove of Italian greats. I had to specifically request it, not sure why. Would say most of the bottles are in the $200+ range, with the average being higher, but there are certainly moderately priced options peppered throughout. Many selections from top Piedmont and Tuscan producers; though as typical in Italian wine, in plenty of cases you are paying more for the name than vintage. With our meal, we very much enjoyed the 2001 Pio Cesare 'il Bricco' Barbaresco ($325).

Service
-Friendly and get the job done, but nothing more or less.
-One wine glass we got had old lipstick imprint on it, which was kind of off putting and something that should have been caught. Took a while to get this corrected.

This place did not disappoint and met all expectations! The ambiance, service and food is on point. Being full Italian, I'm wary of all Italian food and can be a tough critic! My sister and I started with the meatballs which are heavenly. She then got the rigatoni and I got the tortellini, both were superb!! The complimentary mozzarella that is made in house is also to die for. Also loved the bite size desserts at the end that were complimentary! Can't wait to go back next time I'm visiting NYC!

My review of Carbone would have to be like Action Bronson's of some other Italian joint. It is out of this world. The ambiance, the food, the music, the service .. it all took me to another world.

It's a cozy scene with reservations that are quite difficult, but well worth every last morsel you'll take home because you definitely decided to order with your eyes first.

From the delicious burrata appetizer and amazing bread and cheese to start, you then head to the grand carni and macaroni.

The rigatoni is magical. Spicy. Vodka. Goodness. Just go have it. It is an orgasm as you take each bite. Definitely share some with your company and order either 1.5 or 2 sizes so you can take some home as well.

Also the holy veal parmagiannooo. Wow, quantity and quality both fit this plate superbly. Each bite of the veal melts in your mouth.

All in all, one of my favorite locations and experiences. Low key, delicious, and a tiny bar with drinks galore to boot. Grazie ragazzi Carbone!
Obviously the greatest spicy rigatoni you'll find in the city. Very good and uniquely done baked clams as well. Impeccable service. Great atmosphere! Will be returning soon!

This place is really good.  Service is excellent, atmosphere is great -- both 5/5.  Food is very good -- 3.5 or 4 out of 5.  Not spectacular, and there is definitely better Italian-American food in NYC.  One dish (linguine with clams) was almost inedibly salty. Everything else was really tasty.  It's all a little overpriced for what they're offering.  The real gem here is the service, which is wonderful.

After finally getting a reservation (note: you can do this by emailing the restaurant at exactly 9am a month before you want to go), I was excited to finally try the spicy rigatoni vodka. It was good (unique combo of creamy, cheesy, sweet and spicy) but perhaps not worth $32. With the meal, complimentary yummy tomato bread was provided as an appetizer and delicious rainbow cookies for dessert. 

4 stars for the cool old school ambience, good food. Probably more of a one or two time experience due to the ROI.

Wow amazing food and service. Worth the wait getting in. Spicy Rigatoni was out of this world. Also had the lobster ravioli topped with fresh lobster. Insane! Staff was very pleasant and service perfect. We got there half hour early and they took us right in.
Outstanding. Everything we were told it would be and more! The Rigatoni was out of control and the wine list was perfection. So happy!
A wonderful experience all around. Food, service,  and atmosphere were outstanding. It was the perfect place for celebrating our 25th anniversary. Highly recommend.

Exactly what you want out of NYC dining. Hard to get a reservation, 5 star service, exceptional wines in a romantic sceney space. Before you are even given a menu, the waitstaff has presented you with a basket of three different made from heaven breads and a freshly cut piece of parmesan out of a wheel they carry to your table. 

Must Order: a (few) full-size spicy rigatonis (and then a few more), Off menu meatballs

Pass on: The veal parmesan & the tortellini.  Don't get me wrong, the tortellinis were perfect, but they just couldn't compete with the rigatoni.
