Have to try once: I can't say I would order it again, because there are too many other things on the menu to try, but the salmon had to have been the best I've ever had.  So soft and buttery and perfectly cooked medium rare, finished with a flavorful oregano​ sauce.

The Spicy Rigatoni is all it claims to be and more. The Steak Diana was also delicious. The fresh mozzarella and prosciutto is a must order. The bread basket and fresh chunk of parmigiana that is complimentary are also rockstars. Cannot say there was anything I didn't love and rant about after leaving. Make a reservation a month in advance and be ready to spend some money (~$300 before wine) on possibly the best meal of life.
Great food, amazing service, and romantic atmosphere. Would recommend sharing meals so that you can try a little bit of everything. Leave room for desert!

Wow! Loved loved loved this place. Excellent food 
Great wine selection and phenomenal service. Spicy rigatoni was the best. The bread was so yummy it was served with a piece of Parmesan cheese. If you are in NY this place is a must.

TL;DR: Pros- several complimentary things to start, and complimentary dessert
Great ambience
Cons: Average pasta
Restaurant smells unpleasant
Brisk service

Carbone is probably one of the most hyped Italian restaurants in New York, and one of the hardest to get a reservation at. After keeping an eye out for reservations for some time, I finally managed to score one for a weeknight about 30 days out. 
We came as a party of two on a Wednesday night at 6pm. A man was standing in the foyer, and opened the door for us when we came in, and bid us have a good meal. When we entered the restaurant, the two girls at the desk greeted us, and took our coats, giving us a checking number. The interior of the restaurant was traditional old New York, reminiscent of a dining scene in Mad Men. However, as soon as we stepped inside, I was assaulted by a pungent odor that I can only describe as smelling like    someone had been doing intense exercise at the gym. 
We were shown to our table, which was in a dimly lit corner. They played Frank Sinatra all night, and the restaurant gave off a New York gangster vibe. After being brought copies of the menu, we ordered quickly, and were brought several complimentary things to start, including cauliflower in spicy olive oil, a bread basket with three different kinds of bread, salami, and a chunk of parmigiano reggiano each. The cheese, being rolled in a cheese wheel, was being done so in the midst of the restaurant, and probably was what accounted for the bad smell. Several of the breads were super soft and pillowy, and were great to eat. The cauliflower and cheese were great as well. 
Our appetizers were served quickly after the free stuff - we had the meatballs, and artichoke hearts. My husband and I both agreed the meatballs were some of the best we had. The artichoke hearts in olive oil were okay, nothing special. We had a few things left on our plates but looked like we were done eating, when one of the staff came over and asked if they could clear the table. Thinking they were only going to clear the empty plates, we agreed, but they even cleared the plates that still had food on them, like the cauliflower and artichokes - I was actually quite irritated about this as I was still working through them. 
After about 20 minutes, our pastas were served. They were both on large plates and were ample servings. 
I'd seen a ton of pictures of the spicy vodka rigatoni before, with most reviewers raving on about this as a "must order dish". However, I thought the pasta was only okay - it was good, not terrible, but if someone were coming here for the first time, I wouldn't recommend this as the must order dish. The vodka sauce was creamy, a little spicy, and tasty, but the pasta itself was soft and not al dente. If I had to make a comparison, I would say it tasted like the pasta from Parm. 
My husband's lobster ravioli was similar in terms of taste- good, but nothing special, and not worthy of a recommendation. I liked the creamy and buttery sauce it came in though. 
After our savory courses, we sat at the table unattended for a little bit, until someone finally came to clear away our plates. Then a few minutes after that, a man came around with a giant tray containing four cakes, for a complimentary dessert. Some of the options were carrot cake, New York cheesecake, and a Nutella tiramisu. 
We decided on the tiramisu, which was served quickly after. The serving was giant, and it was topped with a soft, sponge-like cake. Again, it was not bad, but not a dessert to rave about. After dessert, we got the bill and left, and the man who'd been in the foyer before again opened the door for us and bid us goodnight. 
All in all, I would recommend dining at Carbone more for the experience, rather than the food. You will get a glimpse of old-school New York and definitely not leave hungry.

A holiday lunch here is a fantastic way to impress out-of-towners. Old timey New York vibes, jazzy music, the sun streaming in (no squinting necessary as during their super dim dinner service), classy people. Our waiter was slightly awkward but overall was satisfied with his attentiveness and recommendations. 

Start with an impressive complimentary bread basket with the most aromatic buttery garlic bread, salami, and 30-sec mozzarella swimming in olive oil. But save some room for the other stuff. I recommend starting with something light like the caesar salad (5/5) which is as excellent as caesar salad can get, with optional anchovies on the side. Then you have room to try a few pastas - you have to get the spicy rigatoni vodka (5/5) which is at once creamy and tangy and acidic so it does not feel too heavy. I'd also recommend the tortellini al ragu (4/5), plump with creamy cheese filling. I personally did not like the filling of the lobster ravioli, which was like a very firm meatball, but the lobster pieces were very tasty. Still loved the veal parmesan (5/5) - don't neglect to eat the meat on the bone! And dover sole (4.5/5) was again recommended as a classic, beautifully filleted tableside with plenty of capers to cut through the butter. Get a side of mushrooms (5/5) for sure, maybe some broccoli rabe (4.5/5) in hot chili oil, but note that it's bitter, but skip the potatoes (3.5/5) which despite having 3 sauces still lacked flavor. 

Weekday lunch reservations are much easier to come by, and I'd argue it's worth calling in sick for a meal here.

What a time travel experience. It's like stepping into grandma Nonnas home and eating dinner.  Very authentic dishes, made perfectly to order. Everything is prepared perfect and service is old school. Just an amazing experience, even the music in the background transported me to my family's home in Verona.

My experience at Carbone was very interesting. Don't get me wrong, I'm glad I went but I have no desire to go back. Here is my experience from the moment I walked through the door: upon arriving we were greeted by the hostess, she told us our table wasn't ready (even though there were multiple open tables) and that we could head to the bar to get a drink. My friend and I decided to wait until we were seated to order drinks. Once we were seated in the vacant table that was available when we walked through the door we were only handed a drink menu. We felt as though we were essentially being forced to order booze. While this isn't a problem, we both found it to be a bit odd and aggressive. After we ordered our wine, we were served a variety of treats (my favorite was the massive chunk of parmesan cheese). We ordered our food and enjoyed a salad that we split as well as a couple pasta dishes we also split. Nothing was so unique that my mind was blown. All in all the service was weird and the food was good. Perhaps the reason we didn't leave that impressed was because it is incredibly hard to get into Carbone and you constantly hear murmurings of how it is one of NYCs best Italian restaurants. I don't think it is, but I also wouldn't say its a bad restaurant.

Carbone is my absolute FAVORITE Italian in the city. Extremely difficult getting in so be sure to make a reservation a month in advanced via email. 

Service is fairly good for the most part but I wouldn't say outstanding. The food on the other hand will blow you away. To start, they bring out salami, warm bread (the warm pizza-like bread is my favorite), and cauliflower. The salami is some of the best I've ever tasted. We also ordered the burrata to start. While the burrata was extremely creamy, I didn't enjoy the toppings they added to this. Sort of tasted like raisins and figs on top.

For an entree; the spicy rigatoni is my favorite dish on the menu. The first time I had it, it wasn't spicy at all, which I enjoyed since I'm not a fan of spice. The second time I came here, the dish had much more of a kick to it. If you're not a spicy person, I would ask them to make this dish less spicy. I've also ordered the veal parmesan in the past. Was great veal, but since I'm not a veal person, probably wouldn't order this again. 

Overall, Carbone is a very special experience and everyone I've spoken with always leaves satisfied. If you're in the city, it's a must try!!

YES!!! Been wanting to try this spot for years, and it's obviously impossible to get a reservation. We were lucky enough to come on New Year's Day at 6:15 and the hype is so real. 

Firstly, on reservations: they release them at 10am 30 days in advance, but on Reserve they get gobbled up quick. If you have a concierge service (Marriott, Amex Platinum, etc), I recommend using them to facilitate. I've also heard if you email them within a 15-minute window of the 10am time, 30 days in advance, they will slot you in as well. They don't do walk-ins. 

Upon arrival, you are greeted by doorman, and immediately get taken back to a rustic, dining room, secluded from the business of new york city. They typically keep the blinds closed, which adds to the allure and exclusivity. We were immediately greeted by the hostesses who were very kind and seated us upon arrival. They'll ask you if you prefer sparkling or still, which both incur a charge ($9/pp), so be mindful of that if you don't mind tap. 

Our waiter came over and gave us the skinny; I had a good sense of what we wanted to order already via Yelp, but he was helpful in navigating away from some of the shellfish plates given my allergy. The only part of the entire evening that wasn't exceptional was our server trying to upsell us a bit... there was only two of us and we ended up ordering a LOT of food. Then again, it wasn't the end of the world since visits here are few and far between.

For starters they bring out bread and a bit of prosciutto. It's good, but not "THE BEST" bread, like some comments describe. For appetizers, we ordered the Beef Burrata which was probably the best I've ever had (even better than La Sirena and Republique in LA). Next we had the Carpaccio Piemontese, which was good, but a bit superfluous. It was flavorful (not too salty, beef was fresh), but it was probably my least favorite dish of the evening. Next we transitioned to the ever-famous spicy rigatoni, as well as the meatballs, which is a great pairing. The spicy rigatoni is somewhere in-between vodka pasta and hearty mac-n-cheese, with just the right amount of spice. Unbelievable plate. For our final course, we had the Veal Parm, which is a MUST HAVE (really good, second to only Giaccamo's in Boston), and the squash, which was immensely filling. The portions are generous, so I would recommend about 2 per person. We didn't have room for dessert because we were just too full... They do bring out fun Italian colored cookies at the end of the meal, which is a nice touch. 

For those who need a quick review, here are the most popular plates:

Caesar Salad
Beef Burrata
Spicy Rigatoni Vodka
Lobster Ravioli 
Veal Parmasean
Squash Agrodolce
Tiramisu

All said, it came out to about $150/pp, which is really reasonable given the experience. Dress code is business casual / trendy. Some folks were in all black, while others were in blazers. This place is frequented by celebs, so they're very lax about the dress code, just leave the tennis shoes and shorts at home. Excellent place for a nice dinner with friends or your S.O., or a classy dinner with Mom and Dad, but wouldn't recommend for a first date, or kids. Well deserving of their 1-Star, and already one of my favorite restaurants in the country. I can't wait to come back.

I'm not sure what the hype is about this restaurant, yes it's very old school Italian but the majority of the food was average. Maybe I went on an off night, but I didn't find it special, especially for the price. For our appetizer, we shared baked clams made 3 ways. The baked clams were cold and not even browned on top, they looked like they were sitting out for a long time. For our next course, we shared an order of the pasta with mushrooms. I couldn't believe how much garlic was in this dish, it was barely edible. A plate of pasta with an overload of garlic is not good. I ordered the meatballs for my main dish and although the red sauce was good, I would still prefer my Italian grandmother's meatballs. My husband ordered a scallops dish which he said was god but not memorable. The best part of my meal was the bread and chunk of parmigiana cheese they cut you. I wasn't too happy about being charged for two bottles of Pellegrino water when I only ordered one, just a tad too presumptuous in my opinion. Much better Italian restaurants out there, I will not be returning.

I emailed Carbone and managed to snag an early dinner reservation for two. I have been here previously for lunch but never for dinner. The food was delicious - even the bread basket was amazing. We ordered the meatballs, tortellini, spicy rigatoni, veal parmesan, and the tiramisu for dessert. 

The food was definitely five stars, but I have to take one star off for the service. We constantly felt rushed by the waiters. At one point we left a single meatball on the serving plate and a waiter rushed over to ask if we were done yet. We said no and he left but then another waiter came by a few minutes later asking if we wanted him to cut it in half for us. We got the point - they wanted to clear the plates so they could bring out our next course. 

After we received our next round of dishes (rigatoni and veal parm) we were so stuffed that we couldn't finish either of them. We did our best to power through but lo and behold a waiter comes over to ask if we were done (even though we still had food on our plates and neither of the dishes were finished). We were finding it almost comical at this point. Isn't it common knowledge that if there's still food on a customer's plate then that means they're clearly not finished?

In short, you must come for the food, but don't expect much from the service. The service was lacking and needs improvement. The young host/hostesses at the desk need more training because they come off as very pretentious and not very friendly and the waiters need to stop rushing customers. I understand they're just trying flip tables quickly, but it ruins the dining experience when someone keeps coming over and asking if we're finished with our dishes.

Everything was fine. The rigatoni, the veal, the meatballs...all just okay. The rigatoni in particular lacked any discernible flavor, besides a little kick in the end. Not sure why that's so impressive to so many people -- I'll take i Sodi any day of the week. Neither were the meatballs as tender or flavorful as the sycophantic yelp, instagram and infatuation reviewers would have one believe. La Vara has far better. And as far as the veal parm, it's tender, but nothing that would surprise me to discover at a halfway decent midtown lunch buffet and certainly nothing to swoon over (and, yes, that includes the precious bone that is the subject of so many glowing reviews).

All that said, the Manhattan was outstanding as was the tomato focaccia bread they brought out at the beginning. I would have liked to try the fresh mozzarella that usually comes with, but i guess they were out because all I got was a crumble of parmesan (which, btw, was really, really delicious).

YASSS AMAZING!!! It took us 2 months to get reservations at Carbon and it was well worth the wait! Honestly the BEST homemade/fresh pastas I ever tasted. No joke. From the delicious food to the service, 5 stars!! They offer different selection of free bread too which includes salami. 

Things to order:
- Tortellini al Ragu
- Spicy Rigatoni Vodka (MUST GET)
- Casa Carbone's meatballs and marinara sauce
- Baked Clams
- Carrot Cake
- Blackout Cake

I was very happy that I was able to get a lunch reservation around noon on a Monday holiday. The spicy rigatoni were amazing, definitely the best pasta dish I've ever eaten. The sauce was so flavorful and perfectly seasoned. I also really enjoyed the warm fresh mozzarella and garlic bread they served before the meal.

After a long two month wait, I was anxious that the famous Carbone meal would not meet my expectations, but boy was I wrong! The Spicy Rigatoni Vodka was to die for and the Veal Parm was perfection. The fluffy little Tortellini con Ragu were a close second for my favorite pasta dish. The free rainbow cookies provided a perfect end to an absolutely delicious meal! My tip: order extra food to-go so that you can munch on the best Italian food in NYC the next day as well!

Very good, but overly expensive for a bowl of pasta. 
I ordered a salad to start and asked for some more balsamic vinegar. The response I received was the vinegar we use is very expensive we will need to charge you. I'm paying over $17+ for a few pieces of mozzarella and they can't give a little extra vinegar. Not the money, it's the principle.

Delicious delicious delicious!! I wanted to take a star off just because it's so hard to make reservations here. They have the best cocktails (try their manhattan yummmm). We usually go for the usual like calamari or grilled octopus to start. Their bread tastes like pizzas super yum. For the main, we would get the spicy rigatoni, veal parm, and lobster raviolis. Personally, my favorite is the lobster raviolis. Everything is just so amazing here. Everyone is so professional and attentive. One of my favorite Italian places in the city!!! Must try (if you can get a reservation on Resy)!!!!
Applebys quality at Per Se  prices. Started with boring and burnt assorted clams and ok gorgonzola salad. The pork chop entree was tough and salmon ok. Next.
Outstanding, old school appeal. Great food, simple elegant decor, classic tunes. Fried calamari, meatball appetizer, rigatoni spicy vodka sauce, caesar salad, veal chop parm- all amazing.

This might be the best Italian food I have ever had (outside of a grandmother's home cooking). The food was excellent, the service was quick but did not rush you, and the drinks were delicious. If you are able to get a reservation at this place, do not pass it up. This place was also great for celebrations. It was my girlfriends birthday and I asked the server to surprise her with dessert. She had no idea and everything turned out great! Looking forward to going back again.

Carbone elevated my perception of Italian cuisine. Every detail was authentic to Italy - from the food & beverage, plates & cutlery, down to the floor tiles that reminiscent scenes from The Godfather.

Not going to be wordy here and describe every butterfly in my stomach even though every dish was love at first bite. 
-Complimentary starters: garlic bread in a hearty basket, salami plated like a blooming flower, and fresh mozzarella cut in wedges tableside to instantly sped up your heart rate
-Caesar alla ZZ: the one-in-a-million crisp caesar salad that doesn't taste like a plate of caesar-dressing-soup-mush.  
-Spicy Rigatoni Vodka: the infamous pasta dish I can eat all day every day 
-Lobster Ravioli: bouncy lobster, bouncy skin, creamy yet tangy sauce you will end up licking clean
-Mario's Meatballs: flavor bomb just look at that glistening juice (see photo!!!) and feel your mouth water
-Veal Parmesan: pizza's perfect sibling - crispy, meaty, flavorful and one true love (PS. please please savor the bone its the unsung hero of the dish)
-Carrot Cake: highlights of ginger notes, mix of textures between soft cake center and crispy edges, no other carrot cake will compare to this beauty
-Nutella Blackout Cake: lose your mind on a fluffy chocolate cake bed filled with raspberry cream and topped with rich Nutella icecream and crunchy hazelnuts 
-Arneis Piedmont (dry white wine): cleanse your palettes between bites

It is worth the splurge so order everything you want to try for a rare occasion! Why not bring some home and be happy for days right?
Amazing food and service. Drinks will really set you back $$ but honestly worth it for the delicious food and unforgettable experience.

Writing this review makes me so sad, as I was expecting a lovely meal on Valentines day with my husband. Getting a reservation was something he worked very hard for and the tasting menu sounded fabulous. We had a bad experience from the moment we arrived. We got to the door at 5:35ish for our 5:30 reso and we were turned away at the door that they were not open yet. We went next door for a drink and returned at 5:50, were a rude hostess told me that we missed our 5pm reso and they would seat us but needed to turn the table over. As we sat it was 10 minutes before we saw a waiter to order drinks.  The first round of the tasting was great, the carpaccio was very good as was the crab. When the waiter asked if I would like another glass of wine, he did not bring another yet filled up my half full glass and charged for another. Then things took a turn for the worse with the food, my veal was almost inedible and coated in salt. The dessert was no different from a chain restaurant. We had a lovely meal at The Grill last year and I know how fabulous Chef Carbone's meals are and concerned that the quality is being diluted. To the tune of $700 I will not being going back to any of the Major Food group restaurants. So bummed.

4.1
Month: February 2019
Day and time: Saturday lunchtime

Food: 5 stars
We ordered the caesar salad, the spicy rigatoni vodka, and the meatballs. I was sceptical about ordering the salad, but it was a delight. The salt of the anchovies and the citrus dressing combined beautifully. The meatballs were tender and the tomato sauce was chunky and thick. Despite the merits of both, the rigatoni was my favorite dish. The sauce was creamy with a kick, and I could have eaten it as soup. The pasta had structure and life, providing just enough fightback. We didn't even touch the larger plates on the menu. Though all three dishes were small, the richness of the ingredients provided the satisfaction. The complimentary mozzarella and salami to start was a nice touch, and we finished with a large slab of carrot cake. The buttercream took the latter over the edge.

Setting & Atmosphere: 3 stars
I expected more. The walls of the restaurant are royal blue, and the color was distracting and somewhat at odds with the serene ambience. Thompson Street is quiet, and Carbone is quieter still. We were unfortunate to sit at the closest table to the door, meaning the soundtrack to our meal was the host turning away the many walk-ins who hoped to grab a table.

Drink: 3 stars
The cocktail list has all the classics, and I enjoyed an above-average Negroni. The 'by the glass' wine list is short, and forces guests to compromise on either taste preferences or price point - I took a glass of the cabernet sauvignon at $31, not convinced by the other options. For some beguiling reason, one needs to request the wine list.

Service: 3-4 stars
We had no faults with our table service, being attended to regularly and having our food arrive quickly. I've met more welcoming fronts-of-house.

Value: 3 stars
I have a hard time faulting a restaurant on value when it produces such stunning dishes as the three we had. The salad, rigatoni, and meatballs were $25-30 each and punched above their weight and volume. The secondi run up towards $100 for some dishes, and I can only assume those get few hits. My main contention vis-à-vis value concerns the drinks. $20 for classic cocktails in a city where $16 seems standard is a hard sell. However, those prices were amongst the most palatable on offer. We flicked through the wine list and struggled to find bottles below $100.

Return: Yes
I can't remember writing such an imbalanced review. Come for the food and Carbone is divine; filter out or tolerate the rest.

Got a lunch reservation - yes, it is difficult to get one for dinner. The service is very good, the place smells amazing, and I absolutely love the Italian music playing. 

I tend to review restaurants based on how likely I am to return. 

The food was good - however, I have had better Italian food at home, and equally good Italian food at other restaurant, both in and out of NYC. 

Loved the fresh mozz, salami, and garlic bread that was brought to the table. Honestly, I would've enjoyed a meal consisting of just that. We ordered the baked clams, spicy rigatoni, and pork chop with peppers. 

The clams were very good, especially the lemony-buttery broth they were served on. As far as the pasta goes, I appreciate that it was very al dente.. I like much less onions happening in my vodka sauce though. They overpowered the sauce in my opinion.  The pork chop was very well cooked, extremely tender and juicy, but I would've enjoyed the dish a little more if some cherry peppers were thrown into the mix. 

Overall, I don't regret going. I can't say that I was disappointed, either. I want to emphasize that as an Italian American who grew up eating fresh sauce on Sundays, places like this just don't live up to the hype.

Came to Carbone for a birthday celebration and had a lovely time. The waiter was super helpful in suggesting how to order/what to order. Their portions are very large and recommend sharing. We got the baked clams as an appetizer and spicy rigatoni, Ragu tortellini & the veal parm. Would absolutely suggest getting the spicy rigatoni. We also got the carrot cake, that was okay. Overall great experience.
By far the best rigatoni ive ever had. This restaurant is amazing! Outstanding customer service & even better food!!!

Incredible restaurant and food! After waiting a month for our reservation to come (had to push ours back a couple weeks due to conflicts), the date finally arrived and we were ready. 

The restaurant is elegant and old fashioned, with dim lighting and delicious smells wafting from every direction. We were seated a little early at a 4top which was great, meant more room for our food! We started off with rosé, which was absolutely delicious. The service was absolutely impeccable, which is expected but always appreciated. We ordered the beets and Caesar salad for appetizers, had to keep it light somewhere! The bread and cheese plate was absolutely delicious and could have been its own meal in itself! The beets were super fresh and every bite had so much flavor! 

And finally, we were ready for our pasta. We ended up doing two orders of the spicy rigatoni vodka and one of the angel hair. Both were absolutely delicious. As said before, the flavors sprung up in unique and delicious ways and made the food an incredible experience. We finished off the night with gin martinis, which were delicious and strong. While our reservations were late, this allowed for better conversation due to less people being in the establishment. 

As a result, by 2am, we were greeted with a surprise apparence by The Weeknd! He emerged with his party from the back of the restaurant and it provided for an exciting end to the night for us! Every part of the experience was great and seriously, it was the best pasta I've ever had.

LOVE CARBONE... 4.5 Stars, Would've gave it 5!! I've had always been wanting to come here and so got surprised on Valentine's Day to here. Prefix menu was served to everyone for dinner that night. The ambiance is simple old school Italian, and the service was great and attentive. The only reason why I rounded down and said I bumped off half a star was due to the fact I found a tiny crab shell in my appetizer which shouldn't happen from this one-star Michelin and highly recognized Italian restaurant by Mario Carbone & Rich Torsi.

Every dish here was soo on point! The fresh ingredients and produce spoke for itself along with the flavor profiles being done right. Even their free assortment bread starters thats served with salami are some of the best bread baskets I've ever had; the pizza like bread and garlic cheese bread were hot and addicting. For starters we had the truffle king crab dish and beef carpaccio dish, both amazing. Then had pastas to share, the lobster ravioli and spicy rigatoni vodka. The lobster ravioli was stuffed with large chunks of lobster and the spicy rigatoni vodka was my date's favorite dish of the night and even said was the best vodka pasta he's ever had. Main course were great too.

Came here this past Friday afternoon for lunch and boy, it did not disappoint!!! Our waiter, whose name I do not know but he was in a burgundy suit gave OUTSTANDING SERVICE. We were given complimentary garlic bread, salami and homemade mozzarella(OMG I WOULD BUY IT!!!). We had the house chopped salad which our waiter recommended over the Caesar salad... it was delicious, great light dressing on top. We split the spicy rigatoni vodka which was cooked perfectly and just slightly spicy. We shared Mario's meatballs which were great, slightly pink in the center which was because of the blend they use to make them, including veal, they were very flavorful. Our main entree was the veal parm which was great. Complimentary rainbow cookies finished off the meal... which, I would also purchase along with the homemade mozzarella. 

TIPS: YOU MUST MAKE A RESERVATION. DO NOT BE CHEAP, EVERYTHING IS DELICIOUS BUT EXCEPT TO SPEND AN EASY $200 ON TWO PEOPLE. 

Pricing: 
House Chopped Salad $22
Spicy Rigatoni Vodka $32
Mario's Meatballs $27(comes with 3 meatballs)
Veal Parmesan around $60

Went to Carbone with a group of eight people. Seating was tight, especially considering it was a group of eight guys, and it was a business dinner... but we made do.

The meal itself was very very good but not exceptional. Several of the people in the party were regulars at Carbone and noted that one of the factors the the restaurant has in its favor is that it consistently has very very good food. So reliability clearly factored into their choice. Having said this, the meal was indeed quite good.

We had what I am told are the staples. The Caesar alla ZZ was fine. Cold, crispy, refreshing... the salad for "I'm not a salad guy" guys.

 
Favorites were spicy rigatoni vodka and lobster ravioli:

The spicy rigatoni vodka was delicious (I am not a hot/spice lover) it had just the right touch of spice to balance the flavors and cream in my opinion.  

Lobster ravioli is usually one of my favorites, and Carbone didn't fail to impress.  It's a full flavored but not overly heavy dish.

Veal parm was done perfectly. Standard preparation, but done just right.   

The meatball was tasty but reminded me of the style my Italian mother in law makes, very meaty and firm (light on bread & egg) whereas I personally prefer to make them "fluffier" with bread, egg and water so that's a matter of personal preference.  The table was split on texture, but we all agreed the flavor was great.

Service was very attentive, polite and professional.  Overall very happy and it's worth the hype.  Highly recommend!
Overrated hype. Not worth your time or your money. Service is poor. Food is fair. Atmosphere's ok. Music is good. There are much better dining options elsewhere available in NYC...

Several years in the game now and still going strong.  Not the easiest reservation to secure but well worth the effort.  All of the classics executed perfectly here so there are no wrong answers ordering anything on the menu.

Carbone is absolutely worth a visit if you haven't been. Reservations are stupidly annoying to get, but if you put in a little effort, you'll be able to get something, including for dinner on the weekends - though usually for shoulder times like 6-630pm ish or later at 10pm+ (I believe they open resis 30 days ahead of the dining date, and you can email requests starting 9am on the day 30 days before the dining date. Note if you email earlier than 9am, you're out at the end of the line in terms of requests). 

Service was impeccable. Our waiter was attentive without being overbearing, and helpful. Also very well dressed... Scene was basically what you'd expect from an old school Italian restaurant. 

We were a little gluttonous and ordered quite a bit (mostly because I didn't want to go through hassle of resi process again so wasn't sure when we'd ever be back). They were thoughtful about presentation/timing (so our small two person table wasn't overwhelmed but we could also see full plated dish before being served pieces of it) as well as packing up items efficiently for us to take to go. I thought the spicy rigatoni vodka lived up to all its hype - it's not spicy but the sauce is magic. So so good. Pasta perfectly al dente too. I wish I had gotten two of this order so I could take some with me to go. My boyfriend also really enjoyed the veal parm (note if you can't finish, it still tastes great reheated). The third item we ordered - the lasagna - was disappointing. Think the lasagna that night was a vegetarian one- honestly kind of bland and definitely not worth what we paid for it. Presentation was great though - served in the deep tin that it was baked in, with a crusty top layer. And for dessert, I heard the tiramisu was a must try...but we were craving cheesecake so went with that instead and did not regret. It may have honestly been my favorite item of the night - even better than the rigatoni! Not heavy at all - and a great end to a big dinner.

The food here is excellent, as was our waiter. Highly recommend the Mozzarella & Prosciutto and spicy rigatoni vodka!

Unfortunately, I went here to celebrate my boyfriend's birthday and the table next to us was extremely loud and obnoxious (guessing my weight when I first entered, discussing their affairs with prostitutes, etc.). The staff gave them a lot of attention as they were clearly spending a great deal of money on a business dinner. Sadly, it really put a damper on an otherwise great (and expensive) meal.

Carbone was something right out of a mafia movie. We walked into the restaurant around lunch time, without a reservation, as its impossible to get one, and after a 1.5 hour wait we got it. It was worth the wait! It is a cozy restaurant with not too many seats and dim lighting. 

The food is definitely the star of this restaurant and the four of us decided to order family style. We started with the delicate Carpaccio Piemontese, raw beef with mushrooms, and the flavorful Tuna Crudo. For a hot appetizer we had baked clams prepared two ways, one with bacon and the other one with breadcrumbs. The bacon one was better! For our main course we ordered the Spicy Rigatoni Vodka Pasta and the Tortellini al Ragu. The Rigatoni was delicious but the Tortellini al Ragu was our of this world. It was so good we ordered another plate of it! You have to try it! We finished with a Carrot Cake and a Tiramisu, which were sweet and delicious. 

One of my favorite restaurants in NYC. Highly recommended.

Went to Carbone for the hub's bday dinner. The ambiance is on point- very old school New York feel with a tinge of mafia in the design; music was the perfect compliment. Our waiter was attentive, but not annoying and we didn't feel rushed to order. Anyway, let's move to the food. The spicy rigatoni/vodka sauce sitch was AMAZING! We also ordered the lobster ravioli, carpaccio, cesar salad, meatballs, and veal parm. The lobster ravioli was meh- definitely wouldn't recommend it. That's probably one of my favorite dishes of all time, but it tasted fishy- and not in a ''ohhh im eating from the sea" kinda way... Pass. The meatballs were pretty solid (not spicy,) and the veal was good too. All in all (minus the ravioli,) it was a lovely meal.

My daughter picked this place because she heard it was amazing. We were definitely not impressed. The food is overpriced, and although our waiter told us the plates were big enough to share, they actually were not. The free appetizers were very good -- cheese, salami, cauliflower in a yummy garlicky oil and vinegar puddle -- along with a basket of delicious bread. That was the highlight of our meal. We got steak, meatballs, rigatoni and chicken. They all sucked. The meatballs were very undercooked and tasted more like sausage. The chicken also tasted raw and the steak came out cold. Overall it was very disappointing and for a $400+ dinner, we expected just a wee bit better quality and flavor. Next time we'll spend half the amount of money and getter better food on the Jersey side of the Hudson. Will not be back.
Carbone is both mine and my wife's favorite Italian restaurant. Spicy rigatoni and veal Parmesan are a must. The service is spectacular, and the ambience is perfect for small celebrations.

The pasta dishes we had were very good, spicy rigatoni and the meatballs were great. We weren't a big fan of the Chicken Massimo and for the price, even at an expensive place, the portion size was small.  

The service was just not great. We had come to expect a certain level of service from Michelin star places and this place just didn't have it. Every course was rushed to be taken off the table but then took forever for the next one to arrive. We sat 5 feet from the bar but our drink orders took a long time to arrive and multiple reminders. Flagging down our waiter was also an ordeal, even with empty tables around us it seemed like our waiter was always in a different part of the restaurant whenever we needed him.

Overall, I am disappointed with this restaurant. For the price and Michelin star reputation we really thought we would have been wow'd but we've had a much better experience at many Italian places across the city. I would not recommend Carbone.

WOW! Carbone was such a fun experience. It's just one of those places you have to go to if you can. We had a group of 4 ladies to celebrate a birthday and we had a ball! When I left the restaurant my jeans had a hard time staying buttoned :)

To start we had the complimentary bread, cheese, and salami. They literally brought a wheel of cheese to the table and scraped us off some. It was V YUMMY. For appetizers we ordered burrata, which they only make 10 of a night! That was a huge selling point for us not going to lie. It was delicious and came with eggplant as well. We also had the baked clams (duh) for an appetizer. I liked the sea urchin one the best, but the rest of my group loved whatever spicy one it came with. I can't remember the exact flavors I just know they were all unique and amazing.

For our main course we opted to do 3 pastas and a meat. So we ordered the spicy rigatoni, lobster ravioli, and the tortellini ragu. It's very hard to choose which one was my favorite. I had heard that the rigatoni was overrated prior to my visit but I very much disagree with that. It was so creamy, and the perfect amount of spice. The ragu tho just had the best filling flavoring, and the ravioli butter cream sauce was INSANE. All had their highlights and all were so so so so perfect for pasta lovers like myself. For our meat we obviously ordered the veal parmesan. It was just unreal. The cheese on top was so flavorful and the veal was perfectly crispy on the outside.

As I'm writing this I do realize that I'm running out of adjectives to describe my meal but I'm just gonna KEEP GOING.

For dessert the lemon cheesecake really caught our ears so we ordered that along with the nutella cake thing. The lemon cheesecake reminded me of my grandmother's lemon bars, but so much better (sorry Grandma Barb). Our group decided it was the perfect mix of like key lime pie filling, but more lemony, and an A+ cheesecake texture. 

DIVINE. AMAZING. 5 STARS. 

Sadly, I did not see a Kardashian or Ariana Grande. Maybe next time.

Incredibly disappointed. I don't understand all the good reviews. 
It was super loud, impossible to hear each other. Service was slow. Food was the definition of average. 
I literally could not wait to get out of there. Would not recommend.

So in love with Carbone - the hype is REAL! 

Came here for lunch and I can confidently say it was one of the best lunches I've ever had in my life. 

The place itself is quite small and cramped. Might have to get friendly with your neighbors.. not much wiggle room. 

Now onto the food. We had the prosciutto and mozzarella and it was the best I've ever had! Super soft and plump - it melts in your mouth. That's for both the mozz and 'sciutto. :)

The sauce of the spicy rigatoni vodka was reminiscent of Korean spicy rice cakes lol. Nonetheless the cook of the pasta was perfection! A perfect al dente. 

The meatballs were tender and juicy. The veal parmesan was pretty good, I liked that it was still crispy despite being doused in sauce. 

If the industry standard were to Carbone's food - the world would be a better place. You can't go wrong with anything here - everything is game!

Overrated and nothing memorable. I don't understand the hype. Got the $70 veal parm. Wish I had spent the money at a steakhouse instead. The rigatoni a la vodka was decent, but nothing to write home about. The mozzarella appetizer was good, but we won't be back.

Went for a friend's birthday. The service was awesome! Everyone we interacted with was extremely nice/funny and helpful. Especially the sommelier who taught us so much!

The food was good. However, I'm just gonna say it, I've had better Italian. 

What we loved: We all enjoyed the tortellini and were blown away by the lemon cheesecake. We all found the bread/cheese course to be great as well! I loved how they came to the table with a huge wheel of aged Parmesan and sliced pieces right off for us. The spicy rigatoni was very good as well and for sure glad we tried that! 

We also had the baked clams (they were pretty good), the lobster ravioli (not a fan) and the veal Parmesan (it was alright!). 

So all in all, a great experience, good food, but for the price/hype I expected a little more. But again, a solid Manhattan staple.

It pains me to write this review because carbone is our anniversary tradition starting with our very first wedding anniversary. It was our special tradition because not only was the food amazing but the service impeccable but unfortunately this was not the case on our last (and likely final) visit. 

To start, we were told that they take reservations exactly one month before starting at 10am and only by email. My husband sent them an email exactly one month before and at exactly 10am requesting an 8pm reservation and they responded back saying all they have is 6pm. I'm not sure how that's possible since we literally emailed at 10am on the dot but seems like they don't give their prime time reservations to normal people, which isn't great. And we were making a reservation for a Wednesday...

Next, my husband arrived a few mins before me and they took his coat/bag, and sat him immediately. They brought out the bread basket too...even though I hadn't arrived yet so the bread was cold by the time I got there. When I got there, they didn't offer to check my things and I had to sit with my huge jacket and backpack in a tiny table cramped next to two people. For the prices you're paying, they really need to make sure service is impeccable which it wasn't. We felt rushed the whole time (probably why they brought the bread basket out so soon). Each year we've come for our anniversary, they would always bring a little cake or something out for us but this year there was nada. Spicy rigatoni wasn't spicy at all, just sort of tasted like Mac and cheese. Seems like it's gone really downhill over the last few years.

Sadly seems like we'll have to break our anniversary tradition and try somewhere else next year :(. Such a shame!

Probably 4.5 stars.

RESERVATIONS: this was the hardest, most frustrating part of the entire process.  First, you have to calculate when you want to go to Carbone.  They start accepting reservation requests one month in advance to the numerical date. For example, you would email them on March 7th to request availability for April 7th.

Do not look at their online reservations because they are usually a very limited amount of late time slots. That's why you always see reservations at like 9:00 pm or 2:00 pm.

They start accepting reservation requests at 9:00AM via email on weekdays and at 10:00AM on weekends. They answer all emails in the order we receive them. What you should do is save a draft email and then press send (depending on your lag or delay) at 8:59am.  I sent mine at 8:59am and they didn't receive it until around 9:03am and only 5:15pm on a Saturday for 2 was available! However, if you email them before 9:00 am then you will be put at the bottom of the list because they answer emails in the order they receive them starting at 9:00 am.  So you have to time it right (I would test sending emails and when people receive them).

ATMOSPHERE: Carbone looks and feels like it would be a restaurant that has been around since the 1950s but it actually opened in the early 2000s.  They created a space that is a nod to the old Italian restaurants back in the day hence the more "old world" style decor. However, there is a sense of modernism to it so you don't feel like you're in an ancient restaurant.  The inside is pretty fancy and although there are people who dress casually if you come in a nice dress or slacks you won't stand out.  They also play oldies in the background.  The restaurant has 3 main areas, the area near the door, the back area and the area near the restrooms.  If you don't like sitting near the door or where people walk in and out then I would suggest requesting the back room towards the restrooms. 

FOOD: Their menu is large both figuratively and literally.  It takes up half the table! They have food ranging from calamari, to salads, pastas, meats and side dishes.  They are famous for their pasta so I would suggest sticking with that.

BREAD - when you first come in they give you a generous bread basket with cheesy bread on the bottom, a pizza bread and then 2 slices of a regular sourdough/baguette.  They also give you pieces of salami and a parmesan/cheddar cheese, which is really good, and pickled cauliflower.  I did ask for a refill on the bread, which they brought out.  It's pretty filling and a very nice "appetizer."

SPICY VODKA RIGATONI - this is one of their most famous dishes.  If you order it for 2 people and they know you will probably share (they didn't ask, they just assumed for us), they split it for you.  It's definitely on the spicy side but the pasta is perfectly al dente with a slight chew and bite and the sauce is a great vodka sauce, not too heavy or overly saucy either.  The portion size is enough for 1 person to be full but if you're splitting it you definitely need something else.

DIANA RIBEYE - the most disappointing part of the meal but it was still good.  The meat is a tad tough and chewy, but there were good parts with fat as well.  This is one of the more saucy ribeyes I've had because it's cooked or coated with a red wine type of sauce.  They slice it for you and it's suggested medium rare.  Like I said, it was good but not amazing so I think next time I would rather get another pasta.

Overall, there's a reason it's so hard to get reservations for this place! Definitely worth trying if you're a fan of Italian food.

The elusive five stars got earned by Carbone last night. We snagged a same day reservation online and rolled through for a late night dinner worried that this place might be all hype.

It's not. This is the least pretentious spot ever, something that is almost remarkable given the hysteria that surrounds it. Our captain Jared was just tops. He reminded me of NYC back in the day, generous, funny, and charming. I wasn't drinking but they were totally cool with us just ordering by glass. And the food was heavenly--they serve excellent Italian-American dishes like the spots that used to exist in Carroll Gardens. I actually woke up hungry for the spicy rigatoni. But I think for us the staff really sealed the deal. They are cool as hell. We will be back.
The food, service, and ambiance were all amazing!! While it was very hard and annoying to get a reservation, it was all worth it. The spicy rigatoni and carrot cake were the star of the show!!

Truly charming but underwhelming on the palette unfortunately. You go for the setting and maybe to take a cute photo of your girl with the oversized menu. The pasta is fresh, al dente but the spicy rigatoni fell short on the spice (or was completely forgotten?!). I thoroughly enjoyed the lobster ravioli and will give that 4.5 stars.

Spicy rigatoni vodka here is indeed the stuff of dreams, but otherwise... eh, you can skip it. I went to Carbone for a special birthday dinner, and between the hype and the tediousness of getting a reservation here (which my lovely friend did, I do not have the patience to wait until exactly 9am a month in advance to email them), I had high hopes. But my god, unless money is no object for you, this place is not worth it. Besides the rigatoni, I also liked the meatballs we ordered as an appetizer, but at $8 for a SINGLE MEATBALL it better be the best thing I've ever eaten (it was not). The other pasta we ordered was so forgettable I literally can't remember what it was. We also got a side of mushrooms and the carrot cake for dessert, which were good but again, not worth it for how much we paid. 

I'd also say Carbone seems like a lot more fun if you come with a big group, because the portion sizes of some of the entrees are truly enormous and meant for sharing (which is a good thing, since they're also heinously expensive). Service/atmosphere is what you would expect for this price point.

I don't get it.  We've always wanted to eat here and after multiple tries, finally got a reservation.  

First, the good:
Decor and wait staff like a movie set.  Small and unpretentious entry.  Nice but noisy ambience.  Wait staff very attentive.  The breads and pickled cauliflower  and preliminary salami were excellent.

Now, the not so good:
Wine list enormous but wine prices at least four times what the bottle would cost at a store.  Most restaurants mark-up wine (maybe 2x the retail cost) but really?

Food was "OK." Not phenomenal like others state.  Cesar Salad good, not anything extraordinary.  My pasta really resembled something I microwave from a well known national supermarket chain.  My table-mate's entrees were of about that caliber.  The portions were smallish.

Maybe this was an off night.  The place was packed.  One well-known celebrity was eating there.  The final tab was twice what I felt it was worth.  

I can only say, I don't get it

Service was great. Good starters with tasty bread, Parmesan cheese, pickled vegetables. Caesar salad was bland. No garlic, no vinegar, no taste. Veal parmigiana was just ok. Kind of tough and too much breading. Really pissed that the wine list is so so over priced and 85 to bring your own. I checked and 3 to 10 times retail on their list.

Simply amazing place to eat. Although it is very hard to get a reservation doesn't take away from when you do you will love it. The menus are real big and cool looking. It isn't a million things to pick from that will confuse you. That's something I like about places. The price are kinda high but it is al worth it. The waiter was extremely nice and attentive. We never had to wait a long time for anything. Everything came out on time and was soooo good. I would recommend this place to anyone looking for great Italian food. 

The atmosphere also. It seem like it was out of a movie

The food itself is great, but between the service, snobby hostess attitude, wait, price-point and difficulty getting a reservation, it's just not worth it. I made a reservation via email a month in advance for a 2pm lunch, and ended up waiting 40 minutes more despite arriving on time. There was no complimentary drink or anything to fix the wait. Also, it was so busy, the waiter was pretty inattentive. Finally, at 4:45 pm, we were asked to leave our table because they had to set up for dinner service. I understand that, but the table before us was not asked to leave, which was why we were seated so late.  
The rigatoni vodka is great, as is the complimentary bread, carrot cake is pretty good too, albeit a little hard. Skip the tiramisu cake, it's pretty dry.

This was a fabulous dining experience. The setting is lovely, the waitstaff is impeccably trained. The wine list is extensive. The food was delicious but the temperature of the food could have been a tad hotter. But honestly, that was a tiny blip...can't wait to dine here again.

It seems hard to believe but it's true that every time I go to Carbone the food, service and fun factor is better than the last.  It truly is my wife and my favorite restaurant because not only is the food exceptional but everyone treats us like family and it truly is dinner with friends all around us. 

Tonight I took my friend Justin and it was his first time here although I'm sure not his last. 

As to specifics, you are treated well from the moment you arrive. They bring you to start grandma bread and garlic bread that are outstanding along with salami, a piece of fresh Parmesan Cheese and cauliflower for everyone at the table. Each of these starters are wonderful. Jared, our captain, was fantastic as always and had the perfect recommendations. Everyone at a Carbone exudes warmth and a superb knowledge of the menu. I have food allergies to nuts and Jared as always knew exactly what I should avoid. 

For two people, 1 appetizer, 2 pastas and a main course to share are plenty. The prosciutto and mozzarella are simply the best I have ever had. My friend, Justin, raved about it all ride home. The fresh mozzarella is cut at the table and the prosciutto melts in your mouth. 

As for pasta, we had the rigatoni with spicy vodka sauce which is the best vodka sauce pasta I have ever had hands down. It is fresh pasta with a sauce that has a slight chili after bite which is just perfect. The tortellini with cheese filling is like heaven and to try and describe it would be an injustice. It is pillowy soft and melts in your mouth. 

As for main dishes, the Veal parm was perfectly cooked and I confess, I did pick up the bone. The meatballs were soft and the sauce was perfect and the veal parm which  is on the bone is presented perfectly. 

The service is not rushed and well spaced out and everyone lucky enough to have a reservation seems to be having a great time. Every tune played in the great soundtrack seems to fit the bill for a perfect night of extravagance and fun. 

As for desert, the lemon cheesecake was light and  a perfect ending. It was a cross between a  meringue and a cheesecake and it was very refreshing. The coffee was smooth and strong as I like it. 

This is "old school" red sauce Italian but every dish is taken up to a new level. Carbone gives you a fresh take on old standards and it's rendition has now become how I judge other versions of these dishes. 

This is more than just a meal.  Dinner here is an experience, like a show would be, and 5 stars doesn't do it justice. My lovely wife was away on business but I'm sure she is happy knowing that Justin and I were fed well while she was gone and that everyone asked about her.  We did eat her favorite meatballs in her honor.   Thanks again to Julian, Hannah, Jared and everyone at Carbone for your friendship and hospitality and for a wonderful dining experience as always.
we have greatly enjoyed every meal here. front of the house is outstanding, and the food and showmanship is topnotch. a proper nod to a proper night out.

Was so excited to finally get reservations at Carbone. I am allergic to gluten so I ordered the gluten free spicy rigatoni. Just got home and realized that it was definitely not gluten free because I am so sick! Not to mention it wasn't even that great- just an average dish of pasta. Such a shame that a well known restaurant like this ended up to be so average and made the mistake of serving me non gluten free pasta. Will definitely not be returning.

This is by far my favourite restaurant. Whenever I visit NYC or Las Vegas I always visit no matter what! 
I usually stick to what I like best....
Caprese salad, vodka rigatoni, meatballs, veal and corn as a side. I am Italian myself and can honestly say this is one of the best places for authentic Italian and the service is always great. 
My only complaint..... every single time I've dined here I've sat at the same exact table. They have a row of two tops along the front area of the restaurant. It would be nice to have some other options throughout the place for reservations of two so we can experience the restaurant in a different way instead of the same thing every single time.

I usually do not like Italian food, but wow I was a big fan. The vibe is so nice and cozy; I felt like I was in a Woody Allen movie. 

Fire: Cheesy starter bread, Spicy Rigatoni Vodka, Lasagna Verde, and cauliflower. Apparently they only make 2 Verdes a night so I am honored that one of them met my face. Deadass I could eat a whole table of just the cheesy bread from the beginning. 

Needs improvement: meatballs were desert dry, rainbow cakes were uninspiring but very cute, playlist was all over the place stylistically.
Decent restaurant, I don't know what the hype was about this place. Food was average. Service needs improvement.

I know this place is hard to get a reservation but I was lucky to get one a week before. Just keep checking back on their website for available times. The complimentary bread basket, salami, and cheese were very delicious. The caesar salad was prepared on the side and the croutons were crispy on the outside chewy on the inside. The octopus and rigatoni were also very delicious! I gave it four stars since we ordered a bottle of pellegrino and they charged us $9 for each cup!!

The sauce in the spicy rigatoni vodka was out of this world. Best I have ever had. Definitely order this!

The complimentary appetizers were also excellent, which included amazing garlic bread and homemade burrata. The lobster ravioli was also good. 

Could've done without the veal Parm but it wasn't bad. The Caesar salad made at the table was good, though $25 for a salad does hurt a little bit. 

Overall, it's pretty pricey but definitely worth trying! I'll definitely be back to get the spicy rigatoni vodka again and to try some of the other pastas.

Two weeks ago my fiancé and I booked a last minute trip to New York for memorial weekend which also happens to be my birthday weekend. Booking the trip last minute I knew it would be impossible to get reservations at Carbone. 

My fiancé and I decided to walk into Carbone Sunday around 7:00. The ladies at the front desk informed us that they are not taking walk ins because they are fully committed. (I was willing to wait for a cancellation). I informed them that I'm visiting from Los Angeles and I'm willing to wait as long as it takes. 

Luckily there was a cancellation and the ladies were able to seat us. 

The service is unseen of at any other restaurant. Very friendly, informative, and professional. Our server took the time to talk about the menu and was extremely amazing, might I add, everyone was hands on and great. 

We ordered: 
Beef carpaccio (melts in your mouth)
Meatballs (proportion was great and tasted amazing)
I ordered the lobster ravioli and words aren't sufficient enough to explain how amazing it was!
My fiancé ordered the lamb chops and he loved them. 

Overall we had a wonderful experience, and I will definitely come back when I'm in town.

This is worth pulling every string you can. We went as a party of 8 for a friends birthday. It was one of the top 5 best meals of my life and the service was so good at a point they were reading my mind. We spent about $450 a couple and we all left full and tipsy. I would sell my soul for another reservation any day.

This is our favorite Italian restaurant. We have never had something that we didn't enjoy! Once you are seated they bring you over bread, oil and cauliflower and a generous piece of cheese. Their prosciutto & mozz is to die for. For dinner we strongly recommend the spicy rigatoni vodka, tortellini al ragu, veal parmesan. We usually go to Carbone just us two, but when we go with a bigger group they make sure the portions are enough for everyone!

The service is phenomenal. From the moment you are greeted by the doorman you are treated like family. They do not pressure you to over order or pick an expensive wine. 

You must make reservations one month in advance. If you are emailing for a reservation mon-fri, you must email them at 9:00am. If it is a Saturday or Sunday, you can email them at 10:00am. They do not accept emails prior to those times.

Loved Carbone!  Three words:  SPICY RIGATONI VODKA!  The sauce is so creamy and delicious, I probably could have had seconds!  It only took me 4 tries to get a reservation and then had to wait a month after I made it but it was well worth the wait.  

My girlfriend and I started with a glass of wine and snacked on the absolutely amazing bread and cheese platters which come free as starters.  I made cmon they carve you a chunk of Parmesan!  It's amazing.

We got the meatballs which were huge and juicy with a delicious tangy tomato sauce.  She got the tortellini a la ragu which she loved.  We were stuffed and left satisfied.  I've already made another reservation for June 1!

It's worth getting any reservation you can get, the Cesar salad and the spicy rigatoni is delicious. Obviously the service is impeccable. They make the Cesar salad right at your table side. The portions are quite large and can be shared.

My second time at Carbone and it was as good as the first, maybe even better. It's still difficult to get reservations for this place even after all these years. Try for lunch, you'll have better luck than dinner reservations. 

Located on Thompson street in the West Village, you've probably walked by a million times without even noticing them. They're across the street from Lupa and Tomoe sushi. Once you're inside, you're greeted with a blast from the past. The inside is very old school Italian and it's complemented with Sinatra playing in the background. 

We went with the usual orders as why would you want to order anything but the best? Of course the meal started with the free burrata and garlic bread. Amazing as always. We then had the baked clams and special tuna of the day. If you like baked clams, these are amazing. A plus if you like uni. 

We moved on to the spicy vodka rigatoni which is cooked perfectly to al dente and sauced magically. Easily one of the best pasta dishes anywhere. This went very well with Mario's meatballs. Don't freak out from the pink inside, it's not raw, it's salt cured. 

Finally we finished our enormous lunch for two with the famous bonein veal parmigiana and artichoke hearts. It was almost too much food but we caught our second wind and took it down. 

We finally finished the meal with complimentary rainbow cookies. 

Simply put, if you have the chance to come, you should.

It's ok. The restaurant seem like "italian restaurant by italian immigrants to newyork" not really authentic. They charge water per person (unlimited bottles but per person is not needed) the portion was small. Pasta was good though. Didnt like their desserts

Amazing food - try the spicy rigatoni, beef carpaccio, and the veal parm. I've been a few times and the service always changes. I had a reservation and had to wait over 45 mins after to be sat. 2 couples were sat before me even tho they showed up later and reservations were at the same time. I mentioned in 3 different ways that it was my bf's birthday and no mention of it at all. Finally I went up to the waiter at the end and reminded him and he brought out a cake that I ordered. Although he knew the menu well and gave great service otherwise. The hostess is stuck up for no reason, with her nose so high and doesn't acknowledge the restaurant being late for a reservation. Service all around was okayyy but the food was good.

I love the ambiance and the service at Carbone. The waitstaff is attentive  but also very fun and friendly. 
First off the bread!!!!AMAZING! Along with the chunk of parm and everything else they start you off with. 
We started with the baked clams and Cesar salad. Both were excellent, the croutons on the Cesar are worth it alone!
For entrees we shared the rigatoni with spicy pink sauce and the tortellini ragu. We also had the meatballs, which are off menu. Both pastas were great but the tortellini was out of control! Just fantastic, I think possibly the best meat sauce I've had yet. I didn't go as crazy for the meatballs as others, I've had better. People rave over them so worth a try!
For dessert the chocolate cake with cherries and Nutella gelato. Outstanding!
Overall great service, great food!

Overall: 4.5; Food: 4; Atmosphere: 4.5; Service: 4.5

Carbone is one of the few places I've been to in a while that really lived up to the hype. The vibe was totally not what I was expecting. It was upbeat, trendy and fun. There were large groups of tables celebrating, having multiple course meals, people were drinking, music was going. A lot of fun.

Food: 4
- Meal starts with an AWESOME complimentary bread course: garlic, tomato sauce on focaccia and multi-grain white
- Also comes with complimentary pickled vegetables and salami. So delicious. Had to stop myself from eating it all to save room for the mains.
- ***Meatballs: Yum! Delicious tomato sauce. Meatballs cooked perfectly.
- Veal parmigiana: A little disappointing. The veal was soggy - seemed like the sauce was on it a little too long. Veal was also under-seasoned. Came with a big bone that had decadent meat and fat on it, but was hard to eat. Better if they could carve that for you.
- ***Spicy Rigatoni Vodka: I love vodka sauce and this lived up to expectations. Just *slightly* salty.
- Nutella tiramisu: Barely noticed the Nutella. Had a hint of orange. Meh.

Atmosphere: 4.5
See above.

Service: 4.5
Service was great! When our food started to arrive before our bottle of wine, they were quick to bring out two complimentary glasses. They were really friendly.

Finally came to Carbone after stalking the reservations page online, and learning that they open up 4 weeks in advance. 

I made a reservation for two for Monday at 10:30pm, but we walked in and surprised to find our table was ready around 9:30 :) 

We ordered the beef carpaccio, I ordered the spicy rigatoni vodka and bf got the lobster ravioli. Everything was delicious. Service was immaculate. I only took off the one star because of price. I feel like I've had pasta that was on-par to Carbone before for less money. 

Am I glad I came? 100%. 
Would I come back again? For the money, probably not.
Ate here twice.  Tried their meatballs which were excellent.  Excellent spicy rigatoni in vodka sauce.  Loved the veal parmigiana.  Didn't like their lobster ravioli or their chicken dish

Easily one of the most decadent must-try's in New York City - if you manage to get so lucky with a reservation. It goes without saying that Carbone is quite the scene, but it really manages to live up to the hype and its reputation for having some of the best pasta in the city. First of all, the dinner is not just a meal, but a show. You're presented with a comically large-sized menu. Our server for the night suggested we ordered a few from each section for our group of four, which included the carpaccio, homemade pepperoni, spicy rigatoni vodka (duh), veal parm, ribeye diana. We also got to try a seasonal pasta (I believe it was tortellini?) with table-side shaved truffles.

If I had the chance to do it again, I'd say the real must-get is the spicy rigatoni vodka, which is philosophically, one of the best bites of food one can experience (up there with otoro with a sprinkle of truffle salt and a fatty piece of Katz's pastrami). I also wish I had been able to try the meatballs (off-menu), but that just gives me more of an excuse to return.

Long story short, go to Babbo if you want refined bites of pasta with fancy ingredients, but come to Carbone if you want to feel gluttonous, spoiled, and incredibly happy.

Extraordinary!
I was a little skeptical, but it was unfounded. The food and service are sublime.
We ordered way too much. 2 plates for each of us, so had to take home a doggy bag. Our favourites were the Granchio and Pepe. Delicate crab and tiny bow-ties. The flavors and textures were amazing.The rigatoni came in second. The beef carpaccio is in a class of its own and its also a huge portion. The veal parm was outstanding as was the chicken Massimo.

My only complaint was that the wine list really doesn't hav3e a range of moderately priced items. Their pricing at the lower end, below $200 per bottle, is very high with giant markups. The pricier items are more fairly priced but if you are paying 2 grand a bottle do you really care?

Absolutely a place to go back to if you can get a res.
This is nice gem hidden in a small restaurant. I liked it a lot, but be prepared to spend more than expected:)
Delicious food, not spectacular. But good. Accommodating to GF customers which is wonderful.

Had a great lunch, but it's very difficult to get a reservation, especially for dinner. At night, it's packed to the point of being uncomfortable. Highly recommend for lunch. Don't need to tell you to avoid it for dinner since you're unlikely to get a table. Fortunately, NYC has so many other great Italian restaurants.

I don't know what to say but a MUST if you can get in.    Rigatoni app Followed by the veal parm with the bone don't stray off this advice.   You are going to pay those prices because you are eating what it must be like in heaven!    So my advice:   Get  a date to pay, a client dinner or splurge on a big occasion!!!!!!!!     It's one of my shortest reviews ... but no reason to candy coat this one.    

A MUST .... let's  put it this way I did not review the bathroom and if I did they could have a bucket and only hand sanitizer in there and I would still give it an 11!!!!

Is it really worth it? 

That's the #1 question anyone who knows about this restaurant asks.

The short answer for me is yes. My husband thought a little differently - hey it's super pricey- but cost aside in all honesty I think it depends on what you order.

After sitting in a booth or table that is so old school ny, they bring out a mouthwatering spread of fresh bread, sliced meat, marinated vegetables and a huge chunk of deliciously nutty parmesan. Gets you excited about what's to come for sure.

To start we had the baked clams served 3 ways with lowish expectations but a recommendation from our server and boy were they good. Would get again in a heartbeat.

Second course we shared the pasta with vodka sauce (their best seller)... I must say as a vodka snob it is by far the best. Looks like not much on the plate but super rich, hint of spice and so very worth it.

Third course we shared the veal parm, eh not my fav but by all means delicious. Seems to be deep fried but tender.

Forth course, the lobster pasta - jam packed with lobster and delicious (they do not skimp out with that)

I'm embarrassed to say that the 2 of us couldn't finish it all and didn't have room for dessert.

In the time we sat, there must have been at least 10-15 people walk in to try to get reservation for the evening and all were turned away. You're best bet is to email the restaurant directly as slots fill up in seconds.

So to recap the answer is yes, go!

PHENOMENAL Spicy Rigatoni .. Simply the best 

 The bar has been set.

Good Italian old school vibe and food. Small but delicious menu.. Everything fresh and yummy. I had lobster ravioli and a great ceasar salad..i also had calamari light breaded fresh and delicious.we also had Lamb chops and all I can say is wow, I told them to surprise me with a nice sweet drink.. and it was amazing.. not to sweet where I couldn't taste the liquor..a great drink. But the nutella tiramisu cake... OMG The Best.. Best cake I have had in a while..

I'm starting this review of with this: This is one of the best meals I've had in NYC.

I've heard people mention Carbone for a while now and how hard it is to get a reservation. I planned to eat here 3 weeks in advance, and this was one of the best food decisions I made.

This place is pricey, however it is worth it. During lunch, they give you complimentary appetizers including fresh pepperoni and mozzarella. I am not joking when I say this was the best mozzarella I've ever had in my life.

I ordered the veal carpaccio and the lobster ravioli. The veal carpaccio was amazing! It was so tender and tasty, I loved the pine nuts. The lobster ravioli was really delicious and so meat filled. The service was immaculate; the waitstaff really wanted you to feel welcome.

12/10. Would recommend.

We had lunch today at Carbone and I was not impressed. Why there is so much hype....maybe people think they are so lucky to be eating there, their taste buds or sensibilities go awry? 
P
We started with one of the special appetizers, the Big Eye Tuna served raw. Nothing was appealing about this dish; the tuna was mushy and the sauce tasteless. I had two bites and that was plenty. My girlfriend thought better of it but I felt that it was cringe worthy. 

For entrees we both had pasta; she had the rigatoni with vodka sauce and I had the spaghetti  pomodoro. We split the mamas meatballs. The meatballs were ok. Not great, not the world's best...just ok. Both pastas were good but not memorable. Equal to any of a hundred Italian places in the Village. I found the service to be a bit patronizing as if they were doing you a big favor charging $300 for spaghetti and meatballs. And it wasn't great service either as our finished entrees sat for 15 minutes before they were picked up. Ok I've nit picked this poor restaurant to death but here was the one thing I found odd: we had a 1:45 reservation for lunch. The place was at most 1/3 full. While having lunch at least ten walk ins came and were told there was no availability. What's up with that? 
My advice: if you can get a reservation try it. Maybe you will like it better than we did????

Food was phenomenal!!! Service was incredible. Jared made our evening, and Alessandro was super helpful! This place was hands down top 5 restaurants I've been too! Thank you all for the amazing service!

What a little gem in the village. This relatively recent Italian joint has been going strong for a few years. Nestled into an old Italian storefront from a time gone by is the refined take in 20th century Italian American cuisine. Unassuming from the outside, the interior is simple and a bit rustic with touches of elegance. The staff is helpful and on point. The music is straight out of the goodfellas soundtrack. And the food would make any Nonna proud. Rich sauces, tasty pasta, delicious main dishes and solid drinks. We went with a large group. The space like many downtown pre war buildings is tight. It also can get a bit loud. But the food makes up for it. Nothing is reinventing the wheel but all is prepared well. We got the Caesar, octopus, the spicy rigatoni, a special cacio e pepe, veal Marsala, chicken scarpariello, and a beautifully cooked whole branzino. All were good. But make sure to get an order of the meatballs. They are fresh with a beautiful fried basil on top. Also the corn side dish is fantastic!! This is a great place to take people visiting New York to give them an old school Italian American experience with way better food than little Italy!

I really don't see what all the fuss is about. I know I'm critical having been raised in an all Italian family, but based on this my mom deserves a Michelin Star, maybe 2. The lasagna was a bit over salted. The reservation process is ridiculous. I think that is why people give it such high marks. Exclusivity doesn't always = spectacular. Our waiter was great though.
Excellent overall experience. Great food, service, atmosphere. It's expensive, but worth it.

I finally made it in!  Getting a rez here is challenging, at best.  However, it's been worth the wait!  You have to come here prepared to spend a lot of money but once you get past the prices your taste buds will be overjoyed.  The usual restaurant breadbasket is elevated here.  There were three types of bread, all amazing, accompanied by pickled cauliflower, salami, and hunks of Parmesan to start the table off.  The plates were all very cute with colorful designs that took me back to Italy.  The server listed off many specials and gave recommendations.  We ended up starting with the caprese, which our server claimed as better than their burrata (who ever says that?!), but I now believe him.  The tomatoes were vibrant greens, yellows, and reds and the fresh mozzarella was warm and delicious.  If you like Caesar salad, this is the place to get it.  It's heavily dressed in a creamy Caesar that is dressed table side.  We got the spicy rigatoni, something they're famous for, and the lobster ravioli.  The ravioli was both stuffed with lobster as well as topped with it.  We split the veal parm, which was good but honestly the least exciting of the dishes.  The truffle corn was a literal dream.  It is RICH and covered in truffle shavings.  The artichoke hearts were good, but not worth it in comparison to the corn.  For dessert, while the server suggested the carrot cake, we went NY cheesecake and it did not disappoint.  Thick and creamy with a candied lemon on top.  However, because the server wanted us to try it he treated us to the carrot cake as well!  It was a great ending to the meal and, while carrot cake isn't for me, the ginger ice cream it came with was the perfect pairing.

My dining experience at carbone is solid 3stars, which I'm sad about as I read too many good reviews on the restaurant. I'd say that the hype for spicy rigatoni is real. It really is a delish dish and def a highlight of the dinner. I'll happily go back to try their rigatoni again. 

However, I didn't enjoy other dishes as much as I wanted, including veals and meatball which I believed were just okay. I really wanted this dining experience to be perfect as my mom was in town and I made a reservation in advance for this special dinner but my mom wasn't fully satisfied with other dishes. However, I do appreciate the complimentary dessert and impeccable service from the servers.

Reservations open on Resy 30 days in advance. You can cancel either 24 or 48hrs in advance by emailing the Resy help email, otherwise it's $50 cancelation fee per person. I was able to make modification to the number in my party with no problem.
