The food was delicious and the service was outstanding as you would expect. Was it the best Italian I've had? Probably not (Peppolino is delicious if you don't have time to wait for a reservation). Would I recommend? Absolutely. 

The corn side dish was bombbbb. Def don't miss it!

Attempted to come two years ago and it was nearly impossible. The waiting list for reservations was ongoing. Finally got to reserve today on a open spot. After tasting all these dishes from Carbone I understand why it is so busy. The food is amazing!! Hands down one of the best Italian places we have dine. The meatballs are a must have as well as the Spicy Rigatoni Vodka & Tortellini al Ragu!!

I don't understand the hype around this place. The food was fine but not much better than any other italian restaurant in the city. The meatballs were completely cold in the center. The spicy vodka rigatoni was good but nothing I would go out of my way for.. which was super disappointing since that's what I was most looking forward to. The biggest let down though was the veal parm - $65 and below average. Would have been nice to have it over some sort of pasta for that price point. 

Overall super average.

I went to Carbone for the first time last night, and we had an incredible evening. I love the ambience and decor in here. It was crowded as expected, but comfortable. I could hear my party and speak to them without screaming. The bathrooms were super clean. 

First off, the service was the best service I've had in NYC so far. Our waiter Carmine was funny, attentive, and had excellent recommendations. The sommelier (I didn't catch his name) was super helpful and even recommended some wines that they had just gotten and weren't on the menu yet, and they were excellent. We are going to Italy in a month and he gave us some great tips and recommendations about where to go and what to do in Italy and Florence. 

We shared all of the dishes family style, which is how I prefer to eat. The breads and cheese to start were delicious.  We had a special - the scallop carpaccio - and it was the best thing I've eaten in a long time. Just the right amount of salt, perfect texture, and even a little sweet. I could eat this forever and I'm still dreaming about it. 

We also had the spicy vodka rigatoni, which I'm also still dreaming about. At first, it was a little confusing to eat spicy pasta, but the dish got better with every single bite. I've never experienced anything like that - you must try it. We also shared the meatballs, which melted in your mouth. Had the lobster ravioli which was also excellent. 

For dessert we had a chocolate Nutella cake which was what my chocolate dessert dreams are made of. The tiramisu was also to die for. 

We ended dinner with some complimentary limoncello. 

We absolutely cannot wait to be back. My favorite NYC dining experience so far!!!

I've wanted to go to Carbone for YEARS, since I first moved to the city and I am disappointed to say that I think its highly overrated. The food is definitely good, but not worth all the trouble and hype to get a reservation. To get a reservation you have to email them one month out exactly at 9am. Even if you send it right at 9am, sometimes they tell you they have no availability or can only get you a 5p or 10p. 

To eat we got mozzarella and prosciutto, caesar salad, meatballs, spicy rigatoni, tortellini bolognese, and veal parm. Everything was good and it was enough food for 4 people.You also get garlic bread and salami to start. I was most excited about the spicy vodka rigatoni. It did not disappoint BUT later that week I went to Parm (same restaurant group) and got their "Rigatoni Fra Diavola" and it was THE EXACT SAME PASTA--only different was the name and it was half price. 

As far as cost goes, we had 4 people and each got a drink we ended up paying around $100 per person with tip and tax. I thought it was a little overpriced for what it was,but when you go to Carbone you are paying for the ambiance and experience. If you want a more low-key and low-cost experience just go to Parm :)

I loved carbone and have been dreaming about their spicy rigatoni ever since. This restaurant is insanely hard to get a reservation. We booked a month in advance for a friends birthday and were only able to get reservations at 10:30pm. 

I love the decor and ambiance of this restaurant. The service could be a little more friendly but it is what it is. I loved how they automatically start you off with a chunk of Parmesan , sliced meat, bread and marinated vegetables. We ordered the meatballs as an app and I'm sad to say that I wasn't impressed. I am very tough critic when it comes to meatballs. The sauce was good though. 

Did i mention how amazing the spicy rigatoni was? lol . We also tried the salmon oreganata, angel hair pasta and the veal Marsala. Those dishes were delicious as well. If and when I return i think I will just stick with the pasta.

I went here because I've always wanted to try their spicy vodka rigatoni and it was as good, if not, better than I anticipated it to be. I also had the assorted baked clams and the ones topped with uni were amazing. I could eat 2 dozen of those. I deducted 1 Star because I think the food is overpriced.

Carbone is a recreation of an old school Italian fine dining restaurant with a vibe and soundtrack reminiscent of "Goodfella's". The restaurant itself is dark, noisy and cramped but the reservations themselves are quite hard to come by as it is a sought after destination for classically well prepared Italian fare. The dishes are all quite large & served family style which the expertly trained staff are more than happy to arrange to be split as to make sharing easier. The servers are all dressed in tuxedos and not only well educated and versed in the menu but also exceedingly friendly. As far as the food itself, most dishes are perfectly prepared and beautifully plated. Overall this is a great place to dine out for a special evening and a great show to boot.

My favorite Italian restaurant in NYC. A sure thing every time and the service is impeccable. Great for a small group, table for two or dining alone (which I've done at lunch). I always order the tortellini al Ragu. The tiramisu must be tried at least once, as  well as the fresh mozzarella and garlic bread. It's the stuff dreams are made of. Always a sure thing.

This will be an interesting review for sure. For my birthday dinner, we decided to dine at Carbone. This was probably my 3rd or 4th time dining here. Every other experience has been amazing. This visit however, was way different. As soon as we were seated, I said to myself "This is the worst table in the restaurant." It was a makeshift table right alongside the front bar. It was a very closed space, but I thought maybe it would be ok. The first hour of the dinner was fairly non problematic. However, the second half couldn't have been a worse dining experience. Tons of people were at the bar right behind us (never seen this before) who were extremely loud and constantly bumping into me and kicking my chair. The food runners also had to travel between the people and my chair. I couldn't even use my utensils without elbowing someone standing directly behind me. At first we thought we could power through, but after 30 mins of this nonsense, enough was enough. I will say, the Carbone management handled this was class. They asked if we wanted new table, free desserts etc. But at that point, the night seemed to be ruined and we had to get out of there. The assistant GM did come over, apologized, and gave us our entrees on the house. Told us to contact for a reservation in the future, and we will have a better experience. So for that, this place to me is still one of the best in NYC. Just caught it on a busier night than normal. As for the food? It's amazing. 

Here's what you order:
Assorted baked clams
Prosciutto & mozz
Caesar salad
Meatballs
Spicy rigatoni vodka (life changing)
Veal Parmesan 

Carbone draws the crowds and for good reason. Still my favorite place in the city for Italian.

Definitely lives up to the hype and more!!! My favorite restaurant in the city and I will always try to come back whenever I can get a reservation. You must get the spicy rigatoni vodka, the tortellini and the pork chop. The burrata appetizer is excellent too. 

The second time I came here, I was with a friend who is a vegetarian and the waiter kindly put the meat sauce for the tortellini on the side without even any hesitation. The service is incredible here and so are the drinks. I have nothing bad to say except that it can be a bit overpriced, but it's so good that I can't complain!

After dining at the much-hyped and adored Carbone, I have to say many dishes were outstanding...but overall it seems that the restaurant is a bit in cruise control mode as it is has expanded, and the reviews from a few years ago raving about the service, atmosphere, and overall experience etc. are no longer applicable and do not justify the current price tag.

The universally heralded dishes such as the Caesar Salad, Rigatoni with Vodka Sauce and Cheesecake do not disappoint.  Make sure to order these, in addition to the Lobster Ravioli which was the greatest execution of this we have ever eaten.  The complimentary antipasti is also stellar.

The meat dishes tended to fall short.  I highly anticipated the Veal Marsala, but it was just ok.  While the veal itself was high quality and well-cooked, it was an average rendition of marsala sauce, with excessive sweetness akin to that found in versions costing 1/3rd the price at some average Italian restaurant.  Older reviews picture a much larger and more visually appealing portion of this dish...so I think it is simply not at the same standard as it used to be.  I felt similarly about the highly touted meatballs, which were again just good.

Get the caesar salad and stick with the pastas.  If you go in not expecting a transcendent dining, you will be delighted.  It is an even harder reservation to secure, but Rao's is the better version of this classic Italian-American dining experience top-to-bottom...Carbone is the little brother looking up, imitating as reverence.

5 stars for the rigatoni. Everything else is average and not what you would expect from a Michelin Star. The rigatoni though...fiiiiiire. 

Restaurant was unbelievably dark and cramped. I seriously was having trouble reading the menu. Mind you, I'm 28 and not 75.

TL;DR: Carbone is a spot that skates by on the strength of its reputation and perceived exclusivity. Once you're in the door, it's ok food and wine at overinflated prices, poor service if you spend anything under $100 per person, constant upselling totally not befitting an upscale restaurant, and a stuffy environment catered towards old white retirees on an evening out from their old folks home. There are enough amazing Italian spots in NYC at similar price points with better food and service (Lilia, L'Artusi) that you do not need to waste your time here. Glad I came for the experience but would not go back.

One of my friends snagged a reservation so we came as a group of six for dinner around ~6pm on a Sunday. As another reviewer noted, the place has a very old school red sauce Italian American vibe; dark, white tablecloths, closed curtained windows. The servers are all portly white men dressed in suits, and clientele skews older (think parents taking their kids out for their birthday, old men doing business). The closest comparison I think of is Scarpetta, which coincidentally was also terrible on service and mediocre on the food. 

One of the immediate things my friend noted was that the wine list had maybe 2-3 wines under $90, and (as the beginning of poor service) they didn't give us the wine list until we asked. The pastas run ~$30-50 per dish, which is fine until you realize that they are relatively small and, with exception of the rigatoni, are just mostly tasty because they are 
 rich and heavy on the cream and butter. Nothing creative about textures, flavor or presentation. We shared the eggplant to start (amazing, probably highlight of the show), rigatoni (quite good tbh, but mostly for the pasta and not the sauce) mushroom fettuccine (heavy in a cream sauce), and some non-vegetarian other dishes I didnt try. We had the carrot cake to finish (good, very ginger-y) and the chocolate cake (fine, a little heavy). Wine was fine, and the Parmesan we started off with was also fine. In retrospect, all stuff that a talent home chef could make on their own for a fraction of the price. 

Additionally, waiter we had - don't recall his name, but he was a larger man - was super condescending to us. When we put in the order, he curtly told us that wasn't enough food and made us order another pasta, though in retrospect we didn't need it. THEN, he forgot to put in that extra pasta, and when we asked, he said that he would put it in, but "would take a while to come out because we didn't originally agree on that". Da fuq?? Another server then came by and tried to upsell us on another bottle of wine, and at the end, the waiter brought us the check before asking us if we wanted dessert (which we did!) - assuming we weren't going to spend more money. We spent about ~$100 per person, which isn't chump change by any means, but were treated like we spent $10.

Went in with low expectations only because of the hype. Felt this meal was truly outstanding with very little that could be done to make it any better. The decor and interior are dark, romantic, and classic. It is a little cramped.. but it's NYC so wouldn't have expected any additional table space. Split the rigatoni and veal parmigiana. Both were delicious, prepared perfectly, each bite better than the next. This all went down great with a nice bottle of Cabernet. I get this restaurant is known for its swankiness and difficultly landing a reservation but it really does live up to its word.

Disclaimer: I didn't go through the hassle of making a reservation and waiting eagerly for the meal. In fact, I rolled out of bed on a Sunday with literally no plans on the horizon and somehow rolled into Carbone for a power lunch (a friend found a reservation for four ~2 hours beforehand).

With that said, what a fantastic spot! The experience from beginning to end was great all around, from the service to the recommendations to the pacing of the food. To be fair, any place that starts me off with free mozz and meats and garlic-and-parmesan-topped-bread will have a special place in my heart. 

The servers here do a really great job of being upfront with the portion sizes without making it feel like an upsell. They were very clear on the size of the prawns that came with the entree, recommended a second order of the Spicy Rigatoni (because let's face it, they know that's what you came for).

We ended up getting the Fettuccine con Funghi, 2 orders of Spicy Rigatoni, Lobster (which may have been a special), Grilled Asparagus, Mario's Meatballs, Carrot Cake with Ginger Ice Cream, Chocolate Cherry Cake. The only thing that I wouldn't recommend getting is the lobster, which was nice but nothing to write home about. I could've done with an order of the rigatoni all to myself, but certainly didn't need it by the end of the meal. The carrot cake was excellent, and this is coming from someone who h a t e s carrots. 

All in all, by the time I rolled out of lunch two hours later, I was extremely pleased and ready to go back to bed.

Really great spot! The ambiance is very old New York and the place is cozy and intimate. There aren't a lot of tables. Service was wonderful, food was delicious - the spicy rigatoni, tortellini and coarser salad were outstanding. The mozzarella was the best I have had. They also give a really good bread basket to start and tasty complementary salami (I am pregnant and asked them to cook the salami and they gladly obliged!) 
The chicken main dish was good but not amazing. Next time I will try the Veal Parm and desserts. It's a very expensive spot but food quality (especially the pastas) are well worth it!
Great food and ambience. It lives up to the hype and difficulty getting a reservation.

Old school vibe (they play Frank Sinatra), none of the pretense, great food, cozy ambiance. 

The space is small and tables are spaced very close to each other, so I would recommend for small parties only (2 people). 

Food menu contains some Italian classics and some items you don't find often at other Italian restaurants, like veal parmesan, which is what I ordered - and it was delicious! So are the meatballs. The starter bread, cheese and salami was a wonderful treat! 

Be prepared to pay big bucks here as dishes are about double what you would pay elsewhere. Friendly and professional service. Would definitely recommend Carbone for a special occasion dinner. Do make a reservation!

The best part about Carbone is the little fresh mozz they bring to your table at the beginning of the meal. I would have purchased several pieces to go but our server and no. Apparently they are made to order for the table so someone in the back is just making the most amazing fresh mozz all night. We got the Caesar salad which was just ok. The spicy rigatoni vodka IS as amazing as everyone says it is and the veal parm was great too. I'm just taking away stars because it's so difficult to get into and the prices are ridiculous.

Great Food / Fabulous Customer Experience
Yes, Carbone is expensive... but get over it and treat yourself to something special! This is the place you come when you work so hard and want to reap the reward of your labor. The customer experience makes up for 1000% of the costs. Everything is justified; I promise. You have not been waited on like this before. You feel like you own the table for the whole night. You water is always full, your drink is cold, your food is hot, and the table bread is great. I cannot wait to come back and bring my entire department for our holiday dinner. As someone who's grandparents are Italian immigrants, I give this place my stamp of approval. 
Thank you Carbone for the memorable experience.

Let me keep this short and sweet. Let me start this off by saying the food here is next level and it may ruin your food experience for the rest of your life because no veal parm will ever come close to what carbone serves. The spicy vodka rigatoni is a must order and might make you want to join the Italian mafia ( I'm not saying this place is run by the Italian mafia, but I'm not saying it isn't either). Anyways get the veal parm you'll love it, if you don't you had a horrible childhood that you refuse to acknowledge and it's slowly eating away at you. 
5 stars.

If Nyc nonsense had a face it would be a picture of Carbones staff. The reservation was for 4,5 of us came. They wouldn't give us a chair. We begged. 1 person was standing up the entire time. They didn't care. 1700$ bill. For 1700$ you should be able to sit down. Never again!

Sure it's expensive, hard to get a reservation, and the scene is over the top. Fact is the food here is incredible and there's an awesome vibe to the place that's hard to find in the city. Highly recommend first timers go with a standard order of Caesar salad, spicy rigatoni, and veal parm. Everything is priced to an insane premium, but you should've known that before coming! Have fun and enjoy the delicious food, life's too short to worry about the cost

Finally visited Carbone and we loved it!!! Out of the dishes we ordered, my favorites were the Cesar salad, the spicy rigatoni and the Nutella tiramisu. 
The spicy rigatoni was honestly out of this world and totally worth the hype! The service was also impeccable and the restaurant itself is absolutely adorable and very charming. 
If I'm being picky, I would say that it's very annoying that it's so hard to get a dinner reservation. I was told to make my reservation  30 days in advance and at 10am on the dot! By 10:03am, all of the reservations are gone. Even logging in at exactly 10am, there were no dinner reservations from 7-9pm (ideal dinner time) available so those tables are clearly reserved for people who know someone. I understand they want to keep the restaurant exclusive, but I find that a little snooty and unfair. 
In other reviews, people did complain about the price and the portion size, which I can understand, but again, it's NYC and you're paying for what you get, not just the food. 
All in all i would say I loved our experience and I would definitely go back.
Worth every penny. The truffled corn, the spicy rigatoni, it's all absolutely incredible.

This place was great! The ambience was very old school Italian which is a nice touch and the service was impeccable. I tried to spicy rigatoni dish and it was great-think pasta with a. Spicy vodka sauce. Similarly, the carrot cake was delicious and wouldn't change anything about it. The only thing that would have made my meal much better would be a better glass of wine, I wasn't crazy about my glass as it tasted like the bottle had been open for a few days.

absolutely amazing spot! the atmosphere is fun and energetic, and the food is to DIE for. I had the spicy rigatoni vodka and the veal parm, and it was a dream of a meal. It's extremely hard to get a reservation, but if you are willing to book a few weeks in advance and wait, it's completely worth it.
Gluten free spicy rigatoni is all I have to say. To. Die. For.  service is exceptional, everything is delicious. Will come back as often as I can get a table!

Best meal ever!! From the oysters to the hand made Cesar salad made next to you, spicy vodka rigatoni to the mouth watering veal parm, this place is a must. Honestly the veal parm is the best I've ever had in my life. It's all super pricey for Italian food but well worth it!

It's always such a special experience dining at Carbone! They will welcome you with starters, including Parmesan cheese, bread basket, salami and some cauliflower. The pizza bread is SO GOOD. It's sooooo fluffy it's literally like biting into a pillow!!Cocktails are really nice too, so it really sets the right mood for dinner! 

All the food is super well presented, and all the flavors are impeccable! I especially love the Whole Branzino - it's just so flavorful and tender and so good with the sauces!!! 

Highlight of the night gotta be dessert!! They will show you humongous cakes to choose from, and we ended up getting one slice of each! I thought the ginger ice cream that came with the carrot cake was soooo yummy!! 

I just really recommend Carbone for a special celebration because service is really lovely and they will take very good care of you! AND if you're lucky you might bump into celebrities!! Pharrell was eating here on the same night so it definitely made my day!! I love Carbone!

Carbone is the best restaurant in NYC.

Good luck getting a reservation, and take whatever you can get. If it's 5pm, leave work early. If it's 11pm, don't be discouraged. It's worth every penny and more. I've been twice, and I'm counting the days until my next visit.

Small. Old school. Waiters in tuxes. The menu is gigantic in size but very limited in selection, in the best way.

MUST TRY: Spicy Rigatoni, Veal Parm. Both must be on the table if you want to do Carbone the right way. Scallops were great. Baked Clams were incredible. Get the carrot cake for dessert (and i don't even particularly like carrot cake).

5 stars all the way. Carbone is insane.

This place for me was a little over rated. Had the meatballs and I didn't think they were that great. They need to step it up for meatballs that's a main for most Italian restaurants. The tortellini was my favorite dish. I literally said wow. We had the spicy rigatoni which was very good. Also had the veal parm (not pictured) but very enjoyable. The chocolate cake was delicious. Our service was ok I really wasn't feeling our waiter, something about him turned me off and made me want to get up and leave. I guess he was worried about a table that was a bigger group next to us which shouldn't be like that but hey you made the statement with out saying it. But this was my birthday day dinner and my wife specifically asked for a candle on the cake and they didn't produce and that's sad. Probably won't be back honestly though I don't like to be forgotten about when I'm sitting at a high end restaurant.

If you like rubbing shoulders with amazing people and Italian food is your thing. Go no further, you've hit the mother load. Love this place more every time I go. Getting a reservation isn't easy but none of the places worth going ever are.

Amazing business lunch at Carbone today. There may have been movie headliners in the room, but the pasta was the real star of the show.

The meatballs have a ton of flavor, one per person is a generous portion.

The spicy rigatone is everything pasta should be--spicy, al dente, easy the decipher, explosively flavor, simple and deeply detailed.

The tortellini al ragu is another amazing dish. If the rigatone is the straight punch to the temple, this would be the right hook to the jaw.

I would skip the Dover sole next time and get another pasta. 

This may be the best Italian food outside of Italy and Grannies kitchen.

We had a wonderful time! We celebrated my birthday night here & everything from start to finish was perfect! 
We can't wait to come back and enjoy more of the menu!

We enjoyed the tortellini and rigatoni- yum! We can't wait to try the lasagna when we come back with a bigger group- it was just the 2 of us. 

The staff was so friendly. We arrived early and enjoyed a martini at the bar so we got to relax and take in the evening- no one rushed us to the table once it was ready- once again it was a perfect night! 
The chocolate cake was delicious also & the staff had no problem with my husbands request of putting candles on top & having everyone sing happy birthday- such a special night! 
Thank you for a great birthday celebration!

Carbone definitely lived up to the hype. Ambiance and service were excellent.

The food was very good, but I'm aligned with other reviews that you can find the same food in NYC for less $$. 

We ordered the spicy rigatoni, broccoli rabe, clam linguini, meatballs, and carrot cake. Spicy rig (not actually spicy) and carrot cake are definitely must-gets. The linguini and broccoli rabe were good, but not great. The clam linguini was very spicy (you could see the cayenne pepper flakes), which surprised us.

The meatballs, however, I could not even eat, hence the 4 stars. When I cut mine in half, the center was so purple it was rare- practically bleeding! I regret not taking a picture for you. I sent them back and told the waitress they were wayyyyy under cooked. She came back and said that that's how they are served, which is "medium", but mine were definitely "rare". Personally, I've never eaten a meatball that's not cooked entirely through, so I'm not sure why they didn't caveat that when we ordered. Nonetheless, they were very gracious and took it off the bill with no hesitation. It's a shame because I was most excited for the rig and meatballs since that's what everyone seems to get, but there's no way I would ever eat a meatball that was purple inside.

With that being said, I would definitely dine at Carbone again as the A+ service and atmosphere make it a NY staple and great spot. Next time, I'll steer clear of the meatballs.

Don't get me wrong... Carbone was great and definitely a place that I think everyone should try once.. but I do sort of think it was overhyped, and not totally worth the price, which is why I'm not giving it 5 stars. We split everything - a cesar salad, the baked clams, the spicy rigatoni, tortellini, and veal parm. The pasta was INCREDIBLE - some of the best I've ever had. Everything else though was mediocre. The cesar was fine, the clams weren't great, and the veal wasn't anything that blew my mind.  We also got 2 bottles of wine and with all of that the bill was $400. I'm so glad I tried Carbone, but I think I'm good for a 1 and done.

The food is undeniably very, very good. The welcome and the service were outstanding. The reservation staff, the hostess, the runners, the bussers and especially the friendly lady explaining the food and taking our order were absolutely fantastic. Warm, attentive and professional without being pretentious or intimidating. Carbone certainly offers a unique NYC experience and I am happy to have been able to enjoy a lunch there. 

Though none of that, apparently, was nearly as good as the marketing staff or whoever is responsible for turning this into a "velvet rope" restaurant. Because despite the quality of food and service, the prices were so over the top ridiculous I don't think this lived up to the hype. How could it? Obviously one expects to spend a lot when going to Carbone. But this exceeded expectations, and not in a good way. Noticing and feeling the astronomical cost are inescapable. 

The food was very good; it was not "to die for". And at $39 for lobster ravioli and $7 - SEVEN! - for an iced tea, well...

Spicy Rigatoni Vodka: was my friend's order and not generally my thing but there wasn't so much spice and aside from the obvious freshness, I didn't see reason for the hubbub. 

Lobster Ravioli: excellent flavor 

Meatballs: Three large meatballs which tasted great but for $27? Also, I'll agree with other reviews stating these were not cooked enough. 

Carrot Cake: The bomb dot com and dot net. Great, great, great. But, you know, $18.

The fresh mozzarella given to the table was wonderful. Wish it were available for order. 

Overall a very nice place with terrific staff. Truly.  I suppose if you have opportunity it's worth a trip. I suppose. But very confidently I say there are far better options out there which would enable you to maximize quality and value.
Strongly recommend!!! Spicy vodka rigatoni was so so tasty, probably one of the best pasta places I've ever been. But don't order the beets salad, too salty

I have heard from several different people that Carbone is a must go to so I had to try it. I ended up coming here for my birthday and it definitely lived up to the hype. We ordered the burrata to start, then shared the Veal Parm and Spicy Rigatoni as our entrees. This is undeniably the best Veal Parm I have ever had. It was mouthwatering from start to end. If you don't get this when you go, you are doing it wrong! We got the cheesecake for dessert which was also amazing. The menu is pricey so I would recommend coming here for a special occasion but SO worth it. I will 100% be back!!! Thank you for a great birthday!!

Worth the hype! The spicy rigatoni vodka was SO delicious. We went for lunch, and split the meatballs and each got a pasta dish. The meatballs are served very soft and less cooked than I've ever had one, but they told us they were safe to eat. They are made with a salt cured sausage which makes it look more raw than cooked. ‍ They also serves ya garlic bread, mozzarella and salami to start, which was all so good. Then they gave us a few rainbow cookies for dessert. Our waiter was very nice and very knowledgeable about the menu. He gave us great suggestions as well. I would totally go back if I ever can get a reservation again.

I'm very surprised that so many people give this place 5 stars. The spicy rigatoni was simply mediocre. A glorified vodka sauce with crushed red peppers. The tortellini however, was outstanding.
Veal parm was enough for two to share and was very good, def not the best I had (chef volas in AC NJ is 100% better).
Nutella tiramisu was great but the Lady finger that sat on top was the best part.
Service was great. Espresso martini($20each) was delish.
I definitely would not rush back. Glad I tried it, but the entire experience was mediocre at best. Very expensive for average food...

It was good. Expected more with how crazy hard it is to get a reservation. Staff were great,friendly, welcoming. Just wasn't totally blown away with the food. Everyone raves about the spicy rigatoni... we got it.. it was good. Its vodka sauce with a hint of red pepper. Honestly mines better .The tortellini very very good.it had a Bolognese sauce that was delicious . We also had the claim to fame Veal parm . Again, it was good but I've had better. For the price and haste of getting reservation I would not go back. There's a zillion places in NY that's are just as good if not better

Carbone is both very good and very over-hyped. I highly recommend you come in a group since the portions are large and you will want to try multiple things!

I came for lunch on a Sunday in a party of 5. You start with complimentary garlic bread, mozzarella, and salami. This bread is amazing - if it wasn't free I would absolutely pay for it. Next we shared the beef carpaccio and baked clams; both were good but skippable. Onto the mains - we had 2 orders of the spicy rigatoni, 1 order of the tortellini, 1 order of the veal parmesan, and 1 order of the meatballs. You can get away with less - we starved ourselves beforehand and finished all of it. The spicy rigatoni was my favorite dish by far, but everything was good. I would only order the veal parmesan if I was in a large group again given its size. We also shared the carrot cake and cheesecake - both delicious!

Carbone is old-school in terms of decor and vibe and the servers wear full suits. Smart casual is the dress code I would aim for. Service was great; the only oversight was that no one offered to take our coats and it was pouring rain out.

The prices unfortunately reflect the hype. $85pp (including tip) without any drinks is on the very high end. Come here for a special occasion or when visitors are in town; otherwise, I echo the other reviews that you can find similarly good Italian food for less.

My husband and I went to Carbone for a "just married" celebration for lunch. 

We had reservations from a month ago and arrived early and were seated when it was our time. The waiter offered us champagne but we said we don't drink so he took our glasses away. It would've been nice if he offered us a sparkling cider or something instead, since we were celebrating an occasion. 

They offered salami and cheese with bread, on the house. We don't eat pork so couldn't eat the salami but did enjoy the cheese. 

I ordered the spicy rigatoni vodka and my husband ordered the ribeye Diana. I would like to note that the ribeye Diana is Creekstone so it IS halal. We also shared a side of potatoes, which were OK. 

The spicy rigatoni vodka was pretty good and flavorful. The ribeye was OK -- I like my steak just with salt and no seasonings, and this was heavily seasoned. But it was a halal steak at a fancy place so I can't really complain as this is a rare find. 

Overall, it was a nice expensive lunch with an old-school ambiance. I would probably go back again to try another type of pasta.
Great service, great food, great atmosphere. Veal Parm and spicy rigatoni are signatures.  Never had a bad meal or bad service here.

Carbone is cool. Great for groups of 4-6. I am not sure it is a five star level as the staff is a hit or mis based on multiple visits. Getting reservations can be a hassle and best for the patient. The Carpaccio Piemontese and Veal Marsala are to die for.

I plan on going again.

This was our choice for dinner the evening after we got engaged. The wait staff was very accommodating and friendly and gave us a bottle of champagne on the house. The food was excellent and the ambience just what we were looking for. After dinner we took a walk by NYU and enjoyed I a cigar. Highly recommend this place for dinner.

No doubt this is a splurge dinner, but well worth it if you're willing to take the calorie and monetary hit. 

I came in a large group so we were able to try a lot. The standouts were the veal Parmesan, spicy rigatoni vodka, truffle fettuccine, steak, and flambé dessert. 

Service is absolutely phenomenal as well. They really take care of you. Carbone is a definite New York must and will satisfy your italian cravings.

Expensive, heavy dinner. Great service and good ambience. We were seated on the earlier side since I made somewhat a last minute reservation. From the moment you are seated, you are attended to and service is phenomenal. From cheese to pasta, there weren't a menu item that we did not enjoy.

I made reservations through the Resy app a month in advance. It's important to note reservations are available a month before your intended date at 10am. If you haven't already downloaded the Resy app and you're serious about making a reservation, you should download it after you read this review. You really are able to reserve a table as soon as the openings are made available and can be added to the waitlist for any desired date and time within the month timeframe. 
The location is beautiful. As soon as you walk in you feel like you're taken back to the time of Frank Sinatra, and yes his song was playing when we arrived. The location is warm and their attention to details from the tablecloths to the plates is appreciated. We ordered the baked oysters as an appetizer. It was delicious, there was a selection of different style oysters and it was great as our first plate. Everything is served family style, very important detail. The portion are plentiful, and we found this out when our main entree was served. We ordered the spicy rigatoni with meatballs. Fresh Parmesan grated at the table and a great assortment of bread in the basket. We ordered white wine, and after four glasses we realized we should have just ordered the bottle. I cant remember what wine it was but I'll note it next time. For dessert I had a cappuccino and I wished I had enough room for a dessert because the options looked so good as they served a nearby table. Overall a nice experience for a birthday outing. We did notice our waiter was not as smooth as expected and after speaking to one of the managers who came to just say hello, he shared the waiter had recently begun working at the restaurant, so that def explained it. A nice bonus as we drank our wine we had a couple of boys, the NY Yankees walk past us on their way out. What a night!

This place is absolutely delicious and great! The place was so beautifully decorated and has the best ambience. The service is spectacular and the food was delicious. I would say that my favorite dish was actually the complimentary bread! They give you a basket of very buttered up garlic bread with mozzarella and salami! So much yum. The next best dish for me was the beef carrapacio! You just order this. The veal Parmesan was also very well done and the spicy rigatoni which is the most recommended dish was good and very interesting. Our waiter recommended the squash as a side which was surprisingly very good. The portion of the squash was also huge! Overall I would definitely recommend the beef carrapacio and the squash.

If you are coming for a later seating do not bother showing up early. We arrived at 1:30 for a 2pm resy and were not seated until 2:20. There is no place to sit at the bar - standing room only. My friend was cranky from hunger. Once seated the complimentary bread and burrata were tasty. We started with the Caesar salad which arrived quickly thank goodness. I loved the giant croutons (thou could be more garlicky) and the whole anchovies. We fought for them. Give more anchovies! Out of the pastas and mains we all loved the lobster ravioli which was packed with yummy lobster goodness. It was less ravioli and more lobster just how I like it. The veal parm was tasty too. Don't forget to knaw on the giant bone! The meatballs and famous rigatoni were forgettable. We wrapped up the meal with a tasty carrot cake (still prefer magnolias) and average cheesecake. Order that Caesar and lobster ravioli! Your tummy will thank you but your wallet won't. We paid $290 for 3 with no drinks, but left with a sizable doggie bag. Can't wait to make my coworkers seethe with envy at my lunch tom score!

Went to Carbone last week.  We were lucky to snag a 7:45pm reservation, which we got by stalking cancellations the month before.

The restaurant is very old school New York Italian in every way - decor, waiter dress, ambiance.  The tables are really squished together.  Service was great -- we had a really attentive, personable waiter.

We got a few amuse-bouches to start the meal, as well as a chunk of parmesan and a bread basket with garlic bread, grandma's bread, and sesame bread.  This was a great bread basket.  The restaurant was informed that my dining partner and I do not eat meat, so we were not served the meat-based amuse-bouche, which I thought was a really nice touch.

Additionally, I tried the following dishes:

Angel Hair AOP (3.5/5): A decent take on a classic dish.  There was a small amount of spiciness to the dish, and it wasn't too oily.

Fettuccine con Funghi (4/5): My favorite pasta of the three.  The mushroom was so flavorful and went nicely with a buttery sauce and well-cooked pasta.  I enjoyed this a lot.

Spicy Rigatoni Vodka (2.5/5): I was confused by this dish.  It wasn't spicy, which disappointed me.  It was actually a little on the sweeter side, with some sort of spice I couldn't identify that imparted a very strong flavor.  This pasta didn't do it for me.

Carrot Cake (3/5): This was okay.  The cake was presented interestingly but was a little dry.  It came with a cinnamon ice cream.

Cheesecake (4.5/5): A really nice, classic NYC cheesecake.  The crust was crumbly and buttery as hell, and very tasty.

I had high expectations for Carbone, but I didn't feel like it hit the mark for me.  The food was solid, but I wasn't blown away.  Given how difficult it is to get a reservation, I don't think it would be worth attempting to return anytime soon.

AMAZING. All I need to say. I had no idea what this place was but my bf raves about it and says he comes every time he visits NY. We are coming from SF. We brought a very nice wine and the $85 corkage fee is pretty steep but it beats paying for wine that is overpriced at restaurants and the one we brought we definitely enjoyed. Their wine list is actually great they had wines ranging from $80-$3000 and even a $15000 bottle... I'm no JAY-Z so we passed on that. 

For dinner, we ordered half spicy rigatoni and half tortellini with truffle on top, veal parmigiana, and Gorgonzola salad. I wish we got a full order of the spicy rigatoni because I can't stop craving it. I'd pass on the Gorgonzola salad. Honestly I was so full from the breads they gave us I didn't get to enjoy the veal. Way too much food.

I wanted to love this but I do not think it is worth what is being charged. You start with comp mozzarella, meat plate and garlic bread, which is nice and gives the feeling of an authentic Italian meal. We moved into the spicy rigatoni Alla vodka, which was the best dish with everything the perfect consistency. Then we had the meatballs which were lukewarm and fell apart when you put your fork in it. Lastly we had the veal parm, which was solid but could've been from anywhere. I think maybe I had too high of a bar for Carbone, but you can save time, money and effort and go to another one of the countless Italian restaurants in the city.
This was the best food I've ever eaten. Spicy vodka rigatoni will be something I dream of forever. And best yet, the staff was amazing.

Disappointing for a long-standing "gotta try" in my book. As a Life-long NYer, I gave it a go as a throw back to old school NY italian. Appreciated the ambiance, the lovely staff, and the effort to bring back a taste of old NY. Sadly, all it tasted like was over-priced and over-salted "NY Italian". The bread and the parm to start was the highlight of the meal. The meatballs were tough, the proscuit was real fatty, the veal was over breaded and over fried, and the rigatoni was really just ok. 

What's worse is that in the small dining space, large tables are pushed super close together and I had the distinct pleasure of having your classic NY bro basically laying on my back for the entire meal. Seems that the price tag and the buzz may be attracting a less than ideal clientele...one that thinks every dining room is their own because they have a couple bucks in their pocket. After the wait staff addressed this gentleman once and then I had to ask him again to please stop leaning on me he became rude and abrasive. Not the type of experience I expect to have when throwing down a couple hundred bucks for dinner. 

Do yourself a favor, go buy an awesome bottle of Tuscan red and head up the block to Keste for some pizza instead.
Delicios food, very welcoming environment, friendly staff! Beautiful environment! Eddie is the man there.

I was pleasantly surprised by Carbone. Going in I had mixed expectations. I heard the food was good, but worried it would be a stuffy atmosphere - it was not at all! Yes, it had an old, fancy Italian vibe but the entire staff was incredibly nice and went above and beyond! 

When you sit down, they start you off with a housemade bread bowl, salumi, and pickled (?) cauliflower. We ordered the Caesar salad, spicy rigatoni and a special of linguine with shaved white truffle. It was possibly the best pasta I've ever had. The rigatoni didn't look like much - not even any garnish - but it was AMAZING. For dessert we had the lemon cheesecake, but truthfully wasn't a huge fan. 

It was a wonderful dinner and I'd rush to go back... if I can get a reservation!

Oy, what a terrible reservation process! I make reservations online all the time on all the platforms and I've never had such a frustrating experience. After several emails with their team I finally learned that they have a secret requirement that isn't posted anywhere on their site or in their Resy profile . . . you need to enter your credit card in your Resy account BEFORE you try to pick a time slot. I am posting this so that other Yelpers don't have the same issue.

Best Italian in NYC. Obviously a tough reservation.
Everything is amazing. 
Spicy rigatoni melts in your mouth.
Vibe is cool and lively.

Absolutely DELICIOUS! We came for lunch on a Sunday and we definitely were not disappointed. Our waiter was great! I'm sure for dinner they're stricter with their dress policy but it was casual for lunch. They also gave you the option to check your coats in, if you'd like. We sat by the door and could feel the cold draft every time the door was opened, but we quickly forgot about it once we started eating. For starters, we were given complimentary garlic bread, mozzarella and prosciutto. We ordered the house special salad which was absolutely delicious! We decided to get their famous spicy rigatoni and lobster ravioli and then shared the meatballs. It was tough getting a reservation. I had been trying for the past two months. But with the help of Yelp reviewers, I downloaded the RESY app and was able to be notified when there was an availability. We lucked out on street parking since it was a Sunday. But any other day, expect to pay meter or garage parking. It was definitely a splurge but worth every penny.

Food was a hit or miss, I ordered all pastas on the menu.
Service, the worst I have ever had in my dining experience.

I went yesterday, as a party of 8, and it was my Birthday dinner.

Firstly, the Captain was too pushy. He recommended me to double up on 3 pastas, but I came with the intention to try a portion of each of the pastas on the menu. When I told him this, he was upset and was having an attitude.  I had to argue with him to do this? It is a 'recommendation' for a reason,  I can choose to not follow it at my own risk. He was saying things like 'I don't recommend it, but she still wants it so *shrugs*' loudly - for what? I did not feel like I was the customer.  This spoilt my birthday mood. Thankfully, the sommelier was nice and was very PROFESSIONAL, assisting me in my wine selection.

What you should order:

Starters: Calamari, Mozzarella + Prosciutto, Baked Clams
Pastas: Lobster Ravioli,  Spicy Rigatoni and Vongole
Desserts: Tiramisu, Lemon Cheesecake

Other starters were okay. The rest of the pastas were mediocre; perhaps the captain knew about this and recommended accordingly? - should have told me honestly at the start that the rest were not good, instead of having that attitude of his and being upset. What a joke. 

Overall:
WORST experience service wise, and the food does not make up for it. I expect to be treated like a customer, not a child. I am still amused at how 'professional' the captain is, wow.

From my dining experience; those street food style and michelins, this was the worst service I have ever had in my life. Thanks for leaving such an impression.

Thanks for ruining my birthday mood as well, what a special way to celebrate at a 'high end' place.

IMPOSSIBLE to get a reservation. I have been trying to get a dinner reservation at Carbone for almost a year now (randomly logging onto at 9/10am and seeing if there's any openings) and it's impossible to book a dinner reservation here at a reasonable time (6pm - 8pm dinner).

Thankfully, I called my AMEX concierge and they were able to book a Sunday 5:30PM dinner for 2!

Now I know why it's so hard to get a reservation... if I could, I'd be here once a month!

Complimentary appetizers: Upon seating, we were served with a cold cauliflower marinade, 3 types of bread (tomato paste bread, regular, and garlic bread), a plate of salumi, and also a block of cheese on each of our plate. After eating just these complimentary apps, I was about 1/3 full.

Octopus Pizzaiolo (5): Grilled octopus mixed with peppers. The peppers have been stir fried so they're extremely soft and the entire plate has a tomato-y pepper-y sauce over it. This is one of the BEST grilled octopus we've ever had and the sauce was addictive, not to mention two big pieces of octopus which made us both very happy.

Broccoli Rabe (3): Ordered this as a side dish, and i wish they had cut the broccoli rabe so it wasn't these long broccoli stems. It made it hard to chew and it was a tad too oily for our liking. This was pretty much the only dish we brought home and I had to cut it in half to make it easier to eat.

Linguini Vongole (4.5): Even though I would say Italy's linguini vongole is much better, Carbone has THE BEST linguini vongole i've ever had in New York. Btw -- spaghetti vongole is my favorite pasta dish but most restaurants you go to mixes it with either canned clam or canned clam juice which gives it a pretty disgusting taste. However, at Carbone, it felt so fresh and I really appreciated the amount of clams they gave as well.

Tortellini al Ragu (5): WOW the Ragu. They really need a spaghetti al ragu dish or something since I'm personally not a huge fan of cheese (inside the tortellini), but without a doubt the ragu sauce alone makes this dish a MUST order. The ragu was so comforting and the tortellini was so freshly made. My husband thoroughly enjoyed this dish and finished it within minutes!

Atmosphere (5): Service was amazing, waiter/waitresses were extremely nice and kind. This restaurant has such a vibrant vibe and the atmosphere really makes me feel like I'm sitting in an Italian family's home, enjoying their homecooking.

will come back (when I can get a reservation)!

Wow, what an amazing dinner. I took my boyfriend her for his birthday and we were blown away with how tasty the food was. We ordered the clams as an app and then I had the spicy rigatoni vodka and he had the lobster ravioli. All of it was amazing. When we got to dessert, we couldn't  choose between the chocolate cake and the tiramisu....so we got both . Expensive, but worth it for a special occasion.

After waiting months to get a reservation, my friend & I were finally able to visit this weekend. The restaurant gives off a Italian style old school vibe. Very cute decor. Our waiter was nice and offer suggestions on what to order. We ended up getting the spicy rigatoni & mario meatballs. The food was delicious & the meatballs were enough to share! I absolutely loved the rigatoni as well. Well worth the wait. I do have one compliant though 
It would have been a 5-star experience if we weren't rushed. We barely had time to look at the menu & the complimentary appetizers were almost removed off our table if we didn't stop them. With us being rushed, it did take away from the experience. The menu is also pricey so don't be surprised when the bill comes.

The first time I came here a few years ago.. WOW.  I didn't get all the hype for Italian food, but it somehow was the best I've ever had. 

Fast forward to my birthday dinner tonight. Wow, in a bad way. Every dish was more and more salty than the last. The service wasn't the same. Not bad, but just not the experience you'd typically get at this caliber of a restaurant. I had to skip desert which makes me sad being that I was celebrating my birthday. They did take our concerns into consideration with the check, but I definitely will not return... especially for a special occasion.

It's also quite interesting that everyone gets complimentary rainbow cookies and for a birthday, just the check. Big regrets choosing Carbone for my celebratory dinner.

Five stars for the bread with tomato sauce on it. The food is amazing here. It is not overrated although it is very hard to get a reservation here. Great place for a special occasion. Enjoy the bread. Get the clams casino, pastas, I've heard the salads are very good.

This was one of the best meals I have ever eaten - absolutely worth the price and the reservation a month out. We had the clams, calamari, spicy rigatoni vodka, and veal parm and were incredibly full after (probably could have done without the calamari) but every dish was incredible.

I have been waiting to try this place for years! It definitely met and exceeded my expectations. The spicy vodka sauce is so flavorful that it has different layers and different dimensions thorough every bite. The croutons in the Caesar were phenomenal and cooked to perfection. The truffle pasta was beyond phenomenal. Can't wait to travel to NY or LV to have all of this again. 

Please open a location in Los Angeles! It would be a hit.

Reservations are definitely difficult to come by, but this spot is certainly worth the wait.  It is best for special occasions as the bill will quickly add up.  The veal parm is definitely on the best I've ever had list.  The spicy rigatoni in vodka sauce is a perfect accompaniment to the veal parm and is as good as people say.  The real showstopper is the carrot cake for dessert.  I definitely am looking forward to my next dining experience here.

This is a great restaurant! 

If you are looking for an old school, red sauce experience, look no further. The staff is amazing and super helpful. The space is beautiful and reminiscent of another time, tastefully decorated for the holiday season.

When you sit down, you are greeted with garlic bread, fresh homemade mozzarella cheese and salami. Very fresh and delicious. 

We had:

- Chopped Salad - very good. The waiter brought us extra tomatoes for my daughter.

- Spicy Vodka Sauce - delicious with a small kick

- Veal Parm - delicious and on the bone. It is not pounded within an inch of its life like most places.

- Squash Side Dish - this was amazing. Roasted squash with maple syrup and mascarpone cheese. 

- Carrot Cake/Nutella Tiramisu - could have lived without

The food here is terrific and the service is wonderful. We would definitely come back.

Nice service and cozy interior makes for a good intimate experience. 

My coffee came with sambuca and the starting appetizer was wonderful to satiate our initial hunger. 

Surprised that food felt mediocre. That might be an overstatement as when we were there, our meal was fulfilling and especially their lasagna hit the spot. However, after we left, i found very little to reminisce about the flavor and presentation.

Really good Italian food! Came here on a Sunday afternoon for a 2pm reservation and it was great timing since the restaurant closes for a bit before dinner. 

We had the Caesar salad, spicy rigatoni and lobster ravioli. Salad and rigatoni were delish but I would try something else next time instead of the lobster ravioli.

We also had the carrot cake for dessert which was amazing! 

Definitely a very good Italian restaurant but it's pricey for what it is. There are soo many good Italian spots in the city that are more affordable but this is definitely a place to try!
Seriously worth booking a reservation 30 days in advance! Great meal and great service! The vodka rigatoni is to die for!!!

Giving Carbone 3 stars mainly based on the superior service. Third timing dining at Carbone; each time the food gets worse. Everything was incredibly salty. Much better Italian restaurants in the city.

When is a filleted grilled branzino worth $95?  When is lasagna worth $100?  When is veal parmesan worth $69? Or broccoli rabe at $18.  NEVER.  Carbone is all about the hype and "bragging rights" that you have dined at a top-rated NYC restaurant.  Perhaps this is why the restaurant was packed with NYC Millennials.  With 7 dishes shared among our party of 6, none were delectable, none deserved the high prices or any accolades.  OK, maybe the octopus.  If you are really interested in quality food, do not dine here.  The price gauging is beyond imagination - no wonder they do not advertise costs on their website.  And don't look towards the wait staff for help.  We found our waiter to only suggest the highest cost dishes on the menu.  And do you enjoy wine with your dinner?  There are only a handful that are under $100.  I truly believe the people who dine here and give it high marks have a limited palate and have not idea what fine food is all about.  There are so many more worthy restaurants to pay your check at.

Was there last night. Second time I'd been there. First a few years back, which was pleasant. This, eh, not so much -- waiter was particularly rude, rushing us to order, rushing us to leave. I get it, you need to turn the table over; but the service in general was spotty. Drinks were ordered and forgotten, had to bother for wine list, cocktail list. I dunno. You can tolerate this kind of stuff in a diner or your friend's cousin Gino's restaurant in Staten Island, but when you're paying 400 dollars for a plate of spaghetti, it's like....really? For what it's worth, the veal parmigiana was good.

This is my very favorite restaurant in the city! 
I visit New York City a few times a year and this is always  a spot I visit. It is the best pasta I have ever had and I always make a special trip just for this.

I've settled on a 3-star review because dinner here was... fine, but 2 stars on Yelp says, "Meh. I've experienced better" and that perfectly encapsulates Carbone, especially when you consider the price vs. quality, the ridiculous hype, and the way we stood around, waiting in a tiny space where waiters and bussers were literally pushing past us for 30 minutes before our (10:45pm!) reserved table was ready. I'd really never be interested in going back, to be perfectly blunt. That's not because it's terrible -- it's not. It just has nothing really good going for it.

I lied. I'd go back for their bread bowl. Literally the best thing about my dinner here was the amazing Sicilian-pie-like, extra thick, yet fluffy focaccia topping the bread bowl. It was crisp at the bottom, airy through the middle, and soft to the teeth at the top with a nice slather of flavorful tomato sauce. It was close to perfection, and I was ready to be a very happy eater. 10 out of 10 for this. 100 out of 100, really. Moving on...

I honestly came into this dinner with low expectations due to the trendiness of the place and some mixed reviews I'd read earlier in the day. I didn't choose the restaurant, but was invited to a late dinner because a friend got an incredibly elusive reservation, and I thought I should try it. This low-expectations approach usually ends in a pleasant surprise. Let's see how it went.

So I had some of the meatballs, homemade pepperoni, spicy rigatoni vodka, pork chop & peppers, and veal parmesan, and I'll run through them in order.

The Meatballs:

So these were pretty good, but super salty. I'm not sure why this is the case, but I overcame the salt by putting pieces of the meatball on a remaining slice of bread (not the focaccia -- I crushed that almost immediately when it came out) from the aforementioned bread bowl. The sauce was flavorful without being overpowering and the meatball was a good consistency -- not quite melt-in-your-mouth level soft, but nice and tender. It was a nice meatball when eating it with the bread; this coming from an Italian guy who grew up on the incomparable "grandma's meatballs." Going well so far.

The Homemade Pepperoni:

This puck of meat...well...it was basically a spicy Slim Jim, but huge. It was pretty gross, spicier than I'd like, and even after the entire meal was over -- three hours later -- I could still taste it in my mouth. It was like burping up a Coney Island hot dog, but ongoing. I only had one little wedge, about a 6th of the thing. Dreadful.

The Spicy Rigatoni Vodka:

This is their famous dish. It was good. I was pleasantly surprised by the notably sweet flavor of the onions in the sauce. It was only mildly spicy, which isn't a ding on the dish. I think the balance of cream to tomato was a bit too far on the creamy side, though. The rigatoni was nicely al dente, but not pretentiously undercooked. A fine dish, though I've had better pasta hundreds of times at various homes and restaurants. This isn't something to make a special trip or suffer an outrageous reservation time slot for.

The Pork Chop & Peppers:

This was a good pork chop. I'm not a pork chop fan, but this was moist, tender, tasty, and cooked to just the right level of doneness. Combined with the generous crown of peppers and onions, it was a pretty complete dish. I would like a little less vinegar and a little more trust in the flavors of the meat and vegetables, though.

The Veal Parmesan:

Odd that they don't write "Parmigiana" on the menu. They really try hard with the Italian terms in other places, but use the borderline annoying "Parmesan" here. It's actually very inconsistent across menu items, and could ue some editing. About the dish, though, it was OK. I like Carbone's tomato sauce -- what little they use on the meatballs and this cutlet. I would like there to be some more of it here. The cutlet itself is very thin and more crispy and dry than thick and juicy, which isn't ideal. Again, it was fine. Oh, but it was also very salty, like the meatballs. I wonder if it's actually the otherwise tasty tomato sauce that's inexpertly oversalted.

There you go. Carbone is alright, but nothing special. All the rigmarole of getting in, combined with its incongruous pricing for what you're getting, earns this joint a pair or three of stars out of 5.
was really good but not quite worth the hype. the complimentary cheese/peppers/olives/meat at the start of the meal was my favorite part.

Carbone's food is amazing but it is clearly impossible to get a reservation here. I have tried numerous times on resy as the clock strikes 10 am and have put in for a reservation but every time I get  denied. It's not fair. They only have 10 reservation spots and they go in seconds. Before resy it was easy to contact them and get a reservation but now it seems like an impossible effort to get a reservation.

SPICY RIGATONI VODKA. Do it! And the garlic bread! Crispy, chewy, garlicky...but not overwhelmingly so. So good! I would have smuggled some out in my purse, but there just weren't any leftover! Love the fresh mozzarella and salami that comes out when you arrive. The meatballs are awesome. Soft, light and perfectly cooked. But seriously the spicy vodka sauce is amazing. Definitely one of my favorite pasta dishes of all time...and that's saying something! Why they haven't bottled it yet is beyond me. There's a slight kick, sweetness from the onions I think, good depth of flavor, and a lovely velvety creaminess over perfectly al dente pasta. Just heavenly. Most of the other dishes I've tried here are good also in general. Though probably more of a 4/5 than 5. I'm seriously giving 5 stars because the vodka sauce and garlic bread are THAT good. 
Other than that, great staff here. Friendly and effecient. Really nice old school Italian homey atmosphere. Also it's REALLY busy here so reservation is a must!

"Carbone"  has been at the top of my "Places to Go" list since I moved to New York about a decade ago. When I finally got a reservation (and the salary to pay for it), I was ecstatic. January 18th, 2020 at 2pm would be one of the top moments of my life - I was sure of it. 

Arrival was as suspected. A snotty, brunette girl (no judgement) welcomed me and then showed me to an overcrowded bar where I waited until my table was ready. 15 minutes later, we were seated in the middle of an cramped booth. It's cool tho, not the first time I felt like a sardine in NYC and someone has to sit there. 

Within the first few minutes, we placed our drink order - delicious 3 ingredient Negronis. We watch the couple next to us get their meal... finish their meal.... get married...have a baby... etc. and still no drink. 25 minutes later, parched and confused, we asked our server for an update on our drink$ just as two Aperol Spritz were set down in front of us. Not ours, but another 15 mins later our drinks arrived just as our spicy rigatoni did as well. Total time = 40 minutes of pure sober sadness. 

This is just a glimpse into our full experience at Carbone. From the mediocre $18 artichoke side that tasted like something from a Whole Foods Buffet to the full on Mafia fight that we witnessed between servers, our experience at Carbone was less than sub-par and to be honest, reminded me of when I used to go to Olive Garden in the 90's with my grandma.

It took us a looong time to get a reservation to Carbone, and when my boyfriend was finally able to make a reservation we were excited to finally experience Carbone.

He also had a very set idea of what he wanted us to share, but we were thrown for a loop when the waiter told us about the specials! (Clams, tuna, and there was something else I can't remember ) 

When you walk in, it's a pretty small spot, and so we had to walk over to the bar, which was small but that's okay. We did keep having to shift as people joined the bar (there is no bar seating)

When we were finally able to sit and order, we decided on the Mario's meatballs, the veal, the tuna, and the Spicy Rigatoni Pasta. 

We started off with complimentary garlic bread and homemade mozzarella cheese and salami

Mario's meatballs were very good. They looked as though they were cooked medium rare as they had a little pink in the middle. 

The spicy rigatoni was by far my favorite. Whatever  type of sauce they were in was delicious!! We wanted to bring a second order home but they have a new rule where you can't take anything to go anymore as there were customers ordering 10+ orders of pastas to go, so they had stopped it. 

By the time the veal came out we were STUFFED! And so that we ended up taking home. 

Def would go back, and would recommend to friends.

I think this place really sucks! The waiters think they are tough guys from a bad Steven Seagal movie. The food is mediocre at best, i actually think Olive Garden is better and the staff aren't 2 bit MMA fighters. The decor is horrendous. It looks like it was last decorated in 1975. The bar has room for literally 3 people, it's like basically drinking in an airplane bathroom.

Made a reservation for Friday lunch about 2 weeks ahead of time without too much difficulty. 

They start with a bunch of complimentary sides like mozzarella cheese, salami, and garlic bread. They were all delicious and definitely worth eating! 

Ordered the clam pasta and the spicy rigatoni vodka. The spicy rigatoni was creamy and delicious. The sauce was really the highlight as it was wonderfully flavorful and every bite was as delightful as the previous one. 

The clam pasta was also delicious. The sauce was drenched in oil so it was really hot. 

For the price, I definitely expected the portion size to be much larger. This place does have quality sauces, but it's on par with other great Italian places in West Village.

To all the Karen's in the reviews complaining about how expensive Carbone is, did you think you were going to Olive Garden? Don't go to Carbone and complain about prices, it's a Michelin Star restaurant and the place is booked solid.

My experience - truly a fantastic restaurant. Service moves a little slow, but I love not being rushed and enjoying the moment. Food was outstanding, Carbone always has great specials to accompany the staple dishes. The drinks are well crafted and have their own Carbone twist. I could single-handily eat the whole bread basket. 

Know what you're getting yourself into, a decadent meal with great service and the price tag to accompany. Do it once! If it's good enough for Drake, it's good enough for you too.

3.5 stars. Service is A+, Food is C+. Carbone is one of those places you want to go to but can't because you can't get a reservation. I had long given up on visiting due to the difficulty of obtaining one but had a friend who desperately wanted to visit so I did what any good foodie friend would do and stalked resy for a reservation. Even with that, the best we could do was a 5:15pm reservation for a Saturday night.

We started with complimentary appetizers of salami, cheese, cauliflower and bread - all of which were nice. Our first dish of the night was the baked clams which I found fishy and underwhelming. I was disappointed as these had been highly raved about. Our next dish was the spicy rigatoni vodka, which was pleasant enough but frankly unmemorable. Last of the savory dishes, we got the shrimp scampi which was good but expensive. The carrot cake was my favorite dish of the evening, and my friend who does not care for it liked it as well.

Carbone is a beautiful restaurant and the service is impeccable. Even though I was not impressed by most of the dishes we got, I think that it is a great restaurant to showcase the New York dining experience. I wouldn't mind coming again for that reason... I just think I would order a bit differently next time.

Everything about this place was exactly what you want in an old school Italian restaurant in NYC. The vibe is amazing. The food is amazing. The staff is amazing. The drinks are amazing. We decided to let the waitress order for us after we picked a few "must haves" from the menu. She did an amazing job with each pasta and main dish! Cannot go wrong with a night at Carbone!

This place is so classy and cute. I love the decor and the maroon tuxedos that the waiters were wearing. Their music was just adorable and I sang "let me tell ya bout the birds and the bees and the flowers and the trees" as our waiter was taking our order. But I digress.

We shared two glasses of Italian wine. While the by the glass price is steep, it is steep anywhere in NYC. 

Let's talk about the heaven that is the fresh bread with mozzarella and meat that they bring out. I could have eaten that all day. I want to go back just for that.

I was so happy to try the baked clams appetizer as we don't have clams casino in Texas and it is so hard to find on the east coast now! I loved their version with uni.

We shared the meatballs and the spicy rigatoni vodka. Everything was as fresh as it could be but the rigatoni was cooked perfect al dente and was absolutely the most perfect pasta dish I have ever eaten, with a definite taste of "spice". 

I would have loved to have ordered more but were getting ready for a large tasting that night so I had to restrain myself. I would love to go back and just pig out with a few more dishes. This place is legit and just so precious. I can see why it's impossible to get a dinner reservation.

Hands down the best Italian food I have ever had!! Every single dish was beyond delicious and exceeded my every expectation! We started with the complimentary bread basket, pickled cauliflower, meat and cheese. The pizza bread was to die for! We ordered a bottle of wine from the very extensive wine list (over 40 pages). The wine sommelier was incredibly knowledgable and full of wonderful recommendations. For food, we ordered the octopus as a starter. The spicy rigatoni and tortellini in ragu are both must try pasta dishes! Most people tend to rave about the spicy rigatoni, but I actually preferred the tortellini... they were very delicate, filled with a fluffy ricotta mixture and served over a gentle meat ragu. For entree, we split the veal parm. I've had a lot of veal parm in my life but nothing like the one at Carbone, which was served perfectly crispy and cheesy. For dessert, the tiramisu is a must! We enjoyed our meal so much and hope to be lucky enough to get a reservation again soon.

Such an incredible dining experience - from customer service, cute décor, to the amazing pasta!  If you haven't, please treat yourself!  (Remember to book weeks in advance as it's always full).

For starters, we were served Parmesan Cheese, Pickled Cauliflower, Salami, and a basket full of different bread - ALL FOR FREE.
We literally devoured everything, esp the pizza bread.

We each had a glass of the Pinot Noir and yes, it was divine and smooth as hell, but super expensive. It was about $23/glass which I thought wasn't really worth the cost... I looked up bottles online and saw that bottles retailed for $30.00 -_-  

Started off with Baked Clams, which you absolutely have to get! The flavors were something out of this world and I def savored every single bite. For entrees, we ordered Spicy Vodka Rigatoni, Lobster Ravioli, and Spicy Meatball.

- Spicy Vodka Rigatoni was SOOO gooood!!!!! It was so simple yet so rich in flavor. I especially loved how the pasta was so chewy.
- Lobster Ravioli reminded me of dumplings full of lobster meat lolllll. It was BOMB.COM. You could literally taste the sea with each bite you take. The sauce was very creamy and rich
- Spicy Meatball wasn't on the menu and I could've honestly gone without. It was $27 for 3 meatballs - which I thought was a little expensive..... I've had better meatballs in other places, so if you aren't too keen, I would pass on that.

After our meal, we were so full that we passed on dessert, but they gave us complimentary bite sized almond cookies which was a perfect way to end our meal.

4 stars because it is a little overpriced for what we actually got... Nonetheless, great food and great great experience!

Great food and service. The burrata and spicy rigatoni were so good. Though the restaurant is great, and no complaints, I think the difficulty to get a reservation is kind of ridiculous. There are so many Italian restaurants just as good, without having the reservation so impossible to get. You're going here because of the name really, and popularity. If you're lucky enough to get a reservation...great, go! But if not, no worries because NYC has a crazy amount of good Italian restaurants.

We went to carbone for a birthday dinner and it was wonderful! The servers were friendly and the food was great! I particularly loved the grandma bread and chunk of Parmesan (complementary), the croutons in the Caesar salad which were surprisingly soft and sweet, the spicy rigatoni vodka pasta and the lemon cheesecake for dessert.

Some of us don't eat pork and there is some in the ragu for the tortellini, so the waiter told us about an off menu pasta dish - ricotta filled tortellini with a truffle cream sauce. It certainly wasn't cheap ($50 up charge for the truffles - omg) but it was delicious. I also can't say enough amazing things about the lemon cheesecake - it was light and fluffy yet impossibly creamy. It tasted like a mix between cheesecake and a lemon bar. I usually hate a non graham cracker crust, but this sugar cookie crust was perfect!

The pasta was of course perfectly al dente. I can see why the vodka pasta is so popular. We also ordered the veal Parmesan which was crispy like viener schnitzel, but I am not a huge fan of meat so this was not something I would order again. 

Although the food was everything we hoped for, Carbone is a pain to get a reservation and the prices are steep so we may not be back for a long time but were both very happy we chose it for a special dinner.

Yes.....my meal was very tasty, and the service was wonderful.  I can find no fault there.  If this is enough for you as a patron then you will enjoy this restaurant very much.

The main reason for my two stars is primarily my table.  I was seated at the last two top along the wall that is near the bar area.  Throughout my entire meal, I was knocked into by servers and bus staff as they walked back and forth continuously by the table. It was beyond maddening.

To add insult to injury, the people at the bar, waiting for their tables, were huddled behind me and over me.  They also were knocking into me, as well as having boisterous conversations right in my ear. All of this made for a very, very unpleasant dining experience.  At this price point, this is just unacceptable.  

And, yes, the stories that you hear about an overinflated menu are absolutely  true.  To give an example, the cheapest bottle of wine on an extensive wine list was roughly $100.  You get the picture.  

And let me not forget that the noise level was off the charts, and the tables were relatively tight. The combination of all of these factors just did not do it for me.

So although I really wanted to like Carbone, it was a FAIL in my opinion.

You Have Been Warned!!

This place is the worst.  Let's start with the reservations procedure.  They go live at 10am 30 days before your desired date.  I tried twice (one for Friday and one for Saturday) and both times being on and ready starting at 9:45, the absolute nanosecond it turned 10am the only available dinner times are 5:00pm, 5:15, 11:00pm, and 11:15pm.  Not one real dinner time slot is available.  After the first failed attempt I gathered several friends and tried the following day and exact same results.  After contacting the restaurant they claim others are just snatching them faster but that's not true as they are never available.   Carbone - very disappointed in your lies.  Be honest and just say normal dinner times are not available to the general public.  Thumbs down.

Been trying to get a dinner reservation for here for quite some time now, but finally settled for an afternoon lunch reservation.

When my boyfriend and I got there, we were seated right away. The waiters were super attentive and friendly. They first came out with a complimentary basket of garlic bread, fresh mozzarella and salami. All super fresh tasting. For our meal we got:

Spicy rigatoni - very good, the pasta was cooked perfectly al dente and had just the right amount of kick to it. 

Lobster ravioli - this was only okay, reminded me more of a lobster dumpling, wouldn't get this again

Famous meatballs - three big sized meatballs, best I've had. Would come back for that alone.

Very expensive place, so definitely worth going to celebrate a special occasion, not an every day thing for sure but SO WORTH IT! We'll be back to try the other choices on the menu!!

After spending months trying to make a dinner reservation, "We open our reservations up 30 days in advance at 10am online only.
