We do not take reservations via email," we decided to settle for lunch one Saturday afternoon. Upon arrival, we were seated immediately. All the waiters and waitresses were very friendly and quick to take our orders. With our water, they brought out two delicious pieces of garlic bread, fresh mozzarella, and salami. All delicious! For entrées, we went with their famous spicy rigatoni, lobster raviolis, and meatballs. Everything was absolutely delicious! For the spicy rigatoni, I was expecting a difference spice/kick. Not to downgrade the dish, but the sauce tasted a little like buffalo sauce...but could've just been me. The meatballs were the best I've every had hands down! With our check, they also brought out two rainbow cookies which was nice of them. My favorite! Really enjoyed hearing Frank Sinatra and the rest of the Rat Pack playing in the background! We'll probably be back only if we can secure a dinner reservation...which seems closed to the general public.

Find a better Italian place in the city.  The atmosphere is phenomenal and the food is A+.  From the starter of salami and cheese and Cali'flour (and bread) to the main course it's amazing.  The house salad is different and has a very nice crunch to it...the spicy rigatoni is to die for.  The veal marsala is the best I've ever had (it's pricy but worth it).  Not too many places are truly 5 stars but this is one of them.

Highly recommend dining here. We were unable to make a reservation by our own, so we asked our credit card company (Amex) to make a reservation for us which worked, but we still had to wait for a month. This restaurant became one of my favorite italian restaurants in NYC.

We ordered;
1. assorted baked clams $25 - 4.5/5
2. Spicy rigatoni vodka $32 - 5/5
3. tortellini al ragu $34 - 4.5/5
4. supertuscan wine that was recommend by a som (Tenuta di Nozzole Il Pareto 2011) $250? - 5/5
5. veal parm $69 - 5/5

This place is great for a small group (maybe less than 4). Price can be pricey, but definitely worth of every penny. The service was immaculate and people who work here really wanted you to feel welcome. I will definitely bring my family/ friends next time!

After months of trying to secure a reservation I finally got the chance to check out this gem of an establishment. The complimentary salami and cheese was soooo tasty! We ordered the spicy rigatoni, veal parm and Madagascar shrimp! Everything was DELICIOUS! The veal parm was not your typical paper thin piece it was perfect! The spicy rigatoni had just the right amount of kick to it! 
For dessert we ordered the blackout Nutella cake, this was nothing to write home about. It was decent! We got complimentary rainbow cakes as well! 
Overall, I am looking forward to coming back!

Yes!!! Worth the hype. The food and atmosphere were great. I celebrated my birthday here and it was just the vibe I was looking for. It was a bit noisy so be prepared if you're into a more subtle experience. I had the lobster ravioli and it was perfect. We also had the spicy rigatoni and the scallops which my guests thoroughly enjoyed. The drinks were strong but not to my liking so I kept it simple and had champagne . The food is pricey so be prepared as most fine dining in nyc.
Excellent pastas , everything else just ok,reservationist at the door and the host and managers have a real arrogance about them , hard to get a reservation so I guess they get away with it

Very surprised people recommend this place. Prepared to be very underwhelmed if you know good food at all. 

The spicy rigatoni was very salty and just not good. The chicken parm was OK - could've gotten this anywhere. Again meatballs were just fine.. the best part was the bread, cheese, and meat at the beginning! 

Honestly do not understand the hype. If you want good Italian then go to the Bronx.  This is not authentic Italian by any means and is completely overpriced based on this alone. If you have ever been to Italy then stay away from this place or prepared to be disappointed!!

Came here for lunch, we had spicy rigatoni vodka, Tortelini al Ragu and meat balls! Absolutely gorgeous pasta and perfect size for two to share. The house made cheese and garlic bread starters are also very delicious.

Tasty, but overpriced if considering food alone

Dining at Carbone is really paying for the whole old timey boujee NY experience that was popular at some point in time--but done in a way that still feels modern and sleek. Thus, you're paying for that atmosphere, that style of service, etc. It is definitely fun, and definitely something that would appeal both locals and tourists. While similar restaurants exist (perhaps 21 Club), their food is no doubt nowhere as tasty. In that respect, Carbone is the best of its category.

The food we ordered in order of how much we enjoyed it:
1. Rigatoni - $32 for 2 half portions
My partner and I both immensely enjoyed the rigatoni, which feels very similar to Marcella Hazan's onion and tomato sauce, just with the addition of heat and cream sauce. Sweet, creamy, spicy, a little rich, yet simple. The noodles were perfectly chewy. We ordered one plate which came split for us. It seems you can maybe order just half a pasta for $16, but I didn't ask. 
Would get again.

2. Meatballs - $27
We ordered the meatballs, which was advertised as a special for that night. They seem to be some sort of fennel sausage meatballs--very meaty, spiced and seasoned all the way through with an obvious fennel taste. Incredibly tasty if you're a fan of fennel sausage, as we both are. The fried basil leaves provided a nice textural and taste counterpart. Are they worth $10 a meatball? Not sure. Were they really tasty? Undeniably. 
Would get again.

3. Free bread and accoutrements - $0
The free bread was my favorite portion of the meal to be honest. All the breads were delicious. Tomato focaccia I could eat every day and be satisfied. The cheesy baguette (?) was very umami-filled and rich. The sesame bread was uninteresting otherwise, but the sesame was incredibly fragrant. The hunk of parm was really good--I've never just sat there and ate a hunk of good quality parm, and this might've been the start of a bad habit. Salami was tasty and nicely fatty tasting. The pickled cauliflower was great if you like sour things. The rosemary was great in it, and the liquid the cauliflower sat in was a good dipping liquid for the sesame bread. 
Definitely would get again.

4. Veal parmesan - $69
I would say the veal parm is up to 10% better than that of Olive Garden's chicken parm. Take from that what you will. It was for sure good and crispy, but at the same time, not all that much better than the standard. The bone it came with we enjoyed more than the parm--the fat on it somehow tasted like a rich and delicious bone marrow. 
Would not get again.

5. Octopus pizzaiolo - $29
Not a pizza or remotely related to a pizza, and seemingly Spanish in influence. The octopus was good, nicely charred and a little crispy on the outside, not tough on the inside. The sauce was a little sweet and a little tart. The onions were nice, but I'm neither a fan of bell peppers nor plain roasted potatoes. My boyfriend enjoyed the bell peppers and potato, but didn't feel it was great compared to the other dishes we had. 
Would not get again.

6. Glass of San Pellegrino - $9 a glass
I've never been charged for just one glass of water before, so I was rather surprised and put off when I saw the bill. They opened a new bottle for us, but promptly whisked it away, to my confusion.
Would definitely not get again

Food can be really good but there is an air about the service and management that is very uncomfortable, they are very busy and don't have any available tables, but soon with this type of attitude things will change

Given the difficulty in trying to make a reservation.

I refuse to only access this restaurants menu via takeout.

So excited that I finally get to try Carbone! Although I never expected that I would have my first carbone experience at home, it happened and it really brightened my day.

I got the spicy rigatoni, meatballs and Caesar salad. All three dishes were amazing. 

Spicy rigatoni has a delicious spicy creamy sauce and its texture is playfully chewy. 

The meatballs are what impressed me the most - the tomato sauce is so delicious and the meatball itself is perfectly cooked - not too meaty or floury. It is also worth mentioning that the meatball are BIG!!

The Caesar salad is exactly the kind of simple, fresh yet flavorful salad that you want to start your meal with. 

Overall it was a successful delivery experience. I am looking forward to dining in Carbone some time in the future

Pro tip to get your food quickly: order EARLY! I ordered at 5pm sharp and got my food in 45 minutes

Overall I felt this was just average for all the hype and the price, but the meatballs are worth trying and the rainbow cookies are some of the best I've had.

I got the spicy rigatoni, the meatballs and the Italian rainbow cookies.

The rigatoni itself was cooked and sauced well, but it wasn't spicy and I felt like I could make it myself. 

The meatballs themselves were rather good. A very nice blend of meat and spice. The sauce added a little bit of sweetness.

The rainbow cookies had a nice sweetness and were moist and delicate.

I'd come back for a work meal, but don't see the hype for what is their most popular dish. Lupa across the street is equally good if you don't want to travel.

Long overdue review of this place. (Wish I was there right now instead of in my small apartment and cooking for myself.)
This is one of the five best Italian restaurants in New York. The entrees are absolutely spectacular. Some are extremely simple and somehow still amazing. You really can't go wrong with anything. 
I judge a restaurant by its worth item, and Carbone really doesn't have anything I can say is "just OK." Been here about five times and I would say I gravitate to Mario's meatballs and the broccoli rabe. 
It's in a prime Manhattan location so I'm guessing they pay a lot in rent and therefore have to hike up the prices a bit. (That's how it works in New York, unfortunately.) Is it worth the price? I would say yes. 
Wish the chef would open another restaurant because I love Dirty French, Santina and his other spots.
Btw, my other favorites Italian spots are Scalini Fedeli, Scarpetta, Marea and L'Artusi.

Going to break it down by each dish that we ordered/complimentary.

1. Complimentary bread: 5/5 Pretty good bread selection they had and they were toasted to perfection. Not burnt or too crispy where it'll skin the entire roof of your mouth. The garlic bread was also to die for and simply chef's kiss.

2. The cheese/meat complimentary dish: 5/5 Pretty good complimentary meats and cheese. Nothing to really talk about.

3. The Spicy Rigatoni: 5/5 Okay now I understand why Drake made a song about this place and why it is one of his favorite dishes. Honestly, the spicy rigatoni was pretty solid and had a nice kick to it. It wasn't too cheesy and wasn't too spicy. The portion was also very good and it was super nice of them to actually split our order into 2 portions. I actually never had rigatoni before so I'm not sure what to expect but I liked it nonetheless.

4. Meatballs: 5/5 YES amazing! The meatballs were probably one of my favorite dishes that I got there. No questions asked. Get it.

5. Lobster Ravioli: 3/5 Not a huge fan of the lobster ravioli although my friend LOVED it. So I guess it's definitely up to the person's taste. The skin of the ravioli was very thin which is what stood out to me the most.

6. Veal Parm: 3/5 I don't really understand this dish and I don't think they flavored it correctly. My friend and I were disappointed with it because it lacked any salt? Not sure if they forgot the salt or it's supposed to taste like that but literally we tasted nothing LOL. 

7. Carrot cake: 5/5 Pretty solid dessert choice and great way to end the dinner. Would highly recommend- the ice cream that they serve it with goes perfectly with the dense cake.

Decided to treat myself during the quarantine so ordered from this well known spot. Food tasted fine but the portion size was a total ripoff. If your actually hungry order elsewhere. Arturo's around the corner is very good.

Quarantine review!

At long last after many unsuccessful attempts to get reservations and one botched visit to the Vegas location, I can say I've tried Carbone. We took advantage of the fact that they're currently offering delivery on Caviar and had a date night in. Apparently the first few nights they've had some kinks (and our delivery guy said he had to wait for quite a while), but it seems to be much smoother now as we actually got our food.

We split the meatballs, spicy rigatoni, and veal parm. While veal parm probably isn't the best choice for a delivery meal (but much better after being zapped in the microwave for a minute), I can't blame that on the restaurant, and the other two dishes were on. Point. Portions were also large enough to have leftovers for the next day.

Can't wait to one day finally try them in person, but for now I've got the next best thing.

Pre-covid experience: We had been waiting for months to eat here. After finally getting a reservation, they did not disappoint! There were generous portions of bread, pickled cauliflower, and Parmesan cheese to start with. We then ordered vegetables and calamari. We had 4 people and split two vodka pastas and they brought it out on 4 different plates. Everyone was kind and helpful. You definitely did not feel rushed. Expensive but well worth it. I definitely recommend splitting everything between multiple people.

Ordered in from here for our anniversary and the portions for two were solid and the whole meal was great, but not "OMG I gotta do this again" great. Like whitewater rafting or visiting Stonehenge, I've done it once and I'm good. 

The best part of the meal were the meatballs - totally exquisite. You must get these. They taste like the ones my Sicilian grandma makes. Sweet tomato sauce with combos of meat in the meatball. 

The spicy rigatoni has such a great kick at the end of each bite and a creamy sauce, but it's not as outstanding as people say. Again, one time and you're good.

The veal Parmesan was so juicy, and even though I'm not into veal, this was a home run to my boyfriend who is obsessed. 

The carrot cake was moist and good but somewhat disappointing - doesn't have that great cream cheese frosting, but more of a ginger flavor instead.

A lot of press about Carbone making deliveries so we tried it trying to support local businesses. This is a total scam. Caviar advertises Carbone's 4 lamb chops as seen in the pic for $50. What you end up getting is a shoe sole half cut double chop at most 50% of what's shown in the description - see attached. I called Carbone's number online to figure out there's no way to get through to Carbone - it's just the conglomerate's number. I contacted Caviar and after a few hours they said contact Carbone. So I'm in this loop now having paid $100 total for one lamb chop entree and one pasta and having to have resorted to eating hot dogs. I'm such a sucker. I have the lamb chop still since it's so tiny and so absurd. It's just sitting in my fridge. Better way is to call restaurants like Palm or Mudville and just order directly so Caviar/Sesmless don't get 30% of these guys' revenues which is just passed to us in cruddy portions etc. Any ideas anyone? Stay safe. Cheers

Carbone may be the most pretentious restaurant I have ever been to. They know their food is delicious, and they do not hold back their ego. When visiting with friends, we ordered the assorted baked clams, spicy rigatoni vodka, lobster ravioli, lemon cheesecake, and tiramisu. After hearing SO many positive reviews about the spicy rigatoni, I had to try it. While it was very rich and flavorful, I actually loved the lobster ravioli so much more. The ravioli was stuffed with generous lobster portions and was the most delicious ravioli I have ever had. The desserts were great as well, but I do have to say that the service was just average. Maybe this was due to them seeing a table filled with younger guests? I am not sure, but I would suggest visiting another place in Manhattan for a more authentic and welcoming Italian experience.

Haven't been out much recently and have always wanted to try Carbone, so we splurged on a quarantined Carbone order-in.  My oh my, I tried so hard to not fall in love, but I haven't stopped thinking about the Spicy Rigatoni and Veal Parmesan since last week.  Absolutely deserving of its Michelin star - Carbone delivers Italian food that is better than any Italian food you've had before - even if it's as basic as vodka-sauced pasta. 
Overall: 4.8 / Food: 4.95 / Service: n/a / Space: n/a / Value: 4.5

SPICY RIGATONI VODKA - ($32) - This was not a close competition -- this (relatively small) bowl of pasta was probably the greatest cooked pasta I have ever eaten.  There was a remarkable chew and texture to this full-bodied rigatoni that I don't think you can find many other places.  The vodka sauce was flavorful, creamy, and perfectly spicy. It was moreso a mac-and-cheese type consistency. Definitely has a little heat, but just enough to really wake up your senses and not overwhelm your mouth.  It was a decadent dish, but towed the line perfectly without being overly heavy.

VEAL PARMESAN - ($69) - First bite I was a little underwhelmed, I had to heat it in the microwave for a minute, but once it was hot again... it was sublime.  It's a big piece of veal.  I mean big -- it's the size of a dinner plate and thicccc.  The veal and breading were cooked in the perfect amount of oil to give it a really rich feel without being drenched.   The little bit of tomato sauce on top was out of this world, and the mozzarel was standard but so delicious on this dish.  I couldn't decide whether my last bite was going to be the spicy rigatoni or the veal -- both were dreamy.  

LEMON CHEESECAKE - ($15) - I'd say this was less of a cheesecake and more of a lemon-bar.  I say that with excitement since lemon-bars are one of the fav desserts -- but definitely all about the lemon custard feel. Absolutely worth ordering, though I would be going back to Carbone for the food.

My biases: I'm a mid-20s male from NYC with a mean sweet tooth, a desire for large amounts of food, and an appreciation for high-quality food experiences - but only at a value.  Food taste is always the priority.

The spicy rigatoni... amazing- people rant and rave about this dish for a reason. If you get the chance to dine at Carbone you need to order this, no questions asked.  Meatballs- great! Service was top notch and very attentive.

So disappointed with Carbone.  Ordered take out for my birthday and could not be more upset. Been to the restaurant which left a good impression so decided to Order delivery and the portion was dismal.  Same pricing as sit down restaurant yet the portion was 2/3 LESS. What happened?   It's pasta and sauce yet it failed so hard. Tasted so-so. Not impressed. Could not have jyped portion size at a worse time. Never again

Guys! don't order from here. Save the 100 dollars on 2 pastas and order somewhere else.

We ordered 3 pastas and the portion they give you is MUCH smaller than in the restaurant. They are ripping you off. I could have combined the 3 pastas and made 1 plate. 

It was also cold. Nothing mind blowing. I know I know - buts it's Carbone. NO ! Don't do it.

It's disturbing how they are taking advantage of people in this time. I made a mistake and I hope you don't. Support other amazing Italian restaurants who can make you the same tortellini.

Just ate roast beef entre which is part of the Mother's Day Menu.  It was absolutely delicious, cooked to perfection.  Ate the broccoli rabe with it.  A most satisfying lunch.  Ate only half of one slice because the portions are huge.  Saving the lasagna, which I know is  wonderful because I have had it before.  Will enjoy it for dinner.  Living in isolation was definitely made more bearable by this thoughtful gift.  Am looking forward to visiting Carbone's when it reopens.  Abbondanza!

I guess one of the perks of COVID-19 was that I finally got to try Carbone. That being said, I will never waste time and energy to get a a reservation here ever again. There are so many Italian places in the city with much better food. 

You can tell the two most popular dishes (rigatoni and meatballs) were not made to order, as soon as I placed my order online, I got a notification within five minutes that it was out for delivery. 

The meatballs were definitely undercooked and mostly composed of fatty meat. I had to cook it more in my kitchen. There was no way I was eating more than one and the only reason I even ate one was because I was hungry!

The spicy rigatoni vodka was mushy, pasta was not al dente as it should be for any pasta. 

Definitely not worth the money. My leftovers are probably going to someone asking for food on the street today.

******BEWARE***** $65 dollars (to-go)for the Spicy Rigatoni & literally 3 meatballs.  Pasta was mushy and COLD!  Meatballs were tasteless!  Definitely, not worth eating here. I placed my order and waited 10 mins for my food outside.  I want to support local businesses, but did I feel like I got robbed!  Shame on you Carbone for serving cold food and trying to pass it off as freshly prepared made-to-order meals. Shame on you for trying to take advantage of customers who are trying to support you during COVID-19. I will tell all my friends and fellow foodies not to eat here. Pass this place, Lupa (Mario Bitali) across the street serves better food!

First let me start off by saying, I can't imagine the challenges the restaurant industry is going through during these unprecedented times.  I sincerely hope they will survive and eventually thrive once the situation gets back to the "new norm".  
I have wanted to try Carbone for many years, but have never been able to get a res, so delivery during quarantine seemed like a good opportunity to try the food.  I understand the experience and food wouldn't be the same as dining in, but we wanted to give it a shot.  
The food was good, not great, and the portions were ridiculously small.  In particular, the pastas were half the size of better Italian restaurants in the city.  The to go dish was only 1/4 full.  This would be ridiculous under any circumstance, but especially for $32 pasta.  I hope our meal was not indicative of Carbone's regular portions and quality.

Are you kidding me? are you really trying to pass off this mediocre american/italian food as gourmet?  The veal parmesan which the waiter swore was heavenly was an ordinary slab of breaded veal bone-in with a mediocre tomato sauce.  Same with the meatballs, left us scratching our heads. There is NOTHING on the menu that you cannot get a pizzeria anywhere in New York. Veal Parm? Meatballs? Rigatoni?? Really this is what you came up with for your menu??? we totally thought it was a joke as if the restaurant owners said "how much are these idiots willing to pay for a meatball parm if we triple the price and call it gourmet?".    Our friend Daniele is from Milan and was anxious to try it out, he said this was typical 'Good Fellas' style new york italian food and I have to admit, absolutely correct no different than the italian restaurants in Little Italy a few blocks away.

We heard so much about this restaurant from colleagues and clients so we had to try it. The reservation was a month out, finally the 7 of us went for dinner and tried almost everything on the menu.  First of all they call it family style,  some plates were not enough for 2 people.  The chairs are so rickety that you feel you're going to fall out, my friend had to ask for a different chair.  The place is so old and stuffy that you feel claustrophobic in there. All of that would be okay if the food was knock out, instead it leaves you wondering what the hype is about? Makes me wonder about the value of Michelin stars...

Judging from the actions of the wait staff, this is clearly a tourist restaurant.  Lots of of visitors and out of towners and couples out for a romantic dinner, so the waiters just push their own agenda and whatever is on the specials list, you can tell their usual clientele has no idea about Italian food.  I've been reading some of the other posts to understand why the reviews were so misleading, it appears that most of the 5 star are from users who rate everything 5 stars and every meal as the greatest thing they've ever eaten.

Unfortunately Carbone is not the greatest I've ever eaten.  But please go decide for yourself.

I wasn't aware that Carbone had a take out service (probably they didn't before Covid) but somehow I was passing by the other day, saw that the restaurant was open and decided to have my forever favorite pasta !!! Everyone was super friendly and the service was amazingly fast! Can't wait to dine at Carbone again when all this is over!

"Omg is that your $28 dollar salad!?" My friend texted back in horror. 

I was so excited for Carbone tonight, and to say it fell flat would be an understatement. High-end restaurant prices are only justified when you're there for the full experience, and a small, sad salad and pasta eaten out of a plastic container ain't it, my friends. Especially when you have to remind the unfriendly host to give you cutlery. 

With so many places struggling right now, I've decided to give my dollar to much more deserving businesses than a snobby, fat cat restaurant group with a superiority complex, going forward. Not all restaurants are worthy of our pity right now. Certainly not carbone. 

If you're considering ordering from here I suggest that you take a hard pass and find one that doesn't exploit their customers.

Ok I really want to support local restaurants so the 32 pasta dish and the 42 shrimp dish was steep but I looked at is as supporting our great restaurants.  The shrimp dish said 2 shrimp so I expected it to be small.  The rigatoni at 32 bucks is one layer of past in one of those small white circular containers so maybe 7 spoonfuls.  My bill was close to $100 after tipping the courier $8....im sorry Carbone I feel serious raped and with corona where everything has been taken away from us we don't need you to take our money.
Do NOT order takeaway from here. The prices are the same but the portions are TINY!!! Not at all worth it.

I don't see and taste this elegance that everyone speaks highly of. 

Spicy Rigatoni? I've had better honestly. In home dining came in plastic containers, no utensils and a paper bag. 

Food was room temperature. I will visit for the restaurant experience to have a second opinion. In the meantime, it's not worth the hype.

COVID-19 Status - Ordered via Caviar for a pick up. 

We got the Rickys favorite (Caesar alla ZZ, Spicy Rigatoni, Mario's meatballs, veal Parmesan and lemon cheesecake), Chicken Massimo, Fettuccine con Funghi and rainbow cookies. This was good enough food for 5 people and costed us around $250.

My favorite was the chicken massimo- it was delicious, nicely flavored. The fettuccine pasta was definitely better than their famous spicy rigatoni. The salad was average and the meatballs and veal Parmesan were good but nothing extraordinary. 

Neither of the dessert- lemon cheesecake and the rainbow cookies were good. I was very disappointed.

Overall, I think it's not worth the price and the hype. It might be better if I dined in but I'm glad I tried it though.

Carbone recently began doing outdoor dining, and I figured this was my chance to get a table with little effort involved. I was right, and snagged a reservation on a Friday night after setting a Resy alert the day before. 

My boyfriend and I arrived and were seated right away. They had hand sanitizer for all the guests, which was a nice touch, as well as a mobile wine list. The tables were distanced (they only had six tables when we went) and separated from the street by lovely planter boxes. 

As for the food, we started with the complimentary bread basket, then shared the prosciutto & mozz, spicy rigatoni vodka and veal parm. The pasta was the best thing we ate, though the prosciutto was also amazing. I'm not usually a veal fan but the parm was fantastic, and we had leftovers. 

Finally, we had the carrot cake for dessert. While it didn't come with the ginger ice cream (maybe they ran out?) I can definitely forgive that, ha. The cake itself was perfect. Complimentary rainbow cookies were good, nothing special. 

I thought the prices were a bit steep, but it was an excellent meal overall. Glad I went!

I always get the spicy rigatoni, meatballs, and tortellini. the beet and caesar salads are soo really tasty. The wine list is also very good. It's been one of my favorite italian restaurants for years and still is.

I ordered the orecchiette and the rigatoni. Basically, $30 each. The orecchiette was flavorful, but very oily. The rigatoni was with a tomato vodka sauce, it had a slight flavor of ? Velvetta cheese??? Not very good.....So, I had it delivered...$20.00.  Now, I am into this dinner for $80.00.  What was delivered was two small/medium bowls of pasta, no bread, no parma (that would have been an extra $3.00), no napkins, no utensils, no nothing. Yep, that's overpriced to me, even for NYC.

Carbone is perhaps the worst tourist trap in New York. The service ranges from clueless to cloying to downright abusive. The "hospitality" extends only to expense accounters, prostitutes and B list celebrities who frequent the place. The food is atrocious and is priced strictly for Saudi Sheikhs, should they be so unfortunate as to wander in. The food, to any actual New Yorker who knows this city's Italian American food traditions is an abortion. The Caesar salad? How bout undressed, luke warm Romaine hearts right out the package with some shredded plastic cheese on top for $25?! So called "spicy rigatone" is something Chef Boy Ar Dee himself might have barfed up except here it'll set ya back $32 for a quarter portion. Are you a real New Yorker who loves the "Chicken Scap" at the great Don Pepe's in Queens where you get a full chicken perfectly butchered and browned, redolent with garlic and herbs that feeds four? Well, order the Chicken Scapariella at Carbone and expect an undercooked slimy, unseasoned chicken thigh, with a slice or two of sausage and watery sauce for over $40. Are you up for the Branzino, plain and burnt for $95? Better be on somebody else's nickel. How bout some bread? Nope. How bout sides? Of course no dishes come with any, they suck and they run $18 and up. 
They say there's a sucker born every minute and who cares about the imbeciles who would frequent a place like this but now that authentic old School great New York Italian American restaurants have been disappearing at a rapid rate, it is sad that Carbone, an EPCOT quality Italian which holds its customers in contempt, and others like it, may be what will replace them.

Never order Carbone online (through Caviar)! Not only did it come 2hours later than scheduled, all the food came very cold, and we had to microwave it ourselves. Also, there was no utensils in the bag. Really disappointed with the meal which also come at a hefty price for the low quality.
A good place but kinda blown up with hype beast kids spending money to post pics with "last table at Carbone calling plays on the rotary p

The takeout (Spicy Rigatoni, Branzino, Veal Parmesan, and Dirty French Rose) was delicious. My only disappointment was that the meal didn't come with bread or napkins. When you're paying a hefty price, the least a restaurant could do is add napkins. But the food itself was wonderful!

I've been to Carbone a few times and have had a really pleasant experience; however, this weekend was different. 

We were seated at a table outside the restaurant on the sidewalk because you're not able to go inside restaurants right now. We're really excited to eat here we love the menu. They have great gluten-free options and the ambiance is really beautiful. 

We order sparkling water and within two minutes, a bird shits on our table. Not they're fault but the reaction was. We ask if they can clean up the table and move us to a new spot but they don't clean up the table and don't have another place for us to sit. We point out an empty table and are told that table was already claimed for a four-person reservation. 

The next thing we know three girls come by, ask for a table, they separate it into two to accommodate three girls and then another two walk-ins next to them.

Mind you, we are still sitting at a table with bird shit on it as well as in my glass. We then again asked to move to another table but are now told that the kitchen is closing and they may not be able to accommodate us.

Still sitting at this bird shit table, we get up and leave

Have had the spicy rigatoni many times, ordered for my birthday. Got two orders and there was a small hint of sauce on them. Nothing compared to how much sauce is usually on top (Considering the only reason people love this dish is because of the sauce). Tried calling, emailing, and have never heard back. It's been 5 days. $60 for dry plain pasta. Thanks.

If you're reading this - don't order their delivery. This reason for this two star review is based on the to-go delivery and the insanely small portions that came with it. 

If you're craving Carbone - go looked up their recipe for the pasta online (it's there) if you don't want to drop a few hundred and ration the food they send you. 

Appreciate the online recipes, my wife can make this better then the doggy bag sized food that was sent to us.

Some of the best Italian food I've had. They start by giving you fresh mozzarella and their garlic bread (btw some of the best garlic bread I've had). We ordered drinks instead of a bottle of wine. It was during the day and I ordered an old fashion and my gf ordered a margarita. Both were great but I loved my gf's margarita. So I had to order a margarita after I finished my drink. On to the food. We got the spicy rigatoni and oh boy was it delicious. Then we got the veal Parmesan and that was also really good, pairs really well with the broccoli rabe. For dessert we went with the carrot cake and that was divine. The cake was just super moist and not too sweet. Glad I went, been meaning to go here for a long time.

Carbone was a pleasant surprise in the midst of a global pandemic where we're all trying to find something close to normal. Given that all New York City restaurants are only allowed to serve food outdoors at the time of our outing, we naturally dined outside. Carbone offers two outdoor dining locations: one, in front of their restaurant on Thompson Street, and the other in front of Sadelle's on West Broadway (Sadelle's is a part of the same food group). We dined outside of Sadelle's and didn't feel like we missed out on anything experience wise. 

Overall, I'd rate it somewhere between a 4 and a 4.5 stars. The food was great (I won't get into individual review of each dish because I think there are more than enough reviews of the same dishes). I also was very fond of the complimentary appetizers. Great ambiance and just enough space between tables to feel properly socially distanced. 

The only reason it loses a half to a whole star is because of the price. While the food is good, it definitely should not cost this much. I've had amazing food in Rome, so good that it made us come back the next day (Mimi e Coco Trastevere), and it cost a fourth of the price. I didn't get the same feeling of wanting to come back as soon as possible with Carbone.

Rip off! Spent $110.00 and received half portions of mediocre cold food. They should be ashamed of themselves I can get better quality Italian food at numerous places on Arthur Ave for half the price. What a joke!

Came here with friends to enjoy the outdoor dining setup and loved it. We had the spicy rigatoni (just a light kick), caprese salad (the tomatoes were amazing), tuna, carrot cake, and drinks. Everything we got was great, and the staff was even better -- kind, cheerful, and super welcoming. Thank you for serving us and showing us a nice night during this crazy time.

Off the bat, yes it is pricey. But also in my opinion many things there are worth it. The spicy rigatoni is pricy and the portion is relatively small, but I just have not experienced a better pasta in the city. It is rich, it is fresh, it is flavorful, and pairing every bite with a bit of the homemade meatballs and fresh focaccia is just heaven in a bite. I honestly have not been able to beat it and therefore it deserves a premium from me. The lamb was also phenomenal. Perfectly cooked with three delicious dipping sauces (the roasted pepper was my favorite). Now you can debate whether that is worth the $100 price tag. Similarly, the wine was very enjoyable, but again you can debate the price tag. If it wasn't uncouth I'd order three orders of the rigatoni, an order of the meatballs and as much of their homemade bread as they're comfortable giving me, and I would eat until my heart gave out. So for that, you get 5 stars because I can't say there are many things I'd be willing to eat myself to death over.
Not worth the hype! Had better pasta elsewhere and you are better off eating at a different Italian restaurant with better portions for the price.

Truly a delectable experience. I thoroughly enjoyed every aspect of my meal. The bread and cheese were simple and divine, my Rigatoni was the best I have ever had. I am counting down the days to go back and share this meal with my loved ones. A true delight!

Superior service and even better food. I've always wanted to try this place and I'm so glad I was finally able to. You can make reservations by calling two days in advance. They have hand sanitizer available at each table and outdoor seating. The staff is very nice and knowledgeable about their wine selection and food. I appreciated their suggestions as they were thoughtful. Even in the rain, staff was very accommodating bringing umbrellas. I actually didn't mind at all. The food speaks for itself but even during covid, this is a place I'd revisit.

Great service, amazing food! 
Came here for a date and very happy with my food selections. I had a house salad and the spicy rigatoni vodka. Does not disappoint and lives up to the hype!  Must make reservations. Rigatoni Vodka

Carbone being a NYC staple was extremely disappointing. The take out I received was just sad ! For 36.00 dish of cold pasta, no grated cheese included with delivery and the finest portion I've ever seen. Carbone, I used to love you, please step it up.
Very solid and the food was all excellent but quite a limited menu. I'm not sure if that has to do with Covid or if it just is always like that

We went for our 40th wedding celebration. Three people had told the restaurant that it was our anniversary. We never had any acknowledgment on the day, not even a candle let alone a glass of champagne. Don't ask on the reservation if this is a special occasion because you will get ZERO.

We did take out delivery from carbone, just decided to treat ourselves! 

We did the special dinner for 2::: came with Cesar salad, vodka pasta, meatballs, veal parm, lemon cheese cake. 

The portion definitely feeds two, but the value is so so. My favorite part of the meal was the VODKA PASTA: it just really hit the spot, in flavor and pasta texture. The MEATbALLS had super on point flavors, and mix of lean and fat meat - probably more fat hahaha making it so dark tasty!!!!!!!!!! Like mouthwatering tasty. And the LEMON CHEESECAKE - was nice and tart, perfect texture of cream cheese cake, and the cookie crust was perfect texture and amount of sweetness to satisfy any sweet tooth

I truly couldn't have better things to say about Carbone. I have been trying to come here for 3 years and have never been able to get a reservation. I typically find that the places that are the hardest to get into are typically overpriced with rude service. This is one of the rare places that is actually worth the $$. Between the complimentary appetizers and the friendly servers (Jared and Tom) I couldn't recommend this place more. 5/5 and i would run (not walk) here!!
Delivery ord. House chopped salad, meatballs and spicy rigatoni. I do NOT recommend the salad. Wilted, old greens are not worth $22. Meatballs and rigatoni were great.

So it's day two of my Labor Day weekend trek into the city. I'm still out with Jimz, his girl Born After Cool Runnings, and her coupled up friends H and Dimz. Cool had been talking rave reviews about this place and how hard it was to obtain a reservation. I knew it probably had to be special. She gets alerts to her phone and we were able to get a table for 5 during COVID outdoor dining. We got there nice and early at 1130 for our lunch. Seated promptly. Instead of just bread, they gave out garlic bread, fresh mozzarella, and salami. Holy crap. This was AMAZING. I'd order a bottle of wine and sit there eating that all day if they'd let me. The salami was great flavor and thinly sliced. The bread had great crunch but had a softness to it, as well. Amazing garlic flavor to it. The mozzarella though was the key. It was a touch warm with some garlic to it. It was so soft and stretchy. Just amazing. A caveat about the menu was that the specials are only for dinner so unfortunately, we didn't get to try the lasagna. We ordered all the pastas for the table. The orecchiette I thought was okay. Not my favorite. I thought the flavor profile with the vegetables was simple, which I liked but the pasta itself could've been cooked just a touch longer. I liked the spicy rigatoni. It gave just a touch of heat that wasn't overwhelming. My favorites though were the meatball and the fettuccini funghi. The meat ball was so tender but was able to keep it's shape well. The marinara that covered it was so flavorful with basil and tomato flavor. The fettuccini was my absolute favorite though. Just wow. The noodles were so thin and soft. The sauce was so light. I don't even like mushrooms, and I still ate these. My favorite dish. The dessert was bomb too. The carrot cake had a great presentation. It was moist and wasn't covered in icing...just the perfect amount. The lemon cheesecake was just wow. Super soft cheesecake that wasn't too dense and had some give. The layer of lemon on top added a perfect amount of acidity. There was a raspberry compote that gave it sweetness and tartness. The crust was nice and thick on the bottom. 

Overall, if you can get a reservation, I'd go for it.

Had spicy rigatoni, octopus, lobster ravioli and the veal parm and everything was absolutely amazing. Wine was great as well. Only thing I didn't love was a martini (dirty / vodka) but it was off the menu and I was already drunk when I had it so it just wasn't needed. Amazing serious

Carbone is using Resy to book and it's extremely difficult. Despite the good food, this booking process is unorganized and times come and go in a weird fashion. It shouldn't be a lottery pick or luck of the draw to get a reservation at a decent italian restaurant. 

It states that reservations open 2 days in advance and it seems like that's false. I've been constantly checking the app to see when reservations open up and it's not 2 days/48 hours in advance. Carbone should be more transparent and let people know exact times when bookings open. Definitely not a returning customer until they get their act together

Just had the most fantastic night! Ricky and Tony were absolute rockstars.  I was frightened to try the spicy rigatoni thinking it was a catering hall entree gone wrong but it was outstanding.  Drinks were spot on.  Chicken was everything you hope it would be....moist, slightly fun, and crispy.  Finished with their yummy rainbow cookies and a slice of carrot cake.  Wether it was planned or not the serenade by  @howdoyouspellmark was the icing on the cake.

The service was incredible and I love that you get shared plates and they plate them for each person. I had told the host that we were actually suppose to get married yesterday but due to COVID we had to cancel our wedding, and they brought us over complimentary drinks to celebrate. The spicy rigatoni is a must.

The short: excited that some NYC institutions, like Carbone, have figured out ways to open safely during Covid-19. We sat outside of Sadelle's in the street seating. Food was very good. Tables are a little close, but it's overall a nice setup. 

The longer: made a late Resy for a weeknight dinner. We shared a bottle of Sancerre, enjoyed the complimentary bread, cheese and meat-- and then ordered a full meal. 

We shared a Caesar salad, meatball, spicy rigatoni (obv), veal Parmesan & truffle corn -- which our waiter said was a must-not-miss. 

The meatballs and rigatoni were very good. I would skip the veal and the corn next time. The waiter also over-poured the wine, so it was warm towards the end of the meal. 

I wouldn't rush back here - but am very glad to have checked this off the NYC bucket list.

I was finally able to get a reservation to this place during COVID. They had a decent set up for outdoor seating, and the service was fantastic. They also had a nice wine selection. We had-
1. The complimentary bread basket had a nice variety of different types of breads, and the meat and cheese that it came with was a nice touch.
2. I was so excited to try the infamous spicy rigatoni, and while it was definitely really good, I had higher expectations based on how hyped up it is. If it's your first time I'd still recommend it though! 
3. The lemon cheesecake was really good, perfect amount of punch from the lemon without it being overpowering 

I would definitely come back and try other things on the menu! 

Also JLO and Arod stopped by so that was cool

Exceptional service, our waiter was CJ who couldn't have been nicer & gave great recommendations. He went out of his to help you and accommodate you anyway he could which is a rarity.  The food was out of this world, you could tell it was high quality & fresh. Nice strong drinks, overall just a great experience and a fun place to people watch! Can't wait to go back! 
Side note: the meatballs are a must, same with the spicy rigatoni and the lemon cheesecake is amazing!

Oh spicy rigatoni... so good, did not disappoint. The texture of the pasta was perfection, the sauce was sweet, salty, acidic, and spicy in all the best ways!
Let's start from the beginning, we did indoor dining at the west broadway location. I thought the seating was well spaced for indoors.
I thought the service was great except for the fact the fact that our main server was a little cold. He also only looked at my bf when he talked to us which I thought was so weird but anyways, everyone that helped serve us was overall very nice and attentive. I just asked my bf if he thought the server looked at him the whole time and he confirmed and added "can you blame him, have you seen my hot body" lol!

1. Spicy rigatoni- must get this 5/5
There were only three pastas available and the other two did not sound great, they didn't have any of the raviolis on the menu which made me sad but at least the rigatoni delivered.
2. Meatballs - my bf fave dish 5/5
3. Tuna Appetizer - 4.5/5 
4. Mushroom medley side 4.5/5
5. Veal parmigiana- 4.5/5 it's the best version of this you would expect and the meat on the bone was fantastic
6. Carrot cake- 4/5 good, not phenomenal by any means but not bad either 
7. Every white wine that I tried by the glass was so amazing, kudos to whoever picked out their wines they are insanely good! 5/5. I would say skip the rose here was not my favorite
8. I got the earl grey tea after dinner which was definitely well sourced. I might find the brand and buy some myself

In conclusion this place was really very good. I took off a star because:
1. I thought it was overpriced for what it was, our bill for two was $500 and I think given everything we ordered I was expecting it to come out closer to $350-400. We did get some free apps included but outside of the bread basket I felt that they were lacking in this from previous. I wish they were still doing the mozzarella in olive oil.
2. Service - see above
3. I know we are in Covid but can we please have 1 ravioli on the menu for dinner?? I was seriously really excited to try them. And we came for Saturday night dinner so it's not like it was weekday lunchtime or anything. Also the online menu for October showed 5 pasta dishes including both raviolis which is not the same menu that we were presented when we got there with only 3 pasta dishes. Lamesauce.

Ultimately I say go, it's a lot easier to get reservations right now through Resy. Food and wine is great, just go with the expectation of a larger bill than what you were expecting. Cheers!

Amazing food, great outdoor space, and wonderful service from our waiter Luis. He was knowledgeable about the wine menu, suggested food, and boy were we happy we listened! What a lovely place, definitely a great date spot.

Wonderful as expected. Was a bit disappointed to have to be seated at the W. Broadway location... but the great men who serviced us made up for it. Beautiful anniversary dinner, wouldn't have gone any where else. Thank you.

We had a great experience during Covid. I am convinced the only way to get a table at Carbone is if you set up Resy notifications. So my two other friends and I made it our mission to get a reservation one week. Their system is strange in that you can reserve a table and then after the cancellation period is over, they notify you of which location. Kind of sketchy to me. We were notified that we would be seated at their second location on West Broadway which we are not crazy about. But I emailed the restaurant and they agreed to switch us to their location on Thompson Street. Bread basket, cauliflower, salami, cheese, all complimentary appetizers to begin. We got a bottle of Staforte ($79) and the best way to describe it was "exciting." We all loved it. The sommelier actually poured some wine right onto our bread basket and missed my glass...lol. We got spicy vodka rigatoni (obv), mushroom fettuccine, meatballs, and broccoli rabe. I loved the meatballs and the spicy rigatoni. I could have done without the fettuccine pasta. Service was top notch. The bill for our meal was $270 or so with tip. (2 pasta dishes, 1 side veggie, and meatballs, and bottle of wine.)

I'm so glad Carbone is still operating during Covid. There was hand sanitizer on every table and all staff was wearing masks. They did have some indoor seating, but we decided to eat outside. 

They have a great wine list here. I got a glass of the Yantra, which paired well with my meal. 
To start, they brought out the most wonderful complimentary bread basket I've ever gotten at a restaurant. This bread basket had sourdough, garlic bread, and a bread with a tomato sauce on it. My favorite was the garlic bread! Along with the bread basket came pickled cauliflower, cheese and salami. The pickled cauliflower paired with the bread was great. As an appetizer we ordered the eggplant and zucchini scapece...wow! This simplistic dish was packed with flavor. It came with cheese on top (I think burrata), and it was just so perfectly cooked. My husband who is a major meat eater loved it too. For my entree I got the spicy rigatoni vodka (of course!!). I'm pretty sure this is the best pasta I've ever had. Noodles were cooked perfectly, and sauce was so fresh tasting! Also, the portion of sauce to noodles couldn't have been more on point. My only regret here was that we were too full to order dessert. We may have to chill on eating the bread next time and save room for dessert!

Came here before COVID happened for a late dinner reservation but was able to get a normal time reservation with their outdoor dining recently for a quick birthday lunch.

To start, my friends and I ordered whiskey sours and caprese salad. Drinks were great and the caprese salad was pretty good. 

We weren't too hungry so we did not go with the veal parmesan but that is one of the best dishes at Carbone. We did order the spicy rigatoni vodka (another one of their best dishes) and Mario's Meatballs. The rigatoni was amazing both in terms of sauce and pasta consistency/"chew". Meatballs were pretty good. 

To finish, we ordered the carrot cake. Cake was pretty good but not the highlight of the restaurant.

All in all, Carbone is a great Italian classic to check out. Rating 4 instead of 5 stars because I wish the menu had just a little more options. I feel like I'm looking forward to coming here another time but only if I was in the mood for spicy rigatoni vodka and veal parmesan.

Old school joint. White table cloths. They bring cured meat and awesome bread to your table at the start but good luck getting more bread to go with your second course in a timely manner. Over rated. Over hyped. Better pastas at better prices all over the city. Meatballs are fantastic, but I don't feel I need to come back here unless someone else is paying.

The spicy vodka rigatoni pasta is my favorite pasta I've ever had and I can always repeat eat it 

Veal Marsala also incredible 

Service spectacular 

Bread and cheese appetizers (complimentary) are amazing. I think they give you different amounts based on how much you order

Overall can't wait to eat here again if only it was easier to get a reservation.

A NY classic spot. The veal parmesan and the spicy rigatoni was delicious! I would highly recommend the two to be shared together for a full meal. The caesar salad was a good appetizer. Overall, a great birthday dinner.
Food is good. Overpriced even for a Michelin one star. There is a 10% COVID surcharge added to your bill so you will ended up paying food + 30%.

Meh! I have eaten at their Vegas location several times and loved it so when I was invited to dine at the one near me I jumped at the invite. Upon walking in the restaurant it reeked of cheap cleaner and dirty mop stank! Totally turned me off!!!  We sat in the back room in a tucked away table which was great until the waiter SAT AT OUR TABLE as if it was Outback Steakhouse! What the hell?!?!? I first thought it just us but we watched him also sit with other customers while taking their orders....strange. The food was ok.....just ok. The atmosphere flat, the smell still lingering in the background as I ate my food. 
So many better restaurants in our beautiful city so go elsewhere because you aren't missing anything but the name!

Ate here for my birthday with two girlfriends. Food was great as always. I understand it is hard with COVID, but we did wait to sit outside for about 15 mins past our reservation (that was made for outside) with not much of an apology. The waiter was also not very friendly and quite rude when we asked to order an extra plate of pasta at the end (apparently the kitchen was closed but we had no warning of same). Not the service I would expect with a Michelin star.

I am not an Italian food lover but this place blew me away. We got all the main dishes, with the star being the spicy rigatoni. The veal Parmesan is something I would get again too. Make sure you don't get too full off the complimentary bread and cheese! That's a meal in itself, but so good you might not be able to help it. Come hungry and ready to unbutton your pants afterwards, from the tummy expansion lol

I'm glad I went here. It was definitely worth the $ and experience. For apps we got the octopus and tuna. I'm sure people have tried octopus at other restaurants but Carbone takes it to another level. The tuna...wow. It was melt in my mouth sashimi.
For our mains we got the spicy rigatoni vodka and tortellini  ragu. Spicy rigatoni did not disappoint. Perfect in texture and sauce. The tortellini ragu was prob the best ragu I've had. Finally, the service is top in their class. This is one of the best date nights we've had.

Carbone is a New York bucket list place and always booked but we were able to get an indoor dinner reservation during COVID. we sat inside at Sadelles, another Major Food Group location. We ordered the famous spicy rigatoni, a prosciutto and mozzarella starter, meatballs, and the Carbone classic- Veal Parmesan. They were all fantastic. Some people say the rigatoni here is overhyped but I was very impressed. The front door was open the whole night which did make it chilly but just make sure you have a coat. Servers were friendly and efficient. My only regret was I wish I had saved room for dessert!

I have ordered take out twice and let me just say the portions are 1/2 the size as pre-covid in person. Aside from that the food is always Luke warm when we pick it up even though we set a pick up time to ensure its hot. They refuse to give you their free bread on take out orders yet are charging the same prices and 1/2 the portion as in person. Not to mention the carrot cake was also 1/2 the size as in person. As we all know these orders for take out are around $200 And up so is it worth it to order take out? NO!!! We're are incredibly disappointed with the lack of customer service as we brought this to their attention twice and they offered nothing. Also if you want to go in-person don't let the reservation system scare you pit your name on the waitlist lots of people cxl and you will get a table don't let the system scare you they are not as exclusive as they like to portray. YOU CAN and WILL get a table.

After stalking Carbone's Resy page for days, I succeeded in making a reservation for a special anniversary dinner and I have to say, that was time well-spent. Carbone truly lives up to the hype!

We dined at the outdoor location on West Broadway outside Sadelle's. The outdoor setup is pretty and cozy, thanks to well placed heat lamps and orb lights. The tables are not as distant as they are at some other restaurants but still okay. Every table has a hand sanitizer bottle which is a great touch in these times. Coming to the food, we ordered the spicy vodka rigatoni (of course) and ricotta tortellini with truffles which was one of the specials. The meal started with complimentary bread basket, cheese, salami and cauliflower. The bread was insanely good! The first course was a perfect start to the meal, hearty but not so filling that we wouldn't enjoy our mains. The pastas were obviously the highlight of the meal. The vodka rigatoni was as good as Yelp would have you believe but I enjoyed the ricotta tortellini even more. We ended our meal with sambuca laced espresso and chocolate cake.

The service was really nice! Our server was helpful throughout the meal and checked on us several times. The only very small complaint I had was that the menu was quite limited. I'm not sure but maybe they're serving a limited menu these days. But in all, it was a great experience and one of those quintessential NYC experiences that I would wholeheartedly suggest to anyone looking for an indulgent Italian meal and some A+ pampering.

Service and meatballs were world class. The octopus didn't taste fresh and wasn't an impressive dish. Spicy rigatoni and lobster ravioli could be matched at a standard Italian restaurant for $24 to $28 a piece instead of $32 and $39, respectively. Overall unimpressed, except for the meatballs and wait staff were excellent. Not to mention we made a reservation at Carbone and were seated at a sister restaurant -- savvy business move to leave a customer even more disappointed. Come after COVID, I assume it will be much better.

My fourth time at carbone. The spicy rigatoni was good but the tortellini was the star of the pasta course. The baked clams were exceptional. My favorite was with the Uni. The Caesar salad was incredible.

Had a wonderful meal here but more of a bucket list restaurant for me- don't think I would return unless it was for someone's birthday. Obviously get the spicy rigatoni but the veal parm was my favorite dish we ordered.

After dining at Carbone in Vegas this experience was different. We sat outside in the outdoor dining which was nice but the tables seemed a bit close. Staff wore masks and there was sanitizer at the tables. Spicy rigatoni was good and the salmon was also. The side of mushrooms was tasty. The grandma/garlic bread they bring out in the breadbasket is really good. Drinks are between I think 17-20 and up. I got a whiskey sour which was excellent. For the price, I don't think it's worth the hype but I would definitely recommend if you have never been going. They do charge a 10% COVID surcharge and with a 20+% tip and tax things do add up even before the meal so come prepared.

Lives up to the legendary hype. Worth the time watching Resy for a table to open and worth the money. Come hungry! Their staff is so polite and hospitable, what an incredible experience! My friend and I split two pastas and they played them for us to split.

This place is like traveling in a time machine back to manhattan in the 1950s! We came last year around Christmas and it was the perfect time to visit with the decorations, Christmas music tinkling in the background, and waiters dressed in tuxedos. The ambiance is like no other, and the service is superb. We ordered the Caesar salad, spicy rigatoni vodka, and veal parm. We were served garlic bread, fresh mozzarella and salami to start and it was the best bread course I have ever had! The garlic bread was superb. It was crispy yet chewy and perfectly garlicky and buttery. The mozzarella and salami are super high quality and fresh, and made for the perfect bite when combined with the bread. Moving into the Caesar salad, I think this may have been the best Caesar salad I've ever had. The lettuce was perfectly crisp, the croutons were huge and crisp and buttery on the outside while soft on the inside, the anchovies were deliciously salty and fishy, and the Parmesan was fresh. They put the salad together by your table so it made for quite a show. The spicy rigatoni was delicious as well! The pasta was perfectly al dente and the sauce was so deliciously creamy and tomatoey with just a hint of heat (I never knew I was missing spice in my vodka sauce!) The veal Parmesan was very good too, but I think the others were the star of the show. If you're able to snag a reservation, I highly recommend going!

This restaurant is so hard to get a reservation to. I had to stalk the RESY app and was able to secure a reservation for 2 for a Friday night at 8:30. Showed up at 8pm and had to wait until our actual reservation time to be seated. Keep in mind that outside seating was not six feet apart and did not adhere to social distancing if that concerns  you. We had the lobster ravioli but the order only came with 3 very small pieces of pasta. I also ordered the spicy rigatoni aka vodka which was very flavors but again very small portion. Ended with the New York style cheesecake.  Good solid Italian restaurant.

This place was definitely worth the hype. Firstly, their ability to adapt to covid by opening up another location to provide more socially distant seating is awesome. The food is just as good as everyone says. The portion sizes are perfect. NYC Italian restaurants tend to serve huge portions, that make you feek less than ideal after feeding--these were the perfect size. The staff was extremely friendly and attentive. Volkan (our server) was specifically great. We went for my boyfriends birthday, and after deciding we didn't want dessert, he made a point to bring over some cookies with a candle because "no one should have a birthday without blowing out a candle"

I was excited about being back here after my initial pre-covid visit, but left disappointed. We got the spicy rigatoni, veal parm, and lobster ravioli. The spicy rigatoni was good, but I was expecting more. It didn't blow me away or anything. The pasta became cold pretty fast. The veal parm lacked flavor. I felt like I was eating from a pizza restaurant that does pasta. Am I missing something here? I really don't get the hype. The lobster ravioli was okay, nothing special. Portions were very small. The worst part was the 10% covid charge that was tacked onto our bill. They snuck that in and did not bother mentioning it on the bill. I only found out because the charges did not add up on our bill and the total seemed way off. They're supposed to clearly make it visible on the bill, and inform customers about it (which they did not, and it was nowhere mentioned on the menu or website). Mind you, I do not mind helping out business that need help but an institution like carbone should definitely not be charging that fee (especially all 10%). When is asked, the waiter told me it was a mandatory fee. False-it's optional for restaurants, and they can charge up to 10%-not required to do the full 10. I ended up tipping less than I normally do because I did not agree with that charge. There was also a couple in the restaurant with a dog inside who kept barking. Fine dining indeed. I won't be back.

Last table left at Carbone - that's us every time we are in New York. The star of the show is the rigatoni but you cannot go wrong with any choice at Carbone. They always have a gluten free option, which is always excellent as well. The white truffle season is upon us & the dish did not disappoint!

Have been meaning to try Carbone forever! Was worried that it might be over sensationalized but that was totally not the case!  John was a great server, ask for him when you go!! He was super kind and helpful! Everything from food to service was amazing and I can't wait to go back

Pretty tasty, but pricey dinner. The bread basket is amazing, and a strong start! My friend and I shared a veal parm and spicy rigatoni. I wish I could eat that spicy rigatoni every day, damn it was so good. We finished with a chocolate cake for dessert, don't sleep on the desserts- this was honestly better than the veal parm!!

Service was top notch!

Walked up and ordered takeout.  Wanted to try the spicy rigatoni and it was disappointing. Waited 45 minutes for bland pasta NOT spicy and the portion was small for $30 plus dollars.  Not what I expected....smh.  My pasta craving was not satisfied.

Ordered takeout from here. They offered a huge portion. I ordered veal pan which was almost too much for me. The meat was really thick and with lots of oil on the top. I don't know if the stale taste was bc of the long time delivery. Spicy Rigatoni was great though.

The food is great, and we appreciated the still top-notch service during this tough time. We sat on the Amex Winter Patio and it was a very nice setup - although still a bit cold with the windows allowing full exposure to the elements. 

However we did not appreciate the $30 hidden COVID charge - there was no line item for this on the bill, but we noticed our subtotal did not add to the food and drink items purchased. We had to ask in order to get this explanation. I am 100% on board with restaurants adding a COVID charge - and gladly pay it to help them out - but I don't appreciate the sneakiness of not showing this in a line item for customers to understand. It should also be clearly stated on the website. I just think customers should be treated with the respect of full disclosure.

If it allowed me to give NO stars I would!!! 
You would think with COVID going on restaurants are losing out on business managers of these restaurants would be a little more accommodating and treat their customers with a little more respect 
When you order take out "pasta" in particular any place I've ever been to gives you bread with your order .... 
Well we noticed there was no bread in our bag ($70 pasta) and no bread so we decided to go back and ask for two pieces of bread and the manager told us it's their policy that they don't give bread to "to go" orders that they only have a specific amount and it's only given to ppl that are dining in and spending lots of $$$$$ he then said out of principal I will not give you any bread well buddy "out of principal" you just lost 5 customers who came to your OVER-rated restaurant very often!! Guys save your money this place is not even all that. Much better places in the city and in Jersey than this not to mention way BETTER customer service!!!

The worst place in nyc with the most rudest front door staff 
Don't go here so many other fantastic places this place isn't worth it they only accommodate dine in only and if u are running up the bill otherwise they look down to u and mistreat u w disrespect 
Alert dont waste your $ it's not event all that 
Not worth it at all-
Wish I can give zero stars

The service was absolutely amazing!! Carmine and Kathy were extremely friendly and so gracious. The food was incredible and Carmine's recommendations made our entire dinner a 10/10. Highly recommend to anyone visiting NYC!!!

Love love love carbone. Spicy rig and veal parm all the way. The Caesar salad comes with large garlic and butter soaked croutons which are unreal. Service of course is great as expected for major food group.

Came here and sat in the Amex winter patio, IT WAS FREEZING, don't expect those overhead lamps to do much. The outdoor seating was actually warmer because those heat lamps are considerably stronger. My suggestion is break out the Canada goose or potentially your ski pants and jacket  and head out to Carbone for dinner. 

That being said, we are so glad we went! As per usual the food was great. We had the meatballs (yum) and spicy rigatoni to start. Then we had the veal Marsala, the veal was my least favorite but it was only because the pasta and the meatballs were so flavorful I think they blew out my Palate. We had a bottle of wine- a super Tuscan which was reasonably priced. 

Beware there is a Covid charge of 10 percent,
But it's totally worth it and they do alert you beforehand when you make the reservation. 

Try to get an indoor table if you can  but service is always top notch.

Wow. Had too many people recommend this spot and let me you tell you, listen to your recommendations. Service was polite helpful, and timely. We had a complimentary bread basket, pickled cauliflower, and a small cheese and salami sampler to start. We went with a bottle of Chianti and a prosciutto and mozzarella plate to start. AH-MA-ZING. We decided to split the iconic spicy vodka rigatoni and lobster ravioli. Neither disappointed. Th lobster was plump and plentiful. Complimentary cookies at the end. You bet you're bottom dollar I will be back.

Came for the AMEX tent, it was underwhelming. Compared to the Nusr-et tent this one was ok. Space was tight though, if you are coming more than 2 people you'd be better off taking the food home. 

As for the food, I don't have to tell you this. I think everyone by now knows. It's good, but overpriced and overrated. Nothing was extra special. 

Still really yummy especially the pasta and the ravioli. The salad was delicious. If it's your anniversary or a special birthday then come but otherwise I would say it's not worth the hassle many restaurants with good food elsewhere.

Amazing dining experience.

Carbones is a magical place, even with outdoor dining; heat lamps that look like little AC units, friendly service and some delicious breads. Came here for Andreas's 30th birthday, our first time dining at a Michelin star restaurant and it did not disappoint. Some context, Andrea and I are both first generation Italian, our parents are from Bari, Italy and we can be critical of Italian/Italian American food.

Chef Mario Carbone is an artist, combing the family style vibe of a pasta Sunday with the gritty street art atmosphere only NYC can provide. We started the experience with some great bread: garlic bread and focaccia were so good. The giardiniera and cheeses were spot on, some nice acidic flavors and savory, creamy flavors. For the main course we got the spicy rigatoni and lobster ravioli. Rigatoni was prepared wonderfully, aldente, heat and creamy flavors, totally delicious. Lobster ravioli had a cream sage sauce, lobster was sweet, and firm; a very scrumptious bite! Desert obviously followed, carrot cake all the way, moist and refreshing, almost makes up for the gluttonous activity.

Overall, excellent food, vibe and service. Ricky and Antonio were rock stars! I hope the business and individuals working are well and healthy. Cheers, and can't wait to go back.

FINALLY made my way to dinner at Carbone this week. I was able to snag a reservation on Monday for their outdoor patio seating which is only open to Amex card holders. We were impressed! It was enclosed and heated. We for sure were super cozy even though it was in the 30s and windy that night. Our waiter was quick to come over to take our orders. He was really knowledgeable about the menu. 

They start by bringing out the most bomb complimentary appetizers! I don't think I've ever been somewhere that does such a good job as carbone. They bring over a huge bread basket filled with garlic bread, cheesy red sauce bread and sesame bread. They also bring out some Parmesan cheese, salami and olive oil with cauliflower swimming in it. Oh man! We were almost full just from all the carbs!

As our entrees, we got the famous spicy vodka rigatoni and then also got the ragu tortellini. The rigatoni was oh so delicious. I'd say it worth the hype at least to try once. The tortellini was also absolutely amazing. The creamy, cheesy filling is truly addicting. We whipped our plates clean (save some bread for this!)

They brought our two little rainbow cookies as a complimentary dessert. We had such a fabulous experience here! For sure met our hyped up expectations.

When you think of carbone you think of fantasric Italian with an emphasis on fine dining and an experience you'll never forget. I'll never forget my experience at Carbone for sure. I understand these outdoor dining is the new normal but it was clear how little Carbone cared to help protect patrons who were non-amex customers from the wind and elements (they have a partnership with Amex and Resy for their outdoor heated patio which is covered and heated). To get a reservation is close to impossible but once we were there I wanted to get out as fast as I got there. It was cold and we had to stagger the pasta orders so our orders wouldn't get cold, not to mention that the food was good but not amazing. I expected much better from MFG as I've been to several of their restaurants but if this is how they treat their customers after charging them an arm and a leg for their food (plus the 10% COVID surcharge-which was a slap in the face given how little they did to add extra heaters or wind protection) then I will definitely have to re-evaluate where I eat.

What can I say about Carbone it's truly worth not 1 Michelin star but 2! I went here two years ago on my birthday and loved every bite from the freshly made bread basket to the spicy Riggtoni vodka best in all of Manhattan. Also, amazing cocktails too You will not be disappointed 5/5.

The Short: It's a New York staple. If you've never been, go. I'm certainly glad I did. Am I in a rush to go back, however? Not really.. but I will eventually.  

The Long: The food was very good. Not mind-blowing, but very good. The service was excellent. We were taken care of and attended to from the time we got there right up to around closing time when we eventually left. Indoor seating is currently banned, so we enjoyed the AMEX winter patio. It's heated (still bring a coat though), it's appropriately distanced, each table has hand sanitizer, and all servers wore masks. For what current times allow, the overall ambiance was warm while still making us feel safe - kudos. 

Now, the price. Is it worth the price? Here's the thing: If you've never been, you should go. It's a New York staple and you'll be glad you got the experience. The food is really good, but I wouldn't call it mind blowing or an "I'll remember this forever" meal. That high price tag is what you pay for being able to say you experienced Carbone. 

Will I go back? Yes, eventually - if I want to impress a date, or a special night with a few close friends/friends from out of town (I think Carbone is ideal for groups of 3-4 people as all plates are shared). But, am I in a rush to go back? Honestly, no. The Carbone experience is great, but there are better experiences for the price (you'll just have to look a little bit).

Came on Christmas eve. Didn't have a reservation but we arrived very early (before 5pm) and the staff was able to accommodate us. We were blessed with a nice 60F weather and the overhead lamps do a pretty good job. The service was awesome, our servers helped move the table and umbrella to make sure I don't get rained on. The bread basket was legendary. Paired so well with the pickled cauliflower and salami. Cocktails are good, classy and quite strong. We had two appetizers. The clams were good but not extraordinary. I liked the tangy and refreshing eggplant and zucchini scapece a bit more. The spicy rigatoni was truly the star of the show. It hits the spot just right and is actually pretty spicy. It's for sure pricey and I'd save it for some special occasions but the experience was definitely worth it!

This review is solely for the covid outdoor heating seating in the "revered" AMEX winter patio. So, we went on a standard winter evening. -~35 degrees outside, mild wind. This winter patio business, where there are trailer type dining setups in parklets do NOT lend to comfort dining. Also, the tables are NOT 6 feet apart, but there is plexiglass separating you from your neighbors 3 feet apart next door. There are these giant heaters and long velvet drapes. The drapes do guard from the wind, but then heaters are set REAL low, and you do not feel significant heat from above. Be prepared to wear your coat and winter hats the entire dinner. I think it's primarily 'chinsy' in order to get ppl in and out so they don't linger. The food...it's goood! And truly Italian comfort food. I think I would have enjoyed it better in a more warm setting. Also, I feel like being local, I don't have to go far for a good vodka pasta elsewhere FYI, I did do another Michelin 2 star rated outdoor setting a couple days earlier, and the ambience was much better, mainly warmer. AMEX/Resy this is false advertising, for your "comfortable, warm, outdoor dining."

Due to the pandemic inside dining is closed. If you have an American Express you can utilize Resy and sit inside a sponsored section. Unfortunately we picked the coldest day to go. While there was an over head heating lamp, it was still cold. The service was great. We did the clams for an appetizer and of course this spicy vodka pasta. We did have to send it back because it wasn't hot by the time it reached our table. We also got the broccoli and rib eye. Both where great. Overall the experience was good. I would like I try again when they are allowing indoor dining to get the full experience.

*written during COVID restrictions*

Carbone is one of of those NYC things you have to do once. So I've been keeping my eyes peeled for an opportunity to come eat here. I made a reservation for myself on Resy about a week 7 days out. I showed up and was promptly seated (sidewalk seating has barriers between each table, no heaters unless you reserve the Amex lounge). I was offered water and hand sanitizer. 

For starters, there was mozzarella cheese, salami, and savory bread which was SO. GOOD.
