I went for the spicy vodka rigatoni since that's the hottest dish (pun intended) and a lovely wait staff member recommended that it paired nicely with the pinot noir. And it did. My goodness was it good. Hands down some some of the best pasta I've had. At the end of your meal you get complimentary rainbow cookies. I don't even like rainbow cookies like that, but I'd happily make the trip for these particular cookies.

Was it a little on the pricier side? Yes. But I have to say, service was exceptional and the quality of the meal is impeccable. Perfect treat-yoself meal!

I would honestly even pay good money for the complimentary bread basket and starters. So great. Staff was amazing, special shout out to Sal! I have tendency to be underwhelmed by super hyped up places, but this really was such a lovely satisfying meal deserving of its accolade. 

Got the caesar salad (best ever), spicy rigatoni and veal parm. All spectacular. Lots of wine. Really loved our experience here. Support always

Came here for lunch and sat outside on the sidewalk. They had a heater but it wasn't that great at keeping us warm. Unfortunately, if you don't have an Amex card you are stuck with sidewalk seating vs their lux seating set up. 

We ordered the eggplant and zucchini app. This was very very good and tasty! I highly recommend. 

The main dishes we got were the spicy rigatoni and the mushroom pasta dish. Both were ok. Nothing exceptional. Just good. 

We got the cake with Nutella icecream for dessert. Let me tell you. This was the best! Love it. Would come back just for this. Highly recommend. 

The service was good. I'm taking a star away because the food was just ok and towards the end they stopped filling up our water glasses and it took about 30 min for them to bring out our dessert. We were freezing sitting outside and almost didn't want it because it was cold and taking forever. 

Otherwise, it was a good experience. I would go again just for the dessert probably. Def not worth the hype though. It's def a must try at least once experience if you live in nyc.

Worth the hype!! It took wintertime covid to finally be able to get a reservation. Popular opinion, the star of the meal was the spicy rigatoni.  We also got the spaghetti con funghi, the meatballs, and a slice of chocolate cake for dessert!  Would definitely recommend and come again!

The spicy rigatoni vodka from Carbone. I spent all of 2020 dreaming of this beautiful little dish and counting the days till I could eat here again. We finally made it out here on what was a relatively nice day for January in New York. We were seated between two heaters since we had a stroller. Even though we had reservations in their covered winter patio, which looked very cozy, it just wouldn't fit a stroller. Which was fine by us. For drinks we started off with a Gibson and whiskey sour, both very smooth, very delicious. Warmed us up right away. They brought out complimentary garlic bread, homemade mozzarella and prosciutto. We got the tuna appetizer which was sashimi style, very delicious. For the main course, we got two spicy rigatoni vodka and a side of meatballs. This is a very difficult review for me to write because I'm now craving for it. I could write a classic novel about the food here, Jane Austen style, if I had any talent. Oh and they brought out complimentary rainbow cookies which I normally hate. It's one of the worst things to come out of Italy (right up there with fascism and Benito Mussolini) in my opinion. But not here. I LOVE it here. Ok. I'll stop now.
The place is nice. The table is really small.they kind rushed us. We didn't even finish our drink and food. The food are okay.drink is ok

Came in here for our first dinner date for 2021. It was raining all day, so they upgraded our sidewalk reservation to their winter patio (which is exclusive to Amex card holders). 

The bread they served almost got us full lol. We liked the spicy salami & domestic parmesan cheese. The Grandma bread was our favorite. 

The assorted clams was good especially the sea urchin! Ofcourse we couldn't miss the famous Spicy Vodka Rigatoni! I was almost giggling on every scoop. Cravings super satisfied! We ordered everything to share & we got Mario's meatballs which is also one of their signature dish off-menu. It did not disappoint us! 

Love love my first Carbone experience! I know it's pretty much impossible to get a dinner reservation here at a normal time. Well, here's to a few pandemic perks!

Service was great otherwise everything else was meh. 
Items ordered below: 
Octopus: good flavor but overcooked
Clams: ok, unremarkable 
Spicy rigatoni: good but not memorable. Not sure why the hype. 
Some mushroom dish: super salty, no other flavor besides salt. Pasta was well cooked but would not recommended unless you like salt. 
Meatballs: the is was the best dish, very tender and flavorful. 
Black out cake: delish

Good  but not great considering the price. The service is excellent and the food has a nice hearty home made feel to it, but if I am being honest it doesn't justify the prices.. 

We got the baked clams, lobster ravioli, spicy rigatoni aka vodka and cheesecake and while they were all delicious This style of American Italian really shouldn't be pushing $40+ to $50+ for red sauce based pasta, which any decent home chef could cook up at home for a fraction of the price. I don't blame them for charging what they can if people are willing to pay it as I suppose it is more about the scene  so you are paying to eat at a trendy joint, 

but maybe it's my age now.. not something I will do often.
The experience and the food. Can't get any better. Perfect for that special occasion.

This is the place everyone in NYC has to go at least once but maybe just once. Overall it was a great experience but just know you're going for the name and buzz of it. 

The outdoor dining set up for Covid was amazing. We sat at the sidewalk since you need to have an Amex to get into the covered area (which I find a bit too exclusive for what you're getting here) but the heaters keep tables so warm that the cold wasn't even an issue. They really made it work! 

The bread service comes with a lot of food and delicious breads. Of course you must get the spicy rigatoni because it's Carbone, and the meatballs were also amazing however I've had similar ones elsewhere. The mushroom linguine was also good.

In general just know what you're going for. You will spend $300 to try a unique spicy vodka sauce and say you went to carbone. Is is the best Italian food in NYC? No. Do you need to do it anyway? Yes.

Outstanding. Reception was lovely and fit us in without a reservation. Food was a real delight. Absolutely delicious and worth the price tag. Sophisticated nyc street side dining atmosphere -  a la COVID chic.

Went here for an anniversary and had a very pleasant time. We were seated in their West Broadway location (Sadelle's) which offers the same exact Carbone menu. We reserved a sidewalk table, AMEX patio is only for AMEX cardholders, but truthfully I have no complaints about it! We thought we might be cold but their heaters are the best I've ever seen. We were so warm to the point where I had to take my jacket off and was in my dress the entire night. Plus, on the sidewalk you get a nice partial view of the Empire and WTC. Foodwise, here is the breakdown. 

Bread, meats, cheese: 9/10 Amazing, their bread tastes fresh and the cheesy one is addictive, save some for the spicy rigatoni sauce. Cauliflower was okay, a little too vinegar-y for my taste but good. Cheese was strong and spicy salami was solid. 

Eggplant and zucchini: 8/10 Great flavors but it was served cold. I like my veggies warm at least. 

Spicy vodka rigatoni: 10/10 Worth it, get it. Perfect flavors. Just get it. 

Ribeye Diana: 7/10 Good but I've had better. 

Broccoli Rabe: 8/10 Also good but we were so filled up on everything else this really was just a side, we barely touched it. 

Cherry black forest cake: 9/10, very good and flavorful without being too indulging. The cake was soft, the cream had a rich chocolate flavor and the cherry added a nice tang. It was topped with hazelnuts for a nutty taste.

We got the complimentary rainbow cookies which were very good. Would I go back? Yes, for the pasta and bread. Is it the best Italian place I've ever been to? No. But overall the experience was great and Carbone is just one of those things you gotta do as a NY native.

To say I was disappointed would be an understatement. A $400 meal and I would have been happier eating at a local pizzeria. The food is so overpriced for the Medicore food you get. 
The only good dish ordered was the meatballs and the complimentary bread. Other than that save your money on the veal parm and spicy rigatoni. The lobster ravioli and assorted clams were so fishy and nasty.
Save yourself $400 and don't eat here, it's a hype.

COVID review - 

Like everyone before me has said : it was a spectacular experience everyone must have at least once but maybe only once; 

So the food was fine but the service was so stinky that it palled the entire celebratory mood . It was surprise reservation for a place I had been dying to visit but the server made a big stink about not being able to replace the bacon clams with more of the non bacon ones. -- I'm Muslim and keep halal. The water was not filled on time and had to ask various times. While the extra clams were being brought in from across the street on west broadway from the other major food group Resturant pop up, there were no appetizer refreshers. The server was called Claudio I overheard from the group of rowdy gen Z kids he was flirting with and honestly I was very disappointed . 

The dessert: there was no actually menu but the one we got was actually disappointing - I got the black out cake and it was very mediocre . It was supposed to have a raspberry coulis but yea .

It was cold but the outdoor Amex seating was legit and kept me warm/ the fettuccine con fungi was also mediocre at best. 

The greats: 
The price wasn't that steep and honestly the bread bowl ( with delish chunks of parm and culled cauliflower )   the warm  baked and seasoned clams , the chili flaked broccoli rabe and UMazingly perfect lobster ravioli. Compared to other Michelin  restaurants - the service ruined it for me and the fettuccine was underwhelming but overall, it's a check mark  for my fine dining escapades and Michelin foodie bucket list for Nyc

Was alright compared to what I had been imagining. But for the most part, my group enjoyed carbone. Our service was great, so I'll give 4 stars for that but taking away a star since food was less than impressive.
Parmesan and meats as the appetizer were great, the classic spicy rigatoni and veal Parmesan are a must to try while there. Flavorful and worth savoring. Friendly and attentive service!

To management,

Friday 1/29/21 was a special day for us, we were celebrating our anniversary and thought to order in Carbone for our celebration dinner.  We've never been to Carbone and since hearing nothing but amazing things we decided to choose your menu for our dinner.  To our extreme disappointment, when we cut into the meatballs (one of our 2 entrees) they were basically roar.  Needless to say it ruined the whole experience of what we were expecting from a Carbone meal.  We would like to be credited for our full meal so please accommodate our request to confirm at least your level of customer service is stellar since our expected meal was not this time.

Been hearing so much about this place and so glad I finally got the opportunity to try it. Aside from the fact that it was freezing out and we were seated in the winter patio, the food was absolutely delicious. 

To begin, we were given two pieces of bread, some mozzarella and salami. I wish they gave more bread because everything put together only left us craving for more. 

Next, we were given the tortellini al ragu, which they kindly split up for us to share. Keep in mind the portion size is a bit small for what you pay for, but it makes up for it in taste. This was good but definitely found the spicy rigatoni better. The rigatoni has a slight kick, but other than that it's cooked perfectly al dente, and all the other flavors come together for a sensational bite. I would recommend for everyone going to Carbone to try it at least once.

Upon arriving we were not satisfied with the seating, they had a tiny heater in the corner of the outdoor seating arrangement and doors were open on every end. We then asked to be moved to something warmer ( we expected to dress warm but didn't think we would be that cold). After my boyfriend asked to be moved they gladly moved us to another section where there were heaters that ran across the ceiling and was substantially warmer. The whole staff was exceptionally phenomenal including one in particular our main waiter Marc. He really made sure we felt at home ( provided brand new blankets for extra warmth) and also stressed how important it was that we were here supporting. The food is always off the charts. The musts on the menu is the Spicy Rigatoni Vodka and Veal Parmesan. Also if you like coffee, the cappuccinos are a great end to the night ! Repeated customer and will be back again.

My review of 2 stars is based slowly on the presentation/place and quality of the ingredients used. You can tell the food was made with fresh items and nothing felt short on that taste. 
However 
Carbone is severely overpriced for what it served. I was so enthusiastic about going since I've heard so many good things about this place. We ordered the lobster ravioli, spicy rigatoni, and veal parm. Save yourself the trouble and the money, and find a more authentic Italian spot. The spicy rig was so disappointing, it truly is overhyped. The veal was good, but the lobster ravioli made my sister sick. Not sure what it was, can't say it was their fault but might have just been an Off day when we went. 
Also the Amex patio is a great outdoor set up, but the heaters are weak. I watched several other customers raising their hands up to the heater to get some warmth or see if it was even working. 
Our waiter was a kind man but spent the majority of diner engrossed in a conversation with a table behind us. So much so that it was hard for us to order drinks or dessert, at a certain point we just gave up and decided to cut our losses.

Yes, it's very expensive. And yes, it's impossible to get a reservation. However, it is worth it. After snagging an Amex reservation outdoors, I experienced everything Carbone had to offer. 

Just to start, the bread spread cannot be missed - garlic bread, tomato bread, pickled cauliflower, meat and cheese, it was all amazing. 

I ordered the Caesar salad, the spicy rigatoni, and the veal parm (yes I had read that these were the things to order). They were all AMAZING! The rigatoni was better than I ever could have imagined, and the parm was crispy and cheesy and delicious. 

Would highly recommend washing everything down with a couple of old fashioneds - it lives up to the hype!

Not a restaurant to order takeout, much better to go in-person and sit outdoors. Food does not deliver well. A little sad that the veal parm did not arrive with the bone, like at the restaurant. However, we will are looking forward to visit post-Covid and hopefully the experience will be spectacular.

This is my 2nd and last experience eating the food from Carbone. I give props to this place - their PR has allowed them to fool people that it's worth spending over $30 for spicy rigatoni and and nearly $70 for veal parmigiana. This place doesn't live up to the hype and I'm annoyed that I spent so much money for a mediocre meal!

I have been going to carbone for years now. Always great food and drinks. Tonight, my friend and I ordered the meatballs... a first for us. When they arrived at the table, I cut in to one and it looked very undercooked. I told my server and he insisted that they were "supposed to be like that." I didn't feel comfortable eating them but my friend did. She got food poisoning from them. Very disappointed.

Shady business practices - would give a zero star rating, but not possible. I booked a Valentine's dinner for my girlfriend and I a few weeks ago when the spots became available. I get that covid times are tough and Valentine's weekend is busy, but I found it strange that they changed the venue from Carbone's to an overflow location (Sadelle's) without ever mentioning when you make the original reservation. Coincidentally, the first mention of this was after their refund window.

When you try to ask about the switch, Carbone doesn't address this issue directly and they continue being shady. You can't get a hold of a live person when you call their number. The one email response I got back ignored my preference to get seated at the restaurant where I made my reservation. They'll text you to confirm your reservation - but then dodge you again when you ask to speak to someone live.

Worst of all, they jam you because what's the alternative? Cancel your Valentine's dinner plans? Wow.

My SO had booked a Valentine's dinner a few weeks ago at Carbone though Resy the morning all the tables were released. I was super excited to eat there since it is one my favorite restaurants in the city. 

He gets an email 3 days before the reservation asking which venue he would prefer. He emails them back immediately stating that his preference is at the original Carbone location. Stephanie from Carbone ignored or overlooked his reply. When he tried to fix the issue at hand, he wasn't able to get a hold of anyone even after 3 days of trying.  This was a extremely frustrating and disappointing experience!

I visited here during Christmas time in the Amex Winter patio tents. You have to make a reservation on Resy with your Amex card as your method of payment to be able to view the reservations. It was my first time here and the spicy rigatoni vodka definitely lived up to my expectations. They brought cheese and focaccia to the table before our appetizers which was amazing along with pickled cauliflower. We also got the baked clams which were some of the best that I've ever had. I loved having the variety of three different baked clams in one appetizer. My boyfriend and I also ordered the veal Parmesan. We were completely stuffed sharing both the veal and the pasta. They gave us rainbow cookies for dessert and were too full to order anything but will definitely try to make room for next time. The winter patios were very nice although the night we went was a little cold. The service was absolutely phenomenal and the waiter felt like I had known him for years. We were seated early because we got there a little before our reservation which is always a plus. Amazing meal and would love to go back!

Wow, this place was perfect, from the food to the customer service, to the atmosphere. It is a bit pricey, but honestly worth it. The food we ordered was so outstanding. The spicy rigatoni, meatballs, lobster ravioli, and the lemon cheesecake.  Both pastas had so much richness in flavor and the meatballs were so juicy! THE dessert, the lemon cheesecake, just wowwwwww! That was the best cheesecake i have ever tasted. Make sure to make a reservation in advance and make room for the cheesecake, you won't regret it! Have to go back when I go to NY again.

We came here during the covid 19 pandemic and we were seated at the West Broadway location. I can't remember the waiters name but he was very funny and accommodating to us. We had a nice table where we were able to see all the action. The bus boys kept the tables cleaned and our drinks filled. Then soundtrack was nothing less then marvelous and kept my date and I both entertained all night. This meal was special and worth the ticket price imo. The bread to start off with could have enough to please me but the parmesan drenched caesar with the biggest croutons i ever seen, the  creamy spicy rigatoni, meatballs and ribeye diana almost left me with no room for the most satisfying and gigantic piece of carrot cake ever! I will definitely be back at some point as there is a lot of other stuff i need to try. Props the the Major Food group!

Had the Carbone menu at Sardelle's. When you are charging these prices for pasta, it better be perfect. And, Carbone pretty much nails it. Sit down for a complimentary antipasto with three (amazing) types of homemade bread, salami, Parmesan...and cauliflower. Don't skip it! Lightly grilled and then quick pickled in a vinegar dressing. It was amazing. The Rigatoni is to die for. Slightly spicy vodka cream over perfectly toothsome pasta. Chicken Massimo arrived dark brown from the caramelized balsamic glaze, coating succulent moist chicken. We got the lemon curd cheesecake for dessert and it was incredible. Much lighter than a lot of cheesecake, it felt more like a Key Lime Pie. Just the right balance of sweet and tart in a crunchy Graham cracker crust. Save room!
Literally the best gluten free pasta I've ever had !!! Heat lamps were very strong, they give you so many free appetizers you forget it's $35 for a meat free pasta

Ordered the spicy rigatoni from here, $35 including taxes. It came an hour late and was the smallest portion, I couldn't believe $35 got you this little pasta, at best an appetizer size, the container was not even full. So disappointed

I finally made it to Carbone. I can definitely see what all the hype was about. I came here for a milestone birthday. We ordered the rigatoni, and it exceeded our expectations. We also ordered the prime rib and the lobster fra diavlo. Everything was great! The servers were also super helpful, knowledgeable, and attentive. They were also very friendly. So glad I was finally able to get a reservation! The meal was a bit pricey, but definitely worth it.

We dined in one of the outside American express build outs which was cute. A little questionable when a few fire trucks had to pass by, but cute.

The wine was very good. I got a red blend and my friend ordered the margarita. The bread they give the table was delicious, especially the tomato one. If I could order just a plate of that by itself I would. They give bread, Parm cheese, cauliflower in olive oil and meat on a plate before your meal which was good.

We both ordered spicy rigatoni which was good. It was spicy and creamy. They have their restaurant service split between carbones and sadelles at the moment. Only mentioning that because I really wanted the rigatoni to be served on one of the decorative plates fir presentation, but I'm assuming they are low? Not sure, anyways it was good. 

The real winner of the night was the carrot cake. Omg it was so good. It comes as a nice presentation. It's kinda like a moon space and so delicious. Happy we ordered it. Thay also give lil pieces of rainbow cake as part of the meal. 

Overall I was happy with the experience. Maybe next time I can be served on the nice plate so I can post on social media

*** AMBIENCE ***
Patio area was interesting. It was formal but at the same time a little dressed down. Nice red curtains on one side and patterned tile ceiling but then dark blue painted wall on the other side. Heaters did basically nothing (and after much covid outdoor dining I can tell you there are options for heating). 

*** Service ***
A bit conflicted here. Loved our waiter, gave great suggestions. About halfway through we were told our third dish was coming, which we were looking forward to having with our pasta, but it never arrived. When we asked about it at the end of the meal (because we unfortunately didn't see our waiter bedore we finished the pasta) there was no explanation as to what happened and merely that he would "take care of it." Normally (even at "lesser calibur" restaurants) we would at least receive an apology or explanation. Instead, we received the check, as is, with everything else we ordered. Not sure what to make of this as I've never had a dining experience like this. 

*** Food *** 
Highlight for sure. Would've been 5 stars if not for above issues. Rigatone and oricchiette were highlights. The baked clams weren't worth the hype, at least in cold weather. 

*** Drinks *** 
Awesome twists on classics. Old fashioned made with rum and I gotta say I'm a believer.

I'm going to get slammed for this by many of my friends who raved about this place, but I thought Carbone was good, not great. Maybe we ordered the wrong things? Went as a group of 4 and got:

- Grilled octopus: I think Via Carota does it better
- Assorted baked clams: THIS was really, really good. You get a variety of flavors and they're all good in their own way, albeit salty
- Meatballs: decent, but expectations are everything-- server made it sound like these were mindblowing!
- Veal parmesan: it was aite. BUT 100% recommend keeping the rib that comes with it and scraping the meat off of it. This was the highlight for me-- that was some good meat
- Spicy rigatoni vodka: this dish seems to get a lot of attention (someone told me just as good as/better than in Italy), but again, expectations are everything. Really didn't get the hype here

Baked clams and veal parmesan (the rib meat) were solid, but I'd pass on the others. As a side note, the server was a bit impatient and rude-- didn't help the experience

Taste: their famous spicy rigatoni alla vodka is heavenly... my favorite pasta and creamy pasta in the USA. I've been to Italy twice and this is the only place that has creamy pasta similar in taste to what I've had there
Value: an expensive meal ($100-200 for two people) but worth it for sure
Frequency: I come here every 2-3 months to enjoy the vodka rigatoni

I've been here ~4ish times now and ordered quite a bit on take-out/delivery. First time coming here I tried to not have any expectations in spite of all the hype. I can confidently conclude that it does live up to the hype, UNLESS you are one of those interesting people who do not like creamy pastas, or want more 'complexity' in your pasta

This is a very simple pasta executed to the utmost finest subtlties and nuances. The flavor is so rich and lasts a long time on every bite. I don't usually sing so much praise for a single dish but I am VERY picky for pasta and I don't think any other Italian restaurant in NYC comes close to this

I also ordered the Veal Parm. It's good, worth it for rounding out the meal (with party of two), but it's not the main attraction here.
The food was okay.  Nothing to brag about especially for the price.  We have the famous spicy pasta and rainbow cookies.  Just a plain okay to me

Ooh I am in love with everything about this place, starting from the ambience to the pasta! We called in for a rsvp and was able to get one the same night. Walking past the curtains, to their nice dining hall area we were seated in the corner type booth with dim lighting- very intimate! Sinatra was playing and lots of other classics. The service was superb, and very attentive waiters. The manager was also friendly. We started off with their bread and parmesan, and I got baked clams, delicious!!! Also the spicy rigatoni vodka it was very tasty, not even that spicy. Then received a complimentary pasta fettuccine con funghi. The veal parmigiana was crunchy and yum. Definitely a vibe overall with a lovely Italian menu.

Overall great dining experience; great food and great service. Personal favorites were the beef carpacio with truffle (best carpacio I've ever had in m life) and lobster ravioli; those two had the wow factor that makes you want to come back to a restaurant again. The veal parmesian was a disappointment and really nothing special. The famous spicy vodka rigatoni was quite good but I wouldn't come back just for that; the meatballs were solid but no different from many other meatballs across town.  I still want to try the ribs with hot peppers when their full menu is back.

Love the spicy rigatoni and meatballs. The bread basket with mozzarella and salami they give you is delicious too! I'm giving it 4 stars because it is a bit pricey and the out door seating was OK (I know they can't help it due to covid).

Carbone has been a spot we've been wanting to try for a while.  I've dined at a number of Michelin rated restaurants including most of Jean Georges fleet among others and have to say that I was FAR from impressed.  The coveted "spicey vodka ravioli" was good as was the special...carpaccio.  They were "out" of the clams, the branzino, the lobster diavolo, and the salmon.  I got the veal which was huge but flavorless, minus the marsala sauce.  The wait staff was attentive but too much so.  It seemed as though they were pooring our bottle of wine more quickly than we could drink to entice us into a second bottle.  We made a reservation at the origional Thompson Street location but we were "redirected" to the W. Broadway loaction which is, in fact Sadelle's.  I've been to Sadelle's and love their brunch, etc., but Carbone paying to sublease they're space 7 nights per week is just misleading.  If anything, when you go to Carbone, you wait and pay for the classic ambience of a W. Village staple.  Instead, you walk 10 minutes to their "other location" which is obviously their way of making up for tough times during COVID and circumventing the 25-50% limitations imposed by good ol Cuomo.  The bottom line is, poor form for such an highly IG-rated (talk about rigatoni hastags ) and supposedly Michelin staple.  I would spend 3-fold to enjoy the ambience and quality of a truly noteworthy restaurant.  I honestly hope that the hype is worth the visit in the future because tonight I would have been much better served at Locanda Verde or Patsy's.

I hate to give such a low rating, but my group and I could not have been more disappointed. Two friends of mine were visiting, one of whom has been dying to go to Carbone for 4 years. We sat outside in the Amex patio and sincerely had the worst service, completely tainting the meal. The server rushed us from the moment we sat down and had a pompous attitude during the whole meal. Spending over $200 a person on a meal, we figured our waiter would be kind and attentive. However, he could not wait to get us out. We were barely offered dessert before the check came. Door to door we were gone after an hour and a half. Unfortunately, this is my second time to Carbone and the first time I ate here my waiter was absolutely lovely. However, this last experience really shifted my mindset on the restaurant. The pasta was great, but there is a lot of great pasta in NYC. I will be taking visitors to places where we aren't treated so poorly.

One of my favorite Italian spots in the city. I've been to Carbone a few times. I came here this past weekend as restaurants increased their seating capacity. We had an outdoor patio seating that was built out nicely. I felt safe and there were dividers among guests. The star dishes of the night has to be the spicy rigatoni vodka of course ...a must order when visiting Carbone. I also really enjoyed their cheesecake - I typically opt for the tiramisu but wasn't on their menu, but this cheesecake was a 10/10! Excellent service as usual. Our server was top notch. Can't wait to come back again.

Even if I was given $1 million dollars, I wouldn't go back here. The food was so bad. We had traveled here from California and made reservations ahead of time to enjoy the restaurant. We ordered the eggplant appetizer, spicy rigatoni and funghi pasta. The eggplant app was good but the pastas were so salty! I even had to take my blood pressure meds after the meal to counteract the saltiness. We complained to the server and she refused to believe us. She said this is the way the pasta is supposed to taste. I would've rather donated the money I spent here to charity. I created this account just to write this review.

Indoor service at the 2nd Carbone location (Sadelle's) is absolutely terrible. First, no one came up to us with menus after we had been seated and no QR code was available at the table. Then, when we were ready to order, we didn't even know who our waiter was to tell them we were ready to order. 

Sad when you pay $$$ for a meal and don't have the service to match the price. Would recommend sitting outdoors instead.

One of the best meals I've ever had and will always remember!! I loved the spicy rigatoni and the lobster ravioli! Even the bread basket had a delicious assortment of breads and Parmesan/ butter spreads. Our server, Fortune, was the best server I've ever had at any restaurant EVER! He was super personable and made our night a memorable one. Great personality and attention to detail!

The ambiance was great and romantic. Super spacious so you didn't feel jammed in with other guests. 

The martini was amazing and chilled perfectly. For dessert we had the carrot cake and lemon cheesecake. The cheesecake was especially delicious and not too rich. 

Carbone goes on my list of my top favorite restaurants!

Service was great, our waiter was charming and friendly. The food however, was underwhelming. Our complimentary bread, cheese and sopressata was tasty but the spicy rigatoni was so SALTY and this is coming from someone who likes things on the saltier side. It was salty to the point where it was almost inedible. At $174 for a table of 3 I felt like it was overpriced for the quality of food we got.

Overall: Great meal, but as with many Italian places, I recommend going with a group and doing family style. Book ahead - it was completely booked on a Wednesday night for dinner weeks in advanced. 

Location: We were seated at the secondary location (Sadelle's) - super smart to share the space if you serve meals at opposing hours. We opted to sit inside. Very high ceilings and everyone spaced very far apart. We had our own balcony overlooking the entire restaurant. 

Food: When we arrived, we were brought and bowl of breads, pickled cauliflower, fresh Parmesan, and spicy salami. It was a nice start to the meal. 

Octopus Pizzaiolo: Nice proportions of octopus, potatoes, and peppers. It's mostly the flavor of the ingredients and oil. We would still consider it a light appetizer. 

Mario's Meatballs: It came with 3 large meatballs, which is perfect to share for the table. After one, I was starting to get full. Super flavorful mix of meat with the perfect amount of sauce. There wasn't extra sauce left over for dipping bread though, so I would ask for extra if that was your plan. 

Spicy rigatoni and vodka: I'm happy we shared this, and I would recommend it as a shared side for the table. It was very flavorful with red pepper undertones, but just vodka sauce as described. 

Tortellini al Ragu: This was a bit heavier than expect, but not in a bad way. The tortellini was quite fluffy and nicely stuffed. The meat was flavorful and the perfect amount to eat with the dish. 

Carrot cake with ginger cream cheese frosting: it was shaped like a boomerang, which was confusing at first, but the way the iced it, perfectly distributed the icing. The chopped candied walnuts topping and hint of ginger in the icing made it super enjoyable. If they are offering this when you come, definitely recommend!

Yes, the Spicy Rigatoni Vodka is as good as they say!!  So worth trying.  For a party of 2, we ordered:

Caesar Salad: 4/5. Delicious but overpriced for a sinple caesar salad.  They made sure to pile on the cheese

Tuna Calabrese: 4/5. Very good but again it was overpriced. The fish tasted very fresh, but the portion was so small that we only got a couple bites each.  

Meatballs: 4/5. Honestly nothing special but was tasty nonetheless 

Spicy Rigatoni Vodka: 5/5.  The star of the night.  Wish we ordered more of it.  It's rich and creamy yet light. 

Lemon Cheesecake: 5/5. Must try!! Probably the best cheesecake in New York.

Overall, I had a great night and would definitely come back. The service was impeccable as well.

This was probably one of the most overrated and overpriced restaurants I've ever been to. They have a Michelin star. LOL. 

Drinks
WAY overpriced glasses of wine. I literally laughed that they were charging $25 a glass for an Oregon Pinot Noir. Comical.

Food
We ordered the Caesar salad, spicy rigatoni, and the veal parm. All of the dishes were average/below average and did not have any wildly amazing flavor. I was really looking forward to the spicy rigatoni and honestly it just wasn't that good for $32 and the portion size was SO small. Pasta is cheap to make and so is vodka sauce..they can definitely afford to give more. 

Service
We were at the Sadelle's location which I didn't love since I'd prefer to actually eat at Carbone, but the only star is for service. Our server was attentive and the food came out promptly. Also, note to future diners, they charge a 10% COVID fee** and aren't open about it...first I've ever seen that at an already expensive restaurant. 

Ambiance 
We sat on the sidewalk in shitty constructed outdoor seating with barely any heat on a 20 something degree day. The most bizarre thing about it is that our reservation was for 5pm and no one was there, and the staff sat us right on top of another couple. Bizarre. Also, to sit on the sidewalk outside and to pay for pricey food is absurd. The only redeeming factor about the ambiance was the Frank Sinatra music.

Honestly once the meal was over, I couldn't wait to get the hell out of there and go to a REAL Italian restaurant.

Save your money and go to Song e Napule around the corner that's run by the real deal.

If I could give it zero stars I would. Hostess and server were being discriminatory. My friend (Asian woman) and an unrelated Asian male were seated after a group of white men even though my friend and the other Asian male had gotten to the restaurant and were waiting to be seated first. Then when we had asked for a latte or cappuccino the server said that the restaurant only serves coffee. Later I glanced at one of the other tables near me and it was obvious that another party had received a drink with frothed milk. Carbone has never been known for its service but usually the food makes up for it. Given the nature of the political environment right now, however, as an Asian American I can only suggest to boycott the restaurant and #stopasianhate

Very yummy food! 
The Ceasar Salad was perfecto!
The Lobster RAVIOLI was sublime!
The meatballs very nice.
The veal chop Parmigiano on the bone.very good.
Steak Diane was good but the could have had a much better marble.
The drinks we're way too costly!
The lemon cheese cake, superb.
Our server Christina was top notch, truly the greatest!

Pre-meal bread & cheese were good. Tried - meatballs, caesar salad, lobster ravioli, fettuccine funghi, spicy rigatoni vodka, and carrot cake. It was four of us, so ordered 2 plates of rigatonis. Our favorites were, surprisingly, meatballs and lobster ravioli, not the rigatoni. Total came out to be around $300 including tips and 10% covid ppe fee (or whatever they're called haha). Food & service were generally good but not exceptional/irreplaceable that we feel the urge to go back.

My favorite Italian in NYC. The spicy rigatoni and veal parm are NOT overhyped but the veal is truly one of my favorite dishes ever. They start with an amazing bread basket, parm, and salami. 

I didn't love dining outside as much as inside - I feel like you don't get the same experience but the food is always incredible.

Carbone was my first Michelin star experience and I thought it was so absolutely worth. We paid ~$80 for the meal each including tip and tax and walked out waddling because we were so full from all the yummy food.

- Reservation: we had to do the Amex reservation which was a little annoying because I didn't have the card (luckily my friend did). Book at least a week in advance for lunch on the weekend!
- Outdoor seating was cute and they really made the most out of it. There's literally seats along the ENTIRE block, it was wild.
- Service was actually amazing. We had the nicest host who gave us the perfect recommendations and was so fun to talk to. He made it such a memorable experience.
- Got an espresso martini which was solid
- The appetizers were, in our opinion, the best part of the meal. You get these little garlic cheese breads and I could've just had that and been satisfied. I'm SHOOK at how good it is - perfect crust/crunch but also warm and soft inside. Top it with some of the fresh mozzarella or dip it in the olive oil that the mozzarella comes in and WOOW. Honestly this is the reason why I would 100% come in person as opposed to ordering online. There's also a meat (salami?) but I don't eat red meat so didn't try it!
- Rigatoni: really yum, really al dente. The sauce was solid and it was a must try given how famous it was. We definitely ate the whole plate and wiped all the sauce off our plate. I've certainly had better but I think it's worth getting once!
- Garlic angel hair pasta with chillies: not sure if this was a daily special but was soo good. It's such a simple dish - just garlic and parsley and olive oil and chillies but it's one of those dishes thats made with such high quality ingredients and care that it's delicious. Honestly so good, and better than rigatoni. If you get this you HAVEEE to get it with the mushrooms.
- Mushrooms: where the garlic pasta might've been a little bland the mushrooms made up for it in every way. These were so rich and exquisite. I'm not the biggest mushroom fan but HOLY these were good. Just so ridiculously tasty, I don't really know the right words to describe it. They are very rich in flavor though so I would highly recommend eating with the angel hair pasta. The combo of the two was the highlight of our meal (other than the amazing apps)

Given all the hype surorunding Carbone, I would have expected 5-star service. While the hostess, busboys and sommelier were incredibly friendly, our waiter was unfriendly -- bordering on rude -- which really set the tone for an average meal.

The bread was absolutely amazing, and the Spicy Vodka pasta was as advertised, but otherwise everything was very underwhelming. Perhaps we mis-ordered, but frankly given the waiter simply took our orders and did nothing else (besides making snarky comments under his breath), I'm not really sure.

Don Angie, L'Artusi, and Emilio's Ballatto are all significantly better in my experiences.

For a bill that came out to $400 and has a Michelin star I expected better.

I came during covid and was excited because there would be less customers but damn did it sound like a concert inside. Everyone table was screaming. I could barely hear my waiter tell me the daily specials.

It was also freezing indoors since they sometimes keep the door open and constantly went in and out. My first clue should've been that the hostess was wearing a wool jacket. Also since the door kept opening the restaurant kept smelling like cigarettes.

-spicy vodka rigatoni- tasted good but size was laughable
-carrot cake with ginger- I love ginger and carrot cake but the combination together I did not like. Plus I like moist cakes and the slices was mostly crust like. 
-veal parm- was also laughable in size. It was the size of a small personal pizza and $79! 
-meat balls- good. Didn't blow my mind.
-prosciutto with warm cheese- tasted good. 

The food tasted good but not amazing. It tasted like I could go Parm (which is under the same company and much cheaper) and still get the same satisfaction. The only standout was the prosciutto with warm cheese and the spicy vodka rigatoni. 

I also want to add they're notorious for having horrible service because they're playing homage to the "old-school Italian culture." People play it off like it's the culture but it's a relatively new restaurant (2013) not like Peter Luger (1887) who have earned the right and are actually a historic restaurant. 

Plus I didn't like that I asked two separate employees a question that neither of them tried to retrieve the answer nor did they follow up to respond to me. 

They also rushed the meal. So even though I was planning or order another bottle they didn't even give me a chance. 

To show how little they pay attention to detail. On resy I wrote that we were celebrating our anniversary. When we ordered desert they brought it with a candle and told us happy birthday (didn't even sing a birthday song). How do you mess that up?

Overall, I would say if you like to waste money, have the vibe like you're in the club while sitting in an Italian restaurant environment while feeling like the staff is rushing you and don't care about quality of service then this is the restaurant for you.

Reception was lukewarm. Food was OK - nothing to rant about. Service was friendly, but they did manage to forget one of our dishes. Already overpriced ($150 per person and we all had pasta as a main course!) AND they charge an extra 10% for "covid-related expenses". Who does that? 
Very disappointing...

Incredible experience, from the bread to the appetizers and finally, the pasta! Eddy did an incredible job of guiding us through the entire meal and had great recommendations throughout. Only disappointing part was that they out of the baked clams at the beginning and the tiramisu at the end - both key items to be sold out around dinner rush. However, the rest of the meal made up for it. Service was incredible and the food was amazing! Highly recommend the spicy rigatoni (no surprise there) and the prosciutto as an appetizer. It just melts in your mouth. The veal was good but I'm not a big veal fan so it wasn't very noteworthy to me. If you can snag a reservation, don't miss the opportunity to check this place out - even if it means eating dinner after 9pm :) It's worth the wait!

We had the best service and experience at the location around the corner (forgot the name). Our food was amazing . Daniel and Alejandro made sure everything was perfect and were extremely warm people. We tried the Cesar salad, meat balls, large shrimp , fish , pasta and dessert. Everything was outstanding , the atmosphere was perfect, music on point . We will come and eat here every time we're in town.
Overrated  not worth the price especially the veal parmesan tasted like chicken-finger with pizza toppings

Their 2 most popular dishes (rigatoni and veal Parmesan) were tasty but not stellar and not quite worth the price point. However, their seared octopus dish was fantastic !! Wonderful flavor and so tender, highly recommend. Our waiter was also very friendly and overall pleasant vibes, even with outdoor seating.

Fantastic !!! Over meet my expectations!! Was beyond delicious. 
Staff was so amazing and accommodating, beyond hospitable and gracious.. every bite of food was more enjoyable then the next.. just amazing.. can not wait to go back

Ever so slightly overrated, but a great dining experience nonetheless.

I think Carbone is one of those places where you wouldn't come back solely for the food, but perhaps you'd want to come for an occasion/celebration + the food. 

As many other reviewers have said, their bread, salami and mozz appetizer may have been the best part of the meal. The garlic bread was so decadent, garlicy, buttery, crispy.... possibly one of the best garlic breads I've ever had in my life. Top it with the mozz and salami and it was heavenly.

We got the caesar salad and the beef carpaccio as appetizers. Both were good but nothing phenomenal or astounding. 

The spicy vodka pasta was similarly delicious, but once again, nothing life-changing. It actually had a decent kick, which I was pleasantly surprised by.

Veal parmesan - again, it was yummy and I certainly enjoyed it. But nothing that I'd be dreaming about LOL. Tbh, it'd be pretty hard to deep fry a slab of meat and slather it with sauce and cheese and have it NOT be good. I kind of enjoyed the bone a little more than the main... you can actually taste the flavor of the meat on the bone versus the veal flavor being masked by tomato sauce and cheese. 

Tried both the carrot cake and the lemon cheesecake for dessert. The cream cheese frosting on the carrot cake was divine and overall this dessert wasn't too sweet which was nice. There was a nice balance of the carrot + ginger + cream cheese flavor. The lemon cheesecake was a solid slice of cheesecake. Super fluffy and flavorful, with a nice zing from the lemon. Also they give you little rainbow cakes as a free dessert which was a nice touch. 

Service was fantastic which ultimately bumped them from 4 to 5 stars.

I want to caveat this review by saying that I ate at their Sadelle's dining room location. However, everything was spot on and highly enjoyable. The ambiance at Sadelle's was very classy and had an old timey vibe. The waitstaff was courteous and helpful. I had been warned that the pasta dishes were small, so I decided to order a lot, but it ended up being way too much food. They first start you off with assorted bread (the one with tomato on top was outstanding), parmesan, meats, and pickled cauliflower. So I almost got full off of that! For an appetizer, I had the eggplant & zucchini scapese which was really flavorful. It was a large portion and could definitely be shared amongst multiple people. For my main, I tried both the fettuccine con funghi and the spicy rigatoni vodka, both of which were outstanding. The pasta is perfectly al dente and so incredibly flavorful. I was a little hesitant to get the vodka pasta, as the sauce can be heavy, but here it was a light sauce and did not feel overly heavy. I cannot highly recommend this restaurant enough and I cannot wait to come back.

I love this place! Food is awesome and Chris is the best waiter ever! Nice, funny and very attentive! 
Vibe here is really cool too.
So food, service and vibe are great, what more do you need?

First, I love Carbone.  I recently was in NYC and felt fortunate to book a dinner reservation for three.  We had a great meal.  When presented the check I did not notice the Service Charge, so I paid for the meal, the Service Charge, the tax, these totaled $250; then I paid a tip of $50.  I should have paid closer attention, that's on me.  
The service was OK.  Not worthy of a $100 tip on a $200 meal.

First time at Carbone and it was just as I expected, delicious. Service was great. Our waiter was really fun and gave us great suggestions. We of course were given the complimentary bread basket, cauliflower, &Parmesan cheese. Everything was super fresh. We started off with Mario's Meatballs, they were so flavorful, so moist, they were made with a mix of 3 different meats covered in red sauce. I ordered the Tortellini al Ragu which was absolutely amazing. Literally the best sauce I've ever had. The tortellini is stuffed with a nice soft ricotta. The Ragu does contain pork though for you non-pork eaters, It's like a bolognese. We also ordered spicy rigatoni vodka, I mean we had to it's the most popular dish on the menu. The rigatoni was great as well, had a good spice to it. All the Pasta was served al dente. Everything was very flavorful and delicious. I'll definitely be back again, if we can get another reservation lol.

Very disappointed! 
The food was good but the experience overall leaves a lot to be desired.  My husband wanted to take me out to a nice dinner since I'm pregnant and we had been talking about coming here for a long time.  
We booked the amex patio and there were plenty of tables, however they sat us at a 2 top next to a wall. There was a empty table with a window right next to us.   
The assistant waiter was very attentive but our primary waiter was unfriendly.  
The food was good but the other factors you come to expect from Michelin dining were not evident.  The tables were packed very tightly which made serving food somewhat uncomfortable.  They forgot to give us the complementary rainbow cookies but everyone around us seemed to receive them. 
The thing that really bothered me was that after spending 360$ on dinner it would have been nice to have the staff help my husband move the table so that i could get out of the corner I was stuck in due to my 8 month pregnant belly. He had to move the table himself and no one even offered assistance.  Totally inconsiderate!
Came in on a Saturday night, we were sent to the West Broadway location. The food was okay, I thought when I came to Carbone a few years ago was much better.
Beautiful experience. Fantastic service and food. These guys are top Notch. Recommend to anyone. True Michelin experience
Loved the food at carbone. Spicy rigatoni and lemon cheesecake were delicious. Appetizer baked clam was so juicy. Waiter was also very pleasant and nice. Would definitely come back.

Food 5.0/5.0
Service 4.0/5.0
Value 2.5/5.0
Decor 4.0/5.0 
Overall 5.0/5.0

Oh Carbon, you know you are so very good.  Everything is good, spicy rig is not over-rated.  Glad I live far enough that I couldn't come everyday... my wallet couldn't handle it.  Simple menu... don't overthink it.  Servers know what they're doing.

I am thrilled to have gone to Carbone, finally. This is an institution in New York. It's one of the most classic Italian restaurants in New York City and it's known to have fantastic food and fantastic ambiance. A lot of celebrities and famous people have gone / go to Carbone. It is also known to have one of the most rigid processes to get a reservation -- it is very tough but it's worth it. 

The service is really great. It has an old school Italian vibe and when you are seated, we're given bread, salami and olives. The bread is one of the best breads I've had in my life. It is decadent and thick and buttery. 

We started off with the baked clams and caesar salad. Both were delicious. I can't get enough of a quality caesar salad and their croutons were to die for. Baked clams came with 9 pieces, 3 each of different flavors. Creamy, heavy and delicious. 

We ordered two pasta dishes, one mushroom and one vodka pasta. The spicy vodka pasta is the winner and I regret not getting two of these. It is spicy, creamy and perfectly al dente. It is an iconic dish but completely up to the hype. 

We finished off with the carrot cake which is a spectacle itself. It comes with a large beautiful piece with icing beautifully decorated. 

I will come back to Carbone and will order a vodka pasta for myself and try their veal parm next time.

Went for dinner a few nights ago . Seated right at reservation time at a larger than usual fir NYC table .
I got a deliciously cold Kir Royale and crunchy bruschetta, salmon oreganato, and tira misu for dessert. 
It was all lovely and wonderful. 
Love the old school waiters and dark candlelit dining room.  My son had pork chops and our host from Dior had the lobster pasta, everyone enjoyed their dishes very much and a fun time was had by all.

Came here for lunch to celebrate my boyfriend's birthday. We were seated at the patio. The service was impeccable. The main server was very kind and gave us great suggestions. 

We ordered the zucchini and eggplant as a starter and it was very light and tasty. 

We then ordered the spicy rigatoni and the lobster ravioli. Both were delicious and very flavorful. The food really exceeded my expectations! 

10/10!

Came here for a birthday dinner with friends and had a really delightful time. It's pretty packed and loud in the main location, but we were directed to the "other" location 2 blocks away. 

Ambiance: 5
The seating is a bit cramped but typical for nyc. I appreciated that the booths had glass panes to help with the distancing and noise levels.

Food: 4.5
Not as great as the hype but still very delicious. 
For starters, we got baked clams (not amazing but good and unique) and prosciutto with mozzarella (ABSOLUTELY AMAZING!! I loved the combo, probably my favorite of the evening). 
Pastas, we got the spicy rigatoni (very delicious but think it's a little to simple with nothing else but pasta) and fettuccine with mushrooms (really good pick, good flavor and lots of mushrooms without overwhelming the plate) 
Meats, we ordered veal Parmesan (also good but not incredible for me personally) and ribeye (cooked well but nothing outstanding)

Service: 5
I liked how there was a separate person to help us with the wine. We got 2 different bottles and our glasses were filled throughout the whole evening. Our server was helpful and always kept the table clear. 

Overall lovely visit and definitely a place to try at least once!

This place is so lame. I ate here one time prior, but my friend and I booked a reservation for my birthday and they cancelled the reservation on me the morning of. When I emailed them they said sorry there's nothing they can do about it and too bad..horrible customer service. Beware that they might cancel your res without any heads up. Go to L'artusi the food is 10x better and service is impeccable.

I sat outside. It was so hot no fans. The ac kept dripping all over my table and me. I also got bitten 10 times on my legs by mosquitoes and am very insecure abt how swollen they now are. Food was good hard to enjoy hot things in this heat

I didn't know that this was a well known / talked about place going in and lucked out that my friend had made a reservation way in advance for lunchtime.

Everything that we got in the picture was high quality and surprisingly filling given the portion sizes. The most notable items were the Vodka Rigatoni and Carrot Cake. 

Service and ambiance is 5 stars.

So why not a perfect score? Here's my take - I'd come to this place once to check it off my list and would only come back on the company's dime given the $$$$ and portion size. But still worth checking out at least once!

Finally made it! Set a notification on Resy for a Sunday dinner and luckily a 6 PM opened up a few days before. 

We were seated outside next to the restaurant on a 2 seater. The table was slightly slanted because we were seated on the sidewalk cellar door. 

Our server was hilarious, wish I remembered his name. Was excellent with cocktail recommendations (aperol spritz was definitely the mood) and vegetarian food recommendations. 

The complementary bread basket is divine, it comes with an assortment of fresh bread, fresh Parmesan like cheese, lightly pickled cauliflower, and some sort of sausage (which I didn't eat). 

We ordered the following:

+eggplant and zucchini scapece for appetizer: delicious. Even my meat eating friend thought this was amazing. The vegetables were perfectly grilled, and then topped with ricotta, shredded mozzarella, basil, and drizzled with chili oil and balsamic. Also super light because no carbs. 

+spicy rigatoni for shared entree: pasta is perfectly al dente and the sauce is rich yet not too heavy. Great flavor and actually has a kick in my opinion compared to other reviews I've read. This was completely finished. 

+fettuccine con funghi for personal entree: this dish was expertly cooked, has a lighter earthier flavor and was highly recommended by our server. I personally loved the vodka sauce in the rigatoni dish so much that I felt I couldn't enjoy this one as much. Had some leftovers to take home from this. 

+tortellini al Ragu: apparently this can be made vegetarian by subbing the Ragu sauce, for other vegetarians out there. My friend got it as is and said it was delicious. 

They also gave us complementary rainbow cookies to end out meal. 

All in all, would love to return if I can get a reservation again. Expensive but the service, food, and atmosphere is what you pay for and correctly priced.

Carbone is a must on a trip to NYC! The food, service, and ambiance are all great. Once seated, they'll bring you a basket of bread, an assortment of cheeses, and a bowl of pickled vegetables - which are all delicious (currently missing the pickled cauliflower). Their most famous menu item which you must order is the spicy vodka rigatoni. I typically don't like spicy foods or anything with tomatoes but this is SO GOOD, you will love it. On this trip, we also ordered the Langosteen to share (I believe it was there special of the day), Lobster Ravioli, and the Veal Marsala. Everything I've had here has always been amazing, no complaints. We also ordered a few glasses of wine based on the recommendations of the sommelier and they all paired very nicely with our meals. Can't wait to go back and try more!

Only things stopping me from giving a 5 star rating: it is pricy (I mean it does have 4 $'s), portions are a little small, and it's unnecessarily dark inside lol.

One thing to note is that due to COVID and spacing requirements at their original location, they're also operating out of their sister restaurant Sadelle's (menu/food is still the same). My first time at Carbone in October 2019 I ate at their original location. This most recent trip in April 2021, we ate at Sadelle's. Ambiance inside the original location and Sadelle's is very similar - Sadelle's is just much larger so Carbone might be cuter and more intimate for a date while Sadelle's might be better for big groups.

Pasta was perfect, enjoyed the al dente pasta with Carbone's signature vodka sauce. I've been here in the past with friends and stopped by for lunch today after shopping. We were able to get seated without a reservation although I recommend reservations in advance. They have an AmEx dining area which is an outdoor set up that is covered if you're looking to sit outside when the weather is nice. Bonus special was oysters from New Brunswick Canada, believe they were Caraquets or possibly Malpeques, finished with a lemony olive oil mixture. Delicious!

WHAT. A. MEAL.

my dining companion was so clutch and able to get a last minute reservation and we were so hyped!  the restaurant itself is pretty cute and cozy, very old-school vibe.  we were seated in the back and it was pretty comfy.

we got the spicy vodka rigatoni, meatballs, a green lasagna (daily special), and a lemon cheesecake to finish.  they also brought us fresh mozzarella, salami, and garlic bread.  the spicy vodka rigatoni was perfectly cooked to al dente, and the sauce was really flavorful and not spicy at all IMO.  definitely a must!  the meatballs were well-seasoned, and served with a bright and fresh tomato sauce and fried basil.  and the lemon cheesecake?  oh my! it was lemony-bright, creamy, the crust was still crunchy, and with just the right amount of sweetness (a not-too-sweet dessert is very important to me). it was the perfect ending to our meal. the portion size were on the petit side but i felt it was just enough food to share and try, without leaving with an itis.

aside from the food, our server was awesome and a real pro's pro if you will.  he was able give us wine recommendations, super knowledgeable about the menu, and just seemed to be on top of everything.  i'd say service really made this meal.  it was a very pricey meal, but i'm definitely keen to return for special occasions.

Absolutely amazing!! If you are visiting NYC make this a priority! The complimentary appetizers are delicious and be careful not to fill up on the bread. The Veal Parmigiana and Ragu is unmatched!! Reservations go fast!

What can I say that hasn't already been said??

After successfully snagging a last minute reservation (been trying for a very very long time) I finally was fortunate to visit the famous Carbone.

Now the meal me & my companion had was nothing short of delicious. The spicy rigatoni was cooked exceptionally well. The spiciness was perfect, something that eases up on you but is not overwhelming. The meatballs were seasoned & cooked to perfection.  

The Lasagna which was a daily special  was just ok (to me) but my companion enjoyed it very much. I can say that it was cooked very well, wasn't unevenly cooked (like with the usually moist center with dry outer crust). The meal also came with complimentary mozzarella, salami & two pieces of garlic bread which was just mouth watering. 

And to finish everything off, the waiter recommended the lemon cheesecake which to my surprise (not a big cheesecake fan)  was absolutely delicious. Super light, the lemon was not over powering. Just the right amount of flavor, texture & sweetness.

The waiter was absolutely on top of his game, I mean a real pro's pro. I  recently started to consume wine & being nothing of a expert, I told the waiter the specifics of the type of wine I have enjoyed in the past.  To which he proceeded to bring the perfect wine almost exact to my specifications.  He was also tentative but not overly tentative. It's almost as he knows off body language when to & not to approach the table to check on his customers. 

Carbone has been on the top of my list of Italian restaurants to visit for some time now. Overall my experience was what I had always hoped for. Fantastic food, even better service, & just really good ambiance. A real old school Italian restaurant feel. 

The only negative comment I could have is of course the price, but for a place as famous and sought after as the restaurant is you sort of expect that  

Carbone is somewhere I will definitely revisit whenever I can wether it be another lucky hit on a reservation or just going for a special occasion.

5/5 for great food and service
- The bread, mozzarella and salami: crunchy bread that went so well with the cheese. Salami is slightly spicy which we loved 
- Assorted baked clam: love love love. Adding a tiny bit of lemon juice and I can eat 10 more.
- Meat balls: my least favorite in the whole meal. I had better...
- Spicy rigatoni vodka: the star of the show. It's not too creamy. What a well done dish!
- Orecchiette vito: pesto based pasta with Italian sausage and some broccoli. Very good too 
- Tiramisu: for some reasons I tasted orange flavor in the sponge cake, which is a little odd. But it's a good dessert after all.

The service is very attentive. I will come back in my next trip to NYC

Nothing on earth brings me more genuine delight than seeing the carbone sign from down the street. Walking in I feel like I'm transported to an episode of the Sopranos. An old school red sauce joint where the captains treat you like royalty. 

Just the free pre appetizers will show you that you are in good hands. Their bread is divine. The mozzarella is creamy and perfect. And the salami is magnificent. 

Not every pasta on the menu is my favorite but the good ones more than make up for it. The spicy vodka pasta is perfection and almost the best pasta I've ever had. It's not the best pasta I've ever had because of the tortellini al ragu. This was hand crafted by the gods. 

Mario's meatballs are what my grandma wishes her meatballs were like. They are delicious and put generations of my family to shame. The veal parm is perfectly thin, crisp, and flavorful. If you have a complaint about the veal parm there is something wrong with your tastebuds and you don't deserve to be taking up a coveted seat at carbone. 

I love carbone so much I have literally booked tables two nights in a row because nothing will ever compare. If you love good food you must come here

This restaurant is first class... simple, authentic Italian dishes done right.  Beautifully decorated, comfortable seating and staff is friendly, welcoming and knowledgeable.  There are no words to accurately describe the spicy rigatoni vodka, it is heaven- I was happy that they had a GF pasta option which is served perfectly al dente every time.  Bravo!

First off before I begin. Service was exceptional. Water the second your glass was half full. Manager super receptive to birthday wishes (cake).  Bread basket was the best I've had in NYC. Caesar was made table side and lived up to the hype. Fresh, cheesy, salty, and they even ask if you want your anchovies on top or on the side. Croutons were huge gorgeous hunks of lightly toasted bread. To die for.

Veal park was unstoppable. This was why we came. And it lives up to the hype. Delicate crisp cheese saucy goodness.

The spicy rigatoni, in my opinion, was fine. My girlfriend makes a better one musing Barilla and heavy cream. I still enjoyed though but could imagine people thinking it's too spicy.

They generously bright out a huge tiramasu slice for my girlfriends birthday. Appreciated that.

Amazing ambience, service and hope to come back soon

Came here this past weekend for my birthday brunch, though we were almost an hour late, due to circumstances beyond our control, (losing my purse in a cab) Julian the host was kind enough to still sit us. David was our server, we had the mozzarella to start, it had a nice texture and was very tasty/fresh, then the oysters and carpaccio, the oysters were very tasty, but the latter was a bit too acidic for my taste. 
For the mains , we shared the spicy rigatoni vodka, which is 
one of their signature dishes - absolutely tasty, but I didn't care much for the Ragu. Now time for dessert, I'm not big on sweets, never had a sweet tooth, but david the server came and I quote "birthday girl, let us offer you dessert" he then goes on to list  some of the items on the menu,  because of the way he said it, it seemed to us, that it would be on the house, because we really didn't care for more food as we were stuffed, he pushes and we say ok, (afterwards it occurred to us, that he was just up selling and not offering) he brings out the tiramisu with a candle, which was appreciated, but I could barely have any as it wasn't very great to be honest, I've had way better tiramisu in the past, it was all sugar, for $20 it should've been better.
Now, you can see my previous review of this place was a 5 star glowing review, here's where things went awry, the check comes and the dessert is added to the bill, my partner and I look at each other, surprised, it's not about the cost, but that we were blindsided, and to make matters worse, it wasn't great, I bring this up to him, and he feigns surprise/ acts ignorant, he then walks away, waits for us to settle the bill then comes back, with a whole fake concern saying , "oh let me see if I can take it off the bill" this is something he could've said 5 mins before when we complained, and not after we had paid, he did this, knowing we (especially my partner would say it's cool or whatever) I have had better here, and the fact that not all we ordered was top notch was disappointing. More annoying is that, you can never reach them on the phone, to make amendments to a res, why inconvenience guests that way?! Even 5 star restaurants don't act so haughty and impossible to reach. Hence I am taking out two stars. David, do better.
Quality old-school Italian cuisine! I personally prefer more innovative takes on Italian food, but for the classics and the atmosphere Carbone is definitely a great spot.

Food was good but not amazing. The pasta was good. Thought the 10% covid surcharge was a little tacky (they're already charging $30+ for a plate of pasta). The "outside" seating in the little hut was pretty cold also.  Would return but only if I could sit indoors.

Thrilled to have gotten a spot indoors before leaving NY! Excellent food, service, and drinks - weary that it wouldn't live up to the hype but it definitely did. The starting breads were delicious- warm and soft with a block of parmesan and other meats/pickled veggies. Ordered the spicy vodka rigatoni - creamy with a bit of heat and had a unique flavor compared to other vodka sauces- flavor reminded me cheese pizza with pepper flake. Also split the veal parmesan- crispy and thin and the pomodoro sauce was really good. Sadly too full for dessert but they gave us cute Italian rainbow cookies which I really liked. Fantastic experience.

My friend and I had a fantastic time at Carbone. We arrived 15 minutes before our reservation and they were able to seat us which was great. The ambiance inside is so inviting and fun. All of the servers and staff were really lovely and attentive. We started with a Caesar salad which was delicious, and then got the spicy rigatoni and the lobster ravioli. Both dishes were phenomenal! I was pleasantly surprised that the spicy rigatoni was actually spicy since I love spicy food and many similar dishes at other restaurants are never spicy. We ended our meal with the chocolate dessert which was the only disappointing part of our meal since I didn't care for it too much. We ended up staying for 3 hours and had a wonderful evening thanks to the good food and drinks, excellent service, and fun ambiance. I'm already looking forward to my next meal here!

We had an 11:30pm reservation last night, and our experience was nothing short of amazing. They sat us down immediately, and our waiter Paul was such a delight. We had the Caesar salad, spicy rigatoni, lobster ravioli, and the truffle corn. Trust me-- you need the truffle corn. The appetizers were also delicious. We had a great time conversing with Samuel throughout our meal as he picked up our plates. Both Paul and Samuel were AMAZING hosts! Samuel came back to our table right before we left to ask if we enjoyed our meal, and we really appreciated that! We wanted to say our thanks to Paul before leaving as well, but he was in the back so we weren't able to. UNTIL Paul came running out of the restaurant as we left to shake our hands and thank us for coming! If you make reservations here, you NEED the Paul-Samuel duo. Both of them made our experience exceptional.

We had luck making reservations by pre-registering our credit card on the Resy app & refreshing the reservation page until it hit 10am, 2 weeks in advance.
Sooooooooo gooood!!! Tough to get a dinner reservation but worth it! The spicy vodka rigatoni is a must have but the lobster ravioli is the star of the show!

3.75/4

Their pastas and desserts were great. The meat mains -- veal parm, meatballs-- were okay, not spectacular. Don't expect anything super out of the box, the style is more traditional Italian American elevated/ done well. 2nd visit.

We ordered:
- Caesar ZZ
- Corn
- Veal parm
- Meatballs
- Spicy rigatoni
- Lobster ravioli
- Carrot cake
- Chocolate cake
- Cheesecake
- Tiramisu

There is a reason why this place is a NYC favorite. Even the appetizer is phenomenal -- cannot get enough of the Mozzarella! Spicy rigatoni is probably the most chewy and tasteful pasta I have ever had. Parmesan veal was also great except the portion is big so definitively come on an empty stomach or get it to go. 

PRO TIP: 
1. Reservations are hard to get especially during normal dinner time but lunch slots are easier so if you're free definitely grab the lunch slots

Cant say enough about this restaurant that would give it proper justice. Julian is the man so if he's there you will feel right at home. The service is excellent and the food is just unworthy of reviews because you can't explain how amazing everything is without selling it the right way. Most people who eat Italian usually know when the bread is on point you normally are set for a bomb ass meal because even though ur full from the bread u still demolish every other bite of food they bring you. The lamb chops were just illegal because now I can't eat them anywhere else. The clams casino and clam orgasim lol I mean oreganata were by far the best I've ever had and I know people say that a lot but I have Mabye written 3 reviews in my life and the other two were because I usually can't wait to tell u to run away cause I can't stand going out and being disappointed so I'm telling u that combo served together was just ridiculous and anytime a restaurant has things that Arnt on the menu and Arnt a special but they have them everyday. YOU DONT BE STUPID AND YOU ORDER WHATEVER THOSE ITEMS ARE because what that means is we have them until we don't. And I'n this case the meatballs app were also the by far a masterpiece. There will always be one jerkoff who isn't happy but this place is a 5/5 star thru and thru. If this helps atleast one person go here I'm happy because it's just that f**king good. AND just tell Julian as long as he doesn't sit u at me new personal table in the back that corey sent you and I only take a 20% vig
Worst experience ever talking to a host. Please train your host staff better and teach them how to be AT LEAST polite and not degrading

Never disappoints always delicious

Linguine vongole was a killer. First time having the veal Marsala and it's so different from everywhere else. Spicy rigatoni vodka best in the city

First of all our waiter Mark was amazing! He set the stage for a beautiful dinner and experience which is why this 5 stars. Not just the food is amazing but the service and ambiance was perfect. We tried out so many different dishes all fantastic. We will be back!

Before coming here, I had the mindset of giving it one less start of the overall experience based on the annoying and impossible reservation system. But it was just too good honestly. I found this place due to tiktok/Instagram hype, but had no idea how hard it would be to secure a reservation. Ended up getting reservation for Saturday night, which was the day I wanted to go originally. Started with the Cesar salad that the prepare in front of you. And it really is a good as people say it is. The bread and starters the bring to the table as good as well. I don't like cauliflower that much, but whatever they mixed with theirs made it delicious. As a main, we had the spicy rigatoni, tortellini, and meatballs. All were delicious. The rainbow cookies at the end were a plus as well! Will definitely come back here, or visit the Las Vegas location since it's closer. 10/10

I'm here to tell you that the spicy rigatoni indeed lives up to the hype. I was able to get a last minute table for 1 and had the best dinner on the patio. The different breads and charcuterie that they bring out to start is perfect, and the marinated cauliflower salad is some of the best I've ever had. The pasta way perfectly portioned and delightfully creamy and spicy. Can't wait to come back!

One of my favorite restaurants in the city!  I always order the baked clams to start, followed by several pastas.  Vodka rigatoni and lobster raviolis are a must!  I tried the orecchiette the last time I was there as well and that was also really good. I don't think you can go wrong with any of the dishes here.  My husband and I always end the meal with carrot cake and we usually can't finish it because we've eaten way too much pasta.

After much anticipation and difficulty getting a reservation we finally made it to Carbone but unfortunately we're seated in the AMEX patio outside, as this was the only available space.

First course a Caesar salad and the baked clams. Cesar salad was excellent as where the clams quite nicely prepared. Our second chorus was the rigatoni which was exceptional while spicy as the name indicated

The main take away is that the interior is too loud to enjoy your meal. You will have to yell over your neighbor to be heard over the blaring music.

Also the pacing of the courses was too slow. It took 2 hours to eat and near the end you just want to get out of there because of all the yelling and loud music.

Had the tuna starter which tasted good but should of been served in a cold plate rather than a not cold plate that was placed on a big bowl of ice. It doesn't have time to chill.

The vodka pasta is great but you can get the same quality from more causal neighborhood trattorias.

The pork chop and peppers was ok but was expecting more tang from vinegar. It was a little on the fatty side but was well cooked and juicy.

The branzino was very well cooked but is big and not really for one person. It should definitely be shared especially when you are getting many other dishes.
