The artichoke side was very mediocre and not good at all.

The chocolate cake was dense, heavy, and not good at all. The teaspoon of ice cream they put on top melted in 30 seconds.

The bread serving and chunk of Parmesan they give you are nice.

4.75/5

I have been to Carbone 4 times now with work and I will continue to go back whenever possible. However, I will only go back with work due to the cost. This is a corporate card restaurant. Docking .25 stars for cost and noise.

Carbone is a New York Italian-American institution - a temple built to the gods of Parmigiano-Reggiano and Spicy Rigatoni.

Highlights include:

Amuse bouche of a hunk of Parmesan, grandma bread, pickled vegetables

Warm fresh mozzarella with balsamic roasted red peppers and onions (new item I had on my last visit - not sure where this is on the menu)

Spicy Rigatoni Vodka - star of the show

Meatballs

Dover Piccata

Carrot cake

Skip:

Veal Parmesan - overpriced and overhyped

Funghi Trifolati - chewy and forgettable

If you're hungry:

Caesar alla ZZ

Broccoli Rabe

It is easy to overindulge and overeat, so be careful!

I have no doubt that Carbone is a top NYC restaurant and recommend the splurge if you are able to snag a reservation.

Found my favorite restaurant ever. Finally was able to get a reservation here on. Friday at 1 pm for my Birthday  lunch was only time available.  This place is like nothing else. So professional soon as you step inside it takes u to 1930. Service is impeccable.  Such an old school feeling. 
Soon as you sit they bring over to you the best warm creamy Buffalo mozzarella that they cut with a scissors. Garlic bread amazing. 
Spicy capicola melts in mouth on house. 
We ordered meatballs app which I never order out but omg these were amazing just    Meat clouds that melt in mouth. Marinara I wanted to take a bath in. 
Also ordered assorted bake clams. Three different prepared clams one better then the next. Never had such clean fresh explode in your mouth clams. One clam had uni over the top really delish 
There's 2 items that are a must to order when you come here. 
Spicy rigatoni vodka was the best pasta dish I ever had. The sauce was so creamy so decadent spicy exactly enough. Pasta Al dente really incredible dish. They split dish in half for us. 
Still thinking about this dish 
Other dish u must order is veal parmigiana with the bone.  The dish is huge for two people. Comes out and waiter presents it to you then cuts at table. Comes with the bone on plate for you to take under table and gnarl on under table lol. 4 of us shared two veal parm dishes and I have lunch for today. 
On the side we ordered a special creamy corn side dish. Corn was so creamy and cheesy and to top it off they shaved truffles over the top of it. It was truly heaven  .
Then to top off the dinner they came out with a slice of the best chocolate cake I ever had. Covered with fresh marinated cherries and they were nice enough to put a candle in it for us. 
Complimentary Tri color cookies for table too. 
Expresso was legit too 
I found my new best restaurant and my new birthday dinner place 
Only issue is getting a table. It's very hard but worth trying to get here
Yes pain in ass to drive to NYC. 
Yes pain to find parking 
Yes it's extremely expensive 
But once to sit down and they bring out the food it's worth all the aggravation

By far, the best Italian food. The service was incredible. Ask for Daniel, he was so fun and very welcoming and helped with recommendations for
the whole meal. Come with an appetite as portions are big, but great for sharing. Highly recommend getting multiple dishes. Staff was very friendly and amazing! Don't forget to get a little strawberry candy once you leave, you know the ones you would find in your grandmother's purse.

I had the worst experience at carbone. I'm sure the food is great but the staff is condescending, unpleasant and rude. They turned away a table for two after accommodating a table reserved for 8 and allowing them to sit 10 people. The experience is 80 percent of the time spent at a restaurant. I hope you think about re staffing soon because it was horrible .

I can't speak highly enough about our meal and the service at Carbone.  All the food and wine we had was absolutely excellent and worth every penny.  I'll be craving everything we ordered, especially the spicy rigatoni vodka, until the next time we can get over there.

TL;DR: One Michelin star Italian restaurant worth trying just once in your lifetime. Reservations is a pain, food is super expensive due to high demand, but you can expect it to taste like $$$, maybe you'll spot some A-list celebrities or IG model/influencers (whatever you want to call them). There's a hidden service fee.

Review #900. Woot!

Firstly, as everyone stated in their reviews, the reservation system is a pain in the ass. They state that dinner spots are released seven days in advance while lunch spots are released 14 days ahead. I found that to be false as the majority of the reservations are released the day of between 9AM-noon, with the best bet being around 11AM-noon. I was fortunate to grab one on my birthday week, just a few days earlier as I wasn't going to risk not being able to snag a table on my birthday. I was also able to add an additional guest by emailing the corporation that owns this restaurant. I think they allowed it only because I booked an outdoor seat and my reservation was on a Tuesday. It was the only thing I was stressing about the entire day until they finally got back to me about it two hours before the scheduled reservation.

We were seated by the hostess without the entire party, which is rare for a lot of restaurants in NYC. I had one person show up late and I'm glad this didn't cause us to lose our table. We were assisted immediately by one of the busboys, making sure we had plates, utensils, napkins, wine glasses, pretty much what you'd expect from a fine dining restaurant. Next our waiter came out and greeted us, took our drink orders, and provided us with a basket of assorted bread, mozzarella, cauliflower, and salami. Then the waiter disappeared for an hour, which we never placed our food order yet. We ended up placing our order with what appears to be one of the managers?, one of the guys in suits, who checked in on us, luckily. The following is what everyone ordered/shared with the table:

Appetizers
Oysters (6pc) ($24) - imported from Greece, I think, as I loosely remembered what the person stated. $4 per oyster is a lot compared to a lot of spots offering $1 oysters, but you can expect them to taste like $4 oysters, high quality. Don't believe they're on the menu so you have to request them.
Octopus Pizzaiolo ($29) - not worth it. Two pieces of octopus with a bunch of cooked peppers in the mix. 
Assorted Baked Clams (three of each kind) ($25) - I had a party of 5 so I was able to order two more assortments for $7 each. These are definitely worth getting.

Entrees:
Mario's Meatballs (3pc) ($27) - Not on the menu so you'll have to make the request. Make sure you order this because it's a staple.
Lobster Ravioli ($39) - The entree I ordered for myself. Just amazing. Will leave you thinking about it the next day.
Spicy Rigatoni Vodka ($32) - Also a staple. Best to be shared amongst the party.
Linguini Vongole ($36) - No comment. My friends seemed to have nothing bad to say about it.

Towards the end of the meal, the original waiter brought out Rainbow Cookies and we ordered one dessert for my birthday celebration, which was a cheesecake ($18). Don't recommend ordering any of the desserts as they all probably cost double than what they're worth.

Also good to note that they do slap on a service fee of about 18%? You won't know this unless you ask for the full receipt breakdown and they won't tell you about the fee either.

Glad I finally got here. A lot of Carbone lives up to the hype. The classyness of the waitstaff is up there, pretty much hands down the best service I've had in NYC. You really feel like you're being waited on and taken care of, without it feeling uncomfortable or fake. As for the food, everything was certainly good. The complimentary starter of bread basket, salami, cauliflower and cheese were all excellent. The bread and cheese especially were incredible. I've never had cheese like that. My date actually asked for another piece. The bread sticks had a chewy, mochi kind of texture, again this was a first. So, I haven't even gotten to the main courses and this place already is worth the trouble of getting in. I didn't find the spicy rigatoni to be that special, and the meatballs were good but not mind blowing. The veal parmesan however was outstanding, must try this. Carrot cake had good presentation but nothing special taste wise for me. This place has a reputation for being hard to get into but it seems that this is because its not made clear that the dinner reservations are made available at 9 AM one week in advance while the lunch times are made available at 10 AM two weeks in advance. But it appears their lunch menu is nearly identical to the dinner menu anyway so its not the end of the world if you can't get a dinner reservation. If you're on Resy at 9 I think you shouldn't have a problem getting a dinner spot.

It's expensive and hard to get a reservation... but it's good. I wanted to try Carbone, despite the criticisms, and I'm glad I did. The online res system doesn't really work--I checked the exact minute they opened up availability for my target date, and they had nothing posted. But sign up for the notifications, that's how I got an email about an opening and snagged it. My friends and I went for lunch. The inside is dark and well-decorated, making it feel like a classy dinner even in the middle of the day. They bring mozzarella, charcuterie, and bread to the table with the menus (which, side note, are comically large--I felt like I was reading a newspaper). We ordered one of their specials, a caprese made with fresh Pennsylvania heirloom tomatoes and more mozzarella, to share. Then I had the spicy rigatoni vodka pasta. It wasn't what I expected from a vodka sauce--it had a slightly sweet, red pepper taste to it. I liked it a lot, but was surprised by how different it was. I also had a glass of Arneis, which went really well with the pasta and the cheesecake I had for dessert. Because somehow, I had room for dessert after that. The cheesecake was so creamy and well-done, and the layer of lemon curd on top really brought it all together. They also bring some small Italian rainbow cookies for the table. I was really satisfied with the meal, and the service made it even better. Our waiter was kind, funny, full of good suggestions, and knowledgeable about the food and wine. While this was more of an expensive treat than a regular spot, I'm so glad we went.

Exquisite, worth the hype. 

Definitely pricey but Carbone is known across the world as a top Italian restaurant. Their spicy rigatoni does not disappoint along with the plentiful appetizers
Overpriced and underwhelming. The rigatoni is great, but not worth all the hype. Our waiter also made us way way over order for lunch and I felt so sick and full after.

Great food, service and atmosphere. Need I say more?.  Beef carpaccio was awesome as if I was eating soft ice cream. It was so soft.  And I was impressed with their ribye steak.  I would go back this place when I travel back to New York.

Let's start by saying we were looking forward to coming here for weeks. Literally couldn't wait to make it there. We managed to grab some reservations for a Sunday lunch. And boy did this place no disappoint. 

We started with the fresh apps such as the mozzarella, warm incredible bread and cured meat. We started with the clams, my favorite out of the three different types was the uni one. We also had the heirloom tomatoes with fresh mozz. Extremely delicious and fresh. The martinis we had were also made to PERFECTION. We ordered the veal parm, spicy rigatoni, truffle corn, and the tortellini. The spicy rigatoni is life changing, and that was easily the best veal parm I've ever had. So good that after I write this review I'm going to find another reservation ASAP. 

The service was top notch as well, and for everything we ate and drank the bill wasn't anything shocking. Honestly this is one of the nest Italian restaurants I've ever been too and I'm usually a huge fan of mom and pop spots but this takes the cake. Keep up the wonderful work carbone!

Carbone was so worth the wait and the carbs I loaded up on. I was stuffed for the entire day and had absolutely no regrets!

As soon as we were seated, they brought over complimentary bread, spicy salami, and fresh mozzarella. I enjoy the salami and cheese but felt the bread was too crunchy for my liking. I ordered the infamous Spicy Rigatoni Vodka which was love at first bite. The portion was perfect. I shared a few bites with the hubby but this plate was way more than enough for me. Hubby ordered the Lobster Ravioli and had nothing but good things to say about it. His portion looked super tiny but he was quite pleased with it.

We also ordered a few sides: Broccoli Rabe & Funghi Trifolati (mushrooms). I'll be honest, I needed some veggies so it was nice but the sides were portioned a little larger so I don't recommend it that much unless you're dining with more than 2 people. We were stuffed! 

The Italian cookie at the end made my day. It was colorful, moist, and delicious. I secretly wanted to ask for more but could not build up the courage to do it. All in all, I enjoyed my experience at Carbone. It truly lived up to its hype. Cheers.

Carbone is the perfect mix of homey and glamor. The flavors are delicious and unpretentious, while the ambiance makes you feel like the most ordinary day is a special occasion. Love this place - it will never get old!

Before I went people were telling me it's not as good, they're too commercial now, etc, etc. We loved it! The food was excellent - especially the chicken parm and the penne vodka. We also loved the vibe, great music, and great service. Definitely going back!

In short: not worth the hype, or the all-for-show hassle of getting a reservation.

We had a 5 45pm reservation, and until 7pm, half of the outdoor tables (and 2 of maybe 10 indoor tables) were completely empty! There was even 1 guy dining alone at a table for 4. By the time we left at 8 30pm, there were still approx. 3 open tables outside, that had never been used all night. Pretty ridiculous when the reservations are 'so hard to snag', making people eat early bird or late night specials!

Yes, the famous Spicy Rigatoni Vodka was incredible (should be at $32!!)--although, super disappointingly, it came out lukewarm. The Lemon Ricotta Cheesecake was to die for--like eating a pillowy cloud; not too lemony, and the thin graham cracker crust gave it the perfect, balanced crunch.

The $20 cocktails are alarmingly expensive, especially for the size. The Caesar alla ZZ was very oversauced. The Meatballs (always available, though off-menu) had a very sweet flavor, which was unexpected. And the Tiramisu was dryer than a mothball--my friend said the ladyfinger tasted like chemicals and forbid me to try it.

The infamous star of the show was the Asian lady manager, who I'm told lives for the bad press. Our (incredibly nice) server let my friend join for a quick drink while we waited for our next course (it takes a w h i l e for courses to come out). We were at an outdoor table for 2 and he said no problem, just pull up a chair for a bit. Next thing we knew, this manager was hovering over us, passive aggressively dismissing our explanation of why we'd pulled up a chair, not even really looking at us, and treating us as if we were idiots and had conceived of the (preposterous idea) ourselves. Before we could get a word in, she had tyrannically informed us to kick our friend out asap, essentially get ahold of ourselves (lol), and then huffed off.

That said, the rest of the wait and service staff was stellar and very kind :) Quick fill waters, ask if we needed anything else, check on how things were--a little too quick to clear still-being-eaten food though!

All in all, there are much better (and less expensive) pasta-focused restaurants within a 10 minute radius--go there instead.

Barely snagged a late night reservation, but hey it's Carbone! I was suuuuper excited for this place while I was in NY, however, I was kind of disappointed. I felt like it was overhyped, yes even the famous rigatoni pasta. We ordered a bunch of things and shared. The service was great though. 

Spicy Rigatoni Pasta: 4/5
Lobster Ravioli: 4/5
Meatballs: 3/5
Veal Parmigiana: 2/5 
Caesar Salad: 1/5 okay, my husband and I both hated it. Tasted old.  
Mozzarella: 4/5 I thought this was free, but they charged for it?

It's a pain to get a reservation here but I think it's worth the hype. My advice would be to stick to ordering the pastas and the appetizers. The spicy vodka rigatoni is a must order.  Of the desserts, I'd reccomend the carrot cake but for $18 you can get something better in the neighborhood.

I'm surprised this only has 4 stars overall. This place is awesome ! And very very nice. The service here is 11/10. We loved our waiter he was so jolly and personable and really made you feel like royalty. Such a treat. The vibe is insanely cozy and old world class. There's a reason this is such a popular spot today. My favorite was the hot house-made mozzarella on the caprese salad started. Talk about authentic and fresh. The best damn tomato's I've ever had too and I typically hate tomato's lol. Can't say enough about that hot mozzarella that was so professionally cut right infront of us. Seriously an exquisite experience ! But the free bread and antipasto alone at the beginning was a win too. Tomato pie bread, classic Italian, and even garlic bread with cold cut meat and cauliflower. Then a man came over and legit cut off a piece of Parmesan (maybe? ) cheese off a massive wheel on a plate and gave it to us. It was soooo cool. Like what?!!! The queen of all bread baskets forreal. Although I must say I did not like that cauliflower. Which was fine because I didn't come to be healthy. Spicy rigatoni was not spicy. But very very good. We had the specials meat balls with it and it was too much food to eat but that's always a good thing. They were delicious. My friend loved the tortellini. All cream sauce bases for our table and we loved. We got free Italian cookies for dessert too upon not ordering dessert. Waiter said he couldn't let us leave without something sweet which was very SWEET of him haha! He was really great about drinks too and made my friend a wonderful cocktail after requesting just something with vodka and refreshing since she didn't know wht she wanted. I loved it here and felt so cool being there. Must try for anyone looking for some good Italian with a fabulous experience as well.
Food was top-notch and this place lives up to its reputation. The price is high but the flawless service and exceptional quality makes it seem worth it... for special occasions would recommend.

I flew in from Los Angeles just to try this place. I have been dreaming of coming here since four years ago. And let me tell you... 

I had very very high expectations for this place. I've always seen their spicy rigatoni vodka on Instagram and was always drawn to try it. I don't even like tomato based sauces but something about this one I had to just taste. 

Each day that passed after making the decision I needed to try carbone, I would literally hear about Carbone from celebrities like Halsey and Selena Gomez periodically through interviews or paparazzi photos. It was a sign that I needed to try it.

As you enter into the restaurant, the vibe is very cute and almost old fashioned. The service is an 11/10. Unbelievable. They take their time with you. They speak to you with grace and patience. They also give you a large complimentary platter of bread with salami and pickled cauliflower which all tasted so delectable.

For mains, we ordered the lobster ravioli and of course my highly anticipated spicy rigatoni vodka. The lobster ravioli was a fan favorite of my group, but the spicy rigatoni vodka exceeded all of my very high set expectations. It has almost a seafood sauce flavor with an echo of spice at the same time. The pop of flavor you get with each bite is incredible. We ordered a double portioned rigatoni for our table of 5. We also got the tortellini which was okay! 

We also got a palette cleansing Italian flag cake prior to our dessert. It tasted so good! We also got the chocolate almond cherry cake and a carrot cake. The carrot cake was ok. The chocolate almond cherry cake was better! So soft and moist with a light flavor that wasn't too rich or heavy. 

Overall, amazing experience that exceeded all of my expectations. A truly epic New York dining experience. This place is no joke and lives up to the hype. Highly recommend going here if you are planning to go to NYC.
From start to finish, Carbone lived up to its hype.  Rigatoni vodka and tableside Caesar salad for two were excellent.  Chianti was also excellent.

I've been in the hospitality business for close to 50 years.  We had very high expectations for Carbone.  The expectations were exceeded.  Great service from the moment we stepped in til we completed our meal. Wonderful food.  Will return. Thank you

After trying to get reservations INSIDE, we finally got the opportunity to come try this place. From the moment we entered until we left the service was impeccable. We started off with the spicy rigatoni (yes we wanted to split) and got some meatballs and pork chops. The pork chops were absolutely delicious, the best pork chops I have ever had in my life. The meatballs were perfectly seasoned and melted. The spicy rigatoni was absolutely delicious. Our server Chris was great and super friendly and accommodating. They start you off with fresh mozzarella, pepperoni and garlic bread. All of the food was absolutely delicious, I definitely would like to come back here and try more things off the menu. Terrific place, if you get reservations don't let them slip away.

#Carbone - a NYC Italian-American favorite for many. 

Reservations are highly recommended (indoor/outdoor tables available). 

Vaccine check at the door. We were seated in the back room. It's dimly lit, has the old school Italian vibe.

Upon being seated, you are asked for your drink order and a basket of different bread, salami, cauliflower, and parmesan-reggiano is set on the table. This appears to be on the house but at the end of the bill - we noticed $18.00 for "2 panna". Just something to note about this hidden service fee.

DISHES: Spicy Rigatoni, Tortellini al Ragu, Mario's meatballs. This was brought out family style so we got to serve ourselves. My favorite dish was the Spicy Rigatoni. I was savoring every bite. The rest of the dishes felt like something I can find at a local Italian place with half the price tag.
 
I love ending my meals with dessert. I had the Black Forest Cake ($18.00). This was unmemorable and overprice. I would skip out on dessert. 

I went with 4 stars due to feeling rushed throughout our dinner. I turned to get bread and before I knew it, one of the dishes was gone. I was still working on it. I noticed one of the waiter/bus-boys continue looking my way to see if I was done with my pasta. It was uncomfortable. If we are paying a bill that is about to be over $200.00 - I want to take my time enjoying the dishes especially considering this was just about half an hour into the dinner. 

I'm glad I got to try Carbone at least once. Would I come back for a second time? I'm not rushing back - I think there's other NYC gems that I have to to try before returning

Carbone is a NYC staple where it's hard to get a reservation, bookings only thru Resy, no phone # listed for restaurant. No reply on IG or via email either. The restaurant is super small about 10 tables which is probably why it's so hard to get a reservation because although the food is good it's NOT amazing! 
The complimentary bread bowl was pretty good, comes with pickled cauliflower which is VERY sour. 
The assorted baked clams are a great app choice, comes with 3 different types of clams (9 PCs $25). Caprese salad was ok ($24) 
For entree we had the spicy rigatoni which is the main reason we come here, I wish the portion was bigger!  
Spaghetti pomodoro was tasteless , also a small portion ($28)  
Shrimp scampi - large Madagascar shrimp, $24 per piece, shrimp were very large but also tasteless and a little undercooked
Salmon is a large portion, it was good but also undercooked, sent it back to cook more and they didn't really cook it much. 
For dessert we had the Nutella tiramisu, it was big enough to share.
They give you complimentary rainbow cookies at the end. 
Waiter was very friendly and attentive.
Overall not worth $500 for 4 people (we had 1 round of drinks).
Cake cutting fee $15 per person 
I debated between 3 or 4 stars, decided on 4 because the waiter, baked clams , & spicy rigatoni made up for the rest

Much like everyone else, this was the best pasta I've ever had!!! We got the Spicy Rigatoni Vodka as usual and it's mind blowing. Yes, THAT GOOD. The waiter told us about some eggplant appetizer and we decided to give it a shot and it was fresh and delightful! The bread here is also *chefs kiss* 

If you can get a reservation, run to Carbone!!!

Went to Carbone to celebrate my birthday. Getting a reservation was a pain,  but oh boy was it worth it. In all honesty, I can say that Carbone truly lives up to the hype. The food was delicious and while on the pricier side, the portions were very generous. The overall experience, including food, quality of service, and ambience is definitely a 10/10. 

I had the Caesar alla zz, the spicy rigatoni, the veal Parmesan and the carrot cake. Undoubtedly, the highlight of my meal was the spicy rigatoni which is even better and more scrumptious than I imagined. Also, not too many mention this but free appetizers are truly a game changer!

Reservations: They say you can reserve on Resy two weeks in advance for lunch and one week in advance for dinner, but I found that that's not always true. They actually had open some dinner reservations two weeks in advance at 10am Eastern. (That means if you wanted to get a reservation on Aug. 14, you'd book on Aug. 1 at 10am.) The times were limited though--I think they had 5pm and 10pm open. Otherwise, I think they open the rest of the dinner reservations at 9am one week in advance. Lunch reservations open at 10am two weeks in advance. They disappear quickly but if you book right when it opens, you should have no trouble getting any time you want. For Resy, make sure you have your credit card information already entered in your profile so you don't waste any time securing the reservation once you're ready to book it. 

Food: pricey, but worth it. It was about ~$400 for 5 people, and we ordered drinks, an appetizer, and dessert. You definitely don't have to shell out the big bucks just to eat here, but we were celebrating a birthday so we decided to splurge. Was a little worried this place would be overhyped, but the portions weren't bad, which was a nice surprise, and the food tasted great. Spicy rigatoni vodka was excellent. I also loved the scallops. I would stick with the entrees, the desserts weren't super special (we had cheesecake, tiramisu, and the chocolate cake). If you tell them it's your birthday on Resy, they will bring you a cake with a candle! We left feeling satisfied, and I would recommend!
Lobster ravioli never disappoints. Great wine, great food, great service. Off menu items are great too.

Finally was able to get another reservation tonight and carbone never disappoints. The food and service are best in class and always consistent! We love the spicy rigatoni, grandma's meatballs, almond cookies for dessert and the bread basket! We have tried a few other dishes but these are always the favorites!

Walked into a quaint italian restaurant which had a charming decor and ambience.  There are two separate dining rooms, I would recommend the back room if you want less traffic around you and privacy. Homemade mozzarella is well described on other reviews.  It was warm and nice but nothing that blows you away.  Half shell oysters were fresh and nicely prepped without overpowering vinaigrette.  It was delicious.  Baked clams came in three different preparations.  One with Uni is worth trying but the dish as a whole was underwhelming.   I had the spicy rigatoni as I was having a craving for pasta.  It was cooked nicely but too salty and not very savory.  This is an overly hyped dish.  I left disappointed.

When you accidentally eat at a Michelin-starred restaurant. When in NYC!

Food & atmosphere: Carbone made me feel like I'm dining in Italy, with the beautiful garden parklet outside and the Godfather vibes inside. This New York institution is not to be missed!  Amazing drinks and the best vodka pasta I've ever had.  Reservations are not easy to get but I managed to snag a cancellation. 

Service: A little strange. The waiter was friendly but seemed to be rushing us to order when I was indecisive. We also asked him how much he recommended us to order - he said two starters and two entrees, so we took his advice. However what we ordered was WAY too much for 2 people - it was enough for 4 people. So we spent twice the amount of money that we needed to and a lot of the food also went to waste. =/
My son wanted to take us to one of his fav Michelin's. Good food! Nice servings. A bit noisy tonight. I guess folks are over excited for the holiday weekend.

It lives up to the name and hype for me. The staff were so kind and love the ambience of a true NYC Italian spot. We had the Caesar that was so good, and a burrata salad (wow) the spicy rigatoni with a scallop dish () , and truth be told, they prepared the meal very well. 

I also appreciated the gesture of bread and fresh burrata they serve to start and the rainbow cookie at the end! Thank you to the staff!

This place is so overrated honestly. The old world charm and decor appeals to the neighbourhood crowd but the food standards are essentially very low. Mediocre food, a 50 minute wait for the food. Appetiser sized entrees, excess cream and salt. We had at reservation confirmation at 1:30pm and once we showed up they said that it wasn't in their system. Instead of checking if a table was available they kept talking in an aggressive tone and saying "it's not in our system". We had a reservation at 1:30pm and the food reached our table at 3:15pm. Even a Serafina is a million times better than this junk!

Carbone came recommended and more than lived up to my expectations which were high to begin with. The meal started with complimentary bread and focaccia al pomodoro, soppressata and cauliflowers marinated in oil and chili, all of which were excellent. We then tried the flavorful and fresh caprese salad, the tangy eggplant and zucchini scapece. Next came the stars of the show, the rigatoni alla vodka and tortellini al ragù. We ended the meal with the lemon cheesecake. Everything was excellent but the Vodka sauce and lemon cheesecake were the best I have ever had. Service was prompt, friendly and entertaining despite being put through hell by another table where a customer made a scene for 45 minutes complaining incessantly about feeling unsafe dining outside despite Carbone's setup being among the best I've experienced in an urban setting.

The best pasta in the world!!! Not to mention the veal parmigiana is incredible. Hard to get a resy but definitely worth it - wish they brought take out and delivery back. That was nice to get this type of food without waiting forever. Will always be a staple. The spicy rigatoni is perfect

Yes, this place has soooo much hype which I feel always leaves a lot of people with crazy unrealistic expectations and disappointment, but despite all of that it is an experience worth having if you can. 

Strongly recommend reservations, especially on the weekend. 

Some things you should expect: 
-Old school Italian vibe, very intimate (small restaurant, tables very close together)
-Lively, loud, and somewhat sceney. 
-Fairly long dinner (food comes at a pace, rather than all at once).
-Expensive (this isn't $15 dollar pasta people). 

Food-wise, ordered the below for 4 people and it was too much (they also give an insane amount of free apps which is the best):

-Caesar Salad: they make table side. Yum and perfect size to share.

-Prosciutto and Melon: they also make table side. There is an insane amount of prosciutto and perfect for sharing.

-Spicy Rigatoni: an absolute must if you come. This is what put the restaurant on the map. We ordered 3 servings to share, which was excessive. 

-Linguini Vongole: clam pasta with a white wine sauce. Yum! 

-Veal Parm: giant size. I normally really like, but it was a bit dry and under salted. I would recommend asking for this and the spicy rigatoni to come out together. 

-Dover Piccata: this was better than I thought. Very light and buttery. Also massive in size.

Late review from June. Did not have a yelp account until this morning. Flawless experience at Carbone. Thankfully American Express was able to get us a short notice reservation for two at 8 o'clock on a Thursday night. We were seated promptly and immediately provided bread, pickled vegetables, meat and cheese. The overall vibe of this place is consistent with what you would expect after reading all the reviews and the hype. Totally lived up to the expectations. The wait staff were amongst the most professional I have ever experienced. Prompt, friendly without being intrusive. Ordered wine, pasta vodka, tortellini, salads and a couple desserts. Everything was perfect. I will be returning to Manhattan in December and hopefully get a rez and do it all again.

Hands down the best pasta I've had in New York and I've had a lot of pasta in the city.

The spicy rigatoni and tortellini are the perfect complementary pairing for each other. Lobster ravioli was also good, but not at the same level as the others. Cheesecake was light and creamy though the meal was so good, my pants were probably just as creamy by the end of it.

Also big shout out to AmEx concierge for helping me land this reservation.

Would give this place a 2 overall. Food was subpar and overpriced. Have had way better pasta, save your time. Spicy rigatoni legit tasted like something I could make myself and the lobster ravioli was just not fresh and disappointing. Also felt like we were being rushed out. Anyways Expected better.

No wonder it is extremely difficult to secure a reservation. Carbone is a small-size restaurant with approximately 30 tables. 

Environment [4/5] - This place instantly transferred you to the 80s. Nice vibe but probably not COVID friendly. Tables are very closed to each other and noise level is high. 

Service [4/5] - My server was doing his job but nothing to write home about. He seems nice and took our order in a professional manner but never came by to check on our table. 

Food [4/5] - Most of the Yelp reviews mentioned small portion and so I was surprised I left with a filling stomach. They give you a complimentary garlic bread basket, fresh mozzarella and salami to start the meal. I would give it a 5/5. I mean who can resist fresh mozzarella, right!?
* Caesar alla ZZ [$25]: 3/5. Yelpers mentioned they make this tableside but that didn't happen for our table. Our table is located at the corner and it was hard for them to set up next to us. Does this $25 caesar salad taste better than the $10 caesar salad at your local store? Nope! Save your money unless you enjoy watching live veggie-tossing. 
* Assorted Baked Clams [$25]: 4/5. Good! They give you three types of baked clams but honestly they all tasted the same. 
* Lobster Ravioli [$39]: 4/5. Get this! I was amazed by the texture of this ravioli. No doubt the dough was nicely made because it was so bouncy and fresh. 
* Spicy Rigatoni Vodka [$32]: 4/5. You don't need additional comment here just get this!
* Linguini Vongole [$36]: 3/5. Skip this and you wouldn't regret.

This place is absolutely worth the hype! It's expensive but the food is amazing. We got the meatball appetizer (not on the menu), baked clams, spicy rigatoni vodka, and the lobster ravioli. If you love lobster the lobster ravioli is for you. The meatballs and rigatoni vodka were our favorites. Everything is super expensive but imo worth it for a special occasion!

I've been lucky enough to come back a few times since my initial visit, and Carbone is as exquisite as ever. I love that they've expanded their dining outdoors because of COVID, but it still requires planning a month in advance to get a good reservation time. 

The pastas are impeccable - truly the most perfectly cooked pasta.

Additions to my initial review: All of their classic cocktails are fantastic. The fish is good, but I wouldn't go out of my way to reorder it. The way the staff debones the fish is absolutely insane though. 

It is a true treat to come here, and it is so impressive that Carbone continues to operate at the same insanely high level and deliver everyone an amazing dining experience.

I'm lucky to have come here a second time, and pretty much did the exact same as the first time because it was so good! I got the famed spicy vodka rigatoni, that is the MUST-ORDER dish at Carbone - it is just so flavorful & the pasta is cooked so perfectly. I wouldn't even add any seasonings, because they did it so perfectly. The environment is surprisingly a bit tacky with cheesy Italian music blasting behind you, but that's easy to get past once you start eating. We also got an incredible chocolate cake with hazelnut ice cream dessert - I'm not usually a dessert-orderer, but this may have converted me.

Food is really good here, worst thing is just waiting for an open reservation which almost seems nearly impossible at times! I have been here quite a few times but my friends never manage to get a reservation. Atmosphere is great and their pasta and appetizers are amazing. Their chocolate black cherry cake is really good too!
Penne al vodka and veal parm is SO delicious here- hard to get reservations but food and service is top notch.

Yes it was everything I expected and more! From the food, to the service, to the atmosphere, to the drinks, a perfect night! Our favorite for sure was the famous Carbone Spicy Rigatoni!! Who knew Calabrian chili pepper would taste so good on pasta!
Had the assorted clams and spicy rigatoni. Both were amazing and worth the hype. Definitely a restaurant everyone needs to try at least once.

Look - the food is good here but it doesn't necessarily justify the price and so where some other places may not have good service, the food makes up for it since it's reasonably priced. Here - it does not justify the service at all. For food, get the portioned rigatoni, lobster ravioli, and meatballs. 

It was my birthday and we came, both notifying in the reservation and letting the host know. We legitimately waited 30 min between courses or more while the table next to us of 6+ people got food immediately. Especially ordering the cake at the end which is premade - the table ordered one of each and got their cake 30 min before they brought us one slice. They also did not provide any candle or comp the cake and the server was not at all apologetic.

All I'm saying is, don't be prepared to get the money you paid for through good service, so you gotta justify the food quality. I honestly regretted going for my birthday and it did not provide a happy setting. Tbh they prob will value your table more if you come in a bigger group so maybe consider that.

Highly recommend. This place is amazing all around. We sat outside and it was beautiful. Service all around is incredible. Unsure of the guy that brought us our apps but our server, Azdren (idk how to spell it) was amazing. One of the best servers we've had anywhere. Thanks for a great experience.

Everything was great! The spicy rigatoni was hyped up way too much though! It was fine, nothing super special about it. I feel like people who were raving about it never had pasta w some kick to it so that's why they were so crazy about it. It was just ok to us. They get some of their ingredients from Arthur Ave in the Bronx, I asked the waitress. The steak was good, cooked to my liking. The pork chops good. The bread, mozz and salami at the beginning were great. Meatballs are pork, beef and lamb - really good . The potatoes are cooked in duck fat and garlic - they tasted like crispy home fries but garlicky, really good . The waitress was awesome!!!  Overall the food was good but very overpriced!

My friends and I were lucky to get a last minute reservation at 11:30pm on a Tuesday night. We ordered the Caesar salad, spicy rigatoni, branzino, mushrooms and pork chop. Everything was amazing. Our server Chris was so welcoming, he explained the menu to us and guided us on what to order. Of course at the end of the night they ran out of a few things we ordered  but he was nice enough to bring other food items out. We all had such a great experience here and can't wait to come back!
Amazing food and service.  The rigatoni is especially good.  It is hard to get a reservation, but if you get on the notify list, your chances are pretty good.

My favorite restaurant period. Got lucky booking a last minute reservation. Customer service was excellent. They treated us like family and the food was amazing. The veal marsala - a must have! Great wine list too!
Over price bad Italian that is more of a scene than a restaurant. Not the place to go for Italian! It's a joke at best. $30 pasta dish served by arrogant staff rushing you out the door.

Dining at Carbone was such a great experience! The hostesses and waitstaff were so friendly and welcoming. We were treated as if we were family right away! To start, we received complimentary bread, pickled cauliflower, and Italian salami. It was all super tasty while we were waiting for our appetizer and mains. For our appetizer we got a seasonal salad with fennel, hazelnuts, and a Gorgonzola dressing. It was delicious. We ordered the signature spicy rigatoni vodka and they were nice enough to split it into portions for each person at the table. It was the perfect amount of spice level and sauce. The fettuccini funghi was also great, it was light and tasty. Lastly we ordered the tiramisu for dessert which was a great a huge portion and came with complimentary marzipan rainbow cookies. If you can get a reservation, I definitely recommend dining here, it is just as great as everybody says!

Enjoyed a lovely Wednesday afternoon lunch at Carbone. Worth the hype? Possibly. I think you must try it once in your lifetime. Reservations are tricky to come by so make sure to constantly check Resy! Pretty sure they don't take walk-ins. 

They start you off with this delicious bread, fresh mozzarella they cut up, and spicy salami. It's delicious! I ordered the spicy rigatoni, meatball, and prosciutto. I had a margarita to drink. The food was delicious - the pasta had the right spice level. The meatball basically melts in your mouth, and I love the prosciutto. Note - the cocktail prices online I believe say $18 - they're actually $20 as of 10/27. You gotta experience it. The wait staff were friendly, attentive, and I didn't feel rushed. They give you an Italian cookie complimentary as part of dessert. I paid maybe $115 including tip. Expensive? Yes. I say go just to say you went. All in all - a wonderful experience :)
What can you say that hasn't already been said.  The vodka sauce is amazing, the drinks are amazing, the service is wonderful.  Would eat here every week if I could.
Amazing spicy rigatoni and steak. A bit pricey but you do get what you pay for. I would argue the deserts can be passed up as they taste the same about anywhere.

I'll start by saying I don't normally eat Italian food, but heard too many good things about Carbone from my foodie friends. I was also skeptical about the vodka rigatoni being their signature dish cuz... how good can that be anyways? But boy was I glad to be proven wrong. The flavor, the texture. That dish is the definition of perfection, especially coming from someone who doesn't like the taste of carbs and now I want to eat it every week! We also tried the lobster ravioli. Each ravioli was stuffed with a very generous amount of lobster and shrimp. The sauce was creamy with a hint of citrus - the perfect amount to cut through the creaminess in the sauce. I licked the plate. Their meatball was also the best I've had. According to our server they use 3 different types of meat to get the right flavor and tenderness. Steak and pork chop were also amazing, I'd give them 4/5 stars only because the pasta dishes were so out of this world. 
Overall 4.99/5 stars. Took off 0.01 cuz reservation is next to impossible to get. So if you see an open spot, GRAB IT!!

Carbone has been called one of the hardest reservations to get in New York City and it does not disappoint! We got the spicy rigatoni and the fettuccini al fungi and they were both fantastic. The added touch of complementary bread, cheese, and cookies is always a welcomed start to the meal.  Worth the wait!

The food here is superb, no wonder it's expanded to Vegas and Miami. Also the ambiance and service is great. Started with the clams and Ceasers salad, which are a must. Other favorites included the veal parm and the arrabiata pasta. Can't wait to go back.

Obviously been on my list for a long long time, and finally the reservation was secured! Would it be worth the hype?
The inside of the restaurant isn't small, but feels tight and narrow. There's a small hallway that led us to the back of the restaurant where we were seated. It's sort of mood lighting all around inside with white tablecloths of course! All waiters or "captains" as they call them, are decked out in burgundy suits and Frank Sinatra is playing over the speakers. Definitely an old-school Italian vibe all around. The menu itself is "huge" but just in size, not in the number of items.
They serve you "complimentary" appetizers, which included gardenia, bread basket, salami & a slice of parmesean from the wheel. I wouldn't necessarily call these complimentary, but rather built into the price of your meal - and this place is pricey! I was under the assumption the fresh mozzarella was complimentary as well, so when it wasn't served up with the rest of those appetizers, I ordered it for an additional $10. 
For our main course, we ordered the meatballs which are HUGE. I did not expect them to be this big. They typically come in an order of 3, but our waiter was able to make it 4 so that they'd be a nice even number and we could have 2 each. The meatballs did not live up to the hype. The outside was nice, not too soft or hard. Inside, was essentially raw and chewy. Yuck. Happy that I tried them, since they are written about all over Yelp, but a warning to those who may not like their meat rare - skip on these!
With the meatballs, we both ordered the spicy rigatoni which is another dish that everyone raves about. The rigatoni was amaaaaaazing! Portion was a bit on the small side. The rigatoni are cooked to perfection and the sauce is just the right amount of spicy and creamy. 
No dessert for us, we were stuffed - but we were served 2 small rainbow cookies which were good.
Overall, I'd probably rate it at a solid 3.5. Happy I tried it, but likely would not be back given the price and how difficult it is to get a reservation.

Not a lot that can be said that has not already been said. Came here from CA to celebrate my girlfriends birthday. We literally flew in for this. The Rigatoni leaves a lasting impression, service is absolutely amazing. The oysters were great, wine selection and sommelier were on point. The desert was also excellent. Wasn't blown away by the shrimp dish or the artichokes.  

Where our experience fell short (and this is a review of our experience, not the restaurant itself) was a crowded and obnoxiously loud table of 6 celebrating a birthday just behind us. I mean these people barely ordered anything, they came in to laugh as loud as they could and that was about it. The table next to ours seemed just as bothered by them. We couldn't even hear our waiter let alone the amazing music that was playing through speakers just above our heads. I feel like this unfortunate, bad hand dampened our experience and my impression of what the true experience at Carbone is and can be. 

Will definitely be back and will also recommend this restaurant to friends but for now, docking 2 stars on my review for a situation that was completely obvious but also casually ignored by staff. The restaurant is a real destination, overly disruptive tables should be approached and calmed down.

Calibrate your expectations and you're in for a great time! Maybe pass on the tiramisu though.

I do think Carbone is a bit overhyped, with the scarcity of reservations not helping its case. It's solid 'elevated' italian-american fare, and worth trying, if a bit pricey. Try making better dish choices than I did too 

Beautiful interior, atmospheric, good service, and tasty food for my lunch. There's a complimentary starter of garlic bread, salami, and freshly made mozz, which were delicious. Ordered oysters on the half shell ($24), the lobster ravioli ($49), and the tiramisu ($18).

Lobster ravioli was very good, pasta texture was perfectly al dente, lobster and shrimp were done well, and the dish had a nice light creamy sauce. Oysters were nothing to write home about. Tiramisu was more like a cake than what I like. Fairly dense, and not actually much espresso-soaked insides which I really missed.

I had a good time for a one-time fancy lunch. I'd want to come for dinner and also try the Spicy Rigatoni Vodka before passing final judgement.

The food here is excellent, as the previous reviewers have described in much detail. However, it's still very overpriced for what is on offer. $7 for espresso, $22 for a shot of grappa, $28 for pasta pomodoro? I'd pass.

The service was also very lousy and sloppy. Upon entering the restaurant, I waited over five minutes while several waiters walked past me countless times with none coming over to check on my reservation and seat me. I had to call out "excuse me" quite loudly for any of them to pay attention, and they seemed indifferent to this. It seems they developed a sense of entitlement and rest on their laurels because of the restaurant's reputation.

Was fortunate to snag a lunch res while in NYC. The restaurant has a very elite feel from the moment you walk in. For starters they serve you garlic bread, fresh (I mean FRESH) mozzarella, and some salami. 10/10. I ordered the signature spicy vodka rigatoni as my main dish and was not disappointed. Flavorful with hint of spice and perfectly cooked rigatoni. I would come back again just to get the rigatoni. Menu itself is small with few items to choose from.

Value 1/5
Taste 2/5
Service 1/5
Presentation of food 2/5
Appearance of the establishment 2/5

Food was mediocre, not even close to justifying the price. Overpriced regular Italian food

Soho/west village border houses this heavy hitter where the beautiful come to wine and dine. At the beginning of summer, somehow they let in Pete and I to eat here.

The bread basket includes foccachia and garlic bread which is super fun! They also open the meal with a little antipasto of salami, cheese and the pickled cauliflower (my favorite!). That was my favorite part of the meal and the best thing I ate. 

The food was OK. The "speciality of the house" spicy rigatoni vodka was very reminiscent of an Upstate NY classic, chicken riggies. If you're from Utica, you know exactly what  I'm talking about. It was not that spicy if you'd like to try it but you don't do well with spice. I also think it's best ordered shared as an app, not as an entree as one person. That way everyone gets a taste. 

Do NOT bring your upstate parents here, they will faint when they see bill. It's a monster.  They added a whopping 20% covid surcharge, and that is NOT the gratuity, so please still tip accordingly.
Went with my hubby from a gift card that mine and his kids gave for Xmas. Excellent on both service and food.

I never give out three stars (I'm usually a five or one-er), but this place? A hard three stars. Mainly because the service was great, the place is beautifully decorated for the holidays and the food was very much adequate. The lacking stars are mainly due to its inaccessibility and food quality for its price. 

I really am so glad that we went because I WANT to have an opinion of this place. My main annoyance is at how difficult it is to get a reservation here. You'd think that a place this hard to get into would have STELLAR food, so the reality was a bit disappointing. If reservations weren't so obnoxiously hard to get, then I could maybe see the appeal of this place. And maybe we should've gotten more meat entrees instead of only sticking with their pastas. But I mean... it's an Italian restaurant... shouldn't all of their pastas take your breath away with a reputation like theirs? 

The best things we ate were the tortellini al ragu ($34) and the garlic bread (free). Both truly great. The spicy rigatoni vodka ($32) is their most celebrated pasta and honestly it was good but not at all worth the hype. The fettuccini con funghi ($32) was disappointing mainly because of the bell peppers included... because why are they in there? Such a gross flavour with the creaminess of a soft fettuccine.

I really did want to love this place, but there are far superior Italian places in this city (L'Artusi, Lilia, even the pastas at Patsy's for christsake). Take your money elsewhere.
2nd time here and it still didn't disappoint. Loved it just as much as the first time. The lobster ravioli is 100% my favorite and a must have!!!!

I know the hype. I know Italian food (both from Italy and Nyc style). This place is so overrated. Small portion of average Italian food. 
Meatballs - raw and cold on the inside, sauce on top was average. 
I complained about the raw meatballs, but the waiter did not offer any other option. The proper thing to do would have been to take it back and offer something else. 

Artichoke hearts - pretty good

Spicy rigatoni - I'm sorry, but $32 for a regular bowl of pasta is ridiculous, and it didn't live up to the hype. It was average but not $32 worth. 

Don't sit in the back room. It's next to the kitchen with no airflow, easily 80 degrees in that room. We moved to the front and were happier. 

This is New York City... I can name 10 Italian restaurants with better food, half the price and better ambiance. 

Sorry Carbone, it's all hype and no substance.

Managed to snag a 10pm reservation here on a Monday night -- I'm guessing because there was a cancellation. Have heard of this place from "influencers" and celebrity sightings so when I saw an open reservation, I knew I couldn't pass on the opportunity! 

I had booked the outdoor patio, but they seated us indoor, which was fine. We got drinks at the bar since we were a few minutes early. The espresso martini was definitely good, but not worth the price IMO.

Now let's move on to the food - so yes, they do send a platter of complimentary bread, cauliflower marinated in oil, and spicy salami your way. This was all very delicious and a pleasant surprise!

We ordered the meatballs, spicy rigatoni vodka and the lobster ravioli and they were all wonderful! We asked for Parmesan cheese and red pepper flakes and they did not disappoint. My favorite was the spicy rigatoni vodka -- it was so creamy and flavorful! The meatballs were also epic (was surprised to see the cost though!). The lobster portion was actually generous, which we were surprised about. 

Ambiance was excellent -- they had fun Italian music playing, our servers were kind and funny and all in all it felt very upscale.

Overall, I would give this place a 4/5. Definitely glad I experienced it, and may return at some point but am not in a hurry to come back as the options for good Italian places in NYC are endless (not to mention, cheaper).

Carbone deserves every single star on this review + they know it. This legendary Italian restaurant is one of the most highly coveted restaurants in the city. Although extremely hard to get a reservation to... when you have the opportunity to give it a go - you'll understand all of the hype. I've had the single best thing I have ever eaten in my lifetime at this restaurant + have shared truly beautiful memories here. You feel the history the moment you walk through their doors but oddly enough there is also such a beautiful new energy/vibe to the place which lends Carbone to not feeling "stuffy". The staff are extremely professional, charismatic + knowledgeable of the menu. And the bartenders here are truly talented. If I could roll in here for a cocktail on a weekday night, I would... Simply put, some of the best cocktails I have ever had were at Carbone. If you visit, don't skip out on the following: the godly delicious mozzarella, the calamari, the assorted baked clams, and the one and only spicy rigatoni!

So much fun!  Made a lunch date with my gal, jump at an open res online. Tuesday at 11:45, ok, we're down.
Our waiter was one cool dude,  guided us throughout our meal & was on point with every selection. 
Began with a crafted cocktail, celebrating a birthday is serious business in our fam.
Two spicy margarita, a house specialty, yes please! Perfection in a glass, not too much spice, savory deliciousness. 
Just go! Yes, get on the wait list, so worth it!

I was lucky enough get an AMEX reservation table through Resy! They'll open up last minute reservation on the app for you if you have an AMEX club, and NOW I understand why it's always booked up.

THE CLAMS.
THE RIGATONI.
THE ROSE.

The AMEX seating was a bit tight, but the food more than made up for it.

This is definitely a must stop in NYC when Im around to visit.

Great food! Good drinks. Service was fairly slow, but amazing atmosphere. The spicy rigatoni was great. They did charge us $54 for water $9/person. Make sure you ask them for tap water not still water or else they will charge you this outrageous amount for water. Overall great restaurant, but may have been understaffed so understandable for slow service.

Much like what everyone says, the food is good but will definitely not change your life. The quintessential spicy rigatoni is good but nothing to write home about. My favorite part of the meal was actually the bread basket which is the perfect starter to the meal and you can't really go wrong with the desserts either. Overall a good time but this restaurant is just SO hyped up that it's impossible for it to meet expectations anymore. Def worth a one-time visit but will unfortunately not be going back.

Been wanting to come here forever but thought it wouldn't be worth the hype -- it absolutely was and then some. Absolute top tier favorites include the complimentary garlic bread and mozzarella (it's hot and hands down the best mozzarella I've ever had), as well as the spicy rigatoni vodka and carrot cake. We also really enjoyed the ricotta tortellini and clams, and while still delicious, I'd opt out of the veal parm next time for an additional pasta. Service is both efficient and professional. Reservations are, as you can imagine, hard to come by, so keep an eye out on Resy!

TLDR: The single best pasta dish I've ever had. The spicy rigatoni is a must order. 
If you like meatballs, I would recommend giving an order of it but the Carbone experience already includes a variety of small bites that are quite filling. The spicy rigatoni I feel is their star dish and main attraction. The pasta itself is perfectly al dente and the sauce is unmatched. The tortellini is a good break from just the Rigatoni but if you're only ordering one dish, then the Rigatoni is the way to go. The chocolate cake dessert was a nice way to round out the meal though maybe unnecessary given that they provide a sweet bite with the Neapolitan cake.

I think this place is pretty good. But definitely not five stars. The complementary appetizers of meat, bread, and fresh mozzarella is fantastic with the perfect amount of spice and salt. The variety of clams as the appetizer was also quite tasty. This place in my opinion does not deserve five stars because the spicy rigatoni was a huge letdown. It truly reminded me of the gravy that is served at Indian restaurants and they took that gravy and mixed it with high quality, perfectly cooked pasta. I'm not saying that it wasn't tasty, but it was nothing extraordinary and certainly did not live up to the hype as a signature dish that this restaurant thrives on. I had the tiramisu and it was underwhelming. Overall I would come back again and try other dishes but I do not think it Lives up to the hype.

Finally got a reservation here after waiting for months for 10:15 pm last night. Pretty crowded for a Monday night as expected. We sat outside at the Amex patio which was lovely and heated. The service was great. Everything was brought out in a timely fashion, but we didn't feel rushed and our waiter was very friendly. The bread/apps they start you with were some of the best things we had. The pizza bread, garlic bread, pickled cauliflower and salami were all very good. We ended up ordering the fresh mozz/proscuitto and Caesar salad as additional apps, then the spicy rigatoni and veal parm with a side of broccoli rabe for our entree. We were STUFFED by the end of it. Everything was quite oily and salty making it all so rich. We all agreed the spicy rigatoni was our favorite. Overall, I would say it's not overrated. It's certainly delicious and worth the experience, however, I can't say it was the best Italian food I've ever had.

Still my favorite Italian restaurant of all time

Pro:
The servers are spectacular. Especially the gentleman in the red glasses. 
I went twice over the summer and the host (white male) that greets you at the door definitely stood out to me with his award-winning smile. 

Cons:
Not a spacious place
Very claustrophobic
Very loud 

(All things I can live with for the spectacular food)
Everything here was absolutely amazing! From the service to the outdoor dining to the dishes! It was hard to get a reservation but it was absolutely worth it!

Worth the wait! My husband and We're trying to make reservations for weeks. The food was absolutely phenomenal. We started off with assorted baked clams and octopus. For dinner we shared veal Parmesan and spicy rigatoni vodka. We would order all of it again. Everything was delicious.

Everything at Carbone was as solid as I had expected. The old-school-chic vibe was on point -- when you walk in, you feel like you've traveled into a set for a Scorsese/Coppola movie. 

The complementary bread, mozz and soppressata were tasty. I had heard a lot about the caeser, and while it was good (especially their homemade croutons), they went a little overboard with the dressing. The pasta entrees made up for it, though -- I know the spicy rigatoni gets all the hype, but the lobster ravioli beats it as far as I'm concerned.

Today after many many days of scouring resy I finally made it and got myself a reservation at Carbone! The food is worth the hype! I know the spicy rigatoni is supposed to be the star of the show but their other pasta dishes were just as amazing! I highly recommend the lobster ravioli and fettuccine con fungi. Also do not skip out on the chocolate hazelnut cake for dessert! 

Instagram: nycgirlseat

Extremely pleasant experience at SoHO! Yes, it was extremely difficult to find availability here due to popular demand but we are glad we did! 
When you enter the restaurant, you are greeted by very friendly hosts (compares to snobby hosts at other fancy nyc restaurants). The environment reminds a lot of the typical old school glamorous NYC style which we love! The dim lights and candles make it perfect for a romantic dinner. 
Their bread basket was exceptional and we really liked the two appetizers we got (including their famous burrata with prosciutto)! As far as the main pasta courses are concerned, we found them ok - hence 4/5 stars given that was the main reason of the hype for this restaurant. 
Would like to also note that the staff was extraordinarily polite and connected well with the crowd. 
Will try to come back again

The service here is pretty good, but the interior could use a good cleaning. Not necessarily the cleanest restaurant I've been to. 

The food was 4 stars -- I felt that the presentation was 5 stars, but that the presentation masked the okay-ness of the food. 

I would come back.

Listen if you are in NYC, you are not living if you don't dine at Carbone. The moment you walk in the door you feel the authentic Italian vibes. Tables are tough to come by so make sure you go online well in advance for a reservation. 

The classic menu items are delicious and they have a bunch of specials as well. For antipasti we started with the carpaccio w/ black truffles and the octopus. The carpaccio was to die for and melted in your mouth. The octopus was delicious, soft on the inside with a smokey crisp outside. For our main we had the spicy rigatoni vodka and the veal parm. The combo of the two were unmatched. The veal had a wonderful breading, but cut like butter. For dessert we had the tiramisu and carrot cake. I loved both, but the carrot cake was unbelievable. It was crunchy yet soft on the inside and not overwhelmingly sweet. 

For drinks you gotta roll w the super Tuscan red. What's an Italian meal without it? The staff is unbelievable, friendly and so attentive. Probably one of the best dining experiences I've ever had. Carbone is king of Italian.

Tried to get a reservation at Carbone for weeks, and had to set multiple alerts in Resy, but was FINALLY able to snag a res here at 9:45 pm on a Tuesday night and it was definitely worth the wait!

It was freezing outside so I arrived about 10 min early and they mentioned I could wait by the bar. The restaurant itself is pretty small so there's not a whole lot of room to wait inside the actual restaurant and I felt like I was in everyone's way but I decided to grab a drink while I waited. The second I ordered my drink, they came to seat me (about 5 min after arriving), which was no problem, because they just brought my drink over to my table when it was ready. I ordered an Old Fashioned and I must say, it was a really good one and even had the big block of ice, which is what I always notice right away :) 

The service was pretty great all around. A few min after sitting down, my server came over, introduced himself, brought me a menu, and let me know that he would give me some time to look it over. Just a heads up, the tables are VERY close together which I wasn't expecting but ended up being fun chatting with the couple next to me. 

I immediately knew that I was ordering the Spicy Vodka Rigatoni bc I had been hearing about it from multiple people and it seemed like a must.

After a few min of sitting down, a server brought over a warm basket of bread, pickled (?) cauliflower, and some type of meat in the shape of a flower...great presentation and it was all incredible. The bread was to die for.

Shortly after, my server came over to take my food order and he was SO nice. I was dining alone and he came over and sat across from me at my table, shooting the s***, asked how I was doing, and asked what I was thinking for my food. He gave me a few recs and helped me decide on a few additional items to order that I had not planned on. He recommended the caesar salad that they make tableside and insisted that I ordered one meatball (even though I had no intention of ordering one). Definitely a good salesman lol, plus, who am I to turn down a meatball?!

All the food was incredible. I don't think it was the best pasta I've ever had in my life but it was still truly delicious but I would be interested in trying another dish next time!

I ended up ordering a glass of the Super Tuscan wine and it was so yummy. My server also came over later in the meal and gave me a refill which was VERY kind. I was SO full, I had zero room for dessert - which I usually end up ordering even when I'm stuffed, but that's how full I was....and a sign that I was stuffing my face with too much bread.  

Anywhooo, highly recommend Carbone if you're lucky enough to get a reservation! Plus, you'll probably also see a celebrity bc I know I did and it was for sure a highlight of my night.

Veal. Parmesan.
I have never experienced what I experienced in this establishment.

God bless you, Mario Carbone. Your rigatoni is everything. Your dining atmosphere is out of this world.

Will always be back whenever god gives me a reservation opportunity.

Amazing.. from the service to the food everything was great. Came here on a Tuesday night for a late dinner and was thorough impressed. We had the meatballs, spicy rigatoni, and lobster ravioli. The creamy lobster ravioli was to die for. They

Definitely one of my favorite Italian restaurants! From their garlic bread to all the entrees, everything is just phenomenal! My favorite is of course their infamous Spicy Rigatoni. It is always consistent and delicious! The veal parm is also unreal. Amazing service. My only complaint is that they are always fully booked! I was lucky enough to snap a last minute booking during the same week. Can't wait to be back!

I had given up getting a reservation at a reasonable time (not 10pm) but since I had a friend visiting from my home country I decided it was worthy to set up all possible alerts on Resy (lol). Luckily, we were able to come for a Saturday lunch. We were all very excited to try Carbone in NYC and, in case you just want the conclusion, it did not disappoint AT ALL! We started off with drinks and the Aperol Spritz was delicious! From appetizers to main courses, everything is served family style. Extra points for their beautiful dinnerware! The whole environment feels like an old school Italian dinner and it's awesome. The service is top notch and they make sure you are happy. Yes, the famous vodka sauce is amazing and worth the hype. The veal milanese is also amazing, definitely recommend that! They had a seasonal corn side dish with truffles that I could eat all day. Love dessert/coffee time as they bring you their delicious Italian rainbow cookies. Overall amazing experience and worth setting an alert on Resy!

So this food was great, and I can't take that away from them. HOWEVER, be ready to pay an arm and a leg for small portions of pasta. 

We started with the prosciutto which was just a tad bit too salty. They bring fresh mozzarella and soppressata out in the beginning with some bread and the mozzarella is FANTASTIC, wish we had more. 
We then started with pastas and this is where I tried my favorite dish which was the lobster ravioli. The ravioli are STUFFED with lobster and there's tons of lobster on the plate as well. The specials for that day included a bunch of white truffle dishes which piqued our interest. We got the gnocchi with Parmesan and shaved white truffle which was cooked perfectly and was very light. It was delicious but definitely not worth the $150 we payed for that small plate.
Now, everyone knows Carbone for its spicy vodka rigatoni and this was so overrated. I cannot emphasize how much this dish is not worth the money or the hassle of getting a reservation. It's good, but I've had better vodka pasta at local pizzerias‍
The veal Parmesan was delicious and a large portion good for multiple people to share but, again, nothing to write home about.

Overall, the service was good and the food was good but definitely not worth the price.
Good food and good ambiance but very expensive for the amount you get. Waiters are a bit too quick to take things away. Spicy rigatoni is not overhyped.

Carbone definitely lives up to the hype, but you'll pay a pretty penny for the experience. 

Is this the best Italian food in town? No. Is the place legendary? Most definitely.

From the moment I walked in, I felt swept into a romantic, old school Italian joint with servers who fit the bill.

The cocktails here are top notch (loved their Negroni). We tried the mozzarella with prosciutto - nothing life-changing, but it was a solid app. I loved the lobster ravioli and thought the famed rigatoni was good, but not up to the hype. We also tried the veal parm, and it was good, but it wasn't a must try to me... you can get way better veal parm for less than $70. We finished with a lemon cheesecake and the tiramisu - both were great, but I thought the cheesecake was a skosh better. Overall, an above average meal with exceptional vibes and service.

A must go to place even if it's once. The service is one of the best . The garlic bread and mozzarella that are complimentary are amazing . The one thing about this place is the quality of the ingredients . My favorite dish was the baked clams 3 ways ( would go back for this ). The famous spicy rigatoni was good but I would add the tomato paste they have with chilli flakes . Another amazing dish was the jumbo shrimp scampi ( use the garlic bread to soak up the sauce. ) .

YES, the food is VERY good. NO, the food is not worth the price. YES, the experience IS worth the price. NO, you probably won't want or need to go back. 

They make you feel incredibly special with remarkable attention to detail. The tables are very close together and the noise level is very high... but that's sort of the point? It's like a time warp to a different time where neighborhood restaurants were a thing... and you were a much cooler and important person than you actually are. 

The bread, mozarella app, and Veal parmesan were all tops. As was the extraordinary carrot cake. 

It's more an experience than a restaurant. And it's a lovely experience. You'd spend almost this much on a Broadway show and how often do you leave a Broadway show with leftovers.

My experience here was very well! Reservations are a bit of a hassle , but I was able to get one. Our server was so good to us. They start you off with bread and fresh mozzarella. For an  appetizer we chose the Caesar salad, the dressing is prepared from scratch table side along with the salad. Simply amazing , the croutons omg to die for . Moving forward to the entrées we chose a few items . The spicy rigatoni is a must ! Lobster ravioli, and the sea bass. The rigatoni was so desirable, the sauce and kick to it was perfect. Lobster ravioli, idk what else to say but GOOD!  The sea bass was so fresh I couldn't believe it, it literally melted in our mouths. Ok for dessert even though we were stuffed , we still wanted to try it. We chose the carrot cake with ginger gelato, ginnnngeeerr gelato come on now! So amazing! The experience was grand , Carbone is a must if you're in Nyc .

Good: the food, bartender/drinks and the service men filling up drinks and cleaning tables 

Bad: took over 30 min to sit down and also very slow kitchen.  

Service wise, this is the worst service I've received from a Michelin restaurant. First off, we were on time and had to stand by a tiny bar for 30 min to wait for our table. After 30 mins, I talked to one of the front desk people and she legit sounded annoyed and said there was nothing they could do bc the table wasn't leaving. They did end up comping our round of drinks at the bar. Once seated, it took awhile for appetizers to get to our table. We also got our pasta more than an hour after sitting down and my friend was served only 1/2 of his pasta and had to wait for the rest (lol!). They never brought out our broccoli rabe. 

Food wise, We ordered calamari (gluten free), octopus (gluten free) and I got the gluten free spicy pasta dish. I liked all the food. Definitely very slow service but food pretty solid. Food here def a solid 4/5 for me. Too bad our dinner service was such a mess. We all tipped at-least 20% still bc the bartender was really legit and the service men filling our water and cleaning our table worked so hard and were so on point.

I want to start by saying how was excited I was to have finally scored a reservation after months of trying- the food and wine lived up to all the hype.  The spicy rigatoni was outstanding and the pork chops with peppers might have been one of the best pieces of meat I've ever had.  Server was attentive and well educated on food allergies- the gluten free pasta was amazing you couldn't tell the difference from the regular dish! 

That being said, after about an hour and forty five minutes of being seated (pasta took a very long time to come out not sure if this was because the dish had to be gluten free) my boyfriend and I were finishing our wine and enjoying each others company when (I assume a manager) came over to ask how our meal was.  We raved about the food and service-only to be told that he was happy to hear that, but he needed the table for another party.  It was extremely unprofessional and distasteful after the amount of money we had just spent on dinner? To add to that, there was an empty table next to us and one directly behind us.  This took away from the experience for sure, can't say we are dying to go back after that.

Super excited to try this place! Ambiance definitely lived up to the hype -- service was INCREDIBLE (definitely a great detail when dining) and food was great. Vodka pasta did not live up to the hype imo but shrimp was SO GOOD! We also ordered the Hazelnut cake for dessert & i definitely RECOMMEND.

Me and my wife enjoyed our first time in carbone. I can honestly say it was some of the best Italian food we have had in a while. The food gets a A+ , the ambiance A+ and the only thing I can say needs work is the reservation. I am not enjoying sitting on my phone like a mad man waiting for another opening. 
Otherwise we loved it.
Hands down the best food I've ever had and the staff was so friendly! Great experience all around

so worth it. the food was delicious and i loved the complimentary antipasti that were brought out! 
we got calamari and caesar to start, this was in addition to the free cauliflower dish, soppressata, and 3 different types of bread!
i got the rigatoni and my boyfriend got the linguini. both dishes were amazing!! lastly we got the nutella tiramisu for dessert which was honestly the best tiramisu i have ever had
the service was great. our server was so nice, the men filling waters and making the salad were also very nice. the ambiance was great as well!
i think it was so worth it especially for our anniversary :)

Carbone lived up to its hype! 
I arrived and from the hostess to Christine the bartender who was amazing! Carmine who wasn't our server but stepped up when realized our server wasn't too attentive definitely over delivered with amazing service! He offered his honest opinions,recommended dishes!
Ask for Christine to make your drinks!

In honor of the baby news today, I'd like to mention that we saw Rihanna at Carbone on Friday! So if you were wondering, yes celebrities go here and yes you may see someone there. 

This visit to Carbone has been a long time coming. If you know Carbone, you know it's very in demand and is quite difficult to get a reservation. We booked a month in advance but boy was it worth it.
