Safe to say this is hands down my new favorite restaurant in the city and it is most definitely lives up to all the hype. 

For starters, the SERVICE. Never have I ever had service quite like this. Our waiters were so attentive and made sure my water was never empty and to check up on us. Going on to the food, we ordered the clams, calamari and Caesar salad for starters. If I had to recommend one thing not to skip out on it'd be the Caesar salad. The croutons were fresh out of the oven, soft yet crunchy, definitely unlike any other Caesar salad you've had before. It's also made right at your table in front of you so it adds to the experience. 

We then went on to the spicy rigatoni of course, chicken entree and funghi spaghetti. Definitely also do not miss out on the funghi pasta it was delicious! The spicy rigatoni as I'm sure you could have guessed was a solid 10/10. We were blown away by the different unique tastes of all 3 dishes. 

There's always room for dessert. But at Carbone especially. Do not leave without trying the chocolate cake. Our waiter described it to us as a Ferrero Rocher and while that was pretty accurate, personally I think it may have been ever better than that. This cake was next level and the vanilla ice cream was so rich and paired so well with it. 

Needless to say I am in the works of making my next reservation and cannot wait to come back to my new favorite restaurant.

The service was great! However the food fell short of the hype. We tried the prosciutto & mozz (this was good) spicy rigatoni, lobster ravioli, & chocolate cake dessert. The spicy rigatoni was ok, a little sweeter than I'd like & the lobster ravioli lacked flavor. The chocolate cake was also mediocre. My favorite part may have been the pickled cauliflower & bread basket they give as a starter. I don't mind paying for good food but this place is definitely overpriced & not worth it.

Was so excited to try this place and it was on my restaurant list for a while - for the price and how everyone raves about Carbone, food is overhyped and average at best. 

We ordered the beef carpaccio, lobster ravioli, spicy rigatoni vodka, and veal parmesan. Veal parmesan and beef carpaccio were the best items we got. The lobster ravioli was nothing to write home about and the spicy rigatoni vodka you can get the same dish for half the cost at Parm (sister restaurant). 

Overall, staff were nice, decor is beautiful inside, but in my opinion there are much better Italian restaurants in NYC.

True Old School Italian flare with a touch of modern spin on the menu, Carbone is everything a Michelin Starred Italian restaurant should be.

Every dish is worthy of a high rating, but they have a few items that are truly elite/best-in-class. 1) The Rigatoni A la Vodka 2) The Beef Carpaccio 3) The Veal Parm.

The caliber of the food however is only to be outdone by the service. From start to finish Asdren was attentive, charismatic and informative. He knew everything off the top of his head from ingredients to preparation. Asdren noted he was born and raised in the area, and his energy is a perfect marriage with everything Carbone represents. If you want to take your Carbone experience up a notch, I highly recommend requesting Asdren.

Simply outstanding, service was amazing, food was incredible, anyone giving this place under 5 stars is doing it because it's popular.. it was an incredible experience and I couldn't recommend higher. From the waiter to the somm to the incredible quality of the food. Amazing dinner. The manager came around and made sure we had a great experience, despite how busy and in demand the restaurant is.
WORTH THE WAIT!! The hype is real. top notch service and food. Spicy rigatoni pasta and the veal parm was everything. Super hard to get reservations and usually booked for months.

What a pleasant experience! From the minute you walk in till the minute you walk out everything was just spectacular. It felt as if this place belonged in a Sopranos episode. Where do I start, the music is fantastic, super lively and very traditional. The service was outstanding, our server Blake was great! Super attentive and just welcoming in every aspect. He was super nice and answered all questions we had for him. But the best part of course was the food!!!  To start off the starter bread, fresh mozzarella and pepperoni are to die for! Every single plate was just delicious! I had the clams which were delicious followed by the spicy pasta & the meatballs, super delish! We had a few margaritas which were honestly super tasty! Unique in its own way but very nice. I absolutely loved everything about this place! Btw.. it took us about 5 weeks to get this reservation but it was worth the wait!

Overall, a good meal! However, I think I had way too high of an expectation. It is difficult to get a reservation at Carbone, so I had a high expectation for the food. We got assorted baked clams, Mario's famous meatball, Spicy Rigatoni Vodka, veal Parmesan, Fettuccine con Funghi, and chocolate cake for dessert. My favorite dishes are the baked clams and spicy rigatoni vodka. The spicy rigatoni vodka is famous for a reason, so make sure you get this one you visit!! Everything else are good and all, but they weren't mind-blowingly good. The service was alright. The restaurant itself is still very cute and nicely decorated.

To beat the drum some more, Carbone has top notch food and service, even considering it's price point. The free salami, mozzarella, and garlic bread to start were delicious and a nice touch. The spicy rigatoni and meatballs were out of this world. I might skip the tortellini next time, but honestly I wouldn't be disappointed if I got it again. The tiramisu was very generously portioned and also unmatched. The free starters, meatballs, 2 pastas and a dessert actually turned out to be too much for 2, and we left uncomfortably full but very happy.

Very average.
I never, ever leave a comment here but this place needs to be humbled! I don't understand the hype.
The wait list is more than a month but We managed to get a reservation through someone.
The grilled octopus was bad honestly, not fresh, overcooked and came with pepper that are obviously from a can and dry potatoes.
The pasta is normal not worth the hype. The spicy rigatoni a la vodka i could replicate at home. Nothing special. If I recommend one thing it would be the lobster ravioli, it's good.
The place inside is not that fancy it's very tiny and the decoration is mid

honestly been trying to get a reservation for two months now, I have sent emails and phone Carbone. IMPOSSIBLE TO GET IN. would love to try but I guess unless you know someone you will never get in to try this amazing place! rating based on availability noth
ing else

Spicy Rigatoni is to die for. Appetizer bread is phenomenal. Lobster Ravioli is also very well done. The special (linguini with shaved truffle) was good. Caesar salad is okay. The cake desert was very rich but good.

Most importantly, the ambiance and the level of service is the best part. Candidly the wait/hassle to get a reservation probably isn't worth the effort but if you're able to get a table it's a no brainer.
So delicious, worth every hype! You must get the spicy rigatoni but also Mario's meatballs. I dream about it to this day!

The food is very good and the waiters are excellent. Alexander was one of the best servers I've ever met! He made the entire meal feel like an experience. I love that the mozzarella is homemade and comes out warm in olive oil. Everything was rich in flavor! Don't let the rude hosts push you out the door! It's really hard to get a table but your best bet is going right when they open -it's never too early for pasta!

I REALLY wanted to love this restaurant but this was a very mediocre at best experience for me (hopefully this was an off day for them).

TLDR: 
+Positives: the service of the staff were super nice and attentive on the front facing, the pasta was yummy and they did a good job with the outdoor
-Room for improvement: for a restaurant that was one michelin star I truly expected the food to be well done for EACH and every dish (very salty side dishes that accompanied the entree) and the service timing to be  took 1 hour wait to get entree served.

The Experience:
Made a reservation for a very late 10pm weekday dinner because their slots are impossible to get but it's been on my list forever since I've heard SO MUCH about the food so the second I saw a reservation available I had to grab it even though it was not the most ideal time.

We reserved an outdoor dining booth which was really well done. It was a full outdoor built area that was heated and well-decorated, it felt like you were actually indoor and part of the extension of the restaurant so even though it was cold outside, the dining ambiance wasn't impacted by the cold weather. They had decor in the tents and even had music playing!

I was really excited about the food. Got the clams for appetizers, the ribs for entree and of course the famous vodka rigatoni.

I liked the bread service - 3 different types of bread nicely warmed with sides of salami, cheese, as well as cauliflower. This was a nice touch but it definitely took probably 15-20 minutes from when we first sat to get the bread service.

Appetizer: The clams had 3 different sauces and came as sets of 3 - they were okay, the sea urchin one was my favorite but some of them were a little fishy!

Entree: The wait from appetizer to entree though took almost a whole hour so we sat there well after 11pm just waiting for our food. When we got the food, I wasn't even hungry anymore because it just took so long :(

The ribs were well done, the flavor was great but the side salad that was underneath was so heavily covered with vinaigrette and it was so salty I could barely properly eat it on a standalone so that really took away from the dish.

The vodka rigatoni was really good. The pasta sauce was so tomatoe-y and so creamy! The texture of the rigatoni was well done. This was a good dish, and deserves to be the signature.

Overall, I might get the rigatoni again but the overall experience besides that dish was generally quite disappointing. I do applaud the staff for a great customer-facing service though.

This place just about lives up to the hype. I had been dying to eat here for years and finally managed it pre-pandemic at 11:30 AM one day before a matinee. The complimentary bread service was a nice touch (you get a complimentary cookie with coffee, too) and the spicy rigatoni seemed better than the version you can get at Parm. The service was excellent, though it was early and the restaurant was not full. Finished the meal with a tiramisu that was only alright, though the cookie on top was the best part. It was an expensive meal, but I had a lot of food and enjoyed myself; it felt well worth the experience. Ambiance is very old school Hollywood Italian, which was fun, too. Worth a trip at least once.

Doesn't look like much when you pass but when you walk in it's aesthetically beautiful and the details have it that Italian feel. 
Joey was our server he was attentive , friendly and accommodating ! Thank you Joey .
I wish I took pictures of the inside . Definitely a place that is a must visit.
The only thing I can say regarding the food was the soup was salty but nothing eater can't fix ! 
Joey as I said is accommodating, listened to our feed back & it was a nice surprise he took that item off our order. 
In the end my experience was wonderful!
I will be coming back when I visit.

Loved Carbone in NYC! We got reservations for a weeknight to celebrate a special occasion. The service was great and we loved the food. So many great vegetarian items such as minestrone soup, eggplant & zucchini appetizer, and the spicy rigatoni vodka. The Nutella tiramisu was also delish. Highly recommend and maybe you will see a celebrity!

the infamous carbone. one of the hardest restaurants to get a reservations at in NYC

given the hype and anticipation around this meal, there's only question there to ask. was worth the hype? in short, yes. from the moment you step in the restaurant you are transported. the staff was excellent and the food was exquisite. the assorted baked clams are a great place to start before diving into the main attraction - the pasta. the spicy rigatoni vodka was a no brainer but the tortellini al ragu proved to be a worthy competitor in richness and flavour. we finished our lunch with a new york style lemon cheesecake and coffee. definitely the best lunch i've ever 

if you're able to get a reservation, i would highly encourage you to go (or else ill go in your place )

side note: if you're not trying to break the bank @parm is under the @majorfoodgroup alongside with carbone where you can try the the twin version of the spicy rigatoni vodka
Managed to snag a reservation. The spicy rigatoni was good, maybe a bit overhyped, but the experience was great and the vibe was good. Loved the fresh salami and mozz cheese served with bread!
As expected - the food at Carbone is absolutely delicious and the service was exceptional! 5 stars here!
The rainbow cookie made me wet! 6 stars!! Will definitely be back!!!!!!!!!! Oh and don't forget the espresso martini! Marone

I was thrilled when I was able get a reservation at the infamous Carbone for my birthday. If you've ever tired to make a reservation here than you know how difficult it can be. As soon as I walked into the establishment the first thing I noticed was the cozy atmosphere and I felt as though I was in the 70's. My eyes gravitated towards the small bar that was located a little further into the restaurant. I was seated within minutes and was taken into their second room. One thing I can say is that Carbone is very generous and offers many appetizers on the house. As soon as my party and I sat down plates of garlic bread, salami, pickled cabbage and cheese was placed in front of us. Everyone from the hostess, to the waiters and the bus boys were super friendly and took amazing care of my guests and I. Now lets talk about the food, some of the appetizers that I ordered were the assorted baked clams which came with a total of 9 but were prepared in a variety of ways. I also ordered the beef Carpaccio Peimontese which was thinly sliced raw beef, this was very light and tasty. I also ordered their classic Cesar salad which was prepared fresh and right in front of me. Now onto the main courses, I had to try the spicy rigatoni vodka pasta. It definitely lived up to the hype, it was spicy, creamy and packed with great flavor. I also ordered the veal parmesan which was breaded and topped with fresh mozzarella and marinara sauce. 
Carbone made my birthday extremely special, all the waiters came out and sang happy birthday. For dessert I ordered fresh strawberries with home made whipped cream, the lemon cheese cake and the carrot cake that came with a scoop of vanilla ice cream. You can't go wrong with any of these options, everything was absolutely perfect. 

Thank you Carbone

This place is a must go! Definitely try to experience it one time. 
Spicy vodka a must!!
Got the veal parm - thin moist and crispy.
Ended with the carrot cake dessert! Not too sweet and it's one of the best carrot cakes I had! 
Services are top notch!
Love the place and the appetizers were all good! 
Not a lot of people choose the octopus appetizer but it's def a must imo! 
Def will come back again to try other plates!

I was fortunate enough to snag a reservation with my boyfriend at Carbone on Saturday for lunch, and I was not disappointed! For those of you who haven't heard, Carbone is one of the hardest reservations to get in NYC. Reservations open up on Resy 30 days in advance at 10 am. Carbone is an Italian restaurant filled with years and years of history and known as an attraction for celebrity A-listers. They also have one Michelin Star for their high-quality food. Once we arrived, we were seated in the back dining room which was not too crowded and perfect for an intimate lunch. We were then introduced to our waitress who was so amazing and thorough with her personal recommendations. As we were deciding on what to order, we received complimentary garlic bread, mozzarella, and salami. These alone were just mind-blowing - extremely fresh and tasty. For appetizers, we chose to order the baked clams. Our waitress informed us that the baked clams were assorted - casino, oreganata, and fantasia with sea urchin. The baked clams were delicious and very fresh as well. For entrees, I had to order the spicy rigatoni vodka since it is a Carbone staple. My boyfriend ordered the lobster ravioli which is a more nontraditional item on their menu. The spicy rigatoni vodka was amazing to say the least! Even though it looks like a basic vodka pasta, it was unlike any other that I've had. The sauce was so creamy and not too spicy, which I really appreciated. I would definitely come back here just for this. I had a taste of the lobster ravioli and honestly, it was not that great. The lobster was fishy tasting and it was very overpowering when paired with the squid ink pasta. Since the portions were smaller since it was lunch time, we definitely had some space for dessert. We tried the lemon cheesecake and it was such a hit! Usually, I don't like pastries with lemon tart, but paired with this cheesecake, it was soo good. I had such a great experience at Carbone and I would definitely recommend checking it out if you are able to get a reservation. Cheers 

Food: 4.5 out of 5 
Service: 5 out of 5 
Ambiance: 5 out of 5 
Value: 4 out of 5 
Noise level: 4 out of 5 
Overall rating: 4.5 out of 5

We ordered a variety of dishes. They were mostly average. The truffle tortellini was $75 and tasted like it was made for $7.50. The rest of the food was just ok. Bill was $315 and I expected way more from a place like this. There are other Italian places in Vegas that are more well deserving of your funds.

I live in California and have never been to Carbones, but I just had their Pasta Sauce from a jar and after years of trying many different sauces to find the best, I can proclaim Carbones as the absolute best. It puts RAOs to shame. Definitely worth the price.

The best Italian restaurant in NYC! Undisputed! Treats you like a
VIP! Great food. Great service.

First, getting a reservation here is extremely difficult- it is like the supreme drop of resy. If you are lucky (and patient) enough to get a reservation, it is definitely worth a visit!

The bread basket and the accompanying pickled cauliflower, salami, and parmesan cheese were amazing. I got the baked clam trio, and while the clam with the uni on top was amazing, the other two were just ok. I also got the caesar salad which was delicious and their giant croutons are to die for. Would choose the salad over the clam trio in my opinion!

On to the main, I got the signature spicy vodka rigatoni and meatballs on the side. I loved the spicy vodka sauce, but thought the the pasta itself was slightly overcooked for my preference. Felt like it needed a minute less of cook time to have that perfect al dente texture. The meatball was so flavorful and juicy, and would definitely recommend. 

For dessert I got the tiramisu. While it was delicious, and it tasted like it may have had some orange liqueur-esque flavor, it wasn't my favorite. I personally love the super wet, pudding like tiramisu and less the "cake style" tiramisu. 

The service was amazing and the waiters were super nice and accommodating. While I do recommend coming here at least once, it felt a little overhyped.

Great Italian food that I can honestly say lived up to the hype. We ordered 3 things: the Veal Parm, Baked Clams, and the Spicy Rigatoni Vodka. Highly recommend the Veal Parm and Baked Clams. Surprisingly, though it's like the most popular item on the menu, I'd say you could skip on the Spicy Rigatoni Vodka. The pasta was perfectly al dente and the sauce super creamy but not overly heavy, but I just felt it was lacking a bit of flavor (maybe could've had a bit more tomato paste). The Veal Parm, on the other hand, is CHEF'S KISS!! Perfectly cheesy goodness on top of tender and breaded veal cuts. And the Baked Clams omg...please get that also. It's a mix/variety of different toppings on the clams but they're all amazing. My favorite was probably the pesto one. The starter they serve you is by far the best bread starter I've ever had at an Italian (or any American) restaurant. The bread already starts of as a super loaded garlic bread on its own, and then it comes with fresh mozzarella and salami on the side for pairing. Ugh amazing.

I'll start by saying this place has a great atmosphere, but to me does not live up to the hype. For starters its a pain to get a reservation and eating outside (although beautifully decorated) is not worth the money you pay for the food. I've had a lot of great food and don't mind paying extra if its spectacular, but I feel like it wasn't particularly memorable.

BELIEVE THE HYPE. I was lucky enough to score a reservation here, and it absolutely did not disappoint. I knew this was going to be my kind of place the moment a waiter waltzed up and gave me a totally unsolicited giant hunk of cheese. Which was delicious. The complimentary basket of bread (especially the foccacia with red sauce) was also excellent. From that moment on, everything from the wine (get the Oregon Pinot Noir - it's fantastic) on to the dessert was epic. I started with the carpaccio pimentaro - which was the best carpaccio I've ever had. I progressed to the spicy vodka rigatoni which also exceeded even my very high expectations (it's their signature dish) and truly was spicy. I had the chocolate hazelnut cake for dessert which was fantastic as well. The whole time, I was serenaded with 50s tunes from classic folks like Dion while also enjoying some of the best people watching New York has to offer. (To non-native New Yorkers, you have to do it on the DL while pretending to be totally disinterested.) The restaurant is intimate, authentically and lovingly decorated, and has outstanding service. Get to work scoring yourself a reservation here 30 days in advance because it is completely worth it.

Went here for lunch with a friend. We both got the spicy rigatoni vodka pasta-- the sauce was spicy and flavorful which was good but otherwise a pretty plain pasta. Not sure if the person taking our order was the manager or a server (he was dressed in a suit), but he was very brusque and made us feel rushed. He seemed annoyed since we didn't order drinks or dessert. I noticed that he made a point to ask the couple next to us, who arrived at the same time, how their meal was going and then completely ignored our table. The other waitstaff and the hostess were very nice though. 

Food- 3/5
Service -3/5
A bit overrated tbh. The best was the shrimp dumplings but the pasta & lamb dishes that I got weren't that great - very average. Won't be coming again either.

What can I say, its carbone. Always phenomenal but honestly the carbone miami is better. Everything is fresh, service is spectacular. Food is either really big hit or miss (that's why its getting a 4 star). Otherwise, its amazing and if you can snag up a reservation at carbone I suggest you take it. You'll leave full & satisfied

Amazing evening and great experience with lively vibe, staff was super friendly and attentive.  My favorite was the lobster ravioli, the spicy rigatoni and tortellini ragu was so delicious! And have to get Mario's meatballs!  Had the clams appetizers and Gibson to start, such a great meal!

The experience of dining at carbone is fun, but honestly not worth the price. I've had so much good Italian food over the years and I didn't understand what the fuss was about at this establishment. Glad I experienced it, but wouldn't go out of my way to go back again.

Sadly, what was once an amazing concept - upscale mid-century American-Italian - is now a caricature, by design.

Reservations are essentially impossible unless you have a connect (and ALL prime time tables are reserved for connects - you CANNOT get an 8pm table here, ever). The rest are jammed with tourists and out-of-towners who are ok taking an 11pm reservation for the pleasure of making Jeff Zalaznick more wealthy.

That all might be ok if the food hadn't seriously gone downhill the past few years and the prices continued to rise. Now the only good thing about this place is the fact that they kept the old Rocco's sign.
This place really meets up to its hype. Not only is the food great, but the service is amazing. They're super friendly as if you've dined here for years. I dream of the bread basket.

If you manage to get a reservation at Carbone, you HAVE to get the Oysters Posillipo. A very underrated appetizer. The spicy rigatoni was okay - nothing too special, but our waiter recommended to order with the special of the day which was mixed meat meatballs, which made it better. Also, skip the tiramisu and get the lemon cheesecake. As someone who's not a fan of lemon, the cheesecake exceeded my expectations. Moist with a crisp base.

This place is famous for a reason! I was determined to get a dinner reservation and was lucky enough to snag one during our NY stay. The service is beyond exceptional, almost overwhelming. I felt like all of the staff was attentive and friendly. Loved that Ricky our server was Italian, made it feel so authentic. The pasta and ravioli was amazing. The only thing I did not like was that the seating we so close together since the restaurant is small and quaint. Luckily the reservation was a right at opening time and we asked to move to an edge seat and staff were accommodating. A beautiful place for a romantic dinner if you're lucky to get a reservation!

Yes it's pricy. Yes it's insanely hard to get in. Yes you might have to call every day and pray for a cancellation. But you'll be glad you did. I've never been to a restaurant where it seems like everyone loves working there and truly takes pride in their job. The waiters and sommeliers and everyone that works here have that vibe. And duh, you have to try the spicy rigatoni. It's a given.

2 words, spicy rigatoni. Must try!! We also split the veal parmesan, its HUGE, good enough for 3/4 people to share honestly. Sit either indoors or outdoors, both are really pretty. I didn't think spicy rigatoni could be this delicious but it was. Also get the meatballs!

Everything Aligned in Resy somehow and we got a reservation for the 3 days we were visiting NYC. And for a large party too!  Noon on a Sunday so was very fortunate.  But from what I hear it is near to impossible to get a prime spot on a prime day...unless you have a connect. Service was top-notch, professional, and responsive. We ordered everything that was recommended and was really good but for the hype...thought there were a lot better options without having to go through the reservation fiasco. Nonetheless, The spicy rigatoni vodka pasta was superb along with the meatballs. Prices were what you expect. $50-70 + for a dish and a drink menu averaging $30 a drink. Overall was a great experience to do once imo. Enjoy!

Getting a reservation at Carbone was not easy but well worth the effort. I dined solo at 11:30 AM on a Wednesday and loved everything about the food and ambiance. The complimentary garlic bread with salami and mozzarella and Italian cookies were incredible. I ordered the baked clams, a meatball, and of course, the spicy rigatoni. Everything was every bit as good as I was expecting based on the hype. Can't wait to go back again someday!

CARBONE!! So psyched I got to dine at Carbone last night. Let me share the deetz on whether it's worth the hype- it's not lol. But you must experience it atleast once in your life! It was my boyfriend's birthday so we went HAM and ordered 4 apps and 2 entreés for 2 people... Kind of regret some choices, but atleast we have a truckload of leftovers haha. 

A lot of people said to order the caesar salad so I did, and it was not tossed tableside! I wanted the show and was disappointed when they brought it out dressed. The assorted clams were great, but the prosciutto and fresh mozzarella really blew us away. Presentation, taste, and tableside assembly was immaculate! Don't get the calamari. Just. Don't. 

For mains, we ordered...you guessed it... the spicy rigatoni! And it was as delicious as everyone says. Will definitely be getting it for take-out every now and then. The veal parm was good, but not for the price. We were already busting out of our pants, so we probably should've skipped that one. 

All in all, an unforgettable experience. Fantastic service throughout and it's great Italian food. I just think that you can also find great Italian food at many other places without having your wallet in a choke-hold and your blood pressure out the roof from trying to get a reservation.

By far my favorite spot to get spicy vodka rigatoni in the city. I've been to a handful of the most popular and difficult to get reservation Italian spots and Carbone still reigns as number one in my book. From the service to quality to taste of food, this dining experience is something that I will remember forever and will keep me coming back for more. 

My boyfriend and I came here on a Saturday night during prime time for dinner and every table was full - inside and outside. We were seated inside at a cozy table in the back room; it was dimly lit and a very romantic setting. The service was friendly, swift, and efficient which matched the freshness and quality of the food we ordered. 

We had the freshly made table-side Caesar salad to start with an assortment of bread, followed by prosciutto and meatballs. For our mains we got the spicy vodka rigatoni and veal parmesan. To finish our meal we got the cheesecake and Affogato as well as complimentary treats from the kitchen. Everything was high quality and delicious, the spicy vodka rigatoni is a must get with its incredibly rich flavor profile unmatched by anywhere else in the city. 

I highly recommend this place for a special occasion; from the restaurant setting to the food, it'll make a memorable experience.

Went to website - 30 days in advance for three consecutive days - even called American Express Concierge to check availability - three different days...  not a chance.....  went straight to notify list... never heard a word... walk ins? Who knows
Terrible..

Booked my reservation a month in advance and I was only able to come for lunch! The service is really nice and you'll get your food and drinks quickly too. Lots of complimentary items too!
I got a mojito to start with and it was really good. They start you off with garlic bread, spicy salami and fresh mozzarella. The cheese was amazing and so soft and fresh. 
For entrees, I got the famous spicy rigatoni and I was wondering at first if this would be too over hyped but I actually thought it was really good. They mix sautéed onions into the sauce and the spice level was good too. 
They gave complimentary rainbow cookies as a dessert and I was too full to get anything else but I have to come back for dessert. 
Overall, I'm really happy with my experience here. The service was great, the ambiance was adorable and the food met expectations.
It's good we know. Is it worth dying to get in at prob not. There's better spots in the city that you don't have to wait months for... but it's an institution so recommend going 1x if you can get in.

My best friend and I went in today when they opened for lunch at 11:30. We have been unable to get reservations, but asked the hostess if we could get a table. She was able to place us in the patio dining room, which was lovely. She was a nice and gracious hostess. 

Our waiter was a very pleasant man and I was pleased to have met him. The bread was very good, but the mozzarella is what really wins you over. Spicy rigatoni was a hit, of course. We also got the lobster ravioli which was very, very rich and had tons of lobster. 

Service and food 10/10

My life has changed. I am a changed lady. Carbone is good. Don't let the negative Nancy cry babies get to your head. If you can get a reservation please try to do it. Their bread is so good, mozzarella is very fresh, and now the star of the show... spicy pasta I LOVE IT!!!!!!!!!! The lobster raviolis were filled with lobster and just so creamy and rich! Everyone was very kind and attentive!
The ambiance is the best part. The crowd is filled with all types of people and the old school service is classic NY. The food was good, not great. Cocktails great and wine list extensive.

This place is absolutely difficult to get into. However I stayed a Baccarat hotel and went through Concierge to get a reservation without hesitation. They start off with bringing complimentary bread 3 different kinds, Salami , cheese and pickled Cauliflower.  It was all amazing but pace yourself as it's very good and filling.   I ordered a margarita which again was amazing not too sweet.  I also ordered meatballs, Lamb and spicy rigatoni.  Once again everything was simply delicious.  If you can get an opportunity to visit Carbone I highly suggest you go hungry and yes it's expensive but worth the experience ambiance and money.  SPLURGE  if you don't have the means... it's a lifetime experience and besides you never know who you may be dinning next to.   Highly recommend.
One of the few experiences in my life, dining or otherwise, that far exceeded the astronomical expectations and hype. Brilliant! Still dreaming about this meal and expect to be for a long while.

People loveee to knock Carbone, but I still think it is one of the absolute greatest restaurants in New York City. I've been five times for both lunch and dinner. Have sat both indoors and outdoors. No matter where I'm sitting or what time of day it is, the food and dining experience is always top tier. I love how they serve soppresseta, fresh mozzarella and bread to start and I love how attentive the waiters are.  If you're visiting NYC and know that you're going just one time only, I would be sure to get two plates of the spicy rigatoni as well as the meatballs. Both items are by far the greatest on the menu and although it's fun to try many different things, there's really nothing quite like the spicy rigatoni. Make sure you save room for the carrot cake after your meal!

Do not go here if you are looking to save money. This is the most justifiable Italian place to spend some Benjamins so don't complain about it!

The key to getting a reservation: wait on Carbone's resy page a month in advanced of your desired date... the reservations start to open at 10 am on the dot.

A few of my friends and I finally get a reservation at this restaurant, it was a very hard one to get a reservation..
Was it worth it? To be honest it was just okay for me,,
Nothing wrong with the food, everything was actually on point.. The pasta are all dente and the seasonings are great..
The only thing was just the restaurant settings was a bit off, the tables were very crowded and too close to each other makes us a little uncomfortable, we spend less than 40 mins dining because how much uncomfortable sitting there..
Once you get in, you cant even move because there is barely any space to even cross your legs because behind you there is another chair with other customers..
I guess to get overall experience we need to have a balance on both dining experience and food.. but they were lacking on the experience.. I will think about it again whether if I would like to come back here.. Once in a lifetime should you try it? I would say that There are a lot of other great Italian restaurants in the city that might not be as famous as this but offers delicious food too.. Its your call.. Cheers..
Amazing food and absolutely great service. Attended a corporate dinner here and was so amazed at how great each entree was. Definitely making another reservation ASAP.
You can't get a reservation and they say to go on Resy a month before you want to go but it's a lie because you can't get a res on Resy either. ‍

I'm a big pasta fan and let me tell you... best pasta in NYC! It's a place to come hang out with your besties or go on a date. You will definitely spot a celebrity or two. It's a hot spot. Make sure to make a reservation in advance! We came for a late night dinner and I am so glad we did! Carbone is the pasta STANDARD!

It's good.  But it's only about par.  

Cocktails, apps, pastas, meats and desserts.  Arrived early but was seated and had a cocktail.  Love it. Free starters included good mozz, salami and unfortunately dry and crusty cheesy garlic bread.  Service was ok.  Dishes were brought without explanation (variations of baked clams) and missing follow up service (portioning veal).  But our main server did offer helpful suggestions on portions and choices.  

2 rounds of cocktails, decently tasty and strong. Ended up with Caesar salad, baked clams (primally satisfying), one single meatball, double rigatoni, veal (lived up to expectations), chicken (surprisingly good).  Natalie waved us off from the mushroom pasta, a full serving of meatballs and the broccoli rabe, and she was right as we only managed half of the veal even after the adjustments.  Left us space for the lemon cheesecake (good tartness for balance)and chocolate cake (not overwhelmingly sweet or heavy), and espressos.  

The quality is there but given the prices I think they (only) met expectations.  Still, it's a good time all in so it's worth a visit, if you can get a booking.

Spicy rigatoni is as good as they say. I am a bit lukewarm on other dishes though. The tortellini a la ragu is good but I've had better. Liked but didn't love the lobster ravioli. Meatballs are pretty good but not mind blowing. However, one star must be deducted for a surprisingly sub standard service. While our server Natalie is polite, attentive and informative, the other staffs' performance left a lot to be desired. They almost slammed the plates in our face. Came out with the breadcrumbs for the ravioli when we already had a few bites and looked so eager to send us away. They were in such a rush to clear out the dished on our tables when we weren't even finished eating them! When there were a few morsels left on the sharing plate, they just haphazardly threw them on our individual plates without asking. You could've mistaken their service for a cheap restaurant. The terrible service alone almost ruined our experience! Not sure if the food totally made up for the service though. I will not mention anything about the price because it's carbone. You already know what's coming.

Told my fiancé this place was a must try for me and as per usual he delivered! Got us reservations for lunch and boy did Carbone meet my expectations! Their spicy rigatoni has been an endeavor and today I came and conquered haha! It was everything I expected it to be, not overtly spicy, pasta made to perfection, and just the right portion amount. As an antipasti we had the Baked clams, which include 9 clams served in portions of 3 different styles. All were delish!!! My fiancé had their shrimp scampi which included Madagascar shrimps and for dessert we had their tiramisu and chocolate cake. The chocolate cake was the perfect balance of moist and rich, it was paired with Vanilla Gelato topped with gold foil on a base that included a blended cream like sauce. Truly mouth watering! Their tiramisu was a bit underwhelming especially after having had their chocolate cake haha but it wasn't mediocre. I loved their music which included varieties of Jazz. Their setting consists of low ceilings, dim lighting, brick walls, and classic italian decor, all of which worked cohesively to give you a true Italian experience. I absolutely loved it here! The staff were all gentlemen not only in attire but persona as well. The host who greeted us was very kind also! We will be back! I forgot to mention their huge menus (literally) which I consider to now be a staple as I was not expecting them to be that large haha- I loved it!

I really wanted to believe this restaurant was overhyped, since it's *impossible* to get a reservation, but Carbone was well worth it, and just so delicious... I was finally able to snag a reservation and went for lunch. Everything was amazing: the food, the setting, and the service. I definitely understand the hype and will definitely be one of the people contributing to hyping Carbone. They offer a large selection of items, and seasonal foods as well.

One of the reasons I fell in love with Carbone was the fresh Mozzarella, Prosciutto and Garlic Bread they bring out once you are seated. Just look at this spread... This was really good, and a great start to our lunch.

Carpaccio Ciemontese~ I expected to be underwhelmed but this dish was created to perfection. Fresh mushrooms, cracked pepper, and delicious olive oil complemented the beef perfectly. Can't forget to mention that the beef was brushed with a ~truffle emulsion~...

Eggplant & Zucchini Scapece~ This was addictive. I am a bit biased since I absolutely love eggplant and zucchini, but this was one of a kind. Ricotta and
parmesan were the perfect addition to the perfectly roasted vegetables. If you like eggplant and zucchini, this is the appetizer for you.

SEASONAL ITEM~ We were lucky to try the Tomato Heirloom Salad. If you are lucky enough to get a reservation  at Carbone, and lucky enough to go when they have the tomato salad... Get it. I am not usually the biggest pesto fan but here, it complemented the tomatoes perfectly.

Spicy Rigatoni Vodka~ Yes, it lived up to the hype. The pasta is perfectly cooked and the sauce is perfectly spicy. This is definitely one of the best pastas in the city - lots of places try to copycat this dish but they just don't live up to the original.

Mario's Meatballs~ *wow*. They're big, shareable, and so tasty. I don't know what they add to their tomato sauce to make it so good, but this is a must.

Now for an item that honestly topped everything we ate. The Veal Parmesan. I suggest 2-4 people share this dish as it is pretty copious. When my boyfriend suggested we get this dish, I was hesitant at first because I wanted to focus all my efforts on the spicy rigatoni. I am so happy that I listened - the Veal Parm topped the spicy rigatoni (yes, I said it). The Veal was soft, juicy, perfectly seasoned and with a crispy crust. The tomato sauce was just amazing. The mozzarella on top was exactly what we needed. ORDER THIS!

Carrot Cake~ The waiter had informed us that this was one of the most popular items. And let me just say, I don't usually understand veggies' place in desserts but this, I understood. This Carrot Cake was delicious.

If you know me at all you know that I am a sucker for Lemon Cheesecakes. So, when I saw Carbone had one on the menu... It had to be ordered. It did NOT disappoint... Dare I say: one of my favorite cheesecakes in the city?

Unfortunately not as life changing as I remembered. Food is very good, service is great but it just didn't stand out like I remembered. I think the spicy rigatoni just wasn't spicy at all and that may be why it wasn't as addictively good as my last time long ago. Veal parm is good. Is it worth 3x the price of an old school Italian place? No, and might not even be as good. If money is no object it's good, not great.

That spicy rigatoni vodka is what dreams are made of. My boyfriend and I had such a great time here. We were able to snag lunch reservations on a Saturday for our anniversary and we're not disappointed. I was so thrilled I forgot to take pictures of anything but the pasta. We got a couple appetizers, in addition to the complementary bread with mozzarella and salami that comes to the table. They were good but large for only two people. For our entrees we got the spicy rigatoni vodka and lobster ravioli. I am a vegetarian so I didn't try the lobster ravioli, but my boyfriend said it was the best lobster ravioli he's ever had. It had a good amount of lobster in the dish compared to other establishments. We didn't order dessert as we were too full, but we enjoyed the little complementary rainbow cookies. We had a wonderful server, I can't remember her name, but she was very sweet and created a welcoming environment. Can't wait to go back !!
Amazing service! Recommend going exactly at the reservation time, it's so packed you can't sit early and the bar doesn't have seats so walk in at the exact time

Heard about all the hype about this restaurant and my boyfriend and I decided to try it. Got a Resy reservation and after a few months, finally got a lunchtime spot!

Service was phenomenal, from the water refills to the food time getting to our tables in a quick time. Our server Joey was very friendly and attentive which was great!

For food, we got the spicy rigatoni in vodka sauce and it was my favorite dish! We also got the meatballs and I really enjoyed them being served together! We got the pork chops and it was OK, I definitely liked our first course more. Lastly, we got the tiramisu and it was delicious! The Nutella crusts on the outside of each slice was really good too. 

We got mai tais and they were very refreshing!

I would come back for the spicy rigatoni

After the long awaited hype and the difficulty in securing a reservation, my friends and I managed to snag a spot to try the famous Carbone. I've heard from people that it's great or overhyped. But to try it and to form my own opinion. 

My opinion is to agree that the food is overhyped and there's nothing that blows this place out of the park to live up to the word of mouth that passes around of this place. The pasta were all very normal, replicable at home, and overpriced. I've been to many places in LA that the pasta is much tastier and more special (and not to mention a larger portion). A vodka rigatoni could hardly justify $25 to me when I can make my own vodka rigatoni that's just as good (if not better) at home for at least half the cost. Also, who is purchasing a branzino for $95. Please tell me. 

Overall, OK food at best and would not come here again. If a friend is curious, would tell them to try it out for the hype but would not be a recommendation.
Today we had the luck to ate at Carbone, and it was even better that what we image, the service is the best part, everybody there is so nice, everything was so delicious.
Too hard to get a review and definitely not worth the hype anyways. Go to a home in the wall instead...

"Finally!"This is known to be one of nyc's more difficult restaurants to get a Resy for, you really need to make an effort and put in some work to book a table. All my stars aligned one day and booked a table for two for a Saturday afternoon. I knew exactly what I wanted once I sat down in this elegant, old fashioned restaurant; the spicy rigatoni vodka. In addition, we ordered the mushroom pasta(its called something fancier on the menu), and  their baked garlic potatoes. I would say each dish was very hearty and delicious, but next time I would recommend balancing out the meal by ordering a salad instead of a dish of hot potatoes which we tried to finish. Paring a fresh cold salad w/ some fresh warm pasta would've been the best pairing! (Other tables ordered their table side Caesar). Overall, I gave this place a 4/5 because personally although their spicy rigatoni pasta was good w/ a nice spice kick, I wasn't like AMAZED like it was the best pasta dish I've had. It was more of the experience to be honest that I felt most proud to being part of which was to get a seat at a table here and review their popular dish. The exclusivity is it's own gem

I am giving this review 5 stars mainly from our server Natalie. On top of giving amazing service, she went above and beyond to fix a problem that had happened with another server when I had come in February 2022. She truly made our experience amazing, and the food was great as well.

Beyond expectation.  Beyond good.   Service is unreal.   You feel like you're in grandmas kitchen plus a few extra friends.   Tried the octopus this time.  It is now added to the must try list every time.  In addition the spicy rigatoni is as alway to die for.  And the yummy cookies.   Heaven and don't forget some berries and cream.

Carbone in Greenwich Village is a New York institution that lives up to the hype.  The restaurant is incredibly well kept, and the food was phenomenal. 

When you enter the restaurant, the decoration and wait staff will make you feel like stepping back in time.  Classic Italian food while being serenaded in Frank Sinatra, it's absolutely worth the experience if you're able to get secure a reservation.
Great for a classic Italian meal. The zucchini and eggplant is exceptional as well as the complementary starters. Standout was the veal parm.

Carbone is ICONIC. The food and ambiance is a 10/10. Chico the server was amazing and needs to be upgraded to waiter. The spicy rigatoni is a MUST. We were a little disappointed in the "rush", for an expensive restaurant with an iconic reputation, we felt extremely rushed. We sat down for a 2pm reservation at 2:10 because our table was paying & we're told we had to order by 2:20 because the kitchen closes soon. They were also out of the Cesar salad which we were looking forward to... Our waitress was terrible. She barely checked in & by the time our reservation was over we were being rushed out!! they continued to mention the "check" and kept clearing our plates as if we HAD to leave. I would go back for the food and ambiance but the service needs to be adjusted. if it wasn't for chico, our experience would not be the same

My nephew is the family expert on Carbone and I came along for the ride on this one.  When the seeds of our NYC foodie trip were planted months ago, he said I'll try to get us into Carbone.  I looked it up, saw it's Italian (and not some new fusion what not or another), and said "what's so special about Carbone" and he goes "it's the best Italian restaurant in the country".  "Oh, one of those, huh?"  I said skeptically.  But Carbone does have a one star Michelin rating.

Well, after weeks of trying/waiting, he somehow (hint: he's an Amex spender) got us a last minute and prime 12:30pm Thursday lunch opening and we had no scheduled conflicts, perfect!  When I first walked in, it reminded me of seeing Chicago's Au Cheval the shocking first time - tiny, given its renown!  No wonder reservations are impossible!  Their prices for the portions are also maybe 2-3x "average", but plenty of people are willing to pay for something here.  That something is a classy old-world intimate Italian setting but with dishes served in trend-setting distinctive style and tip-top quality.  Also kinda cool for an NYC visitor, this renowned restaurant is located inconspicuously and unassumingly on a quiet, older residential street, taking us back to yesteryear.

Our threesome had the following for lunch:

- two old-fashioned's and an iced tea (the OF's were delicious but smallish for $20)
- complimentary bread service
- Caesar salad
- spicy rigatoni vodka
- baked clams served in 3 assortments
- tortellini al ragu
- meatballs
- broccoli rabe
- complimentary rainbow dessert cookies

It was a cheesy and filling lunch, and also memorable and spectacular.  Some notable distinctions and recalls:

The bread service with garlic bread, salami slices, and those amazing mozzarella balls.  The server pre-cuts the mozzarella with scissors.  I tried to cut some off with a butter knife, and it was a struggle as it was so thick and gooey and clingy in a good distinctive way.  I'll probably never see that freshness and quality again.

The Caesar salad was prepared tableside by our head server John.  I've never had that happen.  It also contained huge croutons and whole anchovy slices, another new experience.  Anchovy paste is typically used for some brininess in Caesar salad dressing, but here's it's the whole anchovy.

The spicy rigatoni vodka is their signature dish.  Wow, delicious and filling with nice al dente pasta and it had a surprising medium strong spice level that builds with each mouthful.  The vodka sauces I've had were all mild, and I don't recall even seeing spicy offered at the Italian places I usually go to.  Something to look for in future and this place is the benchmark for this dish.  They also prepared a total of 1.5 servings, so we each got a 1/2 serving which was perfect.

Baked clams, another wowy distinctive dish.  9 clams are served in 3 styles - ha, so convenient for our party of 3.  Oreganata with breadcrumbs, Casino with bacon (lardon) and peppers, and Fantasia with sweet sea urchin.  The baked clams were all soft and tender and not chewy.  The lardon was distinctive and like a clear plastic sheet - virtually all fat, but so smoky and tasty.  The sea urchin was also delicate and fatty like bone marrow.  I really liked them all, but if I were to pick just one for another taste - it might be the Oreganata just to taste more of the perfectly baked clam.

Tortellini al ragu - delicious, hearty, and filling.  Maybe only because it was mild, it was overshadowed by its rigatoni star sister.

Meatballs - these aren't on the menu and you need to know to request them. 
They're made with beef, pork, and veal and were tasty and delicate and it had a nice mildly fried texture on the surface.

Broccoli rabe - honestly I didn't like.  It's apparently in the turnip family, and was on bitter and chewy side, but nice to try anyway.

The head servers are dressed in maroon tuxedos and all other male staff had bow ties.  Service was classy and good as you would expect.  John was our head server and I'll just say he did his job but the guy I really liked was his assistant Elliott.  Elliott was friendly and engaging and took pics for us both outside (coincidentally) and inside the restaurant.  The restaurant is small and tight but charming.  Besides the tables you can see as you walk in, there's just one other small room in the back through a hallway.  I guess this is what it's like to have had dinner with say Frank Sinatra and it was a most memorable special occasion outing for us.

This restaurant thrives on the hype that securing a reservation is unattainable. Meanwhile, Saturday night there were several empty tables and now I understand
why. Funny, because I just read this morning that Justin Bieber and his wife were actually turned away Saturday night (the same night
that I dined there) because they didn't have a reservation. This restaurant loves the publicity they receive in the press that they turned away celebs such as Bieber and George Clooney. It makes their
establishment appear even that more exclusive, which is a joke! They are running an extremely successful smoke and mirror
campaign. I booked my reservation through my American Express Platinum Card and was seated in their sponsored patio. It was a
glorified portable hallway with cheesy artificial floral arrangements and fruit. It wasn't even a wide enough space for the waiter to make a table side Caesar salad. The food was mediocre at best with pretentious prices. I'd compare the food quality to that of a Buca Di Beppo or Olive Garden to be honest. There is nothing special about this restaurant. The meatballs arrived cold and undercooked (we sent them back) and their famous spicy rigatoni was very chewy pasta with vodka sauce that actually tasted like it came right out of a jar. My husband and I were very disappointed to say the least in this experience, and will obviously never return. Advice...don't follow the herd like I did!!

My visit to Carbone was highly anticipated, and it did not disappoint!  I have watched and read many reviews for Carbone and after visiting, it's hard to not be impressed!  The service was solid, and the restaurant was very clean and efficiently run.  Hard not to have a good time dining here.  From the host, waiter, to the bussing staff, they were all top notch.  

Our group ordered: Caesar Salad, Assorted Baked Clams, Tortellini al Ragu, Spicy Rigatoni Vodka, Broccoli Rabe, and side of Meatballs. The top 3 of what we ordered were the clams, rigatoni and meatballs.  

The Caesar salad was extra fancy with table side prep with the fresh grated cheese, anchovy fillets, and mixed right in front of you!

The assorted clams are great to share with a group, and prepared 3 ways bread crumbs, with sea urchin, and with lardon.  My favorite way was the standard with bread crumbs, but the others were good to try as well. 

The rigatoni was also one of the most popular dishes and I can see why.  It was prepared really well. The sauce was built up nice, and had a good level of flavor and spice which matched the pasta well.  

After visiting I can see where all the good and bad reviews come from.  If you get the $33 rigatoni and it comes with the garlic bread, salami, and cheese, with the cookie for dessert, this could be a lovely experience.  If you ordered the $89 veal parmesan and it doesn't knock your socks off, you might be underwhelmed. 

I can't say this is my favorite Italian restaurant, but it's definitely top 5.  I definitely wouldn't miss it if I was in NYC and was lucky enough to get reservations!

I have been dying to try Carbone for forever, as I'm sure a lot of people also have been. A reservation is almost impossible to get, with it always being completely sold out. However, one day, I was randomly checking and they had a lunch spot open!! It was 2 hours before an important midterm for me but I knew I couldn't miss it. Anyways the food was sooo good. Highly highly recommend their pasta. We also got a seafood dish (I think it was a special for the day because it wasn't on their menu, we asked the waiter for a seafood recommendation and he mentioned this one, but then went off to ask someone else for the price, which makes me think it was off menu) and a meat dish. Both of those dishes were really good, a solid 9/10, but it was the pasta that really blew me away. If you are able to get an impossible resy here, I'd highly highly recommend. Wasn't too expensive either, $185 for the two of us (including tip and tax).

So iconic and for good reason. The spicy rigatoni here is surprisingly actually as good as everyone says it is. The lobster ravioli is also delicious and is packed with tons of lobster meat, but I would definitely just get my own spicy rigatoni next time. Also love the garlic bread, prosciutto, and mozzarella that comes with your meal. The mozzarella is so good that I would also order the antipasti next time. The potatoes Louie side dish is amazing as well. Definitely worth it if you can get a reservation!

Overall, great experience. To start we had their fresh mozzarella and bread, which may have been some of the best mozzarella we've ever had. The lobster ravioli and spicy rigatoni were perfect. Delicious and packed with flavors. The veal parm, although highly recommended, didn't live up to the hype. Was very salty and mostly tasted the breaded exterior. Maybe a one time deal but wasn't impressed at all. Otherwise, very good.

Before going, I found myself wondering if this place is worth the hype. It mostly is, although the prices are a bit steep. Rigatoni really is very good. They get a bonus star from me, though for turning away Justin Bieber

We finally landed a dinner reservation on Friday night and it was amazing! The only reason for 4 stars instead of 5 is because our waiter was a little condescending. It started with an espresso martini at the bar while we waited for our table to be ready. Then once we were seated the complimentary breads and salami came out (but no fresh mozz?!) which was delicious, I could only get a 9:45 resy so I was very hungry when we sat down. For apps we ordered the baked clams and marinated artichoke hearts (a side that we ordered as an app). Both were unbelievable, but in the clam spread the regular oreganata clam was my favorite. For entrees we split the spicy rigatoni, lobster ravioli and side of meatballs. I would absolutely recommend everything we ordered and I need to go back to try other menu items we didn't get to. Bravo!
Probably the best meal I have ever had! Delicious! Great service and very memorable! We got the eggplant appetizer, spicy rigatoni vodka, and tortellini ragu. Highly recommend!

Exceptional. The only thing I don't recommend is the carpaccio, but that could just be me. The rigatoni, meatballs, bread course, lobster ravioli, and veal Parmesan were next level. The atmosphere is perfect, the staff is very pleasant. GO THERE NOW!

We ordered the lobster ravioli, two spicy rigatonis, fettuccine con fungi, linguini vongole, orecchiette vito and carrot cake. Everything was overpriced and overhyped. I wouldn't visit Carbone again. Though I have to note that the service was nice. I appreciated the complimentary breads and rainbow cookies as well. Gigi Hadid's spicy pasta recipe tastes just like Carbone's.
Hit the spot! I loved everything I tried from the spicy rigatoni, to the dessert, to the amazing starters.

Did I think that it was the best spicy vodka rigatoni that I ever had? Yes. Is that a reason to go back? No. 

While the spicy vodka rigatoni pasta lived up to the hype, I think that you can get a better Italian experience elsewhere. The lobster ravioli, while good, was nothing extraordinary.

Bottom line is I don't think the food justifies the hype or price.

Spicy rigatoni is the best dish I have had the pleasure of partaking!  It is the perfect combination of texture, taste, and heat.  I am an avid fan of great Italian, and nothing tops the food, service, or ambience of Carbone.  

The bread, three different textures and flavors along with a great parnesean wheel slice are a perfect combo.   The halibut special and ribeye at carbone is second to none and dessert was perfect.

I love Frasca in boulder, and some Chicago top spots, Tadich in sf, yet Carbone sits alone at the top for us!

We ate at Carbone on Friday night.  We coincidentally sat next to Brent (review immediately below) and his son!  Was a really fun, wonderful experience.  Service was so great.  Agree that the 3 kinds of bread, parmesan wheel and pickled cauliflower that they bring out at the beginning are amazing.  I thought that the spicy rigatoni was very good but it was so rich that I could not eat more than a few bites.  The dover sole was amazing but I was so full from everything else that it was hard to eat very much of it.  One of my favorite dishes was the side order of mushrooms.  Delicious!  Lemon ricotta cheesecake was also very tasty.  Would definitely go back!

Chocolate cake and spicy rigatoni are to die for! This place is always hard to get into in NYC - Miami is somewhat easier, as the space is larger. Don't miss out on a chance to eat here. What really makes this place extra special is all of the extra food items that they give you... Extra cheese, their bread basket, their cauliflower and the rainbow cookies with dessert!!

I love love love Carbone. I had a stellar time there and I will always remember it. The food, the ambiance, and the service were 100% perfect. I look forward to going again in the future and even saw they have a Dallas location when I was just there. Knowing there is a Carbine in Dallas means I can take my parents and show them a little taste of what my life in NYC is like. Always a good time

I'll be honest with you; I'm too full to think straight right now and I am still trying to finish my second cocktail because these babies are STIFF, but the food at carbone was delicious and Blake was a fantastic server.

The place gives you the feel of an old school red sauce Italian restaurant you'd find in little Italy, except the food is actually good and there is no one standing at the door harassing you to come inside. Quite the opposite, it's hard as sh*t to get a reservation. I had a million *notify*s set on Resy and literally none of them ever worked, but finally one day I found a random available table for 2. Sorry that I can't offer better advice!

The daiquiri was delicious; it has always been one of my favorite cocktails! I will say it is a little on the sweeter side but most of the other patrons were women far younger than I so I understand the adherence to a different palate. The margarita I ordered was also good, but again, a little sweet.

The baked clams were a revelation, especially the ones with the uni, and the fresh mozzarella they give you with the bread before your meal tasted like pizza in the best way possible.

I can't say I will be back just because I don't know if I'll ever get another reservation ahaha, but my meal was great!

My friend managed to snag a reservation for a party of 2 on a Wednesday afternoon at 1:30pm. We strolled in got seated and enjoyed our meal and left at 3:00pm stuffed. Just for the service alone, I would give Carbone 5 stars. Staff is really attentive and helpful.  

I ordered an espresso martini and really enjoyed it. It was a nice amount of espresso and a nice amount of martini, made well. We ordered baked clams, spicy rigatoni, lobster ravioli and ended the meal with a dessert: carrot cake. The bread was probably my favorite out of the entire meal... On a side note though, the baked clams were really good. Spicy Rigatoni -- I wasn't too crazy about, it's worth the try it's good. I enjoyed the Lobster Ravioli -- it was creamy and complimented the Spicy Rigatoni. The carrot cake was a great note to end with, not too sweet. 

Personally, I wouldn't go again. BUT, if you manage to snag a reservation, it's worth the experience. :)
Amazing food, plain and simple. Very pricey but worth it. My favorite dishes are the Spicy Vodka Pasta& Ribeye Diana

I would say I was happy with everything but I wasn't wowed by anything. Idk if it lives up to they hype-- it's a great restaurant, but there's also a LOT of hype. Of course reservations are hard to come by-- you have to be on resy at 10 am on the dot, logged in, and they're gone within 2 min. If you're flexible you can also sign up for notifications, I've had pretty good luck with people canceling. Went on a super hot day and I think I might actually prefer the outdoor dining over indoor; their outdoor setup is really well done, less crowded, and with more of a breeze. Service was great and their famous starter bread and mozzarella was really yummy. They were sadly out of like half their dishes when I went for some reason? So I couldn't try everything I wanted to. But the oyster appetizer was really well cooked, their vodka rigatoni was simple but addicting, sea bass was delicate and flaky, and pork chops were decent as well. Loved the tortellini ragu, which I think is definitely underrated. Beer there is surprisingly good. Lemon ricotta cheesecake was a nice way to end the meal.
dinner at Carbone was amazing! The spicy rigatoni is definitely worth it, everything else was good too. The bread given at the beginning is one of the best parts

Beautiful restaurant, very good service. All dishes ordered were good except the so-called spicy rigatoni. No spice at all and a very sweet-tasting sauce. Tasted like I was eating a bowl of cereal.  Note to Chef/owner don't add sugar to your sauces! 

Would go back, but no rigatoni for me!

Got a reservation for outdoor lunch. Their outdoor set up is one of the best I've seen, feels like we're inside the actual restaurant and service doesn't miss a beat. 

We got some fresh bread, mozzarella and soppressata to start. For app we went  with the beets siciliana -- which was excellent, especially on a hot summer day. For our entrees we both wanted to try the spicy rigatoni vodka Carbone is known for. My husband liked it but it was VERY salty for me. It's one of the few pastas I didn't have to use crushed red pepper for so yes it definitely has flavor and spice but the salt overpowered the dish for me. We got the corn special -- which was excellent, the truffle was nice without being too overpowering. 

For dessert we got the chocolate hazelnut cake which I highly recommend.

Overall, we had a nice time and the service was great but disappointed in the main dish we wanted to try.

After many failed attempts to score a reservation at this coveted restaurant I thought eating at Carbone would be a distant dream.  Then on a random Thursday afternoon about 1:30PM I walked by the restaurant by happenstance and asked if I could have a table for 1.  And to my surprise they accommodated me.  Five minutes later I'm sitting in the patio and served complimentary garlic bread and warm mozzarella in olive oil.  I couldn't believe this deliciousness was free, I could've easily eaten as an appetizer.  I then ordered the famous spicy rigatoni and it is truly as advertised.  Entree served al dente, hot with just the right amount of creaminess and spice.  

I must note that I was severely underdressed in shorts and sneakers as I wasn't expecting to eat at a fine dining establishment, but I felt no air of pretensioness from the staff.  

At the end of my glorious meal, I was rewarded two complimentary rainbow cookies.  I had a Devine culinary experience and one that would last me a lifetime

Sometimes its really good sometimes its ok. 
They can be more consistent with the food quality.

Finally was able to get a reservation to try Carbone. It did not disappoint. The interior is small and intimate. There is the option for outdoor seating that also looked nice. After being seated and looking over the menu we started with the Caesar salad which was prepared table side and was delicious. We then split a spicy rigatoni and meatballs order. All dishes are meant to be shared and the portions were substantial. Too full for dessert. A great time at a great restaurant. I hope to make it back.
Amazing service, atmosphere and the food. Really loved lobster ravioli which was the best I've had as well as the baked clams. Iced cappuccino is also a must try.

Always gotta stop here when I'm in the city, the spicy vodka rigatoni is the best! Love the vibes and design of the restaurant. Have tried a handful of things on the menu and I must say it's all delicious

I finally got a reservation here after trying for two months! Sure it was on a Friday afternoon (past peak lunch hour), but this was my only chance after trying for so long. Though they were steady busy, this worked out to be the best time because you beat the crazy weekend rush and evening dinner crowds. The restaurant is larger than I expected with three dining areas. Enter the first area and you'll see tables as well as a small bar where drinks are made. To the left is another room with round tables for large groups. (Also, where the restroom is.) The most ideal spot is to continue straight when you enter and past the bar to the more private dining area. I was so happy to be seated here for my first Carbone experience. (I imagine this is where Drake or Rihanna sat. lol) This area has two round booths for large groups and offers more privacy, while there are other tables set along the wall are all great for 1-2 guests. The opposite side has a few larger tables. The lighting is dim and gives a fancy Italian/romantic vibe. The servers are all dressed in deep purple suits offering an added layer of sophistication to the venue. Everyone working there seemed jolly and helpful in answering any questions. My server Joey even asked if there were any allergies before he made recommendations on menu items for a vegetarian. I just wanted to know how 'spicy' is the spicy rigatoni?! His assessment of a 4 out of 10 spice level was accurate. 

On to the food - everyone gets a complimentary garlic bread and fresh mozzarella cheese in olive oil. After reading so many reviews about this spicy rigatoni, I knew I had to order this despite some other good vegetarian friendly options. I agree that this was THE BEST pasta! Tasted fresh and the sauce...wow! It has a little kick to it, but it doesn't linger. This coming from a person who can't handle a dot of Sriracha hot sauce! If you eat it with the mozzarella and bread provided it also tones down the spice level. The pasta is $33 for a plate and pretty filling for one. At this point there was just no room for a heavy Italian dessert or espresso. I asked for the check and was pleasantly surprised to get little complimentary mini rainbow cakes. The perfect end to this highly anticipated dining experience. Being so dim where I dined, it felt like I just had a pasta dinner until I left the restaurant and realized it was just late afternoon. I was happy to have a heavy meal earlier in the day. They move fast, but you don't feel rushed. I think I was out of there in less than 40 minutes. Overall, expensive but highly recommend trying at least once! I might just buy their sauce and try making it at home someday. 

Tips:
- Try to go for a reservation on an off-peak day or time. Might increase your chances of getting in. Also, keep your group small 1-2 people for faster seating. 
- Try to get seated in the back room for the classic fancy Italian dining experience. They have an enclosed outdoor seating area but seems this is just for staff to prep table settings. 
- When I placed my order, I was told I could not add anything later and would need to decide then. Not sure if this was based on timing and kitchen closing? 2pm on a weekday with steady customers coming in, I wasn't sure. Ask your server about that one. Seems like I could order dessert after or espresso though. 
- Note there is a cancellation fee if you don't do this early enough (I think within 24-48 hours?). You should get a text a few days prior to your reservation to confirm you are still going. 
- Be quick with your photos as wait staff is constantly zooming through the restaurant with plates and seating others.

Rigatoni Vodka---best ever, but expensive and small portion. They want you to buy other stuff, but the other stuff isn't as good. For example, wasn't impressed with the meatballs or spaghetti pomodoro and my colleagues didn't think the oysters were that great. Vibe is great during dinner and ok during lunch.

I was skeptical...a place THIS hyped, this famous, and this hard to get into that even cool guy Drake raps about it. Surely it can't live up to the expectations, especially when all I see on the menu are basic Italian staples I've been eating since I left the womb. But it was NOT a letdown. 

Started with Meatballs and the famed Caesar Salad. Solid. And I'll contradict myself here a bit...the Caesar was maybe a tad overrated because I've been hearing about this thing going on a decade now. But then again, how good can a Caesar salad be? Good. Just good. And I did love the giant croutons, but still made me wish I got the also-popular baked clams.

Ok, now for the notorious...glorious...Spicy Rigatoni Vodka, because that one's a must get, right? Amazing. Different (and better) than every vodka-sauced pasta iteration you've ever had. Made it worth the trip and every garbage juice puddle on Thompson Street I stepped into with my day old Nike Killshot II's

Didn't get the gargantuan Veal Parm like everyone else does. Was torn between that and the Veal Marsala. Very happy with that call. The veal wasn't pounded thin like you're probably used to. It was more like a bone-in NY strip steak, nicely carved and ready to share. A great cut and an even better sauce.

Service was great. Music, decor, and overall ambiance was, for lack of a better word, just really cool. Felt like a scene out of Goodfellas, except the wiseguys were missing, probably in the even-more-exclusive back dining room that a mere peasant like you or I will never step foot in.

Oh and get the carrot cake.

Definitely hit the spot with solid Italian dining and excellent service. We ordered the spicy rigatoni, beef carpaccio, eggplant antipasta, lobster ravioli, hazelnut cake, and tiramisu. Lobster ravioli and hazelnut cake definitely exceeded my expectations. Spicy rigatoni was very flavorful and is certainly worth coming back for. Cocktails were STRONG which made the food experience even more enjoyable.

The service here is incredible. The staff is very attentive as they provided us with amazing hospitality. When you come here you have to order the Spicy rigatoni . The rigatoni is all that it is hyped up to be but I personally didn't think it was that spicy .  They say the plates are family size but I think if you want to order the plate for your self it would be fine honestly the portions aren't huge .  We also ordered the Chicken Scarpariello , the chicken was tender . It had a mix of flavor , my partner personally didn't like the sauce , I thought it was ok . Still worth ordering regardless . For desert we ordered the carrot cake . I believe it had a ginger bread mix . Keep in mind I do not like cake but I must say this desert was mouthwatering, it was soft the ice cream and crumbles that was paired with it complemented it well . It was really great . The only reason I'm giving Carbone 4 stars is b/c I wish the food was hotter , it was less than warm and I didn't like that but I definitely would go back . It is hard to get a reservation but not impossible. Can't wait to go back

The best part about carbone besides the rainbow
Cakes, is the incredible service. Very old school New York. Of course the bread is incredible, along with the spicy rigatoni- you have to at least try it!!

We got lucky and snagged a last minute 11:30pm reservation. The atmosphere is amazing here, very old school & classy. They bring you a delicious bread basket with cheese, pickled cauliflower & salami complimentary. We ordered the spicy vodka rigatoni and the lobster ravioli for our main entrees. I wouldn't say it's the best pasta I've had but it was good. What did stand out was the caprese salad! It was outstanding. Really friendly staff as well. It's worth the hype.

Probably some of the best service I've had. Amazing food and even better ambiance. Pricey for the portion but I guess you pay for the experience and the pictures... 
The starting bread and mozzarella are great. In fact it may be the best mozzarella I've had at a restaurant to date. The caprese was probably the best caprese I've had also. The spicy rigatoni lives up to the hype, especially for vegetarians. I also got the tortellini in a vegetarian red sauce it was some of the best vegetarian tortellini I've had. The Nutella tiramisu is not that great though.

Clearly Carbone doesn't need my good review to stay in business, but since I was a major skeptic coming in, I'm writing one for anyone else like me! 

My husband and I finally had dinner after four months of trying to get a reservation at a Normal Dinner Time (it took Amex concierge's help). Looking at the prices and the fact that a pasta with..nothing but sauce seemed to be everyone's favorite dish, we expected this would be a fine-but-not-worth-the-$$ New York dining experience crossed off the list.

Well, we were so wrong -- and altogether impressed. The Carbone atmosphere is real: feels clubby, secret, a world away from the bustle of NYU Land surrounding it (and the '50s doowop soundtrack is A+). Our waiter was super nice and unpretentious. The on the house little plates -- spicy salami, parmigiano reggiano, pickled spicy cauliflower and excellent bread -- are a nice pre-meal touch.

We ordered the off menu meatballs, linguini vongole and spicy rigatoni -- a perfect amount of food for two people (we considered also getting the cherry pepper ribs; it definitely would have been overdoing the food quantity).
