The meatballs are loosely packed and light as they go, definitely the best we've had in a restaurant in some time. The linguini sauce is delicious, super garlic and herby and a bit spicy, and packed with clams. And the spicy rigatoni--well, I get the obsession now. It's the most flavorful vodka sauce I've ever had, one you'll want to scrape up w a spoon when the pasta is gone. We were too full for dessert, but the complimentary rainbow cake was ...the best rainbow cake I've ever had.

All in all, Carbone really won us over, and is certainly the most standout red sauce Italian we've had in the city.

Anyone who rated this less than five stars is crazy.

Is it over the top expensive, yes. Will you have a better Italian dining experience in New York City, or possibly beyond? No.

From the ambience, to the music (mostly sinatra) , to the staff, you feel like you are in an old Hollywood mobster film. It's a great environment, and intoxicating. It definitely makes you purchase several bottles of wine.  We made sure to try all of the staples. Below are my rankings on must-try dishes. Also, my big honorable mention is the bread and cheese that they start the meal with. They basically give you marinara bread, Texas toast, plain bread and butter, and a piece of delicious cheese even before you order a dish.

Spicy rigatoni
Tortellini Ragu
Meatballs
Bronzino
Oysters
Cesar

Again. There were no misses. But the top 3 I would 100% get again.

I was so excited for Carbone, because everyone was raving about it. I was so upset because my pasta was so salty it was inedible. Everything else tasted amazing, we had so many complimentary starters which I was thankful for! Their mozz and peppers were great, the corn amazing! But the pasta, the star of the show, was so inedible we couldn't finish our meal. I had to squeeze that sauce out of the noodles to eat it. I definitely think it was made incorrectly, but everything else was so good I can't tell if that was an accident or if it's actually supposed to taste that way.

Honestly, it lives up to the hype. I got a reservation on resy and they were so friendly when I checked in. The pasta was fabulous. Honestly, one of the best carrot cakes I've ever had. Lovely decor, location!

Carbone is a New York City must! Reservations are available 30 days in advance, and open at 10am ET - they book up within minutes so make sure to be quick. We were seated right at our reservation time, and the waitstaff was extremely attentive. 

To start, they brought out garlic bread, prosciutto, and mozzarella. The caprese was a perfect summer appetizer with the tomatoes and mozzarella, very light and cool during a heat wave. For our entrees, we ordered the spicy rigatoni vodka and the tortellini al ragu - both were AMAZING. The portions were a bit smaller than expected, but we were still extremely happy with our lunch. We also ordered the hazelnut cake with vanilla ice cream/gelato as our dessert. I will definitely be coming back the next time I visit!

This review will help you understand why you can not get in and you do not need to waste your time.  

I really do not write reviews anymore but I'm so disgusted but the way they business I can not help myself. 

First of all unless you 
KNOW "someone"
BRIBE "someone" 
Sacrifice your first born child 
Who knows what else...

You are NOT going to get in.  It will not happen!

However, the Notify Me List really does come in handy and has been a success for booking last minute reservations. We encourage you and the guests interested to add yourself to it, and stay on top of those alerts that come in!"

Reservation become "available" 30 days in advance on Resy at 10am I could bet my life this is not true it is a LIE.  I have sat with friends and coworkers hitting refresh over and over to get in and yet not one of us has ever gotten in.  

I emailed over 20 times with plenty of notice even for my birthday... NOTHING 

Scripted responses of "we don't give a shit" 

I'm not Justin Bieber turning me away won't get you any public drama or publicity?! I can not tell what their goal is but it is not customer service or client relations.  

Disgusted by the dishonesty.  

Shame on you

Shame on you 

Shame on you
Best food I've had in my life. Not only the food, but the service and experience as well. The rig is a must try obviously, but everything else on the menu was incredible.

Three stars for annoying fellow diners, and disappointing dishes. 
The spicy rigatoni is really the only thing worth your money. We tried the Cesar salad (more entertaining to watch it being made, than how it tastes. For $28 you are playing for the circus of high pouring dressing, tossing of the lettuce and dramatic overture of cheese sprinkling. 

The meatballs were OK, nothing so flavorful that made them worth the price. The tortellini was good, but the nutmeg overpowered EVERY other ingredient. The fungi pasta was pretty good, but again, no wonderful flavors here. 

Why three stars: the Tik Tok instagram Influencers walk in with flash on, recording every moment they breathe throughout their entire dining experience. Loud, rambunctious, and killing the entire ambiance of the back dining room. I get this place has notoriety (hi deuxmoi) but the management staff should make some attempt at preserving what the restaurant was before it turned into a social media sensation. ADDITIONALLY, we ordered one bottle of acquapanna at the beginning of meal service. The servers kept refilling our glass practically after each sip. They never asked us if we wanted another bottle or transition to tap. I served tables for years, and I know the difference between prestigious service and running the check up with $10 bottles of water. It takes little to no effort to ask a table if they want to continue drinking what they initially ordered, and that was absent. I don't like that at all. 

I've been twice, I doubt I'll ever be back.
If you can get a reservation, it's worth the price of entry.  Some of the best American style Italian food I've ever had.

By far the best dining experience I have ever had, everything was immaculate from the music, to the service, the taste and even the little details including switching the China for each course. I cannot say enough good things about this restaurant! If you're lucky enough to get a reservation, don't skip out on the spicy vodka rigatoni and meatballs!

Phenomenal flavor and quality. I didn't go her per se, but my room mate brought home left overs from a work dinner. I had the pleasure of tasting the lobster squid in ravioli, meatballs, and of course spicy rigatoni. I give carbone one less star due to the fact the ravioli is not home made or at least I don't think it is. The meals are very heavy, so small portions are better. Meatballs flavorful and huge, the red sauce was delicious. The real star was the lobster ravs. Wow just wow. Stuffed with real lobster, and a cream sauce. I'm looking forward to going here and trying it fresh. Definitely a great spot for expensive pasta and ambiance

This place is one that 1000000% lives up to the hype (and this is coming from a food snob). The bread is phenomenal, the atmosphere, the wine, the service, the food, everything is done perfectly right.

We of course had the spicy vodka rigatoni, the veal Parmesan, corn, caprese salad, and octopus. 

Worth the hassle for the reservation!

If you can manage to get a reservation at what is notoriously one of the hardest place to get a decent reservation in NYC, then you'll be in for a treat!

Reservations are opened up a month in advance on Resy at 10am. Reservations are filled up within seconds of release, so best to be tenacious when making that res! 

I came here with a party of 4 on a Wednesday evening. It was very busy and lively despite it being a weeknight. We were seated outside in the Amex patio, which was an enclosed space and more comfortable in personal space compared to the seating inside the restaurant.

The decor is very rustic and it's a nice touch. The service was very attentive, much of what's expected of a Michelin star restaurant. Our server was detailed and gave us good recommendations.

For dinner we ordered:
Baked Clam Casino
Spicy Rigatoni (x2)
Tortellini Al Ragu
Scallops 
Veal Parmigiana

The bread they give as sampler were fresh and still warm when they come out. They are surprisingly very good and they are also given with an olive oil dip and parmesan pieces.
The baked clams were really good. It comes in three different styles: spicy breadcrumbs, uni, and spicy bacon and peppers. Highly recommend this dish! 
Tortellini Al Ragu was good texture and the ragu sauce was on point and flavorful!
The main star of the show is the spicy rigatoni pasta! If it's anything, you must order this! The spicy rigatoni is their signature dish and it lives up to its hype. It's a perfect blend of spicy and creamy sauce with perfectly cooked al dente rigatoni. One may describe the taste as harmonious and steady!
The veal parmigiana is also another popular dish. I wasn't particularly wow'd by it, but I did like it. 
The scallop dish was replaced by their sea bass selection during the dinner. It was well seared and tasted great! At the very end they gave complimentary rainbow cookies, which was rich in flavor. 

Overall experience it was great. Quality of food was above standards. The price of the food is steep but it's more so for the experience!

I was really excited to finally get a reservation at Carbone, but ultimately I am not sure they are worth the hype (or the 11pm late night reservation I was able to secure).

The spicy rigatoni lived up to its reputation, but everything else was just good. The cesar salad was yummy, but the croutons were really what made it stand out from others I've had. The baked clams were also just alright. The linguini vongole was actually not very good at all and I wouldn't order again.

Overall I had a nice time and was excited to try one of the more exclusive restaurants in NYC, but don't see myself making much of an effort to return anytime soon.

Amazing experience and food. The staff was incredibly welcoming and explained the menu in detail, which was so helpful. It also reminded me that typical Italian meals consist of several courses. The appetizer, salad, pasta, entree, dessert. We decided to go with a smaller option of an appetizer, pasta dish, and dessert. Everything was cooked to perfection. The appetizer and dessert were good, but the pasta was spectacular. I had the spicy vodka rigatoni and my partner had the spaghetti puttanesca. I wished I lived closer so I could order the pasta more often. The bread was 
a great treat too! Fresh from the oven and three types. We were both full by the end and there was no possible way we could have eaten the entree course. The food and staff at this restaurant is amazing and worth going to enjoy the atmosphere and food.
Have gone to two of the carbone locations. The original one and the one at sadelles. Both times were for birthday celebrations. Food and service is Awesome and delicious.

There's not much to add to the consensus on Carbone. The rigatoni is fantastic -- silky sauce, al dente pasta, a light hit of heat. The complimentary first course was also really well done. The garlic bread packed incredible flavour into a crispy, chewy slice; and the mozzarella was so fresh, with a rich creaminess and a balance of bouncy and soft textures.

The Caesar salad would have been unremarkable except for the croutons, which were another textural marvel. These guys are good at toast. I'm glad I got the meatball, but I'm not sure I'd get it again. The carrot cake was inventive, but there was lots of dried fruit, which isn't my preference.

I had a 2PM reservation and did not need dinner. All in all, it was worth the fuss and money -- at least for the classics at Carbone. I want to go again.

We dined at Carbone for dinner this past weekend. Our expectations were high because of all the amazing things we have heard about it - and how hard it is to get a reservation! 

We started with the calamari which was wonderful and tasty. It wasn't chewy and had great flavor. 
We wanted the caprese, but the chef was not offering it that night. I requested to just have some mozzarella sent to the table. It was phenomenal. I have heard things about the mozzarella, and our friend said we must try it. I am glad we did. I am a sucker for Italian food that tastes authentic - and this place does. My entree was the tortellini and I finished the entire plate. The ragu sauce was perfection- along with the cheese stuffing in the tortellini. My boyfriend got the spicy rigatoni. He was not as impressed with the spicy rigatoni, but did still enjoy it.

Overall, it was a wonderful meal & I would recommend trying it out. We felt the prices were on point with the service, location, and flavors.

Extremely overhyped. It's good food, but crazy hard to get a reservation and also crazy expensive. The spicy rigatoni vodka was good, but needed something in it other than just pasta and sauce. The meatballs were a little undercooked, and the tortellini was pretty one note.

For how difficult it was to reserve, and how expensive it was, I wouldn't go back.

I LOVE THIS PLACE! This is an overdue review from my visit in May. My friend was lucky to snag us a late dinner reservation at 9:30 on mother's day. 

They started us off with some complimentary garlic bread, prosciutto, and mozzarella. The bread was warm, soft, and flavorful. It's the best complimentary bread I've ever got at a restaurant. The waitress was soo nice and gave us all her recommendations and even stopped us from ordering too much food. Since we were sharing the spicy rigatoni, they brought it out in smaller plates which I thought was very nice. As we were waiting for our food, we saw Cardi B and Offset walking in for their dinner.

We ordered:
Baked Clams 
Caesar salad
Spicy Rigatoni 
Lobster Ravioli
Carrot Cake 

Everything was SOOO good, there were no misses and I would definitely order everything again. I didn't try the carrot cake because I was too full but my friends said it was very good!

I can't wait to come back, this is my favorite Italian place!!

Scheduled this lunch at least a month in advance and truly lived up to the hype. I don't need to tell you that their spicy vodka rigatoni was possibly the best pasta I've ever had, but I will!
To start: Caesar salad was fantastic. Probably 8/10. Freshly made by the table but felt like something was  missing. They also have house bread, mozzarella and thin meat.
Entree: spicy vodka rigatoni, tortellini, and Mario's meatballs. All delicious but the rigatoni def had the spotlight. 
Dessert: berries and cream type dessert, and tiramisu. Tiramisu was delicious. Had a little bit of an almond taste so little different but great. The berries and create were so simple but delicious as well.
in my opinion worth the hype!! the baked clams and spicy rigatoni vodka are excellent!!

Came for lunch after finally getting a reservation ! We started if with the baked clams trio (which was very nice), then we got the carpaccio which I liked but I felt was a bit salty, and my favorite out of the appetizers was the Tuna it was very good, and fresh , but the flavors were just wow. For dinner, I got the pasta with vongole, and it was a bit spicy that my eye started tearing up, but the flavors were very good, my spouse got the pasta with funghi, it was nice and flavorful, my second favorite part of the night was dessert, I got the chocolate cake with prailines and nocciola and salted caramel ice cream.. all in all, which was very good not too sweet. Oh, and my waitress was such a sweetheart, which made the experience so much better!! I really wanted to take her home so we could become great friends :)

How this restaurant isn't 5 stars on Yelp is absolutely beyond me but it deserves every single star in the world.  The service alone is unmatched and unparalleled. I've been here with friends and by myself and they treat me like I'm famous (I'm very much NOT famous).  

Most recently, I came here by myself. They sat me an hour and a half before my reservation, and treated me like I was the most famous person in the place.  The food is simply divine, of course.  What really wowed me though, was the service.  What I was expecting was a quiet dinner on my own, people watching and keeping to myself as I ate my plate of rigatoni.  Instead, I found the entire experience anything but lonely. Not that they hover or are overbearing in any way. But they could see I was alone, and really made an effort to be so kind-- that effort went a long way with me.  Everyone around me was of course with someone but they treated me no different.  

I arrived embarrassed to be by myself. I'm leaving here tonight having had one of the best dinners I've ever had and solo. Thank you all for such a great dinner and dining experience.  This is why it's my favorite restaurant in the city and yes, the world.

Also HUGE shoutout to Mark, my waiter.  He deserves a raise, for his phone to always be charged and for everything good in this world. He was the best!

I am SO disappointed. I expected top quality italian food from carbone seeing as its popular amongst celebrities and very difficult to get a reservation at. We finally got a res and it was 10:30pm. They took a half hour to seat us, and then their kitchen took FOREVER. We didn't finish our meal until 1AM. And the food was atrocious. I did not enjoy it. The Linguini Vongole was deff made in salt water because it was SO SALTY. And the other pastas were tasteless imo. The Espresso martinis were the highlight of the night. The apps were average. I do not get the hype and it is not even worth the trip there for the clout.

I heard so many amazing things about this place so I searched far and wide for a reservation (& managed to snag one thanks to Resy priority notify). & of course, I came in with sky high expectations. The service here is excellent; the workers are very polite and personable! We ordered the spicy vodka rigatoni (of course) and the tortellini al ragu, to our waiter's dismay -- he recommended we try a dish from each menu section but we were just feeling pasta for our meal. The rigatoni was delicious, but not life changing (especially given the price). The tortellini was very tasty but the portion was teeny tiny :) However I have to say Carbone has the best complimentary bread I have ever tried -- cheesy garlic bread with warm mozzarella and salami. Each bite was glorious!!

Honestly it was okay. Made reservations a month in advance and was excited but it's literally your average Italian restaurant food quality wise. They try to make your dining experience classy with the dim ambiance & old timey music but it's nothing WOW inside. The baked clams were really good & so was the lobster ravioli. We also got the famous spicy rigatoni and was so disappointed. Aside from how small the portion was, it wasn't spicy at all and more on the tomato sweet side? It was bland tasting I couldn't believe people hyped this up. The bill was $250 after tip for 2 people because we also got drinks but I don't think I'd come back again.

Look... I wanted to love Carbone. Carbone has the charm: it's extremely exclusive, making the reservation one of the hardest to get, it's known for its signature rigatoni, and is often a celebrity hot spot. It's like the restaurant reservation that's a golden ticket since it's nearly impossible to get one if you don't know someone. I was so excited to learn we had landed a reservation for their last seating at 11:30pm. When we arrived, the ambiance was dim, paired with some Sinatra in the background and a full room of guests. To start, they brought out their fresh bread, mozzarella, soppressata and pickled cauliflower. We opted to have their mozzarella with peppers, and it was probably one of the best things we had that night. Their complimentary starters were okay, so we were pretty excited to see how the rest of the meal would be. For our appetizers we got the assorted baked clams, which were just alright. We ordered by suggestion a Cab and a Chianti for our table, which both were solid. Moving on to our mains, we ordered their off-the-menu meatballs, their grilled branzino, 2 orders of the spicy rigatoni, and (not pictured) their fettuccine con funghi. It was the moment of truth about their spicy rigatoni and it was not good. I thought it totally lacked flavor and to denote something as "spicy" and it doesn't even taste like it has a smidge of pepper is "interesting". next, the meatballs were okay, and the sauce was a nice classic marinara. The branzino was alright, they accompany it with three sauces and only two of them were okay. Lastly, the funghi pasta is why I think they should be rated 2 stars. It was quite frankly terrible. For dessert, they gave complimentary rainbow cookies, and we ordered their carrot cake. Overall, I have mixed feelings about my experience. I don't think the service was that good, the food was meh, and the ambiance way just okay. I think coming here I came with huge expectations, so maybe I even ruined the meal for myself. However, I wouldn't say I would never try it again. I could have came on an off night and I am merely rating this off of my first experience. I hope to try it maybe one more time, but after this visit I was left slight disappointed.
Not worth the hype but overall a good experience. My ribs were served cold. The bartender wasn't the friendliest but a spot at the bar while waiting for our table was nice. Probably won't return

Solid restaurant with great service. The food itself was good Italian, but you definitely go there for the vibes and service. Definitely a restaurant where you share and do family style. We tried all the regulars that people recommend. However, not even gonna lie one of my favorites for the meal was the strawberries with mascarpone. It was the perfect way to finish the meal.

The food is good & flavorful but the portions are very small. We enjoyed the bake clams, spicy rigatoni, and lobster ravioli but after spending about $100 each we didn't feel completely satisfied or full. The food is tasty & the service is great but definitely not worth the hype and definitely not worth having to book a month in advance.
I love carbone the spicy uffff the best I f the next and the service I'm in love with the Bread

I am going to rate this place in parts. It will be more clear as to why I go three once you read it. 

1. Ambiance- cool place. A little tight but service and crowd are a 5 star
2. Bread, cheese and gardenia- 4.5 . Cheese is delicious. I just wish they gave me more .
3. Caesar- small portion. Too much dressing. 20 bucks- 3
4. Spicy rigatoni- expensive but still a 4.5. Pasta is perfectly done and delicious . 
5. Meatballs- very firm and filling. Not the best meatball though. 3. I could name several meatballs that are better . Dibruno in Philly for example has a better meatball. It is not in my top 10 of meatballs.

6. Veal chop cutlet- I would rate it fair, but not great . For 60 bucks I thought it would be fantastic. It was good but nothing about it blew me away. 3.5.I would not go back for the parm. I have eaten better parm for sure . 
7. Brocolli rabe- it was fine. More on the bitter side. Nothing to get excited over . 

8. Dessert was a 4 . Chocolate praline cake. Pretty good .

Walked in for lunch at 12 on a Thursday for 2 without a res and got seated right away. All I can say really is it lives up to the hype. Service was good and our server recommended we get one dish from every part of the menu (app, pasta, entree, side). We opted for just 2 pastas since we weren't too hungry, and that was the perfect amount for us. 

They serve you complimentary garlic bread, mozzarella, and salami, and the mozzarella with bread was so good. Definitely made us excited for the rest of the meal

Spicy rigatoni - the creamy sauce coats the pasta so well, perfect amount of spice, there isnt an overwhelming amount of cheese. Al dente was just right and every bite leaves you wanting more. You want to savor each piece instead of devouring multiple at a time.

Linguini with clams - not as impressive as the rigatoni but still really good. The wine flavor shines through and they give you a lot of clam.

What a nasty restaurant! My son was taking his girlfriend there for her birthday they were all dressed up he couldn't get a reservation so he bought one online. There's nothing anywhere on Carbone's website or any place else it says you can't buy a reservation. They got there and you wouldn't let them in they were tons of restaurants to go in New York avoid these assholes no food is worth ruining someone's 25th birthday

Spicy Rigatoni Vodka and Tortellini Ragu... wow! so good! 

also the complimentary apps - the garlic bread, salami and mozzarella are beyond good too. My boyfriend also loved everything. I did notice both pastas increased in price by a dollar as opposed to the prices on some of the menus on yelp but it's nbd. 

Would love to come back here again and bring some friends  Let's see if I can get another ressie

There is a lot of talk about this place about how hard it is to get reservations - they are always gone within seconds of release. I got "lucky" that I was able to legitimately (going on Resy and actually booking it by hand without any code) score reservations with just 2 tries, the 2nd try being for Saturday indoor dining (not Amex patio even though I am an Amex cardholder, since indoor is a lot nicer and spacious). So it is doable legitimately, just need to be fast!

In terms of being overrated, I would disagree. Yes, the hype is crazy, but the dining experience matches the quality. To start, they gave us a nicely designed menu and equally pretty plates to start, as well as some garlic bread, burrata infused with olive oil, and salami. I particularly liked the burrata as it has a nice subtle creaminess, more so than a lot of the burratas I have tried, and it is simple. Then, we ordered the following to share:

We each got our own cocktails. I got the classic negroni which was made super well. They have the alcohol ratios correct. My friend got the Jack Rose which is more sweet.

Tuna Calabrese (not on menu) - tuna sashimi with eggplant and puree - the tuna is prepared very well: no tendons, very soft / almost melt in your mouth texture. The eggplant is nicely diced and did not have too strong of a flavor. You can taste the freshness of the tuna amongst the other ingredients as the other ingredients are very mild in flavor and only help enhance the overall dish. I am not an eggplant fan but this was still a great appetizer.

Bass Alison - the fish was very tender. However, it still had a slight fishiness taste but it seems like the focus is more on the main ingredient than the other supplementals. There are still some lemon and potatoes that complement the dish.

Veal Parmesan - seems like this is the dish that people order for the entree. The veal is quite juicy and there is a lot of cheese and tomato sauce, yet it is still quite crunchy overall. However, it was a bit unevenly salted so that could be something they could improve on, given that this was quite pricey, at $89.

Spicy Rigatoni Vodka - the dish that almost everyone orders for the pasta and possibly why this place is very popular. The sauce is quite rich, and the pasta is cooked absolutely perfectly. A lot of Italian restaurants just do not have the cooking time right - it is either slightly undercooked or a bit too soft. This pasta is very chewy. It is on the smaller portion and seems plain for $34, but at least they do it super well.

Service is overall phenomenal. Water refills are frequent and they check up on you periodically but not overbearing. They do the usual fancy dinner stuff like clearing out breadcrumbs and replacing dishes and utensils as they course each meal. Waiter was overall friendly. Price is on par for a Michelin star restaurant and we did order a lot. We ended up spending close to $320 total for 2 people after tax and tip. The reason this is 4 stars and not 5 stars are 2 things: they forgot the mushrooms order when the waiter commented this is a lot and made sure we are able to finish it (that's fine since the bill is lower haha) and the fact that the veal parmesan is unevenly salted.

Each time I come here I leave more unimpressed. My friends were dying to come here and try the average Rigatoni D, which you could make better at home. Over food was a 2.5 out of 5 and service was a 0. Once they realized we don't drink or eat pork, our service just disappeared. All the tables around us got their food quickly, table side fresh parm and we were treated like the garbage on the street. 

I'm not sure why the hype, guess you must need to consume a lot of alcohol to think the food is good or  to get better service.

This is def the last time I humor an out of town guest!

The food here honestly exceeded my expectations.  Usually with very hyped up restaurants, I get too skeptical to try but Carbone def lives up to its hype.  

My friend and I ordered the assorted baked clams, meatballs, lobster ravioli, and the spicy rigatoni vodka.  I would recommend all the dishes except for the meatballs, as we both thought it was too salty.  The baked clams were seasoned in 3 different ways which I felt like was interested, and the pasta were both creamy yet flavorful.  Would def come back, and although it can be pricy I would recommend everyone to try it at least once when they come to NYC. 

The service here I felt like was average but I do think the food makes up for it.

Honestly for many years  I wanted to try this place and now I can say that I have. It was overrated. Spicy rigatoni is what they are known for and their copy cat recipes online taste better than the real thing. Caesar salad with anchovies was good but drenched in Parmesan. Highlight of the meal were the assorted clams, casino and Oreganata as well as another variation. Ribeye was very rich in flavor. The shrimp scampi (yes shrimp-singular) was good but it's just one giant piece of Madagascar shrimp, solo / not accompanied by anything. Overall, it's a swanky dimly lit establishment but I think it's a place to try and check off your bucket list, not to be kept in rotation.

We got there 2 minutes after our grace period which is understandable, but really two minutes and you won't let a party of 8 in. I'm sorry but from a business standpoint, when you have a party of 8 coming in which they allowed at 11:30 pm which is already late for a dinner reservation and then turn us down at 11:47? We didn't want to go to dinner at 11:30 and even asked if that wasn't too late because it showed they closed at 11:30, and they said they would accommodate to the time with no worries. May I add we're coming from San Diego, so it's no short flight nor trip. Very disappointing.

Service was impeccable.  The decor was classy and sophisticated.  I arrived late for my dinner party so I didn't get to try the appetizers or bread. I really enjoyed the zucchini and Cesar salad. The Spicy Rigatoni Vodka was amazing. I had it topped with a large super soft meatball. The broccoli Rabe was good, but spicy. The squash agrodolce was the best, tied with the rigatoni and I'm not normally a fan of acorn squash. The steak was good, but fish was better.  I wasn't a fan of the carrot cake as I thought it was dry, however, my table mate liked it. I really liked the chocolate hazelnut cake. Nice for a special occasion or if in the area.
Definitely over priced and over rated.  I've certainly had better Italian elsewhere at a lesser cost
Good restaurant would recommend it is a very family friendly restaurant family Italian food

Food 10/10
So I came in with negative expectations because I've heard so many mixed reviews about this place, saying it was overpriced and overhyped. As a result, I had super low expectations, and I was ABSOLUTELY BLOWN AWAY. Our reservation was for 2pm on a Saturday, and even though the kitchen was closing, they were generous to have us seated and we were served complimentary mozzarella and salami, so already a great start. The Aperol spritz was delicious and magnified each dish. 

For an appetizer, we ordered the Carpaccio Piemontese-super tender beef tartare layered with crunch and flavor. We then ordered the FAMED spicy rigatoni, lobster ravioli, and linguine vongole, as well as the veal parmesan. All of the dishes were perfectly al-dente and the flavors seeped so deeply into the pasta. All were incredibly unique, creamy, and fresh. I especially liked the rigatoni (yes very basic), but they did do an incredible job. The lobster ravioli was also very special, as it came out in the shape of black dumplings. Didn't enjoy the veal parmesan as much, but the fatty meat on the bone was delicious. We were so full at this point, but couldn't resist dessert, so we got the tiramisu and carrot cake. I am a huge fan of carrot cake, and this one might be one of my favorites. SUPER MOIST and BEAUTIFULLY PRESENTED, it paired really well with the ginger ice cream. The tiramisu was also amazing.

Atmosphere 10/10
Love the interior design, cute lighting and bar setup, blue walls were super vibey.

Service 8/10
Solid service, would love to come back if I get the chance!
This place is all fluff. They pretend all their tables are taken. As per my friends experience there are other places in the city that are way better.

I'm not a big fan of Italian food, so my opinion is probably not worth much. This place wasn't bad, but I'm not hankering to come back. Apparently it's hard to get reservations so when my brother got a lunch one, I went with him to check it out.

We had the clam appetizer, artichoke hearts side, veal parmesan, and spicy rigatoni. There was also some mozz and cured meat and garlic bread served for the table. My favorite was the mozz and the clams. This was some of the best soft cheese, marinated in olive olive oil and a perfect texture and light taste. The clams were also excellent. They came in three different preparations and each was done really well. I liked the bread crumbs one the best. The clams themselves were substantial too, and I always (half) joke with him that we have superior seafood on the west coast, but had to admit these were tasty.

The veal parmesan was okay. I liked the light crisp of the outside and the brightness of the sauce, but overall it was too salty. I was cool to just have one cut, though it was pretty big portion. Artichoke hearts were also okay. I wanted something a little lighter to offset the other stuff we got so asked the server for a recommendation on sides. I asked if there was something interesting and these were. They had chili flakes and a sauce, maybe anchovy? Not great, but interesting to try and did make the meal feel a little lighter.

Spicy rigatoni was tasty too, a creamy sauce with firm but chewy pasta. No complaints there, despite not being a pasta person. Also a decent sized portion. We had leftovers.

Service was good but it did take awhile in some parts just because it was so busy. We were seated by the kitchen so it was kind of noisy. Not a big deal, but noticeable. Fine meal overall.

Carbone gets a lot of talk, so I decided to go in with absolutely zero expectations. Somehow my boyfriend's sister managed to get a res for 2 and very very graciously offered it to the two of us, so we figured why not. 

Let me say, I do like it and I do get why people like it so much. We were immediately sat in the gorgeous and dim space and given the magnificently large menus -- I loved it. I felt very  dignified with it in my hands. Then comes the complimentary goodies: loads of bread, giardiniera, and salami. The free stuff is definitely the best part, hands down. We snacked a lot as we waited for our eggplant & zucchini scapece, spicy rigatoni vodka, and broccoli rabe. The eggplant & zucchini was light and easy to eat. I would pass on the broccoli rabe next time. And then unfortunately, it took a really long while for the spicy rigatoni to get to our table. The adjacent table seated after us got their two orders of the past before we did. Thankfully we asked where our order was at and then it immediately got to to us. And man, I was slightly peeved about the wait, but the pasta was perfectly cooked, the sauce was complex and tangy. It was so good. Ended the night with the rainbow cookies "made with love." 

Lovely date spot if you get the chance. Again, the free stuff is great!

Carbone is one of the best restaurants in nyc.  I promise u this place worth of ur every penny. 
We are here for a thanksgiving dinner where everything is prefixed. 
Starting with the bread, they offered threee kinds of bread n each one is uniquely good. 
Salad n tuna is also delicious. 
We are astonished by how creative they had done in their pasta sauce. 
The most surprising meal is the turkey dish. I have not eaten any turkey as juicy as it is here. I felt like I am now a fan of turkey meat now. 
Dessert is also great. Pecan pie n cheese cake are great. 
Overall, I highly recommend this place. If I could, I wish I could be here having dinner everyday. Finger cross that we can reserve this place soon!
Lipstick on a pig, tourist trap. The escorts that work the front door seemed like they could be real nice and fun.

This is one of those places where you doubt the experience will live up to the reputation. I'm here to confirm it does. The ambiance is sexy, with dark interiors, a small bar in the back, and small quarters. The service was excellent and they were kind enough to split our food in the back so we didn't have to do it at the table. We tried the famous spicy rigatoni and I was shocked at how spicy it was (and I'm Indian!), Highly recommend because it really is different from other restaurants. We also tried the eggplant starter, chicken main, and tiramisu. Everything was good but the pasta and the tiramisu really stood out. They're kind enough to provide bread with some small bites so be prepared to leave full.

Got a very unique experience with carbone. Instead of eating at the flagship location they gave us one of their other spots. Beautiful old school nyc interior, candles all over very cool art on the walls & from what they said its a breakfast place. But that night they catered our dinner. 

Great service. I never talk about service or the inside of a place but this place was worth it just for the look & service. Ok lets get to the impt stuff.

Passed hors d'oeuvres meatballs were fantastic, truffle, rice, balls were awesome & beef tartare was perfect.

On the table we had meat balls & spicy vodka sauce, very tasty & cooked perfect. The rib eye & ch scarpiello were full of flavor.  This was the first time at a carbone location it it didnt disappoint. Great job my the chef, manager & servers. 

Imo this location should be a restaurant, its way too beautiful inside to be a breakfast place. Great job!

Just really good Italian food with excellent service and ambiance. We had the spicy rigatoni, tortellini, and the veal Parmesan. All delicious. The veal I was particularly impressed with. But the bread served in the beginning and the house made mozzarella cheese were also very good. We got the carrot cake for dessert and that was great as well. Not disappointed at all from all the hype after our meal. Hope to come back sooner than later!

This place was quite the experience, but in my opinion the food is quite overrated. We went as a large group of 8 and shared several of their dishes to try a variety. 

In terms of the experience, the vibe of the restaurant is really nice. It's a small location so they can't accommodate many tables, but that makes it feel more intimate and unique of an experience. However, as friendly as our waiter was, he kept trying to rewrite our order, insisting we needed to order more portions of each item and not even telling us for the meatballs that he wrote down 2 portions. We ended up having a lot of leftovers, and I wish he would have let us just order the amount we knew we needed. 

Aside from that, we loved certain details of the service, from the amazing starter bread that's provided to the slicing of this big wheel of Parmesan on the table for us. 

Since we shared all the dishes, here are my thoughts: 
 Spicy rigatoni - we were eager to try it and had high expectations because of this dish's reputations, but it ultimately disappointed us. The sauce didn't really feel thattt different from other restaurants and the pasta was pretty regular. 

Meatballs - also similar, they were tasty and the sauce they came in was also fresh and flavorful, but nothing extraordinary 

Veal parm - I really enjoyed this dish! The veal was well cooked and the "slice" was nice and cheesy and packed with flavor from the sauce 

Orecchiette- yummy pasta cooked Al dente but reallyyy salty for some reason. I liked the pesto meat sauce it came with, but could not get over the salt 

Tortellini al ragu - my favorite dish! The tortellini tasted fresh and the filling was light and creamy. The red sauce complimented tn tortellini perfectly. 

Carrot cake - really dry. It looked really aesthetic, but I honestly didn't want to eat more of it after the first bite, and I usually love carrot cake 

Lemon cheesecake - the better of the two deserts, but not lemony or flavorful enough in my opinion! 

So overall, there were dishes I enjoyed, but several did not meet our expectations. May not be worth the price and the effort it takes to make a reservation.
A place that does not answer phones !???? Come on now. You can't leave a message! No place is this good. No way to communicate.

Very good! But not worth the hype. The atmosphere is fun, service is EXCELLENT. The salad is good, croutons are probably a highlight of the meal. The meatballs have good flavor, the sauce is a bit bland. The spicy rigatoni vodka is delicious. My favorite dish was the tortellini, the  fresh sauce balances perfectly with the hearty pasta. The little cookies are amazing, but can found other places. Overall very much worth checking out, but probably won't go back.

Had lunch at Carbone on Saturday afternoon. It is impressive how despite the numerous accolades and expansions, they still can put out such a consistent and delicious experience.

Quality: The hype is real at this Italian joint, it is near impossible not to love. We stuck with all of their signature dishes, and I wouldn't change a thing. The Prosciutto & Mozzarella is a lovely way to start, three different types of meat and more of their incredible cheese. Mario's Meatballs are simple and delicious. The Spicy Rigatoni Vodka is iconic for a reason, the sauce is unbelievable. The Veal Parmesan is an impressive size, and incredibly well cooked. The meat is tender with the perfect proportions of sauce, cheese, and breading. The Broccoli Rabe was a nice infusion of greens, though would be the first item to go if you are worried it is too much.
Quantity: Large dishes, made to share.
Value: $20 for Cocktails. $29 for the Prosciutto & Mozzarella. $27 for Mario's Meatballs. $34 for the Spicy Rigatoni Vodka. $89 for the Veal Parmesan. $19 for the Broccoli Rabe.
Ambiance: Carbone has the old-school charm of a classic New York Italian restaurant. It is located in Greenwich, with the iconic neon sign outside. They have one of the most elaborate outdoor dining set-ups I have seen, it looks almost as impressive as inside. The inside space is not particularly big, with two main rooms. Each room feels snug, with lots of small touches to take you back in time. Traditional pop and Italian crooners songs filled the space throughout.
Crowd: Reservations are extremely hard to secure. Unless you have an in, you may want to look at odd times and weekdays.
Service: Very friendly and they have the pacing down to a science.
Parking: Limited street parking as the street has been taken over by outdoor dining spaces.
Such a great experience and wait staff was super accommodating. Food was great and definitely recommend a night out in the village.

I'm not sure what all the hype is about! I ordered the Spicy Rigatoni Vodka and it was good, but not great. It felt pretty basic in my opinion. It was really flavorful, but I felt as if the pasta was too hard. It was nice because the service comes with garlic bread, salami, and mozzeralla, but overall, I would not come back. Their old fashioneds tasted cheap, and the tables are SO close together, you can't even get out without pushing the table out. The restaurant also had a weird smell inside and I felt as if staff were a bit rude to me and my date. They ALSO charged us $10 each for sparking water and then proceeded to dilute it with still water...LOL would not recommend ):

Carbone did live up to the hype but I wouldn't necessarily return back- it was definitely a one and done type of thing for me personally.  My friend and I got Mario's Meatballs, Spicy Rigatoni Vodka, and Fettuccine con Funghi.  Surprisingly my favorite was not the spicy rigatoni vodka everyone raves about but was Mario's Meatballs instead- the meatballs were cooked perfectly and that red sauce...*chef's kiss.*. The fettuccine was great too but had a little too much olive oil for my liking (yes olive oil is fantastic but I don't want my pasta drowning in it).  The cake was fantastic but I am a sucker for Italian sweets (I mean, who isn't)?  All in all, I would definitely return back but I wouldn't go out of my way for it ie actively seeking a reservation as I had before.

After hearing about Carbone losing a Michelin star, I still would come back to this restaurant! I will begin this review by answering some of the common questions. How do you reserve a table? How far in advance can you make reservations? Are walk-ins available to dine? First I will begin by saying, BE PREPARED and BE FAST when booking a reservation through the Resy app. You must book your reservation prior to your ideal dining date. Be open to a few days as booking a reservation is very difficult. Also, be open to booking a different time as most likely you will be competing with every other foodie trying to dine at the restaurant. 

As for the aesthetics, Carbone is a very small and intimate Italian restaurant. Ambience can be slightly loud and the restaurant itself is well decorated. You are greeted at the front by a host who will check for your name and reservation time. We were seated right away. 

Now for the food review, we came in hungry and like many others searched for recommendations through Yelp, YouTube, blogs etc. After our research, we knew we had to try their Spicy Vodka Rigatoni. I must admit, it was DELICIOUS and the best rigatoni I have ever tasted so far. We were also given some fresh garlic bread, prosciutto and a warm mozzarella cheese ball to start! We ordered a lobster ravioli and spicy vodka rigatoni to share. Portions were good enough for two people.  IMPORTANT!!! They will tell you that due to the high volume of orders they will kindly ask you to place all orders in your initial order to avoid any long wait times! So if you are a hungry person, order extra just in case! Overall experience, 9.5/10. 

Don't let the news of this restaurant losing a Michelin star deter you from eating here! Go try it out! 

Pros:
- Spicy Vodka Rigatoni was amazing. Noodles cooked perfectly not too chewy or overcooked.
- Great place to dine for a casual or special event.
- Not crazy expensive like other Michel star restaurants

Cons:
- Reservation process is a nightmare, BUT was worth the wait! (I like the thrill of competing for reservations, it's a foodie battle!) 
- Can be very loud
- Not spacious at all but you are there for the food anyways!

I would never spend my money on this place. They messed up my reservation time and refused to seat us. They we're extremely rude and arrogant and did not entice  us to stay. I am extremely disappointed in the service here.
I had a really great time here. Their pasta is goat. Even it' really hard to reserve, I can say it's worth. Staffs are friendly and very professional. Place mood is cozy and classy.

Had a wonderful time with my girlfriends at Carbone for our friend's bachelorette dinner. There was a small confusion about our reservation and the host was sure to fix it right away! So we were pleased with that. Now on to the food.

We started with some crudos and caviar. The crudos (a fish and scallop) were okay but the caviar was so delicious and very memorable. Every pop filled my mouth with happiness. Even our 16 year old guest loved it.

Next up a Caesar salad. These croutons! You won't ever forget them. Airy but crunchy and absolutely delectable.  Dressing tasted homemade and fresh which is what you want in a Caesar. 

For entrees we had the spicy rigatoni (of course), the lobster ravioli, tortellini ragu, ribeye diana and the chicken scarpiello.

Our least favorite was the chicken, we actually ended up sending it back. It just had a weird taste so one star off for that.

Everything else was divine! Pastas cooked to perfection and tasted fresh. Sauces were simple, well prepared and flavorful! The ribeye was cooked just right and the portion was extremely large. We shared everything and was ready to burst by the end of this meal.

Service was a 10/10 and made the experience great. But the food was just meh. We started with fried calamari - too fishy. Mozzarella with peppers - delicious. Got the Caesar in between and it was too fishy as the anchovies were overpowering. Then got the spicy rigatoni - that was of course delicious since they are known for that!!! Lastly we got the veal parm - too chewy and just not good. I would not go out of my way to come back here unless I was craving their pasta!

To get a reservation here, I just left my Resy notifications on for all dates and times I was available and when a reservation popped up, I instantly snatched it. My boyfriend and I loved the ambiance, it felt like a very cozy upscale hole in the wall (but it definitely was not). We ordered the corn appetizer, meatballs, spicy rigatoni and the ragu tortellini. The starting bread was good, I liked the variety, but the spicy rigatoni pasta tasted very underwhelming. It felt like something I could easily make at home, the corn was fresh but also not unique. The meatballs were our favorite dish and it complimented the pasta quite well. But for the price point and difficulty to get a reservation, I think this spot is too overhyped.
Food exceeded my expectations!  The service was absolutely phenomenal!  I will definitely be going back.
Spicy rigatoni deserves ALL the hype. Everything else was great too, just not as worth it as the spicy rigatoni.

Came here on a whim. After reading the reviews, we were afraid we wouldn't be able to eat since it sounded like it was reservations only. However when we showed up, we asked for a table for 2 and was seated immediately (only outside tables were available) 

Service: super attentive and kind. He made some great recommendations on what to order

Ambiance: the inside was cozy but we were only inside for to grab a table for 2 and ended up sitting outside with the heaters

Food: baked clams- 9/10, I forgot which one was which but all 3 variations were great. Spicy rigatoni- 9.5/10 (mind you, the picture shows half portion split between the 2 of us) it's a 9.5 because I needed more lol. The sauce was phenomenal. Veal parm was a 8.5/10, we also split that but in the picture is a full portion. It can definitely be split between 3-4 people.

We finally got our reservations through the Resy app with last-minute cancellation notification. Service was great--We were seated right away near the kitchen. Our waiter had a lot of humor and was very nice. We got most of their signature dishes: spicy vodka rigatoni, baked clams, veal parmesan, and a side of artichokes. They also give you complimentary bread with fresh mozzarella and salami. This was actually our favorite! 

For our main entrees, everything was definitely unique but nothing that was worth the hardship of getting reservations here. It is definitely something to try once but I wouldn't give it a second visit.

I got a last minute reservation to Carbone, I was excited! My party ordered the spicy rigatoni, veal parm, 2 glasses of wine, and a lemon cheesecake and the bill was around $250. 

If the server knows you're sharing the pasta, you can ask them to split it into two plates for you. My favorite was the pasta and lemon cheesecake. Veal parm was alright. 

The service is great and decor is beautiful, even inside the outdoor patio. For me, it's one of those places you try once. I'm not a big pasta lover to begin with so I'm okay with going to a $$ Italian restaurant instead, for the price reasons.

Good food - even better service. I just don't think Carbone lives up to the hype/ cost. Spicy rigatoni was fine but the tortalini was much better! Very flavorful and delicate. Carpaccio was also pretty good. Carbone is at least worth a visit.

Carbone is a very small, rustic-looking restaurant with an upscale and (slightly snobby) vibe. It's near impossible to get a reservation without a connection or an American Express platinum card. We got in through a friend who has been there several times, and even then we had to reserve a month in advance. 

The exclusivity definitely makes it more enticing, and the food- while overpriced- is worth the hype. The food truly was incredible from start to finish. The service was impeccable- our waiter was very attentive and passionate about the food he suggested to us, making the experience more fun. He checked in on us often and made sure everything went as smoothly as possible- which it did. 

The food lived up to my expectation. I can understand the hype around this place, although the food is not new or unique in any way (not really sure how Italian food can be unique). It's just very very veryyy good quality and delicious food. However, I do have to admit that if you venture out to Staten Island, you will find similar places with the same quality food for a much more reasonable price (and not as hard to get in to). 

Tip- get the mozzarella & prosciutto instead of the burrata, the meatballs are a must with the spicy rigatoni vodka, veal parm is also great if you like veal, black truffle tortellini was a hidden gem on the specials menu.

stop itttt this place is worth the hype !! 
is it expensive uhhh heck yes lol but it's nice to splurge every once in awhile on yourself! 

i honestly have nothing negative to say except that my wallet hurt LOL but food, service and ambiance were amazing. 

for apps we got the caesar salad and the assorted clams. 
the caesar salad itself was good and i feel like you do have to try it atleast once (i've never had table side salad, i'm sad i couldn't see them make it though it was being made in the other room) but again still good but probably wouldn't order again, just felt like it was a must for my first time (: oh and the complimentary apps omgggg that mozzarella is to DIE for!! i've never had mozz like that. on top of the garlic bread with the spicy sorpesatta bomb bomb bomb the perfect bite !! 

the assorted clams were BOMB!! omgggg i saw mixed reviews where people didn't like it but i normally don't like baked clams and i thought it was sooo goooood. the uni one was the best one for me (: it came in an assortment of  like a regular baked clam, a umami baked clam with uni and then one with like bacon lard or something like that but all was bomb honestly! 

for pastas we did the spicy rigatoni of courseeee and that was met the hype for me honestly. the sauce was so good, creamy, perfect amount of spice, flavorful and perfectly aldente and fresh pasta. it was just amazing. perfect sauce pockets with the choice of pasta. we also got the tortellini with ragu sauce also delicious perfect little clouds of ricotta and a hint of lemon zest just honestly so good. 

for the main course we did the veal and steak. both were so good! honestly the best tasting veal. sometimes i feel like veal has a funny flavor but this once didn't at all. it was cooked to perfection. steak was sus at first cus i normally don't like sauce on my steak but also delicious! such an interesting flavor i feel like i never had, wish i knew what it was but yeah steak was also cooked to perfection and super flavorful. 

dessert oh man lol we almost ordered all 4 but we opted out of the carrot cake. we got the ny style lemon cheesecake, the tiramisu and the nutella chocolate cake. my favorite was the cheesecake so decadently thick and creamy and tart all in one bite. bomb. the nutella chocolate cake was the favorite of the table tastes exactly like a ferrero rocher!!! and the tiramisu was so different than any others i've had but that lady finger / madeline on top was the best part lolll i could eat tons of those haha

to add their cocktails are delicious, crafted so well with delicious flavors. 

while the food was amazing honestly what made it was the service. they honestly make u feel at home. normally with nicer establishments you feel as if they're a little pretentious but here not at all they all are so welcoming, make conversation and are relatable. loved our server forgot her name tho  but thank you girl! lolll
Amazing customer service and a wonderful meal. Difficult to get a reservation but always worth it!

.
This was the most mouth watering carrot cake I've ever had. It was presented so beautifully and the structure was unlike something ive seen before I didn't even want to take a bite. The cream cheese frosting was light and the cake was moist. It was paired with a ginger ice cream. The candied walnuts garnished the cake and gave it a nice crunch. ( if you have nut allergies you can opt out of the walnuts) . If you go to @carbonefinefood do not sleep on the carrot cake because you will regret it !!

This place is rad. Food and service is top notch. It is a 10x Italian restaurant vibe. Not a single thing we ate was average. Also had carrot cake and the meal came with bread service. It is pricey but you will enjoy every dollar you spend.
Outstanding Italian food, overall amazing experience but we must go back to try the lasagna. Beet sciliana was great.

My FAVORITE restaurant in life. Yes, fall for the hype. The spicy rigatoni is everything. The baked clams are also a fave & theres 3 assorted clam types in an order. IT IS very difficult to get a reservation on resy but it's worth the stalking. I definitely go every-time I get a reservation no matter the time.

P.S they give you free rainbow cookies for dessert

I had lunch today with another couple. Waited a long time to get a reservation. When we arrived we were greeted by the hostess, who was very rude regarding our arrival time, which was 25 minutes earlier. We were not offered any accommodation, or offered to have a seat while waiting. On the contrary, we walked and stayed outside in the cold while waiting for my time to be seated. We sat all the way in the back of the restaurant, which seem doomed and gloomed. The waiter was extremely rude, pushy, and arrogant. Left the restaurant hungry and smelling like food. Not worth the experience or the extremely expensive price for pasta dinner. Not recommended.

Best Italian food ever!!! It was definitely worth the wait. Everything was incredible and I've had my share of Italian food having been raised in the Bronx. Everything was fantastic from the hot and cold appetizers, the pasta was amazing and I couldn't resist the veal parmigiana. The service was first rate as well, our server was a true professional a true throwback from the good ole' days. His recommendations and attention to detail was top notch. The place has an old world feel about it with a little NY NY thing going while the classics play in the background at just the right level. The atmosphere was just right. I would Highly recommend Carbone to anyone, if you can get in that is.. Can't wait to go again. Keep up the good work Carbone and don't change a thing!

Although I didn't taste an ounce of spice in the signature spicy rigatoni, I would still go back just for the atmosphere and amazing experience. They start you with a mini charcuterie situation and some bread as well. Music was great, we were seated in the outdoor area unfortunately, despite making an indoor reservation. In the end though, we actually preferred our spot because the inside rooms are incredibly loud. Outside was a little more romantic and we could watch the front door for any celebrity sightings lol. I would definitely recommend coming here for a special date night such as an anniversary! We knew a connection who got us in, but I do see some tables pop up on Resy occasionally since I have a platinum Amex

Been here a few times but waking up to try and snatch a reservation a month in advance gets kinda old and tiring. My friends and I usually get the caesar salad and baked variety clams for appetizers and we would share the spicy rigatoni, lobster ravioli and another pasta! The service is always nice and if you're lucky you might even spot some celebrities but everyone is pretty respectful and usually leave them be. The ambiance and bathroom is such a vibe but I def think I can make the spicy rigatoni at home. I think it's a great place to try if you can grab a reservation but there's also plenty of other pasta places in the city if you can't!
The Best Italian Restaurant in NYC. Variedad de platos, postres y las porciones excelente en calidad.
This experience was absolutely worth all of the hype! The lobster dish was impeccable! Our server, Eddie was adorable! The atmosphere was to die for! Absolutely would do it all over again!

After living in New York for ~3 years, I used to avoid Carbone like the plague because everyone used to tell me it was overhyped and underwhelming. However, I picked up a res the day before and decided to eat here with a friend on a whim and let me tell you that I enjoyed this meal as much as I Sodi, Don Angie, and Rezdora (and even more because our server was fantastic). The spicy rigatoni is spicier than you would think and the truffle tortellini was phenomenal. The Caesar salad, which they make in front of you, is a must-get. Drinks are alright.

It lives up to the hype, and this is all you really need to know. Snag a reservation when you can, treat yourself to its classics, don't overthink it, and indulge. And leave room for dessert! I was unexpectedly and utterly blown away by the panettone: it was so spectacularly good that I'm trying to source my own from Italy and figure out how to make a decent orange-infused crème anglaise.

Favorite meal of all time! Loved the whole experience from start to finish!  The service was amazing, the food was amazing, the vibe was amazing!  I don't care what people say Carbone is not overrated!!!

Nonstop talk about Carbone from everyone and finally we were able to get a reservation for ourselves after 2 months. Came with my boyfriend for an 8:30PM dinner, we couldn't sit inside so they sat us in their outdoor seating. To be honest wasn't too happy about it; spending all this money to be seated outside of the restaurant listening to all the cars passing by was disappointing; but we made the best of it.

To start they gave us complimentary breads, salami, cheese, and cauliflower. For our appetizer we got the Prosciutto & Mozzarella. They cut the fresh mozzarella in front of us and plated it; tasted good but nothing so out of this world.

We were sitting so close to another table it was hard to have a conversation without the person next to us hearing everything. Sitting outside the experience felt very rushed and it was very annoying to have to go inside of the restaurant to use the restroom. For our entrée we shared the Veal Parmesan and 2 orders of Spicy Rigatoni Vodka. They decided to combine our pasta orders into one plate instead of giving it to us separate like we ordered. The pasta was very good, but for the price not worth it. Same with the Veal Parmesan thinly fried, good flavor but not worth the price. Maybe they should add a tad more to their portions for the price we are paying.

Of course, people come here for the name, and I was happy I tried it for myself. Would I be back? Yes, sure if someone was paying the bill for me.  Maybe if we were sitting inside, we would've had a different experience. We finished our wine and decided to grab the check and take dessert to go. We got the Tiramisu, also nothing special, tasted a bit dry.

Are you kidding me? I don't care about the hype beast dorks that flock to this place to try and get a glimpse of Melo or Carl Lentz - the food, the Captains, the decor - the feeling that it's possible for Fredo could be bound through the front door and be lit up like a Christmas tree is what makes this place special. TBH the mozzarella at the beginning might by my favorite. The whimsy and delight of cheese being snipped before your eyes is almost too much to handle. 100/10 would recommend.

Incredible service 
Incredible food
Incredible scene 
The veal chop Marsala was pricy but I stopped caring about the price after first bite

I've been trying to get a reservation here for a while and finally scored one for brunch this past weekend. It was everything and more. The service was fantastic. Everyone was super attentive and helpful. The food was very fresh and flavorful. The drinks were strong which is nice especially at their $24 price point. It was freezing outside and the restaurant was a nice cozy reprieve from that. 10/10 recommend and worth the hype.

Is this place worth the hype? The answer is unequivocally yes! Food and service both top tier. The complimentary garlic bread, salami, and mozzarella is delicious, ESPECIALLY the mozzarella. Caesar salad had crisp romaine, the perfect amount of dressing, croutons that were crunchy on the outside and soft on the inside, and a heaping amount of shredded cheese, just the way I like it. Next we got the spicy rigatoni which was delicious, with incredibly creamy sauce with just the right amount of kick. Pork chops were amazing as well. The tortellini Al ragu was surprisingly my favorite dish! Would 100% come back.
If you're lucky enough to get a reservation this is the tastiest Italian food you'll ever have
Spicy rigatoni danced on my tongue like Michael Jackson moonwalking to Billie Jean. Wish I could order chicken too though, but definitely worth a visit (if u can get the reservation!)

I almost hate to say this but Carbone is some of the best tasting food I've had and the tiramisu is to die for!! My Espresso Martini was so delicious and my after dinner Espresso was not bitter at all, it was delish as is. Definitely will return and look forward to it!

Worth it!!!! I took my wife here for her bday dinner. Even though I've been trying to get reservations here since July 2022, finally was able to go here February 2023. The food was amazing especially the Spicy rigatoni. The bread was great. And the atmosphere was great. Waiter was smooth and all our food came out together. Expensive but it's worth it. I would recommend and we have reservations again.

Spicy rigatoni & the starter off bread was really good!! We also ordered ribs (not my favorite) they are very fatty and you really have to dig into those. Alfredo is not that good, I would recommend Olive Garden Alfredo better. Lol. Caesar salad was pretty good too, the croutons are homemade and amazing!! 
Service was okay. Not very outstanding
Just fantastic. From their homemade burrata (are you kidding?!), to the pasta and mushrooms. Yum yum yum all around. Great service too. Looking forward to my next visit.

Pros: all of the staff is incredible and very attentive. They also do not rush you. The vibe is great-- we were fortunate to be seated in the back dining room. The menus are massive which was a funny surprise. They do offer you some complimentary items such as garlic bread, mozzarella, salami, and cookies.

Cons: The spicy rigatoni is overhyped which makes it hard to meet expectations. I recommend trying something different! Also be prepared to pay a minimum price point of $95 if you would like a bottle of wine.

Tip: when booking on resy sometimes it does not release right at 10, keep checking around 10-10:15am and make sure you check at 10am NY time. Also Amex has a priority wait list you can be added to by calling Amex. From there you can turn on resy notifications and get a 15 minute heads up on when a spot opens. Finally if you do not get it the first time, don't be discouraged they do open more spots especially a few days before. Click fast when you get the notification!

I don't understand why this place gets such great reviews. I would bet money that they make reservations super hard to create hype. The interior is very cute and the service was good, but the food is just meh. We got the veal parm ($89) the spicy rigatoni and it was mediocre. I could definitely have replicated the rigatoni at home. Don't believe the hype!

Finally grabbed a reservation for this place and was hesitant from all the hype on social media...but man did it not disappoint! The service was immaculate, and you feel like royalty as your captain explains the menu. Once seated, you're brought salami, garlic bread, and house made fresh mozzarella that is to die for. Honestly, that alone is worth the visit! We tried a few pastas and the Caesar salad made table side, and everything was so fresh and delicious. We were too stuffed for dessert, but were so pleased when they brought out a couple of rainbow cookies for one last sweet treat. The restaurant is small, but once inside you're transported to NYC in the 1940s/50s with classic decor and it feels as if you're right at home. Can't wait to go back and try more!

I tried t make a reservation at Carbone but they were booked. I went on the waitlist. THE DAY OF they emailed that they had a cancellation. I could not take the reservation at that point and did not accept it. THERE IS NO WAY TO PHONE CARBONE OR MAJOR FOOD GROUP!!  I received a NO SHOW charge for $108.88 ($50 per person PLUS TAX) on a credit card I hadn't used in over four years (they must have dug it up in their system somehow). Now I have to fight the charge through my credit card company since there is still no one to talk to and they don't respond to email. WHAT A SCAM!

Carbone was a pleasant experience - cute decor, awesome service, and great Italian food! However, I did feel that the prices were a bit high for what it was and unsure if its worth revisiting since its extremely difficult to make a reservation. I would pass on the veal parm, but the spicy rigatoni was delicious!! perfect al dente texture covered in flavorful, creamy sauce. Make sure to order this!

Pretty overhyped for what it is. It's extremely hard to get in to this restaurant first of all. You need to reserve way in advance.  the spicy rigatoni is good but it's not amazing. They had a special lasagna that wasn't on the menu and I thought that was pretty bad (1/5). It was lacking meat and sauce. My other friends who got the clam linguini had to send their food back. The free bread and mozzarella was spectacular though but I won't be returning.

My favorite Italian. It is such a vibe, the wine is flowing and the scene is everything! Date night, girls night out, business, it's great for anyone. The food is beyond and the energy is strong. We have one in Miami now much closer but this on was my favorite by far. There is no service anywhere like New York City

After all the hype I have heard about this place, me and my girlfriend were finally able to get a reservation. I believe they are released at 10am (EST) every day for about a month in advance? I can't remember the specific parameters around reservations, so take a look online well before your preferred date. We went on a Friday at 12:30pm for a fairly early lunch.

We got quite a bit of food since we've heard so many good things about the place. I will list out everything we got and my thoughts on each item.

Appetizers:
1. Garlic bread, salami, and house-made fresh mozzarella: This was honestly so so good, it may have been my favorite thing that I got here!
2. Caesar Salad: The salad wasn't the best Caesar salad, but it was alright. I did enjoy the large morsel croutons though.
3. Broccoli Rabe: The broccoli rabe was alright. Even with all the garlic on it, it still tasted very bitter.

Main Course:
1. Spicy Rigatoni Vodka: The famous spicy rigatoni vodka. Honestly, I was not impressed. It did not live up to it's hype. If you looked online, you could probably make a better version of this at home. Not worth it, in my opinion.
2. Lobster Ravioli: I am not the biggest fan of seafood in pasta, so I only tried a small bite of my girlfriend's plate. It was okay. She also said the same thing. She enjoys seafood pasta dishes, but she wasn't too satisfied with this one. 

Dessert:
1. Rainbow Cookies: These were complimentary. They weren't too good. They were very dry.  If I'm eating dessert, I want my sweet tooth to be activated, these cookies did not do that for me. 

Overall, I don't think this restaurant is worth the hype. The prices are outrageous and the process of actually getting a reservation is so stressful, that you don't even wanna go. I will say the service is excellent though. We got a bottle of red that was recommended to us by one of the servers and it tasted pretty good, and they even let us try it first. If you're able to secure a reservation, try what you want, not what everyone else is trying.
The food and drinks were incredible. The Veal Parmesan and Spicy Rigatoni were phenomenal! The drinks were delicious! The ambiance was impeccable and the service was top notch.

Wow wow wow. It's worth the hype! We were lucky to get a last minute late reservation through resy. All of the food was SO good. The bread is out of this world. Cesaer salad = amazing! They have an extensive wine list. Spicy vodka rigatoni is a must order. Finished our meal with coffee and a delicious dessert.

Too many years later, still so outstanding. This visit, we got the baked clams, the Caesar salad, burrata with eggplant caponata (special), spicy rigatoni, tortellini, meatballs, and ended with cheesecake. All of it was excellent, with the spicy rigatoni being the biggest automatic re-order no matter how many times we get it here. The burrata was also really amazing, although I'm not sure how often they have it. I'd also gladly get the cheesecake, the Caesar, or the clams again. The tortellini was great but I think we'd probably sub it out next time.

I see why everyone raves about the spicy rigatoni but the pork chop and peppers really stuck out. Rich flavor that would definitely keep me coming back. Apart from that. Really like their wine selection and the waiters recommendations were great. Definitely one of my favorite spots in the city.
Truly the best food experience you will have. Worth the wait and the hype. The service on its own is exceptional. Ambiance is warm and cozy. Order the spicy rigatoni and you will not regret it.

Carbone is the definition of you can still be good and overrated at the same time. I can see why this place is so popular! The food was all delicious, but desert takes the cake! (No pun intended). The service was good, however our "Captain" was a bit dry. The other servers were great, especially Sergio! We started off our meal with their famous meatballs which we were told would pair great with the vodka rigatoni. This combo did not disappoint. The vodka sauce is spectacular, a must have! Meatballs we're good, I liked the marinara it paired with better than the actual meatball. For our entre we had the steak Diana with the grilled asparagus. The asparagus was perfectly cooked. The steak was tasty but a bit chewy even at medium rare. The desert was amazing! The carrot cake with the ginger gelato is a must and the lemon cheesecake was just as good! Honorable mention: their tomato bread. You'll want a second round! Overall 4/5 stars and would definitely return.

I can't believe I'm actually leaving an OK review for Carbone, especially given how hard you have to work to even get a reservation. When we arrived everyone was wonderful, from the doorman to the hosts to the servers. Everyone is absolutely lovely. The space is TIGHT. I know NYC is known for our tiny spaces, but I don't like when you have to move the neighboring table in order to get in and out of the booth side. That's Carbone. :( I recall ordering a bottle of wine, but it felt like the server just kept the glasses topped off the entire time, which had to be more than a bottle....and, trust me, we were not complaining. We started with the rigatoni, which was fine, and I had the salmon, which was also fine. The vibe was chill, with the exception of the drama-filled table near us and that was pure entertainment. So, why only 3 stars? Because given how SERIOUSLY HARD you have to work to obtain a reservation, I would expect food that would make me want to lick the entire plate. Instead the food is fine- nothing spectacular, which it should've been since you have to juggle 20 fire-breathing dragons in order to get in the restaurant in the first place. This is a NYC experience and I would only recommend it for that reason...and if you have 3 months to habitually call daily and try to get a reservation for an upcoming month. Otherwise, it's definitely a skip.

Definitely yum, but definitely overhyped. 

Complimentary bread, salami, and fresh mozzarella was appreciated. Caesar was solid - the croutons were amazing. Spicy rigatoni was unique - more spicy and savory than others I've tried. Lobster ravioli had so much lobster! Meatballs were underwhelming.

Service was amazing. They fold your napkin whenever you get up lol. The ambiance was also great - intimate, cozy, and great oldie music definitely set the mood.

Overall, the food was good but it wasn't the best Italian food I've had. Personally, I am satisfied with trying it just once.

Carbone's vibe literally makes u feel like ur in an old italian movie, pair it with the spicy rigatoni & a glass of wine and u literally could not be happier. Spicy rigatoni is the real reason why most people come here, I have tried parm's rigatoni and i have to say carbone's is so much better and creamier.

A little overrated. Definitely better sports in nyc. Not saying it was bad but it wasn't the best. spicy rigatoni was good not great lacked salt and other seasonings the prosciutto mozzarella was good. one of my favorites on the menu. wine selection is good and has a good ambience. overall good service good food and good ambiance. Other places are better in nyc and carbone is hard to get into. If you can get in go it'll be food and you'll have fun. But again there's definitely better places in nyc.

I was less than impressed this time, staff was great to get us seated ahead of our reservation time. Physical is on the dark side and the seats are small and the tables are cramped together. For the largest guy at our table, he was constantly getting bumped into on the back because of the distance between tables. Service was good generally with plate and utensils switched between courses.

Bread basket was great; the sesame bread and grandma's bread were excellent. The pickled cauliflower in olive oil would've been better had we had a spoon to put the olive oil on our own plates to dip the bread into; forks didn't cut it here.
