We started with appetizers; the special burrata was fantastic, quite possibly the best dish of the night. Oysters filled with too much salt, like ocean water. The calamari was good, though, and the crudo was so-so, nothing stood out there though nothing bad about it. The Caesar salad was interestingly prepared to the side in a bowl used for the mixing purpose, and croutons were good, but the lettuce was bitter. The anchovies were nice on the side, a touch more sour than savory. There was a guy who came around carving a piece of cheese for each person at the table, too, almost like parmesan but much less salty. 

The pasta course was the overall best, the spicy rigatoni was excellent. The $60 truffle ravioli special was good ravioli, the truffle was probably overkill but probably a better enjoyed garnish if you love truffles. The meatballs would have been really good ... But one was severely undercooked. Raw meat at the center was no good for two of the diners at our table; the third meatball was more thoroughly cooked and enjoyed.

Main course had a pork chop, medium rare, which was gristly and fatty. The veal parm was good, but nothing surprising. The giant prawns were ... Large shrimp. Grilled and the head was undercooked, body overcooked (hard not to with the size).

Dessert was started with rainbow cookies, tasty. The carrot cake was an interesting curved piece and decor, plus what seemed like an olive oil ice cream, but the cake itself was dry and tasted not of carrots but flour and baking soda. The tiramisu ladyfinger at the top didn't hold together well but people liked that a lot more than the carrot cake. 

Wine selection good, only one beer, strong cocktails, and they almost thought they didn't have the port for dessert. They did forget to bring my iced tea, though. 

Overall the bread, burrata, calamari, and spicy rigatoni were excellent. The rest of the food, I was disappointed or didn't find much to impress me with. My thought for next time, get a lot more pastas, skip the meat mains, and make sure they cook the meatballs more.

First and foremost, the mozzarella at Carbone is out of this world. It's fresh, creamy, and simply melts in your mouth, and is always a standout dish that never fails to impress.  Paired perfectly with Mario's Meatballs. Moving on to the Beef Carpaccio, it's a must-try dish for any carnivore. The thinly sliced raw beef is served with a drizzle of olive oil, lemon juice, and a sprinkle of capers and parmesan cheese. The result is a beautifully balanced dish that is bursting with flavor and texture. The freshness and quality of the ingredients shine through in every bite.

And last but not least, the Spicy Rigatoni is a dish that I can't get enough of. The rigatoni is cooked perfectly al dente and is smothered in a rich and spicy tomato sauce, which adds a tangy and salty flavor that perfectly complements the heat of the sauce. It's a dish that is sure to leave you feeling warm and satisfied.

Overall, Carbone Italian restaurant in New York is a must-visit spot for anyone looking for an unforgettable Italian dining experience. From the mozzarella to the Beef Carpaccio to the Spicy Rigatoni, the quality of the ingredients and the craftsmanship of the dishes are truly exceptional. The atmosphere is lively and welcoming, although a tad bit crowded. However,  service is top-notch. Unfortunately,  this is a place you cannot just walk into so plan accordingly and bring your AMEX.

Was able to get a reservation to Carbone during Valentine's week and the food definitely lived up to the hype.
We were greeted at the door, escorted our table, and handed these extra large menus by our server. We sat in the main area by the entrance which was narrow and I felt like we were right up against the table next to us, which wasn't the most comfortable. The restaurant is dimly lit and rather casual. 
To start, we were served their infamous complimentary starters - pizza bread, salami, pickled cauliflower and parmesan cheese. 
There were a wide variety of things we wanted to try so we ordered a bit of everything.
Prior to coming to Carbone, I read that their warm mozzarella, which is not on their menu, is not to be missed. We ordered the warm mozzarella and roasted red peppers in oil. This was hands down my favorite part of the meal. The mozzarella arrived in a little bowl immersed in olive oil to which the server used a small pair of scissors to cut into 4 pieces, which were then placed on top of the red peppers. The cheese lover in me was in heaven! The mozzarella, coupled with the roasted peppers, was just perfection - the texture and flavor was all there. If you love cheese, do not miss out on this!
Our next course was the assorted clams casino. There were three different types of baked clams, but my favorite was the one with the uni on top. The uni was so creamy and went so well with the clams. 
Next up were the meatballs in marinara sauce and the spicy rigatoni vodka. The meatballs were so tender and juicy and went so well with the rigatoni. The rigatoni was al dente and the sauce was smooth and rich with a kick of spice. 
By this point, we were already pretttty full. This didn't stop us from diving right into our main courses, which were the double lamb chops and veal marsala. The server sliced the lamb chops for us table-side and the portion was very generous. The lamb was cooked to perfection, flavorful and came with several sauces. The veal was tender and the marsala sauce was very rich. I really enjoyed the garlicky oyster mushrooms on top of it! 
We had a side of potatoes louis which went really well with both the lamb and veal. 
After our main course, the waiter approached with a large tray of cakes, beautifully presented. We couldn't resist the dessert so we ordered the tiramisu. The tiramisu was light and fluffy - a great way to end the meal. The server also brought out two pieces of their complimentary rainbow cookies which were also very good!
Overall, we had a delicious meal, tasty cocktails, great wine and exceptional service. Highly recommend Carbone for a date night if you want to splurge a little and eat a lot.

Carbone lost its Michelin star for a reason. Eating here is not worth it and is very much just hype. 

The reason I gave 2 stars is because the service is good but the food was not worth it in the slightest.

The environment is okay, it's a bit loud with the music and considering it's a higher end restaurant the table cloths are not pressed and we received a chipped plate.

Onto the food: 
Bread Basket had fresh mozzarella and garlic bread 

Baked Clams had 3 different varieties in the one portion of 9 (the best is the one with the sea urchin, another is spicy and not good, and the other is a lemon which is okay.)

Lobster Ravioli came with 5 ravioli and had a lot of lobster but the ravioli itself tasted very fishy and not very creamy. The lobster itself was a bit more chewy because it was over cooked.

Spicy Rigatoni was okay, my sister enjoyed it the most out of everything. I personally have had better and was not impressed.

We also had meatballs also which did not impress me.

The artichoke was unfortunately one of the best things I have there and would recommend.

We also had the chicken which comes with ham , eggplants, and peppers which arguably was one of the better foods that we ate but tasted more like braised beef.

We also had the lobster diablo and were told it was 3 pounds. It definitely was not but also the flavor was not good at all. It tasted it was cooked in a bottle of straight up hot sauce and was terrible. It comes cut up and does not come with the claws.

I can confidently say that the desserts were the only thing I enjoyed. We had rainbow cookies, the lemon cello sorbet, and the tiramisu: I am not a fan of tiramisu but my family who is did not enjoy it either. The sorbet was really good and the cookies were good as well.

Overall, I would not recommend, and would not return to a place that is overhyped.

I'm sure someone you know has been to or has talked about Carbone at least once. The service is phenomenal. Very friendly and attentive staff. I was not sure if I would like the Aperol Spritz and the server said I could order it and if I didn't like it he would bring a different drink for me to try. (I did not end up liking it and he was gracious enough to let me get something else). 

Reservations go very quick so keep that in mind if you don't know already! Prosciutto & Mozzarella to start is always great. The fresh bread + Parmesan cheese should always be considered. Went for the classic Spicy Rigatoni Vodka and was not disappointed.

Very old school classic dining room. Low lighting + candles and classic wood accents with art. Delicious food and have been back since.

Glamorous Italian spot with high-end pastas + meats that are arguably the best in the city but also undoubtedly the most expensive. Tables book fast so reserve in advance and if fortunate enough to get one, order the spicy rigatoni but be ready to spend a small fortune for the experience. $50 a dish. 4.5/5 stars as a dinner spot.

Was excited that I was finally able to make a 2pm reservation after multiple attempts on Resy. If you ask me- if Carbone is worth the hype? I would say, no. There's definitely better italian spots out there, but the service was amazing. They gave us garlic bread, salami and fresh mozzarella to start, which might have been my favorite there. We ordered some of their signature dishes- baked clams (which came with three different kinds), Mario's meatballs, spicy ragatoni vodka and tortellini al ragu. The meatballs were juicy and tender. The ragatoni was cooked al dente. The sauce was smooth and had a slight hint of spice, but in my opinion, definitely did not live up to it's hype. 

One important thing to keep in mind- double check your bill! Since, they charge you $50 plus tax per person as a deposit for making a reservation on Resy, it should be deducted from the bill- which didn't happen in our case and we had to remind them.

Basic food for overpriced prices and hype. Their entire model is based on you can't get a table so psychologically you want a table. Don't fall for it. You can get better Italian food for a fraction of the cost and absolutely no attitude or pretentious behavior. Decor is cool, but again, it's all hype and trend. It will die as well like anything else.

Had a great time, definitely a place to check off your restaurant checklist. The service was superb. Made me feel like royalty. There was a tad bit of a wait as they got our table together.

The dining room and the art is enchanting. It isn't a dainty NYC setting. Its a fancy yet rustic decor. Sat in the back dining room and was great seeing the diversity of people in attendance. As for dress, not sure if there is a code but every one was dressed in business causal.
Don't expect to be in and out. Our experience lasted about 2 hours and some change.

Now lets get to the food. Is it overpriced? yes. Are you paying for the totality of an experience? yes. Some items were an absolute hit, some not so much. 

HITs: The Spicy Rigatoni lived up to all the social media hype. Creamy, spicy and cooked perfectly. They split the portion. 
The Caesar Salad sounds so simple but outstanding. The jumbo croutons and the whole oily anchovies were wildly good.
I didn't order the meatball but a pair next to us shared with me. And wow! they were good.

Miss: My partner had the Linguini Vongole which she had me try and it was way overdone. chicken scarpariello was good but nothing special.

Last tip for getting reservations. They open reservations daily at noon but honestly its closer to 12:30pm. The times aren't always ideal but you could get a 2/2:30/3pm on a weekday. Also check day of because people do cancel. The deposit is also subtracted from your bill.

Had a lot of expectations given how hard of a reservation it was to come by, and the price point. From the second we showed up, everything was fantastic. The service, the drinks, the vibe... even something as simple as the spaghetti pomodoro is to die for. Veal parm is a must. Would love to go back!
Incredible food, incredible service. We dined outside and our server was very knowledgeable and friendly. Such a lovely institution.
Great service. Intimate restaurant. Decor is cute. Food is quite mediocre. Average wine list. I put a lot of the "buzz" around Carbone down to excellent marketing.

So lucky to score a reservation at Carbone for lunch time. It's true what they say, their spicy rigatoni is truly amazing and probably something that's super hard to re create at home. 

My friend loved their scalloped potatoes and it was soft and so buttery but crispy on the top and edges. I would definitely come back for their rigatoni and tiramisu. 

The only annoying thing was some confusion around the bill (since we had to put down an initial deposit upon ordering), so hopefully that gets sorted soon. The food was worth it though and service was great.

Not only is this great food but it was a very nice experience and I would say a Top Five dining experience of all-time.  Outstanding service, also.  I was here with some coworkers and I think we tried everything - make sure you fast or something before you come to make sure you have room for all of the excellent dishes!

A+ on the service and ambiance. The spicy rigatoni ended up being my favorite and the tortellini al ragu came in second. The branzino was cooked really well, I'd get it again but it's the whole fish so definitely shareable. Everything is basically shareable. The chicken was okay. I didn't care for the lobster ravioli or the fettuccine con funghi maybe because I wasn't in the mood for it but my sister and cousin really enjoyed the fettuccine. I didn't like the margarita, it's not a traditional margarita but this was my first time having a Whitehall Lane Cabernet Sauvignon and I fell in love, my new favorite wine. I'll definitely go back.

Food is very good but when going to Carbone you truly are paying for the experience and service...I had been before and enjoyed thoroughly but this last time truly ruined any chances of me returning.  I was there for a casual Thursday night dinner and the Sommelier came around and asked if I had any questions related to the wine list. I simply asked if they had any Tuscan reds in the $120 range, his response was "I don't know...you know this is Carbone" in a condescending tone basically insinuating I was being cheap and out of place being there for asking such a question.  Very unprofessional and rude. FYI there is a $90 Chianti on the menu. Ended up going with a $145 bottle which was totally fine but he did not need to come across so pretentious and rude. Not what I expected out of the staff there...very disappointing...soured the evening.

Spicy rigatoni was good - not as worth the hype it has but definitely good and not too expensive to be honest. The waiter was rushing us the whole time, so much so that we were done half an hour before he needed the table back and only when we were getting to coffees he said 'no rush' as if the whole dinner hadn't been rushed beforehand. Hovered a lot and made it unenjoyable because it felt like he was just trying to get us out of there, which, to his credit, he succeeded at with plenty time to spare. Second time I've been because my friends have wanted to go but would probably never go back. If a waiter at any other restaurant had done the same I would have walked out.
My boyfriend got food poisoning here because they served him raw meatballs. Will not be eating here again

Was able to grab a lunch reservation on a Friday so I literally took a half day off to try Carbone! It was slightly fancier than I had anticipated, but not stuffy fancy. 

They start you off with a complimentary salami, warm mozzarella, and garlic bread appetizer and this might've been my favorite part of the whole meal! I will dream about this appetizer.

We also got the prosciutto appetizer and it was great. They give you 3 different types and another ball if mozzerella. It was some of the best prosciutto I've ever had.

The pastas were good but definitely over hyped! Not disappointing, but also not worth the price and effort of the reservation.

We ended with the tiramisu and it was so good. The lady fingers seemed like they were made in house and had a hint of lemon to them.

3.5 Hmmm. Despite its hot rep and craziness to get a res, this place is very mid lol. The pasta sauces are good but the pasta itself is not that different from other normal Italian places. The bass is a bit bland. I liked the baked clams and broccolini. Honestly the garlic bread + mozzarella were pretty dope. 

Very dark, old school romance vibes - also not super up my alley. Overall, mid and I don't think worth the hassle of getting a res. Also overpriced.

Our patio server Joey, was an amazing guy. He's so nice and friendly and made us feel so welcomed. We had the best complimentary bread with oliveoil cauliflower, its honestly the best beginning of our meal. Then we had the appetizer mozzarella and calamari, its honestly calamari 10/10, made with potato flour and baking soda. Its paired with this best sauce its mindblowing.

The shrimps were soo huge it made me so happy. Joey got us lemons and limes it was so good. clams linguine was so fresh and perfectly salted. There was the perfectly cooked al dente pastas. The spicy rigatoni was nice w clear onions and could be more spicy. I love the al dente tho.

Nd they gave us wet towels to wipe our hands with, and change our plates and cleaned our table cloth after every course :)  I also loved their plates. 

The veal parm was nicely crusted tasted like chicken and looked like pizza.

The two bathrooms was dimly lit and very pretty. One is more spacious than the other but love the soaps and paper towels. Things were pricy but definitely very filling.

I was able to get a reservation here during my week trip to NYC. Of course, everyone was talking about Carbone so I wanted to see what the hype was about. Overall, very good experience but I would try the other hundreds of great of Italian places before ever coming back here.

The service was fantastic. Very attentive, polite, and made it feel like a special experience. Side note, the inside gets really loud so if you want more privacy I would recommend outdoor patio seating which is what we did. 

The food was good, but not sure it justifies the price. The rigatoni was worth it so get that for sure. That sauce was perfection. The veal parm though, definitely not worth $90 in my opinion. 

Surprisingly the best thing we ate was probably the chocolate hazelnut cake. I'm not a huge sweets guy but it was amazing. 

Again great experience and great food. I just think that it's overpriced and you can get just as good food at other places in the city for half the price and without the impossible reservations.

Came to Carbone again last night for a date night and as usual it was a great experience! However, the service this time was not as good as previous trips. Our food was very slow to come, as well as our drinks, and at times it felt like that they forget about us. We were the last guests in the restaurant for this reason and the vibe completely changed for the end of our meal (playlist changed from their classic 1950s music to really loud and explicit rap, which I don't dislike but kind of ruined some of the fun)

The food was fabulous as always. The beef carpaccio is probably my favorite thing on the menu, but honestly everything is good. Also highly recommend the Caesar salad, SO GOOD!

Everyone knows this is a tough reservation to get. My friends and I literally practiced a month before to try to get in and we got it. It was what our whole New York trip was based off actually! The food was incredible and did not disappoint. We ordered the spicy rigatoni and tortellini and meatballs. We had to stop ourselves from ordering one of everything. The ambiance is very sopranos and godfather which I love and expect out of an Italian restaurant. The only thing is the seats in the front of the restaurant we're so close together we were practically having lunch with them. We could hear their entire conversation. Other than that, great great experience!

Would give this place a 3.5. Given how difficult it is to secure a reservation and the overall hype around it (and the huge price tag!!), the experience here is a bit underwhelming, but still worth going to at least once. Interior felt very authentic, but not too special. 

Spicy Rigatoni Vodka - 4.5/5 The must-have at this spot. The sauce is extremely good and is the special point of the dish. The pasta itself was a nice al dente, but nothing out of the ordinary. The quantity is quite small though (my photo shows what 1/2 an order looks like)

Mario's Meatballs - 3/5 You can immediately tell that the quality of the meat used is good (less fat, and more lean meat). However, it is a bit dry, even accompanied with the tomato sauce (which was quite good though).

Tortellini al Ragu - 3.5/5 A bit too overwhelmingly cheesy for my taste, but was solid. Nothing too special though.

Whole Branzino - 2.5/5 I was pretty disappointed by this one. Fish quality is pretty good, but is quite tasteless. It was also slightly overcooked. Definitely have had better.

Tiramisu - 3.5/5 Taste of alcohol is a lot stronger in this rendition, which is personally not my taste, but definitely has its crowd. Quantity is also surprisingly large considering the portion sizes of the other dishes.

One of the hardest places to get a reservation in NYC. All the tables would be gone within the first hour they release the reservation. 

It is a small charming Italian restaurant. If your are an Amex card member, you could request their outdoor seating. Just don't expect Amex Concierge would able to book you a table there because I tried. 

We ordered Eggplant & Zucchini Scapece, Beets Siciliana and Assorted Baked Clams as our appetizers. Highly recommend the baked clams dish if you are a seafood lover. Both the Eggplant & Zucchini and Beets dishes were refreshing with the right balance of Olivia oil and vinegar. Also, they gave each table a basket of freshly toasted garlic bread, mozzarella cheese and anti pasta. 

We ordered their famous Spicy rigatoni and Meatball. The Rigatoni pasta was tossed in a yummy spicy creamy sauce. I totally understand why it is their famous dish because it is addictive. The pasta was cooked to al dente. Just perfect. The traditional Italian meat balls was juicy and the ground meat was flavorful. 

We decided to try their Tiramisu even we were full. The creamy texture of mascarpone cheese layered with coffee soaked lady fingers was rich with a right amount of sweetness. It melted in your mouth. So I will recommend you to save room for this exceptional dessert. It is a good restaurant to go when you visit NYC; if you are lucky enough to reserve a table.
You must order the carpaccio! It is beyond amazing and they add walnuts for a crunch and it elevates the dish.

We never got to experience the ambience of the restaurant, as we were seated in an outside (but enclosed) building. The food was good but everything seemed a bit rushed. We were in and out in about an hour. Its worth a visit,  but there are alot of equally fine dining Italian spots at a more reasonable price

service 10/10
food 8/10 (slightly salty for my taste but i think that's italian food in general) it is A LOT of food! we had to bring most stuff home cuz we were too full.
ambiance 5/10 we sat indoors and it was crowded and tables were very close to each other like we could hear the table next to us' conversation clearly and they weren't even speaking loudly to each other (but most places in nyc are crowded so wasn't a big surprise to us )

overall i still think it's a must have experience especially if you live in nyc, carbone is a classic; every other person in new york knows carbone. it's an experience, and it's a nyc memory that would be nice to have while you're a here in the city!
Incredible.  All around. The food, the atmosphere, the service. Can't recommend enough.  Still thinking about the truffle tagliatelle.

So it is very hard to get a reservation but if you do the food is worth it. The wait staff is top notch and explain everything. Clams are amazing you get 3 different kinds to try. We also got the veal. It is absolutely enough to share and incredibly tender. The only issue we had were the tables are so close together it is a little uncomfortable. Besides that it was amazing.

The pasta and appetizer were so good but the minestrone soup was perhaps the worst soup I have ever had in my life. The service was great and the ambiance is dark and cozy which is perfect for a night out. However, based on all the positive reviews I was let down. I think it's a restaurant you should try at least once but I don't know if I would be willingly to go back.

This was my first time here and this place is over hyped. Food is whatever, went for lunch portions are small but good flavor. You would think for a restaurant to be booked out a month in advanced the service would be a1. Service lacked A lot! If you're looking to take food to go or order more food make sure you order everything when waiter asks. Our waiter failed to let us know that was a "rule". Overall food was ok but wouldn't be back/recommend.

This place is worth the hype!! Came with my family of 5 and it was DELICIOUS!! We made reservations a month in advance and came on Wednesday during lunch. Of course the place was packed. The bread, spicy rigatoni, and cappacio were my favorite!! Everything was so good. 10/10 and would def come back when i get the chance. Prices are fair. Service and ambiance were great too!
If you can get a reservation, put Carbone at top of your list. It is classic New York old school Italian feel with great food

We seat down 8:30 we order few appetizers and $290 steak that until 11pm wasn't in our table 
After complaining we had it 11:30 :(
That was to late to eat STK.

THE SERVICE WAS HORRIBLE. And by service I mean the ladies in the front. They are disgustingly rude and quite literally looked down at me and my friends. I came here to spend my money on good food. And they literally watched us in our face after we showed them confirmation of our reservation and refused to seat us. STUCK UP BROKE WHITE GIRLS TOO

Was Carbone worth all the hype? The answer is a (surprising) resounding yes!!! Everything that was prepared today was executed PERFECTLY! This was by far the BEST Caesar salad I've EVER had! I kept shaking my head in disbelief with every bite. Like... HOW IS THIS SO GOOD?! The clams were EPIC. They also had the most moist and delicious meatballs ever - and for being so big they were all still cooked to perfection! And then that aldente spicy rigatoni? *chef's * I need a nap, but guys, trust me. I know I'm late to the game but I'm in it for the long haul now. (Disclaimer: I know nothing of sports or sports references. ‍)

The thing about Carbone is you end up paying for the overall experience at one of the premiere Italian spots in the city. There's a reason it's a formidable force and nearly impossible to get a reservation at. I will say, though, that if your sole purpose in going here is to try the "ungodly" spicy  rigatoni that is raved by so many, you will likely be disappointed. 

There's a lot more to Carbone, from the ambiance, to the array of free appetizers they give you or even the wait staff. You truly get an experience that makes it worth your while despite the cost. At the risk of Carbone becoming too commercialized from its locations in Vegas or Miami, and the recent demotion of the Michelin star, Carbone still felt like a place worth visiting in New York City. The quality of the ingredients...the presentation....the balance of the meal with the heavy Italian flavors contrasted by the salad and the appetizers, very solid.

Please enjoy with your friends and family and get as many dishes as you can, the spicy rigatoni was the least memorable for me, but had to get it just to try it!

Reasons why I docked one star was because of the level of difficulty in getting a reservation at this place (it really doesn't need to be that exclusive lol) and Rigatoni was literally just rigatoni in vodka sauce.

Finally was able to dine at Carbone and I was pleasantly surprised. I was worried the restaurant would be overhyped but both service and quality were great! We were able to taste test a wine before getting a full glass. The complementary bread, mozzarella, and soppressata tasted delicious and fresh. For entrees we got the spicy rigatoni and the lobster ravioli. The rigatoni exceeded my expectations. It had the right amount of spice without needing to add crushed red pepper. The ravioli was a 3/5. I expected it to be more creamy than fishy but it tasted good. We got tiramisu as a dessert and the portion was huge! There was something very acidic in the mascarpone that made it hard to finish. Overall I had a nice dining experience!

Forever 5 stars in my book! 

When I tell you the hype of the spicy rigatoni is real, it's REAL and you should buy extra leftovers. All food was great overall. Carpaccio, oysters for an app and it was perfect with lots of taste! We all good different dish and I think an underrate dish is the tortellini, it was delicious!

The waiter was very attentive and helpful with the menu choice and wine guidance! 

Whole experience was very special for our girls trip and we will definitely be back!

Way over rated and over priced. The vegetarian items are pretty good, but it is not worth paying for the meat. And the veal Parmesan is their "signature" dish but it's bland and uninteresting. The vodka rigatoni is delicious but not sure the price point is worth it.

Obviously this place is on everyone's must-go list and we finally got a reservation but it was for lunch. We wanted to just go and see what the hype was about and honestly I'm conflicted. 

Food: The starters were great. The mozzarella cheese was amazing but I felt the bread was too crunchy. We didn't get the cauliflower dish and they didn't have any Potatoes Louie the day we went. Like everyone we got the spicy rigatoni and were not disappointed. It lived up to its hype although I felt the portion was a bit small compared to what I was expecting.

The Eggplant & Zucchini Scapece was the best! I didn't get a picture of it because we literally just ate it so quickly. For dessert we had tiramisu and I've had better for sure.

Service: we had a few hiccups with the service. Don't know if it's just the usual or the lunch crowd but we had to remind the waiter about our drinks which took some time to arrive. The host and everyone else were nice and welcoming. 

Ambience: I think the restaurant is just way too dark and while I get the concept of it, some extra lighting would help, especially if people are coming to experience the ambience and take pictures. I mean after all, it is Carbone. 

With that said, I would like to go again and see how it is in the night time and for that, we have to once again wait for some time to get a reservation off the Resy app. (Which makes no sense because I saw plenty of empty tables while having lunch so I'm not sure how they work out their reservations).
Pure Old School New York City Italian family style Resteaurant ..... I went there went when it was Rocco's too .. really miss it ... but I'll have to give a thumbs up for Carbone

I know a place like Carbone isn't going to care about a bad yelp review but it's worth sharing how absolutely absurd and awful their reservation process is. I've had alarms set in my phone to book for months and went to book right at 10am. Picked my time and it wants to charge me $200 for a reservation and not even give me the 30 seconds to put my card info in before giving my reservation away. I had all my info in by 10:02 and every single reservation was gone. I know Resy allows you to give people a hold time window to put in their freaking information.


This is so annoying and terrible customer care. $200 for a reservation and not 1 single minute to give them that ridiculous amount of money to hold a table. Stupid.

In general, our experience at Carbone was underwhelming. While the staff was polite and the food was good (above average), there were a number of miscues that justify a 3 star rating.

Reservations-
Having one is an absolute must. Reservations open every morning at 10:00am EST for the date 30 days in advance.  My wife made our 5/11 reservation on 4/11 at 7:00 AM PST.

Ambiance-
I'm sure it's nice inside, though based on their frequent star clientele, we never got to see. Instead, we were seated in the Covid Era outdoor seating in the street. It was nice enough, comfortable and quiet enough to have a conversation without raising your voice. You are in the street however, cars zipping past literally rock the structure. 

Service-
Servers are polite and seem to be knowledgeable enough but the attention to detail just isn't where it should be. My wife ordered a Grey Goose dirty martini which took a little longer than you'd expect and was served a gin martini . It took a few more minutes to send it back and get the correct drink delivered.

The small antipasto style parmesan/salami/cauliflower served with a basket of bread was terrific, just try not to fill up on bread. I dare you!

We ordered a $125 burrata/caviar appetizer and were served a basket of scorched bread to spread the delightful concoction on. In addition to the bread, the server took the pearl serving spoons away and left us to use the metal spoon to dish out and spread the caviar and burrata. This sounds incredibly snobby, and maybe it is. But that was my first time trying caviar and my wife does a lot of research before we try new things and everything she has read says that using metal taints the flavor of the caviar...something a 5 star restaurant would probably not overlook.

Our entrées were tasty, again a little above average quality there. My wife had the lobster ravioli and I swear I've never seen that much lobster in a pasta dish. I had the spicy rigatoni, no complaints. The Broccoli Rabe was incredibly oily which was a bummer. 

We ordered espresso martinis to close out the night and after about 12 minutes we has to remind our server. It was getting late and nobody's perfect but again, 5 star establishments knock that stuff out.

As for price, it's NYC so I expect to spend quite a bit of money but I definitely didn't get what I paid for.

bad service, rude maitre D. below average food. disappointing

reservation at 9:30, sat at 10:15. rude staff all around

I had a lot of high hopes for this place, concerning that it took me months to get a reservation. This place is definitely overrated. Literally the only reason this place gets this much clout, is because Leonardo DiCaprio comes here once in a blue moon.

First, I'll start with the service. We sat outside in the outdoor dining area (which I'll add was set up very nicely). I felt like I was having dinner at a café because the decor was very detailed. Our server was very weird, hovering over us. It's like he was rushing us to finish from the moment we sat down. 

The food was mediocre. When I asked for spicy rigatoni, I expect it to be spicy. It just did not do the job for me. The lobster ravioli however, was really delicious. Each entrée was about $30-$40, so I definitely do not think it's worth it, especially when there's numerous other Italian restaurants where you can get a decent plate of pasta for cheaper. The broccoli ragu was absolutely disgusting and bitter. And the tiramisu was very dry.  

I'm not sure what else I can see about this place. You'll have better luck trying Arthur and Sons or Osteria 57, both Italian restaurants within walking vicinity. 

I really tried to love you, Carbone, I really did. But better luck next time.

I mean....the spicy rigatoni lived up to the hype. Worth every penny. I understand why people come to Carbone just for that dish. 

We also ordered the Caesar salad. Would not recommend. It was expensive and nothing special

Managed to grab a reservation weeks in advance although I'd say for lunch-it was fairly easier to do so than during the evening for dinner. Very cute inside and very cute "oversized" menus for a small selection. I honestly do wish the service was better as I was waiting quite a bit to have my order taken (both drink and then food). The drinks are delicious, I had the margarita a few times but not sure if $24 was worth it. The pastas were fantastic and I was surprisingly taken aback by the fettuccine given it was with mushroom which is not my most favorite texture. The spicy rigatoni was also great but was very satisfied with both. The broccoli was okay, I think the least appetizing of our lunch and would not order again although huge portion.
Worth the hype!! The atmosphere, service and the food were impeccable. The Caesar salad, whole branzino, and spicy rigatoni are plate licking worthy (I would never)!

The ambiance was great and the service is top notch. However, while the pasta was great, it wasn't so spectacular that it justified the high price. The lunch portion also felt a bit small. I've had great pasta like for half the price. Don't get me wrong, it was delicious! Just a little overpriced. But since it's a famous restaurant, even among celebrities, I guess I can understand the upcharge. 

To be honest, the star in my opinion was the cheesecake and the tiramisu. Absolutely delightful!

Come here for a special occasion since it's on the pricey side, but they set up the outdoor area to look fancy! I believe there's only a few tables inside. I suggest two main pastas for two. I loved the complimentary three different types of bread, the salami, and the pickled cauliflower. They even come around and slice off some cheese off a block. The spicy rigatoni vodka really was the best! If you get one thing, it would be this dish. We also got the fettuccine con funghi.The Mario's meatball was a good addition. They also give a complimentary sponge cake dessert which is also delicious. I was too full for dessert, but they have some nice options.

Dined in the outdoor seating area on a Sunday at 5:45pm.  The complimentary starters were absolutely delicious.  We ordered the baked clams, spicy rigatoni and Mario's meatballs.  The baked clams trio was phenomenal. The spicy rigatoni was delicious but the portion was tiny!! The pasta was brought to us already split in 2 and I think my husband and I were given 10 rigatoni each.  For that price point and considering the cost of pasta, we were very disappointed.  I also was not impressed with the meatballs.  They had a strange texture, odd flavor, and were very dense. Another disappointment was the wine.  We paid $22 per glass and were not even given a full glass!!  Im ok with paying $22 for a nice glass of wine but  it better be a nice pour!  The overall experience was satisfactory and the quality of ingredients was amazing but the amount of food/wine given was quite a disappointment.

Great food, vibe but you already know this.
Service feels like family.
Love love love

This was not just a meal.  It was an event that I'll remember for decades.  To me, everything was perfect.  Don't go there on a budget.  Don't go thinking it's Olive Garden.  Don't go if you are going to fret over the bill.  Did we have a $500 bottle of wine?  Yes.  Did we order everything we wanted?  No, because there wasn't enough room.  It didn't hurt that the meal was comp'd, but I wouldn't care if I had to pay cash that once in so many years.  The service was among the best I have had anywhere around the world with a cheerful waiter who, if possible, made the experience even better.

I could not believe my husband got us reservations here! I was totally surprised. You all know how hard it is to get a reservation. No need to explain. 

We love the entire atmosphere. I felt like I was back in time and loved their playlist! They played classic Frank Sinatra and doo wop songs. The vibe was perfect. 

The service was great and the food was delicious.

I would say it was definitely worth trying. 

Appetizers: 
Sizzling pancetta- Wow! It was delicious!

Pasta:
Lobster ravioli - loved it because it was filled with lobster!
Spicy Rigatoni Vodka- Must have! It's their specialty. 

Entrees 
Pork chop with peppers
Shrimp scampi

Dessert 
Lemon cheese cake: we got it by accident but it was delicious and they still gave us what we ordered...
Nutella tiramisu... we actually liked the lemon cheese cake better.
Never had a bad meal here! Such a nostalgic experience and the food is simply amazing.

If can you can get a reservation don't think twice food is amazing and the vibe is great. 
SOMEONE PLEASE GET ME A RESERVATION AGAIN.

RUDE RUDE RUDE.  3 girls standing in front with RBF.  Stood inside for 15 mins then we were told to wait outside because she "thinks they open at 11:30".  Waited outside and after 11:30 didn't even come out to let us know we can come in.  New staff needed asap.  They think they're all that and exclusive - but they aren't.  Would never go there again.  They need to clean house for sure.  Much better places to eat than Carbone.  Funny thing - it was the same girl from when we visited last year.  She needs to get a job outside of customer service bc she def lacks that!!!

I was able to get a reservation the day I went cuz I was lucky, but I wouldn't sell your soul for one. I'd def go though. The starters are very good though I was sad they got rid of the warm mozzarella. The spicy rigatoni is as good as people say it is but the caesar salad and orchiette left me a bit underwhelmed. We should've ordered more tho. Also the waiter budded into my conversation about Michelin to give me his knowledge on Michelin which is funny considering THEY JUST LOST THEIR STAR. Still good service other than that. Would go again if somebody took me. Forgot the pasta photos...

First off: good luck getting a reservation here. We tried for months and finally lucked out with a lunch reservation on a weekend. Would highly recommend going for this approach!

The restaurant itself was gorgeous! It's much smaller than I thought it would be which definitely explains why it's harder to get a reservation. But that's only part of it. The food absolutely exceeded my expectations!

I'm usually wary of restaurants like Carbone because they tend to be overrated and overpriced. However, Carbone was quite the opposite! The food was incredible. Their iconic spicy rigatoni was so good and even served to us in half portions so that we could also enjoy the other food.

I would definitely recommend getting the lobster ravioli as well but the spicy rigatoni is a must try. Although, the food is a little pricey it is so worth it. I definitely plan to come back here and recommend still trying to get that reservation!

The staff was really nice and kept checking in on us. Also, dress smart casual at least. I was definitely underdressed.

I was so excited when I snagged a reservation here. I know it's not easy, but I was so determined. This was my birthday dinner and I can't even begin to describe how pleasant my experience was. We sat outside and they really made the area beautiful. We had Claudio as a server and he helped us pick out the most perfect meal. From the bread basket to the dessert, everything was top notch. We also had the pleasure of meeting Sergio at the end of the night. This was a memorable birthday and if I am able to come back I will. Next time I'll hopefully get to sit inside!!
Make sure you order extras pasta. You will regret you didn't doggie bag some home. The bread and gabagool is

Famous but the jarred pasta sauce they shill. Like, why? In an already crowded market, it's indulgent AF. 

Is the place for tourists? Who goes there these days? Reveal, friends

I really enjoyed our experience here, but I am not surprised that they lost their Michelin star. 

The service is good, but not great. 
I was happy I went in to use the restroom before we left so I could see the indoor ambiance, and let me tell you, patio seating is NOT the move. We knew the outside tent was rickety, but inside is really actually very nice so that made the tent even worse. I think the experience would be elevated ten fold if we sat inside.

The absolutely best part of dining is the small plates they bring out: bread, little nub of Parmesan, etc.

Really good espresso martini, probably best I've ever had. 
Our server said the lemon cheesecake made Kris Jenner cry and it was good but not worthy of tears.

After many Resy alerts, I finally snagged a reservation at Carbone for lunch. 

After ordering off of a ridiculously larger menu, you start your meal off with an appetizer of garlic bread, fresh mozzarella, and meat. From there we were served our 3 pastas:

1. Spicy Rigatoni Vodka: this is THE dish that everyone orders. In fact, they serve it to you already on 2 separate plates (for a table of 2) since they know you'll be sharing. Taste wise I liked it but wasn't wowed but my boyfriend loved it.

2. Tortellini Al Ragu: I could've skipped this one. It was just ok.

3. Lobster Ravioli: I can't actually comment on this one since I'm allergic but my boyfriend had it. Taste wise he felt like it fell somewhere in between the spicy rigatoni vodka and the tortellini Al Ragu - not a must have but tasted good. It also had a pretty generous amount of lobster.

We rounded out the meal with a massive piece of carrot cake. One one side of the cake it was nice and moist, the other side was very dry so it was an inconsistent experience.

At the end of the meal, our bill came to about $200! It was a nice meal but not nearly worth that amount in my opinion.

So so good and the service is superb - definitely hard to get a table as most of you know but worth trying and if you can't get a table parm in Nolita has same owners (I think) and they have the same famous spicy rigatoni

Carbone is a very exclusive restaurant where it is very difficult to get a reservation. We waited 6 months on the waitlist and finally got an 1130 AM reservation on a Tuesday (lol) 

I missed work to have this famous food and really wasn't disappointed. 

We sat in the American Express lounge which is jsut outdoor seating. Not very nice but we're here for the food. 

Spicy rigatoni was truly exceptional. Great flavor and even the gluten free pasta was delicious. 

We also had the lobster ravioli which was delicious. 

Overall recommend this place to anyone who can get a seat.

Too expensive for what you get. Food was delicious but tiny. The service is great. The ambiance is also nice, but still, I didn't think too highly of it overall, given the price and all. The menu choices didn't come off as very appetizing to me either. I had one of their pasta dishes; which was great but small. And super expensive. The free bread was the best part of the meal imo. LOL. I understand everything is freshly made and imported ingredients, but I suppose it just isn't for me. I also felt very sluggish after my meal, but I didn't even eat all that much, which is interesting at least.

Super super great experience here. I walked in with my sister for her bday. I wanted to surprise her after failing to get a reservation for months. The host Hailey was so beyond kind. She accommodated us both at 8pm their busiest time. Had the best server Mike. All his food recommendations were on point & delicious. Ambiance was classic New York restaurant night life I was looking for. It was the perfect evening.

Honestly I expected much more from this place. I feel like it's been tremendously overhyped; there's no reason for reservations to book up so quick. This is just a run of the mill Italian restaurant with decent food and average service. One thing that really bothered me, is the "patio" seating: not a patio at all, about five enclosed tables on the sidewalk with minimal a/c, noise from passersby, and that awful trash/city smell. It felt set up with minimal thought in an effort to create more tables to bring in money. Food brought to our tables had to be rushed across the sidewalk in between random people walking. And again, service was very mediocre. Overall, ~$250 for an okay lunch for two people, severely overpriced and overhyped.

Finally got the chance to try the famous carbone and it did not disappoint!! First off, i want to acknowledge how great the service is. We were immediately greeted by our waiters and given drink menus. We ordered a delicious white wine off the drink menu that paired very well with all the food. We ordered all the pastas family style and was the perfect amount. I loved that they had this option available for bigger groups. My favorite dishes was the spicy rigatoni and the linguine vongola. The pasta was perfectly al dente and the sauce didn't feel to heavy. I also really enjoyed the baked clams and calamari. The calamari has a very thin light breading that was done really well. The free bread and cheese was honestly one of the highlights for me as well. Hopefully i get to come back soon!!

We were really pleasantly surprised by our experience at Carbone. Going into this, we were a little apprehensive - after all, there is a notorious wait for reservations, a lot of hype around its celebrity clientele (will we see Drake there? turns out not this time!), and tons of mystery around what it meant that Carbone was a restaurant "to see and to be seen". We're not really "sceney" people, so I was a little curious to see if the food lived up to the hype. 

As it turns out, we loved everything we tried. As for the reservation story - we set alerts for it while we were on the way traveling to new york, and then got an 11:30 pm reservation for dinner on Sunday. Carbone then reached out and changed our reservation to 11:00 pm due to a cancellation last minute. My boyfriend has global dining access which I think helped. 

We arrived promptly at 11, and went to the bar for a drink while we waited for our table to be ready. the service was great - our waiter was a little pushy on upselling stuff to us, but everyone was really great. We opted for the tableside caesar salad, nonna's meatballs which were off the menu, spicy rigatoni, lobster ravioli, and to finish off for dessert, tiramisu and a lemon cheesecake with a blueberry compote especially for the summer! 

They're known for their infamous bread basket - our accoutrements came with salami, a focaccia, sesame bread, and their garlic bread, along with pickled cauliflower. we loved their pickled cauliflower - it was delicious. 

The tableside caesar was really great, but it's not anything you can't make. Everything was really fresh, and there were jumbo croutons that were delicious. I'd probably skip this next time. We also got the meatballs, which were super tender and soft - they were huge! it looked like they wrapped the outer section with beef and inside was the pork/veal meat mix potentially, topped with a fried basil leaf. They were good, but probably could be replicated. 

The two outstanding things were truly the pasta dishes, which is what they're known for. the spicy rigatoni lived up to the hype. peppery, tomatoey, it was a perfect balance with the chili kick right after. No wonder it's famous. The second pasta dish did not disappoint either - the lobster ravioli came dressed in TONS of lobster, covered with this delicious bechamel style sauce that I had to resist licking off the of the plate. The pasta is worth its ridiculous wrangling for reservations. 

I didn't love the tiramisu because it came off as strongly alcoholic, and I don't drink - I would probably skip this next time. But the lemon cheesecake was truly delicious and comes with a lemon curd topping in place of the traditional sour cream layer. our waiter topped it off with this seasonal blueberry compote and it was the perfect summer dessert. 

The check will knock off about $100 per person with starters, drinks, a pasta, and a dessert. But we'd definitely come back again....if only it was easy to snag a casual reservation! And as for the ambiance - it was perfect. dark blue walls, checkerboard floors, with small cozy tables - and they play motown oldies that set the scene. While many complain about how trendy it is, it's no joke - carbone is probably a self selecting scene, but there's a reason why the mainstay dishes are still enjoying their flowers.

Food- free garlic bread and mozzarella were really good. Spiny rigatoni is overblown-super average despite the hype. Fettuccini was pretty good and the side potatoes were also decent. Does not at all meet the hyper and the price point (wtf)

Marcos were great, but the somellier and man in suit greeting us were super cold and thinks they're above the customer because they work at carbone. Chill dude your food is overhyped. Y'all are just lucky riding the wave of hype and overcharging.

Ambiance is cute but the coldness of the staff were just shit

Hard to get a reservation at Carbone.  We set up alarms for us to try and was so happy to get a spot after trying several times.  Only late night available but wanted to see what the hype was all about.  Tasty but pricey.  They also stayed to mass market and sell their own line of pasta sauces.  I think next time, better off just buying their pasta sauces so don't have to go through the hassle of trying to secure a reservation.

Came back to Carbone in a bigger group and was able to try more dishes! I miss the complimentary mozzarella they used to serve. We ordered the baked clams, calamari, spicy rigatoni, tortellini, linguini vongole, and veal marsala. I would definitely order the calamari, spicy rig, and linguini vongole again!!!! all so delicious. I wouldn't recommend the tortellini or veal marsala. Service and vibes were great, cant wait to come back to try more dishes :)

We go to a lot of nice places and love trying food and experiences and honestly I don't get the hype. Sorry. 

Let me start at the beginning. It's impossible to get a reservation here . I'm not sure why. 

The vibe is old fashioned Italian glamorous . Very cute table seatings and ambience . There's a front section that's brighter and a back wood sectioned more cozy back section . 

Drinks : My hubby got an old fashioned which he enjoyed very much and I ended up getting the Cabernet Chappellet which was really delicious . I actually wanted to get a glass of their zero dosage  Michel Gonet champagne but it was awful . I think they were upset I tried it and didn't like it but umm isn't that the point of getting you a tasting before pouring you a full glass . Like cmon . If not don't go through the motions and allow for a tasting . 

We ordered a lot of food . They start you off with some bread , mozzarella dipped in olive oil which was all ok but the salami was freakin delicious . 

We then got the Caesar Alla which was a basic Caesar salad and was just ok imo , my husband enjoyed it more than I did . The buttered toasted croutons were the absolute highlight and freakin delicious star of that dish . So I'd get it just to try those croutons . 

Next we got the Spicy Rigatoni Pasta which was their best dish we tried . This is a good portion as well. The sauce on this is incredible . It's got tomatoes and onions within the vodka sauce and it's just so fabulous . You have to get this dish if you come here . No question . 

Then we got their white lasagna which was quite good . We also got a serving of their Mario's meatballs which came in a cute little dish and was quite good but honestly but something I would order again and I've had better . 

By this point I was a little full and but my husband said that we had to try their veal parm . It's priced at $89. Ok so this was the most underwhelming dish we had . It was totally not worth the price tbh . Like I'm not sure why it's so popular . The bone that comes with it is pretty good but that's about it. Would've rather have spent that money on one of their fish or chicken dishes . 

They give you rainbow cookies at the end of your meal so you don't have to get dessert. The hubs ate both so I didn't get to try them so not sure if they are any good . 

They don't have a dessert menu but he listed off some desserts - cheesecake , carrot cake , Nutella tiramisu and I can't remember the rest. It was between the Nutella tiramisu and the hazelnut chocolate cake and I quickly checked some reviews and went with the hazelnut cake , and good thing I did! Because this was phenomenal . It was so delicious . I'm partial to hazelnut but it was actually quite yummy. It came with a hazelnut crème anglaise and that was incredibly delicious I just wanted to drink that up whole . You have to get this dessert if you're getting anything . I kinda wish they had a smaller section for cocktails and desserts so I could come back and just get this . Or get it to go . Because I doubt I'm coming back here . 

Ok so the service was not great. Not sure if it was our server that day or what. He was just so unpleasant . And not friendly and didn't add to our dining experience . I really enjoy good meals but if the food isn't 100% epic they better have damned good service . Here, it was just underwhelming on both counts. In fact, the server messed up something with the couple who were sitting next to us order and of course she wasn't quiet about it (good for her) and they ended up giving them glasses of limoncello on the house and a dessert on the house and it's kinda like ok so you have to get someone mad or upset and then cater to them . Why not try and just cater to your patrons in general. 

Ok so I don't understand the hype and defn not going back

Had a great time at Carbone. It was an excuse to dress up and the service was absolutely wonderful - very attentive, very fun and friendly. Loved the bread basket. They give a lot of free appetizers (salami, large chunks of Parmesan cheese, and a large bread basket). Got the spicy rigatoni which was good - I think we ordered too much though - it's fine to just try a few noodles each. Got the lobster ravioli for something different and didn't really like it. The Caesar salad and meatballs were pretty good (the tomato sauce was a bit salty). The veal Parmesan was delicious - would highly recommend. And then we got this corn side dish with truffle which was recommended to us and just OK (we were too full by this point). Finally, we finished with their lemon cheesecake which was the best cheesecake I've ever had - probably the most outstanding item of the entire evening. We didn't love the orange tiramisu. Overall a super fun and delicious evening - would love to go back if we can ever get another reservation!
Soooo yummy and amazing service. Very cute and cozy inside. Definitely worth the hype.

there are a few things that really bothered me about our experience here and which will prevent me from coming back:
- reservations are made by booking through resy. you're required to pay a 50/person upfront deposit which is applied against your bill when you dine. i sent a polite email ahead of our dinner to ask whether i could swap out the credit card on file for the deposit and was given a really rude, curt response in the negative, which left a really sour taste in my mouth from the outset
- the day we came in to dine, we were offered water, still or sparkling... when the bill came, it turned out we were charged $10 EACH for water, which was not disclosed in any way ahead of time.

 with that out of the way, the meal was quite good other than one hiccup. the free starters (bread/cheese/salami, no cauliflower) were delicious, i really enjoyed the salami. free rainbow cookies were also really tasty with a super strong almond flavor. we ordered the baked clams, spicy rigatoni vodka, mario's meatballs, and lemon cheesecake. spicy rigatoni lived up to the hype for us, that sauce was top notch. lemon cheesecake also delicious, extremely lemony and tart. the meatballs were good but not particularly memorable for me. the flavors of the clams were good but some of the clams were a little chewier than others and hadn't been cleaned thoroughly - i got bits of shell/etc in one of mine!

tldr glad we tried it but once was enough for me.

Well it's been about a month since dining at Carbone and all I can say is wow...It was a disappointment to say the least. We were lucky to finally get a reservation through Resy with AMEX and it was for Sunday June 11 @ 1130pm. The time was not ideal but we made it work considering we had not been able to get in prior to this point. They texted us to see if we would come earlier due to some last minute cancellations but we had our day plan considering we needed to keep busy in order to have dinnner so late. 

We arrived and got seated with no issues and our server, a middle aged woman that was wearing a pony tail was checking her phone for the time from the moment we got in. I'm sorry but if you close at 1130 why would you accept reservations at that time knowing that you close? Clearly you are going to be there past close regardless. 

The complimentary bread, prosciutto, and CAULIFLOWER came out which I believe was suppose to be mozzarella? No one explained anything on the table they just dumped it and left. When I asked the server she reluctantly told us what each bread was.

We ordered the table side  Caesar  salad and I just so happened to look up and the server with the pony tail was making it "table side" by the host stand, very confusing. I tried to remain positive because again we had been wanting to dine at Carbone for some time now. 

Drinks were the only thing that kept me in a good mood and we got wine so luckily they didn't mess that up. 

For entrée I got the vodka rigatoni and it was simply OK. The first one came out super salty so they offered to make me a new one which was equally as salty so I just took the L, boxed it up, and left it for a homeless person to enjoy. 

Overall this was a poor dining experience and we won't be coming back.


I will add videos and photos. Server we had can be seen in the first clip walking towards the bar.

Service: 4/5. Not spectacular, but not bad. 

Spicy rigatoni: 3/5. Not a mind-blowing dish by any stretch. Good, not great. 

Meatballs: 1/5. They arrived raw in the middle. Not undercooked, not rare, but raw ground beef and pork. When an Italian restaurant can't cook a meatball correctly that is cause for concern.

Veal parm: 3/5. It's a good dish, but it's not worth the $85.

Ambiance: 1/5. This place is incredibly difficult to get a reservation for, as everyone knows. It shouldn't be that hard because it's not that good. I booked for Lunch on a Saturday. I now know the kind of person this place generally attracts and it's more for people who want to let everyone else know where they eat and where they've been. It's not for serious foodies. 

The two women seated next to us were among the most annoying, loud, obnoxious people in New York City, and that's saying a lot. 

If your self-worth is directly connected to the number of engagements you get on an Instagram post, this is a great place for you. If you like to eat and have had world-class Italian food in your lifetime, this is not the place for you.

Overall rating: 3.6

I'm gonna keep this short and sweet. The infamous pasta that was impossible to get a reservation for is not worth $35+. This is very overrated & if I was an influencer, I still wouldn't want to go here. 

Make it at home or go to another spot that has more reasonable servings and prices. Just my two cents.

As a self-proclaimed foodie I had to try Carbone at some point whether it was worth it or not. Thankfully, I thoroughly enjoyed every aspect of our experience. My friend had to set alerts for a while in order to get a reservation and we finally landed one, week of, on a Friday at 12 pm for 3 people. We were sat outside in the Amex Patio and it was a hot day so I was grateful for the air conditioning in the enclosed patio.

Our waiter took great care of us, checking in often and giving us recommendations and thorough descriptions of every dish we. ordered. We didn't mention it but he happened to notice that our table was a little wobbly and he was able to stabilize it for us without us even asking. 

The complimentary starter cheese and bread was really good. We started with the Prosciutto & Melon by recommendation - it was refreshing with a couple different types of melon and perfect for a summer day. The Caesar salad was good with definitely homemade croutons but at the end of the day it was just a normal Caesar salad. For mains we got the Spicy Rigatoni (of course), Salmon Oreganata, and the Meatballs. The Spicy Rigatoni and Meatballs were both fantastic! 

I think at the end of the day, Carbone is definitely going to be a good (pricey) experience if you get a chance to go but if you can't get a reservation there are endless Italian restaurants in NYC that will be just as good if not better so it's not the end of the world to miss out. I've also heard that Parm has the same exact spicy rigatoni recipe but for half the price so that's always an option!

We went to Carbone after a lot of hearing from friends how it's an awesome place to go to and how hard it is to get a reservation - thankfully Amex platinum has to help with snagging a lunch time weekend reservation. This place is a cute Italian place that really takes you back to Italy and away from the craziness of New York into a new world. Once seated we were served with some garlic bread, mozzarella and some meat slices. We decided to order:

* Caesar salad - my favorite part of this was the croutons which were fresh and crispy as well as full of butter. The anchovies were okay - overall good salad but nothing out of the world 

* spicy vodka rigatoni - this was my favorite dish, this was saucy and flavorful and every bite was delicious and creamy

* lobster ravioli - I wish I liked this dish more given the price - they definitely give a decent amount of lobster and I liked the cream sauce, but for me the stuffing of these raviolis was not my favorite 

They ended our lunch by giving us some small cracker things which looked like cookies which was cute and enjoyed this as a little treat. Overall, we enjoyed the food at carbone but definitely felt it was a little hyped.

Honestly sad that I loved it, considering how hard it is to get a reservation at one of the most exclusive restaurants.

Carbone has been on my list FOREVER and I finally secured a reservation thanks to AMEX Platinum. you get priority notifications for when a table is available on Resy but even then, it would be gone in seconds. finally was able to get one for lunch time and you pay $50 per person for a deposit! 

The hype is so real!! we got the Table-side Caesar Salad, Assorted Baked Clams, Spicy Rigatoni Vodka, and Veal Parmesan. the meal also starts with amazing garlic bread, salami, and mozzarella cheese and ends with a rainbow cookie. I can't even tell you what my favorite was. the Salad was so delicious w the thiccc croutons, Baked Clams was a pleasant surprise with how amazing each one was, the Rigatoni was the perfect amount of creamy w a kick, and the Veal was tender and cooked perfectly. service was also exceptional! I'm gonna need a reservation again ASAP!!

Salad $32/Clams $36/Rigatoni $34/Veal $89

Honestly a 3.5, but rounding up to 4 because the service was so stellar I have to give it to them.

Listen, I was excited to go here - even though the only res we could snag was 5:30. From the start, the service was A+ with great wait staff that was attentive, friendly and acted like you were at a million dollar event.

However, tbh food was lackluster. For the price and the hype, every dish left me with nothing notable to say. What we got
- baked clams: good, definitely a nice way to start because it wasn't very heavy, but it definitely could be skipped 
- spicy rigatoni: because obviously we had to get it ... but for what? Did not stand out from any vodka pasta except for its hefty price tag
- tortellini: PASS. Lacked all flavor and the texture of the meat on top just didn't match the pasta (my friend said it reminded her of baby vomit)
- meatball: this actually was quite delicious and rich, perfect fully cooked
- hazelnut cake: yes. A must get. No notes she was sweet and moist and the scoop of gelato was the cherry on top

All around, probably won't ever go back, but happy we went to say we did!
This was one of the best dining experiences I've ever had. Meticulous service. Amazing food. Great drinks. All nestled in a unique environment. Simply fantastic!!!

Perfect Italian atmosphere! Smart bar and nice tables. A friend and I spit the fettuccine fungi and the veal parm. The fettuccine was light and the mushrooms were tasty (not briny). The veal parm... divine! Neutral sauce (not too spicy, not too acidic) in a good way. PERFECT service. On the pricy side - but all prices have gone up. I will return!

Carbone was one of those highly sought-after restaurants in New York, and even though it lost its Michelin star, it's still a bit tough to get reservations. However, when an opening popped up, I didn't hesitate to book it. The service at Carbone is truly top-notch, and our waiter was friendly and attentive, making the experience even more enjoyable.

We sat in the Amex Patio, thanks to our Resy, and were a bit worried about the heat. But to our surprise, the little shack was cozy and beautifully decorated, and they had ACs to keep us cool. It turned out to be quite comfortable, even cooler than the main restaurant.

Being adventurous, we decided to order quite a few items from the menu. The free mozzarella ball was a delightful start, and we wished they kept them coming. As for the dishes we ordered, the Spicy Rigatoni Vodka stood out as a winner, absolutely delicious. However, the rest of the dishes were just average. Considering the prices, we expected mind-blowing flavors, but unfortunately, they didn't quite deliver.

I'm glad I got the chance to try Carbone and cross it off my New York foodie list. However, I'm not sure if I'd go back, as there are other Italian restaurants in the city that offer better dishes at a more reasonable price. Nevertheless, it was still a good experience, especially with the superb service and cozy ambiance.

Unpopular opinion: The Caesar salad is the star at Carbone! Everyone knows that getting a reservation here is close to impossible so we were so excited to finally try this restaurant!!  The spicy rigatoni wasn't as phenomenal as they make it, being their signature-I've had better. The lobster ravioli is also nothing worth ordering.. The meatballs and salad were great to order again!
Excellent Food and friendly, attentive staff. The eggplant was really good and pasta. Food portions are good for sharing.

I admit that I was influenced by the ~*influencers*~ to come here. I wasn't sure if this would be worth it or not because I was reading that people either loved Carbone or thought it was overrated. I'm here to report that I was one of the people that loved it! Except its price point.

I got a lunch reservation probably 30 seconds after 10 am hit. Dinner was sold out, but that's ok considering dinner prices are more expensive and it's all the same food. I left with some leftovers and feeling stuffed.

We started with drinks and the espresso martini and house margaritas were delicious! The bread, cheese, and meat was amazing. Truly some of the best I've had. We also got oysters to start and whatever they put on top of them was incredible. The caesar salad was also very good and the croutons were unlike anything I've ever had before.

For our main meals I got the spicy vodka rigatoni and my boyfriend got the lobster ravioli. I loved my dish! He liked his, but wish that there had been more cheese in the ravioli. They were very dense and lobster heavy, not much cheese going on. The tiramisu for dessert was an interesting take, but good!

Service was quick, but not too quick. Everything was timed well and our server was nice. I'm glad I tried here once and I thought it was worth it for a birthday celebration, but I would probably check out another place before I come back!

A night out with my cousins in NYC... Kumanan somehow got us in, despite a last minute decision to finally find out what the hype was all about... In the bustling arteries of New York City, Carbone sits like a revered vinyl in an old jukebox. The place resonates with an echo of an Italy that perhaps only exists in our fondest dreams - where time-honored recipes shake hands with the audacity of the present. Dive into their menu, and you'll find the Spicy Rigatoni staring back, defiantly declaring itself as more than just a dish, but an anthem. A dance of fiery spice and silken cream, it's a taste that parallels the relentless pulse of the city's streets. Carbone doesn't just serve food, it curates memories, offering a fleeting return ticket to a nostalgic Italian era. And in the end, as the city lights merge with the horizon, it leaves you with an insatiable yearning, not unlike the enduring embers of a Manhattan dusk.

Tina's take: 12/10 

Ok so my friend and I were able to finally snag a reservation on their website they open them at 10 am. They have indoor dining option and their Amex patio which is their outdoor dining. We wanted to sit indoors to get the whole experience and we did. I want to say the staff was absolutely amazing and made it truly such a nice time. They started us off with mozzarella, garlic toast, and salami. The mozzarella was fresh and warm. Then we got a Cesar salad to share, we asked for the anchovies on the side. The croutons were great. Then we had to get the spicy rigatoni each , and it really did not disappoint. Whoever says they don't like it, are liars. Then we also got the meatballs and shrimp scampi. The shrimp is only one shrimp, but it is the size of my forearm. The meatballs were good, but I am also biased for my moms meatballs. For desert they gave us 7 layer cookies but, we wanted to go out for a bang. We got three different opinions from the staff and we ended up with the lemon cheesecake. I have not one complaint, thank you so much to the staff who made our time memorable. We cannot wait to go back!!

Made a lunch reservation 30 days out to go to Carbone. I've heard about it so much and it is definitely worth the hype. The service is absolutely top tier. 

I ordered the famous spicy rigatoni vodka and it was amazing. My friend ordered the fettuccine con funghi with a side of meatballs. This was also delicious. 

I definitely want to go back and add a house chopped salad next time. The table next to us got this and it looked incredibly fresh. I'm already dreaming about my next New York trip!

So glad I was finally able to make it here! We had a reservation for lunch and had a great time. Even the outdoor patio, which is where we sat, was pretty comfortable and nicely decorated. Everything was pretty solid, we particularly loved the Spicy rigatoni and the tomato sauce on the Meatball and Veal parmesan. Another highlight was seeing them assembling the Caesar Salad right in front of you, the croutons and anchovies were great. The Funghi trifolati was another favorite. We had the chocolate cake for dessert, which was good but not incredible. Overall, we had a positive experience but it didn't surprise us. Service was friendly and attentive. But at this price point, it left us wanting a little more.

Freshly made mozzarella and the spicy Rigatoni Vodka are to die for! The side of corn was delicious too! Tiramisu with Nutella and Cappuccino were the desserts, they were alright. Service is brilliant and pretty quick.

Believe the hype !

Yes, reservations are 30 days out on Resy. Please have your card info ready in the app, the spots disappear QUICKLY but it's totally worth the effort.

We were greeted oh so pleasantly, with smiles and superb service. From the host to our waiter, service was amazing. We chose outdoor seating for our reservation and enjoyed the ambiance of being in a smaller setting outside.

I opted for the famous spicy rigatoni which was creamy with a comfortable "spicy" touch.  My friend ordered the veal Parmesan, and wow, soooo good and large portion for sharing. Both were very fresh and delectable. Truly enjoyed an authentic Italian, Al dente pasta and fresh flavors!

I can't say enough good things, this is the closest to my cuisine in Verona, Italy here in the states.

Holistically, the meal was great. I thoroughly enjoyed every dish I tried within a group of four, and was satiated by the end. In terms of service, the food came out appropriately fast, and waiters were very attentive (folded our napkins, filled our waters, etc.). Unfortunately, I felt that our waiter was quite pushy when it came to ordering. I was uncomfortable when he kept suggesting we order more, even though we had stated we were fine with what we had. I would suggest previewing the menu before you go.

As for the food:

There was free bread with 3 varieties (sesame, foccacia, and garlic), served with parmesan. Foccacia was a crowd favorite!

Assorted Baked Clams ($36): The starter came out with 3 types of flavors, 3 clams each. Since we were a group of four, they offered us the option of adding on a fourth clam, but we declined. Overall, this was my least favorite dish. The flavors fell a little flat, and I thought the price was steep for the amount we got.

Caesar alla ZZ ($34): This caesar salad came with anchovies, which we asked for on the side. The highlight of this dish was the croutons, which are large and slightly sweet. 

Tortellini al Ragu ($35): This was my favorite dish, although I felt that the ricotta to dough ratio could've been improved. Ragu sauce was delicious!

Spicy Rigatoni Vodka ($34): Probably their most well-known dish! I have to say, the sauce was delicious and the pasta was cooked perfectly. Definitely worth the hype.

We ended with free Italian-style cookies. Overall, this was a great one-time meal, though I don't think it's worth the hassle of getting a reservation.
The food was wonderful. The service was even better. Roberto was very friendly and attentive, and made our dining experience even more impressive.

Obviously a very hype restaurant but if you're looking for that old school Italian vibe you won't be disappointed. The veal parm and the rigatoni are the staples and they are GOOD. Vibe is great, you'll feel like you're on set in the Godfather. Good drinks and wine recs. Service was friendly and great right up until the end: The server made a point to open up the check and point out what number we should tip on.  SUPER rude and closed the experience making me feel like I was at a Denny's instead of dropping $300+ on a casual lunch for two.  Certainly not fitting of an establishment with a standing like Carbone, and hence the loss of a star (and 5% of the servers tip). Do better.

As soon as I plan my trip to NYC, I knew I had to try Carbone. I knew 30 days before at 10 AM Eastern time I had to login to get reservations and I was likely able to snag a table for lunch. 
Finally, the day arrived. I was so excited when I walked in.  The ambience of the place was wonderful. You don't feel like you were in New York City anymore as you're completely transported to a different time and place I felt. The music added the extra wonderful touch to this place.
