We wanted to do a late lunch as we were going to be walking around New York grazing on other food and also had dinner reservations , but I felt like our waiter was slightly pushy with the "Are you sure", "are you sure?". 
After we ordered, they brought out the garlic, bread, warm, mozzarella and salami. Such a delicious combo! They brought out our chopped salad along with the other appetizer, and I felt that the waiter was a bit pushy with serving us, and wanting to clear the table. My friend noted that that was just the Italian way of doing things and feeding people. They then brought out the two pastas we ordered to share, which were good. I won't lie and say they were the most amazing I've ever had but they were pretty good. 
We ended the meal with the little almond cookies they gave us which is a perfect little treat. 
Would I come here again probably not. Am I glad I tried it at least once 100% yes.

I recently went to Carbone, and I truly do have mixed reviews on this restaurant. Keep in mind, this is my second time here. I go out to nice places once in a while, but when I do, I don't mind spending, we ordered A-LOT for two people. We started off with three appetizers, baked clams, the prosciutto Al melone, and the Cesar salad. The prosciutto was great, They gave you three different types, and they really did differ between each other. The salad did not disappoint, those croutons have a very buttery taste, however I feel like they were missing the crunch, they were a little too soft, not gonna complain about that too much though. Now with the clams, those were not great. They came out kind of cold , and they really were not packed with flavor, considering that's a 36 dollar dish it was a bit disappointing. We ordered three different types of pastas. We had the tortellini Al ragu, orecchiette Vito, and the spicy rigatoni. This was probably the best part of the meal. Obviously, the spicy rigatoni was amazing, it does live up to the hype, however, I feel like the tortellini are not hyped up enough. THEY ARE SPECTACULAR, so creamy, and the sauce is perfect not too tangy because of tomato acidity, and perfectly sweet. The orecchiette Vito in my honest opinion as a non picky eater was disgusting. It was bitter because of the broccoli rabe or spinach sauce, not very sure which of the two it was, even though I would lean towards the spinach. The sweet sausage that came with it was also lacking flavor. Lastly the orecchiette were too Al dente, definitely too chewy. Had force that one down if I'm being honest. Tragic. We then ordered the pork chop, and the chicken Massimo. The pork chop is delicious, it's as tender as filet mignon, truly incredible. However, the Chicken Massimo was another disappointment. At times it tasted burnt and at other times it tasted flavorless. Maybe it was lacking balsamic vinaigrette?? I'm not sure, but definitely not worth the price. We then finished the meal with two desserts, which were both amazing. The tiramisu did not disappoint, even though it's a little bit expensive, and neither did the lemon cheesecake. Overall, I'm giving the restaurant three stars mostly because of the over hype that it has. The fact that the clams were a little bland and the fact that they came out cold is kind of insulting to me, considering that they are expensive and I had to wait one month for a table here. The fact that the croutons were a little soggy also kind of indicated a lack of care into the food, which I didn't really like, but I wouldn't of had a problem if it wasn't for the other things. I almost never consider food disgusting, the orecchiette Vito was reaching that point which is insulting. And the fact that the chicken Massimo was just overall inconsistent in flavor, and at times tasted burnt, really disappoints. In summary, I don't think Carbone is worth the hype, there are many Italian restaurants out there that serve incredible food and you don't have to wait a month to get into.

The famous Carbone! It felt so exclusive, fun, and cozy. My thoughts:
- staff are extremely professional and courteous!
- venue is a bit tight on space, but enough space between tables so you aren't pinched in
- rigatoni was excellent and they helped us split it up
- meatballs are a must
- caesar salad had the best crutons I've ever had!

Overall, it was good. The bread basket was very small with garlic bread (Vegas had a bouquet of bread), which was a bit disappointing. We had a 1:45pm seating, but the last call for the kitchen was at 2:00pm, so we ended up ordering 3 dishes + 2 appetizers, but could have eaten more. Wish our waiter had told us that it was last call and that the amount we ordered was not enough. 

I think the 1:45pm lunch seating is high risk, given the limited time span, so I would recommend doing dinner. There was no choice of dessert, unfortunately. Will come again for dinner soon.

It's Carbone so most people either know what they're getting themselves into or have at least heard from multiple people. It's sceney, the service is fast, the food is pretty good, and unless you know somebody grabbing a prime time res is a major pain. 

Service was efficient and accommodating. We got half orders of the spicy rigatoni each and the servers made sure to accommodate everyone's dietary needs. Table side Caesar Salad is always fun and you get the feeling that the restaurant runs like a well-oiled machine. 

Food overall was excellent and are elevated takes on Italian-American fare. Star of the show for us was surprisingly the eggplant & zucchini scapece which kind of surprised us. The spicy rigatoni is the classic but I felt like this time around it was teetering on the edge of over seasoned. The mains were tasty with the veal parmesan being a highlight. 

If you can score a res, I feel like you have to at least try this place once.

Sorry to be "That guy." This place was way overhyped. I finally managed to secure the highly coveted and sought after reservation. My cousin and I met for lunch, and we were seated outside on their little contained patio. They took our order and brought out the salad shortly after. When he checked back in with us after a few minutes, and alerted us that our next course would be out momentarily. 35 mins later he came back to check on us again. Never received our entrees, nor did we feel like we were on his radar at all. Honestly though; my review isn't based on poor service. The food was mid, and I will likely make a better version of this menu on a typical weeknight for my kids.
Everything was great - our host, food, and overall ambiance of the restaurant. The pizza beead and picklee cauliflower starters were perfect. The porterhouse steak...delicious!

This place is so overrated. Made our reservations a month in advance like you have to. We were tucked away in a dark corner instead of given a window. Our server was not pleasant, and the food was so mid. Our eggplant appetizer was doused in vinegar and almost inedible. The server could see we were not eating it but chose to ignore us. We had to flag the host down to get attention. They did switch it out for us, but the server had also tried to pressure us into ordering more when we didn't need to. The dishes are way overpriced and are poorly described on the menu. Our lobster ravioli tasted fishy and the one shrimp we ordered was very average. We took the spicy rigatoni to go and ate that cold at the hotel at night. It was the best thing we ordered.
The couple next to us was allergic to nuts but since the menu is only titles, they were not aware there were walnuts in their appetizer until they started poking around at it. The server had to remove everything and give them new place settings. Disaster averted, but it was a close call. Like just explain the dishes? This place needs to do better overall.

Second time here and I brought my boyfriend this time.
Food was amazing, my boyfriend fell in love with the spicy rigatoni and fettuchini. He loved the beer-menabrea and also had an amaretto sour. I enjoyed my Negroni as well. Service was top notch per usual, very friendly and polite. We sat in the amex patio which was nice and intimate. Overall loved Carbone once again.

This was my second trip to Carbone but first to the NY location. The service was top notch and exactly what you would expect from a Michelin (well, formerly Michelin) restaurant. Our waiter was attentive and went the extra mile- even walking guests to the bathroom when inquiring where it was. 

I went for lunch and the environment was not as intimate as I expected but still great never the less. The music was soft, the lighting was bright. 

I ordered the meatballs and they were great but a bit underdone. With a restaurant like this I would never send food back but I would have enjoyed them a bit more if they were rare and not still almost alive! The spicy rigatoni was amazing, as always. 

Overall, good experience. Just wished the ambiance was a bit more intimate (but, again, it may be at dinner!).

This was my second time there, but first time for lunch. In my opinion, sitting either inside or in the Amex patio provide really nice dining experiences. The food is incredible and eating here should be on your priority list. Thank you to our waiter for meeting my allergy restrictions by providing a new beef carpaccio without walnuts. I also left with a full menu as a nice souvenir (gifted by the waiter, of course).

My boyfriend and I had lunch around 1:20pm. We got seated by the restroom inside. Luckily there is a wall dividing the tables from the restroom. The only downfall is people get on line and would stand next to our table since they have only 2 restrooms. 

After we sat down, they gave us small starters on the house. They were pepperoni slices, fresh mozarella and garlic bread. The garlic bread was hard, but the mozarella drenched in olive oil was warm and delicious.

My boyfriend ordered margarita and I, a frose. We ordered eggplant & zucchini scapece, Spicy Rigatoni Vodka and Chicken Scarpariello. We really enjoyed the eggplant & zucchini scapece. I also really liked the spicy rigatoni vodka. I ate the whole thing.

For desserts, we each ordered coffee to compliment the Chocolate hazelnut cake and lemon cheesecake. 

Excellent service! Clean with cozy ambiance inside. 

We ate way too much, but indulged ourselves to the fullest. I am glad we checked this place out, but we don't think their dishes are outstanding or worth the price to come back.

This place was HARD to get a reservation for. Of course, they bring you the free apps and the garlic bread was my favorite. The spicy rigatoni was very good but the I didn't like the mushroom fettuccine. The noodles were really soft/overcooked and not chewy at all. If you come try to sit inside because the Amex patio is really intimate and it's awkward that the servers are right next to you and can hear your whole conversation. Overall, I think it's worth trying this place once for the experience!
Carbone is a great NYC experience! This hard to get into eatery is classic Italian. Be prepared for a lively evening with some excellent food. Bring your appetite and your wallet.

The reservations were a pain to get but between us calling exactly at the reservation release and Amex concierge we secured a decent time. 

I wouldn't say "greeted" by security but I would say intercepted by security we then checked in with the host who was very friendly. However, they have an extension to the restaurant out front, like a manufactured home which is where we dined. I was super bummed by this since this was my restaurant of choice for our trip. Most people who posted about Carbone said if the meal doesn't live up to the hype then the vibes will make up for it. Let's just say neither really did. 

Salad: it was ok. Nothing about this Caesar salad stood out compared to other table side Caesar's I've had. We left the croutons because they were a bit too dry.

Meatballs: they were good. Comes in 3. Again- they were ok, filling. 

Rigatoni: the best thing we ordered. Pasta was cooked perfectly and the sauce wasn't spicy at all but still delicious. Did I go home dreaming of it? No. Would I order it again- yes but I also wouldn't be sad to try other things. 

Artichoke hearts: pretty bland but filling. 

For such the hype, reservation difficulty, and the "outdoor" seating- I would not go through the trouble again.
I love this place. Very yummy food. Prices not that bad given the quality . Amazing service too. We get reservations by clicking "Notify" on Resy. It works often

I don't know why everyone says that this place was overrated and wasn't worth the hassle.  

It blew our minds! Each dish was flavored well and uniquely. Definitely was not mediocre.  

What we got: 

Antipasti -- eggplant and zucchini scapece (5/5 stars) (maybe a little on the sweet side but not too much). Don't sleep on this one. 

Pastas

-- Spicy Rigatoni (4/5) - it was great as a pasta dish. I liked it a lot to eat it regularly. It tasted like sweet flaming hot Cheetos on pasta to me but that might just be me. Still wonderful though. 

-- Spaghetti Pomodoro (5/5 stars) - The unexpected  highlight of our meal.  It was not what most would expect from a typical spaghetti dish.  Seriously - do NOT sleep on this one. All the right flavors and the right balance. 

-- Linguine Vongole (3.5/5 stars) - good but needed a pinch of salt or something to it.  Unexpectedly spicy which was a nice surprise! If we didn't also have the spaghetti pomodoro, we probably would have thought this dish was 4/5 stars.

Table Service (3/5 stars) - host was attentive but seemed to be a bit scattered at times like he was trying to give the absolute best service but on a time limit.  Very rushed.  

Also our orders were mixed up in communication a lot.  We asked for meatballs, he countered with asking if we wanted pasta to go along with it, we said sure and picked a pasta.  Only when the pasta came out, the meatballs never did.  The same thing happened with desserts. He listed the desserts, we picked the Tiramisu....he said ok, laughed, but then came back with our check and no dessert. We were really confused like we were Jedi mind-mind-tricked or something.  We didn't bother speaking up cause honestly we didn't need the extra food anyway....but...wtf...I get that we got in on the 2 PM reservation and the place closes up at 3...and they were slowing down trying to clear everyone out....but that was not our choice.  It was the ONLY time slot we were able to grab after having tried for 2-3 months to get a reservation. 

Bar service (5/5 stars) - shoutout to John the bartender in the corner! Absolute professional and very attentive and friendly. Didn't make us feel like we were uncultured swines like some of these bougie places do in this city. 

Ambiance - cozy, intimate, great bathroom!
I loved this place so much but really hard to make reservation. I gave up. I went over 3 days in a row. Each day I was told no chance. Make a reservation on line. Good luck with that.

Carbone has everything together and going for it except, ironically enough, their hype.  Is it the best Italian restaurant in New York? Wrong question at this level of culinary craft. 

The spicy rigatoni, meatballs, baked clams and eggplant zucchini scapece were the stars of the show and delicious. We didn't get warm fresh mozzarella which was supposed to be customary, disappointing. Maybe seasonal? 

Carbone has redemption work to do with a more cultured New York palate that fled to Italy this summer to compete for
By far the best Italian food I've had in my entire life. Excellent service that takes a nice modern Italian place to the high point of New York.

Hard pass. 

If you just discovered New York or haven't been to NY in ages, you might assume Carbone was a refined version of an old New York restaurant straight out of a Billy Joel song.

Friend, this is none of that.  It's pretentious and bougie AF. For one, you can't just walk in. If that doesn't rub you the wrong way enough, you need to either strike it lucky on Resy or be an Amex cardholder to accelerate your reservation policy. That doesn't mean you make nice, that just means you can pay. 

"And WHO are you?" armed with a pretentious air that uptown Rao's has without so many tables being bought or traded up like a low key mafia assembly, your reputation will determine where they seat you. Though even if you have nearly one million followers on social media, that may still mean in the enclave outdoors. It's nice adorned in a classic saloon fashion, but don't look outside. 

The menu is the ultimate oxymoron of all, huge like a certain chain restaurants huge menu we all adored, but sparse on the inside.  If by chance you can get in here or can blow stacks, just order what you're hungry for. The chefs can probably make that spicy rigatoni vodka in their sleep already, oh the magic of what some good olive oil does to add a little sheen to vodka sauce tossed over boxed pasta. But hey, those who still like to think they're above Olive Garden while enjoying slightly above average Italian American fare, comically are addicted to a pale comparison of penne alle vodka or chicken riggies!

The portions are rather sparse for the price which is also confusing. It's slightly above what you'd expect from a tasting menu but not quite family style. At least there are more Italian-American dishes than the Olive Garden, but really, when you're in NY, you can find thousands upon thousands of family owned Italian immigrant restaurants with an atmosphere that Carbone couldn't replace "for a million. Or two", to quote the late Anthony Bourdain.  

They're quickly disappearing, as is the real old New York, but they're far more worthwhile than this.
I LOVE  all of the Carbone restaurants. This is magnificent. The food 5*. Service 5* Atmosphere 5*. I plan to to go from California to NY every year to visit family and go to Carbone. Exquisite

Bests:
the famous spicy rigatoni :) 
Some sort of other pasta that was cheesy and paired so well with the rigatoni

Good:
assorted baked clams

Just ok:
caesar salad ... sad we didn't try the house chopped

If you haven't heard by now its extremely hard getting reservations here. We were able to snag one for lunch! I had to see what the hype was all about! For starters the ambience, music and the attire the staff wore really set the tone. It's such a nyc dark steakhouse vibe. It's nyc you can be as fashionable as you want any hour, but I'm sure there's a standard dress code. The service was formal and friendly. The food was absolutely delicious. As a picky eater I will say the tomatoes on my jumbo shrimp seemed chilled or maybe it was just cold I would have preferred it hot. The spicy rigatoni was my favorite, the sauce had just the right amount of spice and flavor im still thinking about it! The ribeye steak was cooked to perfection! I found the sauce to be a bit sweet so it really depends on what you like. When making my reservations it asked the occasion and I mentioned my husband and I would be opening our baby gender envelope. The staff went above and beyond to bring out a beautiful piece of China that opened with blue eggs and a dessert celebrating my baby boy! I was completely surprised and blown away ! Many of the staff members stopped by with their blessings and I felt overwhelmed with joy ! Carbone really made it special for me! I can't say one bad thing about my experience and if you want to experience top class service this is the place to dine.
Linguini with clams $47...veal parmigiana $89. Unbelievable.Owners must be laughing all the way to the bank.A lot of suckers out there.

I really, really wanted to love this place. The highlights were the spicy vodka pasta and the complimentary cheese and salami that comes with the bread. Unfortunately, when I opened up a meatball, it was raw. I informed the snooty waiter (who wore obnoxious red circular frames) that it was raw. He immediately replied, "NO, IT IS NOT, (as if I was a child) but I will take it back and cook it more." Why do you dismiss a client when you can visibly see the pink meat rude waiter?  It took over 30 minutes for someone else to bring us the meatballs, and with it came, "Meatballs well done!" as opposed to medium rare? Shouldn't meatballs always be well-done? The issue was handled irrationally and disrespectfully that it left a bad taste in my mouth.

This has been on my foodie bucket list for a while and so excited that I got to try this during my visit to New York. My friend made the reservation on resy for 2 for 12pm. FYI for westcoasters, you have to be ready to reserve at 7am sharp! 

For complimentary starters we got 2 pieces of bread, salumi & warm moz. I was thrilled we got the warm moz! I know they sometimes rotate between the warm moz and fresh parmigiano reggiano so I was very happy we caught them on a good day. The bread selection was weak, there was actually no selection, just 1 pc of bread per person which was a little disappointing, from other photos I've seen, it looks like 3 different kinds of bread for the table. Salumi was fine, no complaints. We didn't get any pickled veg either. Not sure if the reason why we didn't get the full experience is due to being a lunch service instead of dinner.. 

Onto the food, we ordered the Caesar, corn tartufato & spicy rigatoni to share. The Caesar is tableside, kind of, the restaurant is small so it's hard to get a good view of them making the salad if you're not sitting in the both. This was delicious! I loved the anchovies, it was a nice meaty bite and had the acidic element to cut through the dressing. The croutons are delicious, they remind me of garlic bread you get at the Korean bakery, kind of hard on the exterior, soft and airy on the inside, and slightly sweet! The corn tarafuto is a cream corn dish with truffle. I wasn't a big fan of this dish, the truffle in the corn was too aromatic and strong, I believe they used truffle oil which I'm not a fan of. The truffle dusted on top wasn't doing anything for this dish expect visuals. The corn itself with nice and sweet, really good bite to them. I wouldn't order this again. The spicy rigatoni took a long time to come out, I think we waited almost 20 minutes for this. Once it finally came out, it went by quick! The rigatoni is nice and al dente and the sauce is a little tangy yet creamy. I liked the onions in the sauce, it was something else to look forward to in this dish. We finished off with some complimentary rainbow cookies, they tasted like almonds, delicious! 

Overall, service was good, they have coat check service in the front and would re fold napkins if you got up to use the bathroom. I would love to revisit their Las Vegas location, it's closer to me, to try their other dishes and to eat the Caesar again! 

Price wise, you're paying for the experience, ambiance, and a timeless meal. It's a classic spot for a reason.

Just wow - this place truly deserves 5 stars. The ambiance and music is perfect. The waiters are so friendly and the food is mouth watering. It took us a while to get a ressy here so we balled out. Everything was perfect. The carpaccio melted in your mouth. The drinks were delicious and the pasta was cooked to perfection.
Carbone is my all time favorite places to eat in new york. The spicy rigatoni is the star of the show. The deserts and drinks are top tier too.

This experience was way different from our last at Carbone. We first dined here during Covid to see what the hype is all about and it definitely surpassed all our expectations. Quickly became one of our favorite restaurants in NYC. Fast forward a few years and a a lot of dinners/lunch's here and things are trending in the wrong direction. 

As soon as we got there the hospitality and welcome was great. We ordered our food and started to enjoy the delicious perfectly toasted bread and homemade mozzarella. After 20+ minutes still waiting for our 1st course, pastas and meatballs. We got our pastas which were warm and no where near hot. And still waiting for the meatballs. All this time no one checked in on us and no updates were given on our meatballs. Finally got someone to check on it and it finally arrived. My wife noticed right away it was way too tough to cut through with her fork and saw it was raw right away. We checked another meatball and was left disappointed. They were nice enough to return the meatballs for us but this is one of our favorite dishes we look forward to.

Then our veal parm came to close out our lunch and was not the same as we remembered it. This was thankfully hot but the breadcrumbs were falling off and we felt it was  a bit dry. We had this many times and know for a fact this is not how it delivers.

Can't believe we left here sad and not it falls under all hype category.

My expectations for Carbone were high! I mean to get a reservation was HARD, so we called upon AMEX to get us one, secondly Drake is out here rapping about Carbone in his song, so yeah, I was ready to be wowed!

Once we were sat, we were provided complimentary garlic bread, mozzarella cheese and salami, it's possible that this was the best part of our meal, the mozzarella and salami that is, the bread was okay. The mozzarella is soaked in olive oil and is high quality and tasty, the salami is also of good quality, quite frankly I didn't even know I was a salami fan before this. We were off to a great start!

We got the Caesar salad to start, they say they make it tableside, but it's more like off to the side where they can find space due to the small size of the restaurant. I was expecting it to be more of a tableside experience, but it is not intimate like that, nor are you really aware of it being made, which was unfortunate for us to learn. Anyway, the Caesar salad was basic, honestly it was underwhelming, the dressing had nothing going on, the croutons lacked flavor and just overall this was lackluster. 

For our meals we got the meatballs and the spicy rigatoni vodka pasta. The meatballs were okay but again lacked flavor and personality, they were just okay. However, my hubby liked the meatballs better than me, especially paired with the pasta. The pasta was delicious, nicely seasoned and well cooked, however it was not superior like I had built it up to be. Also, the portion size (small) did not match the price. 

For the price, portion size and less than stellar food, I would not go back.

0 stars since I made a reservation 30 days in advance, flew in from Chicago, reservation got canceled due to the rain?? Y'all cooking outside? What is going on. Unacceptable. Chicago would never, even during a blizzard or below freezing temps. BULL.

Yes, reservations were tough to get -- I had to RSVP on the dot of opening for my days in NYC. The only thing decent enough were early dinner reservations in the outdoor patio. With all the hype built up over Carbone NYC -- even with a Carbone in Vegas -- I came in with an open mind.

First off, the free bread basket with salami and pickled cauliflower was good. I was expected the mozzarella included as well, but the waiter said it was only for lunch. I had to pay the extra $10, but it was well worth it to go along with the bread and salami.

For appetizers, we tried the eggplant and beets. Both were excellent, and hearty portions too. At this point, we were getting full. For the main, of course I had to try the spicy rigatoni. Verdict? I loved it. The pasta was al dente, and I kept scooping up the creamy sauce that had just a slight kick. 

Overall, my wife and I had a good experience. That outdoor patio ambiance was fine, and it didn't seem as cramped if I dined inside. Service was efficient. Pricing was on par for NYC dining, so I was fine with it. Happy to knock off this spot on our bookmark list for NYC eats. Plenty of other Italian spots to check out.
Simply the best place in nyc. Service. Food. Atmosphere are all top notch. Cannot say enough good things about this place.

@champagnepapi we actually don't know how it goes when they can't get a reservation at Carbone cause we secured it  

Spicy Vodka Rigatoni 9.42/10- really loved how this was al dente, sauce is creamy but with a tangy hint. Subtle hint of onions in the sauce which gave lots of flavor. However, it was lacking spice and tasted more like Calabrian chilies were used versus dried red pepper flakes. We got 2 portions of this to split. Still very good but I think overrated

Veal Parm 9.58/10- incredibly tender and I loved how it was made with a thin veal cutlet crusted in breadcrumbs and topped with their special sauce. A little dry tbh but the veal meat on the bone was actually fantastic, and very juicy. Cut and served table side 

Cesar Salad 10/10- tbh best salad I've ever tried. It's made and served table side. It is incredibly fresh and I'm not a fan of anchovies, however it added a nice acidic touch to the creamy dressing. The croutons were also so good- I've never had any like it. They reminded  crisp on the outside, light and airy on the inside with a subtle sweet hint. 

Comp App 9.86/10- garlic bread (not pict.), salami, and fresh mozzarella. Truly delicious, everything was very fresh and paired perfectly together. Would order if it was a menu item

Manhattan 2/10- strongest drink on menu, made with rye cherry & cinnamon, it's like taking shots but as an entire drink. 

it's really not that hard to secure a reservation at Carbone. I truly enjoyed the food here (even tho I think it's overrated w/ their reservation system and the hype around it) but the experience even more. Our waiter was incredibly nice and attentive and even felt like a friend throughout our dining experience. Funniest 48 hours of my life. One of the best dining experiences I've ever had, the company made it a million times better too. Food is great however incredibly overpriced esp for portion size. (Ratings don't reflect price taken into consideration) Would def come back but not for a while. They also serve rainbow cookies at the end however I wasn't truly amazed by them.
So much fun!! We really enjoyed the atmosphere. Such an experience! Had the spicy rigatoni, the veal parm and the cheesecake. Great wine list too! Worth the hype.

Five star service
Five star food 
Four star cocktails 

This is just another raving review of one of New York City's hottest Italian restaurants. A group of girlfriends and I went on a Saturday night, pretty last minute thanks to a hook up. Otherwise, I hear it's impossible to get a reservation here. It's also a fairly small restaurant so I can see why bookings go quickly. 

I had already been to Carbone in Miami, so I knew what to expect. We shared a ton of plates so we got to try a little bit of everything. Every single dish was incredible but I have to say the cocktails were underwhelming for how popular this place is. I really wish they got a mixologist to come in and revamp their cocktail menu.

Must try:
- spicy rigatoni, of course 
- lobster ravioli 
- clams platter (I don't eat clams, but these were spectacular)
- table side Caesar salad (although the croutons are a little too hard for my liking)
- truffle corn (just wow, unexpected)

Hear me out... I am Fully aware it is hard to get a reservation here, however this restaurant is where the saying anything worth having is hard to get comes from! When I say everything here is worth all the fuss from the service to the drinks to the food all of it. Even the ambiance dim, great music playing very old New York with that said I highly recommend I don't really know how they get it exactly the same every single time but they have mastered this as I have attended the NY location numerous times as well as the Miami location. The table side Caesar is phenomenal and portion size per cost is reasonable. The fresh mozzarella is and always will be a must for me as it pairs well with the complimentary bread and pickled veggies they bring you once you have been seated the meatballs also pair well with all the above mentioned. I am sure everyone is wondering if the spicy rigatoni lives up to the hype and I am here to assure you it in fact does! Every single time I have ordered this the pasta is perfectly cooked and the sauce is always an immediate delight, smooth, creamy and extremely tasty. A must have for me. Unpopular opinion get the carrot cake and thank me later.

I came on a Wednesday and sat outside. The service was stellar from beginning to end. Roberto really provided a phenomenal experience for me and my party. The food was good, especially the salmon. Great experience overall.
Carbone Restaurant in Thompson St New York,  Beautifully Decoration an amazing italian Food  100%. The Restaurant will transport you to Italia once in side you will for get you are in New York.
Honestly the best pasta I've had in my life Riga vodka. That is all that is need to be said.

I've wanted to come here ever since I read a review, here on Yelp, where a woman favorably compared Carbone to Chef's Table at Brooklyn Fare... That was maybe four years ago, she said the atmosphere was more fun and enjoyable and the food was equally amazing. Needless to say, much has changed in the past four years, and it feels like "the shine has gone..."

There are four rooms, one constructed out front on the sidewalk (A), one up front by the host stand where the bar is located (B), one on the side by the bathrooms (C), and one in the back by the kitchen (D). i had dinner at Carbone twice in the past month, first dinner in D & second dinner in B. Unfortunately both dining experiences in two different seating areas were marred by the same problems, people waiting for tables taking extended photoshoots of themselves and their friends. One couple took extremely bright pictures of themselves for 25 minutes straight, not even kidding. This could be prevented if they didn't overbook. It's very obvious they overbook, so in the front room there were always at least a dozen people waiting at the bar, pushing into the backroom to explore out of curiosity, pushing into the side room to use the bathroom, pushing their way in and out of the front door to go smoke cigarettes. And there are so so so many runners shoving past everybody to deliver plates of food & trays of drinks. It's NOT the luxurious leisurely indulgent decadent experience I wanted. 

The food? I've had the "Rigatoni Carbone" at Parm Vesey & Parm Mulberry & Parm Columbus, and somehow, perplexingly, maddeningly, it was twice as expensive but only half as good at Carbone? Here it had exponentially more onions which made the sauce slimy, and the pasta was overcooked. The Chicken Scarpariello was salty and overcooked, the Octopus was dry and overcooked. My favorite courses were Calamari & the Meatballs, but, sadly, the Meatballs are the only reason I'd ever even bother coming back.

Excellent food. Menu is extensive and seasonal to a particularly high standard. Definitely fine dining. It can be expensive but worth it and they do different deals on different nights so it's worth checking them out before you book. Highly recommended.

We walked by this small, humble, hole in the wall and decided to give it a try ;)

In all honesty, we thought that it lived up to the hype! The restaurant itself was beautifully decorated and rustic, with a bar to wait at before you ordered. Our server was very kind and we actually really enjoyed all of the appetizers--the cheese was to die for!! We also got the table-side Caesar salad, which was delicious--very fresh and flavorful (though you might want to ask for the anchovy on the side, depending on your taste).

Finally--the infamous spicy rigatoni. So so so good--creamy, flavorful, decadent, melt-in-your mouth goodness. The pasta is perfectly al-dente, the optimal vessel for getting more of that delicious sauce in your mouth. A bacchanal for the senses! 

Definitely give it a try if you manage to snag a reservation!

Grabbed a resy last week on a whim, there was a cancellation for Sunday at 12pm and I immediately grabbed it. I couldn't believe it! I set expectations where they should be for any hyped up spot.. low. The service and ambiance was 10/10. Service couldn't have been nicer or more attentive. Food was also very good-  the special just seemed a tad over priced for such a small dish. We started with a Paloma and Mai Thai ($24 each) For lunch they start you with fresh mozzarella/ salami, yum. We also ordered Caesar salad ($32- prepared table side), the white truffle tortellini ($165 lol), and their famous spicy rigatoni ($34) - they also charged $20 for bottled Panna- water? We asked for tap. But all good! They are give you rainbow cookies to end. We didn't order dessert. Overall Carmine our server and the entire team was really nice and made the experience special. Would recommend at-least 1x! Get the salad & spicy rig!!!

Carbone New York, nestled in the heart of the city, is a timeless culinary gem that consistently delivers an extraordinary dining experience. As a dedicated member of the Yelp Elite Squad, I've had the privilege of savoring some of the finest cuisines, and Carbone stands out as a masterclass in Italian-American dining.

From the moment you step into Carbone, you're transported to a bygone era of New York City. The ambiance is reminiscent of a classic Italian restaurant, with the perfect blend of old-world charm and contemporary sophistication. The vintage black-and-white tiles, dimly lit space, and elegant décor set the stage for a memorable meal.

Now, let's talk about the food. Carbone's menu is a culinary journey through the flavors of Italian-American cuisine. The classics are executed to perfection. The Caesar salad, with its crisp romaine, rich dressing, and anchovy, is a work of art. The Spaghetti and Meatballs are a revelation, with pasta that's cooked to perfection and meatballs that melt in your mouth.

But it's the veal parmesan that truly steals the show. The tender, breaded veal cutlet is topped with a rich tomato sauce and melted mozzarella cheese, creating a masterpiece of flavor and texture. It's a dish that brings back the nostalgia of a family Sunday dinner.

The service at Carbone is impeccable, with a staff that exudes professionalism and a genuine passion for what they do. They are attentive, knowledgeable, and ready to guide you through the menu, ensuring that your dining experience is nothing short of extraordinary.

What sets Carbone apart is its dedication to authenticity. The ingredients are of the highest quality, and the recipes are time-honored traditions. It's clear that the culinary team here takes pride in preserving the essence of Italian-American cuisine.

In conclusion, Carbone New York is a culinary destination that defines excellence. From the moment you walk in to the last bite of dessert, it's an experience that lingers in your memory. If you're seeking classic Italian-American dishes in an elegant, nostalgic setting, look no further. Carbone is a shining star in the New York dining scene, and it has earned every one of its five stars.
The service was wonderful including their rigatoni pasta. The service was just wonderful and the place it's self is cute

Very accommodating 
Food was great 
Sat outside it was a nice vibe chandelier candles

The famous Carbone ... had the chance to come here on a Wednesday night. I couldn't believed how small it was. We ordered drinks by the very small crammed bar in the corner. The espresso martinis were delicious. The retro hexagon tiled floors, the old china... the vibe was just that - vintage. As soon as we sat we were greeted with antipasto Parmigiano Reggiano cut straight out of the wheel- amazing, pickled cauliflower, salumi and a bread basket with a variety of breads but the garlic toast had me hooked. We ordered the Caesar salad that came covered in cheese with the most delicious piece of toast. But the star of the show was the carpaccio - no words other than truly amazing! We also had the eggplant and zucchini scapece - also very good. The Bronzino came out a bit overcooked but it was still good. But let's not forget their famous spicy rigatoni- from the very first bite you get the Al dente creamy taste with a spicy kick. No red pepper flakes in sight. It was good but nothing exceptional in my opinion. Our waiter was attentive and provided exceptional service - even using a crumber to clean up. For dessert it was my friends bday and they came out with a tiramisu cake but it seemed like  everyone else was celebrating a birthday too. The waiters sang a happy birthday in Italian out loud for everyone who was celebrating. They came over with a big China egg and sprinkled Jordan almonds on the table and gave us complimentary lemoncello shots. The service was exceptional. Is it worth the hype - in my opinion no. But it was definitely an experience that should be had at least once!

First off- if you're lucky enough to snag a reservation, the food is quite delicious. Amazing bread basket to start with a wide assortment of different types of bread and they provide some salami and cheese as well! We got the eggplant and zucchini scapece for an appetizer which was unexpectedly good- would recommend trying it!

For entrees we of course for the spicy vodka rigatoni (not much to say about this besides it was delicious) and the pork chop and peppers. Dare I say the pork chops were the star of the show? So much flavor, so juicy and a change from the pasta that Carbone is known for. 

Service, as others have pointed out, is not *amazing*. It was perfectly fine, our food came on time, and we were never left waiting for an extended period of time for anything. But it's definitely not over-the-top friendly. So as long as you manage your expectations regarding how friendly people are, everything should be fine!

Carbone lives up to the hype. As many other reviews have stated, it is extremely difficult to get a reservation here and there's a reason for that. We were lucky enough to get dinner reservations at Carbone for our last night in NYC. 

I was a little disappointed when we were seated outside and not in the main restaurant, but it was fun to people watch on the street. Our server was wonderful and described the specials for the night, as well as recommendations for dishes. We were also promptly served a variety of complimentary breads (the focaccia and garlic breads are worth trying from the basket), salami, parmesan, and what we thought was marinated or pickled cauliflower.  

We ordered a bottle of Chianti Classico and started with the Prosciutto & Melon, followed by a half dozen oysters from Massachusetts. The prosciutto and melon was nothing special, but still delicious. The oysters had the toppings prepared on top of each oyster already and while my boyfriend loved them, I felt like the toppings overpowered the oyster flavor a bit. 

This was followed by a special on the menu for the night - burrata with caviar. This was for sure one of the highlights of the night. They were generous with the caviar and our server helped to prepare the dish with salt, olive oil, and chives. The combination of the caviar flavor and texture with the burrata was amazing spread over thinly toasted bread. I am still dreaming about it. 

We split 2 pastas for our main. Of course, we had to go with their notorious spicy rigatoni vodka and we also ordered a special on the menu - tortellini with truffle. The spicy rigatoni vodka lives rent free in my head since that night. It's popular for a reason. Such a simple dish, but the smooth sauce texture and balance of spicy and sweet in the sauce just takes it to another level. The truffle tortellini were also amazing, but isn't anything with freshly shaved truffle on top? 

We ended the night with a dessert recommendation from our server - the carrot cake with ginger ice cream. I'm not a big dessert person, so the balance of the carrot cake with the ginger ice cream was perfect. 

I really with they had a location in LA. But there's no doubt that on our next trip to NYC or Vegas we'll be trying to get a reservation at Carbone again.

One of NYC's most famous restaurant - and the best part is that they use Creekstone meat so it's halal - call the day of just to make sure. Definitely check it out, if you're lucky enough to get a reservation! 

Follow our insta: @nyc.halal for more halal food reviews!!

Not worth it. The food was okay but you can honestly cook it at home. Favorite dish was the clam. Everything else was meh - unlikely to return.

As we entered the hostess was super nice and greeted us with a smile. This day was a special day for my spouse and Carbone made it more special. Our food was just amazing and very flavorful.
