I recommend going.. if you can get a reservation. The food is good but for the hype you'd expect it to be better. I personally recommend Parm. The staff is friendly and attentive, the space in general has a great vibe.

I have been to Carbone so many times despite the fact that it is generally difficult to get a reservation.  I really liked the experience during Covid, however, the experience is not necessarily the same anymore.  If you have to go, I would recommend going there for dinner instead of lunch.  

Assorted baked clams and the spicy rigatoni vodka are 2 of my favorite dishes.  

As soon as you place your order, they will bring out complimentary bread, cheese (mozzarella or Parmesan depending on the time of the day) and salami.  I like the bread covered with tomato sauce and the cauliflower dish served during dinner time.  I tried the veal Parmesan before, but it's a hit or miss as sometimes it would taste so cheesy when the protein's not breaded evenly.  I also had veal Marsala at Carbone, but I am not sure if they still carry it on the menu.  

Overall, the dining area at Carbone NY is smaller in size than Carbone Miami.  I remember the experience to be so much better during Covid times.     As this place is getting more and more popular, it will continue to be hard to secure a reservation.

Carbone has been on my radar for a long time - even though it only opened in 2013, the restaurant has become somewhat of an institution in NYC. This is due to its reputation of serving quality food, celebrity clientele, and development into a franchise under the Major Food Group umbrella. I have a pretty high standard when it comes to Italian food, and even though I've heard rumblings of the restaurant being overhyped, I really wanted to experience Carbone for myself. 

Located in Greenwich Village, Carbone sits in the space that used to be Rocco Restaurant, another Italian spot that had its fair share of notable clientele; the original sign remains with a neon "Carbone" sign superimposed over it. Since the restaurant's opening, the brand has expanded to locations in Vegas and Miami, along with the restaurant's sauce being sold in supermarkets. Known for being a regular spot for celebrities, it's infamously difficult to secure a reservation here. The restaurant utilizes Resy to book tables, and they open daily at 10am, 30 days in advance. Even with this, I feel they hold tables at prime times for their regulars and celebrities. I was on Resy exactly at opening on two separate occasions and the only times I saw available for dinner was 5/530pm and 10:30/11pm. I can eat late, so I snatched a 10:30pm table on a Friday night. 

We arrived a few minutes before our reservation time and were greeted with a packed restaurant; we were told our table wasn't ready yet and were guided to the bar area to wait. The restaurant was very well staffed - there were at least 4 people behind the host stand, lots of people on floor, and multiple runners constantly going back and forth with food. There are four main areas with seating: the outdoor patio, front room immediately upon entry, side room, and a back room. The atmosphere is meant to exude a mid-20th century Italian restaurant feel, and I think they did a good job. Tile floors, splashes of color on the wall, floral accents, candles, white tablecloths, and 50s/60s music playing. It's a fun and lively atmosphere, and I enjoyed people watching while waiting for my table. 

We ended up being seated about 35 minutes past our reservation time - which seems to be a norm based on a few other reviews I read. I liked where we were seated as it was in the side room in a corner so we weren't bothered by a lot of foot traffic. Shortly after seating we were started with a bread basket, soppressata, and giardiniera; there was also a server waking around the dining room with a big wheel of parmesan cutting chunks off for patrons. Everything was tasty; the bread basket contained three types: traditional Italian, focaccia, and garlic bread - I was living my best carb life. The cheese, soppressata, and giardiniera were also great and high quality. 

The menu isn't large, and the cuisine is very no-frills Italian. Multiple social media accounts highlighted certain menu items that were "must haves" - we decided to get some but didn't let that dictate our entire dinner. But first, a drink - I had an old fashioned which was very good. For apps we decided to share three: baked clams, calamari Marco, and the prosciutto with mozzarella. Everything was great - the baked clams were served three ways, and the calamari was fried and topped with a tasty sauce. The mozzarella was first presented in a small bowl of oil and cut by our server into four pieces, then set on the plate of prosciutto and drizzled with the oil. This was delicious - the prosciutto wasn't overly salty, and the mozz was melt in your mouth. The mozz specifically is regularly featured across social media and it's definitely worth ordering. 

For my main, I couldn't resist ordering the spicy rigatoni vodka - if there is one dish that is consistently featured on any promotion for Carbone, it's this one. The pasta was tasty - it was cooked al dente, and the sauce had great flavor. To call it spicy seems a bit of a stretch, but there was a mild delayed heat that came after I was about halfway through the dish. While the pasta was tasty, I wouldn't say it was superior to other vodka dishes I've had at other high-quality Italian restaurants. We also ordered two sides: spicy broccoli rabe and artichoke hearts. Both were great - fresh and seasoned well. We couldn't leave without dessert, and decided to share the lemon cheesecake. This was great, good lemon flavor and not too heavy - one of the best slices of cheesecake I've had in a while. 

Service was excellent - everyone was very welcoming and all the courses were served at a good pace. So where does Carbone land for me? There's no doubt that the food is good - it's as good as other great Italian restaurants I've been to. The prices, though, are inflated; I don't necessarily think the quality matches the bill. What you're paying for is the experience and the service - and in that case Carbone delivers. Overall I had a great time, and am glad to have finally made it here.

I don't know where to begin. Carbone was outstanding! The first thing that came out was the bread, which I will be dreaming about because of how good it was. Along with the parmesan cheese & cauliflower salad, and salami, All tasted so fresh. For appetizers, we got the Caesar salad and the fresh mozzarella, and it was delicious. Then, for the entrees, we got the spicy rigatoni vodka, which tasted great, plus the meatballs. As for dessert, we got the chocolate cake and wow, that tasted amazing! But above all, the atmosphere was terrific, the service and the staff were lovely and accommodating. I can't wait to come back here again!

Came for lunch. The food was really good. Service was great. Pasta was delicious. Clams were the best thing we had, might just be the best clams I've ever had. Bill was 300 with tip and no alcohol. 34 dollars for a bottle of sparkling water and two espressos is a bit outrageous, but you pay for the name I suppose.
Beautiful ambiance, delicious food and excellent service. It was everything I hoped and expected it to be!

I was somewhat skeptical to dine here given some of the recent reviews, but pleasantly surprised that we enjoyed Carbone.  The foods were good to excellent but it was the service and ambiance that truly made it special for us.  The spicy rigatoni was spot on but the mushroom pasta was average.  The veal parmigiana was excellent and the clam appetizer was as well.  The squash was very good and the fresh mozzarella with salami was excellent.  Expensive?  Indeed, but worth it we thought

My wife and I made a reservation through the Amex concierge 2 months in advance-- however, reservations open 30 days in advance so we had to wait for confirmation. 

Upon arrival you see the type of service you will experience. They have a what looked like an uber- jacked, New York raised body guard manning the door. Exclusive. 

You walk into what I can only imagine walking into an authentic Italian home feels like. The space was very dim lit giving a warm atmosphere. 

They start you off with some complementary aged parmesan, salami, and a bread basket. We ordered a big Caesar salad to share. They offer anchovies on the Caesar, we respectively declined. The salad is prepared in front of you and the big croutons stood out as a nice touch. A note to add is the Caesar dressing did have a little kick to it but in a good way. 

For the entree I ordered the lobster ravioli and my wife ordered the spicy rigatoni. I thought my ravioli was delicious until I tried the rigatoni. I did not order the entire menu but I would find it hard to believe that there is anything on the menu that could have tasted better than the rigatoni. 

For dessert we had a hazelnut chocolate cake. I don't believe I remember seeing a crumb left when we were finished. 

I was hesitant to eat at Carbone as people on social media say it's overrated and only hyped up because of the exclusivity. However, after taking in the experience and food myself I found it quite delightful and worth the effort to get a reservation. 

The only thing that kept me from rating this 5 stars is the cost outweighs the overall experience.

Carbone is one of those places that you have to go to. It is hard to get a good reservation but if you do... you go. The food is awesome and lives up to the hype. The ambiance is solid too. I think sitting in the back is better. The meatballs were a beautiful starter. The beets were also underrated. The veal parmesan is a must order and probably the best I have had. The porkchop was just ok so I probably wouldn't reorder. The broccoli rabe was delicious. The cheesecake and hazelnut desserts were lovely.  One of my new fav's in nyc.
Lived up to the hype food and service is amazing. Feels like a old school Italian restaurant vibe ambiance is amazing

Besides eating the incredible food that Carbone is famous for, dining there was hands down one of the most memorable hospitality experiences I've had (& I worked at the Ritz Carlton). A big shout out to Bellini for providing a WOW experience. He not only routinely checked up on our table with a friendly, fun and attentive spirit, he also made sure his entire team welcomed us. Every interaction with the staff was so incredibly personable and made us feel like family! Thank you!

Came back to Carbone the week of Thanksgiving and it was just as good as our previous visits. I legitimately cannot get over how good the spicy rigatoni is, absolutely unreal. The service was wonderful and the playlist is always such a vibe. Devastated that they chose to open a location in Dallas instead of Houston but absence only makes the heart grow fonder.

One of the best restaurant experiences I've had. Our server was a consummate professional and handled everything with the utmost care and attention to detail. Every dish seemed to top the other. We had a special occasion to celebrate and were treated with impeccable service and hospitality. I really didn't want to leave. Thank you, Carbone!

Great food every time I come. A bit pricey but it's always a fun experience going. One of the waiters is incredibly charming. If you like carrot cake, I recommend getting it here!! also the meatballs are always banging. Once the older male host was a bit rude but I think that's the only bad experience I've had here.

Hands-down, one of the best Italian restaurants. from the bread that they serve you with the cheese and the pasta it was all amazing. Make sure you get reservations in advance. Definitely worth the wait.

This place is a cute, quaint restaurant near Bleecker Street. It gives very much upscale dining. We started with espresso martinis. This was the best I've ever had. They used grey goose which made it go down pretty smooth. The espresso was just right. It was sweet enough to cut the bitterness. We got the table side ceasar salad. It was garlicky and cheesy. The croutons were hard but soft. A plus is you can get it without anchovies if you want. The leaves for bigger but the lettuce was clearly very fresh and it has a nice subtle flavor. It was so good. We got the spicy rigs. O. M. G. it is worth the hype. The noodles were cooked al dente (aka perfection). The portion looked small but it was just enough. The sauce had a nice balance of sweet and spicy. It has some cheese in it too. I wanted more but if I got more I would have been too full. The garlic bread with fresh mozz and salami was great. The salami was kind of on the saltier side but still good because it was soft. We got the lemon cheesecake and WHAT!!!! the lemon flavor was there but not overpowering. The crust was buttery but still had texture. Also the service was IMPECCABLE. The waiter had so many opinions and recommendations to help guide you.

I definitely knew this place would be slightly overhyped, but I do think it's worth a try if you're in the area. We had a lunch reservation & got the vodka pasta, fettuccine with mushrooms, broccoli rabe & tiramisu.
I must say the bread & mozzarella to start with was incredible, loved the warm & fresh cheese. The vodka pasta was also great! Definitely had some spice. Fettuccine tasted very fresh & I loved the thinly sliced mushrooms. The broccoli rabe felt short, there was so flavor & definitely 0 spice. Tiramisu tasted homemade & was a generous size. 
Resy require you to pay $50 per person to reserve, which gets deducted from the check.
I probably won't be back because I do think there's no shortage of a good Italian spot in the city, but Carbone does have a unique vibe & ambience!

The best dining experience I have ever had. I was able to score this reservation based off a notification list on resy. The food was amazing. My favorite was the meatballs. The marinara sauce was savory. The ambiance was so peaceful and decorated for Christmas. Our waiter was super nice and helpful and even offered to take a picture of my boyfriend and I outside the restaurant at the end! I can't wait to go back!

A Mixed Bag of Flavors and Experiences

Curiosity led me to Carbone, eager to unravel the mysteries behind its acclaimed reputation and the notorious difficulty of securing reservations. Continuing my birthday celebration, my best friend and I opted for an early lunch, and the adventure began.

Initially slotted for the Amex outdoor area, I mustered the courage to ask the front desk if an indoor switch was possible, and to my delight, they accommodated the request. A promising start!

Now, let's delve into the culinary journey. The Caesar salad arrived, but unfortunately, it left me yearning for more. Heavy on the dressing, it missed the mark for my taste. The bread, though, was a saving grace, though I found myself wishing for a more generous portion. Word to the wise: dinner might boast a different bread spread.

Our main courses diverged in success. My brave choice, the spicy rigatoni, proved to be a bit too much for my non-spicy palate, leading to a somewhat disappointing experience. On the other hand, my friend's lobster ravioli was a masterpiece, earning rave reviews. The meatball wasn't that great, didn't leave much to be desired.

Service, however, was the true standout. Impeccable doesn't even begin to describe it. The staff's attentiveness and friendliness elevated the dining experience, turning a potentially mixed meal into an enjoyable event.

While my first foray into Carbone left me with a spicy dilemma, I'm not one to give up easily. I'll be back to explore a different dish that aligns better with my taste buds. The impeccable service alone is reason enough to warrant a return visit. Cheers to the journey of flavors at Carbone!

Who says the best stories start with, "We arrived on time and everything went according to plan"? Not us! Our Carbone adventure began at 1:56 PM, four minutes away from a "Sorry, folks, kitchen's closed" situation. We were those audacious diners, and Carbone not only welcomed us with open arms but also found us a cozy spot faster than you can say "spicy rigatoni"!

Our maestro of the day, Blake, deserves a standing ovation. The man is a zen master of service, handling our chronically tardy selves with the patience of a saint. If Blake were a superhero, his superpower would be turning every meal into an epic saga without ever making us feel like the clock was ticking.

Now, let's talk about those espresso martinis. Are we sure they weren't brewed with liquid gold? We've collectively sipped through thousands of these bad boys, and Carbone's version left us wondering if we've been drinking coffee-flavored water all this time. The espresso martinis were like a symphony for our taste buds--rich, bold, and utterly unforgettable.

The carpaccio waltzed onto our table, showing off like it just won a culinary beauty pageant. Tender, flavorful, and served with an attitude that said, "I'm not your average appetizer." And oh, the spicy rigatoni! We split two plates, but the flavor was so explosive; it felt like we each had a personal firework show in our mouths. The Caesar salad tried to be the unsung hero, but let's be real--when spicy rigatoni's in the room, everyone else is just background noise.

For the grand finale, the lemon cheesecake took center stage. It was like a lemony dream that left us questioning why we ever settled for regular cheesecake in the first place. Carbone, you've officially ruined us for all other desserts.

Now, some misguided souls might call this place overrated. To them, we say, "Have you tried the espresso martinis, carpaccio, spicy rigatoni, and lemon cheesecake?" Exactly. Carbone, you're not overrated; you're underrated if anything. A must-visit for anyone who enjoys bending time, taste buds, and the rules of restaurant punctuality!

We had a 11:30PM reservation. We were sat in the back room and it was still lively and busy on a Tuesday night. They gave us bread + butter, pickled veggies and sliced cured meat to start - remember to save room for your actual order! I was getting full just eating that and drinking my cocktails. The service was great and attentive. We enjoyed everything that we ordered. However, the one item I could do without was the Jumbo Shrimp Scampi- wasn't that flavorful and it was chewy. It's hard to get reservations but it's definitely worth trying. I loved the Caesar salad and the Spicy Rigatoni Vodka! I wanted to try the desserts but was too full and only ordered a scoop each of coffee and vanilla ice cream to share.

What can I say? It's Carbone. At this quaint (and quite famous) spot, the staff makes you feel right at home while singing along to Frank Sinatra, dancing by with delectable Italian dishes all the while serving you with a smile. The rigatoni is heavenly and the lobster ravioli was served with massive juicy chunks of lobster - need I say more? If you can catch a reservation here, you'll leave full and satisfied.

We had finally scored reservations through American Express Concierge 60 days out from our go date. Our reservation confirmation came 30 days after. When we arrived we were greeted by the doorman who ushered us inside. The atmosphere was   very upbeat with a dimly lit room giving it a warm vibe. Carbone offers complementary aged parmesan cheese, a beautifully presented salami platter, and a warm bread basket. Everything was perfect. I had to see what the hype was over the spicy rigatoni so that was at the top of my ticket. I also couldn't pass up an order of the meatballs. The spicy rigatoni was delicious. I like spicy foods so it definitely struck my fancy but others might be turned off by it. The meatballs were also extremely tasty. They were so juicy and flavorful. The true home run was the services. OUTSTANDING! If you can score reservations...GO!

We had a friend scour the internet for a friends meal here. A month in advanced we were able to get a Tuesday lunch reservation at 12:15. I have never been here so I was ready for the experience. My 3 friends had all been here before! The place is much smaller on the inside than you would have thought. There was also seating outside which I didn't realize. We got a nice table inside to the left. 

I forgot to photograph the Caesar salad we got and also the clams. They were both excellent. We also got the meatballs. And my friends all got the spicy rigatoni I got the tortellini Ragu. Spicy is always too much for me. They did the say they could do it without the red pepper flakes which would have been ok. We didn't get any dessert because we were nearing our 2 hour dining limit and we were already so so full. 
Overall excellent

Now I was a bit hesitant to come to Carbone, I had heard  amazing things but I wondered if it was all hype. Luckily I was fortunate enough to secure a reservation via Resy and was excited to join them for dinner. I was celebrating an anniversary with my fiancé and wanted to take her somewhere nice in NYC. The service was absolutely spectacular, our server had us seated immoderately upon our  arrival, he was knowledgeable, and made suggestions on to what offerings we should try. The ambiance was very welcoming, the dinning room was well lite but still had the small mom and pop feel. There was music playing in the background but in an subtle low volume that you could actually have a consecration with the other members of your party. An upscale feel while retaining the privacy and intimacy of a smaller establishment which truly makes for a unique experience. The food was absolutely delicious, the spicy rigatoni was the mouthwatering. The Chicken Scarpariello was undoubtedly the star of the show with the tomato sauce, sausage, mushrooms, and chicken blending perfectly to produce an avalanche of flavor. The Squash Agrodulce perfectly complemented the chicken and was sweat, soft, and light seasoned. For desert we had the Lemon Cheesecake which was sweat, fresh, and effortless melted in your mouth. My advice to anyone who is interested in dinning at Carbone, secure your reservation with time they release them a month in advance. That said, the experience is well worth the reservation hassle and I cannot wait to return.

Carbone is good. We've been to the Miami location and now we were able to get a 11:45am reservation in NYC. Is it the kind of food I want to be eating before noon? Not really, but begers can't be choosers.

The servers were very kind - they didn't seem annoyed we weren't drinking which can happen at places like this. 

The spicy rigatoni is always great. The meatballs are good but very FATTY. The complimentary meats and cheese are good. My brother got the chicken dish and the sausage that came with it seemed very just, not homemade. Chicken was juicy and good.

Table side Ceaser was fresh and great but it's not a huge portion for the price.

It's worth trying, but I would recommend going for dinner and honestly, the location in Miami was prettier.

Good food, EXCELLENT service, small menu, won't frequent but would recommend if you're looking for an iconic meal.

This place lives up to the hype. This was my first time dining at Carbone and man it did not disappoint.  The eggplant scapece was the best tasting eggplant i've ever had (and ive had a lot of eggplant). The spicy rigs also did not disappoint. So creamy and flavorful. Also, the service was incredible. The waitstaff was so on top of everything!

Way too overpriced and way too over hyped. I just don't see why people like this place so much. The ambiance is great but wow I truly don't know how people pay so much for basic pasta and for food that isn't even that great. Would never return again.
Old school charm with excellent service. The spicy rigatoni lived up to its hype. It was a great experience from start to finish.

I've seen several people say the carbone food is overhyped but worth going once for the experience. Maybe it was because I went in with lower expectations, but I thought everything from the food to the service was incredible. From the minute you walk in there's a sense of fine dining and the ambiance is very warm. 

I got a reservation for 2 people during the holiday season. When we arrived we were immediately taken to our table and given complimentary bread, cheese and meat. I ordered an espresso martini which I thought was delicious. Our server was so attentive and friendly which really elevated our experience. I ordered the famous spicy rigatoni and my fiancé ordered the lobster ravioli. Both dishes were delicious and really uniquely made in my opinion. We wanted to order one spicy rigatoni to go and our server said they don't do takeout orders, but he was kind enough to pack the extra dish for us which was very thoughtful. Before dessert they gave us two rainbow cookies after our meals which were very good too. Finally for dessert they bring a whole table of their options to let you see each dessert in person before choosing. Honestly all of the options sounded great but we went with the Nutella tiramisu and it truly was one of the best tiramisus I've had. 

From the service to the food I really think each aspect of our time at carbone was great. If it wasn't so hard to get a reservation I could see us trying to come again.

We were visiting New York for the weekend and  somehow managed to get lunch reservations here. Carbone is such a classic spot and definitely a place you want to visit at least once in your life. The spicy vodka rigatoni lives up to the hype and is truly what dreams are made of. The ambiance and service is lovely - overall, we had a very nice experience!

I've only ever been able to get a lunch reservation at this OG Carbone, and whenever I've gone the restaurant is 80% empty. Very confusing. Anyway the spicy rigatoni and the Caesar salad what I always get. I've tried various other things but always return to those two. With the free apps and dessert, I'm always stuffed. If it's dover sole and truffle season, ask if they're offering the truffle add-on. They charge something ridiculous, but dover sole plus truffle is *chef's kiss*!

Simply put, average quality does not match the obscene prices. Spicy rigatoni was one dimensional, we get it it's slightly spicy but that's really all it was. Meatballs and veal parm flavorless and salty. However, this may have been the best complementary food I've ever been served. The bread was delicious and came with salami and a piece of parmesan.

Underwhelming pasta. Got the spicy rigatoni but there was negative spice. I would recommended people stay way from pasta and just try the starters and proteins. I also got the eggplant & zucchini scapece and I would say it was one of the best things on the menu. Staff were very friendly and attentive.
Duh. A must. Even if you aren't a fan of spicy food- get the spicy rigatoni vodka and thank me later. Service was great, vibes so good, it's a classic for a reason.

Beautiful restaurant. Incredible staff. Delicious food.

I went to Carbone for the first time the other day for lunch and was not disappointed!

After adding a bunch of waitlist spots to carbone via resy i finally snagged a lunchtime reservation! 

immediately upon walking in i thought the decor and overall aesthetic was so charmingg - was giving old time italian old new york vibes. very cozy too - loved it. 

in terms of food they started us with the mozzarella, garlic bread, and prosciutto. great starters and all super delicious. we started with the table side caesar salad which was so savory, crunchy, and actually filling. a very well made caesar salad! 

for pastas we got the spicy rigatoni- probably my fav dish. def one of the best spicy rigatonis ive ever had - definitely order this if you come. we also ordered lobster ravioli and linguini which i will say i didnt care for as much - we all wished we had ordered the spicy rigatoni lolol. 

for dessert we got tiramisu and cheesecake. the tiramisu had a very strong coffee flavor for coffee lovers youd love this. the cheesecake was very authentic and a classic cheesecake i loved it and recommend. had a slight lemon flavor. 

i def would come back and def recommend trying to get a reservation!!!

We got saturday night reservations and seated in the Amex outside heated patio which was nice and warm despite cold weather. The area is small but so is the actual indoor restaurant however it felt intimate and nice. The mozzarella was amazing and our favorite thing were the baked clams! The spicy rigatoni was good and it definitely has a spicy kick to it so if you're not into heat I'd skip out on it. Overall good experience
Food. Service. Atmosphere. All A+. There's a reason this is one of the toughest tables to get in NYC. Not cheap, but so worth it when celebrating a special occasion.
The spicy rigatoni is amazing, expensive but amazing. I do think they need more options for vegetarians. If you can get a reservation you must try

Other than its household name because of the celebrity attendance and difficultly to get a Resy...
 
The pasta is good but there are better options in my opinion in the city.

Go to is the Spicy Rigatoni Vodka and the carrot cake is fire!!!

Solid eats but I think the hype is slightly overrated for what it is. Can also find carbone in Las Vegas and Miami!

I've heard of Carbone for years, and I was finally able to get a reservation during covid. It's now very hard again. Since I went a few years ago, my memory is a bit hazy; however, I do remember that the free mozzarella and sopressata was the best I've ever had. I usually try to get good quality mozzarella and soppressata since I do a lot of cheese and charcuterie, but this was truly exceptional. The pasta alla vodka was excellent as expected, though I felt that it was a bit pricy for the portion and given that it has no meat. I've since been able to find a copycat recipe online that I can make which is pretty easy and similar. I thought the veal was okay and nothing else particularly stood out (since I can't even remember what else we got). The vodka sauce definitely stood out and inspired me to make it. If you're not able to cook fresh pasta on your own, then I would recommend Carbone for a solid Italian meal.

This place is amazing. The staff was attentive and communicated with us about food allergies prior to ordering. My son has an allergy to tree nuts and the restaurant was honest and accommodating. Our server was top notch and very knowledgeable on the menu. Water cup never went unfilled! The staff is excellent! 
The ambience of the restaurant was dark, but in a good way, felt very private to your own party. However it was a bit difficult to read the menu, but no need to read with such knowledge staff with their recommendations. There were many well dressed people, not certain if there is a dress code. My family  seemed to be more than fine in casual wear. The music was oldies that fit just perfect with the feel of the restaurant.
The appetizers were off the charts delicious but be careful not to consume too much.
We ordered family style, having to 2 servings of each dish we ordered. 3 pasta plates was plenty enough for 7 total (5 adults, 2 kids) to share. They also have meal options for the kids. 
Overall great experience!!!!! Can't wait to return.

Amazing dining experience with the most amazing staff and service. First time here and definitely worth the hype. Perfect size dishes for sharing and for ordering a bunch of different items from the menu. Table side fresh mozzarella and bread when you sit down. Dark, cozy ambiance but amazing italian vibes. Hard to get a restaurant but if you're able to, I definitely recommend!

Classic Cesar Salad was delicious 
Spicy Rigatoni was the absolute best thing I had. I don't like spicy food but this was out of this world.

Over-hyped food, crazy expensive for what it is and you have 1.5 hrs for your "reservation" If they sense you are trying to take it slow and enjoy your time, they will rush you along even more. A $32 Cesar with warm plates? Come on...
Our server was a phony jerk, who when we told him we felt rushed said "that's just our steps of service" FAIL. Yucky all around.

the caesar salad ... I still dream of it! made fresh, table side with a tangy house made dressing and the crunchiest, tastiest croutons you'll ever have. the spicy rigatoni is a staple dish and truly delicious. we paired it with the chicken entree, as well. highly recommend if you're able to get a reservation for a guaranteed exceptional dinner.

I had high expectations of Carbone, and I was not disappointed. If you love Italian food, you must plan far in advance to come here. Reservations are required and they open up 30 days in advance, so be sure to go online and book it, because time slots fill up fast. 

The atmosphere feels old school with wood panel walls, and interesting art. The waiter was very thorough going through the menu. They provide complimentary bread, salami, and mozzarella cheese. The mozzarella cheese is incredible. Just melts in your mouth. The bread is okay, a bit on the crispy side. For our appetizer, we had the prosciutto and mozzarella which was terrific. The touch of olive oil was great. For our main dishes, we shared the gluten free spicy rigatoni vodka and the feteccine con Funghi. The spicy rigatoni vodka is their famous dish and understandably so. Definitely has a kick, but not over the top. Even though the pasta was gluten free, not sure I could tell the difference.

A wonderful experience that I would definitely recommend to anyone that like Italian food.

FANTASTIC!

As a bad-wagon hater, I truly wanted to dislike Carbone, but I was so off (thankfully!) 

Getting reservations was one of the most difficult things to go given is popularity and how everything is online. Its also impossible to speak to anyone on the phone.  However, the miracle occurred on my fiance's persistence on the Resy app.  

We went for lunch and unfortunately were unable to sit inside, so were sat in the covered outside seating area.

From the host to the waiters every single person was so kind, professional, and filled with such poise and grace. 

Upon eating, you are given freshy crispy garlic/cheese bread, prosciutto (?) and mozzarella in olive oil. We are not pork eaters, so we returned the dish, and enjoyed the others.

Entrees are family style and here were our selections:  Spicy Rigatoni vodka 1000/5, delicious pasta in a spicy vodka sauce. The sauce was creamy yet not too thick. Squash Agrodolce 1000/5 (my personal fav), was oven baked (?) squash that had tones of salty-sweet like salted cinnamon topped with creme and pumpkin seeds. Soft and decadent. The Chicken Scarpariello (not pictured, sorry) 1000/5 was chicken in sauce with peppers and small sausage bites. 

We then ordered our dessert, but while we waited we were brought almond cookie/cakes - I wasnt a fan, but im biased because ive never liked almond treats of this kind.  

Our dessert was the Lemon cheesecake which was fresh, smooth yet refreshing. 

When I return to NY, I will visit again. But since I live in Miami, ill try my best to explore the one here.

Of course I had to try nyc quintessential italian restaurant, and I'm glad I tried it. It is an experience worth going and trying once.

Reservation: this place is easier to get lunch reservations on a weekday. I stategically planned this place a month in advance when I knew I was off from work on a weekday. Note that you have to spend $50 pp minimum as they take it as a deposit when making the reservation. 

Service was great, servers were attentive. No complaints here.

Food: 
Spicy rigatoni vodka lives up to the hype! It was saucy, the perfect amount of al dente, and flavorful. i liked how different it tastes from other vodka pastas I have had, and this one is pretty solid- wouldn't say it was spicy, just a hint of chili flakes. This dish isn't life changing by any means but is a delicious choice.

Everything else was just alright such as the tortellini and Mario's meatballs. Those dishes can be easily replicated by other italian restaurants.

I'm glad I tried the rigatoni, but would probably only order that if I were to return. Maybe try the other pastas too. But for me, this place isn't a priority.
Everything was fantastic and delicious. Attentive service, and the manager did the best he could, but overall the decor was lovely and I will continue to return.

Food was amazing, but unfinishable. There was just too much of it and the breads, burrata, and salami at the start are dangerously good and filling. We ordered a few different dishes and I tried all of them. All top notch. Service was also excellent. Rarely would I remove a star for such a great meal, however we were seated in the little outdoor section - perhaps cause it was booked through Amex though I'm not sure - and frankly if you're spending that kind of money, it's much nicer to be in the actual restaurant. Would go back, but would call to make sure we're not in the outside section.

My friends told me about this a long time ago about how difficult to get a reservation. I love pasta and wanted to check availability for next month but saw same day dinner availability so pulled the trigger. Amex card can also help you make reservation. 

We were the first party and everyone was ready to greet us. Didnt ask about checking coat though. Overall the service was excellent you dont need to ask things aka splitting a dish onto two plates filling up water etc. 

I loved the free garlic bread and free macaroon dessert at the end lol. To be honest, give  such high hope and ultra rare reservations, the food were not jaw dropping good its really average especially given the price point. I can tell a lot people who comes here are either rich regulars or tourists that wants to check off this from their list. I would give 7/10 for food and 9/10 for service. 

Would I come back or try very hard for a reservation? Probably most likely no, unless its free lol.  I still encourage you to try it here and see /taste it, you might find a complete experience than me.

Amazing classic Italian.   Excellent service.   Lunch is my favorite. I recommend- Cesar salad, meatballs, spicy rigatoni (lives up to the hype), veal parm, and steak is good as well. Didn't love the chicken scarp but might have been too full at that point.

All hype.  Mediocre food served by people who don't know the menu and can't understand English.   I know it's all about the bottom line, but the level of expectation didn't include wrestling with waiters in lounge lizard suits to get our order correct.   If it wasn't for the location and atmosphere not sure anyone would be talking about this place.  Total disappointment.
Amazing , the food lives up to the hype. The meatballs weren't as tasty but everything else was delicious!

Iconic or overhyped?

Here's our honest review: although we enjoyed our meal and loved the presentation of our food and the overall vibe.. we've had better Italian food at a better price point. 

Service was great, our waitress was very sweet and helpful.

Worth to try atleast once if you can manage to snag a resy. 

Complimentary starters:
 garlic bread
 fresh mozzarella 
meats

What we ordered:
 Caesar salad - yummy
 assorted baked clams - nothing special 
 spicy rigatoni vodka - yummy but has better
 whole branzino - parts of the skin was burnt
Ok- I came here and the food was excellent. Down with the naysayers and haters who don't want to 'ride the bandwagon'. We had the spicy ravioli, pork chops, calamari and steak and it was excellent.
Food was overrated for how hard it was to get a reservation - lobster ravioli tasted like $10 shrimp dumplings you can get in chinatown...

Food was amazing !!!! Sooooo Gooood The staff was very friendly and attentive the place was very old school style My new favorite spot to go to will recommend everyone to try and dine again and again i cant wait to come back a 10/10
EXCELLENT!!!!!!  Everything was perfect !!!!  Can't wait to try again!     Each dish was better than the next!! Service was terrific!!

This was my first time visiting Carbone while on a girls trip in NYC and I'm already planning another trip to go again! Firstly, our server Daniel was fantastic. He made the perfect recommendations, kept us laughing, and made us feel so welcome. 10/10 service. My favorite dishes were the tortellini and the potatoes Louie, however I wouldn't order the house chopped or broccoli rabe again. The spicy rigatoni was really good and not too spicy; less than a hot Cheeto for reference. The cheesecake was great, especially if you love a lemon curd. The ambiance was comfortable and intimate. Over 5 stars and will be back!

OMG. Okay so where do I even start? I've been tryingggggg to get reservations for years, at least 8 years. For my birthday, I was able to score reservations at the NYC location. Honestly, it was movie-esq, extremely cinematic. I felt like I teleported to a Robert Dinero movie set. #MobbWives Aesthetic completely done and done a proper fur included. The staff, friendly and warm, completely charming. The food, chefs kiss. The spicy rigatoni was completely from out of my dreams. Superb! I would go back just for the rigatoni. I also had the veal parmesan, ribeye diana, and the squash agrodolce! I didn't care for the steak's brown sauce, next time I'd get it plain, the texture of the steak and squash will literally melt in your mouth! The veal 10/10, squash--so goood 10/10. The rigatoni 1000/10!!!!
Food was really good it's worth the hype. Staff were pleasant and professional and the ambiance is nice & intimate. It was a perfect date night.

This review pains me.  I've wanted to try Carbone for years.   I ate at the original Torrisi years ago and enjoyed my meal but I have never loved Parm so maybe that should have been a warning.

Carbone is good don't get me wrong it is 3 stars because it is too expensive, portions are too small and it's just too hard to get into to warrant the hype.

We started off with the eggplant and zucchini and a caesar salad.   The eggplant was the biggest surprise of the meal.  It was cool and lightly spicy.  Very good.

The caesar was disappointing.  It was good but needed a little more dressing.  The croutons were amazing.

Next we had the spicy rigatoni.  It was good but definitely not the best thing ever.  I found it a little too sweet.  My biggest gripe was the portion is just too small.

In addition to the pasta we went with the meatballs.  These were some great meatballs.  No complaints and some of the best I've had.

Last we got the veal parm.  I have always preferred chicken to veal parm.  I liked the veal but for $92 I could never justify ordering it again.

The service was good.  The espresso martini was great.
Hard work to get and make this reservation but was worth it and vibes, food, everything was perfect! rigatoni actually was spicier which I LOVED and pasta was cooked well too

Coming here always feels a little lame, but I think anyone who says the food is overrated is just wrong. 

The lobster ravioli is way too good. Better than the spicy rigatoni, which unfortunately still slaps. The pasta is cooked so perfectly I really don't quite understand how they achieve it. 

It's expensive, but you also get a ton of bread and cheese and meats at the start and little Italian cookies at the end. All of which are delish. 

If you block out the terrible crowd that this place seems to draw, and manage to snag a table indoors, it's a a fairly enjoyable experience.

Also saw recently that they stuck SELENA GOMEZ in their OUTDOOR seating which tbh is iconic behavior on their part.
Eddie the captain and Gabrielle the Somm made the experience. Incredible - no other words can describe it. Food, service and ambiance 10/10.

What a dream of a restaurant. It was definitely on my bucket list to dine here. The reservations are booked wayyyy in advance so I set reminders/alarms/calendar events to make sure we got the reservation and lo and behold, we did it! The service was impeccable, the ambiance was beautiful and romantic, and the cherry on top was the Caesar salad being made table side. I make spicy vodka pasta at home and I knew I wanted to try what Carbone was known for. Everything was delicious! Can't wait to go back.

This is for the 1% most famous dish is pasta with spicy souce ppl go to meet each other then it works but if u go for the food paying 3-400 for stuff u get any pizzeria firgetabouit if u go to see famous ppl definitely worth it veal 93$ ha it's x7 price

Definitely a scene. The food was good, but the only outstanding memorable dish for me was the spicy rigatoni. 

The atmosphere is the definition of old New York. It's definitely a must- go experience in NY at least once if you can get in. 

We definitely saw a celebrity when we were here (totally blanking on their name at the moment), so that was cool. I think that's pretty common here. 

We did have to dine at 10pm because that was the only available resy we could get for 6, but it was worth the memory. 

The service also is stand out and makes this place memorable. 

Is it my favorite Italian in the city? No. But would I go again if someone invited me to their res? Yes!

The service was great. The spicy pasta that everyone raves was very over rated. I would no come back here, everything was ok nothing was great and for the place to be so hard to get into it's definitely not worth it.
The food was great but what really made our visit memorable was our server Roberto G. Thanks again for everything Roberto!
The food and service is always consist.  The staff is attentive and prompt.  The overall experience is top tier

Truthfully more like 3.5 stars, but rounding up because the great service made up for the mediocre food. I had high expectations for the NYC classic because it's so hyped up and figured it was nearly impossible to get a reservation for a reason! 

The iconic Caesar salad was good- gigantic croutons were great. Assorted baked clams were also good, a little on the salty side but still yum. The iconic spicy rigatoni vodka was just subpar at best. I can handle my spicy food but I found that the sauce was too spicy for a pasta sauce and overpowered the vodka sauce flavors! The pasta was perfectly al dente though, i'll give it that. Mario's meatballs were good until they were too salty after the second bite. We also had their daily special- a tagliatelle with black summer truffle. This was our favorite dish!!! which is a bit sad to say because I expected their classics to be better. 

Overall, glad to say I've tried it but i would not bend over backwards for a resy.

Everything was so incredible from the food to the service. We had a 5:00pm reservation for 2 and we were pretty much the first ones in the restaurant. We were seated in the heated patio and immediately the servers were super welcoming towards us. They were super charismatic and patient with us as it was our first time, offering their recommendations through the dinner and check in on us multiple times. 

Food wise, they started us off with free bread and it also came with salami, pickled cauliflower, and Parmesan - a huuuge spread. We also ordered the octopus to start and this was FIRE, probably my favorite course of the dinner. Then for the main of course we had to get the spicy rigatoni as well as the meatballs. This was super yummy and a hearty portion. We saved room for dessert of course and had to go with our waiter Steven's recommendation, the chocolate hazelnut cake. Steven was right about this one - it was super yummy.

Overall, very impressed all around and would definitely come back again if I can get a reservation!

Every dish was so amazing and delicious wow. This place definitely lived up to its hype Our waiter was super nice and patient. We sat in their outdoor heated patio which was super nice and actually preferred bc it's a lot quieter and intimate! Was a little disappointed that they didn't make our Caesar salad Tableside tho.

The food and ambience were good but I don't think it is worth the price. I think there is more hype behind the restaurant due to the name but don't think it is fully deserved. Portions are small for the price you pay. Overall good food but I wouldn't go again.

All around perfect on some drake shi fr

psa take the matches theyre free and cute to have

Say what you will. 
In my opinion.. 
The food is delicious, the service is impeccable, wine list is good, the interior ambience makes you feel like you're in an old skool mob flick. 
Dining behind us one night  was A$ap Rocky, I mean cmon. 
Before Dorsia you really had to try and put in work to get a reservation. But all that has changed, Been 3 times now and I will always recommend consistency is never an issue. 
I've yet to try Torrisi but I hear good things. Major food group has some of the best & hottest spots in the city that is guaranteed.

Bucket list item checked off and completely exceeded all expectations. Our server Roberto was amazing and made us feel like family and like we were at home. Michael was the gentlemen who welcomed us and he was the sweetest and knew we were in the right place as soon as we got there. We sat in the "outside seating" but didn't feel outside at all. He had the best recommendations and treated our friend's birthday like one of his own. Could not recommend Roberto, Michael, or this place more!

Boy oh boy. I've been wanting to come here with my partner for many months as we wanted to come try this place for our pasta craving appetites. We managed to snag a table outside by spamming the Resy Notifications and staying chronically online for my emails and I finally snagged a table. It was in the AMEX patio which I found to be even more romantic than the inside??? I thought I wouldn't have enjoyed the patio since many people said there wasn't that much room but I thought there was enough room to breathe and maybe even stretch out your arms so I'm happy with the space. There's even windows so on rainy days it's extra romantic because you're right at the window with great lighting! 

Onto the food experience- the menu was gigantic and I wasn't sure how to react when I received it. Our waiter was really great- he matched the vibe completely. Like he was from Italy but he's randomly in New York working for Carbone with an extremely Italian American accent. Old school New York music was played everywhere and it made me reminisce on the old Christmas movies I enjoy watching. I almost can say I enjoyed the service and ambiance more than the food as I wasn't as impressed as I hoped I would be.

The Free Bread Section
The complimentary bread wasn't just bread but garlic bread, fresh mozzarella and prosciutto - I was simply impressed. It's like the courting before dating someone new.

Caesar Alla ZZZ
Some people didn't like this on the reviews but I enjoyed it so much because I love anchovies and they were so fresh here! I would also recommend to cut everything up before eating because they kind of leave this salad full (think huge croutons and full anchovies, uncut romaine)

Scallops
The scallops in this case were cut up micro sized and the sauce was very interesting. I've never had anything like this and I'm assuming this is very Italian style dish as I've had something similar to this in an expensive prefixe Italian dinner in Vancouver. However, did it blow my mind? No. Was it fresh and tasty? fresh - yes, tasty - still thinking on this one as it's not quite my taste palette.

Spicy rigatoni
Since our server noticed we were sharing this he split it by the plate and I would say that this is super underwhelming for me. I thought it was a tad bit too spicy for me and the flavor of the vodka was not as simple as I'd like it to be. It's quite complex and we think that they've added pimento cheese almost in the sauce because it tastes like a little Smokey and cheesy.

Lobster ravioli
This was more of my jam although I had no idea most of this was pork dumplings with a side of fresh lobster. I enjoyed this very much however feel like it could use more lobster.

Dessert
This had me so happy! I enjoyed all the desserts a lot more than the actual meal but I confirmed with the waiter that you cannot come here just for dessert. They gave us almond flour rainbow cake and i loved it as it gave me a lot of nostalgia with growing up in Brooklyn living in Bensonhurst. 
The chocolate cake with the hazelnut and vanilla gelato had my heart and I enjoyed it so much. It literally is a Ferrero rocher cake and I could not be happier. It's not as sweet as other cakes and I enjoyed every bite! The carrot cake was really interesting as well because the ginger gelato had an amazing real ginger flavor and it went well with how moist the carrot cake was and the icing was so smooth and addicting. The downside is that the espresso is $7 each for a normal espresso. I know this is Carbone but this espresso isn't any different from other espresso I've had throughout my life. 

This place took me around my nostalgia track of being a New Yorker and the dream of being here compared to everywhere else versus like an Italian restaurant from Italy. I enjoyed a good fraction of it and I would tell people to just come here to experience it once because now I would probably not go back because the pasta was just ok and I would prefer to just eat somewhere else with my time and money.

You guys will likely never understand the sheer willpower and determination it took to not open this review with a Drake lyric, and I just want my pat on the back. Thank you.

After loosely trying to get a res here for years, we finally got it. Shoutout to my girl Nicole K. on Yelp. She really the plug. I seen she always be in here and asked her how. She flexed up on me and said "You want one? I got you." DAMN, SHE'S LIKE THAT.

Walking into Carbone, I actually felt like the MAN. Was the Drake line "Last table left in Carbone callin plays on a rotary phone," on repeat in my head while walking in? Yes. Yes it was. But it's lowkey been on repeat in my head since 2017 so whatever.

But yeah, right upon entry, I got it. Vibes are IMMACULATE. I'm checking in at the host stand with a classy Italian dude in a beautiful navy blue pinstripe suit, Frank Sinatra playing through the speakers, a vintage Italian decor with low lit lighting, customers dressed to the nines, etc. Just everything you could want out of an experience like this.

We sat down and I wasn't gonna drink, but that glass of Chianti Classico was looking at me soooooo crazy... I folded like a lawn chair ahahaa.

As we were scanning the menu-PLOP! The waiter puts down a basket of bread, a plate of cold cuts, and some pickled cauliflower. This was lowkey a lot of food for just being on the house, I was JUICED. My roommate (Former USC Basketball Superstar) and I tore into this leaving no remnants of any food, we gettin our money's worth ahahahaa.

We both ordered the Spicy Rigatoni and opted to split the meatballs. I almost went with the Lobster Ravioli, but idk. Maybe I'm CRAZY, but lobster just doesn't really do it for me like that. Y'all know Lobster used to be prison & peasant food? What a crazy come up Lobster had lmao. I'm tryna be like Lobster.

The Spicy Rigatoni, as pictured on your friends instagram stories every time they go to Carbone, was delicious and worth every last bit of hype. The Carbone Spicy Rigatoni has to be the world's most photographed pasta.

It's a top 10 plate of pasta I've ever had. Number 1 is easily the Penne Alla Vodka from Alla Vecchia Bettola in Florence, though. That's the LeBron of the pasta game. Oh you haven't been to Florence??? COULDN'T BE ME!

After we demolished the meatballs, I noticed the veal parmesan getting delivered to the table next to us and got the worst FOMO you could ever imagine, as it looked unreal. I can only equate it to the level of FOMO when I was in high school and I saw my close friends all out at a party I wasn't invited to in the back of someone's snapchat story..... No? Just me? Oof.

We were essentially the last table left in this place, with my roommate actually making some business calls on the rotary phone lol it was pretty cool... He does work at Bloomberg though, so.... I ordered a glass of Domina to go with me home.

Typically restaurants that I have high expectations for let me down worse than Amazon's acquisition of Whole Foods, but Carbone exceeded them, and quite easily. They got 5 stars in the holy trinity of the food industry: Great food, great ambiance, and great service. It really is that simple at the end of the day. BELIEVE THE HYPE!
