Top-notch service and terrific food. This is my go-to spot when bringing my non-New York friends for a reliably great dinner. Yes, it can be hard to get a reservation, but if you know how, you now how!
Great if you like shitty food and rude waiters!! We asked them what we should order for dessert and the guy said "make up your mind I have tables to turn"

We came here didn't have a reservation, but they wouldn't accept us even though there was no one in there. Hopefully they have better business ethnics and let walk in come and hopefully the food is worth it it's probably not. We went to lupa's and their food was delicious.
Amazing atmosphere and ambiance! The service was excellent. The food top notch especially the spicy rigatoni and the meatballs, those are two must haves! A must try restaurant!
mewww, waiter was rushing us and food was average (acceptable). The place is falling off

Rarely do hyped up places live up to their expectation, but Carbone certainly did. The service was one of the best I've experienced in New York. Complimentary bread basket with cheese, olives and pickles was great. The spicy vodka lived up to its hype. Spaghetti vongole was good and so were the artichoke hearts. Will be back for sure.
The best vibe, experiences, and food. Love this restaurant and its service. It's so hard to get in so you can reserve reservations please go

The food was excellent. Best Italian food I've eaten! It sounds cliche but the spicy rigatoni and veal parm really were fantastic. The duck fat potatoes were also great. The service was perfect, the drinks were enjoyable. The restaurant is small so it was a bit more cramped than I prefer, but the restaurant was a fun vibe.
The absolute best meatballs and spicy vodka (not really spicy) rigatoni.  The only issue is not being able to get in!

Nice place and chill vibes... cool decor. ribs were likewarm chewey and lacked flavor - waiter acted surprised I have ordered those - and I should have paid attention! "World famous rigatoni" underwhelmed. free snacks were yummy! no complaints about the service ...

Not gonna lie I wasn't expecting much. I'm not an overtly big fan of Italian food. But Carbone was nice. I think it's the service and ambiance and overall experience. Caesar salad was the best I've had. They use a shaved ricotta which has a unique texture. Rigatoni was as expected, excellent. Get the meatballs for sure!  All the freebies are a nice touch too. We got to sit outside in April and that was more enjoyable than inside.

Omg. Actually insane. I was trying to separate the fact that I was at Carbone from quality of the food, to be as unbiased as possible but holy moly. The ambiance is soooo nice. Such a GREAT AMBIANCE inside!!!!!!!!!! I loved it. The interior design & decor was top tier and the vibe was mature but like just amazing. The food was soooooooo amazing. THE BREAD WAS SO GOOD OMG. And the mozzarella is a MUST have. I tried to rigatoni alla vodka (obviously) which did not disappoint. It tasted like the carbone vodka sauce in a jar but just a millions times better. And cauliflower was great too. We also got this angel hair pasta which was amazing but the vodka was my favorite. We ordered the Caesar salad as well and it was also amazing. The lemon cheesecake for dessert was amazing as well. The service was also great. Overall, I would rate it an 11/10. Exceptional. And also, it's Carbone. What do you expect.

Everything is amazing at carbone, you dont have to be a celebrity here to feel like one. From the most incredible, sweet, and kind female matridee, Zufan (which is so rare at upscale restaurants and worth visiting just for the female empowerment) to the melt in your mouth spicy rigatoni to the to die for lemon cheesecake, it's no wonder no one can get a reservation here and it is absolutely worth the hype. Highly recommend you set your notifications on resy ASAP! Truly the most wonderful experience.

Was it hard getting a reservation at Carbone? Not if you're dedicated to the cause. Was it worth the hype? Absolutely, and then some. Carbone doesn't need an intro; it's already a legend. We're all just after that validation to go--so consider this yours. 

The restaurant's interior design is impeccable, showcasing a distinct Italian elegance, particularly notable in the ambiance of the back room. Also, the service team provides exceptional hospitality, extending the highest degree of courtesy and warmth to every guest. The culinary offerings are absolutely delicious. Each dish represents an authentic tribute to Italian cuisine. 

The eggplant & zucchini scapece is an absolute must-order, offering a beautiful complexity with layers of flavors that speak to the quality of the ingredients. The Caesar salad is delightful, accompanied by croutons you'll actually want to eat, which perfectly complement the fresh, crisp greens. The veal parmigiana stands as a centerpiece, its rich and tender meat enveloped in a golden, crispy crust of parmesan perfection. And the spicy rigatoni is a dish of such renown it might as well be automatically billed since you are getting it regardless.

As for the Jordan almonds, maybe you'll be lucky enough to have that splattered on your table.

Go to Resy and book already.

The spicy rigatoni sauce wasn't really like any vodka sauce I've tasted before - it was sweet and spicy, had a good amount of red pepper/onion flavor, and was creamy but not overwhelming. I do get the hype! The veal parm was tasty and breaded perfectly but overpriced and not special imo. I liked the free apps. 

Wouldn't jump through hoops to come back here but I did enjoy my experience and would return if I could easily get a res.

Great food, good portion, very nice services. Reservations are very difficult to get.
Assorted baked clams are amazing, enjoyed all three flavors, would definitely order them again.
Spicy rigatoni vodka is without a doubt the best pasta I've ever had, this dish itself is worth to come back for.
Lobster Ravioli is also pretty good, probably the best ravioli I've ever tried, even though the sauce is a little too rich for me.
The only thing underwhelming is the meatballs, it's not bad, but just some regular meatballs, nothing special about them.

Reservations were pretty easy to get through my Visa Infinite Concierge service since it was for lunch (1:30). Personally, nothing stood out to me, not even the Spicy Rigatoni. We ordered the Assorted Baked Clams, Caesar Salad, and Spicy Rigatoni Pasta. There was also complimentary bread, meats, mozzarella, and rainbow cookies at the end.

Spicy Rigatoni - The best dish we tried was the Spicy Rigatoni, but I would rate this a 3/5. Don't get me wrong, it tastes decent but nothing extraordinary. It also wasn't that spicy? I have definitely tried better elsewhere.

Clams - (2.5/5) I would pass on this. Some of the clams had a very fishy aftertaste.

Caesar Salad - (3/5) The best part of the salad was the crouton by far. I guess it was fun because they made it tableside? Really nothing special.

The restaurant is on the pricier side, but I don't mind that if the flavor is there. Sadly, I was pretty disappointed. The staff, however, were very kind, and the restaurant decor is very beautiful; it felt like we were transported back in time. If you get a reservation, I would say just go try it, but it is overhyped, and you will leave feeling like you could have spent your money elsewhere
Cute space! Food is good but a little overrated. There are much better Italian places in the city at this price point.
i mean people may disagree with me but i think the rigatoni slaps so hard. Parm is not a dupe their version is way less saucy. It's worth it to try and go once! The rest of the sides are just OK

I had exceptionally high expectations for Carbone. After waiting for years and reading through an endless amount of reviews, I finally found myself walking in through Carbone's doors in New York. No review I had read could have prepared me for the actual dining experience. It was much more relaxed than I would have thought but also much more detailed. The service is more thought out than many other restaurants I have been to. Think wait staff folding your napkins every time you get up from your seat to use the restroom. You feel special here. 

For the food itself, the appetizers guise you through a culinary journey right through to the main courses. For our starter, we enjoyed the Carpaccio. I would come back ten more times just to order this dish. It is nutty and meaty but light in the most balanced of ways. I have never tried something quite like this dish. It is something I wish I could try for the first time over and over again. The spicy rigatoni vodka had a perfect chew to it and a perfect spice level. It lives up to the hype and is a must order. The veal parmesan is not talked about enough. The flavors and textures blended so well together and were topped with such a bold flavored cheese. It was an unexpected dish to stand out and something I would order over and over again. 

If you are in the city, dare to dabble into the hype of Carbone. Adventure out and try the dishes that are not so hyped as well, your taste buds will thank you!

Little disappointed especially everyone talk about this place. Food is average for drink garnish horrible especially aperol spritz I was surprised.  The best part it is dessert chocolate witg hazelnut I give 10. The rest is just ok
Thank you

The spicy vodka rigatoni was so good. Worth the hype. I ordered meatballs expecting normal sized meatballs but they were giant, hence them also being $27. Our server was very kind and attentive. The ambience was lively and pleasant.

This place lived up to the hype. The Spicy Rigatoni did not disappoint. I still dream about it ! We went in for a lunch date and it was pretty crowded but we had a reservation so we were able to be seated pretty quickly. Our waiter was an amazing and was so kind and accommodating for us. We had our toddler with us and did his best to keep all of us comfortable. This restaurant is incredibly small. I now understand what's it's almost impossible to get a reservation here, but it's worth the effort!

One Sunday I casually looked on Resy app and was so surprised a 1:15pm slot on Friday was available all of a sudden. I was able to get the resy, which required me to deposit $50 per person plus tax. This amount can be used towards the meal. Upon arriving at the restaurant about 30 minutes early, the hostesses were nice and showed the two of us to our table. Joey was our server and greeted us while the staff asked if we wanted still or sparkling water (important for later). As we perused the menu the staff gave us complimentary garlic bread, hard salami, and warm fresh mozzarella, and we loved it! Joey was really polite, but after hearing our order (assorted clams and spicy rigatoni only, no wine or cocktails) he pushed for us to order more. I understand if a server wanted to ask maybe one clarification question about whether or not we ordered enough, but more than that is rude in my opinion. Also we ate lunch, which isn't that deep versus going somewhere for dinner where maybe I can understand a server pushing. He was trying to upsell the meatballs and I politely declined explaining how we honestly would love to eat more, but between the two of us two dishes will probably be perfect. He said "how about one single meatball?" I was like no that's really nice of you, but we're good. I've just never been pressured to order more from a server in general before, so I think I was taken by surprise. The food was overall delicious, but the price point was a bit high when there are plenty of other options in Manhattan or the other four boroughs for just as high quality Italian food. I also saw other photos of the assorted clams and many of the customers photos showed their clams have more uni. My assorted clams barely had any uni. I was disturbed by the still water charge the server didn't inform me about until he dropped the bill. Maybe I should've asked if tap water was available from the beginning. I guess the "free" mozzarella, salami, and garlic bread make up for the still water charge. I walked away overall a little irked, but satisfied from my first time eating at Carbone. I was surprised how full I was all day from just eating there for lunch. I liked that I scratched an itch with my curuosity, however, the food did not impress me enough to make me want to go back for a repeat experience.

In every possible way, Carbone in New York City is the best. The best is quite literally deserved. As you walk in through the door, quite literally, the old-school, classic Italian-American vibe and vintage décor are spot-on in raising your hopes for a memorable dining experience. What comes next is friendly staff: The service during the meal is on top level, and really, at this place, you feel like being a special and valued guest.

The food here is amazing. Their Spicy Rigatoni Vodka is a masterpiece, very well seasoned and cooked perfectly.

Another winner is the Veal Parmesan, crispy on the outside to a gentle inside, it literally melts in your mouth. One should not miss the Caesar salad either, prepared at the table with great flair and tasting delicious.

The cocktail menu goes at length to make sure it is well developed, offering a perfect match to most of the rich flavors dishes offered. From their cocktail list, I had the Negroni. It is indeed perfectly balanced with so much depth. And do save at least some room for dessert--tiramisu comes out for a curtain call that's definitely worth the indulgence.

Carbone is able to blend sophistication with a warm environment to offer diners a space that meets the need for either a special occasion or the desire to treat oneself to great food. From old-school hospitality to amazing cuisine--everything's just perfect. A huge five-star rating all the way for this outstanding dining establishment!

I get the hype of Carbone. The ambience felt like the old-school, Italian-American vibe. We were seated outdoors which had a different feel from inside the restaurant. We got reservations 30 days prior because we heard that it was difficult to get. Even though we made reservations early, the time we secured was 10:00pm. It felt like our server was rushing us and almost looked down upon us which we did not care for. 

We got the assorted baked clams, spicy rigatoni pasta, tortellini al ragu and meatballs. The baked clams were very flavorful - there was a variety I was not a fan of but overall glad I tried. Spicy rigatoni pasta was very delicious - great flavor, great texture and great portion. The tortellini was ok. I would probably skip this one. The meatballs complimented our pastas very well.

I've been wanting to try Carbone for months now, and my husband was able to get a reservation for us for the "Mother's Day Lunch," which includes a four-course lunch menu. The first course consisted of a bread basket, a chunk of parmesan, few slices of salami & cauliflower salad, which were complimentary, followed by a caesar salad, prosciutto & mozzarella, and tuna calabrese. Second course was our favorite, which consisted of their famous spicy rigatoni vodka and Mario's meatballs. Third course consisted of shrimp scampi, veal parmesan, and grilled asparagus. Last & fourth course consisted of rainbow cookies (comp), carrot cake w/ ginger ice cream, and lemon cheesecake. 

Honestly, the best food we had was probably the bread basket, rigatoni, meatballs, and veal parm. The rigatoni was spicy enough to get your taste buds flowing while the meatballs made you feel like you were in Italy- tender & tasty. The bread basket with plain sesame (my fave), garlic & tomato breads were all delicious, and the veal parm was cooked to perfection. Since our taste pallets were not used to the other food, I won't comment on those items, but just wanted to mention, the cauliflower salad was overly acidic from the vinaigrette and the caesar salad had dijon mustard dressing (not a fan)- the crutons in it were very salty. Everything else tasted fine. 

Service was impeccable from start to finish. Our water always remained full, the staff were friendly & attentive- they frequently checked on us to see if everything was okay, and we got new plates & untesils after every course. If you're lucky enough to get a reservation, you have to try their spicy rigatoni, meatballs & veal parm. This place lives up to the hype.

This place is legendary and for the right reasons. We were able to snag a lunch reservation and weren't disappointed. The service is top notch. Their bread and fresh mozzarella is unbelievable. We got the spicy rigatoni, veal parmigiana and lobster ravioli. The best veal parm I've ever had. The rigatoni is a must and the ravioli was fantastic. 

It's definitely not cheap, but well worth the price.
This is honestly overhyped. The only good thing I enjoyed was the Caesar salad. The waiters were very nice and understanding, the food was just very mediocre in my opinion.

My friend and I went for Mother's Day. I was a bit disappointed that our table was outside in one of the makeshift indoor/outdoor seating arrangements birthed as a result of COVID, BUT the ambiance in there was okay - nothing like the actual restaurant though.

The menu's are huge - so fun. The waitstaff was so professional, welcoming and friendly. 

Complimentary appetizers were so yummy! I don't usually eat meat but that salami was top notch! The cauliflower, I need the recipe!

For our meal we ordered the spicy rigatoni split into, and it was really really good, I wish I had a whole order. Meatballs were tender and juicy and the veal was delicious. The spicy broccoli rabe was yummy (we got the spice on the side and I loved it - not too spicy either).

I wanted dessert but we were stuffed so opted not to order anything, but we were still presented with the yummiest Italian cookies I have ever had.

Such a wonderful experience and memory for us! Thank you!

The elusive Carbone reservation! Our friend from out of town had gotten reservation for 4 at 5pm but her family wasn't able to attend with her. So we accompanied her. 

The doors open exactly at 5pm, they had a bouncer managing the queue to go in. I was annoyed when he let a family that arrived later than us and had a 5:15 reservation cut ahead of us. That party didn't confirm their reservation ahead of time and ended up creating bottle neck while they tried to sort out the situation.  They should have had that party step aside so the rest of the parties that confirmed could be seated. 

Once we were inside, service was better. Our server kept our wine glasses full. 

Here's what we ordered. 
Spicy rigatoni - a little spicy but sour
Angel hair -
T bone Steak for 2 - has a nice char on it
Octopus -delicious 
Calamari - 
Tiramisu - you could taste a light hint of ginger in it 
Apple cake 

I would say the dessert wines was my favorite, followed by the tiramisu.

Ambiance is more loud and very intimate. So sometimes you had to yell to be heard. Was it worth the hype? The food was good but wasn't life changing for me to want to go again.


Note: reservations are a must, they are always full. Saw a number of people trying to do walk in but were told it was full

The atmosphere was bizarre.  Felt like we were sitting in an abandoned mall.  There was a really cool room that looked like Miami location but could only hold a small group.  Portions small.  Wanted to love it....
As amazing as I thought it would be. We tried many things but the stand outs were the tortellini al ragu, spicy rigatoni vodka and the veal parmesan.

The two times I've gone here, I feel like the highlight of my meal has been making an Instagram post. While the food is always delicious, I feel that the high prices don't entirely match. The rigatoni is tasty but nothing you can't find elsewhere in the city. The ambiance is decent, but the vibe is that everyone is there for the trend, making the place seem very LA in terms of influencers. The service isn't too long, but everything else seems fine after waiting over a month for reservations. I'd go back, but I'm not rushing to do so.

This lives up to the hype. Service was fantastic. The mood was very old New York. Great vibes. The food hit. We got the baked clams, lobster ravioli, tortellini ragu and, of course, the spicy rigatoni. Everything was delicious, but the lobster ravioli might have been my favorite. That said the rigatoni was the best vodka sauce I've ever had. 

We also had the cheesecake for dessert which was outstanding. 

Other tables got the table side Caesar which looked perfectly fresh and crunchy. If Resy notify ever comes through again that will be part of the next order.

Food wasn't worth the hype. Sat outside in their little wooden box they have in front of the restaurant and it was 77 degrees in there. Almost dripping sweat. 

Service was fine. 

Wouldn't go back.

This place is a must if visiting NYC and you are able to get a reservation. The prices are the most reasonable when considering nyc pricing. The food is the best Italian I've ever eaten. The cocktails are fantastic as well. I would probably skip the bottle of wine as it may double the price of your dinner like it did for us (our fault, not theirs). Ambiance is charming and cozy with service being really solid and professional as well.

I had a great time dining here. We ate lunch here right when it opened and the service was very fast! The interior is very well decorated! 

We ordered everything family style. The Caesar salad was definitely worth the hype! It was tossed right in front of us and we had the anchovies on the side! The croutons are crispy on the outside and chewy on the inside-- a perfectly delicious combination!! The rigatoni alla vodka is delicious!!! The lobster ravioli and ragu was good as well.

Welcoming, energetic, and delicious all around. We loved our table, the candlelit rooms, the decor, and the various Italian dinnerware settings, which make dining so festive. Except for one dish, everyone loved their dishes and wished we could've had the ability to have seconds ... boy were we stuffed, though. The lobster is slightly overpriced, so ask the MP before you settle on it. However, it was delicious, and I got to take leftovers home.  Also - the monster-sized lobster they showed me as the "selection" was most definitely not the lobster cooked for me, so be aware (even the waiters chuckled at the truth with us), all around a worthwhile visit and not an overhyped place. We can't wait to return.

I did not think this place lived up to the hype. Prices are somewhat reasonable considering it is Carbone after all. I came here for lunch and all the staff was friendly. I tried the spicy rigatoni which did not impress me at all. The ribeye was above average but nothing about this place impressed me at all except for their great service. Service 5/5 and Food 3/5.

I recommend the spicy vodka sauce pasta that one was 10/10. Besides that the food was good not outstanding or mind blowing. I didn't like the lobster pasta here. Service was rude and were rushing us even though we had a reservation and we just entered when the restaurant opened. We had ordered like 200$s of food and weren't sure what to get as the main course and wanted to decide after appetizers & the first course. The waiter told us no u have to put in the order all at once and tried to decide for us what we should get, even though we made it clear we did not want to decide yet. It would add an additional 10 min to the wait time so not sure what his problem was about.
I will fly all the way back to new York everytime just to have mark as my guy.....the restaurant is 10/10 and marks service is 20/20

This place is a solid 3 stars. Definitely overhyped. Genius how they do it. But I won't be going back. Rigatoni was good. But not worth the hype at all. Neither were the other entrees. Cozy and small place but the hosts were bougie and assumed I was a walk in and tried to shoo me away lol. Server was nice but had to flag him down to ask for refills.  Go ahead and keep the hype alive. I'm glad I tried it but, never again.

Made the reservation for Carbone for my fiancé's birthday 30 days in advance and boy was it worth the wait. The ambiance and vibes of the restaurant are old school Italian, I felt like Tony soprano eating here. 

Everything we ate was absolutely outstanding. The spicy vodka rigatoni, which they're famous for, is some of the best I've ever had in my life and was worth the hype. The meatballs and tortellini were also phenomenal. The surprise of the meal was the chocolate hazelnut cake which tasted like ferrero rocher and was seriously top 3 best cake I've ever eaten in my life. I don't care if you have to wait 2 years or sell your first born child to get a reservation here, do whatever you have to do because eating at Carbone is an EXPERIENCE.

The stars must have aligned  just right, and all the right moons must have been in retrograde because after proudly calling myself an NYC resident for six years, I finally snagged a Carbone reservation through Resy's waitlist. It was a lunch reservation, but I was not about to look this gift horse in the mouth, and at least I didn't pay for it. Anywho, I went in fully expecting and even hoping to hate it, as due punishment for being such a royal pain in the ass to get into and for playing with my emotions. I now describe it as my favorite Italian meal experience in New York.

I was feeling like royalty the entire time I was at Carbone! The complimentary appetizer of salami, fresh mozzarella and garlic bread was served immediately, and I might say, this was quite a generous portion of a complimentary appetizer, not some measly little four olives some places graciously bestow onto you.

So as for the damn spicy rigatoni I've been hearing about, it is in fact good. Cooked perfectly al dente, perfect amount of sauce (don't you hate it when there's not enough sauce?!) with a a slight kick to it that's not overbearing. We ordered the spicy broccoli rabe as an attempt to add something green to the table and briefly distract me from the pasta, but then the veal parm arrived. The veal parm does carry a hefty price tag, but I rule it worthy.

The vibes are classy and old school New York with candles  and elaborate flower arrangements, elegant crisp waiters, and all that jazz. I saw a Caesar salad being made at the table next to mine, and that look like a bit of a magic trick of sorts, if you're in the mood for a dinner and a show. I loved every minute of it. Don't judge me.

Carbone is one of New York's most famous and hardest reservation to get. People travel all over to dine here and it is definitely worth the trip! We have been to their NYC and Miami location several times, and have had such great experiences

We find the Miami location is much easier to get a reservation compared to NYC due to their larger dining room. Both locations present the same experience and ambience and have the same menu as well. All reservations can be made 30 days in advance on the Resy app. 

You will begin your meal with a complimentary bread basket, serving various breads, and either fresh mozzarella(NYC) or aged Parmesan (Miami) with salami. This is a great way to get your pallet ready for your meal!

For appetizers, we HIGHLY recommend the meatballs and Caesar Salad. The Caesar is made table side which is a GREAT experience overall!!!! While being absolutely delicious. Additionally, the meatballs are also famous and very delicious. You can't pass up on them! 

For entrées, of course get the spicy rigatoni. It definitely lives up to its name!  This is one of our favorite dishes, we get it every time. We also recommend the Tortellini al Ragu, which is another famous dish and features a Bolognese sauce

You must leave room for dessert because their desserts are truly delicious!  We love their tiramisu and Chocolate Peanut Butter Cake! Yoy also receive complementary rainbow cookies at the end of your meal

Our Favorites:
Cesar alla ZZ
Meatballs 
Spicy Rigatini Vodka
Tortellini al Ragu
Branzino
Tiramisu 
Chocolate Peanut Butter Cake
 Cheesecake

Many think Carbone is overrated and we highly disagree ! The food here is always great, and we love coming here. The spicy rigatoni is the best there is

My friend snagged a lunch reservation in one of the hardest place to get reservations. Three years ago,  dined outside during the transitional COVID phase, but this is my first time dining indoors. 

Inside is pretty small, and it was packed for lunch. I took full advantage of the experience with the wines.  Our server Joey was great and accommodated us to make us feel welcomed. 

We started with complementary bread, salami, and fresh mozzerella. This paired really well with the glass of Brunello. 

Caesar Alla ZZ Salad - although the salad tasted good with the anchovies, the lettuce did not look fresh. Our server served our appropriate portions of this dish. 

Spicy Rigatoni alla Vodka - this infamous dish lived up to the expectation and hype. This is worth ordering, and it paired well with Brunello.

Salmon Oreganata - this dish was also good, and it came with beans. My friend enjoyed it. This would pair well with a Sancerre. 

Finally, for dessert, we ordered the tiramisu and chocolate cake. Tiramisu was a pretty large portion. I took my leftovers home where my other half enjoyed it. My friend enjoyed her chocolate cake. 

Personally I prefer to dine in the restaurant, wine is the way to go. I'd return to try the baked clams but get the spicy Rigatoni alla Vodka and Veal parmesan (price for parmesan dish went up $20 from the last time I dined in 2021).

I was lucky to get a table at this super popular place. It was such a nice experience and worth the hype. To start, they served garlic bread, salami, and burrata all for free. To be honest, I would not hesitate to pay for them because they are just so good. We ordered the spicy rigatoni vodka and the tortellini ragu. Both were cooked to perfection. Next time I would try the lobster ravioli, if I could get another table.

Marry me!!!
I love these people.
Service always amazing.
Anyone who says food is not A+ was not hugged as a child!

The food is ok... 


The service .:: eh 


Over a month to get into this place why??

We arrived 5 min prior to reservation and then had us wait and sat us 30 min after our reservation time !

An old style italian eatery with a modern twist. Pasta is the name of the game here, although the flavors and presentationare just average. All pastas are home made, and all are commonly known...ravioli, fettuccine, rigatoni and others. An uncommon pasta would further add pizzazz to the menu. The physical menu is giant, unexpectedly big and was hard to handle. The drinks are average, the staff attentive but too cozy. Overall a good, not great experience.

So reservations are extremely difficult to get at Carbone, which is what I think adds to the mystery of the restaurant. If you have a credit card, like the Capital One Venture X card, you can use the concierge service to get you reservations. My sister did this for me and also did it for a friend the day before we went. You may not get the exact time you want but they'll most likely be able to find an opening for you that you would not be able to find on your own. Also, if you book with a concierge, a deposit isn't required. I looked online and the deposit is $50 per person, but when we were at the restaurant and our waiter didn't realize at first we didn't pay a deposit, he kept asking are we sure we didn't want to order more food because of the $250 deposit (you have to order all your food at once). Also, not sure why he said $250 and not $100 becauss it was just two of us.

Besides the complimentary starters, we also got these mini complimentary rainbow cookies. 

The spicy rigatoni isn't super spicy but it has a nice kick to it as an after taste. It tasted good and I would order it again. Also, I am surprised the rigatoni is more famous than the tortellini because we thought that the tortellini was really good and the overall the star. The portions are small because they are appetizers. At the price, you'd expect bigger or being that they're appetizers, you'd expect they'd be cheaper.

We also got the lemon cheesecake  for dessert that we loved! The one thing I was a little annoyed about was that I ordered a limeade and it was rung up as a mocktail at $16 which is like wow lol. In total we spent $140 (including tip) for our meal.

Service and ambiance were great!
Incredible experience! Can't wait to come back and enjoy the fresh Parmesan and pastas!

Food was delicious, support staff were all incredibly kind and attentive, but our "captain" was super pushy with trying to get us to order more to the point where it just became uncomfortable. We went for lunch and didn't want to have a huge meal, but we did each order our own plate and wine or a cocktail! He was then irritated that we didn't want dessert or coffee. After we paid with credit card he made sure to circle the total before the deposit was applied so that we would tip on the total amount, which of course I was going to do anyway but after the constant passive aggressiveness at not wanting to order the whole menu it was just the final straw. 

Overall great food and happy I tried it, the lobster ravioli, tortellini, and rigatoni were all delicious. Just left feeling annoyed at being made to feel cheap.

Amazing experience, not overhyped at all. Server was super kind and attentive, the interior was very nicely decorated, and the food was so so good. I wanted to go to Carbone for years now, but could never find an open reservation. However, we somehow managed to get a 2pm lunch reservation on a Sunday (even I was shocked). Even though I heard from a lot of things about Carbone being not worth the hype, I wanted to go see and try it my self. 

We sat in the very back of the restaurant, and it had stunning wall art, flowers, checkerboard floors, and overall great architectural designs. Our waiter was fantastic and enthusiastic. We were given garlic bread, salami, and burrata cheese. The garlic bread was really hard, crunchy, and stale so I didn't want to waste my stomach space trying to eat it. Salami was good, but the fresh burrata was amazing. So delicious. 

We had to get all of the classics on the menu. We opted for the caesar salad and baked clams for starters. The caesar salad was supposed to be made tableside, but it was oddly made in the middle of the room, and no one told us which caesar salad was ours being made. Anyways, the salad was pretty unique, and it had these large bread-like croutons that tasted like a better version of the free garlic bread they gave us. They also put anchovies on the salad, but they ask if you want them on it or not. The anchovies were really salty, so even though it was put on, we removed them because it didn't taste like a caesar salad anymore. Also my brother said the dressing tasted like alcohol, and he's not wrong. It's a strong, pungent taste, a bit like hand sanitizer. The baked clams selection was stunning: there was 9 and each 3 had different flavors. All of them tasted unique and good. 

For entrees, we had to go for the spicy rigatoni vodka, salmon, meatballs and the lobster ravioli. The spicy rigatoni vodka was TO DIE FOR. So hearty, creamy, tangy, and so flavorful. You need to get this if you come, it's a no brainer. The salmon was the softest and most tender salmon I've ever eaten. It didn't even taste like fish, it was that soft. Very good. The lobster ravioli was ok, but the other entrees are better. The ravioli was pretty hard, but I heard the sauce was really good. And lastly, the least expected standout dish in my opinion, were the meatballs. They were bursting with flavor: hands down best meatballs I've ever eaten. So juicy and savory. They were pretty big as well. After eating the meatballs, when I went back to eating my pasta, my pasta tasted like nothing. That's how flavorful the meatballs were. 

For dessert, they give us complimentary Italian cookies, and we got their lemon cheesecake and the chocolate hazelnut cake. The lemon cheesecake was creamy and light, not bad. The chocolate hazelnut cake was delicious though. All of the flavors blended well together: the rich chocolate with the cold ice cream and the crunchy hazelnuts. So so yummy!

To be honest, I thought this was going to be an ok review. But turns out, Carbone fully deserves all of the good raves because it is that good. If you can ever get a reservation. Do it. And don't look back.

Excellent lunch at Carbone NYC. 
The Caesar salad was incredible. The lobster ravioli for the win.

We had the spicy vodka rigatoni as well and the meatballs. 

We didn't have room for dessert but we made room... it looks heavy but it actually was very light.

I felt I was on a movie set until the appetizers arrived and I found my happy place.  The service people were in full uniform too and their delivery was professionally done.
My daughter took us to this special place for Father's Day and my 77 th birthday.  Love her for making me the envy of my friends!

ABSOLUTELY WORTH THE MONEY! 
People usually love the rigatoni (which I did too), but the star of the show for me were the baked clams. Would highly recommend

Worth the difficulties to get a reservation. 
The bread, cheese selection are great. 

The spicy pasta is unique too

Holy cow, I don't know how this place gets such good reviews.  To say it's over priced and over hyped is the understatement of the century. The decor is ghastly. It's like walking into the set of Goodfellas. There's no other way to put it. It's too loud to hear the waitstaff or your date. 
The service is worse than any diner, Denny's, shit hole, you've ever been to. In one night I saw, bottles being turned upside down in glasses to pour; a manager cleared a table by dumping the contents of one plate in air (silverware and all) onto another plate; a hostess pulled out a seat for a lady then just left without pushing her in; the literal pushing of plates and glasses with plates and glasses to make room on the table and my personal favorite, our waiter putting our forks back on the table in between courses. There's no way there's  service training and I doubt anyone FOH has ever eaten at even a semi-nice restaurant.  They have no clue how to act. 
Getting up from the tables is also a feat. They are so tight together I had to help the woman next to us by moving our table. She probably weighed 110lbs. With the dozen FoH staff standing around, you'd think they'd be on top of that but I doubt they even know to help. 

The food... it must be good, right? The dive atmosphere and horrible service it's all a gimmick and the food is spectacular, right??? 
Not by a mile and I was starving. 

The bread service is plentiful, (they aren't serving the mozzarella anymore so forget that. You get sad cauliflower.) the really "elegant" chunk of parm they drop on a plate was tasty but why they serve it like we are a bunch of drunks digging in the fridge at 2 am is a mystery. The grandma bread was also tasty. 
We got the carpaccio which was so bland and not salted we didn't finish it.The sizzling porchetta looks amazing but was "meh" at best. 
The tortellini themselves were very good but for $35 they should be, right?
The fettuccine with funghi was so underwhelming I can't begin to describe. I expected a rich dish with different caramelized mushrooms, cream, egg yolk and parm. What I got was half a sweated trumpet with way too much herb, no salt and nothing rich about it.
We skipped dessert but even those sad rainbow cookies (literally my favorite cookie on the planet) were "meh". 

So how does this place stay so popular?
It has to be the, "It's expensive so it has to be good" syndrome people follow. If you want to go to Carbon because you want to tell people you've been, you'll probably lie to yourself and say it was the best meal. If you actually love food, love dining out and know what a good meal in NYC tastes like, please know, Carbone is not worth the time or money.

I absolutely LOVE carbone and I don't care if it's overrated! The spicy rigatoni is out of this world and it's the only food picture I'm posting because it's the one plate you can't leave here without. I've now been to the one in New York and Vegas, I am very satisfied every single time!

Don't forget to grab an espresso martini, chefs kiss!

This place is amazing!

Great ambiance and music is loud, but you can still have a conservation without fear the music blocks conservations.

Music selection is also very mellow and positive/upbeat; contributing to a very welcoming and relaxing meal.

Service is excellent and everyone is attentive.  Truly, I felt like a king dining with my family.

Surprisingly this place is family friendly and the servers were very understanding, not something I expected from a fine dining establishment.

Portions were decent, not the massive American sized portions or minuscule one bite servings.  Don't be afraid to order a few different dishes, we ordered quite a bit, but finished every bite without left overs.  We left full and definitely enjoyed dining at Carbone!

When we next visit NYC, we'll make reservations in advance to ensure we don't miss out on this fantastic meal.  We were lucky to get a last minute reservation.
Always love Carbone. This was my first time at the NYC location. It is very quaint but really good service, food was delicious, drinks were amazing. A great birthday celebration for my love.

The journey to Carbone began the week before my trip to NYC.  Visiting a friend, we wanted to dine somewhere nice to celebrate a graduation on top of being foodies who love to try new places.  Immediately, Carbone NYC came to mind as the place we had to be.  However, with only a weeks notice, we were sure that the answer would have been one that countless other people hear from Carbone; no.  However, after emailing MFG about a reservation, not only were they incredibly prompt in a response but they were super accommodating and kind  in helping secure my friend and I a reservation at the esteemed establishment.

Walking in, you instantly feel the classy, elegant, and old school Italian American vibe in Carbone.  From the staff sporting tuxedos to Dean Martin and Sinatra controlling the speakers, Carbone screams classic and exudes elegance.  Service from the jump was impeccable and welcoming, especially considering we came from Boston to eat at Carbone.  Our waiter helped guide us through the menu, and helped make sure we had the best experience we could.

To start, we were served bread, local salami, and pickled cauliflower which from the jump were delicious.  After tasting this, we knew we'd be in for a special night.  

Appetizers: The table side caesar was rich, crisp, and the jumbo croutons made it all the better.  The baked clams came with three preparations: oregano, spicy pancetta, and one with sea urchin.  Each clam brought its own flavor profile to the party, while at the same time complimenting each other. All in all the appetizers prepared us for the main stars of the night...the entrees.

Entrees: From all the social media publicity the spicy vodka rigatoni gets, you'd figure that the hype must be bigger than the dish itself, but boy oh boy is that not the case for this dish.  The rich, creamy, and ever so flavorful rigatoni are everything you'd hope from a Carbone meal.  The pasta was cooked to perfection, and the flavor was spicy while not being unbearable.  The rigatoni is a MUST HAVE no questions asked, but what may have stole the show was the tortellini al ragu.  The meat sauce laid a foundation for the flavor that the plump tortellini would have.  Biting in to those tortellini was like biting into a cloud.  The soft, creamy, and rich cheese oozed from the pasta with every bite, adding to the perfection of the tortellini.  We expected the rigatoni to be iconic, but the tortellini is the dish that is a must hiding in the shadows of the rigatoni.  The veal parm was Italian comfort at its finest, flavorful, and crisp.  The truffle corn was creamy, balanced and the perfect side.

For two people, this was the perfect amount of food as everything comes in shareable sizes, and that is what I would recommend you do if you visit Carbone; share.  To eat one dish here is criminal when the restaurant is so delicious, so you're better off sharing and tasting everything at this classic Italian eatery.  To say you'd want to come back is an understatement, because Carbone is the staple that it truly is, from top to bottom and I am sure I will be trying other MFG establishments in the future.

If you are not important, or what "they" perceive as important, you don't matter. I am a teacher and splurged on my kids' graduation trip. My god, have some respect for all people whether famous or normal or poor!!!!!

An enjoyable experience, although in my opinion it is over-priced and a little overhyped. I couldn't get a reservation here for over 5 years, then finally did by being on the "notify me" waitlist for many many attempts. They do have a dress code, so we rerouted our whole afternoon to go home and change after being notified that there was an available reservation hours in advance.

Their bread, cheese and salami were the highlights of the meal. The focaccia and garlic bread were truly perfect and the cheese was insanely good as well.

The yellowtail crudo was solid. Good quality and refreshing. 

The Caesar salad was pretty mediocre. The mustard flavor tasted too heavy to me and it was a little undersalted. But the croutons on top were amazing.

The pastas were average at best. The clam pasta had an unusual ingredient, I think it was green peppers or something, but the flavors did not come together well. The rigatoni was okay. I wouldn't order either of them again.

The atmosphere is very nice - it feels upscale and festive without being too stuffy. Their service was great.

I want to start off by acknowledging the staff - in particular our waitress. She was absolutely wonderful and very attentive. We were seated outside but the ambiance was very nice as they had nice music playing and had a functioning AC. 

The food itself was very underwhelming, which was a bit shocking given that this restaurant is very exclusive and it's hard to obtain a reservation. 

We went during lunch and were given complimentary mozzarella, garlic bread and salami. Mozzarella was too salty; the garlic bread was the winner. 

We started off with the Caesar salad and it wasn't great :( the croutons were the highlight of it. 

For mains, we split the spicy vodka rigatoni and meatball as. Pasta was overcooked and too chewy; the sauce was good and spicy though. The meatballs were okay. 

For dessert, we were given these two Italian complimentary cookies which were delicious. We ordered the carrot cake with ginger ice cream and it tasted a bit stale and just not good at all. The cookies were better. 

The experience was definitely unique and very high end but imho, there are plenty of restaurants in the village that offer better quality.
