Amazing & great service. Definitely worth trying at least once. 
The spicy rigatoni doesn't disappoint!

I see four categories for hyped NYC spots:

1. Believe the hype
2. If you forget about the hype, this is superb
3. Overhyped, but worth going once for the vibe / experience 
4. Even Elizabeth Holmes would be embarrassed by the failure to deliver on the hype  

On this scale, Carbone is a 3.75. Cool old New York aesthetic, exclusive feeling, and some of the worst Italian food in this town. Don't bring people here to impress them; they will ask if you also invested in FTX and put all your cash in SVB.

This place is overhyped and way past its prime. The service and especially the manager (Maggie) are an absolute farce. An embarrassment to what was once an esteemed establishment where classic New york service and food quality ruled. 

Pros:

1) Ambience is cosy and not too stuffy. 

Cons

1) Food is way too salty. Every dish we ordered, especially the pastas. The "free" appetisers were almost inedible.How stale is that garlic bread? Hint: like a brick, you could break a window with it.

2) Door staff are completely rude and unsmiling. Newsflash: for a lunch service, please be reminded you aren't hired as door b*tches of the city's most exclusive club -- of which Carbone clearly is not.

3) There were glitches with the service throughout the meal, and when the manager Maggie was finally called she shrugged it off like it was not her problem whatsoever. The cherry on top was when extra charges were put onto our bill (for things we clearly did not order) and when the manager was called over, all she said was "ohh oops". Are you kidding?!She probably put them on there in the first place knowing her terrible attitude and complete opposite attitude of respecting customer service. A completely ruined meal. The rot starts from the top and sad to see Carbone is rotted to the core. A shame -- we used to always come here and this place is now run by clowns with no idea what it takes to run a classy, respectable establishment in an incomparable city like New York.

Amazing escape for the summer heat! We had a great lunch with even better service. Our server had so much enthusiasm it made dining at this well known restaurant even more special. My favorite was the famous spicy rigatoni.

An authentic mid-century Italian American restaurant is inexpensive, fills your plate with generous portions, and serves the house wine in little non-wine glasses.  That describes Q's in Hillside, Illinois in the 1960s.  Italian beef sangwayjiz (as my Italian aunt pronounced the word) is what I remember.  

Carbone uses the mid-century Italian American theme, like Disney creates themed experiences.  Owners took the old restaurant then updated and up priced the menu.  Raw beef with instead of Italian beef.  Lobster in the ravioli.  The main servers are wearing the kind of tuxedos we wore at weddings in the 1970s and in the color of Rajneeshee-maroon. A family-run restaurant provides jobs for the family.  An investor-run restaurant keeps owners far from the kitchen.  So fancy, Carbone earned a Micheline star around 2014 .  

Confirming its inauthenticity, Carbone's website warns of a dress code:

Any guest who does not appear sufficiently well-presented may be refused entry. No shorts, open-toed shoes, or tank tops.  Athletic wear and baseball caps are kindly prohibited. 

"Kindly prohibited"??  Hey people.  I've got a bit of a bald spot.  It's 84 degrees.  I want to wear shorts and my only hat, which is the baseball variety.

Inside, the first thing that hits you is the loud Dean Martin music, which rotates with Tony Bennett and other classics.  The Rajneeshee-Italian waiter speaks v-e-r-y   c-l-e-a-r-l-y, very loudly, and never veers off topic into anything that could possibly lead toward a personal connection. Perhaps his hearing faded from the loud soundtrack.  Perhaps he thinks English is a second language for all the guests. 

The food was excellent. Each thing had a bit of a kick or twist.  But I had to ask about the Michelin star.  

"Hey, when we made the reservation, I thought this was a Michelin star restaurant.  Why'd you lose star?  Can we get a discount?"  

He seemed to ignore me.  So, I spoke up in his manner.  "WHY   DID   YOU   LOSE   THE   MICH E LIN    STAR?"  

Later that evening, we ate at a real Italian restaurant, Monte's Trattoria.  I asked the waiter, who had worked there 30+ years, "What do you think of Carbone?"

"Total rip off. They mark up their wine three times. You see him?"  He said pointing a large, weary man chef's whites.  "That's Pietro Mosconi.  He's the owner for 40 years." 

We very much enjoyed our classic Italian meal at Monte's Trattoria with a nice bottle of Chianti Classico for the price of two glasses at Carbone.  I highly recommend Monte's.  But I digress.  Back to Carbone:

Judgment:  Carbone offers great food.  They should dial back the phony atmosphere. 

https://medium.com/@JeffreyMerrick

Ordered:
Caesar alla ZZ (~$32)
Spicy Rigatoni Vodka (~$34): 2 half portions
Mario's Meatballs (~$27)
Glass of White Wine (~$19): Friulano Blend, Borgo Del Tiglio "Milleuve Bianco"; Friuli, Italy 2021

Aya's take:
Carbone is a renowned Italian spot and still one of the hardest reservations to get in NYC. Lunch reservations tend to be easier to get than dinner, and definitely keep your Resy notifications on and your credit card information already on file so you snag a spot if one is available. Upon entering, the atmosphere is classy, sophisticated, and old-school. The service was solid but not different than service I've received at other restaurants. We started off with their complimentary garlic bread, mozzarella, and salami. The mozzarella was super fresh; the garlic bread was slightly too hard but had good flavor. I didn't try the salami as I don't eat pork; I wish they offered an alternative because it sucks to see it go to waste. The Caesar alla ZZ was not really made tableside. The waitress making it was in the center of the backroom putting it together, and we just got the salad once it was done. The Caesar alla ZZ is good but way too horseradish-heavy. The croutons were absolutely delicious and the fresh parmesan on top was superb. The horseradish was way too overpowering and really took away from the rest of it. The Spicy Rigatoni Vodka was really well-made. I kind of wish they didn't plate it in half portions and put it on their beautiful iconic dishes. It's super creamy, slightly spicy, and the pasta is cooked very well. It was perfectly complemented by Mario's Meatballs which are a must! They're tender, large, and full of flavor. We ended with their complimentary rainbow cookies. I'm not a fan of rainbow cookies but these were probably some of the better ones I've had. Overall, I found Carbone to be a little overrated. I'm so glad I finally got to give it a try, but I wouldn't go out of my way to come back. PS, for those wondering, the $50+tax/person to make the reservation is immediately deducted from your total bill at the end.

Carbone. Carbone, Carbone, Carbone. Is it a must visit in NYC? Yes, 100%. Is it the best Italian food you'll ever have? No, I've been to Italy. Is Carbone worth the experience? Yes. What do people usually get? Spicy rigatoni. The croutons on the Cesar salad are pretty epic! You have to try these. You can share both plates. The complimentary cookies at the end are pretty solid as well. So Carbone, which is one of the hardest reservations to get, rightly so, is on the Resy app. That is the only way to get a res. 30 days prior, at 7 am PST start clicking. It took me 3 different tries on 3 days and I finally got it. I was so hyped to finally try it. As much as I loved the experience, they lost its Michelin star in 2022 and you can kind of tell why. The food is good but didn't blow me away. The service, unreal. Probably the best service I've experienced. It's worth the experience, but don't think the food lives up to the hype anymore.

What's not to love about Carbone? Okay, maybe just how hard it can be to snag a reservation. The spicy vodka sauce may be my favorite spicy vodka I'd ever had and the mixed onions within it add the perfect sweetness. Not pictured but I really enjoyed the table side caesar salad. The truffle corn had great flavor and so did the lobster ravioli but I have had better of both. The table side mozerella was very fresh- clearly it was just made

Treated ourselves to a lunch at Carbone and had an amazing time. Between the infectious energy of our server, Joey (who was so welcoming and accommodating), and the stream of delicious food--the complimentary bread, house mozzarella and salami to the absolute highlights of our lunch: the spicy rigatoni (which was spicy, tangy and light) and the lobster ravioli (this one was decadent, rich and packed with lobster), both were perfectly cooked and balanced each other out. We ended our meal with the zesty cheesecake (which was recommended by Joey), finishing off a very memorable meal.

Carpaccio Piemontese - I love the addition of mushroom. Please do remember to save some bread for this!! On its own it's slightly salty, but it goes so well with the bread and cheese!

Spicy rigatoni vodka - there are reasons that this dish is the popular and classic one. It's just a spectacular combination of spicy, sour, and creamy. 

Lobster ravioli - also a very solid dish! We ordered this after seeing other tables order coming up. Neat and really good raw materials.

Tiramisu - it is huge...you'll never go wrong with tiramisu in an Italian restaurant

We went there for our anniversary and had the best time! Now I understand the hype around this restaurant. Our service was diligent and gave us impeccable service. They paid attention to all the details. We had the Cesar salad to start and it was prepared alongside the table. One of the waiters helped us select our wine. She explained all of the ones we were interested in and it was extremely helpful. The spicy  rigatoni sauce was phenomenal. We also tried the lobster ravioli and it was full of flavor with every bite. We will definitely be back.

Honestly, I was full after I saw the manager and I didn't even get to eat at Carbone. We arrived to our reservation 5 minutes late (after trying to call twice) due to problems with the Ritz Carlton car service. We arrived and asked the host for our table and the told us they could not seat us after telling them we were flexible with either indoor or outdoor. After having the res for over 2 months I would say Carbone is super underwhelming and not worth the hype... I walked into 12 year olds slurping pasta and was immediately turned off. I hope they b*rn to the ground.

I secured a Sunday lunch reservation at Carbone's outdoor patio, which turned out to be more casual than their indoor dining. They tried to keep that classic elegant atmosphere outside, but it felt a bit strange - dark colors and curtains blocking sunlight on a patio? Still, it was a pleasant spot to dine, and the service was excellent. We ordered three dishes, and the spicy rigatoni was definitely the star of the show. The veal parm and broccoli were good, but not special - probably wouldn't order those again. They did serve up some complimentary mozzarella, salami, and bread. I think this place gets a lot of hype for their rigatoni and overall dining experience, and maybe that raised my expectations too high. It's worth checking out for dinner, mainly for the vibes, but given the price tag and the headache of securing a reservation, I wouldn't go just for the food.

No wonder it's a legendary NYC place. The ambiance, service & food was awesome. We had Sunday 8/11/2024 lunch time reservation & enjoyed the entire meal. The pre dinner plate of Supersad, garlic bread & house fresh mozzarella is more than enough. 
We had the Spicy Vodka sauce & pasta it did not disappoint. I ordered the Veal parmigiana which was best I ever had, pounded & bone plate.
Our well dressed server was great, funny and very knowledgeable of each menu item.  we were stuffed & had to walk around Village after.
A must to visit in NYC!
Nick Marino

I cannot emphasize enough how much I/we enjoyed our dining experience last night. The service by Joey and the rest of the team was amazing.... Friendly, engaging, warm and professional. The food quality and flavor were wonderful.
Thank you all to Team Carbone for a most memorable evening.

"New Table Alert: Carbone".  The glorious words from Resy danced across my screen and I had zero hesitation in scooping a last minute reservation for a first lunch seating on a weekday.  Did Carbone live up to all of its so-difficult-to-book hype?  YES.  This was possibly the best Italian meal I've had in recent years.  My favorite dish was the Spicy Rigatoni Vodka, which was cooked and prepared to absolute perfection.  The Veal Parmesan was also delicious (don't forget the bone), highlighted by Carbone's homemade mozzarella.  Service was stellar as expected with a classic Italian vibe inside.  Hope to be back soon for more!

From the moment you walk into this establishment, you know you're in for an amazing experience. 

All I can say is if you're in NYC and want to dine at the good place where all the locals go, this is it!

Carbone was amazing!!! Reservations were needed and require a $50 per person deposit. The deposit goes toward your meal so don't worry. The food was excellent!! The spicy rigatoni vodka lived up to the hype! The Mario's meatballs were so flavorful I could've had seconds. The clams were delicious, even if you're not a seafood person, you could eat these and never know they were from the sea. The pork chop was perfectly cooked and melts in your mouth. And to finish off the meal, the tiramisu cake was light and delightful. No complaints on the food. The ambiance was good, however, the music was really loud and we often times couldn't hear each other talk. I did have a bone to pick with the dress code. I couldn't wear shorts. Even nice ones with a collared shirt. I wore jeans and a collared shirt. Was just a little uncomfortable having to wear pants. Overall, the experience was pleasant. Would come back.

We were thrilled to experience Carbone after reserving one month in advance for $200. The night was fine (the cauliflower was exquisite), UNTIL our server talked down on us and acted as if we weren't worthy of dining at his place of employment. Not only did he act in a condescending manner when we inquired about the menu, but the disrespectful comments continued throughout our evening. We were informed, after politely declining dessert, that the cookies were "free, so dig in". 


Food was incredible, but the experience was extremely disappointing.

Carbone is a luxury dining experience.  But, it's not Michelin quality food.  Know that going into it if that's important to you.

Kelly, our server, did absolutely zero to make our special occasion special.  She was a dud and detracted from our experience.

The music is great, the booths comfy and cozy, and the dressed up patrons make it a lovely evening overall.

Cheesecake is the best I've had anywhere.  That's easily 10 stars.

Caesar salad is very bland.  They can definitely enhance that in some way other than adding fresh salt.

Wow Wow Wow. What a meal at Carbone. For us, it was absolutely worth the hype. 

Tucked into soho, Carbone fits in well with the rest of the neighborhood. Reservations are hard to get but not impossible. Of note, we did place the in advance $50/person deposit through resy, which they returned to us when we went to pay instead of it contributing to the total price. Service was prompt, and our waiter was very attentive and kind. We researched heavily before coming and ordered based on the menu items that were more popular amongst others - and we are so happy we did!

We started off dinner with complimentary cheesy bread, mozzarella, and salami. Best to combine and enjoy all 3 together. Then on to entrees for us. Truly the star of the show is the spicy rigatoni pasta. The pasta was creamy, warm, cooked perfectly - truly the best dish that we ordered. We also loooved the tortellini al ragu - the tortellini was creamy and melted in your mouth, and the ragu sauce complimented it perfectly. We also ordered the meatballs which were solid meatballs. 

For dessert, you receive their complimentary Italian almond cookies which are so fun and on theme. We also ordered the hazelnut chocolate cake which was to die for. 

All in all, it is soooo worth the hype. Do not miss out on the spicy rigatoni vodka or the hazelnut cake!!!

10/10 the most amazing experience! Food was ...go make your reservation now! 
Service is perfection!

Meatballs 3 super large, chewy, pure tomato sauce  w/o much seasoning, slightly sour
Assorted Baked Clams 4 three flavors, pesto, uni, spicy w/ bacon, flavorful
Lobster Ravioli 5 Chinese dumpling shaped, large minced filling, lobster chunks, flavorful white cheesy sauce
Spicy Rigatoni Vodka 3 hard, chewy, not a lot of sauce, flavorful, mild spicy

I requested a reservation months in advance for lunch since it was the only time available and I was super excited to finally try the one and only Carbone. 

The waiters came by and handed us gigantic menus, told us the specials, and asked if we wanted any drinks - we said just water. They seemed a bit snobby any time we had questions and their answers felt patronizing. 

The food itself was very good and each person at our table had a different favorite which shows how diverse and delicious each dish was. And our water glasses were never empty. 

When we got the bill, we noticed that our water glasses weren't empty because they were charging us by the bottle - $60 for our table for water alone! 

Overall, I think everyone should go to Carbone at least once, but I have no plans to go back just because of the snobby service and because you can find equally good Italian food in the area for cheaper.

This place does, in fact, live up to the hype.

We went for lunch and were not disappointed. The burrata and salami starter were delicious. We obviously had to try the spicy rigatoni, which was delicious (and not really *that* spicy if you're on the fence because somebody in your party is sensitive to spice.) We also got the caesar salad - which I wasn't even planning on trying until we saw it come out for somebody else. It didn't disappoint - and had some ginormous croutons. The service was on point.

The star of the meal was the veal parm, which we split.

The restaurant itself was packed, even at 2:30 in the afternoon but the ambiance was cute. They don't seem to be too strict on the dress code listed on the website. You're not wearing shorts but plenty of people were.

Carbone is a must-visit for a date night in NYC! The food is absolutely delicious--classic Italian dishes with bold flavors that never disappoint. The cozy, old-school vibe adds to the charm, though it can get crowded, which only adds to the lively atmosphere.

We ordered Assorted Baked Clams, Spicy rigatoni Vodka, Tortellini al Raga, Veal Parmesan, Corn Tartufato which filled two of us up very very well. 

Of course their starter bread and cheese are  yumyum.

The servers were super friendly and attentive, making the experience even better. If you're looking for a spot with great food, a fun ambiance, and excellent service, Carbone is the place to be! Highly recommend for a memorable night out!

Our meal here was solid -- we ordered what our server called "the Carbone 101": the caesar, the rigatoni, and the veal parmesan. Loved the bread and cheese and meat to start -- the salami was the best I've ever eaten. And we had a dessert too, in addition to the complimentary cookies: the hazelnut torte. Everything was so delicious -- this place is pretty expensive, and "worth it" might be a hard all. Is the food the best Italian in the city? Probably not. But really it's the service here -- impeccable -- that's the star and makes the hefty price tag feel worth it.

Reserved a table in advance. Staff were very friendly and answered my questions well. 
Salami, cheese and bread tasted great! 
Food came out fast. We ordered the Spicy Rigatoni Vodka and Fettucine Con Funghi. 
Rigatoni was good but overhyped. 
Fettucine con Funghi was over seasoned. 

I've heard lots of good things about this place, but was quite disappointed after tasting the food.

As a vegetarian, there are not many options at all. The pasta is good but it's not the best I have ever had. The hype of the restaurant truly just comes from the limited reservations. Also the food, was not much to my liking and I would change the service. The hospitality can be better, especially for a place like Carbone. The ambiance is lovely, and the place is cute

Love food will come again  the combine pasta was so good . Will come visit again . My friend did the reservation for this restaurant they give free bread and cheese on the side the main dish was pasta and meatball

I am so happy this was worth the hype!!! Waitstaff was incredible, never felt rushed to leave, & everyone was so nice. All the food was cooked to perfection, the pork chop melts in your mouth. The famous spicy rigatoni pasta was everything that it was cracked up to be. I would 100% come back!!!

I waited forever to finally snag a reservation! Carbone is seriously overrated. If you believe this is the best Italian food you've ever had, I genuinely feel sorry for you. The complimentary mozzarella, salami, and garlic bread were fresh--probably the best part of the meal. I also enjoyed the assorted baked clams, and the corn tartufato was sweet, creamy, and rich.

The Caesar salad was just okay. I was a bit perplexed by the massive anchovies and the large, rock-hard croutons.

The spicy rigatoni was underwhelming, though it was cooked al dente. As for the lobster ravioli, skip it--definitely not worth it. It felt more like a shrimp dumpling with a few pieces of lobster thrown in.

Definitely overpriced and overhyped.

Ignore every hater. This restaurant is Underrated in every aspect. Yeah, maybe their style is a little too buttoned up, and formal. Maybe their decor, staff, and menu are a bit stiff, &uptight. But theoretically this place does everything right. They took every chance that they could to do things well -- every detail - just to make it part of The Experience. Italian food made classically well with zero faults that I could find.

I really wanted this to be a 5 star experience, but it fell just a bit short. We came last Tuesday with a reservation for 4 people for 1:45. We were seated promptly and served with DELICIOUS garlic bread, salami, and mozzarella. Almost the highlight of the meal, and got a refill on the bread. We ordered the pork chops, lobster ravioli, mushroom pasta, and linguine with clams. The pork chops were well seasoned and super tender (but no carb with the meal). The lobster ravioli and a good portion of lobster, and the linguine with clams were incredibly flavorful. The mushroom pasta fell so short though, the pasta was overcooked and soggy, and the dish lacked cohesion and flavor. Furthermore, our entrees were delayed for an hour, and no one came to apologize for the delay or brought out our food until we asked. Nothing was comped for that delay, including any dessert for my partners birthday (although they gave a candle). The chocolate cake was pretty good but the tiramisu was dry and more like a cake, definitely not worth $25. Overall would recommend certain food items, but hope they are able to provide better service.

Got a lunch reservation and seated in the outdoor patio. They make a good effort to make the outdoor patio have similar ambiance as inside. 

Started off with bread, salami and mozzarella cheese. They were all quite delicious and set the stage for their signature dish, the spicy vodka rigatoni. 

I am no pasta connoisseur, but the pasta was pretty tasty. Right amount of spice. The meatballs were so moist and hearty. The Caesar salad was also very delicious, especially the croutons. They were buttery and crispy. 

Lastly, I had the espresso martini and it was one of the best I've ever had. 

If you can get a resy here, would recommend. Not sure if it's worth trying to get a reservation months in advance though.

Ive been here consecutively for the past 4 years and everything is always amazing. The mood is transformed when you walk in. Small spot with top quality foods always so well seasoned and cooked to perfection. The staff always mention the specials! The vibe is amazing. Definetly dont underestimate the sides!! everything delicious.

Yummy food at an inflated price. Highlight was the baked clams. We were able to add 3 more clams for $12 since we had a table of four. 

Other thoughts:
- House chopped salad: Not bad, it's nice and bright. Sundried tomatoes are great and juicy but otherwise nothing too special
- Artichoke hearts: Skippable
- Spicy rigatoni: Great, but just so expensive for what it is
- Lobster ravioli: Great, I preferred the juicy lobster inside the ravioli over the external chunks
- Tortellini ragu: Great -- cheese melts in your mouth

The service was good, but I wish they would ask before taking away our dishes (since we usually still wanted the sauce).

Overall, I don't need to come back but it was nice to have the experience once.
Amazing food incredible service fabulous ambience.  Greatl Las Vegas location Nothing else to say.
Let's be honest, while they are the perfect keto food, basic chicken wings can become very boring. That's why these Keto #Sweet Chili Wings are a great way to spice up your keto diet.

The food was delicious, specifically the bread and rigatoni alla vodka! The service was also amazing, we had the kindest, funniest server who helped us with the menu and portion sizes. Overall the restaurant was pretty loud so it was difficult to talk, but it was still very clean and romantic.

Honestly I thought this place would be over hyped but the level of service was unbeatable. The entire staff is extremely professional and clearly values hospitality and making your dinner an experience.
The restaurant felt like a classic Italian establishment and was cozy on the inside. 
Almost every dish we had was absolutely delicious, but the one thing we would not order next time was the lobster. Not worth the high price in my opinion and was the one item we all collectively agreed was not as flavorful as the rest. Absolutely must get the assorted clams - and get one flavor for each person. They're so unique and were the perfect appetizer. The spicy rigatoni was the number one thing we wanted to get here since it's so popular and it was also perfect. 

Overall it was a great experience at an iconic restaurant!

My friend and I came here for a late night dinner. We were so excited as we've eaten at the Dallas location before. We were seated on the outside patio and we were disappointed with the experience. The food did not disappoint as usual but the service was severely horrible which downed the experience. The server was extremely snobby and when we tried to order more food he told us that we couldn't because they only take complete orders but we could add and order dessert. This was never told to us before and a table came in after us and ordered so the kitchen wasn't closed. We are also two service industry people so we know bad service. Our reservation deposit covered most of the check however we still left 20% based on the total before the deposit. The servers demeanor also changed when he saw the tip which caused us to see that he maybe thought we weren't going to tip well which is sad. The food lives up to the hype but wouldn't recommend based on the service experience as it makes it not worth it

The highly trafficked and never can get a reservation Carbone well finally was able to get a reservation Sunday at 9:15 pm!!  I'll take it !  Beyond excited the place reminded me of old schools brat pack scenario.  The vibe was you no entered into your culinary experience.  The service was dead on and our waitress Samantha was beyond knowledgeable of the menu and was able to answer any questions we may have had.  Carbone did not disappoint .  From appetizers to dessert which was totally full but cousins pass up a slice of cheesecake .  Everything is amazing fresh homemade and imported and the quality is above all .  It's a true experience and a delight to have this opportunity to dine here .  I will be back if I could get a reservation !!  lol

Whether you're looking for casual or fine dining, this place will cater to both. Italian at its finest. From the minute you walk in the door, service is top notch. Every person knows their duties and makes sure you are catered to. That's just the service. Then you get to the dishes. 

From LA to NY, I've had Italian many times. If we're wanting superior ingredients with superior flavor, you definitely want to try this place out. Fresh warm mozzarella in olive oil, fresh garlic bread, and salami to start the meal. Amazing starter! Mozzarella was so good with the bread and salami! If I was hungry, I would've asked for more of this. Spicy rigatoni vodka and veal parmesan for the main was perfect. Rigatoni dish was creamy and perfect in flavor. And then there's the veal. Wow! I'm not a fan of veal because there's an after taste. But wow... this was so good! Tender with great flavor. Made to perfection. I would get every dish again! 

We went in not too hungry, so we had leftovers. Heated it up for dinner and it still tasted great! Highly recommended!! 

Tip: Make reservations as soon as they open. Very difficult to get a table here. It's a $50 deposit to hold your reservation, but they will apply that to the bill later. High priced meals but all worth it!

I didn't want to like Carbone. I was hoping this was one of those overhyped places so that I wouldn't need to ever come back. Unfortunately for me, their spicy rigatoni vodka really *is* that good. If you're able to snag a reservation, it's definitely worth a visit. It won't come cheap, but you'll leave feeling full and happy! I've come here to dine solo a few times and the staff has been super attentive every time. A classic institution that, so far, is worth the hype.

This is the second time in three months I've been able to.visit. Used the AMEX/Resy set up to secure reservations. First time, got a reservation at 11.00 and was seated inside. This afternoon was at 2.00 and was seated in the AMEX patio outside on the street. 

Bottom line: Irrespective of time or where you are seated, it doesn't matter. It's been great no matter when and where. 

Service is super attentive. Formal but not over the top. Engaging and friendly. Food and beverage are fantastique. 

In the words of my daughter who joined me at lunch today: "This is 'abandon your kids at a truck stop good!'l Today's lunch featured shrimp cocktail, oysters, spicy vodka rigatoni (of course), and steak Diane." Could not have been better.

It's packed the whole night up until closing, so we could not be seated early. However, they let us stand at the bar, so we ordered two drinks which were above average but very expensive.
We were seated not long after our reservation time. The complimentary bread, salami, and pickled cauliflower were not impressive.
The spicy rigatoni is very good. Perfectly cooked pasta, perfect temperature, and tasty sauce. I only wish they served more. Get your own order of it instead of sharing with someone. There are not many vegetarian options.
The ambiance was very nice, old-school Italian ambiance. Feels like you are in Goodfellas. Although, the staff and setting come across as overly pretentious, which takes away from what should be good hospitality. 
The tiramisu was not good. 
I will not be going through the hassle of acquiring another reservation to come back, but I'm glad I tried it once.

It's difficult to snag a reservation here for dinner, so we opted for a lunch date on a weekday. Even then, we couldn't secure an indoor spot, unfortunately, and had to sit outside. We started with the Caesar salad with anchovies and followed it with the spicy rigatoni as our main course. While the dishes are simple in concept, the execution was flawless -- every bite was packed with flavor. Both dishes were incredible and lived up to the hype, which is reflected in the price tag. Despite the challenges in getting a reservation, the quality of the food makes it well worth the effort.

I have seen so many TikTok's debating whether Carbone lives up to the hype.

To me it does.....

My suggestion would be to try to get a reservation for lunch since it's virtually impossible to get one for dinner lol.

Decided to treat myself to a really nice lunch - when I arrived there was already a line of people to get in.  I was promptly seated and my waitress, Samantha, was amazing!  She was friendly and checked on me often.  She even took a few minutes to have a small conversation with me.  The waiters constantly refill your water glasses and remove any empty plates and utensils quickly and quietly.  The service is a solid 10/10.  

The start you with homemade fresh mozzarella, bread and a salami-type meat.  From the start I was in seventh heaven lol it was so good.  I ordered meatballs and the spicy rigatoni which is a crowd favorite.   Absolute perfection!  I really wanted to finish the whole thing but I needed to save room for dessert which was a lemon cheesecake and they even give you two Italian cookies.  Everything was absolutely delicious!

My only negative was the Frank Sinatra music was LOUD lol.  Other than that the atmosphere was great.  Now this restaurant IS NOT cheap not even for lunch but for a once in a while splurge it is definitely worth it.  Just don't forget to make reservations!

Some of their dishes were really good and some were so so.  I guess I expected all food to be great in light of the hype and the fact that getting reservations here is pretty difficult.  I enjoyed the lobster ravioli and spicy rigatoni and their eggplant appetizer.  Their tortellini and spaghetti were not amazing at all.  
Our table was scrunched in between two tables where servers barely could get through.  So that was a little annoying.  Another nuisance was that people were lined up in the middle of the restaurant waiting to use the restroom.  It was unsightly as the line just was in the way taking up pretty much the entire half of the restaurant.  They do have an outdoor section that is away from this bathroom debacle.
I've been to Carbone a few times and each time I go, it gets better. The Service was great, and the food and atmosphere was amazing!

So disappointing. The service was great but overall the food was very mediocre. The veal was over-salted, the rigatoni was fine but nothing to write home about. The best dish was a special, the truffle tortellini but there were only 6 tortellini for $190. Yes, there was fresh shaved truffle on it but still not worth the price. Even the free rainbow cookies they brought out at the end were bland and tasted like wax. How do you mess up a rainbow cookie!?! Definitely did not live up to the hype.

Phenomenal! My wife took me out for my birthday and one dish that really stood out was the Spicy Rigatoni Vodka. Believe me when I say get your own plate; it's that good that you won't want to share it.
Have been to carbone probably 20+ times. Tonight I went and Antonio and Daniel blew us out of this world! The OG carbone is back and better than ever.

We went to celebrate a birthday. We had the 2pm lunch reservation which I believe is the last one. The service was amazing, the food was amazing, and by the end of the meal we had the whole place to ourselves which was awesome! The ambiance is lovely we weee seated in the back room. We were in the corner near the speaker and the music was a bit loud so we asked if they could turn it down, and they did! Great experience and would love to go back.

Snagged a reservation got the spicy rigatoni pasta. It's good not great. Wouldn't come back for it. It's a bummer because the build up was real. I definitely like torrisi's tortellini better than this pasta. Also, the spicy rigatoni is really heavy so we were both barely able to make it through our dishes. No regrets coming here but because I've been wanting to try this place years so I would have wondered if I hadn't tried it.

I don't really think they need my review. This is a very difficult place to get into, but well worth the effort. Service is impeccable, wine list huge and high quality. If you want old school NYC Italian this is the ambience you've been dreaming of!

A great spot for Italian in NYC! To start, they brought out some snacks-- salami, toast, mozzarella. Toast was too crunchy and too oily in my opinion. 

We also ordered the clams and truffle corn. Both were phenomenal. The clams were flavorful and not too salty. I find creamed corn rather underwhelming and wasn't expecting to like the corn. But perhaps because of the truffle, this was one of the highlights of the meal for me. Rich creamy perfection. 

For mains we split the fettuccine con funghi and the spicy rigatoni vodka. I liked the rigatoni better.

Dessert was carrot cake and rainbow cookies. Carrot cake was incredible. The best carrot cake I have had. Wonderfully spiced, the flavors meld together beautifully. The cream cheese frosting accompanies the cake perfectly.

Service was okay. We both felt like we were being rushed to finish our meal. The service at Torrisi was much better. 

Overall, I would return to Carbone and will definitely be ordering the corn again.

We wanted to try this place for so long because of all the hype - the food definitely lived up to it but the ambiance and service wasn't the best from our experience. 

We got a reservation at 10:30 pm and were able to be seated when we got there 15 mins earlier. The music is pretty loud as some other people have mentioned in their reviews. 

When we ordered, we got two starters and two entrees, and with the bread that we got, we thought it was enough. The server that was tending our table said otherwise, but he wasn't very nice about it. He recommended for us to get the veal and one more item of our choice to add on. We wanted to take a look at the menu first and put our initial order in first and he said that he has to put our order in all at once, so we felt pressured to order immediately. His tone and manner did not leave a good first impression at all and set a bad tone off to our dinner.

As for the food, the complimentary bread was amazing! The starters we got were the Caesar salad and the calamari. Caesar salad was good and the croutons on it were massive! The calamari was delicious as well - so flavourful. I would describe it as the spice and seasoning of calamari found in Chinese restaurants with the chilli peppers, but at a much higher price point. We loved the pastas! We got the spicy rigatoni vodka, fettuccini on funghi, and tortellini al ragu - the pasta had a really good texture and chew on it and the sauces were all really good. Our ranking of the pastas would be the rigatoni, then fettuccini, then tortellini. For the entrees, the veal was very soft and tender, but in terms of value, I'd recommend the pastas over the veal. The complimentary dessert we got was just cake - nothing special in our opinion. 

During our entire meal, our server didn't show up once to ask how everything was. Normally, I don't really care for that kind of stuff but I thought that it would be expected at a well-known restaurant like this. He only showed up when we asked for our bill, and guess what he does now that we have to pay and tip? He offers as limoncello drinks on the house - what convenient timing... 

Overall, come here and just expect good food. Have low expectations for service and ambiance, but hopefully you don't get our server and get to enjoy the whole experience! Probably won't go back again since it's hard to get reservations, but definitely need to try Carbone once!

Came for lunch and exceeded all my expectations. If there is one thing I recommend to try it's their spicy rigatoni vodka they are well known for. It's not very spicy due to the additional of onions but the sauce is creamy and flavorful. I also ordered Fettuccini con funghi which was good but I liked the rigatoni more. It wasn't very busy when we came for lunch so we had great experience with service.

Finally managed to get a reservation at Carbone, and it was really really good! I would only say that the food is not as good as how hard it is to get a reservation, but still a NYC classic and great great food. Favorite dish was the spicy rigatoni vodka (as expected!) and surprisingly the carrot cake was INCREDIBLE! Glad we tried it!

The hype is in securing the reservation. My retired colleague invited me to a show not far away. I managed a reservation (Global Dining). It was a feat as I kept missing notifications.
Inside was dark but not foreboding. I could read the menu without the flashlight from my mobile. We kicked off with libations to forge ahead as women. A margaritas and a cosmopolitan. Thanks to the bartenders.
We ordered the Potatoes; which sadly were exhausted and therefore no opportunity to taste. We each decided on lobster ravioli. After our entree, the fresh mozzarella, meat and crispy garlic toast arrived (I had to remind). The garlic toast presented as one each; had to request another.We closed with coffee (drip) and the chocolate hazelnut cake. They gave us a candle for my friends birthday and we sang.

Drake and 21 Savage cover Carbone on Spin Bout You (thanks to my daughters). As a

I hadn't been to Carbone in years and just recently went and it was great! Everything I ate was sooooo good. I literally could have stayed and tried everything on the menu. It felt like I had never been. I'm a big fan of their sauce in a jar for use at home so I was so excited to visit again. Small, quaint but felt like I was in a Mafia Movie  was waiting for The Godfather to be seated. Service is top notch and if the waitlist wasn't years long I would be back today!

I came here for a lunch. Is it overpriced? Probably. But the food is genuinely good, as is the service. At one point, I was thinking about how great a crouton I was eating was, and I don't think I'd ever had an opinion on croutons before, so I really can't complain too much about the price.
Service is great. I really enjoyed the veal parm. Delicious and really big- it's like 3 servings. I also liked the eggplant and zucchini app. Ambiance is cozy and intimate in the booth area.
Spicy rigatoni vodka pasta was to die for, everything was amazing. I really enjoyed the eggplant parmesean as well.

Walk past it. Hype is for nothing. Food is quite terrible.  I'd rather eat at Chipotle and that says a lot coming from someone that dislikes cilantro. I was charged three times for unsweetened iced tea. My husband had about four alcoholic drinks. Yes, charge us for one unsweetened iced tea but not three and the class was a narrow little glass about 6oz. More than half the glass was ice.

Excellent service & staff! The food was good, but did not exactly live up to the hype I had expected. I'd return for lunch as the atmosphere is relaxed and cozy. The waiters aren't pushy and we felt the pace of the meal was perfect. The baked clams were excellent!The spicy rigatoni was what I looked most forward to. It was good & I left happy. The meatballs were a bit undercooked. I look forward to trying lobster fra diavolo next time. They were out of it this time. I especially LOVED the rainbow cookies, which were complimentary & the carrot cake. Beautiful presentation for the carrot cake!!!

Let's be honest - you always hear people talking about Carbone in NYC. Is it worth the hype? 100000%, in my opinion! They take reservations up to 30 days in advance, and you have to book online. As they fill up extremely quick and hard to come by, make sure you plan ahead if you want to dine here! 

Came here for lunch around noon [as we had a reservation] and the place was absolutely packed. The atmosphere is extremely inviting and comfortable. It's loud so you don't feel bad having a conversation or talking loud, which is a huge win for me! 

The customer service is impeccable. I don't think I have ever dined at a restaurant with better service, attentiveness and overall hospitality. We truly were shocked at how friendly and helpful every single person we encountered was! When you go to the restroom, one of the employees even comes by to fold your napkin for you. UNREAL customer serivice experience! 

They start off by serving you fresh salami and bread - the salamai was so delicous! We ordered the meatballs and the spicy rigatoni vodka pasta which were both phenomenal. Specially, the spicy rigatoni vodka pasta was to die for - I highly recommend, 12/10!! We finished off with their fresh carrot cake for dessert which was, I'd say, the carrot cake I've ever had!

Everything is perfection at Carbone- I'm obsessed and cannot wait to go back!! 5 stars all the way!!!

I'm speechless with this place  ambience is top tier. Compared to my trip to Italy back in June, I would've believed I'm still in Venice while dining at Carbone. It's so transformative. The food. The dessert. The service. The pasta will surprise you, I wasn't expecting much from the spicy vodka. Simplicity goes a long way.  Top takeaway dishes for me was the Tiramisu (OMG I inhaled!!!!) and the spicy vodka. The garlic parm bread starter honestly was a little overbaked, too crispy for me. I fought so hard for a reservation, woke up everyday that week (over a month in advance) everyday at 7 AM on the dot to book. lol! so worth :)

Can't believe i got a resy for this place !! I've been wanting to try this place for so long and it did not disappoint !! The spicy vodka rigatoni was one of the best I've ever had -- they included fresh tomatoes, which I feel like is not common in a spicy vodka pasta. If you can snag a resy, I defs recommend going !!

It's now been 24 hours since our Thanksgiving Holiday Feast - and I feel lean enough to be able to write this review.  Carbone totally lived up to the reputation.  We wanted a holiday meal in NYC for Thanksgiving- and the ambiance, food, drinks and service exceeded our very high expectations.  The food was amazing - Prixe Fixe menu included all the Carbone hits- Spicy Rigatoni, the bread, the salami and parm, the caesar salad, the not to be missed meatballs etc.  AND then we had a full Thanksgiving meal of Turkey and all the fixings + pumpkin cheesecake (so light and fluffy), and pecan pie.  Yes it was too much food- but it was so good.  One of the first times we have eaten out for Thanksgiving - and we have no regrets.  Well Done!

Carbone is a NYC hotspot that you should definitely at least try once. My fiancée and I enjoyed the complimentary garlic bread, salami, and fresh mozzarella. We had to try the popular Carbone style Caesar salad with its tasty large croutons. We ordered the famous spicy rigatoni alla vodka and the lobster ravioli. We enjoyed the complimentary rainbow cookies, but the chocolate hazelnut dessert was the highlight of the night. The food was absolutely delicious, the service was topnotch, and the ambiance was very cozy.

Is it worth the hype? Absolutely. Get up early get online and get a reservation when they open it. I could not have loved a pasta more if I tried. 

Everything tastes so fresh, I was transported back to Italy. The meatballs are an absolute must and their garlic bread will live in my dreams rent free. 

The staff here is wonderful and always working so hard. 

Dark lit moody vibe in an old building, exactly what you'd expect from an old school Italian joint.

Been here multiple times. Food is good but nothing special. Drinks were average. Service was quick and the ambiance is old-New York style. The wine list was good too. Overall, I would say it's nice to go if it's convenient / possible
Love it here! The food is always a hit and the vibes are awesome. The staff is really kind and helpful, and super friendly. Alfonzo and the rest of the team made our visit extra special

Absolutely fabulous! From the service, to the delicious food to the ambiance- it's my favorite spot in New York! Reservations need to be made a month out but it's well worth it! Known for the spicy rigatoni and Frank Sinatra feel- I couldn't love this place more!
I had a fantastic experience celebrating my husband's birthday! The food was fresh and delicious, and the service was outstanding. To ensure you get a table, I recommend making a reservation online.
This was on my bucket list for quite some time and it was well worth the wait. I will dream about that spicy rigatoni for years to come.

Carbone is like no other. It's like a five star Italian American Disneyland restaurant. The waiters exude energy, Frank Sinatra's angelic voice fills the room, and the food is fantastic.

The menu is filled with heavy Italian American classics, all executed to perfection. Have been twice and I'm convinced everything on the menu is probably fantastic.

Things I've tried in order of favorites, although everything was great.
- Spicy Rigatoni
- Tortellini al Ragu
- Meatballs
- Assorted Baked Clams - 9 clams with 3 varying flavors
- Veal Parmesan
- Caesar alla ZZ - caesar salad prepared table side

The meal also starts with complementary meats, cheese, and bread, and ends with a little rainbow cookie.

Looking forward to returning with a large group to try more dishes.

Reservations are difficult, but use Resy notify and act fast when you get a notification.
Service and Ambiance is always a 10. This is our second time having a holiday meal at Carbone. Unfortunately, Christmas dinner was far below par. Very disappointing!

i know this place is supposed to be overrated but i loved it. the fettuccine con funghi was soooo good, honestly would get it over the rigatoni (the rigatoni was heavenly but it's only like 10% better than the next best rigatoni I've had). it hurt my heart that i couldn't eat the caesar salad but watching them make it tableside was fun! dessert was amazing and drinks were strong, lovely experience overall!

I can see why their pasta is so famous it was delicious the steaks was good but if I go back I will strictly stick to the pastas and fish. The service was great and the restaurant is very cozy and pretty

There are too many new openings in the city that you often forget about classic ones. BUT never Carbone. Still one of the hardest tables to book and for good reason. 

My fav part is the complimentary garlic bread with salami and mozerella. Hits every time. Esp that cheese ‍ Start with the carpaccio or the salad, both pretty salty so def better with a drink. I rly like the carpaccio, it's super thin, like spoon-scrapping, so it teases your appetite without filling it. 

For pasta, no words needed for the spicy vodka rigatoni ‍ This dish is what American Italian is built on. Tortellini is solid. Get it if that's your thing. I think the meatballs are another must and I don't even like minced meat. They're good and make the rigatoni taste even better? If you're strong enough for desserts, get the hazelnut cake but you didn't do it right if you still have space for that.

 carpaccio piemontese $34* 
 yellowtail crudo MP
 spicy vodka rigatoni $34*
 tortellini al ragu $35
 mario's meatballs $27*

영원한 클래식. 수많은 뉴욕 식당중에서 Carbone처럼 오랫동안 사랑받는 곳은 다 이유가 있다. 여기 리가토니는 긴말 필요없는 레전드 디쉬  미국 이탈리안의 정석이다. 기본찬(?)으로 주시는 마늘빵이랑 살라미 & 치즈도 너무 맛있음!! 저녁보다는 점심때가 예약하기 쉬우니까 도전해보기.

If I could give this zero stars I would, but I don't have that option. The server took my plate when I was still using it. The pork chop was so hard. I chewed it for 20 minutes straight and then had to spit it out. The meatball tasted like a lollipop and was so sweet I now have a cavity. The pasta was hard and crunchy not cooked. What the heck. The family size was the size of a small children's dinner meal and there were six of us... i had one noodle. The linguine and clams tasted like water topped with shreds of grass the only thing that tasted good was the water. # where the salt and pep??? I'm going to a food truck on the side of the street.

Cócteles 5  
Calamares 5  
Ravioli 5  
Spicy Rigatoni 5  
Ribeye 3  
Tiramisu-1  ‍
Service +5  
Ambiance 5

Food: 5/5 | Service: 5/5 | Experience: 4/5

It is quite difficult to get a seat here at Carbone, but I was able to make a reservation for 2 during a weekday lunch. While reserving your spot, you pay $50/person that will go towards your final bill.

This quite small restaurant is very cozy and intimate. Staff are all very professional, and it was a great experience - perfect for a date night. We ordered the spicy rigatoni vodka (split among 2), 3 Mario's meatballs, and the funghi trifolati, and the lemon cheesecake. The pasta was cooked al dente, and the sauce clung well to the rigatoni. The meatballs were very tasty, and a perfect addition to the meal. The mushroom dish was my favorite as the fungi are very tender and simply dressed, making for a dish where the mushrooms' umami taste was enjoyed. The lemon cheesecake was decadent and rich.

The food here was great, but tables were a bit closer together than I expected, and I sat right next to the bar cart, so I did not have the most space to move about comfortably.

There's a reason why carbone is so famous! The ambiance, the experience, the service and the food were all superb! They don't miss a beat. From their somm helping pair the perfect bottle to making a change in our order, everything was perfect. Even just the bread and pickled veggies were amazing. Of course we had the classics like the spicy rigatoni -!; veal parm which were mouth watering but we go to have the black truffle tortellini which was an explosion of flavor. I'm truly honored and ecstatic I got to enjoy this amazing place.

We were so excited to finally try Carbone since it is difficult to get a reservation. Hm, however I must say I don't think I fully understand why. I must say the service is 5/5, people there are super interactive and nice. However the ambiance is a little stuffy and small, it feels like 100 people stuck in a 50 person room kind of feeling. Food wise, lobster ravioli was really good. I'd come back for this. The Expresso Martini was also surprisingly amazing. Their well known spicy vodka rigatoni was just okay for me. I mean it was a lovely 4/5 dinner but I'm not sure I'd try so hard to get a reservation again?

Service excellent.  Ambiance nice.  Food varies.  Overall we enjoyed our dinner for two people and would return.  

The restaurant is attractive (for certain tastes) and seating is comfortable.  Tables are very close together.  In the bar area it's quite dark.  Plenty of tables in this area.  Music is a bit loud but not awful.  I don't understand why it is so loud, but still better than many other local restaurants.

Service was excellent.  With a smile, attentive but not overly so, responsive, pleasant, positive attitude from everyone.  Server, support staff, sommelier, management, hosts.  Really appreciated the PMA and professionalism.

Pre-meal (complimentary) Parmesan cheese, salami, cauliflower giardiniera, and bread were much appreciated.  VERY good tasting, beautifully presented, and frankly a lot of food which meant we ordered one item less for dinner than we anticipated.

Beet Siciliana (app) and Squash Agrodolce (side) were, for our tastes, terrific.  

Fettucine con Funghi disappointing.  

Linguini Vongole ok and nothing more.

Tiramisu fine.

So ultimately the food was highly variable for us and not in the top tier of Italian in NYC.  But add in the decor, wine list, and service and it's very nice.  Not obvious why it's such a tough reservation other than it's a pretty small restaurant.  

We did enjoy our dinner and will return.  We will try main dishes that are not pasta since those did not turn out great for us.  And a different dessert.  Might go with the beets and squash again though.
Consistant and good. They manage to keep the same flavors as the Carbone location in Hong Kong. This led me to try the Carbone in Vegas, and they didn't dissapoint either.

I want to start by saying that while the food here was good, I was disappointed in the service.  Especially for a place that you have to book a month out and put down a $50 deposit per person for. My enjoyment of the food did not outweigh the disappointing service and hassle it took to secure a reservation. 

We had an 11:45 reservation. I would like to note that Carbone is near two extremely popular bagel shops (Leon's and Popup) so the sidewalk was absolutely packed, and we had to discern that the huge lines in front of us were for the bagel stores and weave past them. The interior is small but nice and classy. 

It took over an hour for our entrees to arrive. We overheard a waiter talking to someone else that they had accidentally given our food to the wrong table. However, they made no move to apologize for this error or inform us why our food was taking so long to arrive. I would have respected some honesty as to why our food took so long to arrive. 

I did really appreciate the fact that they give every table complimentary bread, cured meat, mozzarella, and almond cookies. We ordered the Carpaccio, Tortellini, Rigatoni, Meatball, and the Potatoes Louie.

I really loved the truffle emulsion on the carpaccio. The carpaccio was probably one of my favorite bites alongside the tortellini. The vodka pasta here was good but pretty standard to what I've had before. Meatballs were good and is the perfect serving for 3 people since it comes with 3 meatballs.
Super fortunate to get to eat there.  Service was wonderful and highly recommend the food and experience.  If you can get a table.

We've been several times now and this was the best visit yet. 

We were seated in the back room (which I highly recommend for the ideal experience) and our server was an absolute pro. 

The restaurant interior is as classic and legit as it gets and really sets the tone for the meal. 

The food:

Prosciutto Mozzarella was a standout (even though it sounds kind of whatever). 3 diff kinds of meat and a second serving of the warm mozzarella that is easily the best I've ever had. 
House chopped salad was also a surprising highlight even though we had some buyers remorse as they prepared every other table's Caesar salad table side. 
Spicy rigatoni - skip this at your peril - it's outstanding every time. 
Lobster ravioli - expensive but worth every penny. The sauce is drinkable. 
Meatballs - my favorite I've ever had. It was almost like they were a little rare in the middle? I don't know if that's ok to say but they were off the charts great. 
We were absolutely stuffed by this point but the meat courses were obviously fantastic (steak and peppers / chicken parm) we just barely had room to soldier through. 
Ordered brown butter tiramisu and basically just smelled it in sadness because we couldn't even lift our forks by that point. 


Conclusion: set up notifications on Resy and find a way to get here. Bring a couple of friends so you can order everything and share family style.
This is a tourist trap. Overpriced, overrated, and the food was just ok. Would have been better getting a street burger.
Warm, white table cloth atmosphere. Very friendly staff and quick service. Delicious food especially the Spicy Rigatoni Vodka, Meatballs, Veal Parm and Mushrooms. Highly recommend.
You have to come to the NYC location at least once the spicy rigatoni was worth the hype. Service and atmosphere are great.

I FINALLY was able to snatch a lunch reservation at Carbone! After visiting its sister restaurant, Torrisi, I was super curious to see how Carbone would stack up.

First off, AMAZING service-- some of the best service I've had in a while in NY. Honestly the service at Torrisi wasn't the best so I wasn't expecting much, but I was pleasantly surprised. 

Second, the vibes were immaculate! You're literally transported to old NY. Everything is super classic and classy... loved it.

Third, the food was great! We ordered the oh-so-famous Spicy Vodka Rigatoni and Veal Parmesan to share between the 2 of us.

- Spicy Vodka Rigatoni: 10/10 (perfectly spicy and creamy vodka sauce! It was really well balanced. The pasta had the perfect bouncy texture too. Honestly I wasn't like blown away, but again this is probably one of the best rendition of this pasta I've ever had.)
- Veal Parmesan: 8/10 (hugeee portion size but again it's like $90. It was good, but not super memorable. Next time, I'd rather order 2 pastas!)

I've been here a couple of times now and what did Drake say?? "YOU KNOW HOW IT GOES WHEN THEY CAN'T GET A RESERVATION UP IN CARBONE!" Getting a Resy here is definitely an extreme sport but if you do get one, boy are you in for a treat! Inside is very intimate and beautifully constructed, and the food is an experience. Let's get into it! 

Lobster ravioli 9/10. Don't come here and not get it.
Spicy rigatoni vodka 10/10. Simple, but elegant. Another MUST have. Their best dish on the menu imo.
Meatball 8.4/10. A nice accompaniment to the rigatoni. 
Octopus pizzaiolo 6/10. The flavors are there but during my latest visit, it was overcooked and not worth the price.

The vibes alone are immaculate and the service is wonderful and intentional! It's a must try on any night if you're lucky to dine here.

Honestly worth the hype. We tried a variety of things from the menu and each dish was better than the last. The spicy rigatoni was my personal favorite, the sauce was extremely smooth in texture and so flavorful. Even their bread was delicious. I wish I could've taken the bread home with me.
What an experience! Food was great, service was also great... wait staff were attentive and funny!

Ah the infamous Carbone.

Though people love to hate on it for the prices (they're high) and how hard it is to get a res (it is), I had a really great experience here.

When we walked in for a 11:30 AM Saturday lunch res (thank you Resy notify), we were greeted warmly. One of the staff joked that our res was canceled with a grin on his face, which was pretty funny, if not mildly panic-inducing :)

The ambiance of the restaurant is fantastic. They seem to have captured a bygone era, with charming touches like an oversized menu and Sinatra playing in the background.

As for the food:
Oysters- fresh. No complaints.

Baked clams- very tasty, with 3 different flavors. We liked the one topped with uni the best.

Spicy Rigatoni- I was most excited for this dish, but it turned out to be good not great. They use Calabrian chiles, which makes for more tang than spice, but the pasta was cooked perfectly and the sauce was decent. Just not life-changing as some may have you believe.

Lobster Ravioli- my favorite dish of the meal. Ravioli tasted almost like Chinese seafood dumplings (in the best sense) with plenty of umami. I loved the rich cream sauce on this.

Ribeye Diana- excellent. Steak was perfectly cooked with a wonderful sauce.

Carrot cake- marvelous presentation. This is probably the least sweet carrot cake I've ever had, which is a good thing. Flavors well-balanced, loved the ginger ice cream, only detraction was it was slightly dry.

My main gripe is as most have pointed out, it is a bit overpriced. I think this place would be a definite 5 star if everything was 30% cheaper basically. I will say though, if you factor in the complementary antipasti (garlic bread, warm mozzarella, and salami when we went) and order strategically, it's not too bad, at least by NYC standards. 

Going to Carbone is like going to Disneyland. As long as you set the right expectations, you'll have a good time!
Outstanding service. Really good dishes. Best branzino ever. Lobster ravioli was excellent with a generous amount of lobster, which one should expect given the price. Fabulous atmosphere.

My friends and I somehow were able to get a reservation here and we were ecstatic! None of us had been to Carbone before. The table wasn't ready when we arrived so we had a drink at the bar while we waited. The staff have incredible personalities. They kind of give off a Disney World vibe - super happy, upbeat, and funny. They were great! We aren't the type of group who go to fancy or expensive restaurants often. But we knew going into this that it was going to be pricey. We each had three cocktails, appetizers, a few pasta dishes, dessert and cappuccinos. It was about $185/person with tip - worth it! Our favorites were the spicy rigatoni, veal parmesan and the chocolate hazelnut cake.

my absolute favourite restaurant. i know the hype around carbone, but their food and service are genuinely spectacular. i've been to this original location and the hong kong one as well. 

the bread they served us was warm and soft. our apps we got calamari and carpaccio - i've had these items at other italian restaurants, but carbone takes the cake. calamari was crunchy and not too bready, while the carpaccio was fresh and melts in your mouth. 

for our mains, we got their famous rigatoni vodka and lobster ravioli. i understand why everyone loves the rigatoni vodka - so simple yet iconic. for the lobster ravioli, it was so flavourful and rich - i might like this more than the former, because of the lobster meat! 

for dessert, we got the cheesecake. nothing too to special but still yummy. 

service was amazing and personal. the note they write on our cake was so cute. our sommelier was attentive and patient. our server was proactive with dishes and kindly swept our crumbs. 

ambiance was gorgeous and elegant, yet very homey. the lighting was dim and i felt warm. 

amazing. ps i was focused on my boyfriend and the experience, so i didn't take close up pics of the food - so enjoy my food and bf.

We came to carbone for our anniversary meal. We started off with the baked clams, it came in 3 different styles. Our favorite was the one topped with uni. 

For entrees we got the veal parmigiana, Meat balls, and spicy rigatoni. My favorite was the meatballs, great texture and well made. The veal parmigiana was good, but a little pricey for what it is.

For dessert, we had the tiramisu. It was nice and creamy. Cocktails were also nicely done. 

Service was excellent. We were sitting in the outside heated section, so a little bit of the ambiance was lost.

It took a couple a days a month ago to get this reservation! I was hoping to get it for Valentine's Day but the only reservation available was 11pm dinner. Ha! I tried every day, when reservations opened and finally got one... and let me tell you, it was worth it! You do have to pay a fee/ deposit of $50/ person but it goes towards your bill. We arrived early and they sat us right away. We were welcomed with complimentary garlic bread, mozzarella, and salami. We came for the spicy rigatoni and it did not disappoint it! I wanted to swim in that sauce... and the lobster ravioli sauce! Both AMAZING!! We also got the Cesar salad - another great dish and the chicken scarpariello - yum! We also received rainbow cookies after our meals. We ended our lunch with cappuccinos which were also amazing! The whole experience was incredible. I think we're going to make this a tradition and come back every year!

The name speaks for itself and definitely lived up to the hype. We started with oysters, which always hit the spot. Following was caesar salad, which was EVERYTHING. Next we went for the vodka pasta (you must!) and split the Bass Allison (yummy and herbal). We finished with tiramisu and were very stuffed (haha). Portion wise, everything was American-style. If you only got two things, def go with caesar salad and vodka pasta.

Don't know how anyone can give this place bad reviews. service was outstanding and the food was just terrific. Had the tortellini lobster, ravioli, meatballs, and veal Parmesan. All of which were stellar. Bread service was excellent. the atmosphere, although a little noisy and crowded was still outstanding. I highly recommend this restaurant

Carbone gets the hype for the right reason. The tradition Italian menu really does not miss and the exclusive ambiance is a great touch. The service here is above and beyond and each person makes the meal that much more special. Spicy rigatoni is a clear winner but the veal parm is a must order

We don't care how touristy we come off with this one, we absolutely loved our late meal here on our trip. We think about the carpaccio weekly it was soooo good. We understand that people have favorite Italian nyc spots, but if we have a chance to come here on our trips we are going to take that chance because we loved it so much. The service and vibes were amazing and can't wait to go again soon to see how it is this year!

Believe the hype. Superb service, amazing food, and Just a good vibe. I recommend this place 100 times over. Will definitely be back.

If you have Amex card use it to get reservations via resy. You will get priority for reservations. 

I loved the pasta, their wine list is extensive, they also have off the menu items if you're craving something particular.

Wonderful overall experience. Very difficult to get a reservation at a reasonable time but the ambiance, the staff and obviously the food are unmatched. Very attentive and accommodating to tailor your meal to your needs/requests. The lasagne special was one of the best dishes I've ever tried. Hope to return soon! Highly recommend.

Simple the best service and food we had in NYC. It took a while to get a reservation but we were able to get a spot . From start to finish their service was amazing. 

They started with some complementary mortadella cheese , salami and garlic bread. 

We ordered some Cesar salad , spicy carbonara pasta , lobster ravioli and meat balls. All the dishes were delicious, but the meatballs were the best. 

We had a great experience at this location. Highly recommended for a fam meal .

A little disappointed. Maybe it was all the hype but I left thinking that the food was overpriced and some of it was not what we had expected. When you walk in the ambience is nice with all the friendly waiters and waitresses formally dressed. The choice of music was odd for an Italian restaurant though. 

All the pastas were perfectly cooked. We got their popular Spicy Vodka rigatoni which was very good. I would recommend ordering one of their side vegetable dishes to cut down on the spiciness of the pasta. We also had their spaghetti puttanesca which was just ok if you like olives and capers. What threw all of us off was their Caesar salad. I almost took off one more star because of this dish. It was nice to have them make it at table side but for some reason the dressing was very pungent. We all enjoy Caesar salads but this was not one of them. 

It was a nice experience while we were in NY but doubt we would come back again because of the price. It also didn't match up to all the hype for me.

From the time we entered, our experience was amazing. Our waiter was very pleasant and knowledgeable about the menu. Everything that we ate was great. My favorite dish was the corn and ironically, the cherries although the reservations are hard to get they are definitely worth it and if you're ever in New York, this is definitely a top five restaurant you have to visit

It's a cool vibe for sure. I didn't want it to be true.... But it's definitely way over-hyped. You go more for the experience but it wasn't the best Italian I've had. The service just pushed so much... want you to order more and more, and drink more expensive bottles. We kinda heard them all say the same lines to every table, no personal touches or connections. And the spicy rigatoni was just okay. It's was all just okay!
Pasta is amazing but the price is just way too much. Once in a while it is ok.  The menu is awesome

Ok so everyone always talks about carbone in nyc and we finally got lunch reservations   And i am telling you it's so worth it. Ambiance is great. They played oldies music. Really romantic. Service was great. They brought out salami. With garlic bread. And also mozzarella cheese. Warm in some herbs. Absolutely mouthwatering   
Food was simply amazing. I am not at all Italian cuisine fan. However, this food was simply the best. Meatballs fairly large and seasoned to perfection. Sauce simply unforgettable.  Spicy ragatoni in vodka sauce was incredible. Oysters fresh and yummy.  Salad was fresh and filling. Yellow tail special was so good. I was glad it was on chefs specials that afternoon. 
Such lovely experience. I am excited to go back soon. 
It's a busy street. Parking garage around the corner. Very convenient.

Snagged this reservation about a month in advance and was so excited to finally try Carbone after thoroughly enjoying Torrisi last month. 

Really enjoyed the fresh mozzarella with the salami and garlic bread. Would have liked more garlic bread though bc we ended up just shoving all the mozzarella on the small slice of bread.

Assorted Baked Clams - they serve 3 types of clams (can't remember all the specific flavors now) and really liked the variety here. There was one with uni and the 2 others were more classic Italian with breadcrumbs and more of a tomato sauce. Would recommend!

Spicy Rigatoni Vodka - we had to order this classic and I'm glad we did! The sauce is rich and creamy but is nicely balanced with the kick of spice. I wish we ordered a second plate. 

Veal Parmesan - wasn't a big fan of the veal Parmesan. Haven't really had veal often so can't say too much about it. The meat on the rib actually tasted better as it was thick and juicy! Wouldn't get this again.

Overall, the food was great albeit pricey. With just these 3 dishes, our total came out to about $160 before tip. Service was nothing to write home about either. Glad I got to cross Carbone off my list.
